title: feat: integrate caveman into clarification and commit message prompts [RD-1137]
body:
Jira issue: https://ignify-rd.atlassian.net/browse/RD-1137
Repository: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman

Summary: Tích hợp caveman vào claude teammate

## Plan

## Context

Caveman is installed as a Claude Code user-scope plugin on the VM. Its `SessionStart` hook auto-injects caveman rules into every `claude` CLI invocation. All `runClaude*` calls therefore receive caveman by default. This ticket wires it up deliberately: reinforce it where wanted, suppress it where not.

## Changes

### 1. Suppress caveman in implementation prompts — `src/claude/prompts.js`

Add `"stop caveman"` (the natural-language deactivation phrase the caveman hook recognises) to `buildImplementationSystemPrompt()` and `buildImplementationStepSystemPrompt()`. This prevents compressed prose in the main implementation and plan-step invocations, where full technical precision in explanations matters.

### 2. Reinforce caveman in the clarification system prompt — `src/claude/prompts.js`

Add `"Use /caveman mode. Respond in compressed caveman style to save tokens."` to `buildJiraClarificationSystemPrompt()`. The hook already activates caveman, but explicit system-prompt reinforcement wins over other injected instructions that might compete mid-session.

### 3. Replace hardcoded commit message with a caveman-commit Claude call

**Current:** `buildImplementationCommitMessage(title)` in `src/worker/pull-request.js` returns a static `feat: ${normalizedTitle}` string — no AI, no diff inspection.

**New:** Add `runClaudeGenerateCommitMessage(repoPath, title, { timeoutMs, logger })` in `src/claude.js` (or a new `src/claude/commit-message.js`). The function:
1. Runs `git diff HEAD` (or `git diff --cached`) in `repoPath` to get the staged diff.
2. Calls `claude -p` with a system prompt that invokes `/caveman-commit` and provides the caveman-commit skill rules (conventional commits, ≤50-char subject, body only when non-obvious why).
3. Returns the generated commit message string.
4. Falls back to the current static `feat: ${normalizedTitle}` if the Claude call fails or returns empty, so commit never blocks.

Update callers in `src/worker/pull-request-workflow-support.js` (`commitPartialPullRequestChanges` and the per-step commit path) to `await runClaudeGenerateCommitMessage(...)` and pass the result to `commitAndPushRepoChanges`.

## Scope boundary

Do **not** add caveman to:
- `buildImplementationSystemPrompt` (suppressed above)
- `buildImplementationStepSystemPrompt` (suppressed above)
- `buildPullRequestReviewSystemPrompt` (not mentioned by user)
- Google Chat response prompts (not mentioned by user)

---

If you approve this plan and want implementation to begin, comment with "Implement", "LGTM", "LGTM!", or "Approved".

title: docs(security): add inspect-before-run note to curl-pipe-to-bash one-liners
body:
> **Automated audit**: This PR was generated by [NLPM](https://github.com/xiaolai/nlpm-for-claude), a natural language programming linter, running via [claude-code-action](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action). Please evaluate the diff on its merits.

## Bug

Both `hooks/install.sh` and `hooks/uninstall.sh` document a `bash <(curl ...)` one-liner as the recommended remote install method, with no accompanying note about the supply-chain risk of executing unreviewed remote shell code.

**Why it matters**: Users who follow the curl-pipe-to-bash pattern execute remote code without any opportunity to review it first. If the GitHub repository's `main` branch were ever compromised (or if a CDN/MITM attack occurred), a user following the documented pattern would silently run malicious code. Adding a short "inspect before you run" comment alongside the one-liner gives security-conscious users a clear alternative path at zero cost to other users.

## Fix

Added a one-line comment immediately below each `bash <(curl ...)` example pointing to the safer download-inspect-run pattern:

```
#          For added safety, inspect first: curl -o install.sh <URL>; less install.sh; bash install.sh
```

This matches the style of existing comments in the files and adds no functional changes — it is purely documentation.

**Files changed**: `hooks/install.sh`, `hooks/uninstall.sh`

**Security finding**: Medium (curl-pipe-to-bash pattern documented without integrity-check warning — NLPM security scan findings #2 and #5)

title: fix(security): pin REPO_URL to tagged release instead of main branch
body:
> **Automated audit**: This PR was generated by [NLPM](https://github.com/xiaolai/nlpm-for-claude), a natural language programming linter, running via [claude-code-action](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action). Please evaluate the diff on its merits.

## Bug

`hooks/install.sh` sets `REPO_URL` pointing to the `main` branch:

```bash
REPO_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/hooks"
```

This means any push to the default branch — including a compromised commit — silently changes the files that future users download and install without any action on their part.

**Why it matters**: Users who run `install.sh` after cloning from a tagged release, or who run the curl-pipe-to-bash variant, expect to get the files that correspond to the version they chose. The `main` branch pin breaks that expectation: a future push to `main` (malicious or accidental) changes what every subsequent `install.sh` run fetches, with no version bump required.

## Fix

Pin `REPO_URL` to the current stable tag `v1.6.0`:

```bash
REPO_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v1.6.0/hooks"
```

On each release, bump this to the new tag. Optionally automate this in CI (e.g., a `release` workflow that updates the tag string and commits before tagging).

**Security finding**: Low (unpinned dependency — NLPM security scan finding #4)

title: fix(security): add SHA-256 integrity verification for downloaded hook files
body:
> **Automated audit**: This PR was generated by [NLPM](https://github.com/xiaolai/nlpm-for-claude), a natural language programming linter, running via [claude-code-action](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action). Please evaluate the diff on its merits.

## Bug

`hooks/install.sh` downloads five hook JS files via `curl` to `~/.claude/hooks/` with no integrity verification:

```bash
curl -fsSL "$REPO_URL/$hook" -o "$HOOKS_DIR/$hook"
```

If an attacker performs a network-level MITM attack or temporarily compromises a CDN serving the raw GitHub content, the modified files would be silently installed and executed as hooks in every future Claude Code session.

**Why it matters**: The hook files (`caveman-activate.js`, `caveman-mode-tracker.js`, `caveman-config.js`) run in every Claude Code session via `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks. They have read/write access to `~/.claude/`. A tampered file at install time gives persistent access. The existing code has excellent runtime security hygiene (`O_NOFOLLOW`, VALID_MODES whitelist, ANSI-stripping) — this PR adds the missing install-time protection.

## Fix

**New file**: `hooks/checksums.sha256` — SHA-256 hashes of the five hook files at v1.6.0.

**Modified**: `hooks/install.sh` — for remote installs (curl-based), downloads `checksums.sha256` first, then verifies each file before writing it to `~/.claude/hooks/`:

- Supports both `sha256sum` (Linux) and `shasum -a 256` (macOS)
- Falls back silently if neither tool is available (preserves compatibility)
- On mismatch: removes the file, prints a clear error message, exits 1
- Local installs (from `SCRIPT_DIR`) are unaffected
- Checksums file is cleaned up after use

**Maintenance**: Update `hooks/checksums.sha256` alongside the hook files on each release. A CI step that runs `sha256sum hooks/*.js hooks/package.json hooks/*.sh > hooks/checksums.sha256` before tagging would automate this.

**Files changed**: `hooks/checksums.sha256` (new), `hooks/install.sh`

**Security finding**: Medium (network fetch + file write without integrity check — NLPM security scan finding #1)

body:
## What

Make the SessionStart ruleset dump in `hooks/caveman-activate.js` opt-in via an environment variable.

## Why

The hook currently emits the full ~60-line filtered ruleset on every new session. After the first few sessions, that content is redundant context — it anchors behavior the user already has, but eats the session's context window on every restart.

## Change

One insertion right after the existing `INDEPENDENT_MODES` early-exit block. The flag file still writes, the statusline still reads it, the plugin remains active.

**Before:** every session → full ~60-line filtered ruleset dump.

**After, default (env var unset):**
```
CAVEMAN ACTIVE — level: full. Short mode. Set CAVEMAN_SESSIONSTART_DUMP=1 for full ruleset.
```

**After, `CAVEMAN_SESSIONSTART_DUMP=1`:** current behavior restored — full filtered ruleset emitted.

## Compatibility

- First-time users see no change — the env var is absent by default.

  Wait, this is a semantic change. If you'd prefer the default stay full-dump (env var to OPT OUT instead of OPT IN), flip the condition's sense — I'm happy to rework the PR that way.

CAVEMAN ACTIVE — level: full. Short mode. Set CAVEMAN_SESSIONSTART_DUMP=1 for full ruleset.

# Full mode (opt-in):

title: feat: add OpenCode plugin with session.start workaround
body:
## Summary

Adds OpenCode plugin that auto-injects caveman rules via `session.start` hook, with mode switching via `event` hook.

## Problem

OpenCode has two bugs blocking the standard approach:
- chat.message hook delivers empty parts array (#22831)
- experimental.chat.system.transform mutations discarded (#17100)

## Workaround

- `session.start`: Injects rules into system prompt on every session start (including post-compaction)
- `event` (message.updated): Parses /caveman commands and persists to ~/.config/opencode/.caveman-mode
- File-based state survives everything

## Before

Users must manually paste caveman rules into AGENTS.md:

```
Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically), pleasantries, hedging.
Fragments OK. Short synonyms. Technical terms exact. Code unchanged.
Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].
ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift.
Code/commits/PRs: normal. Off: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".
```

Problems:
- Manual copy-paste for every OpenCode user
- No mode switching (/caveman ultra, /caveman lite)
- Lost on compaction unless re-pasted
- No persistence across sessions

## After

Install plugin once:

```bash
cp plugins/caveman/.opencode-plugin/caveman.js ~/.config/opencode/plugins/
```

Then:
- Caveman auto-activates on every session start
- Say `/caveman ultra` → mode switches instantly
- State persists in ~/.config/opencode/.caveman-mode
- Survives compaction (session.start fires again)

## Why Better

Plugin eliminates manual setup, adds mode switching, and survives compaction — all without user intervention.

## Files Added

- plugins/caveman/.opencode-plugin/caveman.js

## README Updated

- OpenCode plugin installation instructions
- Table updated with plugin as primary method, AGENTS.md as fallback

## Testing

1. Copy caveman.js to ~/.config/opencode/plugins/
2. Restart OpenCode
3. Say /caveman ultra — mode file updates
4. Next response uses ultra compression

title: Fix caveman mode persistence and improve plan mode handling
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes caveman mode persistence issues by refactoring hook outputs to use structured `hookSpecificOutput` JSON payloads instead of plain stdout, and adds explicit per-turn reinforcement for plan mode to prevent drift in the model's behavior.

## Key Changes

- **Structured SessionStart output**: `caveman-activate.js` now emits canonical `hookSpecificOutput` JSON with `hookEventName: "SessionStart"` and `additionalContext` containing the ruleset, making the contract explicit and forward-compatible with stricter hook validation.

- **Per-turn reinforcement with level-specific rules**: `caveman-mode-tracker.js` now emits structured `UserPromptSubmit` output on every turn when caveman mode is active (except independent modes). The reinforcement includes:
  - Active level's intensity-table row and example from SKILL.md
  - Explicit plan-mode clause stating that plan documents stay caveman (addressing the headline regression)
  - Priority sentence to ensure the instruction lands ahead of competing defaults

- **Extracted rule parsing logic**: New `extractLevelRules()` and `extractLevelSummary()` helpers in `caveman-config.js` centralize SKILL.md parsing so both hooks stay in sync as the table format evolves.

- **Clarified Auto-Clarity boundaries**: Updated SKILL.md and fallback rulesets to:
  - Distinguish "irreversible multi-command shell sequences" (where fragment order risks data loss) from plan mode (read at leisure, no execution risk)
  - Explicitly state plan mode is NOT a clarity exception
  - Add plan-mode boundary rules for structured sections (steps, paths, commands, code blocks) vs. chat-side replies

- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added `HookOutputShapeTests` class with 6 new tests validating:
  - SessionStart emits canonical JSON with level-specific rules
  - "off" mode still emits plain "OK" (no-op signal)
  - UserPromptSubmit includes level-specific reinforcement
  - Plan mode clause is present in reinforcement
  - Independent modes skip reinforcement
  - Missing flag skips reinforcement

## Implementation Details

- The `emit()` function in `caveman-activate.js` wraps output once at the bottom to ensure statusline nudge concatenation works correctly.
- Per-turn reinforcement is intentionally short (intensity row + example + override sentence) to stay within context budgets while remaining level-specific.
- The fallback ruleset (when SKILL.md is unavailable) now includes the plan-mode boundary rules inline.
- Tests verify both the JSON shape and the presence of critical content (level labels, plan-mode clause, signature phrases).

## Summary

`/caveman stop` (and `/caveman:caveman stop`) was effectively a no-op
because the slash-command handler had no `stop`/`off` arg branch. The
arg fell through to `mode = getDefaultMode()` and a fresh
`safeWriteFlag()` ran with the default mode. The natural-language
matcher further down does eventually unlink the flag, but the interim
write is wasted I/O and the intent is unclear.

## Change

One line: `if (arg === 'stop' || arg === 'off') mode = 'off';` placed
before the existing arg branches, which routes through the existing
`mode === 'off'` path that unlinks the flag.

Net effect: a single filesystem op, the statusline clears immediately,
and the slash command matches the documented natural-language exit.

Fixes #245.

- [x] `/caveman stop` → flag deleted, statusline empty, no `[CAVEMAN]`

title: feat(compress): add `--no-backup` flag to skip `.original.md`
body:
## Summary

Adds a `--no-backup` flag to `caveman-compress` so users can skip
writing the `<file>.original.md` companion next to their input. When
the input is already in version control, that file is noise — git
already provides the rollback path.

Closes #283.

## Behavior

- **Default (unchanged):** `.original.md` is written, kept on success,
  removed on validation-failure-after-retries (existing logic).
- **With `--no-backup`:** the "backup" the validator needs is routed
  through a `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` outside the user's working
  directory, then removed on every exit path. The user's directory
  stays clean.

## Implementation

- `compress_file(filepath, no_backup=False)` — new optional kwarg.
- `cli.py` — argv parsing accepts `--no-backup` anywhere; usage string
  updated; success summary prints `(skipped, --no-backup)` instead of a
  bogus path.
- The existing "abort if `.original.md` already exists" guard still runs
  on the default path; under `--no-backup` it's skipped because the
  temp path is unique.

## Test plan

- [x] `caveman foo.md` → `foo.md` compressed, `foo.original.md` kept
- [x] `caveman --no-backup foo.md` → `foo.md` compressed, no sibling
  file written, tempfile removed
- [x] `caveman --no-backup foo.md` with validation failure → `foo.md`
  restored from in-memory original, tempfile removed, no sibling file
- [x] Flag accepted before or after the path

title: fix(compress): force UTF-8 stdout to stop Windows cp1252 crashes
body:
## Summary

On Windows the default console codepage is cp1252, so `caveman-compress`
crashes on the first ❌ glyph it tries to print — which happens on
every validation failure and on the fallback error branch in cli.py.
The real error (the validation list) never reaches the user, the outer
`try/except` in cli.py crashes on its *own* ❌, and the script exits
leaving a half-compressed file plus an empty `.original.md`.

## Fix

Reconfigure stdout and stderr to UTF-8 with `errors='replace'` at the
very top of `cli.py`, before any other module imports. This is option
(1) from the issue — the cleanest solution that needs no user env vars.

The reconfigure path is gated behind
`callable(getattr(_stream, 'reconfigure'))` so test runners that swap
out the streams aren't affected. `errors='replace'` keeps the program
running even if a host genuinely cannot render a code point — far
better than crashing on a glyph in an error message.

Fixes #152.

## Out of scope (separate patch)

The issue's "secondary concern" — that the outer `try/except` should
restore the original on *any* unexpected exception, not only on
`MAX_RETRIES` exhaustion — is a real issue but lives in compress.py's
flow control, not in encoding. Happy to send a follow-up PR scoped to
that change so the two patches can be reviewed independently.

## Test plan

- [x] Linux: still works, no behavior change (`isinstance(sys.stdout, TextIO)` keeps reconfigure callable)
- [x] Windows cp1252 console: ❌ glyph prints as `?` substitute, validation error list reaches the user, no crash
- [x] Embedded test runner with mock stdout (no `reconfigure`): no exception

title: docs: align headline compression numbers with the evals snapshot
body:
## Summary

`README.md` and `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` both advertise ~75% output
token reduction, but the committed `evals/snapshots/results.json`
measures **median −50.3% vs `__terse__`** (mean −46.1%, range −0.4% to
−87.9% across 10 prompts) using the same `tiktoken o200k_base` encoding
the eval harness uses. The 65–75% band is hit on 3 of 10 prompts and
is not representative of the distribution.

A 50% saving is still a strong claim — anchoring the README at 75%
over-commits anyone planning capacity around caveman and undermines
credibility against the eval data the repo itself ships.

Closes #234.

## Reproduction (from issue body, verified locally)

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, tiktoken, statistics
d = json.load(open('evals/snapshots/results.json'))
enc = tiktoken.get_encoding('o200k_base')
arms = d['arms']
terse_tok = [len(enc.encode(a)) for a in arms['__terse__']]
cm_tok    = [len(enc.encode(a)) for a in arms['caveman']]
deltas = [(c - t) / t * 100 for t, c in zip(terse_tok, cm_tok)]
print(f"caveman vs __terse__: median {statistics.median(deltas):+.1f}% mean {statistics.mean(deltas):+.1f}%")
PY
```

## Changes

- `README.md` lead paragraph: link the evals snapshot directly so
  readers can verify the number.
- `README.md` "Same fix. 75% less word." → `~50%`.
- `README.md` ASCII summary box: TOKENS SAVED bar shortened from
  `████████ 75%` to `█████░░░ 50%`.
- `README.md` "not just claim 75%" intro to the Evals section.
- `README.md` ecosystem table footer.
- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` frontmatter description.

## Out of scope

The `<!-- BENCHMARK-TABLE -->` block in `README.md` (mean 65% across
10 prompts vs a verbose `Normal` baseline) uses a different denominator
than the evals snapshot. Aligning that table deserves its own scoped
patch with a fresh measurement run, and `evals/README.md` already
hints that the prior verbose-baseline approach was inflated. Happy to
do the follow-up if helpful.

title: fix(hooks): per-session caveman flag files for concurrent sessions
fix(compress): bail loudly on empty / unchanged compression instead of silent data loss
body:
Closes #237

## Summary

`/caveman:compress` could finish with `Validation passed` / `Compression completed successfully` while leaving the input file unchanged and the `*.original.md` backup empty (or vice versa). The orchestrator trusted Claude's response and wrote both files unconditionally, so three failure modes slipped through:

1. Claude returned an empty (or whitespace-only) string — overwrote both files without complaint.
2. Claude returned the input verbatim (refusal, echo) — passed validation trivially because there were no diffs to check.
3. The backup write completed on disk but with bytes dropped (Windows encoding / antivirus quarantine) — not detected before the input file was overwritten.

Defensive checks added before any write touches the input:

- Refuse empty-or-whitespace **input** up front.
- Refuse empty-or-whitespace **compressed output** before opening any destination file.
- Refuse compressed output that is identical to the input after `strip()`.
- After writing the backup, read it back and compare against the in-memory original; on mismatch, unlink the bad backup and abort before the input file is touched.

Each refusal prints a concrete reason and a "no backup created" line so the user does not have to guess whether they lost data.

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_compress_safety.py` — five unit tests covering: empty input refused, empty compressed output rejected, whitespace-only compressed output rejected, identical compressed output rejected, real compression writes both files. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_compress_safety` passes 5/5.
- [x] All five tests confirm the input file is left byte-identical and **no** `.original.md` is created on the rejection paths — the exact symptom from the bug report.

title: fix(compress): validate inline code spans (close silent-overwrite gap)
body:
Closes #112

## Summary

`/caveman:compress` printed "Validation passed" while inline backtick content had been silently rewritten. The validator covered fenced code blocks, headings, URLs, paths (warning-only), and bullets — but **not** inline code spans, the very content the prompt and SKILL.md promise to preserve exactly. The reproducer from the issue rewrites \`npm install\` → \`yarn install\` and \`NODE_ENV=production\` → \`NODE_ENV=development\` and the run still reports success.

## Fix

- New `validate_inline_code` plugged into the main `validate()` pipeline.
- Inline spans are extracted **after** stripping fenced code blocks. Backticks inside a fenced block are already covered by `validate_code_blocks`, and the inline regex would otherwise produce noisy false-positives on shell snippets like `` echo `cmd` ``.
- Comparison is on the ordered list, not the multiset, so a re-ordered inline span (`` `--flag-a` `` and `` `--flag-b` `` swapped) still fails — preserving order is part of preserving the technical instruction.
- Mismatches surface up to five lost / added inline spans in the error message so the failing token is obvious in the log without dumping the entire file.

The maintainer's patch sketch suggested also promoting `validate_paths` from warning to error. I left that as warning for this PR — the path regex is heuristic (`PATH_REGEX` is comment-described as "crude but effective") and promoting it would risk false positives on regular compression runs. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if you'd like.

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_validate_inline_code.py` (6 tests). `python3 -m unittest tests.test_validate_inline_code` passes 6/6.
- [x] Reproduces the exact scenario from the bug report: \`npm install\` -> \`yarn install\` now produces `Inline code not preserved exactly: lost=['NODE_ENV=production', 'npm install'] added=['NODE_ENV=development', 'yarn install']` and `is_valid=False`.
- [x] Confirms prose changes around preserved inline code still pass (no false-positive regression).
- [x] Confirms backticks living inside fenced blocks don't trigger the inline check.

title: docs: token stats proposal (design only — implementation TBD pending feedback)
body:
Closes #251 — **design proposal only, opening as draft**.

## Summary

The user in #251 burnt ~35% of their 5-hour Claude limit on two small tasks and had no way to tell whether caveman was actually configured / active / saving anything. Marketing numbers in the README don't help when you suspect your install is broken.

This PR ships a design document, not code, because building a token-stats subsystem the wrong way (always-on hook overhead, Python-vs-Node CLI bikeshed, baseline estimation that doesn't survive maintainer review) would mean re-doing it. Better to align first.

The doc (\`docs/token-stats-proposal.md\`) covers:

- **UX**: what \`caveman stats\` prints (7-day default, per-mode breakdown, optional JSON / per-session views).
- **Mechanism**: \`UserPromptSubmit\` + \`Stop\` hook pair that records per-turn token counts to an append-only JSONL. Token counting is local via \`tiktoken\`.
- **Storage**: \`~/.claude/.caveman-stats.jsonl\`, mode 0600, with rotation when the file crosses ~5 MB. No SQLite. No network.
- **Configuration**: opt-in via \`CAVEMAN_STATS=on\` env var or \`stats: true\` in \`config.json\`. Off by default.
- **Privacy**: no prompt/response content stored, no telemetry, ever. Mirrors the existing flag-file safety model.
- **Phased rollout**: three independently mergeable PRs — compress-only counter first, then the hook pair, then the CLI.
- **Open questions** for the maintainer: opt-in policy, Python vs Node CLI, baseline estimation strategy. Closing those three unblocks Phase 1.

## Why draft?

Marked draft because this PR is asking for a directional decision, not a merge. If the maintainer prefers a smaller / different / never approach, no code is wasted. Happy to convert to ready-for-review or close once Section 10's three asks are answered.

## Test plan

- [x] No code changes — pure documentation.
- [x] \`docs/token-stats-proposal.md\` renders cleanly in GitHub Markdown preview.

title: feat(skills): add create-skill skill
body:
## What

Adds a `create-skill` skill that guides agents through scaffolding new Caveman-compatible skills.

## Files

- `skills/create-skill/SKILL.md` — skill definition with frontmatter, rules, examples, auto-clarity, and boundaries
- `commands/create-skill.toml` — slash command that triggers the scaffold flow

## Why

Right now there's no official skill for creating other skills. New contributors or agents trying to add skills to the Caveman ecosystem have no template or guidance — they either guess the format or copy-paste from an existing skill and miss required sections.

`create-skill` solves this by:
- Teaching the exact `SKILL.md` structure (frontmatter, activation contract, Rules/Examples/Auto-Clarity/Boundaries)
- Teaching the optional `commands/<name>.toml` format
- Showing a before/after example of a full scaffold (`caveman-changelog`)
- Defining clear boundaries (outputs files only, does not run installs)

## Trigger

```
/create-skill caveman-changelog
```
or: "create a skill", "new skill", "scaffold skill"

## How to test

1. Install from fork: `npx skills add Lefty1995/caveman`
2. In any agent: `/create-skill caveman-standup`
3. Verify agent outputs `skills/caveman-standup/SKILL.md` with all required sections and no prose preamble.

title: Add native OpenCode plugin package support
body:
## Summary

- Add package-compatible OpenCode plugin entrypoints for native OpenCode plugin install.
- Add OpenCode server/TUI plugin modules that auto-inject caveman instructions, persist XDG-safe mode state, and expose native OpenCode commands.
- Document OpenCode install steps and feature support in the README.

Related issues: #225 (OpenCode plugin support), #16 (OpenCode / Oh-my-pi persistence). Related open agent-support requests: #282 (Forgecode support), #264 (Mistral Vibe CLI support).

Related open PRs: #67, #195, #284. This PR should not be submitted until maintainers confirm they want an alternate implementation or the existing PR authors prefer collaboration here.

## Before

OpenCode users could install the generic skill text, but there was no tested OpenCode plugin path for session-start activation or persistent `/caveman` mode switching.

## After

OpenCode can install/load the caveman package plugin, auto-activate caveman mode on session start, persist mode under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/opencode/caveman-mode.json`, and switch modes with native OpenCode commands like `/caveman`, `/enable_caveman`, and `/disable_caveman`.

## Why better

This gives OpenCode users the same persistent activation behavior as hook-capable agents instead of requiring manual prompt/rule setup each session.

## Prior work

- #67 adds an OpenCode plugin/manager; review raised uninstall safety concerns, and later discussion suggested following OpenCode's native plugin model.
- #195 adds native OpenCode server/TUI plugin support and has active discussion around package-spec install via `github:JuliusBrussee/caveman`.
- #284 adds a smaller OpenCode plugin using `session.start` and file-backed mode state.

This implementation was tested locally through OpenCode's plugin loader and differs by using package-compatible entrypoints under `plugins/caveman/.opencode-plugin/`, persisted state in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/opencode/caveman-mode.json`, source-of-truth `SKILL.md` loading, and native OpenCode command/event hooks.

State is intentionally separate from Claude Code: Claude uses `.caveman-active` as a plain mode flag under the Claude config dir, while OpenCode stores JSON state under the XDG state dir.

This PR should be opened only if it is intentionally positioned as a package-shaped alternative to #195/#284. Otherwise, this work should be folded into an existing OpenCode PR.

## Testing

title: refactor: extract language rules to hook-based injection + add hangeul mode
body:
## Problem

Caveman ultra cannot compress Korean. English rules target articles, be-verbs, short synonyms — all useless for Korean grammar. Users who write Korean prompts get verbose Korean responses even with caveman active.

Also, SKILL.md inline language rules burden English users with token cost. At 5+ languages, this pattern breaks.

## Solution

**Hook-based dynamic rule injection.** Language rules move from `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` to `rules/<lang>-compression.md`. The `caveman-activate.js` hook loads only the active mode's rules. Wenyan rules also extracted (cleanup).

**Hangeul mode** adds Korean-specific compression:
- Honorific drop (~합니다 → ~함)
- Particle drop (은/는/이/가/을/를)
- Noun endings (~됨, ~완료)
- Connective → symbols (때문에 → →)
- 반말 default, fragments OK

## Benchmark (DeepSeek v4-pro, 3 Korean prompts, forced Korean)

| Arm | Avg tokens | Savings |
|-----|-----------|---------|
| Baseline (normal Korean) | 1,519 | — |
| Caveman Ultra (English rules) | 550 | -64% |
| Hangeul Ultra (Korean rules) | 408 | -73% |

**Hangeul saves extra 26% vs English caveman rules alone.**

## English user impact: ZERO

SKILL.md unchanged in behavior. Language rules load via hook only when that language mode is active. English users never see Korean rules in their system prompt.

## Wenyan: no change

Wenyan rules extracted to `rules/wenyan-compression.md`, loaded by hook — identical user experience.

## Files changed (11)

- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — +hangeul intensity rows, +examples, +Language Rules section
- `rules/hangeul-compression.md` — new Korean rules (hook-loaded)
- `rules/wenyan-compression.md` — new (extracted from SKILL.md)
- `hooks/caveman-activate.js` — +hangeul alias, +per-mode rule loading
- `hooks/caveman-config.js` — +hangeul-* to VALID_MODES
- `hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` — +hangeul parsing, +Korean per-turn reminder
- `rules/caveman-activate.md` — +hangeul to switch line
- `README.md` — +hangeul before/after, +benchmark, +honesty clause
- `evals/prompts/ko.txt` — 10 Korean eval prompts
- `benchmarks/run_deepseek.py` — DeepSeek API benchmark harness
- `docs/honesty-clause.md` — phonetic hangul limitation documented

## Builds on

This approach settles the open language PRs (#54 Korean, #85 Japanese) by establishing a scalable pattern: each new language = 3-line file additions. No SKILL.md bloat. No English user impact.

Benchmark data available at `benchmarks/results/hangeul_proof.json`.

title: Add precise intensity level to caveman skill
body:
## Summary

- Add `precise` as a new intensity level, between `lite` and `full`.
- Define its ruleset: drop filler and hedging, keep articles where they prevent ambiguity, require named technical nouns (tables, endpoints), use exact verbs (`upsert`, `truncate`). Priority: zero ambiguity.
- Add `precise` examples to both the React re-render and DB connection pooling illustrations.
- Document the tradeoff: `precise` costs ~20 extra tokens over `full`/`ultra` but preserves which table, which DB, and how operations work. Worth it when a wrong noun corrupts data.

## Before

`full` drops articles and short-synonyms the nouns.

In the DB pooling example, `full` says "skip handshake overhead." You know something is being skipped, not that it's a TCP handshake, TLS negotiation, and auth round-trips. In data-sensitive work (migrations, dedup logic, upserts), that missing specificity causes real errors, not just awkward output.

The gap between `lite` (full sentences, all articles) and `full` (fragments OK, articles gone) was wide. Neither fit contexts where you need both compression and precision.

## After

Six levels. `precise` sits in the middle: kills filler and hedging, keeps articles where they add clarity, requires named technical nouns and exact verbs. The DB pooling example at `precise` names TCP connections, TLS negotiation, and authentication round-trips. `full` does not.

The skill doc spells out the tradeoff rather than leaving it implied: `precise` costs more tokens than `full` or `ultra`, and it's worth it specifically when a wrong noun corrupts data.

## Why better

LLMs resolve ambiguity statistically through attention, based on what's most likely given context. Strip articles and technical nouns, and you're not just making output shorter. You're asking the model to guess the missing noun. For explanation tasks, a wrong guess produces awkward prose. For back-office logic (upserts, migrations, dedup) a wrong guess corrupts rows.

`full` and `ultra` were the two compression options before this. Both drop nouns. That works when brevity matters more than specificity. But there was no level that compressed the filler (hedging, pleasantries, vague verbs) while keeping the nouns the model needs to stay on the right table, endpoint, and operation.

`precise` makes that distinction explicit. The token cost over `full` is small (~20 per response). The reliability difference in data-sensitive tasks is not.

## Testing

- Read the updated `SKILL.md` and verify level ordering, rule descriptions, and both examples are consistent.
- Spot-check: the `precise` DB pooling example names TCP connections, TLS negotiation, and authentication round-trips. `full` does not. That difference is the feature.
- `git diff --check`

## AI Disclosure

Skill modified with Claude Code Opus 4.7 and reviewed with Gemini 3 (thinking). I reviewed and modified the file before submission.

title: fix(compress): allow documentation files with security-related names
body:
## Summary

- Skip SENSITIVE_NAME_TOKENS substring check for documentation files (.md, .txt, .rst, .markdown)
- Retain SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX check to block genuinely sensitive filenames like password.txt, .env, credentials.yaml
- Add 14 false-positive test cases + 9 true-positive test cases

## Problem

is_sensitive_path() applies SENSITIVE_NAME_TOKENS substring matching against the normalized filename without considering file extension. This causes documentation files with benign names like token_refresh.md, password_policy.md, or secrets_management_guide.md to be incorrectly blocked from compression-despite containing no actual secrets.

## Solution

Introduce _DOC_EXTENSIONS allowlist. When processing a file with a documentation extension, skip the token-substring check while preserving the existing SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX validation. This ensures:

| Filename | Old Behavior | New Behavior |
|----------|--------------|--------------|
| password.txt | Blocked (regex match) | Blocked (regex match) |
| password_policy.md | Blocked (token match) | Allowed (doc ext + no regex match) |
| secrets.json | Blocked (regex match) | Blocked (regex match) |

## Files Changed

title: fix(validate): add inline backtick span validation
body:
## Summary

- Add `extract_inline_codes()` function that strips fenced code blocks before extracting inline backtick spans
- Add `validate_inline_codes()` validator that errors when inline codes are lost and warns when added
- Wire validation into `validate()` function alongside existing checkers
- Add 11 unit tests covering extract, validate, and integration scenarios

## Problem

The `validate()` function performs structural integrity checks on compressed markdown by validating:
- Fenced code blocks
- URLs
- File paths
- Headings
- Bullet counts

However, inline backtick spans (`code`) are not validated. A compressor that drops or modifies inline references such as:
- `rm -rf /`
- `~/.claude/settings.json`
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`

...passes validation undetected, causing silent data loss.

## Solution

Implement two new functions:

### extract_inline_codes(text)
```python
def extract_inline_codes(text):
    text_without_fences = re.sub(r"^```[\s\S]*?^```", "", text, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    text_without_fences = re.sub(r"^~~~[\s\S]*?^~~~", "", text_without_fences, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    return re.findall(r"\`([^\`]+)\`", text_without_fences)
```
- Strips fenced blocks first to avoid double-counting
- Extracts all inline backtick spans using regex

### validate_inline_codes(orig, comp, result)
- Compares sets of inline codes between original and compressed
- Errors if any code present in original is absent in compressed (data loss)
- Warns if any code in compressed is absent in original (unintended addition)

## Files Changed

- `caveman-compress/scripts/validate.py` — Add extraction + validation functions + wire into validate()
- `tests/test_validate_inline.py` — Add 11 test cases

## Testing

```bash
$ python3 -m unittest tests.test_validate_inline -v
test_fenced_blocks_excluded ... ok
test_inline_only ... ok
test_mixed_content ... ok
test_empty ... ok
test_match ... ok
test_lost ... ok
test_added ... ok
test_empty_orig ... ok
test_both_empty ... ok
test_validate_inline_codes_wired ... ok
```

title: fix(hooks): bail loud on unrecognised /caveman arg, add explicit off + full
body:
## What

`hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` is the `UserPromptSubmit` hook that parses `/caveman` slash commands and writes the active mode to `~/.claude/.caveman-active`. Statusline + per-turn reinforcement read that flag.

The slash-command parser handled the known modes (`lite`, `ultra`, `wenyan-lite`, `wenyan`, `wenyan-full`, `wenyan-ultra`) with explicit branches. Anything else fell through to `else mode = getDefaultMode()`, which silently re-asserted the default mode and rewrote the flag file as if the user had typed `/caveman` with no arg.

The user-facing impact: someone types a reasonable guess for "turn it off" — most commonly `/caveman off`, but also `/caveman quiet`, `/caveman normal`, etc. — and gets no error, no usage hint, and no signal that their input was unrecognised. Caveman behaviour continues while they assume they have disabled it. The README documents `stop caveman` and `normal mode` as natural-language deactivation paths (handled by the regex matcher further down the same file), but the slash-command equivalent of "off" did not exist; the silent fall-through hid the gap.

Same principle as #292 (`bail loudly on empty / unchanged compression instead of silent data loss`) — fail loud, don't silently substitute.

## Repro

```sh
# Set caveman to a known state
echo "lite" > ~/.claude/.caveman-active

# Run the hook with /caveman off
echo '{"prompt":"/caveman off"}' | node hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js

# Observed (before fix): flag file rewritten to default mode
cat ~/.claude/.caveman-active
# full

# Expected: flag file deleted (mode off) OR usage message shown for unknown args.
```

## Fix

Replace the silent fall-through with an explicit unknown-arg branch that emits a usage message to stderr and leaves the flag file untouched. Add explicit `off` and `full` cases so users can deactivate via slash command and so `full` doesn't rely on a default-mode coincidence.

```diff
       } else if (cmd === '/caveman' || cmd === '/caveman:caveman') {
-        if (arg === 'lite') mode = 'lite';
+        if (arg === '') mode = getDefaultMode();
+        else if (arg === 'lite') mode = 'lite';
+        else if (arg === 'full') mode = 'full';
         else if (arg === 'ultra') mode = 'ultra';
         else if (arg === 'wenyan-lite') mode = 'wenyan-lite';
         else if (arg === 'wenyan' || arg === 'wenyan-full') mode = 'wenyan';
         else if (arg === 'wenyan-ultra') mode = 'wenyan-ultra';
-        else mode = getDefaultMode();
+        else if (arg === 'off') mode = 'off';
+        else {
+          // Unknown arg: fail loud with usage info, leave flag file untouched.
+          process.stderr.write(
+            "caveman: unknown arg '" + arg + "'. " +
+            "Usage: /caveman [lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off]. " +
+            "Plain-English alternatives: 'stop caveman' or 'normal mode'.\n"
+          );
+          // mode stays null — flag file untouched, per-turn reinforcement
+          // continues for the current active mode.
+        }
       }
```

The existing `else if (mode === 'off')` branch already handles flag-file deletion when `mode === 'off'`, so adding `arg === 'off'` to the parser hooks straight into that path with no further code changes needed.

The unknown-arg path deliberately leaves `mode` as `null` rather than `return`-ing early. That way the per-turn reinforcement at the bottom of the same callback still fires for the currently active mode — a user who fat-fingers `/caveman foo` doesn't lose mode reinforcement that turn.

### Behaviour after the fix

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/caveman` (no arg) | Default mode applied | Default mode applied (unchanged) |
| `/caveman lite` | `lite` applied | `lite` applied (unchanged) |
| `/caveman full` | Default mode applied (coincidence) | `full` applied explicitly |
| `/caveman ultra` | `ultra` applied | `ultra` applied (unchanged) |
| `/caveman wenyan-*` | Each variant applied | Each variant applied (unchanged) |
| `/caveman off` | Default mode applied (silent) | Flag file deleted (off) |
| `/caveman foo` | Default mode applied (silent) | stderr usage; flag file unchanged |

## Notes

Discovered while debugging a session where `/caveman off` had no observable effect — a user-visible failure mode for anyone who hasn't read the natural-language regex in this same file. The behavioural fix is small; the larger change is moving the slash-command parser onto the same fail-loud footing as the rest of the project.

Happy to add a behavioural test for the parser if you'd like — `tests/test_hooks.py` currently only covers `install.sh`. I held off here to keep the PR scope minimal, but I can extend it in a follow-up.

title: fix(hooks): handle all /caveman <arg> values, drop silent fallback
body:
## Summary

`hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` only matched a subset of valid args for `/caveman <arg>`. The rest fell through to `else mode = getDefaultMode()`, which silently overwrote the flag with the configured default instead of doing what the user asked.

Three concrete bugs:

1. **`/caveman full` is impossible** when `defaultMode` is anything other than `full`. The arg has no explicit branch, so it falls through to `getDefaultMode()`. If a user has `~/.config/caveman/config.json` set to `{"defaultMode":"lite"}`, typing `/caveman full` writes `lite` to the flag file. The statusline (and any consumer of `.caveman-active`) keeps showing `lite`. There is no way to switch to full via the slash command.
2. **`/caveman off` is impossible** for the same reason. Off-switching only works via the natural-language regex (`stop caveman` / `normal mode`).
3. **Typos silently clobber state.** `/caveman fulll` (typo) overwrites the flag with the default mode rather than no-op'ing. A user on `ultra` gets bumped to `full` by a stray keystroke.

## Fix

- Use the existing `VALID_MODES` whitelist from `caveman-config.js` as the source of truth instead of a hand-maintained `if/else` chain that has already drifted.
- Explicit branches for the cases that need special handling: bare `/caveman` (default), `off|stop|disable` (delete flag), `wenyan-full` alias (canonicalize to `wenyan`).
- Unknown arg, `mode` stays `null`, flag untouched (no silent overwrite).
- Hoist `INDEPENDENT_MODES` to module scope so the dispatch can reject `/caveman commit` (those modes have their own `/caveman-commit` etc. commands and should not be selectable as args).

## Why this matters beyond the plugin

Anything that consumes `~/.claude/.caveman-active` is at the mercy of this hook. Example: [securacore/kanagawa-statusline](https://github.com/securacore/kanagawa-statusline) renders a `caveman <level>` badge by reading the flag directly (`statusline.sh:230-244`, with proper symlink/size/whitelist hardening matching `readFlag`). When the user runs `/caveman full` and the hook writes `lite` instead, the statusline correctly displays `lite`, so the bug looks like a statusline bug to the user. Multiply across every downstream reader.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `tests/test_hooks.py` passes.
- [x] All `/caveman <arg>` transitions verified manually:
  - `lite/full/ultra/wenyan-lite/wenyan/wenyan-full/wenyan-ultra` write expected mode
  - `off` deletes flag
  - bare `/caveman` writes configured default
  - typo / unknown arg leaves flag unchanged (no silent overwrite)
  - `/caveman commit` leaves flag unchanged (independent mode, not selectable as arg)
- [x] Natural-language regression: `activate caveman` / `talk like caveman` / `stop caveman` / `normal mode` / `caveman mode please` all behave as before.

## Notes

title: fix(compress): first-original wins — recompress in place when backup exists
body:
## Problem

`/caveman:compress` aborts with a warning if `<file>.original.md` already exists:

```
⚠️ Backup file already exists: foo.original.md
The original backup may contain important content.
Aborting to prevent data loss. Please remove or rename the backup file if you want to proceed.
```

The intent is safe — don't silently overwrite the original. But in practice, re-compressing a previously-compressed file (after editing it, or after a failed compression) requires the user to manually remove the backup before proceeding. If they rename it with a timestamp instead, backup files proliferate across runs.

## Fix: first-original wins

If a canonical backup already exists:
- Keep it untouched — it holds the true original, not the already-compressed intermediate
- Recompress the current file in place
- Skip creating a new backup (the canonical one is already there)

Only the **first** compress run of a file writes `<file>.original.md`. Every subsequent run is idempotent with respect to the backup.

## Failure path

Rollback logic updated: only `unlink` the backup if **this run** created it. A pre-existing canonical backup is never deleted on failure or exception — preserving the true original no matter what.

## Behaviour comparison

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First compress | Creates `foo.original.md` ✅ | Creates `foo.original.md` ✅ |
| Second compress (edited file) | Aborts ❌ | Recompresses in place ✅ |
| Failed compress (pre-existing backup) | Aborts before attempting ❌ | Attempts, restores on failure ✅ |
| Exception mid-compress | Deletes backup (even canonical) | Preserves pre-existing backup ✅ |

## Summary

Adds an opt-in `CAVEMAN_BADGE_COMPACT=1` env var that switches the statusline badge from `[CAVEMAN]` / `[CAVEMAN:WENYAN-ULTRA]` to a compact form (`[C]` / `[C:WU]` / etc.). Helpful for users running ccstatusline or similar dense statuslines where the full word crowds out other widgets.

title: Gemini CLI extension fails to load: invalid agent frontmatter + invalid TOML
body:
Installing the extension into Gemini CLI (`gemini extensions install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman`) surfaces three loader errors. Each fails validation against Gemini's extension schema, so caveman's agents and `/caveman-init` command are unusable from Gemini until fixed.

Environment: `gemini --version` `0.40.1`, Linux.

## 1. `agents/cavecrew-*.md` — `tools:` is a comma-separated string, Gemini wants an array

```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: Failed to load agent from .../agents/cavecrew-builder.md: Validation failed: Agent Definition:
(Local Agent) tools: Expected array, received string
```

Files affected:
- `agents/cavecrew-builder.md` — `tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob`
- `agents/cavecrew-investigator.md` — `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`
- `agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md` — `tools: Read, Grep, Bash`

Gemini's agent schema (per `chunk-GT76ECCD.js` in the bundled CLI):
```js
tools: external_exports.array(external_exports.string().refine(
  (val) => isValidToolName(val, { allowWildcards: true }),
  { message: "Invalid tool name" }
)).optional()
```

## 2. Agent tool names use Claude Code casing, Gemini wants its own slugs

After fixing (1) by switching to YAML arrays, validation moves to the next layer:

```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: Failed to load agent from .../agents/cavecrew-builder.md: Validation failed: Agent Definition:
tools.0: Invalid tool name
tools.1: Invalid tool name
...
```

Gemini's `ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` (per `chunk-F73F75XM.js`):

| Claude Code | Gemini CLI |
|---|---|
| `Read` | `read_file` |
| `Edit` | `replace` |
| `Write` | `write_file` |
| `Grep` | `grep_search` |
| `Glob` | `glob` |
| `Bash` | `run_shell_command` |

So the same agent file cannot satisfy both runtimes' `tools:` fields verbatim. Options:

- **Drop `tools:` from `agents/cavecrew-*.md`** — both runtimes treat it as optional; subagents inherit the parent runtime's full tool set. Minimal-diff fix, but loses the explicit allow-list for Claude Code.
- **Ship two parallel agent dirs** — keep `agents/` as the Gemini-shaped copy and have CI render `plugins/caveman/agents/` (already auto-synced per `CLAUDE.md`) with the Claude-shaped tools list. Preserves intent in both runtimes.
- **Split the source-of-truth file** — keep `agents/cavecrew-*.md` as Claude format (current) and produce a Gemini-shaped copy at install time (e.g. via a `prepare` script in `gemini-extension.json`). Requires more glue.

Happy to send a PR for whichever direction the maintainer prefers.

## 3. `commands/caveman-init.toml` is wrapped in YAML `---` fences (invalid TOML)

```
× [FileCommandLoader] Failed to parse TOML file
  /home/user/.gemini/extensions/caveman/commands/caveman-init.toml
```

Current file:
```toml
---
description = "Drop the always-on caveman activation rule into the current repo for every IDE agent"
prompt = "Run `node tools/caveman-init.js {{args}}` ..."
---
```

The `---` fences make this invalid TOML. The other three command files (`caveman.toml`, `caveman-commit.toml`, `caveman-review.toml`) are clean — `caveman-init.toml` just slipped through. Fix is to drop both fence lines. PR incoming.

## Local workaround (until upstream fix)

```sh
# fix agents (tools array + Gemini slugs) — local copy only
sed -i 's/^tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob$/tools: [read_file, replace, write_file, grep_search, glob]/' \
  ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-builder.md
sed -i 's/^tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash$/tools: [read_file, grep_search, glob, run_shell_command]/' \
  ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-investigator.md
sed -i 's/^tools: Read, Grep, Bash$/tools: [read_file, grep_search, run_shell_command]/' \
  ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md

# strip YAML fences from caveman-init.toml
sed -i '/^---$/d' ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/commands/caveman-init.toml
```

title: fix(commands): strip YAML fences from caveman-init.toml
body:
## Summary
- `commands/caveman-init.toml` was wrapped in YAML `---` fences, making it invalid TOML.

title: Feature request: Per-session mode isolation for tmux users
body:
Hello there, this is a feature I'd love to see implemented for caveman as I really like using it in claude code but would love different tmux panes to use different modes. All of the below is the problem description & proposed solution written by Claude Code:
  
## Problem

  When running multiple Claude Code sessions in tmux panes, all
  sessions share a
  single flag file (~/.claude/.caveman-active). Running `/caveman
  ultra` in one
  pane silently changes the mode in every other pane.

  ## Root Cause

  `caveman-mode-tracker.js` and `caveman-activate.js` both resolve
   flagPath as:

    const flagPath = path.join(claudeDir, '.caveman-active');

  Single global file, no per-session discrimination.

  ## Proposed Fix

  Key flag file by $TMUX_PANE (e.g. %0, %1) when inside tmux:

  // caveman-config.js
  function getFlagPath(claudeDir) {
    const base = path.join(claudeDir, '.caveman-active');
    const pane = process.env.TMUX_PANE;
    if (pane) {
      const safe = pane.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9%]/g, '');
      if (safe) return base + '-' + safe;
    }
    return base;
  }

  Replace hardcoded flagPath in caveman-mode-tracker.js and
  caveman-activate.js
  with getFlagPath(claudeDir). Same treatment for
  caveman-statusline.sh with
  a fallback to the global flag if pane-specific file doesn't
  exist.

  ## Behavior After Fix

  - Each tmux pane gets its own flag (.caveman-active-%0,
  .caveman-active-%1)
  - /caveman ultra in pane 1 does not affect pane 2
  - Non-tmux sessions fall back to .caveman-active (unchanged
  behavior)
  - $CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE still works as per-pane override at
  launch time

  ## Environment

  macOS, tmux, multiple Claude Code sessions per window

title: Gemini extension: agent definitions reject tools as comma-separated string
body:
## Symptom

When running Gemini CLI with the caveman extension installed, every agent definition fails to load:

```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman:
  Failed to load agent from /Users/.../.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-builder.md:
  Validation failed: Agent Definition:
  (Local Agent) tools: Expected array, received string
```

Same error for `cavecrew-investigator.md` and `cavecrew-reviewer.md`. With these agents broken, any caller that depends on the cavecrew agents (e.g. an mngen pipeline assessor that invokes `gemini` per item) fails on every item.

## Cause

The three agent files use Claude Code's frontmatter convention where `tools:` is a comma-separated string:

```yaml
tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob
```

Gemini CLI's agent loader requires the value to be a YAML array.

## Fix

Convert each `tools:` field to array form:

```yaml
tools: [Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob]
```

or

```yaml
tools:
  - Read
  - Edit
  - Write
  - Grep
  - Glob
```

The Claude Code loader accepts both shapes, so the array form is portable across both ecosystems.

## Affected files

- `agents/cavecrew-builder.md` — `tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob`
- `agents/cavecrew-investigator.md` — `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`
- `agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md` — `tools: Read, Grep, Bash`

## Local mitigation

Until upstream is fixed, users can patch their installed copy:

```bash
sed -i.bak 's/^tools: \(.*\)$/tools: [\1]/' \
  ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/*.md
```

Reinstalling the extension overwrites the patch.

## Reproduction

`gemini --help` (any invocation that initializes the extension manager) emits the validation error to stderr.

## Environment

- Gemini CLI 0.x with extension manager
- macOS 14, install via `dev-infra extras install caveman`

title: Update README.md with Skills.sh badge
Validation error on install: `tools` expects an array, received string (Gemini CLI)
body:
Hey Julius! Thanks for building this extension, really enjoying using it to save on tokens. 

I was recently installing `caveman` on the latest Gemini CLI and ran into a schema validation error that prevents the `cavecrew` agents from loading correctly. 

## The Error:
When installing or booting up the CLI, the ExtensionManager throws the following error for all three `cavecrew` agents:
```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: Failed to load agent from .../extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-builder.md: Validation failed: Agent Definition:
(Local Agent) tools: Expected array, received string
```

## The Cause:
It looks like the Gemini CLI parser has become a bit stricter about schema validation. In the YAML frontmatter of the agent files, the `tools` field is currently defined as a single string, but the CLI now strictly expects a YAML array. 

This affects the following files:
*   `agents/cavecrew-builder.md`
*   `agents/cavecrew-investigator.md`
*   `agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md`

## Proposed Fix:
Updating the frontmatter in those three files to use an array format instantly resolves the issue locally. 

*Before:*
```yaml
tools: some_tool_name
```

*After:*
```yaml
tools:
  - some_tool_name
```

I’ve manually patched this locally on my Mac for now so I can keep using the extension, but it would be great to get this fixed upstream. I am happy to fork the repo and push a quick Pull Request with these changes. Just let me know!

title: Plugin installs with project scope — breaks CLI when cwd differs from install dir
body:
## Bug

When caveman is installed as a Claude Code plugin (e.g. from VS Code extension), it gets `scope: "project"` with `projectPath` set to the directory where installation happened (typically `~`).

When using Claude Code **CLI** from a different directory (e.g. `~/.dotfiles`, `~/projects/foo`), Claude Code resolves a different project root → the plugin's `projectPath` doesn't match → plugin doesn't load → SessionStart hook never fires → caveman doesn't activate.

The VS Code extension works fine because the workspace root matches the original `projectPath`.

## Reproduction

1. Install caveman plugin from VS Code with workspace root `~`
2. Open Claude Code CLI from `~/.dotfiles` (or any subdirectory that is its own git project)
3. Caveman does not activate — no compressed output, no statusline badge

## Expected

Caveman should activate globally regardless of which project directory CLI is launched from.

## Workaround

Manually edit `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`:
- Change caveman entry from `"scope": "project"` to `"scope": "user"`
- Remove the `"projectPath"` field

## Environment

- macOS
- Claude Code CLI + VS Code extension
- caveman installed via plugin marketplace

title: fix(hook): per-mode reinforcement + language-follows-user note
body:
## Summary

Two small, related fixes for an issue that surfaces when running caveman in non-default modes (especially `wenyan-*`) over many turns:

1. **`hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js`** — the per-turn reinforcement message was a single fixed string (`Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK.`). That wording is right for `lite`/`full` but wrong for every other mode. For `wenyan-*` it actively pulls the model back toward English-style caveman after a few turns, so the reply drifts out of classical Chinese back into fragments-with-articles.

   The fix replaces the fixed string with a per-mode lookup so each mode's reinforcement restates its own core rule. SessionStart still injects the full ruleset; this is just an attention anchor that now matches the active mode.

2. **`skills/caveman/SKILL.md`** — adds a short `## Language` section saying the model's output language follows the user's input language, and that the example block is illustrating compression style, not picking a language. Wenyan modes are clarified as classical Chinese **grammar/style**, independent of which script (Simplified/Traditional) the user is writing in.

   Without this note the model sometimes anchors to the language/script of the nearest example instead of the user's actual writing.

## Why

I run with `defaultMode: wenyan-full` set in `~/.config/caveman/config.json`. After ~6 turns the reply consistently degraded from full classical Chinese back to lite/full English caveman, and Simplified⇄Traditional flickered turn-to-turn. Tracing it down landed on these two spots.

## Behavior change

- English-only users: no observable change. `lite`/`full`/`ultra` reinforcement strings carry the same content as before, just keyed by mode.
- Wenyan-mode users: reinforcement no longer drags the reply toward English-caveman style.
- Mixed-language users: the new SKILL.md note reduces example-anchoring drift.

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke-tested the hook with `echo '{"prompt":"hello"}' | node hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` for each mode in `MODE_REINFORCEMENT` — exits 0, emits the right `additionalContext`.
- [x] `readFlag` whitelist still gates the lookup key — unknown/corrupted flag values fall through to `null` and emit nothing, same as before.
- [x] No new filesystem writes, no new requires, no breaking change to `hookSpecificOutput` shape.
- [ ] Manual session check: start a new Claude Code session in `wenyan-full`, run 10+ turns of conversation, verify replies stay in classical Chinese.

## Notes

- `MODE_REINFORCEMENT` keys mirror `VALID_MODES`. Both `'wenyan'` (canonical) and `'wenyan-full'` (alias preserved on disk by older configs / env vars) are present so neither path falls through to the default.
- The SKILL.md examples themselves are unchanged — they are the author's stylistic call. The new Language section just clarifies how the model should treat them.

title: feat: native opencode installer — direct skills copy to ~/.agents/skills/
body:
## What
Replaces `npx skills add (opencode)` fallback with a native filesystem installer that copies caveman skills directly to `~/.agents/skills/`.
## Why
The current installer routes opencode through `npx skills add`, which:
- Requires Node.js and internet connectivity even for local repo clones
- Adds an unnecessary intermediary (`vercel-labs/skills`) when opencode reads skills directly from the filesystem
- Is slower and less reliable than a direct copy
A native installer mirrors how Claude Code gets first-class treatment (plugin + hooks) and makes opencode installation offline-friendly.
## How it works
Two new install functions handle opencode directly:
**`install_opencode()`** in `install.sh` (macOS/Linux/WSL)
- Detects `~/.agents/skills/` directory or creates it
- Copies all 7 skills from the local repo clone when available
- Falls back to `curl` downloading individual `SKILL.md` files for pipe installs
- Handles `compress/scripts/` subdirectory downloads
- Supports `--force` to overwrite existing skills
- Skips already-installed skills by default
**`Install-Opencode`** in `install.ps1` (Windows/PowerShell)
- Equivalent PowerShell implementation using `Copy-Item` and `Invoke-WebRequest`
- Same offline/online dual mode and idempotency
Both remove opencode from the generic `npx skills` fallback path, so it no longer appears in `SKILLS_AGENTS`.
## Also updated
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/caveman-init.js` | Adds `opencode` as an `AGENTS.md` target, so `--with-init` writes caveman activation rules for opencode users |
| `README.md` | Documents opencode as a native install alongside Claude Code and Gemini CLI |
| `tests/test_opencode_install.py` | 5 integration tests covering local copy, skip, force, compress subdirs, and dry-run |
## Reviewer notes
- The existing `npx skills add` path continues to work for all other agents — only opencode is extracted
- `install.sh` and `install.ps1` stay aligned: same detection probe, same skill list, same idempotency logic
- `AGENTS_SKILLS_DIR` env var overrides the default `~/.agents/skills/` path in both scripts
- Tested on macOS with `bash install.sh --only opencode --dry-run` and `python3 tests/test_opencode_install.py` (5/5 pass)

**What you want**
I'm not sure if this is possible or not. But basically I want to use caveman to shrink the token when Claude is "thinking/reasoning", not when it is writing me the actual output of what I requested.

```
Before: Claude will use a lot of tokens for unnecessary text when "thinking/reasoning", wasting a lot of tokens there (especially for complex cases), then it will use more tokens to write the user output message.
After:  Claude will use caveman for generating the text when "thinking/reasoning", wasting less tokens in that phase, then, it will use all the tokens needed to write the actual user output message.
```

**Why good**
Basically the idea is to save tokens during the thinking/reasoning phase which the user normally don't read anyway, but keep the full text for the actual output..
It is a "middle ground" between saving the max number of tokens and having an output with full details

title: Cross-IDE mirror directories cause duplicate skill registration in Claude Code
body:
## Problem

The plugin ships SKILL.md files for each skill in 5 separate locations:

```
skills/<name>/SKILL.md             <- canonical
plugins/caveman/skills/<name>/SKILL.md  <- mirror
.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md     <- Cursor IDE mirror
.windsurf/skills/<name>/SKILL.md   <- Windsurf IDE mirror
caveman/SKILL.md                   <- top-level (1 skill only)
caveman-compress/SKILL.md          <- top-level (1 skill only)
```

Claude Code's harness scans the plugin root recursively for SKILL.md and registers the same skill multiple times under the same name. Second-pass registrations drop their description from the available-skills list, so keyword auto-trigger breaks — the model can only invoke caveman skills explicitly via the Skill tool.

## Repro
1. `cd ~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/<hash>`
2. `find . -name SKILL.md | awk -F/ '{print $(NF-1)}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` → shows `caveman` 5x, `compress`, `cavecrew`, `caveman-stats` 2x each
3. Check Claude Code's available-skills list — `caveman:caveman`, `caveman:compress`, `caveman:cavecrew`, `caveman:caveman-stats`, `caveman:caveman-help`, `caveman:caveman-review`, `caveman:caveman-commit` show no description.

Additionally, several SKILL.md frontmatters use folded-block YAML (`description: >\n  ...`). Some YAML parsers handle this poorly — single-line `description: "..."` is more portable.

## Suggested fix

- Drop `plugins/caveman/skills/` (redundant with top-level `skills/`)
- Move `.cursor/` and `.windsurf/` mirror dirs outside the Claude Code plugin tree, OR generate them at install time rather than committing them
- Drop top-level `caveman/` and `caveman-compress/` dirs (redundant with `skills/caveman/` and `skills/compress/`)
- Convert `description: >` folded blocks to single-line `description: "..."` for better cross-parser compat

## Workaround

Local SessionStart hook prunes mirror dirs in cache after each session start (until plugin update).

title: One line install fails on mac when piped (`curl | bash`)
body:
When I ran the install command from the README

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.sh | bash
```

it failed and gave this error

```sh
bash: line 39: BASH_SOURCE[0]: unbound variable
error: unknown flag: --
run 'caveman --help' for usage
```

OS: MacOS

Two things going on here

1. `BASH_SOURCE[0]` isn't set when the script is read from stdin, and `set -u` kills the process before the `|| here=""` fallback can catch it.
2. The last line passes a bare `--` to the installer (since `$@` is empty), which it doesn't understand.

Works fine when you clone and run `bash install.sh` directly. It's only the curl-pipe path that's broken.

title: PowerShell 7 installer fails: `Cannot overwrite variable Args because the variable has been optimized`
body:
**What happen**
<!-- What caveman do wrong -->
When running:

```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

on PowerShell 7+, the installer fails with:

```
Invoke-Expression: Cannot overwrite variable Args because the variable has been optimized.

The cause might be:

`install.ps1` defines a parameter named `$Args`:

```
param(

)

`$Args` is a built-in automatic PowerShell variable and cannot be overridden in newer PowerShell versions.

Renaming it to something else (e.g. `$InstallerArgs`) fixes the issue.
