title: caveman-shrink: nested protected-segment sentinels not restored, enum values lost (e.g. `( 0 )` instead of `(STARTER/BUSINESS)`)
body:
## Summary

`caveman-shrink` (v0.1.0) corrupts parenthetical enumeration values in MCP tool descriptions because nested protected-segment sentinels are not recursively restored. The numeric placeholder leaks into the final output, destroying semantic information the model needs.

## Repro

Wrap the Todoist remote MCP server and dump `tools/list`:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "todoist-shrunk": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "caveman-shrink", "cmd", "/c", "npx -y mcp-remote https://ai.todoist.net/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Observed

`list-workspaces` description:

```
Before: ... plan type (STARTER/BUSINESS), user role (ADMIN/MEMBER/GUEST), ...
After:  ... plan type ( 0 ), user role ( 1 ), ...
```

`user-info`:

```
Before: ... user plan (Free/Pro/Business).
After:  ... user plan ( 1 ).
```

The enum values (`STARTER/BUSINESS`, `ADMIN/MEMBER/GUEST`, `Free/Pro/Business`) are lost. From the model's perspective the tool no longer documents its return enums.

### Expected

Either the enum stays intact, or compression is skipped on segments that mix `/` separators with parens. Anything except numeric placeholders surviving into the model-visible output.

## Root cause

In `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js`, `withProtectedSegments` iterates `PROTECTED_PATTERNS` in order and stores matches in a single `segments[]` array, using ` <index> ` as the sentinel. Two patterns fire on the same span:

1. The **path** pattern `\b[\w.-]*[\/\\][\w.\/\\\-]+` matches `STARTER/BUSINESS` (the `/` qualifies it as a path). → `segments[0] = "STARTER/BUSINESS"`, working text becomes `plan type ( 0 )`.
2. The **function-call** pattern `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\([^)]*\)` then matches `type ( 0 )`. → `segments[1] = "type ( 0 )"`, working text becomes `plan  1 `.

Restoration is a **single pass**:

```js
out = out.replace(/ (\d+) /g, (_, i) => segments[+i]);
```

It replaces ` 1 ` → `type ( 0 )` and stops. The inner ` 0 ` sentinel inside the restored segment is never substituted back, so `( 0 )` reaches the model.

## Suggested fix

Loop until stable (or until a max iteration cap to guard against pathological input):

```js
function restoreAll(out, segments) {
  const sentinel = / (\d+) /g;
  for (let i = 0; i < 8 && sentinel.test(out); i++) {
    sentinel.lastIndex = 0;
    out = out.replace(sentinel, (_, idx) => segments[+idx]);
  }
  return out;
}
```

Or, simpler: make the path pattern not match bare `WORD/WORD` without a leading path-like prefix, so `STARTER/BUSINESS` isn't claimed as a path in the first place. A leading-anchor tweak like `(?<=[\s/\\.])` plus requiring at least one `.` or path char would avoid that false positive. The recursive restore is the more robust fix because other pattern pairs (e.g. function-call inside CONST_CASE) can trigger the same nesting.

## Impact

Anyone wrapping an MCP server whose descriptions contain `Word (A/B/C)` enums (Todoist `list-workspaces`, `user-info`, others) gets silent semantic corruption. The model's tool catalog reads coherent English but the enum payload is gone.

## Environment

- `caveman-shrink` 0.1.0 (npm)
- Node 24.14.0
- Windows 11
- Upstream MCP server: `mcp-remote` proxying `https://ai.todoist.net/mcp`

Happy to send a PR if the recursive-restore direction is preferred.

title: feat: add defaultMode "manual" for opt-in activation (no SessionStart auto-activate, bare /caveman still works)
body:
## Problem

There is currently no way to use caveman as a purely opt-in tool: keep the `/caveman` command available but have it activate **only** when the user explicitly invokes it, with no SessionStart auto-activation.

The closest existing config, `defaultMode: "off"`, is too blunt. Because `getDefaultMode()` is shared by both the SessionStart hook and the UserPromptSubmit hook, setting it to `"off"` disables auto-activation **and** makes bare `/caveman` a no-op:

- `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart): `if (mode === 'off')` -> skip activation. Correct for an opt-in user.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` (bare `/caveman`): `if (!arg) mode = getDefaultMode()` returns `'off'` -> the flag is unlinked, nothing activates.

So with `defaultMode: "off"` the user must type `/caveman full` (explicit level) every time; bare `/caveman` does nothing. That is surprising and undocumented.

## Request

A first-class opt-in policy: auto-activation off, but explicit activation (bare `/caveman`, or NL "talk like caveman") still turns caveman on at a sane default level.

## Proposed design (additive, backward compatible)

Introduce `defaultMode: "manual"` as a **config-only policy value**, distinct from the intensity levels:

1. `caveman-config.js`: add `VALID_DEFAULT_MODES = VALID_MODES.concat(['manual'])` used only to validate the config field, plus `MANUAL_DEFAULT_LEVEL = 'full'`. Add `getExplicitActivationLevel()` which returns `MANUAL_DEFAULT_LEVEL` when the default is `'manual'`, and otherwise passes the value through (so `'off'` stays a no-op on explicit activation — unchanged). Keeping `'manual'` **out** of `VALID_MODES` ensures it can never become a flag-file value or a selectable `/caveman <arg>` level (the `readFlag` whitelist and arg validation stay intact).
2. `caveman-activate.js`: treat `'manual'` like `'off'` at session start (skip auto-activation).
3. `caveman-mode-tracker.js`: bare `/caveman` and NL activation resolve via `getExplicitActivationLevel()` instead of `getDefaultMode()`, so they activate `full` under `manual` while `off` remains a no-op.

Result with `{"defaultMode":"manual"}`:

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Session start | not activated |
| `/caveman` | activates `full` (with normal per-turn reinforcement) |
| `/caveman ultra` | activates `ultra` |
| "normal mode" | deactivates |

Platform-agnostic since it flows through `getDefaultMode()` reading `config.json`, so Codex and other agents inherit it (relevant to #185).

Optionally, an installer flag `--manual` could write `{"defaultMode":"manual"}` during install (aligns with the install-time flag direction in #374).

## Why this matters

Some users want caveman strictly on demand, not auto-applied to every session. This is the inverse of #141 (which asked for stronger cross-session persistence) -- both are legitimate, and a `manual` policy lets each user pick. It is purely additive: existing `off`, `full`, `ultra`, etc. behavior is unchanged.

## Related

- #374 (make bundled extras opt-in) -- same "respect the contract, less intrusion" spirit
- #429 (repo-local config.json for default mode) -- shared config plumbing this builds on
- #141 (closed; persist mode across sessions) -- opposite vector, motivates a per-user toggle
- #185 (codex hook defaultMode behavior) -- would inherit `manual` for free

I have a branch implementing this with tests and am opening a PR alongside this issue.

title: feat(hooks): add defaultMode "manual" for opt-in activation
body:
Closes #447.

## What

Adds a `defaultMode: "manual"` policy so caveman can be used strictly opt-in: the SessionStart hook does **not** auto-activate, but an explicit bare `/caveman` (or natural-language "talk like caveman") still activates at `MANUAL_DEFAULT_LEVEL` (`full`).

This fills the gap between `"off"` (no activation at all -- bare `/caveman` is a no-op) and the default `"full"` (auto-activates every session). Previously, users who wanted on-demand-only had to set `"off"`, which also made bare `/caveman` do nothing, forcing `/caveman full` every time.

## Changes

- **`src/hooks/caveman-config.js`**: add `VALID_DEFAULT_MODES` (config-only superset that includes `manual`) and `MANUAL_DEFAULT_LEVEL`; add `getExplicitActivationLevel()`. `getDefaultMode()` now validates against `VALID_DEFAULT_MODES`. `manual` is deliberately kept **out** of `VALID_MODES`, so it can never be written as a flag value or selected via `/caveman <arg>` (the `readFlag` whitelist and arg validation are unchanged).
- **`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`**: treat `manual` like `off` at session start (no flag, no rules).
- **`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js`**: bare `/caveman` and NL activation resolve via `getExplicitActivationLevel()`, so they activate `full` under `manual`; `off` stays a no-op.
- **`tests/test_hooks.py`**: add `ManualModeTests`.

## Behavior with `{"defaultMode":"manual"}`

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Session start | not activated |
| `/caveman` | activates `full` |
| `/caveman ultra` | activates `ultra` |
| "normal mode" | deactivates |

Backward compatible: `off`, `lite`, `full`, `ultra`, `wenyan*` behavior is unchanged. `off` users keep the existing bare-`/caveman` no-op.

## Testing

Ran locally on macOS, Node v22.19.0:

- New `ManualModeTests` (3 cases): **pass**
  - `test_activate_manual_does_not_auto_activate` -- SessionStart writes no flag under `manual`
  - `test_bare_caveman_activates_full_under_manual` -- bare `/caveman` writes flag `full`
  - `test_bare_caveman_is_noop_under_off` -- regression guard: `off` stays a no-op
- Full `tests/test_hooks.py`: **7/7 pass**
- `npm test` (installer suite): **47 pass, 4 fail**. The 4 failures are all in the unrelated `opencode` installer tests (`not ok 13, 14, 16, 17`) and reproduce identically on a clean `upstream/main` checkout without this change -- i.e. they are pre-existing and not introduced here.

Happy to also add an installer `--manual` flag and a README row for `manual` in a follow-up if this direction is acceptable.

title: Companion tools: savings-mirror dashboard + sovacount tier-router (MIT)
body:
Hi Julius — built two MIT companion-tools for Caveman that might be useful as "see also" entries:

- **savings-mirror** — visual web dashboard that surfaces Caveman compression as per-day token + USD-savings, with 7-day and cumulative breakdowns. Read-only consumer of the `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` transcripts (historical, not just current session). Attribution to you in description + footer.
  → https://github.com/sovareq/savings-mirror

- **sovacount** — scope-level LLM tier-router (haiku/sonnet/opus). Stacks with Caveman: tier-routing cuts cost on *which model* is picked, Caveman cuts cost on *which tokens* are sent. v0.1.1 ships a Windows binary plus a real-Anthropic measurement: on a 10-task classification sample with 5 tasks actually executed against the API, SovaCount's tier-routing alone saved **$0.4154 of $0.4714** versus a pure-Opus baseline (**88.1% on this sample**, raw data + methodology in the repo).
  → https://github.com/sovareq/sovacount

Both MIT, no revenue-share, no IP overlap. Happy to add a "Built on Caveman" badge / footer note if useful, or to remove the attribution if you'd prefer no link from your repo back.

### Relationship to existing work in #251

@DeeptimaanB already shipped `/caveman-stats` in #251 — a terminal command for current-session savings, with Codex + Gemini-CLI work in progress. That's the right shape for **inline CLI introspection**.

`savings-mirror` is a complementary shape: a **standalone web dashboard** that parses the *full transcript history* across sessions and folds in sovacount routing decisions, so a power user can monitor cumulative trends over weeks rather than per-session totals. Different audience, same underlying intent.

Open to whatever framing works for you.

title: feat: /caveman <level> persists across sessions (symmetric)
body:
## What's broken today

The slash command `/caveman` only switches caveman for the current session. The SessionStart hook re-activates whatever the SKILL/hook default is on every session resume — even after the user explicitly asked for a different level (most painfully, `off`).

Verbatim user reactions from real sessions:
- *"i thought i turned caveman off?"*
- *"but the caveman skill itself says you can turn it off and that should persist??"*

SKILL.md said "Level persist until changed or session end" — which is a documentation of the limitation, not a desirable property. Persistent levels via `~/.config/caveman/config.json` already work (`getDefaultMode()` reads it, `caveman-activate.js` honors `defaultMode: "off"` and would honor any other valid level the user wrote there). But the user-facing slash command never wrote that file, so anyone who didn't know about the config layer just saw the bug.

## What this PR changes

`/caveman <level>` now writes `defaultMode: "<level>"` to the platform's caveman config file. The choice persists across sessions in **both directions** — `/caveman off` saves off, `/caveman full` saves full, etc. The persistent choice is whatever the user last asked for. Clearing it is a single action: delete the config file.

**`commands/caveman.toml`** — replaced the one-liner prompt with a "resolve → persist → act" flow:
1. Resolve the requested level (with aliases: `stop`/`disable`/`persist-off` → `off`, `on`/`enable` → `full`, `wenyan` → `wenyan-full`). Reject unknown levels loudly.
2. Merge `{"defaultMode": "<level>"}` into `~/.config/caveman/config.json` (or `%APPDATA%\caveman\config.json` on Windows, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/caveman/...`). Existing JSON fields preserved.
3. Apply the level to the current session.

**`skills/caveman/SKILL.md`** — Persistence and Boundaries sections rewritten to describe symmetric persistence and clarify that the slash command itself is the persistence mechanism (no separate `/caveman persist` and no hand-editing JSON required).

## Why symmetric

The first revision of this PR (90cd5ac) only persisted `off` — other levels stayed session-scope. That produced the next confusing UX: after `/caveman off`, running `/caveman full` re-enabled caveman for the current session, but the config still said `off`, so the next session resume was silent again. Users had to know to delete the config file by hand.

The current revision (66f98a8) makes it symmetric. The mental model becomes: *"`/caveman <level>` sets your caveman level. It persists. Delete the config to reset."*

## Compatibility

The hook layer already handles every `defaultMode` value this command writes — no `caveman-config.js` or `caveman-activate.js` changes. Users who never type `/caveman` see no behavior change.

Users who were relying on slash commands being session-scope (probably few — there's no obvious upside) can still set `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE` in their shell env, which overrides the config file per the existing precedence in `getDefaultMode()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `/caveman off` in a session: bot drops caveman style; config file contains `{"defaultMode": "off"}`.
- [ ] Start a new session: SessionStart hook outputs `OK` only, no "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE" reminder.
- [ ] `/caveman full` in that session: caveman resumes; config now `{"defaultMode": "full"}`.
- [ ] Start a new session: hook outputs the full ruleset reminder.
- [ ] `/caveman ultra`: caveman switches to ultra; config now `{"defaultMode": "ultra"}`. Next session is ultra.
- [ ] `/caveman nonsense`: command refuses with the valid level list, no file write.
- [ ] Pre-existing fields in `~/.config/caveman/config.json` (e.g. user-added `theme: ...`) are preserved after every write.

title: Feature: built-in caveman-skill-description compressor
body:
## Problem

Skill description text in `SKILL.md` frontmatter consumes the model's input budget on every turn (Claude Code surfaces it in the skill listing). Many marketplace skills ship with 4–6 line descriptions that include trigger phrases. With `skillListingBudgetFraction` ~1%, this can be a meaningful slice of context, especially in long sessions.

Caveman already compresses prose-style memory files via `caveman-compress`. Skill descriptions are the same class of artifact — repetitive natural-language metadata loaded every session. They're a natural fit for caveman treatment.

## Proposal

Add `caveman-skill-description` sub-skill (or extend `caveman-compress`) that:

1. Scans installed skill files (user-owned + marketplace).
2. Compresses `description:` frontmatter field while preserving `name:`, `version:`, `metadata:`, and the body.
3. Stores compressed text in a user-owned manifest so plugin git-pulls don't undo the change.
4. Registers a SessionStart hook that re-applies the manifest, making overrides survive marketplace updates.

## Prior art (what I rolled locally)

Sharing in case useful as a starting point.

**Manifest** — `~/.claude/skill-description-overrides.json`:

\`\`\`json
{
  "/absolute/path/to/SKILL.md": "Compressed one-line description."
}
\`\`\`

**Script** — `~/.claude/hooks/apply-skill-overrides.py`:

- Parses YAML frontmatter (handles both `description: \"...\"` and folded `description: >` with indented continuation lines).
- Idempotent: skips files whose current description already matches.
- Silent-fails per file so a single bad path doesn't block session start.

**Hook** — `settings.json` SessionStart entry:

\`\`\`json
{
  "hooks": [{
    "type": "command",
    "command": "python3 ~/.claude/hooks/apply-skill-overrides.py",
    "timeout": 5,
    "statusMessage": "Applying skill description overrides..."
  }]
}
\`\`\`

## Result

Compressed 29 marketplace skills (caveman 7 + magnusprot 18 + claude-md-improver + skill-creator + gpt-5-4-prompting) and 12 user-owned skills. Long descriptions like:

> \"Decision guide for delegating to caveman-style subagents. Tells the main thread WHEN to spawn \`cavecrew-investigator\` (locate code), \`cavecrew-builder\` (1-2 file edit), or \`cavecrew-reviewer\` (diff review) instead of doing the work inline or using vanilla \`Explore\`. Subagent output is caveman-compressed so the tool-result injected back into main context is ~60% smaller — main context lasts longer across long sessions. Trigger: ...\"

become:

> \"Decide WHEN to spawn cavecrew-{investigator,builder,reviewer} subagents (~60% smaller output vs vanilla Explore).\"

Estimated input-token reduction: roughly 60–70% across compressed entries.

## Open questions

- Triggering discoverability: very short descriptions may fail Skill tool auto-trigger if the model relies on keywords in the description. Worth benchmarking against the existing eval harness in \`evals/\`.
- Marketplace authors may not want their descriptions rewritten silently — perhaps gate behind an opt-in flag.
- A two-tier description field (\`description\` for the model, \`description_full\` for humans) would solve this upstream but needs Claude Code core support.

title: opencode startup crashes after installing cavecrew skills (fix here)
body:
**What happened**
opencode startup crashes after installing cavecrew skills.

Macos. Clean install of both opencode and caveman.

**Symptoms:**
Error: 4 of 5 requests failed: Unexpected server error.
Affected startup requests: config.providers, provider.list, app.agents, config.get

**Root Cause:**
Three agent files installed to `~/.config/opencode/agents/` have `tools` as a YAML array, but opencode expects an object:
- `cavecrew-reviewer.md`
- `cavecrew-investigator.md`
- `cavecrew-builder.md`

**Bad format (installed):**
```yaml
tools: [Read, Grep, Bash]
```

**Fix:**
```
tools:
  Read: true
  Grep: true
  Bash: true
```

**Files:** src/plugins/opencode/agents/cavecrew-*.md in the caveman repo.

**Version / Instsall Method**
main branch install script from curl -fsSL 

```curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.sh | bash```

title: Portuguese (PT-BR) adaptation: Troglodita
body:
## Hey! 👋

I built **[Troglodita](https://github.com/leninejunior/troglodita)** — a Portuguese (PT-BR) adaptation of caveman for Brazilian developers.

### Why a separate project?

Caveman's compression rules are English-specific (drop "the/a/an", "just/really/basically"). These don't apply to Portuguese, which has:

- **8 articles** with mandatory gender agreement — dropping them all breaks comprehension
- **Different filler words**: "basicamente", "na verdade", "vale ressaltar", "essencialmente"
- **Different hedging patterns**: "talvez valha a pena", "seria interessante considerar"
- **~20% more verbose** than English by nature — so the potential savings are even higher

### What it does

Same idea, different language. Compression rules designed specifically for PT-BR grammar:

| Normal (48 tokens) | Troglodita (16 tokens) |
|---|---|
| "O componente está re-renderizando porque você está criando uma nova referência de objeto a cada ciclo de renderização. Isso acontece porque objetos inline são recriados sempre." | "Re-render: ref nova cada ciclo (objeto inline recriado). Resolver com `useMemo`." |

### Features

- 3 compression levels: `leve` (lite), `total` (full), `máximo` (ultra)
- `/troglodita-commit` — concise conventional commits
- `/troglodita-review` — one-line code review
- Installer for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex

### Target audience

Brazil has a fast-growing vibecoding community — many of these developers interact with AI agents entirely in Portuguese. Caveman doesn't help them because the compression rules target English. Troglodita fills that gap.

Repo: https://github.com/leninejunior/troglodita

Inspired by your work — credits and MIT attribution included. Would love to be listed in the ecosystem section if you think it fits! 🦴

## Why merge

- Pure docs-only diff (+8 / -0 in README.md), trivial revert
- Both repos MIT, attribution to @JuliusBrussee preserved
- Zero changes to caveman itself — both tools are pure consumers of the existing JSONL format + published compression factor

title: feat: Korean language-aware compression
body:
## Summary

Caveman's compression rules are English-specific (drop articles, English short synonyms), so when it responds in Korean the output breaks — garbled fragments, forced/awkward translation of technical terms, unnatural phrasing. This PR makes caveman **respond in the user's language and compress it natively**.

When responding in Korean it now:
- uses 음슴체/개조식 (Korean's natural terse register) instead of broken grunt
- drops particles (은/는/이/가/을/를) only when grammatical role stays clear
- keeps technical terms in English — first mention `한글(English)`, single form after; `ultra` drops the gloss
- never translates/transliterates code, function/API names, or error strings

## Design

- **Language is orthogonal to intensity.** `lite`/`full`/`ultra` are unchanged; the new rules just describe how each intensity manifests in Korean. No new mode names (no `korean-*`).
- **Auto-detected, not a toggle.** Caveman follows the user's input language, so it "just works" after install. `wenyan-*` stays an *explicit* Classical Chinese override and wins over the auto-detected language (wenyan = chosen style; Korean = following the user's actual language).
- **English behavior is unchanged** — every hunk is additive; existing English rules/examples are untouched. Backward compatible.

## Changes

- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — new `## Language` + `## Korean` sections, Korean lite/full/ultra examples, description note. (Single source of truth; the `plugins/` mirror + `dist/` are left for CI sync per CONTRIBUTING.)
- `src/rules/caveman-activate.md` — language-aware line for the always-on rule body.
- `README.md` — short Korean section + What You Get row.

## Test plan

Ran the edited `SKILL.md` as a system prompt through `claude -p` (mirrors the eval harness setup):
- [x] Korean concept question -> natural 음슴체, English technical terms preserved
- [x] Destructive op (`DROP COLUMN`) -> auto-clarity drops to plain prose for the warning, SQL preserved
- [x] `ultra` -> max compression, English terms only, no 병기 gloss
- [x] English prompt -> unchanged English caveman, no Korean leakage

caveman-stats: opus-4 output price hardcoded at $75/M is stale (Opus 4.5–4.8 is $25/M) → savings estimate 3× high
body:
## Where

`hooks/caveman-stats.js` → `MODEL_OUTPUT_PRICE_PER_M`

```js
const MODEL_OUTPUT_PRICE_PER_M = [
  ['claude-opus-4',     75.00],   // ← stale
  ['claude-sonnet-4',   15.00],
  ['claude-haiku-4',     4.00],   // ← slightly stale
  ...
];
```

`priceForModel()` does a `startsWith` prefix match, so **any** `claude-opus-4*` id (incl. `claude-opus-4-8`) resolves to **$75/M output**.

## Bug

Anthropic's Opus rate card has been **$5/M input, $25/M output since Opus 4.5** (Opus 4.8 shipped 2026-05-28 on the same rate card). The `$75` figure is the legacy **Claude 3 Opus** price.

Result: `deriveSavings()` / `formatStats()` / `formatShare()` overstate the dollar figure **~3×** for every session run on a current Opus model — which is the default for a lot of Claude Code users now.

`claude-haiku-4` is also slightly off: Haiku 4.5 is **$5/M** output, not $4.

## Fix

```js
const MODEL_OUTPUT_PRICE_PER_M = [
  ['claude-opus-4',     25.00],   // Opus 4.5–4.8 = $25/M output
  ['claude-sonnet-4',   15.00],
  ['claude-haiku-4',     5.00],   // Haiku 4.5 = $5/M output
  ['claude-3-5-sonnet', 15.00],
  ['claude-3-5-haiku',   4.00],
  ['claude-3-opus',     75.00],   // legacy Claude 3 Opus, correct
];
```

### Caveat
The `claude-opus-4` prefix also matches the retired **Opus 4.0/4.1** ($15/$75 era). A single prefix row can't be exactly right for both 4.1 and 4.8. Since the realistic case is users on 4.5+, `$25` is right for actual usage and the figure is a self-described estimate anyway. If you want precision, split into `claude-opus-4-0`/`claude-opus-4-1` (75) vs `claude-opus-4` (25) rows ordered most-specific-first.

Refs: <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing>

Happy to send a PR if useful.

title: fix(caveman-stats): correct Opus output price ($75→$25) for 4.5+ era
body:
Fixes #465.

## Problem
`src/hooks/caveman-stats.js` `priceForModel()` prefix-matches every `claude-opus-4*` id to **$75/M** output — the legacy *Claude 3 Opus* rate. Anthropic's Opus rate card has been **$5/M in, $25/M out since Opus 4.5** (4.8 shipped on the same card, 2026-05-28). So `/caveman-stats` overstates the savings/cost figure **~3×** for anyone running a current Opus model — increasingly the default.

`claude-haiku-4` was also stale ($4 vs Haiku 4.5's $5/M).

## Fix
Split the table into legacy vs current Opus, **most-specific prefixes first** (the loop returns the first match), so retired 4.0/4.1 (incl. dated ids like `claude-opus-4-20250514`) keep $75 while 4.5–4.8 resolve to $25:

```js
['claude-opus-4-0',    75.00],
['claude-opus-4-1',    75.00],
['claude-opus-4-2025', 75.00],   // dated 4.0 ids
['claude-opus-4',      25.00],   // 4.5–4.8
...
['claude-haiku-4',      5.00],   // Haiku 4.5
```

This keeps the existing dated-id test (`claude-opus-4-20250101 → 75`) valid instead of regressing it — preferred over a flat constant flip, which is the alternative I floated in #465.

## Tests
`tests/test_caveman_stats.js` updated and green — **29/29**. Added asserts pinning both eras (`claude-opus-4-8 → 25`, `claude-opus-4-1-20250805 → 75`).

> Note: `npm test` (the `tests/installer/*` suite) shows 4 failing `opencode …` tests, but they fail identically on a clean `main` checkout — pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Source: <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing>

title: Claude Code SessionStart hook serves weak fallback — src/hooks/ SKILL.md path off by one
body:
## Summary

After the `src/` restructure, the Claude Code **SessionStart hook can no longer find `SKILL.md`**, so it silently serves the weak hardcoded fallback ruleset on every session. The fallback has no intensity table and no examples, so the model drifts back to verbose prose within a few turns — matching the long-standing "drifts back to natural prose mid-session" / "lasts ~4 msgs" reports.

## Root cause: SKILL.md path is off by one

`.claude-plugin` wires the hook at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, so `__dirname` is now `<plugin_root>/src/hooks/`. But the SKILL.md read still uses:

```js
path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')
```

From `src/hooks/` that resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, which does not exist (skills live at `<plugin_root>/skills/`). `readFileSync` throws, the `catch` swallows it, and the hook falls through to the minimal hardcoded fallback in the `else` branch. The stale comment on the line still says `__dirname = <plugin_root>/hooks/`, confirming the path was never updated for the move.

## Repro

```bash
D=<plugin_root>   # e.g. ~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/<sha>
CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=ultra CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=$D node $D/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
# Observe: output is the fallback ruleset — no "## Intensity" table, no examples.
```

## Fix

Probe both layouts before falling back:

```js
let skillContent = '';
const skillCandidates = [
  path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), // src/hooks/ (current)
  path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'),       // hooks/ (older)
];
for (const candidate of skillCandidates) {
  try { skillContent = fs.readFileSync(candidate, 'utf8'); break; } catch (e) {}
}
```

Also update the stale `__dirname = <plugin_root>/hooks/` comment.

## Environment

- Claude Code, caveman plugin install, mode `ultra` (reproduces on any level).
- Plugin commit `655b7d9` (current HEAD at time of report).

This is the live cause of the drift reports on Claude Code post-restructure. Happy to open a PR.

title: SKILL.md framing invites 'normal answer + Caveman: recap' instead of caveman-only output
body:
## Summary

`skills/caveman/SKILL.md` frames caveman as a *translation layer* over a normal answer rather than the whole answer. The model produces a full normal-prose reply, then appends a terse `Caveman:`-labeled recap. Two spots cause it.

> Note: on Claude Code this is currently masked by #467 (the SessionStart hook serves the fallback ruleset, which omits the examples). It bites once #467 is fixed and the full SKILL.md is injected. Agents that load SKILL.md directly (Cursor/Windsurf/etc.) hit it now.

## Cause

1. The intensity examples are laid out as `question → lite / full / ultra / wenyan` renderings of the same answer. Combined with the base model's verbose bias, this reads as "write the normal answer, then produce the caveman version," yielding a `Caveman:`-labeled recap appended to a full normal reply.
2. The Auto-Clarity example ends with the literal line `> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.`. "Caveman resume." is meant as a meta-annotation but reads as a literal output label, reinforcing the `Caveman:` prefix habit.

## Fix

Add an explicit guard to `## Persistence`:

> Caveman IS the whole answer, not a summary of one. NEVER write a normal-prose answer then a terse recap. NEVER prefix terse output with "Caveman:" or similar label. Examples below are alternate renderings of the SAME answer per level — pick the active level and write only that; they are not "normal answer + caveman translation".

Drop the literal `Caveman resume.` token from the Auto-Clarity example — let the resumed caveman line stand on its own and annotate the transition out-of-band.

## Environment

- Reproduces wherever the full SKILL.md is the active prompt (any level).
- Plugin commit `655b7d9`.

Happy to open a PR (same PR as #467 if preferred).

title: /caveman-stats reports 'Unknown command' in Claude Code — missing commands/caveman-stats.toml
body:
## Summary

Running \`/caveman-stats\` in Claude Code returns:

\`\`\`
Unknown command: /caveman-stats
\`\`\`

The other four caveman slash commands work fine.

## Environment

- macOS 15 (arm64), Node v26
- Claude Code, fresh install via \`node bin/install.js --only claude --non-interactive\` (commit 655b7d9c5431)
- Plugin enabled, hooks installed:

\`\`\`
~/.claude/hooks/
├─ caveman-activate.js
├─ caveman-config.js
├─ caveman-mode-tracker.js
├─ caveman-stats.js
├─ caveman-statusline.sh
└─ ...
\`\`\`

\`settings.json\` correctly wired \`SessionStart\` and \`UserPromptSubmit\` hooks.

## Root Cause

\`commands/\` ships only **4** \`.toml\` files:

\`\`\`
$ ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/caveman/commands/
caveman-commit.toml
caveman-init.toml
caveman-review.toml
caveman.toml
\`\`\`

There is **no \`caveman-stats.toml\`**. Claude Code resolves slash commands by scanning these files first; if no match is found, the input is rejected as "Unknown command" before any \`UserPromptSubmit\` hook gets a chance to inspect it.

So \`caveman-mode-tracker.js\` line ~50 (\`/^\\/caveman(?::caveman)?-stats(?:\\s+(.*))?\$/.exec(prompt)\`) never runs — the prompt never reaches the hook.

## Documented Behavior

README.md and INSTALL.md both reference \`/caveman-stats\` as a usable slash command:

- README.md: \`| \`/caveman-stats\` | Real session token usage + lifetime savings + USD. ...\`
- INSTALL.md: \`After your first /caveman-stats run it appends a savings counter ...\`

But the published plugin doesn't register it.

## Suggested Fix

Add \`commands/caveman-stats.toml\`:

\`\`\`toml
description = "Show real token usage and estimated savings for the current session"
prompt = "/caveman-stats"
\`\`\`

The trivial \`prompt = "/caveman-stats"\` re-emits the literal string into \`UserPromptSubmit\`, which the existing \`caveman-mode-tracker.js\` hook then intercepts via \`decision: "block"\` and replaces with the stats output. (\`--share\`, \`--all\`, \`--since\` args still work because the regex captures \`(.*)\` after the command name.)

Verified locally that this stub fixes the issue end-to-end.

## Workaround

Until merged, users can drop the same \`caveman-stats.toml\` into \`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/caveman/commands/\` after install.

title: Plugin migration leaves orphaned settings.json hooks → 'Cannot find module caveman-activate.js' (loader:1478) every session
body:
## Summary

After migrating from the **manual hook install** (`~/.claude/hooks/caveman-*.js` wired into `settings.json`) to the **Claude Code plugin** (`claude plugin install caveman@caveman`), the old `settings.json` hook entries are left **orphaned**. The plugin migration disables/removes the local `~/.claude/hooks/caveman-activate.js` (mine are now `*.js.disabled`) but does **not** remove the `settings.json` entries that point at them. Result: every session and every prompt, Claude Code runs `node <abs> /…/caveman-activate.js` against a missing file:

```
SessionStart:startup hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1478
Error: Cannot find module '/Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/caveman-activate.js'
```

Same for `caveman-mode-tracker.js` on `UserPromptSubmit`, and the `statusLine` command pointing at `caveman-statusline.sh` (now `.disabled`).

It's non-blocking so caveman still works (the plugin's SessionStart `echo` hook fires), but every session and prompt is noisy with a Node `loader:1478` crash. It also misleads debugging — the error renders directly above the `claude-mem` status banner, so it reads as a claude-mem failure when it is caveman's.

## Root cause

In `bin/lib/settings.js`:

- `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands()` only matches **bare** `node <script>` (`const reBare = /^node\s+(...)\s*$/`) and explicitly skips commands with an absolute node path. My orphaned entries are `"/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.0.0/bin/node" "/…/caveman-activate.js"` — absolute node path → never rewritten, never validated against file existence.
- `removeCavemanHooks(settings, marker='caveman')` *would* match these by substring, but it's only invoked on **uninstall**, not on the plugin-install migration path (`bin/install.js` `claude plugin marketplace add` / `plugin install caveman@caveman`).

So the plugin install adds the plugin's own hooks but never reconciles the pre-existing manual-install hooks, leaving dead `node <missing>.js` entries.

## Repro

1. Have caveman installed the old way (settings.json `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`statusLine` → `~/.claude/hooks/caveman-*.js|sh`).
2. Migrate to the plugin: `claude plugin install caveman@caveman` (local hook files get disabled/renamed).
3. Start a new Claude Code session → `loader:1478` / `Cannot find module … caveman-activate.js` every session; same on each prompt.

## Suggested fix

On plugin-based install, reconcile pre-existing manual hooks. Either:

- Call `removeCavemanHooks(settings)` for the managed basenames (`caveman-activate.js`, `caveman-mode-tracker.js`, `caveman-statusline.sh`, `caveman-stats.js`) during plugin install, **OR**
- Extend the legacy walker to drop/repair any `settings.json` hook command whose referenced managed script no longer exists on disk (covers both bare- and absolute-node shapes), **OR**
- At minimum, when the plugin path is taken, strip the manual `settings.json` SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/statusLine entries the installer itself previously wrote.

A "remove managed hook entries whose target file is missing" pass would be the most robust — it self-heals regardless of how the entry was originally written.

## Workaround

Remove the dead entries from `~/.claude/settings.json`: the `SessionStart` → `caveman-activate.js` block, the `UserPromptSubmit` → `caveman-mode-tracker.js` block, and repoint/remove `statusLine` (point at the existing `…/caveman-statusline.sh.disabled` or a plugin-provided one).

Env: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Claude Code v2.1.156, Node v26, caveman plugin `caveman@caveman` enabled.

title: fix(install): prune orphaned managed hooks from settings.json (#471)
body:
## What

Adds `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks()` to `bin/lib/settings.js` and runs it during `installClaude()` to remove managed `settings.json` hook / statusLine entries whose target script no longer exists on disk.

Fixes #471.

## Why

Migrating an old **manual** hook install (`settings.json` hooks → `~/.claude/hooks/caveman-*.js`) to the **Claude Code plugin** disables/renames the local scripts (e.g. `caveman-activate.js` → `caveman-activate.js.disabled`) but leaves the `settings.json` entries pointing at them. Claude Code then runs `node <missing>` every `SessionStart` / `UserPromptSubmit`:

```
SessionStart:startup hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1478
Error: Cannot find module '…/.claude/hooks/caveman-activate.js'
```

Non-blocking, so caveman still works (plugin manifest fires) — but every session and prompt is noisy, and the error renders directly above unrelated plugins' output, so it misattributes the failure (I chased a different plugin for two sessions before isolating it to caveman).

Existing helpers don't cover it:
- `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` only matches the **bare-node** shape; these orphans are **absolute-node** (`"/opt/…/node" "…/caveman-activate.js"`), which it explicitly skips.
- `removeCavemanHooks` runs only on **uninstall**.

## How

`pruneOrphanedManagedHooks(settings, configDir)`:
- Extracts the script path from any managed-looking hook command — bare- or absolute-node, quoted or not, and `bash …` for the statusline — by matching the managed basenames (`caveman-activate.js`, `caveman-mode-tracker.js`, `caveman-stats.js`, `caveman-statusline.sh`).
- Resolves relative paths against `configDir` (honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`).
- Drops the hook entry / `statusLine` **only when the target file is genuinely missing**. A managed hook whose script still exists is left untouched; non-managed hooks (user/superset notify, `rtk`, etc.) are never touched — safe to run on every install.

`installClaude()` runs the prune **unconditionally**, right after the plugin install step and before the hook-wiring decision, so it self-heals an already-dirty config even when standalone wiring is skipped.

## Relationship to #393

Complementary, not overlapping. #393 prevents the **double-wiring** case (fresh install registers hooks via both plugin manifest and settings.json → fire twice). This cleans **pre-existing orphans** left by a migration that happened before any fix. A user who migrated before #393 still has the dead entries; #393 only gates *new* wiring and never removes them. The two work together.

## Tests

6 new unit cases in `tests/installer/unit.settings.test.mjs`:
- removes absolute-node orphan
- removes bare-node orphan
- keeps managed hook whose target exists
- leaves non-managed hooks alone even if missing
- resolves relative target against `configDir`
- drops orphaned managed `statusLine`

`node --test tests/installer/unit.settings.test.mjs` → 25/25 pass. Verified end-to-end against a `settings.json` reproducing the crash: 3 orphans removed (SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit + statusLine), the superset notify hook preserved.

> Note: `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` fails on a clean checkout here (Node 26 `JSON.parse` strictness on a JSONC fixture) — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

CI will resync any mirrors on merge; no source-of-truth skill files touched.

title: cavecrew subagents fail to load in Gemini CLI extension (invalid tool names + Anthropic model)
body:
## Summary

When caveman is installed as a **Gemini CLI extension**, all three `cavecrew` subagents fail to load. Gemini CLI rejects the agent definitions because their frontmatter uses **Claude Code tool names** (`Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`) and an **Anthropic model** (`model: haiku`), neither of which is valid in Gemini CLI.

The core caveman compression modes still work — only the `cavecrew` multi-agent delegation feature is broken on Gemini.

## Environment

- caveman Gemini extension: release tag `v1.8.2` (note: `gemini-extension.json` still says `version: 1.0.1` — minor aside)
- Gemini CLI: `0.44.1`
- OS: Windows 11 (also applies to macOS/Linux — this is platform-independent validation)

## Reproduction

```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman
gemini extensions list
```

Output:

```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: Failed to load agent from
  .../.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-builder.md:
  Validation failed: Agent Definition:
    tools.0: Invalid tool name
    tools.1: Invalid tool name
    ...
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: ...cavecrew-investigator.md: ... Invalid tool name ...
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: ...cavecrew-reviewer.md: ... Invalid tool name ...
```

## Root cause (verified against gemini-cli source)

1. The Gemini extension loader reads agents from a **hardcoded** path — `path.join(effectiveExtensionPath, "agents")` — with no config option to relocate it. So the extension always loads the repo-root `agents/` directory verbatim.

2. Gemini validates each entry in an agent's `tools:` array with `isValidToolName(name, { allowWildcards: true })`, which only accepts:
   - `ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` (Gemini's own tool ids),
   - `TOOL_LEGACY_ALIASES` (currently empty),
   - the `*` wildcard, MCP/discovered tool prefixes.

   Gemini's builtin tool ids differ from Claude Code's. The relevant mapping:

   | Claude Code (current) | Gemini CLI |
   |---|---|
   | `Read`  | `read_file` |
   | `Edit`  | `replace` |
   | `Write` | `write_file` |
   | `Grep`  | `grep_search` |
   | `Glob`  | `glob` |
   | `Bash`  | `run_shell_command` |

   So `Read`, `Edit`, etc. all fail validation → the whole agent definition is rejected.

3. `model: haiku` (`cavecrew-investigator.md`, `cavecrew-reviewer.md`) is an Anthropic model id. It passes Gemini's permissive `model` schema (any string) but would fail at runtime when the subagent is invoked under Gemini.

## Why this is awkward to fix

Per `CLAUDE.md`, `agents/cavecrew-*.md` is a **single source of truth** consumed by both distributions:

- Claude Code plugin — `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` has `source: "./"`, so it loads the repo-root `agents/`.
- Gemini CLI extension — loads the same repo-root `agents/` (hardcoded, see above).

The two tool namespaces are disjoint, and `model: haiku` is Claude-only, so a single shared file cannot satisfy both platforms without a transform step. There is currently no build step for the Gemini extension (it installs the source tree at the release tag).

## Proposed fixes (in order of preference)

**1. Generate Gemini-flavored agent files (preserves Claude behavior).**
Keep `agents/*.md` Claude-canonical. Add a small transform (extend `sync-skill.yml` / a `bin/` script) that emits Gemini-compatible copies with the tool-name map above and `model: haiku` → a Gemini model (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash`). This fits the repo's "single source of truth, generated mirrors" philosophy. The open question is wiring the generated `agents/` into what the Gemini extension actually installs (release artifact vs. source tree).

**2. Drop `tools:` and `model:` from the shared files.**
Both Claude Code and Gemini treat `tools`/`model` as optional, so the agents would load on both. **Downside:** Claude loses the deliberate per-agent tool scoping (e.g. builder's "no Bash" guard) and the `haiku` cost optimization — a regression for Claude users. The prose-level guidance ("No Bash available …") would remain as soft instruction only.

**3. Exclude `agents/` from the Gemini extension.**
The cavecrew subagents can't function on Gemini with Claude tool names anyway, so shipping them only produces load errors. This needs a build/packaging step since Gemini installs the whole repo tree.

I'm happy to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer — likely (1). Let me know.

---
*(Filed after hitting this on a fresh Windows install. Tool-name mapping and loader path were verified against the installed `@google/gemini-cli@0.44.1` bundle.)*

title: caveman-shrink MCP registered with no upstream → fails on every load
body:
**What happen**

Default install registers the `caveman-shrink` MCP server with no upstream
command, so it fails to start on every session.

Installer (`bin/install.js:804`) runs:

```
claude mcp add caveman-shrink -- npx -y caveman-shrink
```

`caveman-shrink` is a proxy/middleware that wraps an upstream MCP server. With
no upstream argument, `index.js:33-37` writes `caveman-shrink: missing upstream
command` and exits 2. Claude Code then shows `1 MCP server failed · /mcp` on
every session load.

`--with-mcp-shrink` is ON by default, so any default install hits this — it is
not specific to one machine.

**Expected**

A default install should yield an MCP entry that either starts cleanly or is
not registered at all. No "1 MCP server failed" on load.

**Before/after example**

```
Registered:  npx -y caveman-shrink            # no upstream
Got:         exit 2 "caveman-shrink: missing upstream command"
             → Claude Code: "1 MCP server failed · /mcp" every session
Want:        one of —
             (a) don't register caveman-shrink by default, or
             (b) register it wrapping a real upstream MCP server, or
             (c) make caveman-shrink idle/no-op (clean MCP handshake) when no
                 upstream is given, instead of exit 2
```

The installer already prints "Wrap an upstream by editing the mcpServers entry"
(`bin/install.js:806`), confirming the registered entry is non-functional until
hand-edited — but until then it fails the handshake on every load.

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

Summary
Hermes support is tracked, but the current upstream docs/install story still lacks a concrete Hermes-native always-on path comparable to hooks or --with-init rule files for other agents.

What I validated
- Open issue already exists: #427 feat(install): support hermes
- Closed issue exists: #231 feat: Add OpenClaw and Hermes agent support
- Current caveman README advertises always-on support for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini, plus --with-init rule files for Cursor/Windsurf/Cline/Copilot.
- Current INSTALL.md has no Hermes-specific install/docs section.
- In Hermes, a natural always-on path is baseline-managed prefill JSON referenced by config.yaml via prefill_messages_file.

Concrete Hermes-native shape
- config.yaml:
  prefill_messages_file: prefill/main-terse-ultra.json
- prefill file:
  ~/.hermes/prefill/main-terse-ultra.json
- content:
  system message that sets terse/caveman style defaults from turn one

Why this matters
- Hermes does not rely on the same hook/rule-file mechanisms as Claude Code or Cursor.
- Prefill is the closest Hermes-native equivalent to an always-on startup rule.
- Without documenting this, “support Hermes” stays vague and users have no canonical install path.

Suggested acceptance criteria
1. README/INSTALL add a Hermes row/section.
2. Docs show a minimal config.yaml example using prefill_messages_file.
3. Docs show the matching prefill JSON example.
4. Docs explain how Hermes top-level vs delegated/subagent defaults should be expressed, if supported.
5. Docs clarify whether Hermes support is manual-docs only or installer-managed.

Related context
- #427
- #231

title: Hermes support should define how delegated/subagent sessions inherit caveman level
body:
Summary
If Caveman/Hermes support lands, the implementation needs an explicit rule for delegated/subagent sessions instead of only documenting a single global style toggle.

What I observed
- The reference terse policy I reviewed uses a split default:
  - top-level/main session -> terse/caveman ultra
  - delegated child/subagent session -> terse/caveman full
- Caveman upstream already has repeated issues around persistence, mode drift, and per-session behavior in other agents.
- Hermes is especially likely to need a documented distinction because parent and child agents can have different readability/compression needs.

Why this deserves its own issue
- A single global “make Hermes talk caveman” setting is underspecified.
- Delegated workers often need to return summaries to a parent/orchestrator, where ultra-compressed output can become too lossy.
- Without a stated inheritance model, different Hermes integrations will drift.

Suggested decision points
1. Should Hermes always use one caveman level for all sessions?
2. Or should Hermes recommend:
   - main/top-level = ultra
   - delegated/subagent = full
3. If different levels are recommended, where should the distinction live?
   - separate prefill files
   - parent prompt conventions
   - subagent template docs
4. How should users override this per profile/project/session?

Suggested acceptance criteria
- Hermes docs state one canonical inheritance/default model.
- Example config/prefill snippets reflect that model.
- Wording explains how to keep subagent outputs compact without becoming unreadable.

Related context
- #427
- issues about persistence/drift in other agents suggest this should be explicit up front rather than left implied.

fix: rename $Args to $InstallArgs in install.ps1 for Windows
body:
## Problem

`install.ps1` uses `$Args` as a `param()` name, but `$Args` is a [PowerShell automatic variable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_automatic_variables?view=powershell-5.1#args) that cannot be overwritten inside `Invoke-Expression`. When users run the documented one-liner:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

PowerShell throws:

```
Invoke-Expression : Cannot overwrite variable Args because the variable has been optimized.
    + CategoryInfo          : WriteError: (Args:String) [Invoke-Expression], SessionStateUnauthorizedAccessException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : VariableNotWritableRare,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeExpressionCommand
```

This breaks the install on **every Windows machine** using PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell).

### Why it happens

When a script is piped to `Invoke-Expression`, PowerShell compiles the script block in the caller's scope. The automatic `$Args` variable is marked as an optimized/read-only variable in that context, so `param([string[]]$Args)` fails because it tries to reassign it.

Running the script as a file (`& .\install.ps1`) works fine because it gets its own scope — but that defeats the purpose of the one-liner install.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **PowerShell:** 5.1.26100.4061
- **Editor:** VS Code with GitHub Copilot agent
- **Node:** v22.x

## Fix

### 1. `install.ps1` — Rename parameter (3 occurrences)

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `[string[]]$Args` | `[string[]]$InstallArgs` |
| `@Args` (splat in local path) | `@InstallArgs` |
| `@Args` (splat in npx path) | `@InstallArgs` |

Also updated the header comment to use the download-then-run pattern and added a `NOTE` block explaining why `$Args` cannot be used.

### 2. `README.md` — Updated Windows install command

```diff
-# Windows (PowerShell 5.1+)
-irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
+# Windows (PowerShell 5.1+)
+$f = "$env:TEMP\caveman-install.ps1"; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 -OutFile $f; & $f; Remove-Item $f
```

### 3. `INSTALL.md` — Updated install command + troubleshooting

- Updated the Windows install command to match README
- Replaced the `irm | iex` troubleshooting bullet with an explicit warning and the correct command

## Testing

1. **Before fix:** `irm ... | iex` → crashes with `VariableNotWritableRare`
2. **After fix (download-then-run):** Downloads to `%TEMP%`, runs in own scope, installs successfully, cleans up temp file
3. **After fix (local clone):** `& .\install.ps1` still works (no regression)
4. **Verified:** All 7 skills installed successfully for GitHub Copilot on Windows 11

## Checklist

- [x] `$Args` → `$InstallArgs` in `install.ps1` (all 3 occurrences)
- [x] README.md Windows command updated
- [x] INSTALL.md Windows command updated
- [x] INSTALL.md troubleshooting section updated
- [x] No breaking changes for macOS/Linux (`install.sh` untouched)
- [x] No breaking changes for local clone usage (`& .\install.ps1` still works)

title: fix(compress): harden validation, CLI, benchmark, and default model
body:
## Summary

Five fixes to the `caveman-compress` skill (in `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/`
and the synced copy). Each closes a correctness gap where the validator could
pass while the compressed output lost structure, or where a helper failed in an
install-only copy.

### Fixes

- **Validation hardening (`validate.py`)** — five gaps:
  - *Variable-length fences*: `extract_inline_codes` only stripped exact 3-char
    ` ``` `/`~~~` fences, so backticks inside a 4+ backtick block were misread as
    inline code → false failures. Now reuses the CommonMark fence-aware scanner
    (closing fence ≥ opening length).
  - *Indented code blocks*: 4-space/tab blocks were treated as prose and could be
    silently rewritten while validation passed. Now extracted and preserved like
    fenced blocks.
  - *Headings exact*: a heading text/order/level change with equal count was only
    a warning (accepted by `compress_file`). Anchors/TOCs/cross-links depend on
    exact headings → now a hard error.
  - *Redundant warning*: a count mismatch fired both an error and the text-change
    warning; the text branch is now `elif` → one error per condition, no noise.
  - *File paths exact*: a dropped/changed referenced path was only a warning → a
    *lost* path is now a hard error; an extra path-like token only in the output
    stays a warning (PATH_REGEX is broad; caveman prose like "pros/cons" can
    coincidentally match).
- **Extensionless build files (`detect.py`)** — `SKIP_EXTENSIONS` only matched the
  rare `*.dockerfile`/`*.makefile` forms, so real `Dockerfile`/`Makefile`
  (extensionless or `Dockerfile.prod`) fell through and could be compressed as
  prose. Adds a case-insensitive basename match that runs before the extension
  rules.
- **Benchmark degrades gracefully (`benchmark.py`)** — glob/no-args mode called
  `sys.exit(1)` when `tests/caveman-compress` was absent (an install copy without
  the repo's `tests/` tree). Benchmarking bundled fixtures is optional → prints a
  note and exits 0. Direct file-pair mode unchanged.
- **CLI usage (`cli.py`)** — corrects the printed usage to the module invocation.
- **Default model (`compress.py`)** — bumps the default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

### Tests

- Adds `tests/test_validate_inline.py`: fail/pass coverage for variable-length
  fences, indented blocks, heading-exact failures (text/level/count, no redundant
  warning), and path-loss-vs-prose.
- Corrects the `claude-md-project` compressed fixture, which had mutated a heading
  level (`###` → `##`) — that encoded the old warn-only behavior and now fails the
  headings-exact rule.

Local verification on this branch:
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_validate_inline tests.test_compress_safety` → **29 tests OK**
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` → **all checks passed**

---

Co-authored-by: claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Caveman compresses issue/PR/MR titles and descriptions
body:
> :robot: _This was written by an AI agent on behalf of @paolomainardi._

## Problem

The active-mode reminder and the skill boundaries tell the model to write **code, commits, and security warnings** in normal prose. They say nothing about **issue, pull-request, and merge-request titles and descriptions**.

Those are prose artifacts meant for humans (reviewers scanning a board, reading a PR/MR body), not terminal output to compress. In practice, while caveman mode is active the model writes terse, fragmented PR/MR/issue titles and descriptions, which reads badly and undercuts the convention that "narrative artifacts stay normal".

## Where it shows up

The boundary line is hardcoded across the source-of-truth surfaces, e.g.:

- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` — per-turn `UserPromptSubmit` reminder: `Code/commits/security: write normal.`
- `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` — `SessionStart` ruleset `## Boundaries`: `Code/commits/PRs: write normal. ...`
- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — `## Boundaries`
- `src/rules/caveman-activate.md`, `src/tools/caveman-init.js` — auto-activation rule body / per-repo init template

None of these explicitly name issue/PR/MR titles+descriptions, and there is no config knob to extend the carve-out (`~/.config/caveman/config.json` only supports `defaultMode`, validated against a fixed `VALID_MODES` whitelist).

## Proposed fix

Extend the existing boundary line to explicitly cover issue/PR/MR titles and descriptions, e.g.:

```
Code/commits/security/issue+PR+MR titles+descriptions: write normal prose.
```

applied consistently across the source-of-truth surfaces above (CI mirrors under `plugins/` regenerate from these).

## PR

PR #483 implements this.

title: fix: prune orphaned settings.json hooks on plugin migration
body:
## Problem

When migrating from a standalone hook install to the Claude Code plugin, old `settings.json` entries referencing hook files under `~/.claude/hooks/` are not cleaned up. The plugin system takes over hook delivery, but the manual entries remain pointing at files that may no longer exist. Every subsequent session emits noise like:

```
Error: Cannot find module '/Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/caveman-activate.js'
```

Two related root causes:

1. **No cleanup on plugin install** — `removeCavemanHooks()` only runs during `--uninstall`, never during plugin install, so orphaned entries from the previous standalone install persist indefinitely.

2. **`rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` only matched bare `node` commands** — the regex `^node\s+...` silently skipped hooks written with an absolute node path (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.0.0/bin/node`), which is the format written by Homebrew, nvm, and the current installer itself. Stale absolute paths from old Node versions were never updated.

Closes #471

## Changes

### `bin/lib/settings.js`

- **New `extractManagedScriptPath(command)`** — parses any node hook command variant (bare `node`, absolute path, quoted/unquoted) and returns the script path. Used by both functions below.
- **Rewrote `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands()`** — now handles all node executable formats, not just bare `node`. Skips only commands already using the exact target binary; rewrites everything else to the canonical `"<absoluteNode>" "<scriptPath>"` form.
- **New `pruneDeadHookFiles(settings)`** — walks all hook entries, checks `fs.existsSync` for each managed script path, and removes entries whose files are gone. Only touches basenames in `MANAGED_HOOK_BASENAMES`; user-authored hooks are always left alone.

### `bin/install.js`

- **`installClaude()`** — after plugin install (fresh or already-installed), reads `settings.json` and calls `pruneDeadHookFiles`. If orphaned entries are found, writes the cleaned file back and logs how many were removed.
- **`installHooks()`** — calls `pruneDeadHookFiles` before `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` so dead entries and stale node paths are both resolved before idempotency checks run.

## Tests

Added 11 new tests in `tests/installer/unit.settings.test.mjs` (all 28 unit tests pass):

- `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` rewrites stale absolute-node scripts (the old "ignores absolute node" behaviour was the bug)
- `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` skips commands already using the target node binary
- `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands` rewrites unquoted absolute-node scripts
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` removes entries whose managed scripts are missing
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` keeps entries whose managed scripts exist on disk
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` does not touch user-authored hooks even if their files are missing
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` handles multiple events and mixed live/dead entries
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` handles the bare-node command format
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` is a no-op on empty or missing hooks
- `pruneDeadHookFiles` preserves non-hook settings keys (theme, statusLine, etc.)

title: Missing caveman-compress.md in opencode commands causes install failure
body:
### Description

Installing via `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.sh | bash` fails with `ENOENT` when copying opencode command files.

### Error

```
opencode install failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, copyfile
'.../caveman-installer/src/plugins/opencode/commands/caveman-compress.md'
-> '~/.config/opencode/commands/caveman-compress.md'
```

### Root cause

The `OPENCODE_COMMAND_FILES` array in `bin/install.js` (line 467) includes `caveman-compress.md`, but this file does not exist in the repository at `src/plugins/opencode/commands/`.

Existing files in that directory:
- caveman.md
- caveman-commit.md
- caveman-review.md
- caveman-stats.md
- caveman-help.md

Note that `skills/caveman-compress/` directory **does** exist, only the command file is missing. It was likely either:
1. The command file was never created for this skill
2. The file was renamed but the array was not updated

### Impact

The entire opencode install path aborts on this error, leaving all other opencode commands (caveman.md, caveman-commit.md, caveman-review.md) partially installed.

### Suggestion

Either add the missing `caveman-compress.md` to `src/plugins/opencode/commands/`, or remove it from `OPENCODE_COMMAND_FILES` and `OPENCODE_SKILL_DIRS` if the compress feature is not yet ready.

- `--no-mcp-shrink` not required; same failure with and without it.
- Fresh install command:

  ```
- Cause A:
  - `bin/install.js:467` includes `caveman-compress.md` in `OPENCODE_COMMAND_FILES`.
  - `src/plugins/opencode/commands/` has no `caveman-compress.md`.
- Workaround used only to continue validation:
  - Remove `caveman-compress.md` from `OPENCODE_COMMAND_FILES` in `bin/install.js`.
- Failure B (after workaround):
  ```text
  Error: Configuration is invalid at .../.config/opencode/agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md
  ↳ Expected object | undefined, got ["Read","Grep","Bash"] tools
  ```
- Cause B:
  - Installed `agents/cavecrew-*.md` use `tools: [Read, ...]` in frontmatter.
  - OpenCode `1.15.13` schema expects `permission` object.

**Expected**

- Installed cavecrew agents pass `opencode debug config` without manual edits.
- No local patch required for default install path.

Got:   Expected object | undefined, got ["Read","Grep","Bash"] tools
Want:  Config validation passes; cavecrew agent frontmatter matches schema
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode on macOS

**Version / install method**
- OpenCode version: `1.15.13` (`opencode --version`)
- Install source: `github:JuliusBrussee/caveman` (latest `main` as of 2026-06-05)
- Tested commit: `655b7d9c5431f822264b7732e9901c5578ac84cf`
- Install command:
  ```bash

**Impact**

title: fix(claude): SessionStart hook SKILL.md path broken after src/ restructure
body:
Fixes #467

## Problem

After the `src/` restructure, `caveman-activate.js` moved from `hooks/` to `src/hooks/`, but the relative path to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` was not updated. The hook resolved `__dirname/../skills/...` → `src/skills/...` — a path that doesn't exist. `readFileSync` threw, the `catch` swallowed it, and **every session silently served the weak hardcoded fallback ruleset** (no intensity table, no examples). Models drifted back to verbose prose within a few turns.

## Fix

Probe both layouts before falling back:

- `src/hooks/ → ../../skills/caveman/SKILL.md` (current layout)
- `hooks/     → ../skills/caveman/SKILL.md`    (legacy layout)

## Test — real RED → GREEN

`tests/test_activate_skillmd_path.js` spawns the real hook and asserts the full SKILL.md is loaded (the `## Intensity` table is SKILL.md-only — never in the fallback).

**GREEN (fix in place):**
```
✓ activation loads full SKILL.md (not the weak fallback)
✓ intensity table is filtered to the active level
2 passed, 0 failed
```

**RED (candidate path reverted to the stale `../skills`):**
```
✗ activation loads full SKILL.md (not the weak fallback)
    expected SKILL.md content ("## Intensity"), got fallback:
    CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full
    Respond terse like smart caveman. … (hardcoded fallback, no ## Intensity)
✗ intensity table is filtered to the active level
0 passed, 2 failed
```
The reverted hook emits the weak fallback — the exact silent-degradation this issue reports. The test proves the SKILL.md path is actually resolved.

title: fix(shrink): restore nested protected-segment sentinels (#444)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #444

`withProtectedSegments` built sentinels in a single pass and restored them in a single pass. When two `PROTECTED_PATTERNS` matched the same span — path rule swallows `STARTER/BUSINESS`, then function-call rule swallows the resulting `type ( 0 )` — the outer sentinel restored to `type ( 0 )` but the inner ` 0 ` was never substituted back. Enum values reached the model as literal `( 0 )`.

Restore now loops up to `MAX_RESTORE_PASSES` (= 8) and exits early as soon as no sentinel remains. The actual #444 inputs settle in 2 passes.

## Reproduces with

compress('plan type (STARTER/BUSINESS)').compressed
// before: "Plan type ( 0 )"
// after:  "Plan type (STARTER/BUSINESS)"

title: fix(hooks): load SKILL.md from plugin layout
body:
## Summary

- Load `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` from the current plugin `src/hooks` layout before falling back to the legacy flat hook layout.
- Gate the two-level plugin probe to real `src/hooks` installs so standalone hooks under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks` cannot accidentally read unrelated `~/skills` content.
- Add regression tests that verify plugin layout loads the real skill file, cwd-local skills are ignored, and standalone layout still falls back when only home-level skills exist.

## Root Cause

The Claude Code plugin manifest runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, so `__dirname` is `<plugin_root>/src/hooks`. The hook still looked for `../skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, which resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`. That file does not exist, so the hook silently served the hardcoded fallback instead of the source-of-truth skill body.

That fallback is missing the intensity table and wenyan instructions, so plugin installs did not get the full behavior documented in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`.

## Validation

- `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_hooks`
- `node src/hooks/caveman-activate.js | rg '## Intensity|Current level:'`
- `git diff --check`
- `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_compress_safety`
- `node tests/test_symlink_flag.js`

Additional documented checks were run and failed for existing baseline issues unrelated to this change:

- `npm test` fails in OpenCode installer tests (`caveman-compress.md` missing / temp OpenCode files absent / JSONC parse expectation). This same failure was observed on clean upstream `main` before this branch.
- `node tests/test_caveman_init.js` fails count-based assertions around current init targets/OpenClaw handling. This same failure was observed on clean upstream `main`.

## Review Notes

Additional review found two hardening gaps in the first draft: the ungated `../../skills` probe could escape standalone hook installs into `~/skills`, and the plugin-layout test used `cwd=plugin_root`. This version gates the plugin probe to `src/hooks`, runs the regression from an unrelated cwd with a sentinel cwd skill, and adds a standalone-home sentinel test.

## Overlap

Several open PRs touch `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, including #483, #448, #411, #407, #401, and #377. This PR keeps the scope to the SKILL.md path lookup and its regression test so it can be rebased independently. Older dirty PRs such as #285 and #269 touch the pre-`src` hook path and may need the same path logic if revived.

Fixes #467

feat: Auto-Clarity exception for the final task answer (clear prose for the turn-closing summary)
body:
Caveman is perfect for the intermediate messages an agent emits while working (status notes, quick acks between tool calls): that is where the token volume is. But the turn-closing summary, the one message the user actually reads to understand what happened, carries all the comprehension load. Saving ~75% there costs more in re-reading than it saves in tokens.

Proposal: extend Auto-Clarity in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` with one more drop case:

> Also drop caveman for FINAL TASK ANSWER: the turn-closing message that delivers results, summary, or explanation after work done. User reads only that message to understand outcome: write it in normal clear prose, full sentences, explain properly. Caveman stay for intermediate progress notes, status lines, quick acks between tool calls.

**Before** (turn-closing summary, `full`):

> Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Edge: token accepted at exact expiry second. Fix pushed, tests green. Side effect: sessions live 1s longer, no security impact.

**After**:

> Found it: the auth middleware checks token expiry with `<` instead of `<=`, so a token is still accepted at the exact expiry second. Fix is pushed and tests are green. Side effect: sessions now live one second longer, which has no security impact.

Why better: intermediate chatter keeps the full token cut, and the single message per task that a human reads stays clear. If you prefer it opt-in, it could also be a config flag (e.g. `"clearFinalAnswer": true` next to `defaultMode`).

I run this as a local patch and it works well. Happy to send a PR if you are open to it (one paragraph in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`).

title: fix: clean up temp files leaked by failed flag renames
body:
## Bug

`safeWriteFlag` in `src/hooks/caveman-config.js` writes the mode flag via an atomic temp + rename (`.caveman-active.<pid>.<timestamp>` → `.caveman-active`). On Windows, `renameSync` over an existing file fails with `EPERM`/`EBUSY` whenever another process holds the target open — the statusline script reading the flag, or a second hook instance writing concurrently. The silent-fail `catch` (correct per the hook rules) swallows the error, but the temp file is never removed.

Net effect: one orphaned temp file per failed rename, accumulating indefinitely in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Observed in normal daily use on Windows 11: **28 orphans in two weeks**.

## Fix

Two parts, both silent-fail per the hook rules in CLAUDE.md:

1. **`safeWriteFlag` cleans up after itself.** The write + rename now runs inside a `try/finally`; if the rename did not complete, the temp is unlinked. No new failure modes — a failed unlink is swallowed like every other fs error.

2. **`sweepOrphanTemps(flagDir)`** removes temps left by older versions or hard crashes mid-write. Called once per session from `caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart). Deletion criteria are conservative:
   - file older than 24h, **or**
   - owning PID is dead **and** the file is >60s old (grace window so an in-flight write from a live concurrent hook is never touched).

   The strict pattern `^\.caveman-active\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$` can never match the live flag (`.caveman-active`, no suffix). Symlinks matching the pattern are skipped (consistent with the symlink-safety posture of the rest of the module). Nonexistent dirs and fs errors silent-fail.

## Tests

`tests/test_temp_leak.js` (follows `tests/test_symlink_flag.js` conventions), 9 cases:

- successful write leaves no temps
- failed rename (simulated `EPERM`) leaks nothing and leaves the original flag intact
- sweep removes >24h orphans and dead-PID orphans past the grace window
- sweep keeps fresh live-PID temps, dead-PID temps inside the grace window, the live flag, and unrelated files
- sweep skips symlinks matching the temp pattern
- sweep silent-fails on a nonexistent directory

```
9 passed, 0 failed
```

`tests/test_symlink_flag.js` is unchanged by this PR: 5 passed / 7 failed both on `main` and on this branch in my environment — the 7 failures are `EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink` (Windows without Developer Mode cannot create symlinks), pre-existing and unrelated.

## Repro (Windows)

1. Configure the caveman statusline (reads the flag frequently) and use Claude Code normally for a few days, or run two hook instances concurrently.
2. `ls $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-active.*` → orphaned temps accumulate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: install.ps1 drops all flags on Windows PowerShell 5.1 ($Args param collides with the automatic variable; @Args splat into npx.ps1 passes nothing)
body:
**Summary:** On Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default `powershell.exe` on every Windows box), `install.ps1` silently drops every flag it is asked to forward. `--uninstall` runs a plain install. `--force`, `--only`, etc. are lost the same way.

**Root cause:** `install.ps1` declares its passthrough parameter as `$Args`:

```powershell
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)]
  [string[]]$Args
)
...
& npx -y "github:$Repo" @Args
```

`$Args` collides with PowerShell's automatic `$args` variable. Under 5.1, splatting `@Args` works when the callee is a native executable, but when `npx` resolves to `npx.ps1` (which it does whenever the shim runs inside PowerShell, since .ps1 outranks .cmd in command resolution), the splat passes nothing. The inner script receives zero arguments. pwsh 7 does not have this behavior, which is probably why it never showed up in testing.

**Repro (Windows PowerShell 5.1, npm 11.5.1):**

```powershell
# argprobe is any local package whose bin prints process.argv.slice(2)
powershell -NoProfile -Command "& .\install-mimic.ps1 --uninstall"
# where install-mimic.ps1 is the param block above + `& npx -y <argprobe-spec> @Args`
# => node sees []
```

Rename the variable and the same chain forwards correctly:

```powershell
param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)][string[]]$Rest)
& npx -y "github:$Repo" @Rest
# => node sees ["--uninstall"]
```

**Real-world impact:** we shell your installer from a GUI control panel. An uninstall request spawned `install.ps1 --uninstall`, the flag was eaten, and the installer reinstalled instead. `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman --uninstall` invoked directly (cmd resolves `npx.cmd`, no shim) works fine, which is how we narrowed it to the shim.

**Suggested fix:** rename `$Args` to anything that is not an automatic variable (`$Rest`, `$Remaining`, `$Passthru`) in both the param block and the two splat sites. One-line-ish change, no behavior change on pwsh 7.

Happy to confirm a fix against our setup.

 -jjg

title: benchmarks/run.py: default --model claude-sonnet-4-20250514 is retired (404) — bump to claude-sonnet-4-6
body:
**Problem**

`benchmarks/run.py` hardcodes a now-retired model as the argparse default:

https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/25d22f864ad68cc447a4cb93aefde918aa4aec9f/benchmarks/run.py#L244

Anthropic deprecated `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` with retirement on **June 15, 2026**. From that date, running the benchmark without an explicit `--model` flag fails immediately with a 404 `not_found_error` before any benchmarking happens.

**Suggested fix**

Bump the default to the current alias, which is Anthropic's documented drop-in replacement for this model:

```python
parser.add_argument("--model", default="claude-sonnet-4-6", help="Model to use")
```

**Related heads-up: `temperature=0`**

The benchmark also passes `temperature=0` on every request:

https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/25d22f864ad68cc447a4cb93aefde918aa4aec9f/benchmarks/run.py#L56-L59

Newer Anthropic models (Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Fable 5) removed sampling parameters entirely — any request including `temperature` returns a 400. So even an explicit `--model claude-opus-4-8` fails today. Worth dropping `temperature=0` (or passing it only for models that accept it) in the same change, so the `--model` escape hatch works across current models.
