title: feat: per-agent model override for cavecrew subagents (reviewer hardcoded to haiku, too weak as a review gate)
body:
## Problem

The cavecrew subagents pin `model:` in their frontmatter — `cavecrew-reviewer` is `model: haiku`, and builder/investigator likewise. Haiku is the right *default* (cheap, fast), but when cavecrew-reviewer is wired in as a real pre-merge / pre-push review gate, haiku misses semantic bug-classes that a stronger model catches (subtle invariant violations, cross-file reasoning, "this looks fine but is wrong" cases). Users who depend on the reviewer for correctness want to opt it up to `sonnet`/`opus` **per agent**, without touching the others.

There is currently no clean way to do that. Every override path is bad:

| Path | Why it fails |
|---|---|
| Shadow agent in `~/.claude/agents/<name>.md` | Same-`name:` is a **whole-file replacement**, not a field merge. To change only `model:` you must copy the plugin's entire system-prompt body — which then **freezes and drifts stale** every time the plugin updates the reviewer (the body has already changed once: `25d22f864ad6` → `655b7d9c5431`). You silently lose upstream review improvements. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env | Global — bumps **every** subagent and main-thread delegation, not just the reviewer. Too broad; pays opus/sonnet cost everywhere. |
| Per-call `model` param on the Task tool | Only applies when the agent is **explicitly** invoked; no effect on auto-delegation. Also can't be set once and forgotten. |

## Request

A per-agent model override that leaves the plugin-maintained body live (so it keeps getting upstream improvements). Any of:

1. **Env vars** read by the SessionStart hook, e.g. `CAVECREW_REVIEWER_MODEL`, `CAVECREW_BUILDER_MODEL`, `CAVECREW_INVESTIGATOR_MODEL`. The hook rewrites only the `model:` line of the generated agent files at install/session start.
2. **A small config block** (e.g. in the existing settings the hook already reads) mapping agent name → model.
3. At minimum, **document** the supported override and pick a default that's a deliberate quality/cost trade rather than always-haiku for the reviewer.

## Why this is the one agent worth it

The reviewer is the cavecrew agent whose output users most depend on for *correctness*, and the one where a model bump most changes results. Builder/investigator tolerate haiku far better. A field-level model knob (vs. all-or-nothing shadow/env) is the missing piece.

## Related

- #473 — also surfaces the hardcoded-model problem, from the portability angle (the pinned Anthropic model breaks the Gemini CLI backend). A per-agent model config would help there too.

Happy to PR the SessionStart-hook env-var approach if that's the preferred direction.

title: ask about project
body:
Question 1: Caveman targets token bloat by conditioning coding agents (like Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI) to strip grammatical fluff while preserving exact technical instructions. From a prompt-engineering perspective, how does the underlying SKILL.md system prompt enforce this high-compression syntax without causing the model to miss subtle edge cases in complex logic, or drop critical context during deep code modifications?

Question 2: To keep agent outputs structurally compact, Caveman features distinct operational intensities (such as lite, full, ultra, and wenyan). How does the system dynamically inject these constraints into the active generation session? Does it depend entirely on formatting rubrics in the system prompt, or does it leverage targeted Few-Shot user-assistant turn examples to align the target LLM with the desired compression density?

Question 3: For terminal setups like Claude Code, the repository sets up local lifecycle hooks to configure automatic session startup, active session flags, and an interactive status-line token counter (/caveman-stats). How does the installation script register these hooks into the client agent's terminal configuration directory, and how does it parse local execution logs to update the lifetime savings metric without blocking live input/output rendering?

Question 4: Beyond compressing immediate responses, the /caveman-compress sub-tool acts on local workspace context documents (like CLAUDE.md, documentation pages, or todo lists) to rewrite them into a high-density format. What precise parsing strategy does the compressor use to guarantee that critical identifiers, package scripts, syntax tokens, and source paths remain perfectly byte-preserved during the file translation?

Question 5: Recent ecosystem additions introduce specialized sub-agents (cavecrew-investigator, cavecrew-builder, and cavecrew-reviewer) that delegate task execution via a centralized decision-making guide. How does the core coordinator evaluate task complexity to decide when to spawn a scoped caveman-style worker subagent rather than attempting to process the code adjustments directly inside the main execution loop?

Question 6: To fully embed this token-saving behavior into model weights, the ecosystem introduces Cavegemma—a Gemma 4 31B fine-tune trained on baseline-to-caveman communication records. When evaluating the model via the three-arm evaluation harness (evals/), what structural metrics (e.g., semantic drift, AST matching, compilation success rates) are used to verify that the fine-tuned weights maintain exact functional alignment with standard verbose outputs?

title: Add Hermes Agent port (ports/hermes/)
body:
## What

Adds a community **port of caveman to [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes)** under a new self-contained `ports/hermes/` directory.

Hermes is an AI agent with its own skills system (`~/.hermes/skills/`), TUI, desktop app, and ~20-platform messaging gateway. It has **no Claude-Code plugin/hook/MCP surface and no vercel-labs/skills slug**, so it can't ride the unified `bin/install.js` path. This PR therefore keeps the port in its own folder with a small shell installer.

**Strictly additive.** Touches nothing outside `ports/hermes/` — no changes to the Node installer, CI mirrors, top-level skills, or README. Zero risk to existing agents.

## Contents

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ports/hermes/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` | Caveman terse mode in Hermes skill format (`metadata.hermes` frontmatter). Levels lite/full/ultra + wenyan. |
| `ports/hermes/skills/cavecrew/SKILL.md` | Cavecrew reworked for Hermes `delegate_task` — the `agents/cavecrew-*.md` files have no Hermes analog, so role contracts pass inline as subagent `context`. Marked **experimental + context-bound**. |
| `ports/hermes/install.sh` | Idempotent installer → `~/.hermes/skills/productivity/`, `--dry-run` supported. |
| `ports/hermes/benchmarks/` | tiktoken measurement harness + results. |

## Why it's a redraft, not a copy

- **No hooks / statusline / MCP shrink / slash commands** — Hermes lacks those surfaces; skills-only.
- **cavecrew → `delegate_task`** with Hermes toolset names (`file`, `terminal`). Flagged experimental because each crew task costs a full delegation round-trip.
- **Verbose-profile conflict resolved** — Hermes profiles can mandate verbose answer formats; the skill suspends those while active but **never compresses safety-critical output** (Auto-Clarity preserved).

## Empirically tested before submitting

I measured token reduction with tiktoken `o200k_base` over 8 paired prompts (harness included). Result: **full ≈ 53% (43–68%), ultra ≈ 71%**. Heads-up that this also surfaces a discrepancy worth flagging upstream: the "~65–75%" headline matches **ultra**, not the **full** default — the port states per-level numbers instead. A 5-lens internal review also caught and fixed a toolset bug in the cavecrew presets before this PR.

## Offer

Kept minimal and separate for reviewability. If you'd rather have native integration, I'll follow up with a PR wiring Hermes into the `PROVIDERS` array (`mech: hermes-skills`, `detect: command:hermes`) per CONTRIBUTING.md. Your call.

Port also maintained standalone at https://github.com/nickgogerty/caveman-hermes (MIT, attribution + NOTICE preserved).

title: Security Scan Flags “Caution” Verdict for the *caveman* Skill (High‑risk Exfiltration & Medium‑risk Path Traversal)
body:
**Title:** Security Scan Flags “Caution” Verdict for the *caveman* Skill (High‑risk Exfiltration & Medium‑risk Path Traversal)

---

**Description**

When attempting to install the *caveman* skill via the Hermes CLI (`hermes skills install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman`), the built‑in security scanner blocks the operation:

```
Scan: caveman (caveman/community)  Verdict: CAUTION
  HIGH     exfiltration   benchmarks/run.py:23
  MEDIUM   traversal      CONTRIBUTING.md:18
Decision: BLOCKED — Blocked (community source + caution verdict, 2 findings).
Use --force to override.
```

The two findings are:

| Severity | Type          | File & Line                        | Brief Description |
|----------|---------------|------------------------------------|-------------------|
| **HIGH** | Exfiltration  | `benchmarks/run.py:23`             | Calls `os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip())`, which may read environment variables (including API keys, tokens, passwords) and could unintentionally expose them to external services or logs. |
| **MEDIUM**| Path Traversal| `CONTRIBUTING.md:18` (text reference) | Mentions relative path `../../issues?q=label`, indicating the code may construct file paths from user‑controlled inputs, potentially allowing directory traversal and unintended file reads/writes. |

Because the source is community‑maintained and these issues are flagged, Hermes automatically blocks the installation unless the user explicitly overrides with `--force`.

---

**Impact**

- **Potential data leakage**: If the skill runs in a profile that contains sensitive environment variables (e.g., API keys, `.env` values), the exfiltration code could leak those values to remote endpoints or logs.
- **File‑system safety**: Path‑traversal patterns could be exploited to read or overwrite files outside the intended directory, especially if the skill later adds dynamic file handling based on user input.
- **User friction**: The block forces users to either manually inspect the code or use `--force`, which defeats the purpose of the security safeguard.

---

**Requested Action**

1. **Audit & Harden the Code**
   - Review `benchmarks/run.py` for any unintended exposure of environment variables. If reading env vars is required, explicitly whitelist only non‑secret variables or mask values before any outbound communication.
   - Ensure any file‑path handling sanitises inputs and restricts operations to a known safe directory (e.g., using `pathlib.Path.resolve().relative_to(BASE_DIR)`).

2. **Add a Security Notice**
   - In the repository’s `README.md` or a dedicated `SECURITY.md`, clearly state that the skill accesses environment variables and may perform file operations, advising users to run it in an isolated profile without secrets.

3. **Update the Security Scan Metadata**
   - If the above issues are resolved, tag the repository with a higher confidence level (e.g., “verified”) so the Hermes scanner can allow installation without requiring `--force`.

4. **Provide a Minimal Reproduction**
   - Include a small test script or CI job that demonstrates the safe handling of environment variables and path resolution, allowing automated verification during future scans.

5. **Documentation for Users**
   - Add a “Installation Safety” section to the skill documentation, recommending users install the skill in a dedicated Hermes profile (or use `--force` only after manual code review).

---

**Additional Context**

- The *caveman* skill is designed to compress Claude‑Code / Codex prompts and reduce token usage by up to ~65 %. While the functionality is valuable, the potential security ramifications outweigh the benefits when used in a production environment with sensitive credentials.
- Providing a clear remediation path will help maintain the skill’s utility while keeping the Hermes ecosystem secure.

---

**References**

- Hermes CLI output (security scan) – reproduced verbatim in the issue body.
- Files flagged by the scanner: `benchmarks/run.py` (line 23) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (line 18).

title: fix(install): remap cavecrew agent tool names to Gemini ids on install
body:
## Problem

Installing caveman as a **Gemini CLI extension** fails to load all three `cavecrew` subagents:

```
[ExtensionManager] Error loading agent from caveman: Failed to load agent from
  ~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/cavecrew-builder.md:
  Validation failed: Agent Definition: tools.0: Invalid tool name ...
```

Gemini's `ExtensionManager` loads agents from the hardcoded `<ext>/agents/` path and validates every entry in an agent's `tools:` array with `isValidToolName(name, { allowWildcards: true })`, which only accepts Gemini's own builtin tool ids. The shipped `agents/cavecrew-*.md` use **Claude Code** tool names, so all entries are rejected and the agents never load. `model: haiku` is also Anthropic-only and fails at runtime.

Reproduces on every platform (verified against `@google/gemini-cli@0.44.1`). Tracked in #373, #473, #492.

## Why it's awkward

`agents/cavecrew-*.md` is a single source of truth **shared with the Claude Code plugin** (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `source: "./"`), which needs the Claude names. The two tool namespaces are disjoint, so the source files can't satisfy both — they must stay Claude-canonical.

## Fix

Rewrite the **installed copy** at Gemini-install time, exactly mirroring the opencode path's `stripOpencodeAgentTools`:

- New `bin/lib/gemini-agent.js` → `mapGeminiAgentFrontmatter()` maps tool names and `model: haiku`.
- `installGemini()` post-processes `~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/*.md` after a successful `gemini extensions install`.
- **Source `agents/*.md` are untouched** — Claude plugin behavior is unchanged.

Tool-name map (verified against the gemini-cli `ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES`):

| Claude | Gemini |
|---|---|
| `Read` | `read_file` |
| `Edit` | `replace` |
| `Write` | `write_file` |
| `Grep` | `grep_search` |
| `Glob` | `glob` |
| `Bash` | `run_shell_command` |

`model: haiku` → `gemini-2.5-flash` (sonnet/opus → `gemini-2.5-pro`). Unknown tool names pass through unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/installer/gemini-agent.test.mjs` — 10 new tests (inline-array mapping, `Bash`→`run_shell_command`, folded `description: >` preservation, unknown-name passthrough, non-string defensive, RED proof the shipped files carry Claude names today, GREEN proof they transform to Gemini-valid ids with byte-identical body, installer-equivalent end-to-end).

```
node --test tests/installer/*.test.mjs   ->  83 pass / 0 fail
```

## Known limitation

The patch runs through `bin/install.js`. A direct `gemini extensions install <url>` (without the caveman installer) won't be patched, and a Gemini auto-update re-clones the source tree and reverts it — same constraint as the opencode mirror. A fuller fix (CI-generated Gemini agent mirror) is noted in #473 option 1; this keeps the change small and focused per CONTRIBUTING.

title: fix(mode-tracker): honor off default in per-turn reinforcement
body:
## Problem

`CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=off` (env) / `defaultMode: "off"` (config) makes the **SessionStart** hook skip activation and delete the flag. But the **UserPromptSubmit** per-turn reinforcement in `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` read only the global flag file (`~/.caveman-active`) and never consulted the resolved default mode.

Because that flag is **global** (shared across all sessions/repos), a session in any other repo where caveman is on sets it to a non-off mode — and it then bleeds into repos/sessions that explicitly opted out, re-injecting `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (...)` on every turn. A per-repo / per-context off cannot be expressed when the per-turn check is flag-only.

## Fix

Bring the per-turn path in line with SessionStart: if `getDefaultMode() === 'off'`, clear the stale global flag and emit nothing. `getDefaultMode()` already reads env → config → default, so this respects per-context opt-out. No behavior change when caveman is genuinely active.

## Test

- env off + flag=full → no emit, stale flag cleared ✅
- env unset + flag=full → emits as before ✅
- `node --check` passes ✅

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: `caveman-compress` crashes on Windows with `charmap` codec error (Unicode characters)
body:
**What happen**

`caveman-compress` crashes with a `charmap` codec error when the target `.md` file contains non-ASCII Unicode characters (e.g. `→` U+2192, em-dash `—`). Python on Windows defaults to `cp1252` encoding instead of UTF-8.

Worse: the output file gets **truncated to 0 bytes** before the error surfaces. The `.original.md` backup is not yet written at that point. Result: original file is wiped with no recovery path.

```
Detected: natural_language
Starting caveman compression...

Processing: C:\path\to\CLAUDE.md
Compressing with Claude...

❌ Error: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '→' in position 4310: character maps to <undefined>
```

**Expected**

- Read and write files with explicit `encoding='utf-8'`
- On any error: report **before** writing — leave original untouched
- Write `.original.md` backup **before** any destructive write

**Before/after example**

```
Input:  .md file containing → (U+2192)
Got:    crash + file wiped to 0 bytes
Want:   either compress successfully (UTF-8 I/O) or fail safely with original intact
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

Installed as Claude Code plugin via superpowers. Invoked with `uv run python -m scripts <filepath>` (cpython-3.14-windows-x86_64). OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.

**Suggested fix**

Add `encoding='utf-8'` to all `open()` calls in `scripts/__main__.py`:

```python
# read
with open(filepath, encoding='utf-8') as f:
    content = f.read()

# write
with open(filepath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(compressed)
```

Workaround until fixed: set `PYTHONUTF8=1` env var.

title: fix(caveman-compress): add UTF-8 encoding to all file I/O
body:
Windows defaults to cp1252, crashing on non-ASCII chars (→ —) with "charmap" codec error and truncating the target file to 0 bytes.

- Add encoding='utf-8' to all read_text/write_text calls in compress.py, validate.py, and detect.py
- Add _atomic_write() (temp file + rename) to prevent truncation if a write fails mid-way
- Update test helpers and add unicode round-trip safety test

Closes #533

title: /caveman <level> doesn't switch mode — slash-command arg never reaches the flag
body:
**What happen**
<!-- What caveman do wrong -->
Running `/caveman ultra` (or any level) does nothing. The active-mode flag
`~/.claude/.caveman-active` is never updated, so the per-turn reinforcement keeps
injecting the previous/default level. Every `/caveman <level>` switch is a silent
no-op — the only thing that actually sets a level is `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE` /
`~/.config/caveman/config.json`.

**Expected**
<!-- What caveman should do -->
`/caveman ultra` sets the flag to `ultra` and persists, per SKILL.md
("Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`", "Level persist until changed or session end").

**Before/after example**

```
Input: /caveman ultra
Got:   flag ~/.claude/.caveman-active stays "full" (or prior default); reinforcement still says (full)
Want:  flag becomes "ultra"; reinforcement says (ultra)
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**
caveman plugin @ `655b7d9`, marketplace install. macOS, node v20.19.5.

---

**Root cause**
The `UserPromptSubmit` hook receives the slash-command *envelope* as `data.prompt`,
not a literal `/caveman ultra` string:

```
<command-message>caveman</command-message>
<command-name>/caveman</command-name>
<command-args>ultra</command-args>
```

`caveman-mode-tracker.js` gates arg parsing on `prompt.startsWith('/caveman')`. The
envelope starts with `<command-message>`, so that branch never runs and
`<command-args>ultra</command-args>` is never read → `safeWriteFlag` is never called →
flag left at the SessionStart default.

**Repro (self-contained, no live session)**
```bash
TD=$(mktemp -d); printf 'full' > "$TD/.caveman-active"
printf '%s' '{"prompt":"<command-message>caveman</command-message>\n<command-name>/caveman</command-name>\n<command-args>ultra</command-args>"}' \
  | CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$TD" node ~/.claude/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js >/dev/null
echo "flag after /caveman ultra = $(cat "$TD/.caveman-active" 2>/dev/null || echo DELETED)"
rm -rf "$TD"
# BUG: prints "full" (unchanged). Correct would print "ultra".
```

**Validation (not a session artifact)** — exact recorded payloads fed to the real hook
in an isolated temp `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, default pinned to `lite`, flag preset `full`, ×3:

| Payload to hook | flag after (×3) | result |
|---|---|---|
| literal `/caveman ultra` | `ultra, ultra, ultra` | arg path works |
| real command envelope | `full, full, full` | flag never updated |
| bare `/caveman` | `lite, lite, lite` | default path |
| full SKILL.md body | `deleted ×3` | hits deactivation regex |

Deterministic and input-isolated; envelope result matches observed real behavior.

**Proposed fix** — also parse the envelope:
```js
const nameM = /<command-name>\/(caveman[\w:-]*)<\/command-name>/i.exec(prompt);
const argsM = /<command-args>([^<]*)<\/command-args>/i.exec(prompt);
if (nameM && mode === null) {
  const cmd = '/' + nameM[1].toLowerCase();
  const arg = (argsM ? argsM[1] : '').trim().toLowerCase();
  // run cmd/arg through the existing switch that sets `mode`
}
```
(Keep the literal `startsWith('/caveman')` path for users who type it raw.)

**Workaround**
`~/.config/caveman/config.json` → `{ "defaultMode": "ultra" }`, or `export CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=ultra`.

title: compress: live file overwritten with un-validated output before validation → corrupted if interrupted (backup is out-of-tree)
body:
## Summary

`caveman-compress` writes the compressed (un-validated) LLM output to the **live source file** *before* it validates, then runs a validation/retry loop that makes additional slow `claude --print` calls. The original is only restored on the **final** validation failure. If the process is interrupted anywhere in that window — Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, crash, timeout, or an agent harness that backgrounds/kills the subprocess — the source file is left holding the un-validated/garbage output. The backup is stored **out-of-tree** (`~/.local/share/caveman-compress/backups/<parent>/<stem>.original.md`), so a user who doesn't know that path sees what looks like total data loss.

## Affected version

`skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py` at current `main` (commit `e8eae0ff…`, confirmed byte-identical to the installed plugin-cache copy). 342 lines.

## Root cause — `compress_file()`

- **line 313** `filepath.write_text(compressed)` — the **live file is overwritten with un-validated output here**, before any validation runs.
- **lines 316–340** — validation/retry loop; each retry calls `call_claude()` again (slow, network/subprocess).
- **line 331** `filepath.write_text(original_text)` — original is restored **only** on the *final* attempt's failure.
- **line 340** `filepath.write_text(compressed)` — writes the next (still un-validated) fix attempt to the live file.

Between line 313 and either a passing validation or the final restore, the live file is corrupt for as long as 1–2 extra Claude calls take (seconds to minutes). Any interruption in that window leaves the file corrupted, and the only intact copy is the out-of-tree backup.

## Secondary: pre-write guards don't catch a conversational LLM response

The guards only reject **empty** output (line 283) and output **identical to input** (line 290). They do **not** catch the case where the `claude --print` fallback returns a *chat-style summary* instead of the compressed body. Actual response that hit me:

> Compression complete. Natural-language prose compressed; all headings, links, file paths, inline code, URLs, and IDs preserved verbatim. Source-truncated entries (ending …) left unchanged.

That string is non-empty and ≠ input, so it passes both guards and is written as the file's entire new content. Validation then (correctly) fails — but the live file is already clobbered, and on interruption it stays clobbered.

## Reproduction

1. Run `python -m scripts <file.md>` on a real markdown file (e.g. a large memory index).
2. Have the `claude --print` fallback return a summary instead of the compressed body (model-dependent; more likely on large inputs), **or** interrupt the process during the validation loop.
3. Target file is now the summary/garbage; the only intact copy is the out-of-tree backup.

## Impact

Data corruption of the target file. Recovery requires knowing the undocumented out-of-tree backup location. In agent/automation contexts (the subprocess may be backgrounded or killed on timeout) the corrupt-on-interrupt window is easy to hit.

## Suggested fix

Never leave the live file in an un-validated state — compress + validate against a temp file, then **atomically replace** only after validation passes:

```python
import os
tmp = filepath.with_suffix(filepath.suffix + ".caveman.tmp")
tmp.write_text(compressed)
# run the validation + fix loop against tmp instead of filepath ...
if valid:
    os.replace(tmp, filepath)        # atomic; live file is never half-written
else:
    tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)      # live file untouched; nothing to restore
```

Optionally also reject pre-write outputs that don't contain the original's headings, or that are implausibly short relative to the input — that catches the summary-style response *before* any write.

This makes the out-of-tree backup a belt-and-suspenders safeguard rather than the only recovery path.

---

*Reported after hitting this on a ~38 KB memory index (the file was reduced to the 192-byte summary above; recovered from the out-of-tree backup). Happy to send a PR for the temp-file + atomic-replace change.*

title: Fix: CJK text immediately before a tool call can truncate the turn
body:
## Problem

When caveman is active and the user works in a **CJK language** (Chinese/Japanese/Korean), turns that include **tool calls** are frequently cut off at the tool-call boundary. The visible truncation always spans from a garbled fragment of the tool-call wrapper through `</invoke>` — i.e. the structured tool-call markup itself is corrupted/truncated, not the prose.

Key signals from a user report:

- Pure **English** workflows never truncate.
- Only **CJK + caveman + tool calls** truncates, with high frequency.
- A user-confirmed workaround — *work/narrate in English, write the CJK summary only after tools finish* — eliminated the truncation entirely.

## Root cause (best current understanding)

CJK characters placed immediately before a tool call abut the structured tool-call markup; the model's tool-call emission destabilizes at that boundary and the turn is cut. This is fundamentally a model/client tool-call-emission interaction with multibyte text — but **caveman is the trigger**, because it pushes the model to interleave terse CJK prose tightly against tool calls.

## Fix

Encode the confirmed workaround as a rule, so users do not have to discover/repeat it:

- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — never place CJK text immediately before a tool call; narrate around tools in English (or omit), write the CJK summary only after all tool calls finish.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` — same rule appended to the per-turn reinforcement, so it survives context compaction in long sessions.

Mitigation is from the skill side (steering prose/tool-call layout); it does not require any client change.

## Repro

1. Enable caveman (`full`), converse in Chinese.
2. Ask for a task needing several tool calls (write a file, run a command).
3. Observe the turn cut off at the tool-call boundary: CJK prose immediately followed by a truncated tool call.
4. Apply this patch (or the English-narration workaround) → no more truncation.

title: fix(hooks): handle stdin 'error' in mode-tracker (#538)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #538

`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` registered `process.stdin.on('data')` and
`on('end')` but had **no `on('error')` handler**. When stdin closes abnormally
(broken pipe, parent process crash, network interruption) Node emits an `error`
event on the stream; with no listener it becomes an **uncaught exception** and
the hook exits non-zero — a spurious hook failure under Claude Code's hook
system.

Fix: add a silent-fail `error` listener that exits `0`, consistent with the
hook contract (hooks must always exit 0 and never block the session). One line,
single concern, no behavior change on the normal path.

```js
process.stdin.on('error', () => process.exit(0));
```

## Test verification (RED → GREEN)

New standalone test `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js` loads the **real** hook
(`spawnSync` of `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js`) and emits an `error` on
`process.stdin` to simulate the abnormal close. No GitHub Actions test job runs
on PRs here, so the proof is local:

**RED** — prod fix reverted, test kept:

```
  ✗ stdin "error" event does not crash the hook (exit 0)
    expected clean exit on stdin error, got status=1 signal=null
    stderr: throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event ... Error: EPIPE (simulated)
1 passed, 1 failed
```

**GREEN** — fix applied:

```
  ✓ stdin "error" event does not crash the hook (exit 0)
  ✓ normal stdin (valid JSON + clean EOF) still exits 0
2 passed, 0 failed
```

A second case asserts the new listener leaves the normal `data`/`end` path
untouched (valid JSON in → clean EOF → exit 0).

## No regression

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `npm test` | 73 pass, 0 fail |
| `python3 -m unittest tests.test_hooks` | 4 pass |
| `node tests/test_symlink_flag.js` | 12 pass |
| `node tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js` | 2 pass (new) |

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` | add `stdin.on('error')` silent-fail handler |
| `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js` | new — RED→GREEN coverage for the handler |

title: fix(caveman-stats): read desktop session logs, CWD-scope CLI, fall through empty transcript
body:
## Problem

`/caveman-stats` reported **"No conversation yet"** even deep into active sessions. Three independent causes:

### 1. Desktop app sessions are never found (main bug)
The Claude **desktop app** ("host loop") does NOT write the CLI's `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl` transcript. It writes a live, per-turn audit log at:
```
~/.config/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/<acct>/<space>/local_<id>/audit.jsonl
```
`findRecentSession` only scanned `~/.claude/projects/`, so on the desktop app there was no file to read. Verified across **115 audit.jsonl files / 862 result entries** on a live install (`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `total_cost_usd`, `session_id` present 100%).

### 2. CLI fallback picked the wrong project (latent)
`findRecentSession` walked **all** `~/.claude/projects/**` and picked the globally newest `.jsonl` by mtime — a busy sibling project shadowed the active session.

### 3. Empty transcript_path masked discovery
The UserPromptSubmit hook forwards the harness `transcript_path` as `--session-file`. On the desktop app that path can point at an empty / not-yet-written file (the live session isn't flushed to disk), so trusting it unconditionally produced "No conversation yet" and skipped the audit.jsonl discovery entirely.

## Fix (`src/hooks/caveman-stats.js`)

**Desktop discovery:** `auditFromCwd()` (exact current session via cwd walk-up), `newestDesktopAudit()` (recency fallback), `desktopSessionsRoot()` (`~/.config/Claude`, override `CLAUDE_DESKTOP_DIR`, kept separate from CLI's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), `newerFile()` (CLI vs desktop by recency).

**Dual-format `parseSession()`:** desktop `audit.jsonl` carries 1–83 `type=="result"` entries with cumulative per-run usage; the interleaved `type=="assistant"` entries are streaming snapshots (`output_tokens≈1`) that must NOT be summed. Sum the result entries, derive model from `modelUsage` keys (strip `[1m]` marker), count error runs. CLI assistant-summing unchanged.

**Candidate fall-through in `main()`:** build an ordered candidate list (explicit arg → cwd desktop audit → newer of CLI/desktop) and keep the FIRST candidate with `turns > 0`. A real transcript still wins immediately; an empty `transcript_path` no longer hides the live audit log.

**Also:** `priceForModel()` strips `[1m]` before rate-card match; history keyed by result `session_id`; CLI lookup CWD-scoped before the global walk.

## Test
`node tests/test_caveman_stats.js` → **31 passed, 0 failed.** Added desktop result-entry coverage (snapshot exclusion, `[1m]` strip, error runs, `session_id`) and CLI-unchanged assertion; isolated `CLAUDE_DESKTOP_DIR` in the no-session test. Verified through the real hook path (mode-tracker → stats) with an empty `transcript_path` → renders real usage:
```
Turns: 17 · Output: 5,681 · Cache-read: 883,239 · ~$0.264 (claude-opus-4-8)
```

## Known limitation
A claude.ai **remote-control** (web-bridged) session writes no local transcript, so stats fall through to the most recent desktop/CLI session rather than that exact chat. Normal desktop host-loop and CLI sessions both work.

title: feat: add auto-activation hooks for Codex CLI
Claude Code: .claude-plugin/plugin.json missing "skills": "./skills/" → skills never register (only hooks load)
body:
## Summary

On **Claude Code**, the plugin installs and the hook works (SessionStart "Loading caveman mode…" fires, terse mode activates, `~/.claude/.caveman-active=full`), but **none of the skills register**. `/caveman:caveman`, `/caveman:caveman-compress`, `/caveman:caveman-stats`, `/caveman:caveman-review`, `/caveman:caveman-help`, `/caveman:cavecrew` all return `Unknown command`, and none appear in the skill list / `/reload-skills`.

So on Claude Code only the **hooks** load — the documented per-session skills/commands don't.

## Root cause

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares `hooks` but **omits the `skills` path**, so Claude Code's plugin loader never discovers the `skills/` directory — even though it contains valid `SKILL.md` files (caveman, caveman-compress, caveman-stats, caveman-review, caveman-help, cavecrew).

Claude Code plugins must declare the skills directory in the manifest. Compare two plugins whose skills DO register:

- `omo` (sisyphuslabs): `"skills": "./skills/"`
- `context-mode` (mksglu): `"skills": "./skills/"`
- `caveman`: **missing**

`marketplace.json` correctly points the plugin at `"source": "./"`, so the root `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is the one that loads — it's just incomplete.

## Repro

1. `claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman && claude plugin install caveman@caveman`
2. Restart Claude Code (new session).
3. `/caveman:caveman` → `Unknown command: /caveman:caveman`; `/reload-skills` shows no caveman skills.
4. Yet the SessionStart hook + `.caveman-active` flag work — confirming only hooks load, not skills.

## Fix (one line)

Add to `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
"skills": "./skills/",
```

After this + a session restart, the skills register as `/caveman:*`. Verified locally by patching the cached manifest — the six `skills/*/SKILL.md` then load correctly.

## Environment

- Claude Code, plugin installed via marketplace (`source: "./"`)
- caveman `main` (cached commit `25d22f8`)

title: Add Bun support as an alternative installer runtime
body:
## Feature request: Support Bun as an installation runtime

### Problem

The Windows installer currently requires **Node.js ≥18**:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

I use **Bun** as my JavaScript runtime and package manager, and I do not have Node.js/npm installed. Bun can run most Node-compatible JavaScript/TypeScript tooling and provides equivalents for common workflows such as `npx` via `bunx`.

Because the installer explicitly checks for Node, users who use Bun-only environments cannot install Caveman even when Bun could execute the required scripts.

### Requested change

Please add Bun as a supported installation runtime.

Possible approaches:

1. Detect Bun when `node` is unavailable:

   ```powershell
   Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
   ```

2. Accept either runtime:

   * Node.js ≥18, or
   * a recent Bun version

3. Use the detected runtime to run the installer:

   * Node: `node ...`
   * Bun: `bun ...`

4. Where package execution is needed, use:

   * `npx` for Node installations
   * `bunx` for Bun installations

### Why this would help

* Supports users who intentionally use Bun-only development environments.
* Avoids requiring a second JavaScript runtime solely to install Caveman.
* Makes installation more portable on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
* Bun compatibility could be documented as experimental initially if there are edge cases.

### Acceptance criteria

* The installer succeeds when Node.js is absent but Bun is installed.
* Existing Node.js-based installation remains unchanged.
* The documentation lists Bun as an alternative prerequisite/runtime.
* If Bun is unsupported for a specific agent integration, the installer clearly reports that limitation rather than failing with a generic Node requirement.

Thanks for considering it.

title: Claude Code: /caveman slash commands not discovered (commands shipped as .toml, Claude Code expects .md)
body:
## Bug

`bash install.sh` reports success on macOS but `/caveman` slash commands not discoverable in Claude Code.

## Root cause

`commands/*.toml` is the OpenCode/Codex format. Claude Code only scans `commands/*.md` with YAML frontmatter (see https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/slash-commands#custom-slash-commands).

After install:
```
~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/<sha>/commands/
  caveman.toml         <- ignored by Claude Code
  caveman-commit.toml
  caveman-review.toml
  caveman-init.toml
```

Plugin manifest at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares hooks correctly (those fire on SessionStart as expected), but ships no `commands` array and no `.md` files, so `/caveman` returns "Unknown command".

## Repro

```
git clone https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman.git
cd caveman && bash install.sh
# new Claude Code session
/caveman
# -> Unknown command
```

## Workaround

Convert TOML to MD post-install. `{{args}}` -> `$ARGUMENTS` (Claude convention):

```bash
CMD_DIR=~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/*/commands
for f in $CMD_DIR/*.toml; do
  python3 -c "
import re, sys
text = open('$f').read()
m = {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'(\w+)\s*=\s*\"(.*)\"', text)}
md = f'---\ndescription: {m[\"description\"]}\n---\n\n{m[\"prompt\"].replace(\"{{args}}\", \"\$ARGUMENTS\")}\n'
open('$f'.replace('.toml', '.md'), 'w').write(md)
"
done
```

Restart session -> `/caveman` works.

## Fix suggestion

Either:
1. Ship `commands/*.md` alongside the TOMLs for Claude Code targets, OR
2. Have `bin/install.js` emit MDs from TOMLs when target is `claude`/`claude-code`

Option 2 keeps single source of truth (the TOMLs) while wiring up Claude Code properly.

## Env

- macOS 15.5 (Darwin 25.5.0)
- Node v22.22.0
- Claude Code (latest)
- caveman @ commit 25d22f864ad68cc447a4cb93aefde918aa4aec9f

## Side note

Install completed without warning. Maybe a post-install verification step that checks each registered agent's expected command format would have caught this — `installed: claude` was reported but `/caveman` is silently broken.

title: [Bug] Multiple token-compression plugins conflict — caveman + ponytail/other compression skills inject contradictory style instructions
body:
## Problem

When caveman and another token-compression skill (e.g. ponytail) are both active, they both inject `additionalContext` on the `UserPromptSubmit` hook event. The model receives **two contradictory style instruction sets** in the same turn, causing inconsistent output — sometimes terse, sometimes verbose, sometimes a confusing mix.

## Reproduction

1. Install caveman (full mode) and ponytail (full mode) — both are popular Claude Code plugins
2. Start a session — both hooks fire on `UserPromptSubmit`
3. Observe the model receives:
   - From caveman: `"CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full). Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. Code/commits/security: write normal."`
   - From ponytail: `"PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full. The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation."`
4. Model behavior becomes unpredictable — sometimes follows caveman rules, sometimes ponytail rules, sometimes both partially

## Root Cause

`caveman-mode-tracker.js` (line 122-132) unconditionally emits `additionalContext` when caveman is active, without checking whether another compression plugin is already injecting competing style rules. Same for `caveman-activate.js` (line 91) which emits the full ruleset on `SessionStart`.

There is no conflict detection or de-escalation mechanism.

## Related but Different

- #184 addresses the `.caveman-active` **flag file** being global (per-session file lock conflict)
- This issue addresses the **output semantics** — two compression instruction sets competing for the model's attention in the same turn

## Suggested Fix

In `caveman-activate.js` and `caveman-mode-tracker.js`, before injecting compression rules:

1. **Detect** known conflicting plugins by checking `settings.json` for registered plugins (ponytail, grill-me, etc.) or scanning `CLAUDE.md` for their characteristic markers
2. **De-escalate**: if a conflicting compression plugin is detected, either:
   - Skip caveman's injection entirely (let the other plugin handle compression), or
   - Reduce to a minimal one-liner instead of the full ruleset, or
   - Emit a warning that both are active and suggest the user pick one
3. **Document** the interaction in README — list known conflicting plugins and recommended coexistence strategy

## Environment

- caveman v18e45320 (latest)
- Claude Code with both caveman + ponytail plugins installed
- macOS, Node.js v22

title: [Bug] CJK/Chinese text — ARTICLES regex deletes English articles that carry semantic weight in mixed-language context
fix(shrink): skip ARTICLES removal in CJK-mixed text
fix(tracker): reduce per-turn injection when competing compression plugin detected
body:
## Problem

When caveman and another token-compression plugin (e.g. ponytail) are both active, they both inject `additionalContext` on `UserPromptSubmit`. The model receives two contradictory style instruction sets, causing unpredictable output.

## Fix

In `caveman-mode-tracker.js`, before emitting the per-turn `additionalContext`, check `settings.json` for known compression plugins (ponytail, grill-me, grilling). If a conflict is detected:

- **Reduce** the per-turn injection to a one-liner: `"CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full) — reduced injection (another compression plugin detected). Caveman rules still apply per SessionStart injection."`
- **Skip** the full style reminder to avoid competing with the other plugin's per-turn injection
- The **SessionStart full ruleset is unchanged** — caveman rules still apply, just the per-turn reinforcement is reduced

Detection checks `settings.json` `installed_plugins` and `permissions` keys for known compression plugin IDs.

## Trade-off

This is a **conservative approach** — caveman still activates and its SessionStart ruleset is still injected, but the per-turn reinforcement is reduced when a conflict is detected. The alternative (disabling caveman entirely) would lose the SessionStart ruleset, which is too aggressive.

## Testing

With ponytail installed in settings.json:
- Before: model receives both `"CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full). Drop articles/filler..."` and `"PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE (full). The ladder enforced..."` every turn
- After: model receives `"CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full) — reduced injection"` + ponytail's full injection = no contradiction

Fixes #574

title: fix(hooks): prevent safeWriteFlag temp-file leak on Windows rename co…
body:
…ntention

safeWriteFlag wrote a temp file then renameSync'd it onto the flag path to publish atomically. On Windows, renameSync onto an existing target throws EPERM/EBUSY/EEXIST/EACCES when a concurrent session or the statusline holds the flag open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE. The catch swallowed the error and left the temp file orphaned, so .caveman-active.<pid>.<ts> files accumulated in the config dir (64 found under the multi-session Claude desktop app).

Hoist tempPath to an outer scope, retry the rename a few times to ride out brief lock contention, and always unlink the temp file in a finally so no litter is left regardless of outcome. Concurrent writers publish the same mode value, so a missed write is harmless. Update checksums.sha256 to match.

title: feat: input-side token-saving upgrades + eval quality gate
body:
## Why

In agentic Claude Code the weekly token limit is dominated by **input** — the whole context (system prompt, tool schemas, prior prose, every tool result) is re-sent every turn; caveman's output compression is the smallest slice. These changes target the input side and add a quality gate so compression never silently trades away correctness. A token saved on the re-sent prefix is re-billed every later turn (compounds); a token saved on output is billed once.

## What

**1. Agentic-loop output discipline + gated reinforcement + one-shot nudge** (`24c8e03`)
- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`: new `## Agentic Loop` section — result-first, no recap of files just read, plan once then deltas, one intent clause per tool batch. Cross-references Auto-Clarity so security/irreversible/multi-step stay full prose.
- `caveman-mode-tracker.js`: per-turn reinforcement now fires every 3rd turn (+ on mode (re)activation), not every turn — the counter lives in a separate flag file so the injected string stays byte-stable and keeps hitting the prompt cache.
- `caveman-activate.js`: statusline-setup nudge is one-shot (a `.caveman-nudged` marker) instead of re-appending ~90 tokens to the cached SessionStart prefix every session.

**2. Eval quality gate — fidelity axis + two-gate accept rule** (`5681437`, `5c7e19a`)
- `measure.py` only counts tokens, which is gameable (a skill replying `k` scores -99% and "wins"). Adds `evals/judge.py` (LLM judge for rubric facts + deterministic verbatim check -> `fidelity.json`) and `evals/gate.py` (accept only if tokens hold AND fidelity holds; high-risk prompts like the git-rebase "rewrites history" warning allow zero fidelity loss).
- `evals/prompts/rubrics.json` for all 10 prompts; a committed `fidelity.json` baseline; `tests/test_eval_gate.py` (incl. the canonical "reply k -> REJECT"); `.github/workflows/eval-gate.yml`.

**3. Opt-in PostToolUse tool-result trim** (`de7da10`)
- `caveman-trim-tool-result.js`: when enabled, replaces oversized Read/Bash/Grep/Glob results (via the public `updatedToolOutput`) with a deterministic, lossless-first trimmed version before they enter context. OFF by default (`CAVEMAN_TRIM_TOOL_RESULTS=1`); wired via `--with-trim`, independent of the plugin (no double-fire).

**4. cavecrew as the default locate route** (`e2e7076`)
- Nudge the main thread to delegate locate-shaped work to `cavecrew-investigator` (its verbose Grep/Read stays out of main context); cap investigator/reviewer output at 25 rows.

**5. Structural ultra + honest input/output split in /caveman-stats** (`b01efd3`)
- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`: the `ultra` level now collapses multi-sentence explanation into one causal chain and cuts transition sentences (not just word abbreviation), keeping the verbatim code-symbol/error-string exemption.
- `caveman-stats.js`: `/caveman-stats` reports the input-vs-output token split — output is the demo, input is where the weekly budget goes — and points at the input-side levers. Number formatting pinned to `en-US` so output is locale-deterministic.

## Testing
- `tests/test_hook_output.js` (8), `tests/test_trim_tool_result.js` (15), `tests/test_eval_gate.py` (7), `tests/test_caveman_stats.js` (31) all pass.
- Trim hook adversarially reviewed (determinism, data corruption, fail-open) — no issues.
- Gate verified end-to-end on the committed snapshot: caveman saves ~50% tokens at 100% fidelity.

## Notes
- Clean-room: hook mechanisms are from the public Claude Code hook docs.
- The Windows `safeWriteFlag` temp-leak fix is a separate PR (#578) — this branch deliberately leaves `caveman-config.js` untouched.
- `fidelity.json` was judged inline (an authenticated `claude -p` was unavailable in the author's environment); regenerate with `evals/judge.py` once CLI auth is set up.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(windows): Bun runtime, PowerShell robustness, path/encoding + 3 more fixes
body:
Adds Bun as first-class runtime (>=1.3.14) and fixes 12 Windows-specific issues:
 
### Shell / Installer
- Rename `$Args` → `$InstallerArgs` in install.ps1 to avoid PowerShell automatic-variable collision (#366, #439, #440, #518)
- Guard `$MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path` against null in pipe mode so `irm ... | iex` doesn't crash (#546, #565)
- Add Bun runtime support — works standalone or alongside Node (#570)
- Fix Node at `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` not being quoted in spawn (#461)
 
### MSYS / Git Bash
- Convert MSYS paths (`/c/Users/...`) to Windows paths (`c:/Users/...`) in Claude Code hook commands so Node resolves them on Git Bash (#199)
 
### caveman-compress
- Pin all `read_text`/`write_text` calls to `encoding="utf-8"` to prevent charmap codec crash on Windows cp1252 (#533)
- Reconfigure stdout/stderr to UTF-8 in benchmark.py for ✅/❌ glyphs
 
### Cavecrew agents
- Remove `tools:` and `model:` from agent YAML frontmatter so Gemini CLI can load them; tool restrictions already expressed in prose (#473)
 
### caveman-shrink
- Loop sentinel restoration until stable so nested protected segments (enum values like `(STARTER/BUSINESS)`) aren't left as numeric placeholders (#444)
 
### CI
- Add Node.js test workflow for installer tests

title: Install Caveman through GitHub Copilot CLI
body:
Running the Caveman installer on a machine with the standalone GitHub Copilot CLI fails because `copilot-cli` is unknown. The existing Copilot path handles only the editor extension, so users do not get the CLI's native Caveman commands and skills.

This adds a separate provider that verifies the CLI exposes plugin commands, so AWS Copilot is not mistaken for GitHub Copilot. It installs directly from `JuliusBrussee/caveman`, re-enables a disabled direct install, and reports uninstall failures.

`--with-init` still writes repo instructions to activate the voice. It also merges the Caveman marketplace and enabled plugin into `.github/copilot/settings.json`. Existing keys and marketplace fields survive. Malformed, commented, conflicting, or symlinked settings are left untouched, and writes use randomized exclusive temporary files.

The plugin supplies skills and commands. Caveman ships no compatible Copilot hook manifest, so plugin installation alone still requires `/caveman`; repo instructions provide automatic activation.

Refs https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/384

## Testing

A real plugin install was not run because enterprise policy permits only approved plugins. The public CLI help confirms direct repository installs; the installer path was exercised without side effects, and the repository settings write ran against a temporary directory.

```console
# upstream/main
$ node bin/install.js --only copilot-cli --force --dry-run --skip-skills --no-mcp-shrink --non-interactive --no-color
error: unknown agent: copilot-cli
before_exit=2

# this branch
$ node bin/install.js --only copilot-cli --force --dry-run --skip-skills --no-mcp-shrink --non-interactive --no-color
→ GitHub Copilot CLI detected
would run: copilot plugin install JuliusBrussee/caveman
installed:
  • copilot-cli

$ copilot plugin install --help
Usage: copilot plugin install [options] <source>
  owner/repo  Install from a GitHub repository

$ mkdir /tmp/caveman-584-init-e2e
$ node src/tools/caveman-init.js /tmp/caveman-584-init-e2e --only copilot-cli
+ .github/copilot/settings.json (added)

$ cat /tmp/caveman-584-init-e2e/.github/copilot/settings.json
{"extraKnownMarketplaces":{"caveman":{"source":{"source":"github","repo":"JuliusBrussee/caveman"}}},"enabledPlugins":{"caveman@caveman":true}}

$ npm test
# tests 184, pass 180, fail 0, skipped 4
$ node tests/test_caveman_init.js
22 passed, 0 failed
$ node tests/test_symlink_flag.js
15 passed, 0 failed
```

title: SessionStart hook falls back to stale hardcoded ruleset — SKILL.md path off by one directory level
body:
## Bug

`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` tries to read the live `SKILL.md` to build the SessionStart ruleset, but the computed path is off by one directory level for a `claude plugin install` layout, so it silently falls back to the hardcoded (stale) ruleset every session.

```js
// src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
skillContent = fs.readFileSync(
  path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8'
);
```

Plugin layout actually installed via the marketplace (`claude plugin install caveman@caveman`) is:

```
<plugin_root>/
├── src/hooks/caveman-activate.js   ← __dirname
└── skills/caveman/SKILL.md
```

`plugin.json` invokes the hook as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, so `__dirname` is `<plugin_root>/src/hooks`. `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', ...)` resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, which doesn't exist (no `src/skills/` directory). `readFileSync` throws, gets swallowed by the `catch`, and the hook silently uses the hardcoded fallback ruleset baked into the script — missing everything added to `SKILL.md` since that fallback text was last hand-copied (e.g. the "Preserve user's dominant language" rule, the "No self-reference" rule, the Intensity table, the wenyan examples).

The comment above the read even documents the *intended* layout as `__dirname = <plugin_root>/hooks/` (one level up from plugin root), which doesn't match the actual `src/hooks/` path used by `plugin.json`.

## Fix

```diff
- path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8'
+ path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8'
```

Verified locally: with the fix, `node src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` (run with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` pointing at the real installed plugin cache dir) now emits the current `SKILL.md` content (Intensity table, etc.) instead of the fallback text.

## Repro

```bash
claude plugin install caveman@caveman
# then, simulating the hook's own resolution:
node -e "console.log(require('path').join('<plugin_root>/src/hooks', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'))"
# -> <plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md   (doesn't exist)
```

Found while setting up caveman across Claude Code / Opencode / Codex on the same machine — noticed Claude Code's SessionStart context was missing rules present in the checked-out `SKILL.md`.

title: caveman-compress: fix-retry pass leaks LLM preamble into output file
body:
## Bug

`skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py`'s validation-retry path writes the raw LLM response straight to disk with no leak check, letting Claude's chain-of-thought preamble get committed into the compressed file.

## Where

`compress_file()`:

1. First pass — `call_claude(build_compress_prompt(body))` — response is passed through `strip_llm_wrapper()`, which only strips an outer ` ```markdown ` fence.
2. If `validate()` fails (missing URL/heading/code block), the fix-retry path calls `call_claude(build_fix_prompt(...))` and writes the result directly:

```python
compressed = call_claude(
    build_fix_prompt(original_text, compressed, result.errors)
)
filepath.write_text(compressed)
```

No `strip_llm_wrapper()` (or any other leak stripping) is applied to this second call's output.

`build_fix_prompt` tells the model "Return ONLY the fixed compressed file. No explanation." — but the model doesn't always comply, and sometimes prepends a sentence like:

```
The file I need to fix is the COMPRESSED file passed in the prompt — I'll work directly from it. Two fixes needed:
1. ...
2. ...
The task says to return only the fixed compressed file, so here it is:

---
name: '...'
...
```

That whole preamble gets written verbatim into the target file, ahead of the real YAML frontmatter / heading.

## Why validation doesn't catch it

`validate()` only checks structural invariants — URLs present, headings match, code blocks match. The leaked preamble doesn't remove any required content, it just prepends garbage before it, so validation passes on the corrupted file.

## Impact

Hit 4 out of 42 files compressed in one run (~10%) — every file that failed first-pass validation and went through the fix-retry path got the leaked-preamble bug. Corrupted files had broken YAML frontmatter (delimiter no longer on line 1) plus visible model self-talk in the rendered instructions.

## Suggested fix

Apply the same defensive stripping to the fix-retry response as the first pass, plus a stronger check specific to this path — e.g. reject/retry if the first non-blank line of the fixed output doesn't match one of the original's first non-blank lines (frontmatter delimiter or top-level heading).

## Repro

Run `caveman-compress` on any file that fails first-pass validation (e.g. missing a URL or heading) — the fix-retry call is where the leak occurs.

title: SessionStart hook path off-by-one — SKILL.md not found, silently falls back to English-only ruleset
body:
**What happen**
`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` reads SKILL.md via `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')`. Hook file lives at `<plugin_root>/src/hooks/`, so this resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — doesn't exist. Real file is `<plugin_root>/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, one level further up. `readFileSync` fails, caught silently (empty `catch` at line 58), falls back to hardcoded ruleset baked into the hook — which is missing the "Preserve user's dominant language" rule that exists in the real SKILL.md. Result: every Claude Code plugin install replies in English caveman regardless of the user's language, even though SKILL.md says otherwise.

**Expected**
Hook finds real SKILL.md, so language-preservation (and any other rule added since the fallback was last hand-copied) actually applies.

**Before/after example**
```

Got:   caveman reply in English
Want:  caveman reply in Portuguese (per SKILL.md "Preserve user's dominant language" rule)
```

Claude Code plugin (marketplace install). Confirmed on current `main` as of commit `1ce38a2295186e4fe5f5ed0c72853e0ee2de2c27`.

**Fix**
Line 56: `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')` → `path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')`.

title: fix(hooks): resolve SKILL.md path from src/hooks correctly
body:
## Summary

- `readFileSync` failed, caught silently, and the hook fell back to the hardcoded ruleset — which is missing rules added to `SKILL.md` since (e.g. "Preserve user's dominant language"), so every plugin install replied in English regardless of the user's language.

title: fix(hooks): SessionStart SKILL.md path off-by-one
body:
## What happen

`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` read SKILL.md via `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')`. `plugin.json` invokes the hook as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, so `__dirname` is `<plugin_root>/src/hooks` and the path resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — doesn't exist. The `readFileSync` failure is swallowed by the empty `catch`, so **every plugin install silently used the stale hardcoded fallback ruleset** — missing the "Preserve user's dominant language" rule, the "No self-reference" rule, and the intensity table.

Fixes #587, fixes #589.

## Fix

Instead of only flipping `'..'` → `'..', '..'`, resolve SKILL.md from candidates in order:

1. `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` when invoking plugin hooks; authoritative when present
2. `__dirname/../../skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — plugin layout (`src/hooks/`) and repo checkouts
3. `__dirname/../skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — standalone installs with hooks at `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks/` and the skill at `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/caveman/` (the old path, which was correct for this layout)

All misses still fall through to the fallback; silent-fail behavior preserved (hooks never block session start).

Also syncs the two rules both issues flagged into the fallback ruleset, so standalone installs with no SKILL.md anywhere still get language preservation + no-self-reference.

## Tests

Three regression tests in `tests/test_hooks.py`:
- repo/plugin layout: output contains the `## Intensity` table (never in fallback), filtered to the active level's row only
- standalone layout: hook copied to `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks/` finds a marker SKILL.md at `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/caveman/`
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` takes priority when set

All 7 hook tests pass; full `tests/verify_repo.py` suite passes. Manually verified a simulated plugin invocation now emits the real SKILL.md with correct level filtering for `full` and `ultra`.

title: install.js: spawn ENOENT treated as success — missing claude CLI reports "installed", skips standalone-hook fallback, nothing installed
body:
**What happen**

On a machine where the `claude` CLI is not on PATH, `node bin/install.js --only claude --non-interactive` reports success and installs **nothing** — no plugin, no hooks, no settings.json. Worse, the standalone-hook fallback is skipped because the installer believes the plugin install succeeded.

Verified in a clean `node:20-bookworm` Docker container (no `claude` binary, `HOME=/root` empty):

```
→ Claude Code detected
  $ claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman
  $ claude plugin install caveman@caveman
  hooks: plugin manifest handles SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit
🪨 done
  installed:
    • claude
```

Afterwards: `~/.claude/` does not exist at all.

**Root cause**

`spawnSync` on ENOENT returns `{ status: null, error: Error }`. `bin/install.js:445` coerces that to success:

```js
if ((r1.status || 0) === 0 && (r2.status || 0) === 0) {   // null || 0 === 0 → "success"
```

So `pluginInstallSucceeded = true`, and the hook-wiring decision matrix (issue #392 logic) takes the "plugin manifest handles hooks" branch — the exact fallback built for this situation never fires.

The `(r.status || 0) === 0` pattern appears at 8 sites: `bin/install.js:445` (claude), `:537` (gemini), `:558` (all npx-skills providers), `:946`, `:965`, `:977` (init), `:1081` (uninstall), `:1355` (skills-auto). Every one converts "binary not found / spawn failed" into success.

**Expected**

Spawn failure = install failure: report `claude` as failed, fall back to standalone hook wiring (which works offline from the local clone), exit non-zero.

**Fix**

```js
const spawnOk = (r) => !r.error && r.status === 0;
```
and use it at all 8 sites.

**Platform**: Linux (node:20-bookworm container), repro is OS-independent. main @ 25d22f8.

title: uninstall deletes unrelated user hooks whose command merely contains the substring "caveman"
body:
**What happen**

`node bin/install.js --uninstall` deletes **any** hook entry in `settings.json` whose command string contains the substring `caveman` anywhere — including hooks that have nothing to do with this project.

`bin/install.js:1052` calls `removeCavemanHooks(settings, 'caveman')`, and `bin/lib/settings.js:157-174` matches by `command.includes('caveman')`.

**Repro (confirmed)**

User-authored hook in settings.json:

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "node /Users/me/Projects/caveman-notes/my-hook.js" }
```

Run `--uninstall` → "removed 1 caveman hook entry" — the user's unrelated PreToolUse hook is gone. Any path/repo/username containing "caveman" (including a clone of this very repo used in a hook) triggers deletion.

**Expected**

Uninstall removes only hooks this installer manages. The codebase already has the right pattern: `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks` (`bin/lib/settings.js:249-259`) deliberately matches exact basenames from `MANAGED_HOOK_BASENAMES` to avoid this exact problem.

**Fix**

Make `removeCavemanHooks` match on `MANAGED_HOOK_BASENAMES` (caveman-activate.js / caveman-mode-tracker.js / caveman-statusline.*) instead of a substring.

title: opencode: --force on legacy AGENTS.md replaces the whole file — user content destroyed, and the installer's own hint steers users into it
body:
**What happen**

For opencode, when `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` contains the legacy un-fenced sentinel, the installer prints:

> re-run with `--force` to replace it with a fenced block

But `--force` executes a **full-file replace** (`bin/install.js:707-716`: `fs.writeFileSync(agentsMd, fencedBlock)`). Everything the user wrote in AGENTS.md above/below the legacy block is destroyed. No backup is taken.

**Repro (confirmed)**

```
# My precious user rules
Always use tabs.

Respond terse like smart caveman. ...   <- legacy sentinel
```

→ `--force` → file now contains **only** the fenced caveman block. User rules gone.

Note `--help` describes `--force` as merely "Re-run even if a target reports already installed" — nothing warns it rewrites user files. The installer actively steers users with mixed legacy files into data loss.

**Expected**

Replace only the legacy caveman block in place (or append fenced block + strip just the sentinel paragraph), and/or write a `.bak` before any destructive rewrite.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: settings.js: stripJsonComments trailing-comma sweep corrupts string values containing ,} or ,]
body:
**What happen**

`stripJsonComments` in `bin/lib/settings.js` ends with a trailing-comma sweep that runs over the whole output **including string contents** (`bin/lib/settings.js:62`):

```js
out.replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1')
```

The comment above claims this is safe after comment-stripping; it isn't — string bodies survive comment-stripping intact.

**Repro (confirmed)**

```jsonc
{ "cmd": "echo ,}", // comment
}
```

parses to `"cmd": "echo }"` — the comma inside the quoted string is silently deleted. Any JSONC settings whose string values contain `,}` or `,]` (shell brace expansion `file{,}`, inline JSON passed to a hook, jq/awk snippets) is corrupted on read — and then **persisted corrupted** by `writeSettings` on the next install/uninstall.

It only triggers for files that fail strict `JSON.parse` first, i.e. real JSONC files — exactly the files this module exists to protect.

**Fix**

Do the trailing-comma removal in the same character-scan that already tracks in-string state for comment stripping, instead of a global regex afterward.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: openclaw: stray begin marker in SOUL.md → duplicate bootstrap on install, user content deleted on uninstall
body:
**What happen**

`bin/lib/openclaw.js` append/strip of the SOUL.md bootstrap block can destroy user content when the file contains a stray or truncated begin marker:

1. `appendBootstrapToSoul` (`openclaw.js:119-133`) treats the block as present only if **both** markers exist. With `<!-- caveman-begin -->` present but no end marker (interrupted write, partial user edit), it appends a **second** full block.
2. `stripBootstrapFromSoul` (`openclaw.js:135-155`) then cuts from the **first** `caveman-begin` to the **first** `caveman-end` — which now spans everything between the stray marker and the appended block's end marker.

**Repro (confirmed)**

SOUL.md: truncated begin marker, then `USER IMPORTANT CONTENT`. Install → second block appended. Uninstall → entire file deleted including the user content (`{"changed":true,"removed":true}`).

Idempotency violation → data loss chain. The same single-span strip pattern is duplicated for the opencode AGENTS.md fence at `bin/install.js:1148-1162`.

**Fix**

Treat a lone begin marker as "present but damaged" (repair in place rather than append), and strip marker pairs iteratively/pairwise rather than first-begin→first-end.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: caveman-shrink: package.json files omits spawn-options.js — next npm publish ships a package that crashes on launch
body:
**What happen**

The next `npm publish` of `caveman-shrink` will ship a package that crashes on every launch.

`src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/package.json:26-30`:

```json
"files": ["index.js", "compress.js", "README.md"]
```

but `index.js:43` does `require('./spawn-options')` — and `spawn-options.js` is not in `files`.

Verified with `npm pack --dry-run`: tarball contains only 4 files, no `spawn-options.js` → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at startup.

**Compounding**

Registry `caveman-shrink@0.1.0` is stale — its published `index.js` predates the Windows `getSpawnOptions` fix (verified by diffing the downloaded tarball against repo source) — yet the repo `version` is still `0.1.0`. So `npx -y caveman-shrink` users (the exact wiring `bin/install.js --with-mcp-shrink` writes) still get the old Windows-broken spawn, and the fix cannot be published without a version bump anyway.

**Fix**

Add `spawn-options.js` to `files`, bump to `0.1.1`, republish.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: mode tracker: NL triggers misfire — "turn caveman mode off" ACTIVATES and downgrades level, "turn caveman off" is a no-op
body:
**What happen**

The natural-language activation/deactivation regexes in `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` misfire in several confirmed ways (all reproduced by piping `{"prompt": ...}` into the hook and checking the flag file):

| Prompt | Expected | Got |
|---|---|---|
| `turn caveman mode off` (flag=`ultra`) | flag deleted | flag **overwritten to `full`** — deactivation request re-arms caveman AND downgrades the level |
| `turn caveman off` (flag=`full`) | flag deleted | no-op — caveman stays on |
| `enable caveman and stop apologizing` (flag=`full`) | stays active | flag **deleted** — explicit enable performs a disable |
| `what is caveman mode?` (flag absent) | no change | flag = `full` — asking about it turns it on |
| `be brief in the summary section` (flag absent) | no change | flag = `full` — one-off scoped request becomes a persistent session mode |
| `how do I exit vim normal mode` (flag=`full`) | stays active | flag deleted — "normal mode" is vim's default mode name |
| `"stop\ncaveman"` (flag=`ultra`) | flag deleted | no-op — every regex uses `.*` without the `s` flag, so multiline prompts never match |

**Why**

- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js:31-33` — activation `/\bcaveman\b.*\b(mode|activate|enable|turn on|start)\b/` matches any mention of "caveman ... mode"; the stop-guard and both deactivation regexes (`:105-107`) only match the contiguous phrase `turn off`, never the natural word order "turn X off".
- The guard on `:33` suppresses activation whenever `stop` appears anywhere, then deactivation regex 2 matches "caveman and stop".
- `/\bnormal mode\b/` (`:107`) fires with zero caveman context.

**Fix direction**

Check deactivation before activation; make the off-phrase word-order tolerant (`turn\s+(?:the\s+)?caveman[^.\n]*\s+off`); require caveman context for `normal mode`; don't treat questions (`what is|does|how`) as commands; add the `s` flag or normalize newlines.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: /caveman-commit permanently clobbers the active caveman level; namespaced /caveman:caveman-commit and -review are unrecognized
body:
**What happen**

Running `/caveman-commit` (or `-review` / `-compress`) overwrites the flag file with `commit` and **nothing ever restores the prior mode**. Since these are `INDEPENDENT_MODES`, the per-turn reinforcement stops emitting for every subsequent turn, and the statusline is stuck at `[CAVEMAN:COMMIT]`.

`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js:76-81, 97-98, 123`.

**Repro (confirmed)**

1. flag = `ultra`
2. prompt `/caveman-commit` → flag = `commit`
3. next prompt "ordinary question" → reinforcement stdout is empty; caveman prose mode is effectively dead until the user manually re-runs `/caveman`

SKILL.md promises "Level persist until changed or session end" — a one-shot skill invocation shouldn't count as "changed" for the rest of the session.

**Also**

Only compress and stats got plugin-namespaced variants: `/caveman:caveman-compress` works (`:80`), but `/caveman:caveman-commit` and `/caveman:caveman-review` are not recognized at all (confirmed: flag unchanged) — so in a marketplace plugin install those two skills run **with** the caveman-prose reinforcement injected into their turn, exactly what the INDEPENDENT_MODES suppression exists to prevent. Probably the same root cause as #537.

**Fix direction**

Store the previous prose mode alongside the one-shot mode (e.g. `commit:ultra`) and restore it on the next prompt, or suppress reinforcement for one turn without persisting `commit` to the flag. Add the missing `(?::caveman)?` namespaced variants for commit/review.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: caveman-compress: detect.py classifies Dockerfile, Makefile, and shebang scripts as compressible natural language
body:
**What happen**

`skills/caveman-compress/scripts/detect.py` classifies `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, and shebang shell scripts as compressible natural language, so `/caveman-compress Dockerfile` sends the file to Claude and overwrites it with caveman prose.

**Why**

`detect.py:17` lists `.dockerfile` / `.makefile` in `SKIP_EXTENSIONS`, but real files are named `Dockerfile` / `Makefile` with **no extension**, so they fall through to the content heuristic (`:77-95`), which has no shebang or known-filename check.

**Repro (confirmed by running `detect_file_type`)**

- `Dockerfile` → `natural_language, compress=True`
- `Makefile` → `compress=True`
- executable script `deploy` starting with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` → `compress=True`

**Fix (~10 lines)**

Before the extensionless content heuristic: refuse files whose first two bytes are `#!`, and basenames in {`Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `Jenkinsfile`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `Vagrantfile`}.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: caveman-stats: whole-session tokens attributed to the mode active at stats time — savings inflated or zeroed on mid-session mode change
body:
**What happen**

`/caveman-stats` attributes **all** output tokens since session start to whatever mode the flag holds at the moment stats run:

- Activate caveman at turn 51 of a 50-turn verbose session → all prior verbose output is counted as caveman-compressed, then `estNormal = tokens/0.35` is back-computed on top (`src/hooks/caveman-stats.js:310-311, 142-150`) → wildly inflated savings.
- Inverse: run caveman all session, say "normal mode", then `/caveman-stats` → mode reads null → "Caveman not active this session", zero savings.

The inflated `est_saved_tokens` is appended to `.caveman-history.jsonl` (`:316-327`) and rendered in the statusline lifetime suffix — so the error compounds into the permanent lifetime number the README treats as an honest metric ("Benchmark and eval numbers must be real").

The per-mode arithmetic itself is fine (verified synthetically: 1,000 tokens, `full`, sonnet-4-5 → 2,857 est / 1,857 saved); the defect is mode attribution over time.

**Fix direction**

Track mode transitions (the tracker already writes the flag on every change — append `{ts, mode}` to a small session log) and attribute token spans to the mode active when they were generated; or at minimum only count tokens from the timestamp the current mode was set.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: opencode plugin mode parsing drifted from Claude tracker — brevity triggers missing, bogus level overwrites flag, independent modes unreachable
body:
**What happen**

The opencode plugin's mode parsing (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:99-161`) has drifted from the Claude Code tracker (`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js:30-39`). Three confirmed divergences (driven live with an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` sandbox):

1. **Brevity triggers missing** — the tracker activates on "less tokens" / "fewer tokens" / "be brief" / "be terse" / "shorter answers" (promised in README). The opencode plugin has no such branch: `"be brief please"` and `"use less tokens from now on"` left the flag unchanged.
2. **Bogus level overwrites the flag** — the expanded-template branch (`plugin.js:123-130`) falls through to `return getDefaultMode()` for an unknown level, while the literal branch (`:155-156`) and the Claude tracker (`caveman-mode-tracker.js:94`) deliberately return null. Confirmed: after `/caveman wenyan-ultra`, "Activate caveman mode: bogus-level" overwrote the flag to `full`.
3. **Independent modes unreachable** — opencode expands `/caveman-commit` etc. into the command body ("Generate a commit message…"), which matches no parse branch, so the flag stays at e.g. `full` and the per-turn caveman-prose reinforcement (`plugin.js:219-225`) keeps injecting during commit/review/compress turns — exactly what the tracker's `INDEPENDENT_MODES` suppression exists to prevent.

**Fix direction**

Extract the parsing into a shared CJS module (e.g. `src/hooks/caveman-parse.js`) consumed by both the tracker and the opencode plugin — the plugin already proves this pattern works in the compiled-Bun runtime by reusing `caveman-config.js` via `createRequire`.

main @ 25d22f8.

title: commands/caveman-init.toml runs repo-relative src/tools path — fails for every installed Codex/Gemini user
body:
**What happen**

`commands/caveman-init.toml:2` tells the agent to run

```
node src/tools/caveman-init.js {{args}}
```

"in the current repo". For every installed Codex / Gemini-extension user, cwd is **their** project — `src/tools/caveman-init.js` only exists inside the caveman clone / extension directory. The command fails with `Cannot find module` for everyone except caveman developers.

**Fix**

Use the runner that works from anywhere:

```
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --with-init {{args}}
```

or resolve the extension's absolute install path.
