title: fix(install): treat spawn ENOENT as failure, not success
body:
## What happen

`spawnSync` reports a missing binary as `{ status: null, error }`. The installer's `(r.status || 0) === 0` checks coerce that `null` to success. Verified in a clean `node:20-bookworm` container: `node bin/install.js --only claude --non-interactive` on a box without the `claude` CLI printed `installed: • claude`, skipped the standalone-hook fallback with `hooks: plugin manifest handles SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit`, and left `~/.claude/` nonexistent — success reported, nothing installed.

Fixes #592.

## Fix

- New `spawnOk(r)` helper: `!!r && !r.error && r.status === 0`. Dry-run results (`{status: 0}`, no `error`) still pass.
- Used at all 8 coercion sites: claude plugin install, gemini extension install, npx-skills providers, mcp-shrink registration, `runInit` (local + curl-fallback paths), claude plugin uninstall, and the skills auto-detect fallback.
- `installClaude` now warns `claude CLI not found on PATH (or could not be spawned)` before recording the failure, so the summary isn't mysterious.

With this, the existing hook-wiring decision matrix does the right thing automatically: plugin install fails → `falling back to standalone wiring` → hooks copied from the local clone (works offline) and merged into settings.json.

## Tests

New e2e test in `tests/installer/e2e.freshinstall.test.mjs` runs the real installer with an **empty PATH** (guaranteed ENOENT even on machines that have `claude`), asserting: failure is reported, `claude` is not listed as installed, the standalone fallback triggers, hook files exist on disk, and `settings.json` has the SessionStart wiring. Passes everywhere since it doesn't depend on the CLI being present.

Full suites: 29/29 dry-run + unit, new test green, `node --check` clean.

title: fix(uninstall): match managed hook basenames, not substring
body:
## What happen

`--uninstall` deleted **any** hook entry in settings.json whose command contained the substring `caveman` anywhere — `bin/install.js` called `removeCavemanHooks(settings, 'caveman')` and `bin/lib/settings.js` matched with `command.includes(marker)`. A user-authored hook like

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "node /Users/me/Projects/caveman-notes/my-hook.js" }
```

was silently destroyed ("removed 1 caveman hook entry"). Any path, repo, or username containing the word — including a clone of this repo used in a hook — triggered deletion.

Fixes #593.

## Fix

`removeCavemanHooks` now tokenizes each command (quote-aware, same tokenizer the prune pass already used — hoisted to module scope and shared) and removes an entry only when a token's **exact basename** is one of `MANAGED_HOOK_BASENAMES`. This is the same design `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks` deliberately adopted to avoid this exact false-positive class; uninstall now follows it.

Details:
- `path.win32.basename` (splits on both `/` and `\`) so a settings.json written on Windows is handled correctly anywhere.
- `caveman-statusline.ps1` added to `MANAGED_HOOK_BASENAMES` — the installer wires it on Windows but it was missing from the set, so Windows statusline entries were invisible to both removal and the #471 orphan-prune self-heal.
- `mycaveman-activate.js` (superstring basename) and `caveman-notes/` paths are never matched.

## Tests

Unit tests updated to exercise real managed-script commands, plus two new regression tests: user hooks that merely mention "caveman" survive uninstall, and Windows-style `caveman-stats.js` wiring is removed. 31/31 unit + dry-run suites pass. Also verified end-to-end: synthetic settings.json with one managed hook + one `caveman-notes` user hook → `--uninstall` removes exactly the managed entry.

title: fix(compress): never classify build files or shebang scripts as prose
body:
## What happen

`detect.py` lists `.dockerfile` / `.makefile` in `SKIP_EXTENSIONS`, but real files are named `Dockerfile` / `Makefile` with **no extension**, so they fall through to the content heuristic — which has no shebang or known-filename check — and come back `natural_language, compress=True`. Net effect: `/caveman-compress Dockerfile` sends the file to Claude and overwrites it with caveman prose. Confirmed for `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, and a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script with no extension.

Fixes #600.

## Fix

Two small guards in `detect_file_type`:

1. **Basename check before any extension rule** — `KNOWN_CODE_FILENAMES` (case-insensitive): Dockerfile, Makefile, GNUmakefile, Jenkinsfile, Vagrantfile, Rakefile, Gemfile, Justfile, Procfile, Brewfile, CMakeLists.txt. It must run before extension classification because `CMakeLists.txt` would otherwise ride the compressible `.txt` rule.
2. **Shebang check** in the extensionless branch — first two bytes `#!` → `code`, never prose.

The plugin mirror copy (`plugins/caveman/skills/caveman-compress/scripts/detect.py`) is synced in the same commit: the sync workflow only triggers on `skills/**/SKILL.md` changes, so a scripts-only change has to carry its mirror along (same as bdcba4c did).

## Tests

New `tests/test_detect.py` (7 tests): Dockerfile/Makefile/CMakeLists.txt/shebang scripts classify as code and refuse compression; case-insensitivity; and two guards that extensionless prose (`NOTES`) and `README.md` **stay** compressible. Full `tests/verify_repo.py` suite and `tests/test_compress_safety.py` still pass.

title: fix(settings): string-aware trailing-comma removal in JSONC reader
body:
## What happen

`stripJsonComments` ended with a global regex sweep `out.replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1')` over the whole comment-stripped output — **including string contents**. A JSONC settings.json whose string values contain `,}` or `,]` (shell brace expansion `file{,}`, inline JSON in hook args, jq/awk snippets) was silently corrupted on read: `{"cmd": "echo ,}"}` parsed to `"cmd": "echo }"` — then persisted corrupted by `writeSettings` on the next install/uninstall. It only triggers for files that fail strict `JSON.parse` first, i.e. real JSONC files — exactly what this module exists to protect.

Fixes #595.

## Fix

Replace the regex with `stripTrailingCommas()` — a scan that tracks string state (same approach as the comment stripper above it, including backslash escapes) and drops a comma only when it's outside a string and the next non-whitespace char is `}` or `]`.

## Tests

Three new unit tests: `,}` / `,]` inside string values survive, real trailing commas after strings are still removed, and escaped quotes before `,}` inside strings are handled. 30/30 unit suite passes; full installer suites (77 tests) and `verify_repo.py` green locally **and in a clean node:20-bookworm container**.

title: fix(hooks): NL trigger misfires + one-shot independent modes
body:
## What happen

Two mode-tracker issues, both reproduced by piping prompts into the hook:

**#598 — natural-language matching misfires:**
| Prompt | Before this PR |
|---|---|
| `turn caveman mode off` (flag=ultra) | flag **overwritten to full** — deactivation re-armed caveman and downgraded the level |
| `turn caveman off` | no-op — only the contiguous phrase "turn off" matched |
| `enable caveman and stop apologizing` | flag **deleted** — explicit enable performed a disable |
| `what is caveman mode?` | activated the mode |
| `how do I exit vim normal mode` | deactivated the session mode |
| `stop\ncaveman` (multiline) | no-op — `.*` without the `s` flag |

**#599 — one-shot modes clobber the level:** `/caveman-commit` overwrote the flag with `commit` permanently — per-turn reinforcement stopped for the rest of the session and the statusline stuck at `[CAVEMAN:COMMIT]`, despite SKILL.md's "Level persist until changed or session end". Also, only compress/stats had plugin-namespaced variants: `/caveman:caveman-commit` and `-review` were unrecognized entirely.

Fixes #598, fixes #599.

## Fix

- Deactivation intent computed **first** and word-order tolerant; "normal mode" deactivates only as a command (prompt-initial, optionally with a switch-back verb) or with caveman context; questions are not commands; prompts normalized to one line; scoped brevity ("be brief in the summary section") stays a one-off instruction.
- Independent modes save the displaced prose mode to `.caveman-active.prev` (via `safeWriteFlag`, per the CLAUDE.md rule); the next ordinary prompt restores it — or deactivates if caveman wasn't active before. Chained one-shots (`/caveman-commit` → `/caveman-review`) keep the original. Deactivation clears the saved prev. Namespaced `-commit`/`-review` variants added.

## Tests

New `tests/test_mode_tracker.py` — 23 tests covering every confirmed misfire, the README-promised triggers that must keep working ("activate caveman", "turn on caveman mode", "talk like caveman", bare "caveman mode", "be brief"), slash-command switching, and the full one-shot save/restore lifecycle. All 23 pass; `verify_repo.py` (which pins `/caveman ultra`, "normal mode", and default-off behavior) passes unchanged, locally **and in a clean node:20-bookworm container**.

title: fix(openclaw): stray SOUL.md marker no longer chains into data loss
body:
## What happen

A truncated/stray marker in SOUL.md (interrupted write, partial user edit) chained into data loss:

1. `appendBootstrapToSoul` treats the block as present only when **both** markers exist — a lone begin marker meant it appended a **second** full block.
2. `stripBootstrapFromSoul` cut from the **first** begin to the **first** end — which now spanned all user content between the stray marker and the appended block.

Reproduced end state: the entire SOUL.md deleted, user content included (`{"changed":true,"removed":true}`).

Fixes #596.

## Fix

New `stripAllBootstrapBlocks` scan: each begin marker pairs with the nearest end **before the next begin**; an unpaired marker is removed as just the marker text — never as a span over user content. Handles multiple blocks and orphan end markers. `appendBootstrapToSoul` now detects damaged markers (orphans, duplicates), strips them safely, and writes one clean block (`{repaired: true}`); a single well-formed block remains a no-op.

The same single-span pattern exists for the opencode AGENTS.md fence in `bin/install.js` (uninstall path) — happy to follow up there once this approach is approved.

## Tests

Four new tests driving the helper directly: the exact #596 chain (truncated begin + user content → append → strip → content survives, exactly one begin marker after repair), pairwise multi-block strip keeping content between blocks, orphan end marker removal, and append-idempotency on a well-formed block. All 9 openclaw tests pass (5 existing + 4 new); full suites green locally **and in a clean node:20-bookworm container**.

title: fix(opencode): --force migrates legacy AGENTS.md, never wipes it
body:
## What happen

When `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` contains the legacy un-fenced sentinel, the installer prints *"re-run with `--force` to replace it with a fenced block"* — and `--force` then executed a **full-file replace** (`fs.writeFileSync(agentsMd, fencedBlock)`). All user-authored content around the legacy block was destroyed, no backup taken. The installer's own hint steered users with mixed files into data loss, and `--help` describes `--force` as merely "Re-run even if a target reports already installed".

Fixes #594.

## Fix

Migrate instead of wipe:

1. One-time backup to `AGENTS.md.bak` before any rewrite (same once-only pattern as `opencode.json.bak`).
2. Remove **only the legacy block**: exact match of the current rule body when possible; otherwise cut from the sentinel's paragraph start to EOF — the legacy path *appended* the block, so user content precedes it, and the heuristic path says so explicitly and points at the backup.
3. Write the fenced block after the preserved user content.

## Tests

New e2e test drives the real installer against a mixed legacy AGENTS.md (user rules + legacy body): user content survives, the fence is present, the legacy un-fenced copy is gone, and the backup contains the original. The older-revision heuristic path verified manually (user notes above sentinel survive, `.bak` written). Full suites green locally **and in a clean node:20-bookworm container**, including a targeted container repro of the exact reported scenario.

title: Codex: shipped [features] hooks key is silently ignored on codex-cli <=0.120.0 (pre-rename versions) — auto-activation inert
body:
## Environment

- caveman v1.9.0 (installed from marketplace)
- codex-cli 0.120.0 (homebrew, macOS arm64) — deliberately not the latest; that version skew is the point of this report
- Tested in an isolated `CODEX_HOME` (real config untouched)

## What happens

`.codex/config.toml` ships `[features] hooks = true` — the current flag name after the #350 rename (`codex_hooks` → `hooks`), which tracks the latest Codex config syntax.

On codex-cli 0.120.0 (and presumably any pre-rename version):

```
$ codex features list
codex_hooks   under development   false

$ codex features enable hooks
Error: Unknown feature flag: hooks
```

And with the shipped raw config (`[features]` / `hooks = true`): the key is **silently ignored** — `codex_hooks` stays `false`, no warning, no error. So on pre-rename Codex versions, caveman auto-activation is silently inert: users get no failure signal, caveman simply never activates.

## Suggestion

Either:
- write both keys in the shipped config (`hooks = true` and `codex_hooks = true`) — on 0.120.0 the unknown `hooks` key is already ignored silently, so the symmetric case is plausibly harmless on new versions, worth verifying; or
- document a minimum Codex version for auto-start in INSTALL.md.

Possibly moot if #247 (migration to `.codex/settings.json`) lands first — in that case a compat note in the docs may be all that's needed.

## Disclosure

Found during an agent-assisted portability audit of caveman + ponytail. Environment: Claude Code (Fable 5 orchestrator, Sonnet subagents; caveman, ponytail, superpowers plugins installed). The Codex behavior above comes from live commands run in an isolated `CODEX_HOME`, not inferred from docs. Duplicate check done against open/closed issues mentioning codex (#350, #247, #568, #513, #573, #185): none reports the pre-rename silent-ignore case. No PR attached — reporting the finding.

fix(caveman-compress): protect code by construction (mask-and-splice), force UTF-8 file I/O + integrity gate, fix inline-code extractor fence bug
body:
**Title:** fix(caveman-compress): protect code by construction (mask-and-splice), force UTF-8 file I/O + integrity gate, fix inline-code extractor fence bug

**Disclosure:** this PR (diagnosis, patches, and tests) was drafted by Claude (Anthropic's Claude Code). I (@FatalMerlin) hit each of these failures directly on real files, worked through the fixes with Claude, reviewed the diagnosis and the diffs myself, and I'm signing off on them as accurate and correct before submitting — this is a reviewed and approved contribution, not raw unreviewed model output. (The third commit, the UTF-8 fix, was surfaced the same way: a real batch-compression run on a set of memory files.)

## Summary

- `extract_inline_codes()` used a fragile, column-0-anchored regex to strip fenced blocks before scanning for inline code. Any fence not flush-left (e.g. indented under a list item) was invisible to it, and the fallback then paired backticks *across* the fence, producing garbage tokens instead of the real inline code (repro + regression test in the diff).
- More fundamentally: code preservation during compression was only ever a **prompt instruction** to the compression model (`build_compress_prompt`'s "do NOT modify code blocks/backticks" rules), then checked byte-exact after the fact by `validate.py`. That's asking a non-deterministic model to behave, not guaranteeing it — on my install this currently means a hard fail + discard after 2 retries on real code-dense files, rather than silent corruption, but the underlying gap is the same one #112 reported.
- **Sibling gap in the file layer:** the same "protect it, but only softly" problem existed for **non-ASCII prose**, one level down from the model. The skill's file I/O read/wrote with no explicit `encoding=`, so on Windows it fell back to the locale codepage (cp1252). Prose characters outside cp1252 (`→`, `≠`) raised `UnicodeEncodeError` mid-write; characters *inside* cp1252 but not ASCII (em-dash `—`, curly quotes, bullet, ellipsis) were silently mis-encoded and the output became invalid UTF-8 while the run still exited 0 with "Validation passed" — the mask/validate layer only guards code and frontmatter, not general text integrity.

**Prior art / why this isn't a resubmit:** #309, #307, and #293 each tried fixing this bug class before (adding an inline-code check with its own from-scratch regex) and were closed unmerged; #481 fixed `extract_code_blocks` itself but didn't touch `extract_inline_codes`, so the bug above is still live on `main`. All of those were *detect-after-the-fact* approaches. This PR's masking commit is a different strategy — *prevent by construction* — so it's meant to complement/supersede that line of attempts, not repeat it.

## What this PR does

1. **Fix `extract_inline_codes`** (`validate.py`) to reuse the existing line-based `extract_code_blocks` fence extractor instead of its own regex, so both checks agree on what counts as "inside a fence."
2. **Add mechanical code protection** (`compress.py`): before the compression prompt is built, `mask_code()` replaces every fenced block and inline `` `span` `` with an opaque placeholder token (`⟦CVMN-CODE-n⟧` — non-markdown-active Unicode brackets, chosen so a whitespace-normalizing compressor can't fracture them). The model compresses prose + placeholders only, never real code. `unmask_code()` splices the originals back verbatim by index afterward.
3. **Fail closed on code**: if a placeholder is dropped, duplicated, or otherwise altered by the model, `unmask_code` raises `PlaceholderIntegrityError` and `compress_file` aborts before any backup/write — original file untouched, no partial or best-guess splice.
4. **Force UTF-8 file I/O + fail closed on text** (`compress.py`, `validate.py`, `detect.py`): pin `encoding="utf-8"` on every read/write in the skill so file I/O no longer depends on the host locale, and add a `UnicodeIntegrityError` gate before overwrite — the compressed output must round-trip encode/decode as UTF-8 and introduce no new `U+FFFD` versus the source, else abort without writing. Also reconfigure `stdout`/`stderr` to UTF-8 so the tool's own emoji status `print()`s don't crash on a cp1252 console.
5. **SKILL.md**: documents the masking step, and fixes a doc/behavior mismatch — the backup was described as `FILE.original.md` beside the source, but the code actually writes it out-of-tree under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/caveman-compress/backups/...` (intentional, so auto-loaders don't re-ingest it — just undocumented).

## Why this approach

Masking makes `validate_code_blocks` / `validate_inline_codes` structurally un-failable — the spliced-back text is byte-identical to the original by construction, so those checks become a backstop rather than the primary defense. The UTF-8 gate applies the same philosophy to prose: guarantee it at the I/O boundary and fail loudly if a future regression breaks it, instead of trusting the environment. No change needed to the validator itself. Existing `MAX_RETRIES` fix-pass logic is untouched.

## Testing

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

- Added `tests/test_mask_code.py`: round-trip fidelity through a simulated aggressive rewrite, no real code leaking into the masked prompt text, fence-first masking so inline code inside a fence isn't double-masked, and three fail-closed cases (dropped placeholder, duplicated placeholder, no-op when nothing was masked).
- Added `tests/test_unicode_prose.py`: a deterministic mask → rewrite → write → reread round-trip over a fixture containing `— → ≠ … " ' •`, asserting the written file re-reads as valid UTF-8 with every character intact (fails on the pre-fix code).
- Added a regression test to `tests/test_validate_inline.py` (`test_indented_fence_not_leaked_as_inline_code`) pinning the extractor bug above.
- The encoding fix also cleared 4 pre-existing errors in `test_compress_safety.py` (emoji status `print()`s crashing on cp1252 stdout — same root cause).
- Full suite: **23 tests pass**, 0 failures, 0 errors.
- Beyond the unit tests, also ran the real `compress_file` pipeline end-to-end (via `claude --print`) against a synthetic code-dense markdown file (inline commands + a fenced YAML block with a comment) — output validated byte-identical on fenced blocks and inline code, including preserving a YAML comment the model would otherwise be inclined to strip. Repro file available on request if useful as a fixture; kept out of the diff since it's synthetic and not needed for the unit tests to pass.

title: fix(agents): move cavecrew investigator/reviewer off haiku
body:
## What

Re-tiers two cavecrew subagents away from `model: haiku`:

- `cavecrew-investigator` → `model: sonnet` + `effort: low`
- `cavecrew-reviewer` → `model: sonnet` + `effort: medium`

Also updates the corresponding rows in `CLAUDE.md`. CI sync will mirror the agent files into `plugins/caveman/agents/`.

## Why

Haiku 4.5 has become a poor fit for multi-step agentic subagents:

1. **Confirmed tool-loop failure mode** — Haiku 4.5 re-calls already-completed tools and stalls multi-step plans in agentic chains: anthropics/claude-code#10029. Both of these agents run tool chains (Grep/Glob/Read/Bash iterations), so a single looped run erases the price advantage and returns unreliable findings.
2. **No effort support** — Haiku 4.5 rejects the `effort` parameter (400 error; it is absent from the supported-models list at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort), so the cheap-tier slot can't be tuned down. Sonnet at `low` effort fills that slot: official docs describe low as "significant token savings, some capability reduction", which matches the locate/report workload.
3. **Staleness** — Haiku 4.5 (Oct 2025) is now two generations behind Sonnet 5 with no newer Haiku announced.

Cost impact is modest and bounded: Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 per MTok (intro through Aug 31, 2026; $3/$15 after) vs Haiku's $1/$5, and the reviewer especially benefits — one-line severity-tagged findings are judgment work that haiku frequently fumbles.

The reviewer was arguably mis-tiered even before this: diff review is judgment work, which the model-routing literature consistently puts at least one tier above the mechanical bucket.

title: feat(hooks): propagate caveman mode to subagents via SubagentStart
body:
## Problem

SessionStart hook context reaches the parent thread only — it never propagates to Task-spawned subagents. So in an active caveman session, every subagent (Explore, custom agents, etc.) runs without the caveman ruleset and emits full-verbosity output, forfeiting the token savings exactly where output volume is highest.

## Fix

A SubagentStart hook (`src/hooks/caveman-subagent.js`) that re-reads the active caveman level from the same flag file the other hooks use and re-injects the ruleset into each spawned subagent via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`. When caveman is off or the flag is absent it exits silently with no output. Fail-open everywhere: a hook error can never block a subagent spawn.

The pattern is borrowed from ponytail (MIT, [DietrichGebert/ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail)), which fixed the same parent-only-context gap for its own mode (their issue #252).

## Changes

- `src/hooks/caveman-subagent.js` — the hook (new)
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — SubagentStart entry
- `bin/install.js` + `src/hooks/install.sh` — standalone-install wiring (idempotent, marker-guarded like existing hooks)
- `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` — new hook entry

## Verification

- `node --check` passes
- Flag absent → exit 0, no output
- Flag `full`/`ultra` → valid SubagentStart JSON, additionalContext starts with "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: ..." (works both with plugin SKILL.md present and standalone fallback)
- `sha256sum -c src/hooks/checksums.sha256` passes
- `.codex/hooks.json` intentionally untouched — Codex has no SubagentStart equivalent

title: fix(hooks): deliver /caveman-stats via additionalContext for macOS app compat
body:
`/caveman-stats` works in terminal Claude Code but shows nothing in the macOS app.

**Root cause:** the hook delivered stats via `{decision:'block', reason:...}` on `UserPromptSubmit`. Terminal renders the blocked prompt's `reason`; the macOS app honors the block (swallows the prompt) but never renders `reason` → stats vanish silently.

**Fix:** deliver the stats via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` instead, which is honored by both terminal and app. The model prints the block verbatim on behalf of the hook.

Fixes #618

title: fix(parse): extract shared mode parser to fix three drifts between tracker and opencode plugin
body:
## Problem

The opencode plugin mode parsing (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:99-161`) had drifted from the Claude Code tracker (`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js`). Three confirmed divergences:

1. **Brevity triggers missing** — "less tokens" / "fewer tokens" / "be brief" / "be terse" / "shorter answers" only worked in the tracker, not the plugin.
2. **Bogus level overwrites flag** — expanded-template branch fell through to `getDefaultMode()` for unknown levels, silently overwriting the flag. Tracker and slash-command branch correctly return null.
3. **Independent modes unreachable** — opencode expands `/caveman-commit` etc. into command descriptions that match no parse branch, so the flag never flipped and per-turn reinforcement kept injecting.

## Fix

Extracted the parsing into `src/hooks/caveman-parse.js` — a shared CJS module consumed by both the tracker and the opencode plugin. `bin/install.js` updated to copy `caveman-parse.{js->cjs}` alongside `caveman-config.{js->cjs}` for the opencode plugin install path.

All three bugs are fixed in the single shared `parseModeChange()`: brevity triggers are included, unknown levels return null, and independent modes are reachable via their slash commands.

## Validation

- 28 unit tests passing covering all three bugs, deactivation, activation, slash commands, and quote unwrapping
- All four changed files pass Node.js syntax check

Closes #602

title: fix(commands): /caveman-init works for installed users
body:
## What happen

`commands/caveman-init.toml` tells the agent to run `node src/tools/caveman-init.js {{args}}` "in the current repo". For every installed Codex / Gemini-extension user, cwd is **their** project — that path only exists inside a caveman clone, so `/caveman-init` fails with `Cannot find module` for everyone except caveman developers.

Fixes #603.

## Fix

Two parts:

1. **New `--init-only` flag in `bin/install.js`** — writes the per-repo IDE rule files and skips everything else: the provider install matrix, the interactive TTY picker, and the npx-skills auto-detect fallback. Rationale: the TOML can't just use `--with-init`, because that runs the full agent-install matrix as a side effect — a slash command named *init* must not silently install plugins.
2. **TOML now runs the installer that works from anywhere:** `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --init-only {{args}}`. `--dry-run` / `--force` pass straight through, so the existing prompt guidance ("dry-run first unless the user passed --force") keeps working.

The other three TOML stubs are prompt-only (no paths) — unaffected.

## Tests

New dry-run e2e test: `--init-only --dry-run` plans rule files, and asserts **no** provider output appears (no `Claude Code detected`, no `would run: claude plugin`, no `skills add`), and nothing is written. Also verified live in a scratch git repo (with `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE` isolated): `.cursor/`, `.windsurf/`, `.clinerules/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`, `AGENTS.md` written; zero agent installs triggered. Dry-run suite 3/3, `node --check` clean.

title: test(mcp-shrink): guard npm files[] against missing relative requires
body:
## What this is now

title: fix(compress): UTF-8 I/O + atomic writes, no more wiped files
body:
## What happen

Every file read/write in `compress.py` / `validate.py` / `benchmark.py` used the platform default encoding. On Windows that's cp1252, so any non-ASCII character (`→`, `—`, accented text, CJK) crashed with `UnicodeEncodeError` — and because `Path.write_text` **opens-and-truncates the destination before encoding the string**, the crash left the user's live file at 0 bytes. At that point the backup readback hadn't completed its job either, so there was no recovery path.

Reproduced in a clean `node:20-bookworm` container by forcing the same failure class (`LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0` → ASCII default encoding, mocked `call_claude`):

| | result | live file after |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode '\u2192'` | **0 bytes (wiped)** |
| this branch | `ok=True` | 19 bytes, `A → B done.` intact |

Fixes #533.

## Fix

- **`encoding='utf-8'`** pinned on every file read (`compress.py:249,304`, `validate.py:31`, `benchmark.py:26-27`). The repo already pins UTF-8 for the CLI subprocess and stdout — file I/O was the gap.
- **New `write_text_atomic()`** used for all four writes (backup, live write, retry write, restore): encode **first** (an encode error can no longer touch the file), write to a temp file in the same directory, fsync, `os.replace` — atomic on POSIX and Windows. Failure at any step leaves the destination untouched and cleans up the temp file.
- **Fix-retry loop guarded against `call_claude` returning `None`/empty** — previously `Path.write_text(None)` raised `TypeError` *after* truncating the live file (same data-loss class). Now it skips the write and lets the retry cap restore the original.
- `detect.py:79` deliberately left alone: reads with `errors='ignore'` never crash, it's classification-only, and PR #606 already touches that region — avoiding a cross-PR conflict.
- Plugin mirror (`plugins/caveman/skills/caveman-compress/scripts/`) synced in the same commit, since the CI sync workflow only triggers on `SKILL.md` changes.

## Tests

Four new tests in `tests/test_compress_safety.py`: UTF-8 bytes on disk; **write failure leaves destination untouched + no temp-file litter** (surrogate encode error); full unicode round-trip through `compress_file` (file + backup); `None` fix-retry output restores the original instead of crashing. Full safety suite passes locally (exit 0) and in the container.

title: fix(install): verify caveman-init.js integrity before executing (#262)
Fable-class harnesses: full/ultra style-compression now conflicts with model readability instructions — proposal: additive 'smart' level (selectivity compression)
body:
## Problem

On newer frontier agents, caveman's signature compression (`full`/`ultra`) now collides with the agent harness itself. Claude Code's system prompt for Claude Fable 5 instructs, verbatim:

> "The way to keep output short is to be selective about what you include […], **not to compress the writing into fragments, abbreviations, arrow chains like `A → B → fails`, or jargon.**"

and

> "Being readable and being concise are different things, and **readability matters more**."

That is a near-literal blocklist of `full`/`ultra` mechanics (fragments OK / drop articles / `X → Y` causality arrows / prose abbreviations). So with caveman active, a Fable-class model holds two standing instructions that directly contradict each other on every turn. Anthropic's official [Fable 5 prompting guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5) additionally warns that over-prescriptive style instruction sets written for older models can degrade output quality on Fable — instruction conflict is the worst case of that.

Ran caveman daily on Claude Code (Opus 4.8, now Fable 5) for weeks. Observed drift under the conflict: the model quietly reverts to harness style in long/complex replies (persistence loss), or produces awkward hybrids.

## Token math worth stating in the docs

Syntax compression (articles, fragments, short synonyms) saves a small, bounded fraction of output tokens. The big wins are **selectivity**: dropping recaps of unchanged plans, restated tool output, surveys of options not chosen, pleasantries, hedging. Selectivity compression is fully compatible with the readability instructions above — it cuts *content*, not *grammar* — so it survives on strict harnesses where `full`/`ultra` fight the model.

## Proposal (additive, no behavior change for existing levels)

1. New intensity level `smart` — selectivity compression:

   > **smart** | Cut content, not grammar. Full sentences, zero fluff: drop recaps of unchanged plans, restated tool output, options not chosen, pleasantries, hedging, repeated paths/ids. Complex replies end with one plain-language TLDR line. Differs from `lite` at reply scale (what gets included), not sentence scale (how it reads). For agents whose system prompts enforce readability (e.g. Claude Code on Fable-class models).

2. A short **Model compatibility** note in SKILL.md recommending `lite`/`smart` over `full`/`ultra` on harnesses that instruct full-sentence readability, naming Claude Code + Fable 5 as the known case today.

Happy to send the small focused PR for `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` (source of truth only; mirrors left to the rebuild per CONTRIBUTING). Caveman like simple: `smart` = same hunt, fewer grunts, no fight with cave rules.

title: feat(intensity): add 'smart' level - selectivity compression for readability-enforcing harnesses
body:
Closes #629 (rationale + evidence there).

## What

New additive intensity level `smart`: cut content, not grammar. Full sentences, zero fluff — drop recaps, restated tool output, options-not-chosen, pleasantries, hedging; complex replies end with one plain-language TLDR line. Plus a short **Model Compatibility** note in SKILL.md.

## Why

On harnesses that enforce full-sentence readability in the system prompt (Claude Code on Claude Fable 5 today — its prompt explicitly forbids fragments, dropped articles, and arrow chains), `full`/`ultra` create a standing instruction conflict every turn, and the model drifts back to harness style. `smart` keeps caveman's token mission alive there by compressing at reply scale (what gets included) instead of sentence scale (how sentences read). Details + citations in #629.

## Changes

- `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` — `smart` row in intensity table, frontmatter level list, switch hint, Model Compatibility section (source of truth only; mirrors under `plugins/` left to the rebuild per CONTRIBUTING)
- `src/hooks/caveman-config.js` — `smart` in `VALID_MODES`

- `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`, `src/rules/caveman-activate.md`, `src/tools/caveman-init.js`, `bin/lib/openclaw.js` — switch-hint strings
- `skills/caveman-help/SKILL.md` — help table row

## Testing

- `node tests/test_symlink_flag.js` passes

Small focused PR. Same hunt, fewer grunts, no fight with cave rules.

title: fix(hooks): respect repo-local defaultMode=off in per-turn reinforcement
body:
## Problem

The UserPromptSubmit flag file (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-active`) is global, shared across all concurrent Claude Code sessions on a machine. If session A (in some directory) activates caveman mode, it writes that flag. A concurrent session B sitting in a repo whose `.caveman.json` sets `defaultMode: "off"` would still see B's stale/foreign flag and re-inject the per-turn "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE" reinforcement context on every prompt — silently defeating the repo-local off config.

Separately, `getDefaultMode()` always resolved the repo-local config walk from `process.cwd()` (the hook process's spawn cwd) rather than the cwd of the prompt actually being handled, so directory-scoped config could miss mid-session directory changes.

## Fix

- `src/hooks/caveman-config.js`: `getDefaultMode()` gains an optional `startDir` param, used as the start of the repo-local config walk (`findRepoConfigPath(startDir || process.cwd())`). Fully backward compatible — existing callers passing nothing behave identically.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js`:
  - Natural-language activation now calls `getDefaultMode(data.cwd)`, using the per-prompt `cwd` from the hook's stdin JSON instead of the hook process's spawn cwd.
  - The per-turn reinforcement emit is additionally gated on `getDefaultMode(data.cwd) !== 'off'`, so a foreign/stale global flag can no longer override a directory's repo-local `off` config.

## Verification

Ran the full existing suite against the patched clone — all pass, no regressions:
- `npm test` — 112/112 pass
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_compress_safety` — OK
- `node tests/test_caveman_init.js` — 8/8 pass
- `node tests/test_symlink_flag.js` — 12/12 pass

Additionally hand-verified the exact scenario this fixes, using a scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and a test dir with `.caveman.json` = `{"defaultMode":"off"}`, piping JSON directly into `caveman-mode-tracker.js`:

| # | stdin | flag before | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `{"prompt":"hello there","cwd":"<off-dir>"}` | `full` | no output | ✅ no output |
| B | `{"prompt":"hello there","cwd":"<normal-dir>"}` | `full` | JSON `additionalContext` emitted | ✅ emitted |
| C | `{"prompt":"be brief please","cwd":"<off-dir>"}` | none | flag NOT created | ✅ not created |
| D | `{"prompt":"be brief please","cwd":"<normal-dir>"}` | none | flag created, contents `full` | ✅ created, `full` |

Also smoke-tested `caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart hook, unaffected by this change) run from the off-dir vs. a normal dir to confirm no regression: off-dir → no flag written, mode `off`; normal dir → flag written, `full`.

## Backward compatibility

`getDefaultMode()` is called elsewhere (e.g. `caveman-activate.js`) with no argument — `startDir` is optional and falls back to `process.cwd()`, so those call sites are unaffected.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: uninstall leaves all caveman state files in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — stale lifetime badge and mode-log attribution on reinstall
body:
**What happen**

`--uninstall` strips settings.json wiring and deletes hook files, but never removes the state files the hooks/stats own in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Verified on main (0d95a81): seeded all five, ran `node bin/install.js --uninstall --non-interactive --config-dir <tmp>`, all five remain:

```
.caveman-active
.caveman-active.prev
.caveman-history.jsonl
.caveman-mode-log.jsonl
.caveman-statusline-suffix
```

(`uninstall()` in bin/install.js removes hooks + settings entries only; the opencode section does remove *its* flag at ~/.config/opencode/.caveman-active, so the Claude one looks like an oversight rather than a policy.)

**Why it matters**

- Reinstall later → `.caveman-mode-log.jsonl` still holds pre-uninstall transition rows, which the new #601 attribution joins against fresh sessions; `.caveman-statusline-suffix` immediately renders the old lifetime number as if it were current.
- `.caveman-active` left set means caveman reads as armed the moment hooks come back, even if the user had turned it off before uninstalling.
- Plain hygiene: uninstall should not leave five dotfiles behind.

**Expected**

Uninstall removes the ephemeral state files it owns (`.caveman-active`, `.caveman-active.prev`, `.caveman-mode-log.jsonl`, `.caveman-statusline-suffix`). `.caveman-history.jsonl` is arguably user data (lifetime stats) — keeping it with a printed note, or removing it too, both defensible; PR incoming proposes keep + note.

**Platform**

All (macOS/Linux/Windows — same code path).

title: fix(uninstall): remove hook/stats state files from config dir
body:
## What happen

`--uninstall` removes `.caveman-active` but leaves the newer state files behind in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:

- `.caveman-active.prev` — one-shot mode restore (from #608)
- `.caveman-mode-log.jsonl` — the #601 mode-transition log (e9cb843)

On a later reinstall, the stale mode-log feeds transition rows from the previous install into the #601 stats attribution, and the suffix resurrects the old lifetime number immediately. Verified in a clean `node:20-bookworm` container (details and an honest correction of my original repro in #635).

Fixes #635.

## Fix

Consolidates state-file removal into one block in `uninstall()` (replacing the lone `// Flag file` removal at the tail): `.caveman-active`, `.caveman-active.prev`, `.caveman-mode-log.jsonl`, `.caveman-statusline-suffix` are removed; `.caveman-history.jsonl` is **deliberately kept** — it's the user's lifetime stats record — with a printed `kept … delete manually if unwanted` note so the choice is visible rather than silent. Happy to flip that to remove-by-default if you'd rather uninstall leave zero trace.

## Tests

title: proposal: diff-first output rule — never reprint a full file for a local change
body:
## Idea

The biggest remaining token waste isn't wording — it's assistants reprinting a 300-line file to change one line. Caveman's SKILL.md already bans decorative fluff and raw log dumps; the same principle extends naturally to code output:

**Proposed addition to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` Rules section** (exact wording for your edit/veto):

> Code changes: show smallest diff, not whole file. Patch block, changed function, or `- old` / `+ new` lines with 1-2 context lines. Full file only when user ask, file is new, or most of file change anyway.
>
> Follow-up answers: only the delta. No restating what previous answer already establish.

## Where the savings land (honest scoping)

- **Chat-style assistants** (Copilot chat, web UIs, opencode ask-mode): large — reprinting files is their default failure mode.
- **Agentic tools** (Claude Code): smaller — edits go through tool calls that never hit chat output. The rule still helps for explanations and review commentary.

Worth stating that split in README/docs if adopted — fits the docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md ethos.

## Why an issue instead of a PR

SKILL.md is the product; wording changes belong to you. Happy to turn the blessed wording into a PR (SKILL.md + mirror sync + eval prompt exercising the rule) — or you just commit it directly, also fine.

Related: the auto-clarity rule already covers when NOT to compress; this covers what never needed printing at all.

title: proposal: caveman-lint — make wasted tokens visible and measurable
body:
## Idea

A read-only CLI that reports where an AI answer (or any prose file) wastes tokens — the measurement counterpart to caveman's compression:

```
caveman-lint: answer.md
────────────────────────────────────────
Total tokens:   412  (tiktoken cl100k_base)
Wasted tokens:  118  (~29% of document)
────────────────────────────────────────
  greeting               2×  ~21 tokens
      · Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that
  hedging                3×  ~24 tokens
      · It's important to note that
  boilerplate            2×  ~19 tokens
  filler-word           11×  ~11 tokens
  duplicate-sentence     1×  ~43 tokens
────────────────────────────────────────
  advisory: 1 code block over 80 lines — prefer a diff unless the
  full file was requested. Not counted as waste.
```

It scans for the same waste families SKILL.md tells models to drop, so it doubles as a regression check on caveman's own outputs (evals integration could come later).

## Honesty by construction (project policy baked in)

- fenced/inline code is never counted as waste
- overlapping matches are span-claimed — nothing counted twice
- token counts via tiktoken when installed, else chars/4 — the report says which was used
- oversized code blocks are advisory only, excluded from the waste total (the user may have asked for the full file)

## Status

Working implementation with 7 tests, validated in a clean container — PR incoming referencing this issue. Placement: `src/tools/caveman-lint.py` (pure stdlib, tiktoken optional), same spot as caveman-init. Zero new dependencies.

title: feat(compress): --undo restores the pre-compression backup
body:
## What

`caveman-compress` keeps a backup, but restoring it means manually copying a file out of a platform-specific data dir most users will never find. New command:

```
python3 -m scripts --undo <file>
```

Finds the backup (out-of-tree #420 layout first, legacy in-tree `<file>.original.md` sibling as fallback), restores **byte-exact** via atomic temp+`os.replace`, verifies the readback, then removes the backup — `compress_file` refuses to run while a backup exists, so keeping it would block the next compression of the same file. Clear error (file untouched) when there's nothing to undo. SKILL.md documents the trigger ("undo/restore/revert a compression"); mirror synced same-commit.

Deliberately implemented entirely in `cli.py` so it can't conflict with #626 (which touches `compress.py`).

## Tests

4 new tests: out-of-tree restore + backup removal, legacy sibling fallback, no-backup error path leaves the file alone, missing file errors. Validated in a clean `node:20-bookworm` container: 9/9 (undo + compress-safety suites), plus a live round-trip — unicode content restored byte-exact.

title: feat(tools): caveman-lint — report wasted tokens in AI prose
body:
Implements #638 — see the issue for the full pitch and honesty rules.

## What

`python3 src/tools/caveman-lint.py <file...> [--json] [--max-code-lines N]` — read-only report of wasted tokens per category (greeting, apology, hedging, boilerplate, filler-word, duplicate-heading, duplicate-sentence), the same waste families SKILL.md tells models to drop.

Design points worth review attention:

- **Span-claiming**: overlapping matches (`Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that` also contains `I'd be happy to` and `Sure!`) are counted once — greedy left-to-right, longest-first. Without this the waste total overstates ~30% on typical AI prose, which would violate the honest-numbers policy.
- **Fence-aware**: code blocks and inline code are stripped before matching; a fenced block full of trigger phrases produces zero findings (tested).
- **Token counting**: tiktoken (cl100k_base) when installed, chars/4 otherwise — the report labels which was used.
- **Oversized code blocks** (default >80 lines) are an *advisory* line, excluded from the waste total — the user may have asked for the full file. (Pairs with the diff-first proposal in #637.)

Pure stdlib, tiktoken optional, no new dependencies. Placement mirrors caveman-init (`src/tools/`).

## Tests

7 tests: category detection on verbose prose, clean caveman prose yields zero waste, fence trap, advisory-not-waste for big code blocks, short-repeat exemption, `--json` CLI contract, missing-file exit code. Green locally and in a clean container.

title: feat(cli): caveman config show/get/set/unset
body:
## What

The repo-local and user config files already drive the default mode (the `getDefaultMode` resolution chain), but changing them means hand-editing JSON in a platform-specific path (`~/.config/caveman/`, `%APPDATA%\caveman\`, `.caveman/config.json`). CLI sugar over the exact same files:

```
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- config show              # resolution chain + effective mode
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- config set intensity ultra
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- config set mode full --project
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- config unset mode
```

- Canonical key is `defaultMode` (what the hooks read); `mode` and `intensity` are accepted aliases since the README speaks in intensities.
- Values validated against `VALID_MODES` — a typo exits 2 and writes nothing, so a bad value can never silently break activation.
- `--project` updates the **nearest** checked-in config via the existing walk-up (`findRepoConfigPath`) instead of sprinkling new `.caveman/` dirs in subdirectories.
- Reuses the JSONC-tolerant atomic read/write from `bin/lib/settings.js`; resolution logic is required from `src/hooks/caveman-config.js`, not duplicated.

## Tests

title: SessionStart hook reads SKILL.md from a wrong path, so the fallback ruleset always loads
body:
`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` (line 56 at commit 25d22f8) loads the skill ruleset with:

```js
fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8')
```

`__dirname` is `<plugin_root>/src/hooks`, so this resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, which does not exist. The real file lives at `<plugin_root>/skills/caveman/SKILL.md`. The comment above the call assumes `__dirname` is `<plugin_root>/hooks/`, which is not the shipped layout. Result: the read throws every session and the weaker hardcoded fallback ruleset is silently injected instead of the SKILL.md source of truth.

Fix: `path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md')`, keeping the existing fallback for standalone installs.

Verified with `node -e "console.log(require('fs').existsSync(...))"` on a clean plugin install at commit 25d22f8.

Second, smaller item (happy to split into its own issue): `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py` refuses obviously sensitive files by basename (`.env`, `credentials.*`, key files), but the denylist misses common PII-bearing files (user profile notes, CRM exports). Since the script copies full file bodies to `~/.local/share/caveman-compress/backups` and ships them to the API, consider letting users extend the denylist via config, and documenting the backup location in the README.

title: caveman-compress truncates target file to 0 bytes with no backup on Windows (non-ASCII content)
body:
# Bug: `/caveman-compress` truncates target file to 0 bytes with no backup on Windows (non-ASCII content)

## Summary

On Windows, `caveman-compress` can **destroy the file it is compressing** — leaving it empty (0 bytes) with **no `.original.md` backup** — whenever the file (or the compressed output) contains any character outside cp1252 (e.g. `⚠️`, `→`, `—`, smart quotes). The file is unrecoverable unless the user has a copy elsewhere.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.14.3
- Plugin: `caveman` @ commit `0d95a81d35a9`
- Path: no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set → `claude --print` CLI fallback path
- File: a personal `RTK.md` (~964 bytes) containing `⚠️` and `→`

## Repro

1. Take any prose `.md` containing a non-cp1252 char (e.g. a line with `⚠️` or an `→` arrow).
2. Run `/caveman-compress <file>` on Windows (default codepage, no `PYTHONUTF8`).
3. Observed:
   ```
   Processing: ...\RTK.md
   Compressing with Claude...
   ❌ Error: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 648-649: character maps to <undefined>
   ```
4. The target file is now **0 bytes**. No `*.original.md` backup exists. Re-running then reports `❌ Refusing to compress: file is empty or whitespace-only.`

## Root cause

`scripts/compress.py` correctly pins `encoding="utf-8"` on the **subprocess** call to `claude` (lines 157–165, per the issue #152 comment) — but every **file I/O** call omits `encoding=`, so on Windows they default to cp1252:

- L249 `original_text = filepath.read_text(errors="ignore")`
- L303 `backup_path.write_text(original_text)`
- L304 `backup_path.read_text(errors="ignore")`
- L313 `filepath.write_text(compressed)`
- L331 `filepath.write_text(original_text)`  *(the "restore original" path — itself fails on Windows)*
- L340 `filepath.write_text(compressed)`

Two distinct defects follow:

1. **Data loss (0-byte file).** `Path.write_text()` opens the file in `"w"` mode, which **truncates immediately**, and *then* encodes the string. When the string contains a char cp1252 can't encode, `.write()` raises `UnicodeEncodeError` **after** truncation — leaving a 0-byte file. Because the same missing-`encoding` bug hits the backup write (L303) too, the backup either never completes or is corrupt, so there is no recovery copy. The `restore original` fallback (L331) has the identical flaw, so even the built-in recovery path fails on Windows.

2. **Silent corruption (latent).** L249 reads a UTF-8 file as cp1252 with `errors="ignore"`, producing mojibake / dropped bytes. Even when a write *doesn't* crash, the "original" that gets backed up and the body sent to Claude are already corrupted.

## Suggested fix

Add `encoding="utf-8"` to every `read_text` / `write_text` in `compress.py` — the same fix already applied to the subprocess:

```python
original_text = filepath.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")   # L249
backup_path.write_text(original_text, encoding="utf-8")                  # L303
backup_readback = backup_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")  # L304
filepath.write_text(compressed, encoding="utf-8")                        # L313, L340
filepath.write_text(original_text, encoding="utf-8")                     # L331
```

Optional hardening so a crash can never truncate the primary:
- Write to a temp file in the same dir, `fsync`, then `os.replace()` onto the target (atomic on Windows and POSIX). A failed encode then leaves the original untouched.
- Drop `errors="ignore"` on the source read, or warn — silently dropping bytes corrupts the "original" backup.

## Impact

High. Runs against a user's `CLAUDE.md`, todos, or notes — exactly the prose files the skill targets — and warehouse/dev docs routinely contain `→`, `—`, `✓`, emoji. On Windows this is a straight-up unrecoverable delete of the input.

title: caveman-compress: Windows default-codepage write crashes mid-write and truncates the target file to empty
body:
## Summary
`scripts/compress.py`'s `compress_file()` writes files via plain `Path.write_text(...)` with no `encoding=` argument, three times:

- `backup_path.write_text(original_text)`
- `filepath.write_text(compressed)` (right after backup verification, before the validation loop)
- `filepath.write_text(compressed)` again inside the retry loop

On Windows, `Path.write_text()` without an explicit encoding uses the system codepage (commonly cp1252), not UTF-8. If the compressed output contains any character outside that codepage — an arrow (`→`), em-dash, checkmark, etc. — the write raises `UnicodeEncodeError` partway through. Because `open(..., "w")` truncates the file immediately on open, this leaves the **target file at 0 bytes**, not the original content.

## Repro
1. Compress a `SKILL.md` (or any markdown) whose content — or Claude's compressed output — contains a non-cp1252 character, e.g. `→`.
2. On Windows, without `PYTHONUTF8=1` set:
   ```
   ❌ Error: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '→' in position 1412
   ```
3. The target file is now empty (0 bytes). No restore happened.

## Why it's worse than it looks
- The *first* `filepath.write_text(compressed)` call (right after backup verification, before entering the `for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES)` validation loop) has **no try/except and no restore-on-failure**. The retry loop's own write *is* guarded (`if attempt == MAX_RETRIES - 1: filepath.write_text(original_text); ...`), but that safety net doesn't cover this earlier call site.
- The backup at `backup_dir_for(filepath)` is written successfully before this (it's a separate write of `original_text`, which apparently round-trips fine even containing the same `→` in my repro — so backups are safe), so no permanent data loss *if* the user knows to look for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\caveman-compress\backups\<dir>\<stem>.original.md` and restore manually. But the CLI's own error message gives no indication the file was truncated or where the backup lives (it does print the backup path — but only on a *successful* run's completion message, not on this crash path).
- `cli.py` already reconfigures `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to UTF-8 for print statements (per its own comment referencing issue #152), but that doesn't touch the plain `write_text()`/`read_text()` calls in `compress.py`, which is the actual crash site here.

## Suggested fix
1. Pass `encoding="utf-8"` explicitly on every `read_text()`/`write_text()` call in `compress.py` (backup write, both primary writes, and the original read). This is the root fix — don't rely on the caller having `PYTHONUTF8=1` set.
2. Wrap the pre-validation-loop `filepath.write_text(compressed)` in the same try/except + restore-from-backup pattern the retry loop already has, so a crash there can't leave the target file truncated.
3. On any write failure, print the backup path so the user isn't left guessing where their content went.

Confirmed the fix direction works: setting `PYTHONUTF8=1` before running the script avoids the crash entirely (proves it's the default-encoding issue, not something else). Happy to send a PR with the `encoding="utf-8"` fix + the missing restore-on-failure guard if useful.

## What

`safeWriteFlag` write temp file then `renameSync` over `.caveman-active`. On Windows, rename fail with EPERM when another process (statusline poll) hold flag open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Result: mode switch silently lost + one orphan `.caveman-active.<pid>.<ts>` temp file leak per switch.

Hit this on real machine: Windows 11, pwsh statusline from settings.json, temp litter in `~/.claude/`.

## Fix

- Catch rename failure → in-place `O_TRUNC` write fallback. Non-atomic, acceptable: flag is best-effort 4-byte mode string, and write path already symlink-guarded above.
- Sweep orphan temps matching exact pattern `.caveman-active.<digits>.<digits>` older than 1h — cleans litter from pre-fix versions too. Fresh temps kept (possible concurrent writer).
- `checksums.sha256`: caveman-config.js line updated (hash of LF blob = raw.githubusercontent bytes; verified HEAD blob hash matches existing manifest).

## Tests

2 new cases in `tests/test_symlink_flag.js`:
- rename-failure fallback (monkeypatched `fs.renameSync` → EPERM): flag written, no temp leak
- orphan sweep: stale temp removed, fresh temp survives

`node tests/test_symlink_flag.js` → 14/14 pass. `npm test` Windows failures identical on `main` (path-separator regexes in installer tests) — unrelated to this change.

title: feat: reply in user's language under caveman mode
body:
## Problem

Caveman's rulesets are written in English with English-only examples (`Drop articles (a/an/the)`, `Token expiry check use \`<\` not \`<=\``) and never tell the model to keep the user's language. For non-English users, caveman replies drift to English — the model only switches back after the user explicitly asks for their language. Reproduced in Claude Code with a Chinese-speaking user: every turn came back in English until "讲中文".

Root cause: terseness rules bias the model toward the language they're written in, and there's no counter-instruction pinning output to the user's language.

## Fix

Add a `Language` rule at all three injection points so **caveman = terse, not English**:

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` | New `## Language` section (behavior source of truth) |
| `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` | Same rule in the standalone-install fallback ruleset |
| `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` | Per-turn reinforcement reminder now carries the language rule |

Output language always matches the user (Chinese in → Chinese out); article/filler-drop rules apply to the per-language equivalent.

Did not touch `plugins/caveman/skills/` — left for the CI sync workflow per `CLAUDE.md`.

## Testing

- `node -c` passes on both edited hooks.
- `npm test` failures are limited to the two pre-existing environment-dependent cases (`uninstall … skipped without claude CLI`, `openclaw uninstall …`) — identical failures on clean `main` before this change; no new failures introduced.

title: fix: remove duplicate command files shadowed by skills
body:
## Problem

Four features are registered twice, once as a legacy slash command
under `commands/`, once as a skill under `skills/`:

| name           | command file                          | skill dir                    |
|----------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| `caveman`      | `commands/caveman.md` + `.toml`        | `skills/caveman/`             |
| `caveman-commit` | `commands/caveman-commit.md` + `.toml` | `skills/caveman-commit/`     |
| `caveman-review` | `commands/caveman-review.md` + `.toml` | `skills/caveman-review/`     |
| `caveman-stats`  | `commands/caveman-stats.md` + `.toml`  | `skills/caveman-stats/`      |

Claude Code (and likely other agent platforms that support both
command and skill plugin surfaces) treats these as two separate
registries. Both get exposed under `/`, so each of the four names
above shows up twice in the slash-command menu — once as a bare
`/name`, once as `plugin:name` — with slightly different, drifted
descriptions for what is meant to be the same feature. This is
confusing for anyone typing `/` to discover commands and makes the
plugin look broken/duplicated.

`commands/caveman-init.md` is the one command with no skill
counterpart — it's unaffected and left in place.

## Fix

Delete the four redundant `commands/*.md` + `.toml` pairs that are
fully superseded by their skill equivalents. The skills already cover
the same trigger phrases (`/caveman`, `/caveman-commit`, etc.) via
their `description` frontmatter, so no functionality is lost.

## Testing

Confirmed no other file in the repo (docs, README, other skills)
references the deleted command paths.

title: fix(hooks): shrink per-turn reinforcement to minimal anchor (~57% smaller)

## Problem

title: fix(gemini): make extension install cleanly
body:
## Summary
- Pass `--consent` when the installer invokes `gemini extensions install` so non-interactive installs do not stall on Gemini's extension security prompt.
- Remove provider-specific `tools:` frontmatter from the shared cavecrew agent files so Gemini can load the extension root `agents/` directly.
- Keep the opencode sanitizer covering legacy `tools: [...]` agent files and add Gemini regression coverage.

## Root cause
Gemini CLI validates subagent `tools` entries against Gemini tool names while loading extension root `agents/*.md`. The shared cavecrew agents used Claude-style names like `Read`, `Grep`, and `Bash`, which made Gemini report `Invalid tool name` after installing the extension. The installer also invoked Gemini without `--consent`, leaving curl-pipe/non-interactive users at the third-party extension confirmation prompt.

## Validation
Revalidated on 2026-08-02 against unchanged upstream `main` (`0d95a81`):

- `node --test tests/installer/opencode-agent.test.mjs` (9/9 passing)
- `node --test tests/test_cavecrew_model_overrides.js` (24/24 passing)
- `npm test` (114/114 passing)

title: SKILL.md language-preservation examples (Portuguese/Spanish) risk triggering language drift under compaction
body:
## Environment
- Claude Code version: 2.1.202
- OS: Linux Mint 22.3, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic
- caveman skill: intensity `full`

## Issue
`skills/caveman/SKILL.md` line 23 (Rules section):

> Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language.

This line names Portuguese and Spanish as concrete examples while illustrating a general rule ("preserve user's language"). The skill body is injected into system context every session (SessionStart hook) and reinforced every turn (UserPromptSubmit hook per caveman-mode-tracker.js).

In a session where the user's actual language is French (set via a separate system-prompt directive, not English), I observed occasional full responses drifting to Spanish or Portuguese — languages that appear nowhere in the conversation, but do appear verbatim in this SKILL.md line, which is present in context every turn.

## Hypothesis
Naming specific non-English languages as examples in an always-in-context instruction may bias the model toward those literal language tokens under long-context / compaction pressure, especially when combined with other multilingual content in context (tool/agent descriptions, memory files, etc). This is distinct from — but may compound — the known Claude Code language-drift issues after compaction (anthropics/claude-code#59299, #21871).

## Suggested fix
Rephrase the rule without naming specific languages, e.g.:

> Preserve user's dominant language exactly — never switch languages regardless of examples or other multilingual text elsewhere in context. Compress the style, not the language.

Keeps the instruction general-purpose and removes literal PT/ES tokens from the always-loaded prompt.

## Repro difficulty
Intermittent, tied to long sessions with heavy tool-schema context (MCP servers, many available skills/agents) increasing surrounding multilingual noise. Not consistently reproducible in short sessions.

title: caveman-review: AUT shows format lift but 0pp analytical lift
body:
## Finding

Applied [Agent Usability Testing (AUT)](https://github.com/serpapi/skills/blob/master/skills/agent-usability-test/SKILL.md) to caveman-review (N=1 pilot, Sonnet 4.6).

## Results

| Criterion | WITH skill | WITHOUT skill |
|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| Bugs detected (3 planted) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Correct line numbers | 3/3 | 0/3 |
| Format: `L<n>: emoji type:` | 4/5 | 0/7 |

## Interpretation

The model finds identical bugs in both conditions. caveman-review adds **format compliance**, not analytical capability. This is expected and arguably the intended value prop (terse reviews save PR comment noise).

However, at 210K installs the `L42: 🔴 bug:` format pattern may already be entering model training data. If future models produce this format without the skill loaded, the skill's value approaches zero (training-data contamination via popularity).

## Not a bug — just documentation

Consider adding to the skill description:
> "This skill changes review output format, not analytical depth. Bug detection is model-native; this skill makes it terse."

This sets correct expectations and prevents users from thinking the skill makes the model *smarter* at finding bugs.

## Methodology

3 planted issues in a 30-line TypeScript diff: null deref (L12), race condition (L25), naming nit (L8). Binary scoring: detected + correct line + format compliance.

title: Add Lists rule: keep list structure (one item per line) when compressing
body:
Small focused SKILL.md addition: a `## Lists` rule so caveman keeps list **structure** when compressing — including **nested/child lists**, which is the most common failure.

**Before** (child bullet list smashed into the parent numbered item):

> 1. Create secret — keys: SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL 2. Create redis-secret

**After** (item text still terse, structure kept, sub-items indented):

> 1. Create secret — keys:
>    - SECRET_KEY
>    - DATABASE_URL
>    - REDIS_URL
> 2. Create redis-secret

**Why:** an inline-collapsed list is unreadable in any renderer (terminal, Markdown, chat UIs) and loses step order; the nested case is worst — a numbered step with its own bullet detail gets flattened into one run-on line. Caveman should shorten words, not destroy list layout. This also lines up with the existing **Auto-Clarity** rule about compression not garbling multi-step sequences.

(Origin: caveman-mode agents whose output renders as chat HTML, where smashed nested lists are especially bad — but the fix is renderer-agnostic, kept general here.)

title: fix(skill): switch syntax for all 6 levels + off, never-drop-negations rule, persisted-text boundary
body:
Spec-hardening pass over `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` + the doc surfaces that mirror it. Four files, +14/−11 lines, no behavior change to hooks/installer — every line documents what the code already does, plus one new safety rule.

## What

| Edit | Closes / refs |
|---|---|
| **Switch syntax completed**: `/caveman lite\|full\|ultra\|wenyan-{lite,full,ultra}\|off` — all six declared levels + `off` now reachable from the documented syntax; `wenyan` = `wenyan-full` and `stop`/`disable` = `off` aliases spelled out. Matches what `caveman-mode-tracker.js:123-133` already parses. `commands/caveman.md` argument-hint synced. | closes #548 |
| **Arg semantics documented**: no arg = configured default (env > repo config > user config > `full`); non-level arg = task, answered at current level. Documents the post-fix behavior of the arg-parsing path. | refs #537, #623 |
| **New safety rule** (one line in Rules): `NEVER drop not/never/only/except, numbers, units. NEVER flip do into don't.` Style compression must never invert meaning — worst failure mode of dropping words is losing a negation in an instruction like "do not deploy". No existing issue; smallest possible fix. | — |
| **Boundary rewritten**: `Persisted outside chat = write normal: code, comments, commits, docs, issue/PR/MR text (PR descriptions: repo convention), memory files (/caveman-compress exempt), third-party messages.` | closes #484; consolidates #483 (@ same wording intent, credit to its author), #562, #582 |
| **wenyan honesty**: table row now says `80-90% character reduction — chars, not tokens.` CJK chars are ≥1 token each, so character cuts ≠ token cuts. README wenyan note aligned (`meaning per *character*`, link to Honest Numbers). | refs #516, HONEST-NUMBERS register |
| **Docs synced in same commit**: README slash-command table (6 levels + off), README off-switch tip (`/caveman off`), caveman-help card (Off row + deactivate line). | — |

## What this deliberately does NOT touch

- **Frontmatter triggers** ("be brief" / auto-trigger): the hook still session-activates on those phrases, so narrowing only the description would desync doc from code. Left for #662's description rework.
- **`smart` level** (#629): owned by pending #630/#642.
- **List-structure rule**: owned by pending #669.
- **`plugins/` mirrors**: left to `sync-skill.yml` per CONTRIBUTING.

## Token tax

SKILL.md is injected every turn, so growth is a per-turn cost on every user: **+335 bytes** (5227 → 5562), most of it the safety rule and the completed switch line. Wordings were adversarially compressed several rounds to get here.

## Tests

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_mode_tracker tests.test_hooks tests.test_detect tests.test_validate_inline` — 47/47 pass

title: fix(hooks): unwrap Claude Code slash-command envelope so /caveman <level> and /caveman off work (#537)
body:
Fixes #537.

## Bug mechanism

Claude Code delivers slash commands to `UserPromptSubmit` hooks as an envelope, not the literal command string:

```
<command-message>caveman</command-message>
<command-name>/caveman</command-name>
<command-args>ultra</command-args>
```

`caveman-mode-tracker.js` gates all slash parsing on `prompt.startsWith('/caveman')`. The envelope starts with `<command-message>`, so that branch never ran: `<command-args>` was never read, `safeWriteFlag` was never called, and every `/caveman <level>` switch — **and `/caveman off`** — issued through the real slash UI was a silent no-op. The flag stayed at the SessionStart default and the per-turn reinforcement kept naming the old level. Only raw-typed commands (pasted as plain text) ever worked.

## Fix

Immediately after the existing whitespace collapse — before the `/caveman-stats` regex and the `startsWith` gate — extract `<command-name>` and `<command-args>` (one-line and newline-separated forms both; the collapse normalizes them) and, **only when the name starts with `/caveman`**, reconstruct `'<name> <args>'` and let it flow through the existing parsing unchanged. No new parsing paths: stats, level switch, off, namespaced `/caveman:caveman-*`, and one-shot independent modes all reuse the code that already handled raw-typed commands. Foreign-command envelopes (e.g. `/commit`) are left untouched, so NL detection still sees the user's own words and never misfires on another command's arguments.

## Tests

8 new cases in `tests/test_mode_tracker.py`:
- one-line envelope switches level (full → lite) and reinforcement names the new level
- one-line envelope activates with no prior flag
- newline envelope (the exact #537 form) switches full → ultra
- `/caveman off` envelope deletes the flag
- `/caveman-stats` envelope still reaches the stats branch (`"decision":"block"`) and leaves the flag alone
- non-level arg via envelope does not silently overwrite the flag (same contract as raw)
- raw-typed `/caveman lite` regression guard
- foreign-command envelope is not rewritten and does not disturb the flag

Full suites green: `tests.test_mode_tracker` (31), `tests.test_hooks` + `tests.test_detect` (14), `npm test` (108 pass / 0 fail / 4 skipped), `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js` (2).

The issue's self-contained repro (envelope payload, flag preset `full`, isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) was re-run 3x against the patched hook: flag flips to `ultra` every time; pre-patch it stayed `full`.

title: Caveman increases costs rather than saving
body:
**What happen**
I ran a test between off, on (across multiple caveman modes), and in each, it seemed that although caveman was saving on output tokens, it was still ultimately costing more.

```
full vs normal costs:
- full: $0.6255 vs normal: $0.5083 → caveman full is 23% MORE EXPENSIVE
- Output tokens only -8.2% but hook overhead is 4.5% of cost

ultra/wenyan-ultra vs normal costs:
- wenyan-ultra: $0.4668 vs normal: $0.4628 → effectively identical
- ultra: $0.5288 vs normal: $0.4628 → ultra is 14% more expensive

Per-prompt pattern:
- BOSH debug: full saves -33.6% output tokens — caveman genuinely compresses troubleshooting prose
- k8s scheduling, Go explain: full generates MORE tokens (+7.5%, +29.5%) — explanatory content gets longer, not shorter
- Short prompts (monorepo): high variance makes results unreliable

Bottom line: caveman reduces tokens on diagnostic/factual responses but increases them on explanatory content. Hook overhead (~500 tokens/turn × cache_creation pricing) is non-trivial enough that the net cost is worse for full and ultra modes, not better.
```

**Expected**

This should save money not spend it? Though I'm not sure if this is a fundamental result of how LLM's work under-the-hood because you're having to spend thinking on altering already-thought text into new text.

title: fix(compress): write UTF-8 files atomically
body:
Fixes #655

## What
- Force caveman-compress file I/O through UTF-8 reads and writes.
- Write backups and primary files through same-directory atomic replacement.
- Preserve existing file mode and report the backup path if a primary write fails.

## Why
Windows default codepages can reject characters like arrows during `Path.write_text()` and truncate the target before raising. Atomic UTF-8 writes avoid the codepage crash and keep the original/backup recoverable on write failure.

## Coverage added
- Non-cp1252 compressed output writes successfully via UTF-8.
- Primary write failure leaves original and backup intact and prints backup location.
- Atomic replacement preserves existing file mode.
