title: Auto-Clarity English example block leaks verbatim into non-English sessions
body:
## Environment
- Claude Code CLI 2.1.205 (`claude -p`, single-shot), macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
- caveman: main @ 0d95a81
- Models: claude-opus-4-8, claude-fable-5
- Arms per the evals honesty rule: skill arm = `"Answer concisely.\n\n"` + `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` (+ level line); control = `"Answer concisely."` only

## Issue
The Auto-Clarity section's only concrete output template (SKILL.md lines 69–74) is an English warning block. In a Korean session that triggers Auto-Clarity, the model can reproduce that English template near-verbatim inside an otherwise all-Korean response — violating the Rules-section promise "Preserve user's dominant language. … Compress the style, not the language" (line 23).

## Reproduction (`full` level, Korean)
Prompt: `users 테이블에서 컬럼 드랍하는 마이그레이션인데 지금 실행해도 안전할까?`

The response was Korean throughout (checklist, follow-up questions, particles intact) — except the Auto-Clarity warning, emitted in English, structurally matching the SKILL.md line 70 example:

> **Warning:** Dropping a column permanently deletes that column's data and cannot be undone by re-running the migration. Verify a backup or snapshot exists before running it against any shared or production database.

Intermittent: the same prompt at `ultra` localized correctly — a full-sentence Korean warning ending `Caveman 재개.` (the Korean analog of the example's `Caveman resume.`). Auto-Clarity detection itself fired correctly in both runs; only the output language flips.

## Hypothesis
The English block is the section's only concrete exemplar. Under the Auto-Clarity trigger the model reaches for the nearest template and reproduces it literally, language included.

## Suggested fix
One added line in the Auto-Clarity section marking the example as format-only — the warning must be written in the session language. PR to follow.

Related: #658 keeps the response language generally (complementary — no shared surface; this issue is about the hardcoded example template specifically). Raw transcripts retained, happy to attach.

title: SKILL.md: English-centric drop rules degrade Korean at full/ultra — particle drops flip subject/object; in-context wenyan examples leak hanja into Korean output
body:
## Environment
- Claude Code CLI 2.1.205 (`claude -p` single-shot and `--continue` multi-turn chains), macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
- caveman: main @ 0d95a81
- Models: claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4-8
- Arms per the evals honesty rule (skill vs terse control): skill = `"Answer concisely.\n\n"` + SKILL.md + level line; control = `"Answer concisely."` only

## Issue
Two Rules-section lines interact badly in Korean sessions.

Line 21:

> Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler … Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for").

Line 23:

> Preserve user's dominant language. … Compress the style, not the language.

**Defect 1 — particle drops flip subject/object.** Line 21's drop list is English morphology. Korean has no articles; the nearest small grammatical morphemes are case particles (조사: 이/가/을/를/은/는/에/에서/…), which — unlike articles — carry subject/object case relations. When "drop articles" generalizes onto Korean and "short synonyms" pushes toward a transitive-verb stand-in, compression deletes exactly the morpheme that disambiguates who does what to whom. That is a comprehension break, i.e. a violation of line 23's own promise.

**Defect 2 — hanja leaks into Korean output.** The six wenyan example outputs (lines 47–56) sit in context every session. Under `ultra`'s compression pressure the model occasionally swaps a Korean word for a classical character to shorten (있음 → 有). Korean users experience this as random hanja appearing mid-sentence in otherwise normal Korean answers.

## Reproduction

**Defect 1 (`ultra` + skill).** Prompt: `React 컴포넌트가 계속 리렌더링되는 이유가 뭐야?` — item 1 of the answer, verbatim:

> 1. **부모 리렌더** — 부모 그리면 자식도 그림. `React.memo`로 차단.

`그리다` ("draw", chosen as compressed stand-in for "render") is transitive. With the subject particle dropped, `부모 그리면` reads more naturally as "if (you) draw the parent" than "if the parent renders". The terse control compressed the same fact unambiguously via noun-compound form: `부모 리렌더 → 자식 전부 리렌더`. Skill-induced, not inherent to concise Korean.

**Defect 2 — three evidence tiers.**

1. **Field-condition repro.** Four 12-turn Korean-only conversations (no prompt ever mentions anything Chinese/classical; a per-turn caveman reminder was prefixed to each prompt, mimicking the UserPromptSubmit hook). 48 assistant turns → 1 hanja occurrence (claude-fable-5, turn 6): a cache-invalidation comparison table cell compressing 있음 to a single classical character:

   > `| CDC 이벤트 | 중상 (지연 有) | 높음 | …`

   ≈2% per turn — matches the intermittent, random pattern reported from real usage.
2. **Amplified mechanism repro.** Twenty 2-turn sessions (claude-opus-4-8): turn 1 elicits a wenyan-register answer into history, turn 2 asks a plain Korean question. **16/20** turn-2 outputs contained classical characters — 15 stuck in full wenyan register (a one-off wenyan-style request persists as if the level had been switched), 1 mixed Korean+hanja. With an explicit "이제 평소처럼 한국어로" cue: 0/1. The model readily borrows in-context classical material for Korean answers under compression pressure.
3. **Single-turn negative control.** 29 single-shot skill-arm outputs (lite/full/ultra, both models): 0 hanja. The trigger needs accumulated context — consistent with tier 1's low per-turn rate.

## Not reproduced / honest scope
- `lite`: clean across all runs — its own row scopes the failure away ("Keep articles + full sentences").
- Particle damage is not universal: object-particle drops on intransitive verbs or telegraphic noun+verb pairs read as standard Korean note register, unambiguous. The break needs the transitive-verb + dropped-case-particle interaction.

## Hypothesis
Line 21 is written in English morphology; applied to particle-marked (agglutinative) languages it maps onto case particles that carry grammatical relations articles don't. The wenyan examples supply in-context classical-character material that `ultra`'s "one word when one word enough" pressure occasionally borrows for Korean output; once any classical register enters conversation history, the effect compounds (16/20).

## Suggested fix (PR to follow, ≤10 added lines, pure addition to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`)
1. Rules section: scope "drop articles" to article languages — particles/case-markers are grammar, keep them; compress politeness/hedging/filler instead. Principle stated generally (no language-name list, per #665's concern), one Korean Not/Yes pair.
2. After the wenyan examples: classical characters belong to wenyan modes only; never swap a word to a classical character to shorten; a one-off classical-style request covers that answer only.

## Relationship to open work
- #658 — complementary: that PR keeps the response language; this fixes compression quality *within* the language. SKILL.md-only, no hook surface.
- #667 — no conflict: line 23 untouched, additions only.
- #665 — the fix deliberately avoids adding language-name tokens to always-in-context text.
- #536 — wenyan untouched, only scoped.

Raw transcripts (67 outputs across all conditions) retained; happy to attach.

title: fix(skill): keep particles, scope hanja to wenyan
body:
Fixes #680.

## Problem

Korean sessions break SKILL.md's own promise ("Preserve user's dominant language. … Compress the style, not the language", Rules section):

1. **Particle drops flip subject/object.** "Drop articles (a/an/the)" is English morphology; models generalize it to Korean case particles (조사), which carry the case relations themselves. Reproduced at `ultra`: `부모 그리면 자식도 그림` — with the subject particle dropped and a transitive verb, agent/patient flips. The terse control compressed the same fact unambiguously.
2. **Classical characters leak into Korean output.** The six in-context wenyan examples supply classical-character material that compression pressure occasionally borrows (있음 → 有). Field-reproduced: 4×12-turn Korean-only sessions (no prompt mentions anything classical), 1/48 turns emitted hanja inside an otherwise normal Korean table cell (`지연 有`) — matching the intermittent pattern Korean users report.

## Fix — 10 added lines in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, pure addition, no line rewritten

1. **Rules:** scope "drop articles" to article languages; case particles and connective endings are grammar — keep them, compress politeness/hedging/filler instead. Stated as a general principle (no language-name list, per #665's drift concern) + one Korean Not/Yes pair mirroring the existing example format.
2. **After the wenyan examples:** classical characters and wenyan register belong to wenyan modes only — never swap a word to a classical character to shorten (있음, never 有; 연결, never 連結).
3. **Final line:** per-answer script guard (recency anchor).

## Measured results (real runs)

Token savings — Korean, `ultra`, **skill vs terse** per the repo's honest-delta rule, claude-fable-5, 10 prompts, tiktoken o200k (approximates Claude tokenizer for CJK; ratios meaningful, absolutes approximate):

| | before fix | after fix |
|---|---|---|
| median savings | 8.8% | **23.3%** |
| pooled savings | 8.9% | **25.1%** |
| worst prompt | **−27.7%** (worse than terse) | +8.1% |

The particle rule gives the model an explicit Korean compression strategy (cut politeness forms/hedging/filler, keep particles), so savings become consistent instead of occasionally negative.

Particle ambiguity — `ultra`, the #680 React repro prompt, 5 after-fix runs: **0/5** ambiguous transitive clauses; the same clause now renders with the particle retained (`부모가 그리면 자식도 그림`).

Hanja under adversarial stress — 20 two-turn sessions (claude-opus-4-8), turn 1 elicits a wenyan-register answer into history, turn 2 asks plain Korean: before **16/20** turn-2 outputs contained classical characters → after **11/20**. Honest limitation: register momentum in conversation history partially beats system-prompt text; this diff halves the adversarial case but does not eliminate it (noted in #680 — full elimination likely needs hook-level handling). The field condition — no wenyan in history, leakage from the in-context examples alone — is the primary target.

Single-shot Korean after fix: 0 hanja across 30 outputs.

## Relationship to open work

- **#658** — complementary, no textual conflict (its SKILL.md hunk inserts after L11; these sit at ~L25/L60/EOF). Its "article/filler-drop rules apply to the per-language equivalent" clause needs exactly this guardrail so models don't pick particles as the Korean article-equivalent.
- **#667** — line 23 untouched; additions only.
- **#665** — no new language-name tokens in always-in-context rules.
- **#536** — wenyan modes untouched, only scoped.
- `plugins/caveman/skills/` mirror left for the CI sync workflow per CLAUDE.md.

Raw transcripts of all runs retained; happy to attach.

title: caveman-compress: missing encoding="utf-8" on file I/O corrupts non-ASCII files on Windows (data loss, no crash)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py` (and `validate.py`, `detect.py`) call `Path.read_text()` / `Path.write_text()` without an explicit `encoding` argument. Python falls back to the OS locale's preferred encoding — on a Korean-locale Windows machine that's `cp949`, not UTF-8.

This silently corrupts any UTF-8 source file containing non-ASCII characters (Korean text, em dashes, arrows, etc.), and in the worst case **truncates the original file to 0 bytes with no usable backup**.

## Root cause

- `filepath.read_text(errors="ignore")` (compress.py:249) decodes UTF-8 bytes as cp949 → mojibake, with `errors="ignore"` silently dropping bytes it can't decode (lossy, not reversible).
- That already-corrupted text is what gets sent to the LLM for compression and what gets written to the backup file.
- `filepath.write_text(compressed)` (compress.py:313) encodes the LLM's compressed output back with the locale codec. `Path.write_text` opens the file in `'w'` mode, which **truncates immediately on open**. If the compressed text contains a character not representable in the locale codec (e.g. an em dash `—`, common in the LLM's own output style), `str.encode()` raises `UnicodeEncodeError` mid-write — after truncation, before any bytes are flushed. Net effect: the original file is left at **0 bytes**, the exception bubbles up to `cli.py`'s generic `except Exception` handler, and the user sees a generic `❌ Error: 'cp949' codec can't encode character ...` with no indication the source file was just destroyed.
- `validate.py`'s `read_file()` has the same missing-encoding bug when comparing original vs. compressed.

## Repro

On Windows with a non-English system locale (e.g. Korean, `cp949`):

```powershell
py -m scripts "path\to\some_korean_language.md"
```

Any `.md` file containing Korean text (or other non-cp1252/cp949-safe punctuation) is at risk. In our case this corrupted a project `CLAUDE.md` (truncated to 0 bytes) and a global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (fully mojibake'd, including its on-disk backup, since the backup is written from the already-mis-decoded text) with no clean way to recover — we only recovered because the original text happened to still be visible earlier in the conversation transcript.

## Fix

Explicitly pass `encoding="utf-8"` on every `read_text` / `write_text` call in `compress.py`, `validate.py`, and `detect.py`. This is a one-line change per call site and fully resolves the corruption — verified locally by patching all call sites and re-running the compression successfully on the previously-affected files.

Call sites needing the fix (paths relative to `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/`):
- `compress.py`: `filepath.read_text(...)`, `backup_path.write_text(...)`, `backup_path.read_text(...)`, `filepath.write_text(...)` (×3 call sites total for write_text)
- `validate.py`: `read_file()`
- `detect.py`: the extensionless-file content sniff

## Suggested additional hardening

Independent of the encoding fix, `compress.py`'s backup flow means the *original* file (`filepath`) can be truncated by `Path.write_text()`'s truncate-on-open behavior even when the subsequent encode fails. Consider writing to a temp file in the same directory and renaming (atomic replace) instead of writing directly to `filepath`, so a mid-write encode failure can never leave the user's source file empty.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Locale: Korean (`cp949`)
- Plugin version: 0.1.0 (per `package.json`)

title: SessionStart hook reads SKILL.md from wrong path — silently serves hardcoded fallback
fix: SessionStart re-fires must not clobber an already-active mode
body:
## Problem

`caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart hook) unconditionally calls
`safeWriteFlag(flagPath, getDefaultMode())` every time it runs.
Claude Code fires SessionStart more than once per conversation
(session resume, context compaction), so any mode change made at
runtime — `/caveman ultra`, a natural-language switch, or a direct
edit of `.caveman-active` — gets silently reset back to the
configured default (project/user config file, or `full`) on the
next re-fire. In practice this shows up as caveman intensity
randomly reverting mid-session with no user action to explain it.

## Fix

Read the existing flag before deciding what to write. If it already
holds a valid mode, keep it (and skip the `off`-unlink branch too) —
SessionStart only writes the resolved default when there's no
existing flag to preserve.

## Tests

Added two regression tests to `tests/test_hooks.py`:
- `test_activate_preserves_existing_flag_across_rerun` — pre-seeds
  `.caveman-active` with `ultra`, re-runs the hook, asserts the flag
  and emitted ruleset both stay on `ultra` instead of reverting to
  the default `full`.
- `test_activate_writes_default_when_no_existing_flag` — confirms
  the original "write configured default when nothing is set yet"
  behavior is unchanged.

Full suite (`tests/test_hooks.py`, `test_mode_tracker.py`,
`test_detect.py`, `test_validate_inline.py`,
`test_compress_safety.py`, `test_repo_local_config.js`,
`test_symlink_flag.js`) passes locally with no regressions.

title: fix(evals): make llm_run.py fault-tolerant (save partial snapshot on failure)
body:
## Problem
evals/llm_run.py ran every prompt x arm with no error handling and subprocess.run(check=True). A single failed claude -p call (auth expiry, rate limit, transient network, or a bad CAVEMAN_EVAL_MODEL) aborted the entire multi-dollar run and wrote nothing - SNAPSHOT.write_text(...) is the last statement in main().

Reproduced locally: mocking subprocess.run to fail on the 2nd call makes the real main() crash with CalledProcessError after 2 calls, with no results.json produced.

## Fix
- safe_run() wraps each claude call, catching CalledProcessError / TimeoutExpired / any exception and recording an __ERROR__: marker instead of crashing.
- run_claude now takes a timeout (via CAVEMAN_EVAL_TIMEOUT, default 300s) so a hung call cannot block the whole run forever.
- On any failure the run still writes results.partial.json (progress saved) and exits non-zero; the canonical results.json is left untouched, so CI measure.py stays correct.

## Test
- Add evals/test_llm_run.py (stdlib unittest, no claude CLI needed): the success path writes the canonical snapshot; a mid-run failure no longer crashes, writes the partial snapshot, and leaves the canonical untouched.

Verified locally: both cases pass.

title: Skip caveman reinforcement on scheduled-task (unattended) runs
body:
## Problem

The `caveman-mode-tracker.js` UserPromptSubmit hook injects the per-turn "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE" reinforcement on **every** session, including Claude Code scheduled-task (cron) runs, which are unattended.

On a lightweight scheduled task the caveman persona overrides the task prompt and the model responds with a greeting like **"Yo. What need?"** instead of doing the task. In my setup this silently broke a scheduled `trigger-runner` that fires due follow-up actions: it greeted every hour instead of polling. SessionStart activation alone is (by design) too weak to cause this; the per-turn reinforcement is what flips the model into caveman voice.

## Fix

Claude Code wraps scheduled runs in a `<scheduled-task name=... file=...>` marker at the start of the prompt. When that marker is present, return early, before any flag mutation or reinforcement. Interactive chat is unaffected.

```js
if (/<scheduled-task\b/.test(prompt)) return;
```

## Test

Added a regression test to `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js`:

- active flag + scheduled-task prompt -> **no** output (the guard)
- same active flag + ordinary prompt -> reinforced (control, proves it is the guard and not an inactive flag)

```
3 passed, 0 failed
```

title: Pre-tool-call narration lines emitted in English during Chinese sessions, despite full-mode's "no tool-call narration" rule
body:
## Environment
- Claude Code CLI, plugin install (`claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman` + `claude plugin install caveman@caveman`, scope: user)
- caveman: main @ 0d95a81
- caveman level: `full`
- Session language: Chinese throughout (all user prompts Chinese)

## Issue
With caveman `full` active in an all-Chinese session, the final substantive answer to the user is correctly written in Chinese (per the Rules-section promise "Preserve user's dominant language … Compress the style, not the language"). But the short one-line status statement emitted immediately before each tool call (the harness convention of stating one sentence before invoking a tool) comes out in English, or English-verb + Chinese-noun mixed — even though it's the same turn, same model, same session.

Observed in a real (unrelated) project session:
- Before a Bash call: `Verify. Check EDI code carrier分支.`
- Before another Bash call: `Read send dialog + G1/G2/G4 guard 看是否真共用同一发送机制。`
- The turn's actual answer bullet, fully Chinese: `不是"完全没变化只是PDF不一样"。发送机制共用一套，但有实质分支。`

Note: caveman `full` mode's own Intensity table explicitly says **"No tool-call narration"** — so arguably these lines shouldn't be emitted at all, in any language. Their presence suggests the narration-suppression rule isn't reliably honored, and when narration does slip through, it isn't covered by the language-preservation rule either (that rule's wording targets "reply", and this status line may not register as "the reply" to the model).

## Hypothesis
The pre-tool-call narration is a harness-level convention independent of SKILL.md, so SKILL.md's language-preservation rule doesn't obviously apply to it. When caveman `full` compresses it into terse fragments, the compression pattern likely borrows sentence structure from SKILL.md's own English-only examples (e.g. "Bug in auth middleware. Fix:") — same general mechanism as #679 and #665 (English-only in-context example text biasing output under compression pressure), but a different specific surface (tool narration, not the reply body or the Auto-Clarity block).

## Suggested fix
Either:
1. Extend the language-preservation rule's scope to explicitly cover any auxiliary/status text the model emits, not just the final reply, or
2. Reinforce "No tool-call narration" so this text is suppressed entirely at `full`/`ultra`, sidestepping the language question.

Related: #679 (Auto-Clarity English block leak), #665 (named-language examples risk drift under compaction) — same class of bug, different surface.

title: fix(skill): scope language-preservation rule to every emitted line
body:
Fixes #701.

## Problem

Pre-tool-call status statements (harness-required, not caveman-specific — the "state one sentence before tool use" convention) weren't covered by the Rules-section language-preservation promise, since that rule's wording targeted "reply" specifically. In a fully Chinese session with `full` active, the final answer stayed correctly Chinese, but the one-line status statement immediately before each tool call came out in English or English-verb + Chinese-noun mixed:

- `Verify. Check EDI code carrier分支.`
- `Read send dialog + G1/G2/G4 guard 看是否真共用同一发送机制。`

while the turn's actual answer bullet was fully Chinese. Repro detail and screenshots in #701.

## Fix — 2 added lines in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, pure addition, no line rewritten

One sentence appended after the existing language-preservation paragraph (Rules section), making explicit that the rule covers every line the model emits this turn, not just the final reply, and that a harness-required pre-tool-call status line must not default to English.

I considered instead just reinforcing the existing "no tool-call narration" instruction so the line wouldn't be emitted at all — but that narration is a harness-level convention outside caveman's control (the instruction to state one sentence before tool use lives in the harness system prompt, not in SKILL.md), so suppressing it isn't reliably actionable from the skill side. Scoping the language rule to cover it instead is.

Related: #679 (Auto-Clarity English block leak), #665 (named-language examples risk drift under compaction) — same class of bug (English-only in-context text biasing output under compression pressure), different surface. `plugins/caveman/skills/` mirror left for the CI sync workflow per CLAUDE.md.

title: Optional rolling-window savings suffix for the statusline
body:
## Motivation

The statusline suffix (`⛏ 346.0k`) written by `caveman-stats.js` is a lifetime total — `aggregateHistory(historyPath, null)`. Once the number gets big it barely moves, so as a statusline signal it goes stale: you can't see what caveman saved you *today*.

The stats engine already has everything needed for a windowed number: `/caveman-stats --since 24h` works, and `aggregateHistory(historyPath, sinceMs)` takes the window directly.

## Proposal

An opt-in env knob, e.g. `CAVEMAN_STATUSLINE_SINCE=24h`: when set, `caveman-stats.js` writes the suffix from `aggregateHistory(historyPath, sinceMs)` instead of the lifetime aggregate (perhaps rendered as `⛏ 12.4k/24h`). Default behavior unchanged.

## Context

I have a rolling variant working locally — an external sampler over the per-session snapshots in `.caveman-history.jsonl` that renders a delta over a configurable window next to the `[CAVEMAN]` badge — and day-to-day it's a much more interesting number than the lifetime total. Doing it natively via the existing `--since` path would be cleaner than my out-of-tree version. I don't know whether you want this in the plugin, but if so I'm happy to open a PR.

title: Add native Hermes Agent plugin support
body:
**What you want**

Caveman should use Hermes Agent's native plugin APIs instead of stopping at skills-only installation.

What exists today on `main`:

- Hermes is detected by the unified installer.
- The seven Caveman skills can be copied into Hermes (`#524`).
- Hermes can read the skill instructions when they are explicitly selected.

What is still missing:

- Native turn hooks that persist and reinforce Caveman mode across sessions.
- Deterministic `/caveman` mode control and safe natural-language activation/deactivation.
- Hermes `SessionDB`-backed token statistics with measured per-mode attribution.
- Provider-agnostic, revision-bound document compression with validation, backup, and atomic replacement.
- A native `hermes caveman init` command for project-only rule installation.
- Ownership-aware install, reinstall, disable, uninstall, and optional MCP-shrink lifecycle that preserves user-modified files and unrelated Hermes config.
- Native Cavecrew routing through Hermes `delegate_task` rather than Claude-specific subagent tools.

Desired behavior:

- Installing Caveman for Hermes installs and enables one native plugin plus the seven existing skills.
- New Hermes sessions default to configured Caveman mode and inject the matching skill guidance each turn.
- Mode changes survive fresh processes and `off` remains durable.
- Stats read real Hermes session totals; savings remain clearly labeled estimates.
- Compression never invokes a hard-coded provider and never replaces a file unless the exact prepared revision still matches.
- Disable preserves files/state; uninstall removes only unchanged owned content and preserves lifetime history unless explicitly purged.

**Before/after example**
```text
Before: Hermes receives Caveman SKILL.md files, but has no native hooks, commands,
        persistent mode, SessionDB stats, safe compression tools, or owned lifecycle.

After:  `node bin/install.js --only hermes` installs an enabled native plugin.
        `/caveman ultra` persists across sessions, each turn receives scoped guidance,
        `caveman_stats` reads Hermes SessionDB, compression uses prepare/apply revision
        tokens, and uninstall preserves user-owned content and unrelated config.
```

**Why good**

Hermes already exposes the plugin surfaces Caveman needs. Using those native APIs gives Hermes users feature parity without adding Hermes-core patches, provider coupling, network dependencies, or global shell hooks.

This is narrower than the general Hermes-support request in `#427`: it covers the runtime parity missing after the skills-only work in `#524`. Related installer/docs discussions: `#475`, `#476`, `#525`, `#545`, and `#611`.

title: feat: add native Hermes Agent plugin support
body:
Closes #706

Related: #427, #475, #476, #524, #525, #545, #611

## What changed

Adds native Hermes Agent support as one focused integration:

- Registers three Hermes hooks: `on_session_start`, `pre_llm_call`, and `post_llm_call`.
- Registers `/caveman`, `/caveman-init`, `hermes caveman init`, seven skills, and three native tools.
- Persists mode under `HERMES_HOME`, including durable `off` and fresh-process continuity.
- Uses Hermes `SessionDB` cumulative token totals for measured per-turn/mode attribution.
- Adds `caveman_prepare_compression` / `caveman_apply_compression`; the active provider proposes text, while the plugin validates protected structure, exact digest/metadata, backup integrity, and atomic replacement.
- Routes Cavecrew through Hermes-native `delegate_task` and removes Claude-specific `Task` assumptions from the Hermes path.
- Extends the unified installer with native install/reinstall/disable/uninstall and optional MCP-shrink registration.
- Documents install, commands, state, privacy, MCP, verification, and uninstall behavior.

## Ownership and safety

- Installer writes an explicit SHA-256 ownership manifest.
- Reinstall updates unchanged owned files, removes obsolete unchanged payload, and preserves modified/unowned files.
- Uninstall rejects non-canonical manifest paths, symlink/non-regular collisions, and digest mismatches; ephemeral cleanup is anchored with `dir_fd` and `O_NOFOLLOW`.
- `--force` collision replacement creates verified backups; exact previous MCP config is restored on uninstall.
- MCP command input is tokenized into argv and never executed through a shell.
- Runtime state uses private permissions, no-follow opens, atomic replacement, and POSIX cross-process locks.
- Compression refuses sensitive/unsupported paths, stale revisions, source races, changed protected content, existing backups, and non-regular files; final commit claims the source entry and installs only if its pathname remains absent.
- Default uninstall preserves lifetime history; `--purge-history` is explicit and symlink-safe.
- Plugin security-policy inspection happens through Hermes' own config parser before enable; failed lifecycle phases restore exact plugin/MCP state and return non-zero globally.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 136 passed.
- Hermes/Python discovery — 53 passed.
- Broad Node suites — 7/7 tests passed.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` — passed.
- `npm pack --dry-run --json` — 105 entries; required Hermes payload present; no `__pycache__`, bytecode, or `.env` artifacts.
- Disposable Hermes Agent v0.18.2 acceptance — real install and plugin discovery; 3 hooks, 3 tools, 2 commands, 7 skills; SessionDB stats; prepare/apply compression with verified backup; fresh-process mode persistence; uninstall directly from disabled state; exact sibling config, generated security policy, and lifetime history cleanup verified.
- All acceptance paths isolated `HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, and XDG directories; no active user profile was modified.

## Distribution note

Top-level skill sources remain canonical. CI will resync the Cavecrew mirror under `plugins/caveman/skills/...` after merge.

title: fix: make caveman hooks robust to non-standard or absent interpreters
body:
## Summary
Two coordinated changes that both serve issue #65's theme. (1) Portable shebangs: change `src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh`, `src/hooks/install.sh`, and `src/hooks/uninstall.sh` from hardcoded `#!/bin/bash` to `#!/usr/bin/env bash` (keep `bash` where the scripts use bash-isms; downgrade `caveman-statusline.sh` to `#!/usr/bin/env sh` only if it is verified POSIX-clean).

## Why this matters
Installing the caveman plugin emits `Plugin hook error: /bin/sh: line 1: node: command not found` (SessionStart) and `UserPromptSubmit hook error` for users whose environment does not expose `node` on the hook runner's PATH, or who have no Node at all. Three distinct reporters confirmed it: a NixOS user (`sh` not at the usual path), a Bun-only user (no `node`), and a Debian user who intentionally runs without Node. The literal ask in the title is to use portable `#!/usr/bin/env` shebangs; the thread's most detailed comment (cgty, 2026-07-13) clarifies the real failure: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` launches the hooks as bare `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/*.js"`, so a shebang change alone cannot help when Node is absent. The single concern is: caveman's hooks must not hard-fail the Claude Code session when the interpreter is at a non-standard path or missing.

## Testing
- Happy path: with `node` on PATH, `run-hook.sh <script.js>` execs Node and the hook runs exactly as before (existing `tests/test_hooks.py` behavior preserved).
- Node absent: with a PATH that has no `node`, `run-hook.sh` exits 0 and produces no error, so the session start / prompt submit degrades gracefully.
- Structural: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit commands route through `run-hook.sh` (no bare `node` invocation remains).
- Shebang assertions: `src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh`, `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh` start with a `#!/usr/bin/env` shebang, not a hardcoded `#!/bin/bash`.
- Regression: `bash src/hooks/install.sh` still installs the statusline hook and writes settings.json correctly (existing `HookScriptTests` continue to pass).

Fixes #65

AI was used for assistance.

title: fix: strip Claude-schema tools frontmatter so cavecrew agents load on Gemini/Antigravity
body:
## What

Fixes #497 - caveman fails to load on Google Antigravity / Gemini CLI.

## Why

Installing the extension with `gemini extensions install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman` makes Gemini's ExtensionManager reject all three cavecrew agents:

```
Validation failed: Agent Definition: tools.0: Invalid tool name
```

The `agents/cavecrew-*.md` files carry Claude Code schema frontmatter (`tools: [Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob]`). Gemini validates each entry against its own tool vocabulary and refuses the Claude names, so the cavecrew subagents never load and the extension is broken on Antigravity. This is the same class of schema mismatch already fixed for opencode in #386 via `stripOpencodeAgentTools()`.

## How

Mirror the opencode #386 fix on the Gemini/Antigravity distribution path, reusing the proven transform:

- `bin/lib/opencode-agent.js`: generalize the existing helper into a schema-agnostic `stripAgentTools()` that removes the frontmatter `tools:` key (and its wrapped continuation lines), keeping `stripOpencodeAgentTools` as a thin alias so the existing opencode call site and test stay unchanged.
- `bin/install.js`: after `gemini extensions install` lands the extension at `~/.gemini/extensions/caveman/agents/`, rewrite the three installed cavecrew agent files in place with the `tools:` line stripped (Gemini then falls back to its default tool set; the subagent prompts already self-restrict scope in their bodies). The same strip is applied to the Antigravity `npx skills` agent copies. Missing files are skipped silently, honoring the installer's fail-soft-on-filesystem-error invariant.

Top-level source-of-truth agents are untouched, so the Claude plugin mirror still ships the full `tools:` schema via CI. Only the Gemini/Antigravity on-disk copies are rewritten.

## Tests

Adds `tests/installer/gemini-agents.test.mjs` (5 cases): only the frontmatter `tools:` key is stripped (inline body prose preserved), opencode-alias equivalence and idempotency, end-to-end Gemini install strips every distributed agent, `--force` re-run idempotency + missing-file skip, and the Antigravity path. The existing `tests/installer/opencode-agent.test.mjs` continues to pass unchanged.

```
$ node --test tests/installer/gemini-agents.test.mjs
# tests 5 | pass 5 | fail 0
$ node --test tests/installer/opencode-agent.test.mjs
# tests 9 | pass 9 | fail 0
```

title: statusline: empty .caveman-statusline-suffix file makes script exit 1 — Claude Code hides the status bar
body:
## Summary

If `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-statusline-suffix` exists but is **empty** (0 bytes), `src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh` prints the badge correctly but exits with status **1**. Claude Code hides the status bar entirely when the statusline command exits non-zero, so the caveman badge silently disappears even though the script's stdout is fine.

## Root cause

The savings-suffix block is the last thing in the script:

```bash
if [ "${CAVEMAN_STATUSLINE_SAVINGS:-1}" != "0" ]; then
  SAVINGS_FILE="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/.caveman-statusline-suffix"
  if [ -f "$SAVINGS_FILE" ] && [ ! -L "$SAVINGS_FILE" ]; then
    SAVINGS=$(head -c 64 "$SAVINGS_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\000-\037')
    [ -n "$SAVINGS" ] && printf ' \033[38;5;172m%s\033[0m' "$SAVINGS"
  fi
fi
```

When the suffix file exists but is empty (or contains only control bytes), `[ -n "$SAVINGS" ]` is false, so the `A && B` compound returns 1. Since it's the last command executed, the whole script exits 1.

The same failure mode applies to a suffix file that ends up empty for any reason — e.g. a `caveman-stats.js` run interrupted mid-write, or a session with no recorded savings.

## Repro

```bash
touch "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/.caveman-statusline-suffix"
echo '{}' | bash src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh; echo "exit=$?"
# prints the badge, then: exit=1
# → Claude Code stops rendering the status bar
```

## Fix

Terminate the script with an explicit success, e.g. append at the end:

```bash
exit 0
```

(or restructure so `[ -n "$SAVINGS" ] && printf ...` isn't the final command, e.g. `if [ -n "$SAVINGS" ]; then printf ...; fi`). Verified locally that with `exit 0` appended, all three states — no suffix file, empty suffix file, populated suffix file — exit 0 and render correctly.

## Environment

- caveman plugin via Claude Code plugin marketplace (cache rev `0d95a81d35a9`); bug also present in current `main`
- Claude Code on Linux (RHEL 9), bash 5.x

title: Tool-call silence rule does not define direct-call behavior or exceptions
body:
**What happen**

`skills/caveman/SKILL.md` says `No tool-call narration`, but it does not define what counts as narration, when a tool should be called directly, what may be emitted between chained tool calls, or which safety/ambiguity cases justify text before a call. Models can therefore satisfy the rule loosely while still emitting a preamble, plan, progress update, or reason before routine tool calls.

#713 reports the broader Claude token-bloat symptom, but its scope is not specific enough to make one policy change independently reviewable. This issue narrows that report to model-authored text immediately around tool calls; it does not claim to resolve every source of provider verbosity.

**Expected**

- When the next action is safe and unambiguous, call the tool directly.
- Do not emit a preamble, plan, progress update, or reason immediately before the call.
- After a tool result, call the next tool directly instead of announcing it.
- Emit only a material result or a next action requiring user input.
- Allow text first when clarification, a security/risk warning, irreversible-action confirmation, or ambiguity resolution is required.
- State the limitation honestly: prompt text cannot override higher-priority provider/harness instructions or mechanically suppress their output.

**Before/after example**

```text
Input: Read package.json and tell me the test command.
Before: I'll inspect package.json first so I can identify the configured test script.
        [tool call]
After:  [tool call with no preceding prose]
        Test command: npm run test.
```

**Acceptance**

- [x] The canonical `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` contains the complete policy above.
- [x] A focused repository check guards every policy boundary and fails against current `main`.
- [x] Generated skill mirrors remain owned by the existing CI sync.
- [x] The change remains independent from open PRs.

**Platform**

- [x] Claude Code — initial report/reproduction
- [x] Codex — shared policy applies, but native-plugin UAT exposed a higher-priority host conflict described below
- [x] Other: Hermes Agent — native integration UAT described below

**Cross-host UAT**

- **Codex CLI 0.144.4, project `AGENTS.md`: PASS.** Routine and chained-tool scenarios emitted no `agent_message` before tool calls; clarification appeared only after evidence collection.
- **Codex CLI 0.144.4, native local-marketplace plugin: HOST BLOCKED.** Codex loaded the exact final candidate skill, then emitted two intermediate progress `agent_message` events during the ambiguity scenario. The skill alone cannot guarantee suppression where higher-priority host instructions conflict; this proposed policy does not claim otherwise.
- **Hermes Agent 0.18.2 with native integration from #707: PASS for model-authored text.** After an exact-source reinstall into a disposable `HERMES_HOME`, routine and clarification sessions had 1 and 2 assistant tool-call records respectively, all with empty `content`; final material output/clarification followed the tool chain. Hermes may still render provider reasoning summaries separately, which is harness output and outside this policy's control.

**Version / install method**

Related: #713. This issue narrows its broad token-bloat report to a testable tool-call policy.
Related: #701 and #702. Those cover language preservation when a harness-required status line is emitted; they do not define whether routine narration should be emitted.

title: fix(skill): define tool-call silence
body:
Closes #714

Related: #713, #701, #702

## What changes

- expands the canonical `No tool-call narration` rule into an explicit before/between/after tool-call contract;
- requires chained tool calls to proceed directly instead of announcing the next call;
- preserves clarification, security/risk, irreversible-action, and ambiguity exceptions;
- states that prompt text cannot override higher-priority provider/harness instructions or mechanically suppress their output;
- adds a focused repository verifier for every policy boundary.

## Before / after

Before: `No tool-call narration` left `narration`, chained calls, and exceptions undefined.

After: safe, unambiguous actions call tools directly; no preamble, plan, progress update, or reason precedes a call; a chained call is not announced; post-tool prose is limited to a material result or an action requiring user input.

This remains narrower than #713's general verbosity report. It does not overlap #702's language-preservation change: that PR governs the language of a harness-required status line, while this PR defines when model-authored narration should be absent and explicitly records higher-priority host limitations.

## Scope

- canonical `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` only;
- focused verifier in `tests/verify_repo.py`;
- no generated mirror or ZIP edits; CI will resync `plugins/caveman/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` and `dist/caveman.skill` after merge;
- no claim of deterministic provider-output suppression or override of higher-priority host instructions.

## Cross-host UAT

| Host/path | Result | Evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex CLI 0.144.4 with candidate policy as project `AGENTS.md` | PASS | Routine call started with tool execution; chained investigation had no intermediate `agent_message`; clarification was final material output. |
| Codex CLI 0.144.4 native local-marketplace plugin | HOST BLOCKED | Codex loaded the exact final candidate skill, then emitted two intermediate progress `agent_message` events in the ambiguity scenario. The skill alone cannot guarantee suppression where higher-priority host instructions conflict. |

Provider reasoning summaries may still be rendered by the harness. |

- RED 2: Codex chained-tool UAT exposed narration allowed by the original `material result or next action` wording.
- RED 3: focused verifier failed on `After a tool result, call the next tool directly` before the chained-call refinement.

body:
## Problem

The lifetime number has two problems: it is incomplete, and what it shows talks like an accountant.

History has one writer: `main()` in `src/hooks/caveman-stats.js` (append at `:495-506`), and it runs only when the user types `/caveman-stats` (`skills/caveman-stats/SKILL.md`: "Triggers on /caveman-stats"). Forget the command → session never counted. `--all`, `--since 7d`, and the `⛏` statusline badge undercount forever. Verified on main @ 0d95a81.

```
Before: 10 caveman sessions, /caveman-stats typed in 2

Caveman Stats — Lifetime
──────────────────────────
Sessions:   2                  ← 8 sessions gone. pile has hole.
Output tokens:         81,340
Est. tokens saved:     151,060
Est. saved (USD):      ~$2.27
```

## Request

1. **SessionEnd hook auto-records a snapshot.** New `--record` flag on `caveman-stats.js`: same parse → attribute → append path, no stdout. Safe by design — `aggregateHistory` keeps only the latest row per `session_id` (`:492-494`), so extra appends fold away. Verified end-to-end on Claude Code v2.1.212: `SessionEnd` delivers `{session_id, transcript_path, reason}` on stdin, and the **unmodified** script already appends the correct row from `transcript_path` (622 output tokens / 2 turns; `est_saved_tokens: 0` with caveman off — no savings invented). A hard-killed session gets no `SessionEnd`; the dedup above means a per-turn upgrade can close that gap later.

2. **`--all` grunts like caveman.** Same numbers, same honesty rules (`est.` labels, output-only, never call it "usage" — per the `outputReductionPct` comment), caveman voice:

```
After:

~$11.50 stay in cave

```

Two PRs if preferred — record first, grunt second. One concern per PR.

## Why good

The repo already treats invented savings as a bug (#601, docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md) — undercounting is the same sickness in the other direction. #703's rolling statusline window only means something over dense history. And the pile view makes the user smile on every `--all`. Small mouth, big pile.

title: Resolve OS command injection in /app/caveman/bin/install.js
body:
**Title**: Command Injection via Malicious Directory Name or MCP Command (Windows)
**Vulnerability Type**: OS command injection
**File Path**: `/app/caveman/bin/install.js`

#### Analysis
The `spawnXplat` function in `bin/install.js` is used to execute commands on Windows with `shell: true`. When joining arguments to form the command string, it uses a `quoteWinArg` helper that only adds double quotes if the argument contains a space or a double quote. It does not escape or quote other shell meta-characters such as `&`, `|`, `(`, `)`, `<`, `>`, `^`, or `%`. 

An attacker can exploit this by:
1. Trick a user into running the installer (e.g., via `npx`) from a directory whose name contains a meta-character (e.g., `C:\projects\repo&calc&`). The `runInit` function passes `process.cwd()` as an argument to `runSpawn`, which calls `spawnXplat`.
2. Providing a malicious string to the `--with-mcp-shrink` flag (e.g., `--with-mcp-shrink="npx & calc"`). The installer will then execute a command string containing the unquoted `&`, leading to arbitrary command execution by `cmd.exe`.

title: stats: surface the net-negative regime (#145), not just gross savings
body:
## The pain

`docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` is blunt about when caveman loses:

> the skill costs ~1–1.5k input tokens every turn. If it saves less output than that, you are paying to use it.

#145 measured exactly that. But the tool the docs point users to — `/caveman-stats` — can't show it. `deriveSavings` only computes gross output savings, so `Est. tokens saved` is always positive and the net-negative case is invisible in the one instrument meant to reveal it. The page's own creed — *"If caveman lose for your workload, this page tell you to turn it off"* — isn't wired into the page.

## The change

Adds the missing half:

- **`Est. rule overhead`** — the per-turn input cost of the injected rules (default `1250` tokens ≈ the ~5 KB `SKILL.md` at the ~4-chars/token approximation already used here; override with `CAVEMAN_RULE_OVERHEAD_TOKENS` if you've measured your own setup).
- **`Est. net`** = output saved − rule input. Negative → it says so and tells you to turn caveman off for that workload.

Shown in the single-mode session view and the lifetime `--all` view.

Before / after on a short reply (120 output tokens, 1 turn, `full`):

```
Est. tokens saved:     223 (~65% of output)          # previously the whole story
Est. rule overhead:    1,250 (input, ~1,250/turn over 1 turn)
Est. net:              -1,027 (caveman cost more than it saved — turn it off for this workload)
```

## Honesty guardrails

- Net is shown only where savings can actually be estimated (full-mode spans). Unattributed spans get **no** net line — no guessing, consistent with the #601 attribution logic.
- Overhead is an estimate, labeled as such, cited to `HONEST-NUMBERS.md`; it's a named constant, env-overridable.
- No new output-token claims; the reduction line still says output-only. Lifetime net only counts sessions logged since this change (older rows carry no turn count, so they're left out rather than guessed).

## Tests

`node tests/test_caveman_stats.js` — **44 pass** (37 existing + 7 new: positive net, the negative-net #145 case, the env override, the no-guessing unattributed path, lifetime aggregation, and the legacy-row omission).

title: fix(openclaw): stop stamping stale version, add --no-always opt-out
body:
## Problem

Found while integrating caveman into an OpenClaw deployment and reading `bin/lib/openclaw.js`:

1. **Stale version stamp.** `SKILL_VERSION = '1.0.0'` is hardcoded and gets written into every installed skill's frontmatter regardless of the actual release — currently v1.9.1. `openclaw skills list` reports a version that's never been accurate since the constant was introduced.
2. **No opt-out for always-on.** `installOpenclaw()` unconditionally stamps `always: true` and writes the SOUL.md bootstrap block. There's no flag to install caveman as a discoverable, load-on-demand skill only (which the module's own top-of-file comment describes as a supported mode — "Skills there... are loaded on-demand by the model" — but nothing in the installer actually lets you land in that mode).

## Fix

Both scoped narrowly, no default-behavior change:

- **Version**: `mergeOpenclawFrontmatter()` / `installOpenclaw()` accept an explicit `version` override. `bin/install.js`'s `--only openclaw` path now passes `PINNED_REF` (already bumped on every release for hook-integrity pinning — this reuses that existing, maintained value instead of introducing a second version source). `SKILL_VERSION` stays as the fallback for callers that don't pass one explicitly.
- **`--no-always`**: new flag. Skips the `always: true` frontmatter stamp and the SOUL.md write; only the skill file is installed. Re-running `--no-always` over an already always-on install does **not** retroactively strip the existing SOUL.md block — it only changes what a *new* install does (covered by a test).

## Before / after

```diff
- version: 1.0.0
+ version: 1.9.1
```

```bash
# new: install caveman for OpenClaw without forcing always-on
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --only openclaw --no-always
```

## Tests

4 new cases in `tests/installer/e2e.freshinstall.test.mjs`:
- version threading (`CAVEMAN_REF` override → frontmatter reflects it, not the fallback)
- `--no-always`: skill written, versioned, no `always:` key, SOUL.md not created
- `--no-always` idempotency: doesn't strip a SOUL.md block from a prior always-on install

Existing openclaw suite (always-on default, idempotent re-run, uninstall, marker damage-tolerance from #596) is unmodified and still green — confirms the default install path is unchanged.

`npm test`: 113/115 pass locally, including all 4 new tests. The 2 failures are **pre-existing** — they reproduce on an unmodified checkout of `main` in this sandbox, caused by a real `claude` CLI + `~/.openclaw` present in the environment (tests documented as "skipped without `claude` CLI" detect it and take a different path). Unrelated to this change; not touched here.

## Scope note

`src/tools/caveman-init.js` (the per-repo rule-file installer) also calls `helper.installOpenclaw()` for its `openclaw` target, and is left unchanged — it's a differently-scoped tool (drops rule files for many editors into a target repo, explicitly documented as installing an "always-on caveman rule") and extending it is a separate concern per the one-PR-one-concern guidance in CONTRIBUTING.md. Happy to follow up there if useful.

title: Windows: ~/.config/caveman/config.json silently ignored — real path is %APPDATA%\caveman\config.json
body:
## Problem

On native Windows (`process.platform === 'win32'`), `getConfigDir()` in
`caveman-config.js` resolves the user config path to
`%APPDATA%\caveman\config.json`. It only falls back to
`~/.config/caveman/config.json` if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set — which it
isn't, by default, on a stock Windows install.

The doc comment at the top of `caveman-config.js` lists the resolution
order as:
  1. CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE env var
  2. repo-local .caveman/config.json / .caveman.json
  3. ~/.config/caveman/config.json (macOS / Linux fallback) — OR
     %APPDATA%\caveman\config.json (Windows fallback)
  4. 'full'

This is accurate, but easy to misread on a skim — nothing else in the
plugin (README, /caveman-help card) foregrounds the Windows-specific
path. A Windows user (or an AI assistant editing config on their
behalf, using generic Unix-style docs/muscle memory) naturally writes
`defaultMode` to `~/.config/caveman/config.json` — which resolves via
Git Bash / any POSIX-ish shell to a real, writable path
(`C:\Users\<user>\.config\caveman\config.json`) — and sees **zero
effect**, silently. No warning, no error. The file just isn't in the
lookup chain.

## Impact

Wasted a full debugging session (confirmed independently twice, same
day, in two parallel Claude Code sessions) before finding the actual
active path. Symptom looked exactly like "caveman ignores 'stop
caveman' / ignores defaultMode" — actually just two config files, one
live, one silently inert.

## Suggested fixes (any one would help)

1. On win32, also check `~/.config/caveman/config.json` as a secondary
   fallback before the hardcoded `'full'` — cheap, matches what users
   intuitively write.
2. Or: if no config is found at the platform-correct path but one
   *is* found at the other platform's path, emit a warning (stderr,
   or a SessionStart notice) — "found a config at X, but the active
   path on this OS is Y".
3. Or at minimum, make the Windows-specific path more prominent in
   README / caveman-help — right now it's one clause in a longer
   bullet.

Related: #375 (same category — Windows config-path assumption
silently no-ops, different plugin surface). #447's proposed `manual`
defaultMode would have surfaced this faster (off-by-default rather
than fighting the `full` fallback).

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell primary, Git Bash available
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`: unset

title: Benchmark results and three questions - 0 savings E2E
body:
Hi Julius — I maintain [LemonCrow](https://github.com/lemoncrow-lab/lemoncrow). I spent 10 years at Google, where part of my work involved analyzing and improving performance, cost, and latency. 

I tested Caveman as one arm in a small benchmark and wanted to share the results in case they are useful.

The question I was trying to answer was simple:

**Does a shorter answer also reduce the total cost of the agent run?**

On this workload, Caveman consistently made the answers shorter. The total cost was roughly the same as baseline.

## Results

Each run used the same 20 engineering prompts, 5 repetitions per prompt, and `claude-opus-4-8`.

| Run | Baseline cost | Caveman cost | Difference | Output difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-07-08 | $8.928 | $8.773 | -1.74% | -43.0% |
| 2026-07-16 | $8.679 | $8.575 | -1.20% | -47.7% |
| 2026-07-17 | $8.399 | $8.673 | +3.27% | -41.4% |

Combined across 300 runs per arm:

| Metric | Baseline | Caveman | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cost | $26.0058 | $26.0204 | **+0.06%** |
| Fresh input | 1,053,795 | 1,053,255 | -0.05% |
| Cache reads | 6,863,748 | 5,854,017 | -14.7% |
| Initial cached context | 879,808 | 1,339,463 | **+52.2%** |
| Extra initial context vs baseline | 0 | **+459,655** | **+1,532 per run** |
| Billed output | 369,825 | 206,894 | **-44.1%** |
| Total token volume | 9,167,176 | 8,453,629 | -7.8% |

My reading is that Caveman’s output reduction is real and repeatable. In these runs, the smaller output was balanced by more initial cached context, leaving the final cost close to baseline.

The historical artifacts do not preserve a separate thinking-token count, so billed output cannot be split reliably into visible text and thinking tokens.

## Three questions

1. **Does this look like a fair Caveman setup?** I used the committed [`skills/caveman/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/main/skills/caveman/SKILL.md) as the only additional system instruction for the Caveman arm. If that is not the intended setup, please let me know what should change.

2. **Are the raw API benchmark results published somewhere else?** I found the benchmark runner under `benchmarks/`, while generated `benchmarks/results/*.json` files appear to be ignored. I may simply have missed the published artifacts, so a pointer would be helpful.

3. **Do you have plans to target total run cost as well as answer length?** The shorter output is a clear benefit here, but the total cost stayed close to baseline on this workload. I would be interested to know whether reducing the added initial context is something you plan to explore.

## Data and reproduction

- [Method and per-prompt results](https://github.com/lemoncrow-lab/lemoncrow/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md#telegraphic-qa-benchmark)
- [Raw results and transcripts](https://github.com/lemoncrow-lab/lemoncrow/tree/main/benchmarks/codebench/results/telegraphic_2026_07_17)
- [Aggregate CSV](https://github.com/lemoncrow-lab/lemoncrow/blob/main/benchmarks/codebench/results/telegraphic_2026_07_17/summary.csv)

```bash
uv run lemoncrow benchmark telegraphic \
  --arm baseline --arm lemoncrow --arm caveman \
  --model claude-opus-4-8 \
  --reps 5 \
  --max-turns 50 \
  --jobs 4 \
  -y
```

Thanks for taking a look. Corrections to the setup or interpretation are welcome.

title: UserPromptSubmit hook waits for stdin EOF, so Claude Code kills it at the 5s timeout — 2.3% of runs inject nothing
body:
## Summary

`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` does all of its work inside `process.stdin.on('end', …)`. The hook therefore does nothing until the caller closes stdin — and when that EOF is late, Claude Code kills the process at its 5000 ms timeout. The flag file is never written and the per-turn reinforcement is never injected.

The failure is silent. Nothing is printed, the prompt goes through normally, and the only trace is a `hook_cancelled` attachment in the session transcript.

Not a duplicate of #538 (missing `stdin.on('error')`, already fixed on `main`) or #397 (broken-pipe socket write). Those are about stdin closing *abnormally*; this is about stdin not closing *promptly*.

## Evidence

30 days of Claude Code transcripts on one machine, counting `attachment` rows by hook:

| hook | delivered | cancelled at timeout | rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `UserPromptSubmit` — *"Tracking caveman mode…"* | 2028 | **48** | **2.3%** |
| `SessionStart:startup` — *"Loading caveman mode…"* | 223 | 1 | 0.4% |

The SessionStart hook is the control: `caveman-activate.js` never reads stdin and is essentially never cancelled. The tracker is, and the recorded `durationMs` on the cancelled runs goes up to **25618 ms** against a `timeoutMs` of 5000 — the process is sitting in the event loop waiting for an EOF, not doing work.

Reproduction against `main` (0d95a81) — write one complete payload, leave stdin open, which is exactly what a caller that has not yet closed the pipe does:

```python
p = subprocess.Popen(['node', 'src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js'], stdin=PIPE, stdout=PIPE)
p.stdin.write(b'{"prompt":"hello"}'); p.stdin.flush()   # complete payload, stdin stays open
p.wait(timeout=6)
```

```
UPSTREAM main: STILL RUNNING at 6.01s -> would be killed at the 5s hook timeout
```

With `~/.claude/.caveman-active` set to `full`, the injection the hook exists to produce is simply absent:

```
BEFORE: STILL RUNNING at 6.01s -> killed at the 5s hook timeout
   injected: b''
```

## Impact

Roughly 1 prompt in 43 loses its per-turn reinforcement — the mechanism added precisely because models drift back to prose when other plugins inject competing style instructions (#233, #303). It also means a `/caveman <level>` or `/caveman off` typed on an unlucky turn is dropped: the flag file is never written, so the mode silently does not change.

## Suggested fix

Act on a **complete payload** rather than on EOF: parse on each `data` chunk, run the body as soon as the accumulated input is valid JSON, then destroy stdin. A partial payload is not an error — it just keeps reading — and the `end` listener stays as the fallback for input that never parses.

Destroying stdin rather than calling `process.exit()` matters: stdin is the only handle holding the event loop open, so releasing it lets Node drain and flush stdout on its own, whereas exiting outright can truncate the injection.

PR follows with three regression tests, each verified red against the current hook.

title: fix(hooks): act on a complete payload instead of waiting for stdin EOF
body:
Fixes #729

`caveman-mode-tracker.js` does all of its work inside `process.stdin.on('end', …)`, so the hook sits idle until the caller closes stdin. When that EOF is late, Claude Code kills the process at its 5000 ms timeout — before the flag file is written and before the per-turn reinforcement is injected. Silently: nothing is printed, and the only trace is a `hook_cancelled` attachment in the transcript.

Measured over 30 days of transcripts on one machine: **48 of 2076** `UserPromptSubmit` runs cancelled at the timeout (**2.3%**), some with a recorded `durationMs` of 25618 against `timeoutMs: 5000`. The sibling `SessionStart` hook — which never reads stdin — was cancelled once in 224 runs. Full numbers in the issue.

## The change

Parse on each `data` chunk and run the body as soon as the accumulated input is valid JSON, then destroy stdin. A partial payload is not an error, it just keeps reading; the `end` listener stays as the fallback for input that never parses, and a `handled` flag keeps the body from running twice when both fire.

**`process.stdin.destroy()` rather than `process.exit()`** — stdin is the only handle holding the event loop open, so releasing it lets Node drain and flush stdout on its own. Exiting outright races the write and can truncate the injection.

The diff is confined to the stdin wiring; the body is unchanged apart from being moved into a named function (the early `return` in the `/caveman-stats` branch behaves identically inside it).

## Tests

Three cases added to `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js`, each verified to fail without the fix:


title: OpenCode plugin never calls recordModeChange - /caveman-stats has no data
body:
**Bug: OpenCode plugin.js never writes history, so /caveman-stats is always empty**

Environment
caveman installed via npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --only opencode
Files installed: ~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman/plugin.js, caveman-config.cjs, package.json
OS: Windows 11, PowerShell 5.1
What's happening
plugins/caveman/plugin.js imports only a subset of exports from caveman-config.cjs:

const { getDefaultMode, safeWriteFlag, readFlag, VALID_MODES } = config;
But caveman-config.cjs also exports appendFlag, readHistory, recordModeChange, MODE_LOG_BASENAME — none of which are imported or called anywhere in plugin.js.

Meanwhile, commands/caveman-stats.md (installed into ~/.config/opencode/commands/caveman-stats.md) instructs the model to:

Read the lifetime history log at ~/.config/caveman/.caveman-history.jsonl (or wherever the caveman-stats script writes it). Output: total saved, sessions counted, avg ratio.

Since nothing in the OpenCode plugin ever calls recordModeChange/appendFlag, this history file is never created or updated. Running /caveman-stats in OpenCode therefore always reads an empty/nonexistent log — it can never report real numbers, unlike the Claude Code integration where hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js presumably wires this up.

Expected
plugin.js's chat.message handler (or the session-created handler) should call recordModeChange/appendFlag whenever the caveman mode is toggled, mirroring whatever caveman-mode-tracker.js does for Claude Code, so /caveman-stats has real data to read in OpenCode too.

Suggested fix location
plugin.js around applyModeChange() (~line 163) and handleSessionCreated() (~line 175) — both currently only call safeWriteFlag/unlinkSync, never recordModeChange/appendFlag.

title: fix(hooks): make caveman-statusline.sh always exit 0
body:
Refs #711.

## Update: superseded by 7693a04, narrowed to regression tests

This PR originally added the same fix independently. Rebasing onto current
`main` showed that `7693a04` already shipped the identical fix upstream
(an explicit `exit 0` after the savings-suffix block in
`caveman-statusline.sh`, for the same reason described below), so that part
of this PR is now redundant and has been dropped in the rebase. The
`caveman-statusline.sh` diff here is empty; it now matches `main` exactly.

What remains is `StatuslineExitCodeTests` in `tests/test_hooks.py`, which
`main` does not have. It pins the behavior in place: empty suffix file,
missing suffix file, and populated suffix file must all exit 0.

Entirely your call whether these tests are worth merging as-is, folding
into another PR, or just closing this one.

## Original root cause (for context, already fixed on main by 7693a04)

`caveman-statusline.sh`'s last statement is:

```sh
[ -n "$SAVINGS" ] && printf ' \033[38;5;172m%s\033[0m' "$SAVINGS"
```

When `.caveman-statusline-suffix` exists but is empty (interrupted write, or
a fresh install before `caveman-stats` has produced its first value),
`$SAVINGS` is empty, the test fails, and since this is the last command in
the script its exit status (1) becomes the script's exit status, even
though the badge itself already printed correctly. Claude Code hides the
whole statusline on a non-zero exit, so the badge disappears entirely
instead of just dropping the optional suffix.

## Verification

Rebased onto current `main` (`fcf7663`) and ran the full `tests/test_hooks.py`
and `npm test` suites in a `node:22-slim` + `python3` container: 10/10 and
125/125 (121 pass, 4 pre-existing skips) green, no regressions. The three
new `StatuslineExitCodeTests` pass against `main`'s already-fixed script.

title: src/hooks/install.sh and install.ps1 curl-pipe fallback 404s: REPO_URL still points at pre-refactor hooks/ path
body:
## Summary

The curl-pipe fallback in `src/hooks/install.sh` and `src/hooks/install.ps1` downloads every hook file from a hardcoded URL that still points at the pre-refactor top-level `hooks/` directory. Every file in `HOOK_FILES`/`$HookFiles` 404s, so the documented one-liner install fails.

## Repro

```bash
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/hooks/caveman-config.js
# 404
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/src/hooks/caveman-config.js
# 200
```

Running the script's own documented curl-pipe form:

```bash
bash <(cat src/hooks/install.sh)
```

prints `Installing caveman hooks...`, then aborts on the first `curl -fsSL "$REPO_URL/$hook" -o ...` with a 404 under `set -e`, so zero hooks get installed.

## Root cause

`REPO_URL` in `src/hooks/install.sh:38` and `$RepoUrl` in `src/hooks/install.ps1:25` are both hardcoded to `.../main/hooks`. Commit `1ce38a2` ("refactor: consolidate hooks/ rules/ tools/ mcp-servers/ under src/") moved the physical files to `src/hooks/` but never updated these two download URLs, which only run on the curl-pipe path (no local clone). The local-clone path (`cp` from `$SCRIPT_DIR`) is unaffected, which is why the existing tests, all of which run against a local clone, never caught it.

## Fix

Update both URLs to `.../main/src/hooks`.

## Environment

Reproduced against current `main` (`0d95a81`).

fix(opencode): record mode changes
body:
Fixes #734

## Summary

The opencode plugin imported `getDefaultMode`, `safeWriteFlag` and `readFlag` from
`caveman-config`, but never `recordModeChange` — so every caveman mode transition in
opencode wrote the flag file and nothing else. `.caveman-mode-log.jsonl` was never
created, and `caveman-stats` had no transitions to attribute messages to.

This wires `recordModeChange` into all four transition sites the plugin owns:

- `applyModeChange` — slash/natural-language activation (`set`) and deactivation (`clear`)
- `handleSessionCreated` — session start, both the resolved-mode path and the
  `off` path

`opencodeConfigDir()` is hoisted to a module-level `opencodeDir` so the log lands
beside the flag it describes, instead of recomputing the directory per call.

Ordering matters and is deliberate: `recordModeChange` reads the *current* flag to
fill the row's `prev` field, so it runs before `safeWriteFlag`/`removeFlag`, never
after. Writes go through the existing symlink-safe `appendFlag` helper and inherit
its silent-fail contract, so a bad log path can never break session start.

## Test verification (RED → GREEN)

RED — unmodified upstream `main` (`a42ef76`) with **only** the test changes applied,
production `plugin.js` untouched:

```text
$ git status --porcelain
 M tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs

$ node --test --test-force-exit tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs
not ok 11 - opencode plugin handles /caveman ultra, stop caveman, and session init via real hooks
  error: 'mode log missing after slash activation'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 12
# pass 11
# fail 1
```

GREEN — same tests with the fix:

```text
$ node --test --test-force-exit tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs
# tests 12
# pass 12
# fail 0
```

Every `recordModeChange` call site the fix adds is asserted, not merely executed:
activation asserts the row's `mode`, deactivation asserts `mode: null`, and both
`handleSessionCreated` branches assert `{mode, prev}` so the session-start
transition is pinned in both directions.

## Scope note

`src/plugins/opencode/commands/caveman-stats.md` still points the model at
`~/.config/caveman/.caveman-history.jsonl`. That is the lifetime-savings file, a
different artifact from the mode log, and nothing on the opencode side writes it
today — it was already stale before this change. Deciding what opencode's
`/caveman-stats` should read is a separate call, so it is left out of a PR titled
"record mode changes" rather than folded in silently.

title: caveman-shrink never forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to its spawned upstream server, orphaning it
body:
**What happen**

caveman-shrink (the MCP proxy that wraps an upstream MCP server and compresses tool
descriptions) never forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to the upstream process it spawned. If
something tears down the caveman-shrink process directly with a signal (an MCP host
ending a session, disabling a tool, reloading config) instead of killing a whole
process group, the wrapped upstream server is left running, reparented to PID 1,
indefinitely.

`src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js` only registers handlers for the child's own
`exit`/`error` events:

```js
const upstream = spawn(args[0], args.slice(1), getSpawnOptions());

upstream.on('error', err => { ... });
upstream.on('exit', (code, signal) => { ... });
```

There is no `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)` / `process.on('SIGINT', ...)` on the parent to
forward the signal (or kill the child) before exiting.

**Expected**

Sending SIGTERM to the caveman-shrink process should also stop the upstream child it
spawned, not leave it running orphaned.

**Repro**

```
# fake long-running upstream (never exits on its own)
cat > /tmp/fake-upstream.js <<'EOF'
process.stdin.resume();
setInterval(() => {}, 1000000);
EOF

node src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js node /tmp/fake-upstream.js &
WRAPPER_PID=$!
sleep 1
kill -TERM $WRAPPER_PID
sleep 1
ps -o pid,ppid,stat,args
```

Verified today in a clean `node:20-alpine` container against current `main`
(0d95a81d35a9f2d123a5e9430d1cfc43d55f1bb0): the wrapper process becomes a zombie, and
the fake-upstream process is still alive with `PPID 1` (reparented, orphaned), never
having received a signal.

**Platform**

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: any MCP host wrapping a server via `caveman-shrink` (not agent-specific)

**Version / install method**

`main` @ `0d95a81d`, ran the script directly from the repo (not through the packaged
installer).

Happy to send a PR (forward SIGTERM/SIGINT to the child, mirroring the existing
`upstream.on('exit', ...)` handling) if useful.

body:
## What

Fixes seven confirmed bugs in the natural-language activation classifier (`src/hooks/caveman-config.js`) and the opencode plugin (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`):

1. **Negated brevity activates** — "don't be brief, explain everything in detail" wrongly turned caveman on. Negator within 3 words of a brevity trigger now suppresses activation.
2. **Contrastive deactivation** — "use caveman instead of normal mode" wrongly turned caveman off via the "normal mode" substring. Contrastive forms (`instead of`, `rather than`, `not`, `versus`, …) before "normal mode" now suppress deactivation.
3. **Negated deactivation** — "don't turn off caveman" / "do not disable caveman" wrongly deactivated. Now classified as neither.
4. **Polite question-form off** — "can you switch back to normal mode? caveman is hard to read" failed to deactivate. Polite prefixes (`can/could/would you`, `please`, …) are stripped before pattern matching, and the question heuristic runs on the stripped core.
5. **Pronoun-reference off** — "caveman is annoying, please turn it off" failed to deactivate. Added `turn/shut/switch it|that|this off` clauses gated on the prompt mentioning caveman.
6. **Polite question-form on** — "can you talk like a caveman?" failed to activate. Fixed by the same polite-prefix strip.
7. **opencode stale-config crash** — a stale sibling `caveman-config.cjs` missing `classifyPrompt` threw `TypeError: classifyPrompt is not a function` on every message. `loadConfig` now validates all expected exports, falls back to the dev copy, and fails safe: natural-language parsing goes inert (slash commands keep working), and the `safeWriteFlag` stub is a no-op so no raw flag writes ever happen.

## Summary

Add **Grok CLI** (Grok Build TUI / xAI) as a native installer provider so caveman is **always on from message one**.

Grok loads `$GROK_HOME/rules/*.md` and `AGENTS.md` every session. SessionStart hook stdout is ignored, so always-on uses the same pattern as opencode/OpenClaw (rules + fenced AGENTS.md), not Claude Code hooks.

### What install does

- Detect: `command:grok` or `dir:~/.grok`
- Write `$GROK_HOME/rules/caveman.md` from `src/rules/caveman-activate.md` (default intensity **full**)
- Append marker-fenced block to `$GROK_HOME/AGENTS.md` (idempotent; preserves user content)
- Copy skills (`caveman`, `caveman-commit`, `caveman-review`, `caveman-help`, `caveman-stats`, `caveman-compress`, `cavecrew`) into `$GROK_HOME/skills/`
- Copy cavecrew agents into `$GROK_HOME/agents/`
- `GROK_HOME` set → install only there (tests / single-account override)
- `GROK_HOME` unset → discover `~/.grok` + `~/.grok-accounts/*`
- Uninstall strips fence + removes owned files; leaves user AGENTS.md prefix

### Docs

- `INSTALL.md` install table row
- `README.md` tip + one-liner + details block (same shape as OpenClaw)
- `CLAUDE.md` agent distribution row

```bash

node bin/install.js --uninstall
```

Native copy needs a local clone (same as hermes/opencode) so skills/rules come from disk.

body:
# SKILL.md never loads in plugin installs — intensity levels are silently cosmetic

**Version:** caveman plugin, cache dir `25d22f864ad6`
**Effect:** `lite`, `full`, `ultra`, and every `wenyan-*` level emit byte-identical output. The intensity table in `SKILL.md` is never applied.

## Cause

`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` resolves SKILL.md relative to `__dirname`:

```js
skillContent = fs.readFileSync(
  path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8'
);
```

The comment above it assumes `__dirname = <plugin_root>/hooks/`. In this build the hooks ship at **`<plugin_root>/src/hooks/`**, so `'..'` resolves to `<plugin_root>/src/`, and `<plugin_root>/src/skills/` does not exist. The read throws, the `catch` swallows it, and the hardcoded fallback is used for every level.

Because the fallback is level-independent, `getDefaultMode()` still resolves correctly — the mode label in the header is right — but the behavioural rules attached to that level are never emitted.

## Reproduction

```bash
P=~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/25d22f864ad6
ls "$P/src/skills"                 # No such file or directory
ls "$P/skills/caveman/SKILL.md"    # exists

for m in lite full ultra; do
  printf '%-6s ' "$m"
  CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=$m node "$P/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js" | wc -c
done
```

Before fix — all three identical, all using the fallback:
```
lite   1667
full   1667
ultra  1667
```

After fix:
```
lite   3408
full   3491
ultra  3500
```

## Fix

Try both layouts instead of assuming one:

```js
let skillContent = '';
for (const candidate of [
  path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'),
  path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'skills', 'caveman', 'SKILL.md'),
]) {
  try {
    skillContent = fs.readFileSync(candidate, 'utf8');
    break;
  } catch (e) { /* try next layout */ }
}
```

## Why it matters

Measured on 3 technical questions, same prompts, same model, comparing generated rulesets against an uninstructed baseline:

| | baseline | full | ultra |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| total output chars | 5,674 | 3,493 (−38.4%) | 2,507 (−55.8%) |

`ultra` is worth roughly 17 percentage points of output reduction over `full` — the entire point of the level, unavailable in plugin installs until the path resolves. Users selecting `ultra` have been getting `full`-equivalent fallback text.

## Suggestion

Consider failing loudly (or emitting a one-line warning) when SKILL.md can't be found, rather than silently degrading to the fallback. The current failure mode is invisible: the header still prints the requested level, so there's no signal that the level had no effect.

title: fix(skill): drop caveman when the agent asks the user a question
