title: wrap (Windows): which() picks the unusable extensionless npm shim over .cmd/.exe, breaking every native agent launch
body:
`caveman claude` fails on Windows with:
```
failed to exec C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude: spawn C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude ENOENT
```

Root cause: `executableCandidateNames()` (portable-command.js/index.js) puts the bare command name first in the candidate list, and `which()`'s `isExecutable()` check uses `accessSync(p, fs.constants.X_OK)`, which on Windows doesn't verify real executability — it passes for any readable file, including the extensionless POSIX shell shim npm always installs alongside `.cmd`/`.ps1` for git-bash/WSL compatibility. So `which(claude)` returns the bare `claude` script (a `#!/bin/sh` file), and `spawn()` (no shell) can't execute it, since Windows `CreateProcess` doesn't understand shebangs — hence ENOENT.

**Repro:** any Windows machine with `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` installed via `npm install -g`, then `caveman claude`.

**Suggested fix:** on `win32`, only accept extensionless candidates when the file is verified to be a valid PE image (or simply try `.CMD`/`.EXE`/`.BAT` candidates before the bare name).

**Workaround** we used locally: hardlink the agent's real native binary (e.g. `node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-code\bin\claude.exe`) into a small directory prepended to PATH, so `which()` matches an extensioned candidate before ever reaching the broken bare shim.

title: wrap (Windows): hook commands use backslash paths, which git-bash's /bin/sh hook runner strips, breaking every installed hook
body:
Follows on from #834 — after working around that one, `caveman claude` starts but every hook (PreToolUse:Skill/Bash/Read) fails:
```
/usr/bin/bash: line 1: C:Users<user>AppDataRoamingnpmcaveman: command not found
```

Root cause: `cavemanBinForHook()` returns `which(caveman)`, a Windows path built with `path.join` (backslash-separated), embedded directly as a hook `command` string. Claude Code appears to execute hook commands via a POSIX shell (`/bin/sh -c`) even on native Windows, which treats `\` as an escape character and strips it — `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\caveman` becomes `C:Users<user>AppDataRoamingnpmcaveman`, which obviously doesn't resolve.

**Suggested fix:** normalize `\` → `/` when building any hook command string on `win32`. Confirmed this specific fix works — forward-slash absolute paths execute fine under the same hook runner (this is also how we resolved an unrelated hook path issue on the same machine, for a different tool, using the identical pattern).

**Workaround** we used locally: patched `cavemanBinForHook()` in the installed `dist/index.js` to `.replace(/\\/g, /)` on win32 before returning.

title: Cursor install missing -g: skills land in cwd/.agents/skills, not ~/.cursor/skills
body:
# What happen
Running the official one-liner installs for Cursor successfully, but skills land in the wrong place and do not show up in Cursor’s Skills UI.
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v1.10.0/install.sh | bash
```
Installer detects Cursor and runs:
```bash
npx -y skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman --skill * -a cursor --yes
```
There is no `-g` / `--global`. Without that flag, `skills` writes to **project-local** `./.agents/skills` under the current working directory.
I ran the install from `~/.local/bin`, so skills were copied to:
```text
~/.local/bin/.agents/skills/
```
Cursor’s Skills section reads personal skills from:
```text
~/.cursor/skills/
```
Result: installer prints “Installation complete” / “copy → Cursor”, but caveman skills never appear in Cursor Skills.
Root cause in installer (`installViaSkills`):
```js
const args = ['-y', 'skills', 'add', REPO, '--skill', '*', '-a', prov.profile, '--yes'];
```
`--skill '*'` and `--yes` are handled (TTY / multi-agent issues), but `-g` is never passed for Cursor.
## Expected
For Cursor (and likely other IDE agents whose Skills UI is global-home based), the installer should pass `-g` so skills install to `~/.cursor/skills/`, e.g.:
```bash
npx -y skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman --skill '*' -a cursor --yes -g
```
Docs / README one-liner should mention that without `-g`, install is cwd-relative and will miss Cursor’s Skills panel unless run from a repo (and even then project `.agents/skills` may not match what the Skills UI lists).
## Before/after example
```text
Input: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v1.10.0/install.sh | bash
       (run from ~/.local/bin on macOS; Cursor detected)
Got:   Installed 20 skills → ~/.local/bin/.agents/skills/*
       Report: "copy → Cursor" / "installed: cursor"
       Cursor Skills UI: no caveman skills
Want:  Installed 20 skills → ~/.cursor/skills/*
       Cursor Skills UI: caveman, caveman-commit, … visible
```
## Platform
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Cursor
- [ ] Other: ___
## Version / install method
- caveman `v1.10.0`
- `curl …/install.sh | bash`
- macOS (darwin), Node ≥18, `npx skills` via installer
- Workaround that worked: symlink `~/.local/bin/.agents/skills/*` → `~/.cursor/skills/`, or re-run with `-g`

title: fix(hooks): unresolved /caveman arg is silent; prose fires NL triggers
body:
Rebased onto `c72984e` and rewritten against `src/hooks/caveman-parse.js` — the first version of this PR targeted the pre-#602 tracker. Both defects survive on current main.

## 1. Punctuation glued to the mode

`/caveman ultra; still too verbose` parses the argument as `ultra;`, matches no mode, leaves the level untouched, says nothing.

Only `parts[1]` is ever read, so extra *words* after the mode were already harmless. It is the character glued to the mode that breaks it.

Fix: strip trailing punctuation. An argument that still resolves to nothing now returns `{ action: 'unresolved' }` instead of `null`, and the tracker turns that into a notice naming the valid modes.

Notice is built from `VALID_MODES` minus `INDEPENDENT_MODES`, so it cannot drift from the parser. It never echoes the rejected argument — that string lands in model context and is untrusted input.

`unresolved` is additive: `applyModeChange` in the opencode plugin acts only on `set`/`clear`. Three existing tests asserted `null` for a bogus level; they now assert the new verdict and still guard the original danger — a bogus level must never activate the default.

## 2. Prose that quotes the trigger phrases fires them

Natural-language triggers run over the whole prompt. A bug report quoting the `/caveman-help` card's own line —

> Say "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

— switched caveman off mid-task. #537's envelope unwrap closes the slash-command path; this is the prose path, which needs no envelope. Any pasted changelog, issue text, or doc carrying those words does the same.

Fix: triggers require a short, command-like utterance — 120 chars or fewer, not slash-initiated. Slash parsing untouched and never length-capped, so `/caveman off` works inside a prompt of any size. 120 clears every documented form with headroom; the longest, "back to normal mode please", is 26.

## Tests

9 new cases in `tests/test_caveman_parse.js` plus 2 parity cases, and 5 integration cases in `tests/test_mode_tracker.py`.

Verified against pristine files first: 9 of the new JS cases and 4 of the 5 python cases fail on unmodified `c72984e`. The one that passes both ways is the short `stop caveman` control — it is there to prove the silence in the negative cases is the scoping and not the harness.

Suites green: 44 parse, 28 mode-tracker, 11 stdin.

## Note

`src/hooks/checksums.sha256` still carries the old hashes for the two changed hook files. Manifest looks per-release, so leaving it to your release cut rather than guessing — say the word if you want it in this PR.

title: feat(hooks): level-aware per-turn reinforcement
body:
**Stacks on #838.** Rebased onto `c72984e`; the diff shows #838's commit too until it merges. Review the second commit only.

## Problem

Switching level mid-session moves the statusline badge and changes nothing about the output.

Two causes:

1. Every level injects the same per-turn line — `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (<level>) — session ruleset applies.` Only the label differs, so `lite`, `full`, `ultra` and the three wenyan variants are indistinguishable to the model.
2. The level-specific ruleset is emitted only by the SessionStart hook, so only for whatever level the session opened at. `/caveman ultra` on turn 40 never re-emits ultra's rules.

Net effect: a user switches to ultra, sees the badge change, sees output stay the same, reports the feature as broken. That is exactly how this was found.

## Change

Per-level directive lines, drawn from the intensity table in `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`.

On a level CHANGE, re-emit that level's filtered rows once. Ordinary turns still cost one short line. The read is best-effort with the same candidate paths the SessionStart hook uses, and returns empty when no skills dir is present, so a standalone hook install never breaks on it.

## Also: the exemptions, restated per turn

The reminder now names what stays verbatim — code, commit messages, security warnings, error strings, and fixed-format blocks required by whatever else is instructing the model (protocol blocks, gates, checklists, audit blocks).

This is where caveman loses in practice. Another instruction set demands structured multi-line output, caveman demands compression, and the model resolves the clash by dropping one of them. They govern different things; a required block is a structured artifact like a code block, and the prose around it still compresses.

Wording is generic — no host-specific tooling named. Happy to drop this half if you would rather keep the reminder purely about prose.

## Tests

6 new cases in `tests/test_mode_tracker.py`: levels inject different text, a switch re-emits that level's row and no other level's, an ordinary turn does not re-emit, re-switching to the same level does not re-emit, the exemption clause is present, and `wenyan` reports its canonical `wenyan-full` label.

4 of the 6 fail against the parent commit. The 2 that pass are absence-assertions whose positive control is the re-emission test.

title: fix(opencode): strip bare model aliases
body:
## Symptom

OpenCode 1.18.18 parses cavecrew agents with `model: haiku` as provider `haiku` plus an empty model ID, then fails at runtime with `Model not found: haiku/`.

## Cause

The OpenCode installer transform strips Claude-style `tools:` frontmatter but leaves Claude-only bare model aliases. OpenCode model references require `provider/model-id`.

## Fix

Strip exact bare Claude aliases (`haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`) while copying agent frontmatter for OpenCode. With `model` omitted, subagents inherit the invoking primary model. Slash-qualified IDs such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` remain byte-identical.

title: caveman-proxy cannot forward to custom/local relay (loopback upstream blocked + non-standard key)
body:
## caveman-proxy cannot forward to a custom/local relay — SSRF guard blocks loopback upstream + non-standard key

### What happens

`caveman codex` (and `caveman wrap -- codex`) cannot route traffic through the proxy when Codex is configured with a **custom provider** whose `base_url` points to a local relay (e.g. a self-hosted or third-party API gateway on `127.0.0.1`). The proxy either returns 502 `cave_upstream_unavailable` or times out, and no outbound connection is ever made to the relay.

This is related to but distinct from #827 (which fixed the mihomo TUN fake-IP range `198.18.0.0/15`). The fix in `83e4db38` added `selfHostedSyntheticPrefixes` for TUN fake IPs, but the proxy still cannot reach a plain loopback upstream like `127.0.0.1:<port>`.

### Reproduction

Codex `config.toml`:

```toml
model = "glm-5.2"
model_provider = "custom"

[model_providers.custom]
name = "custom"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1"
```

`auth.json`:

```json
{"OPENAI_API_KEY": "7493bf..."}
```

The key is a relay-internal token, not a standard `sk-` OpenAI key. The relay (in this case a local process `CodexPlus` on port 57321) forwards to the actual model provider.

Steps:

```bash
# Proxy binaries installed and verified
caveman setup --install   # OK — all 6 binaries present
caveman enable codex      # OK — writes config.toml + hooks.json

# Start proxy
OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1" caveman start --port 8787

# Try a request through the proxy
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/codex/responses" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer 7493bf..." \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.2","input":"Say hi","max_output_tokens":20}'
```

### Expected

The proxy forwards the request to the upstream relay at `127.0.0.1:57321` (as configured in `OPENAI_BASE_URL` or derived from `config.toml`'s `base_url`) and returns the relay's response.

### Actual

Two failure modes observed:

**1. `cave_route_not_found`** — the proxy does not recognize the `/w/codex` path for this request shape.

```
{"error":{"type":"cave_gateway_error","code":"cave_route_not_found","message":"Proxy path is not recognized."}}
```

**2. Timeout / `cave_upstream_unreachable`** — when the route resolves, the proxy cannot dial the loopback upstream. The SSRF dial guard appears to block `127.0.0.1` in the same way it blocked `198.18.0.0/15` before `83e4db38`.

### Root cause (two layers)

**Layer 1: SSRF guard blocks loopback upstream.**

`StandaloneHTTPClient` wraps the upstream client in `ssrf.NewHTTPClient` (`proxy/internal/standalone/standalone.go`). The SSRF guard blocks private/loopback ranges. The `selfHostedSyntheticPrefixes` list added in `83e4db38` only covers mihomo's TUN fake-IP pools (`198.18.0.0/15` and `fdfe:dcba::/32`), not RFC1918/loopback ranges like `127.0.0.0/8`. A local relay at `127.0.0.1:<port>` is therefore unreachable.

**Layer 2: Upstream inference assumes standard provider keys.**

The proxy determines the upstream provider from the API key format (`sk-` → `api.openai.com`, `sk-ant-` → `api.anthropic.com`). A non-standard key (like a relay-internal token) cannot be mapped to any known provider, so the proxy has no way to determine where to forward the request even if the SSRF guard allowed it.

`OPENAI_BASE_URL` set in the proxy's environment is **not consulted** — consistent with the finding in #827 that `ssrf.NewHTTPClient` sets `t.Proxy = nil` explicitly.

### Why this matters

Custom providers / local relays are a legitimate and increasingly common setup:
- Third-party API gateways (OneAPI, NewAPI, OpenRouter via local proxy)
- Self-hosted models behind an OpenAI-compatible API (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio)
- Corporate proxies that terminate TLS and inject internal auth tokens

For all of these, the Caveman Proxy's input compression is currently unusable, while the skill (output compression) works fine.

### Proposed approach

A minimal fix could allow an explicit upstream override, for example:

```toml
# caveman.yaml
[upstream]
forward_url = "http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1"
```

or via env:

```bash
CAVE_UPSTREAM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1
```

When set, the proxy would bypass key-based provider inference and forward directly to `forward_url`, with the SSRF guard relaxed for that explicitly-configured destination (similar to how `selfHostedSyntheticPrefixes` relaxes the TUN ranges).

This would also address the broader request in #201 (optional local model backend for compress).

### Environment

- caveman CLI: `@caveman-ai/cli@1.1.0`, binary release `bin-v1.0.0`
- Codex: `codex-cli 0.147.0-alpha.6.5` (embedded in ChatGPT desktop app, "Powered by Codex & OWL")
- Provider: custom local relay (`CodexPlus`) at `127.0.0.1:57321` → GLM-5.2
- Platform: macOS (Apple Silicon), Clash Verge running (mixed port 7897) but relay is on loopback, not behind TUN
- `caveman status`: all 6 binaries present, `compress on`, not signed in (local-only)

### Related

- #827 — SSRF guard blocking mihomo TUN fake IPs (fixed in `83e4db38`)
- #201 — Feature request: optional local model backend for caveman-compress
- #111 — Use caveman with local models (Ollama / LM Studio)

title: Merge PR #162 with conflict resolution: pi extension + bun as root package manager
SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks hard-crash with MODULE_NOT_FOUND when a sibling hook file is missing — bare top-level require('./caveman-config') in 3 of 4 entrypoints
body:
Every session start prints:

```
SessionStart:startup hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1408
```

Root cause is a missing sibling file (`src/hooks/caveman-config.js`) in the installed plugin dir. But the reason it surfaces as an opaque loader stack trace instead of a diagnosable message is a code issue in caveman: **3 of the 4 hook entrypoints require `./caveman-config` at top level with no guard**, so any missing/unreadable sibling turns into an uncaught `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and exit 1 on *every* SessionStart and *every* UserPromptSubmit.

## Reproduction

```console
$ echo '{"session_id":"t","cwd":"/tmp","hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup"}' \
    | node ~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/27d5a3981a34/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1408
  throw err;
  ^

Error: Cannot find module './caveman-config'
Require stack:
- .../src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
    at Function._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1405:15)
    ...
    at Object.<anonymous> (.../src/hooks/caveman-activate.js:12:84)
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
$ echo $?
1
```

## The code issue

`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` L12 — mandatory dependency, unguarded:

```js
const { getDefaultMode, safeWriteFlag, recordModeChange, readFlag, VALID_MODES } = require('./caveman-config');
```

Same shape in `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` L9 and `src/hooks/caveman-stats.js` L13.

`src/hooks/caveman-parse.js` L43-48 already does the right thing for the identical import:

```js
let cavemanConfig;
try {
  cavemanConfig = require('./caveman-config');
} catch (e) {
  cavemanConfig = require('./caveman-config.cjs');
}
```

And `caveman-activate.js` itself demonstrates the fail-soft philosophy 18 lines further down (L30-33), for the *optional* dep:

```js
// Best-effort: any error is swallowed so SessionStart is never blocked.
try {
  const { applyOverrides, resolvePluginRoot } = require('./cavecrew-model-overrides');
  applyOverrides(resolvePluginRoot(__dirname));
} catch (e) {}
```

So the codebase already treats "a sibling hook file may be absent" as a real risk — it just guards one of the four call sites. This is the same failure class as #801 (`install.sh`/`install.ps1` omitting `caveman-parse.js`); that fix added the file to the copy list, but the underlying "top-level require ⇒ hard crash" remains, so the next missing file reproduces it.

## How the file went missing

I could not attribute the deletion, and I am **not** claiming caveman deleted it — reporting the observed state in case it is a known install-path problem:

The installed plugin dir is a git worktree at the exact HEAD commit, and git reports the file as deleted from the worktree only:

```console
$ git -C ~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/27d5a3981a34 status --porcelain
 D src/hooks/caveman-config.js
 D src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/README.md
 D src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js
 D src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js
 D src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/package.json
 D src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/spawn-options.js
 D src/rules/caveman-activate.md
 D src/rules/caveman-openclaw-bootstrap.md
?? .in_use/
```

Exactly 8 tracked files, all under `src/`, all present at HEAD (`git ls-tree HEAD src/hooks/` lists `caveman-config.js`, blob `d94131b`, and the blob is present in `.git/objects`). Not sparse-checkout (`fatal: this worktree is not sparse`), not gitignored (`git check-ignore` exits 1 for all three paths). The marketplace clone at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/caveman` has all 8 files. Other cached version dirs for the same 2.0.0 release (`613d7f0402fb`, `a0109974ea32`, `c72984e4392c`, `099327780ef6`) all have `caveman-config.js`; only the current `27d5a3981a34` does not. `git status` on this worktree shows no other drift, so it is not a broad truncation.

Note that `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` **already lists** `caveman-config.js` — the manifest that would have caught this ships with the plugin, but nothing verifies it at runtime.

Workaround that fixed it locally:

```console
$ git -C ~/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/27d5a3981a34 restore src/hooks/caveman-config.js src/mcp-servers src/rules
$ echo '{"session_id":"t","cwd":"/tmp","hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup"}' \
    | node .../src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full
...
$ echo $?
0
```

## Suggested fix

1. Guard the three unguarded requires the way `caveman-parse.js` already does — a hook must never exit non-zero because a sibling is missing. On failure, degrade to the built-in fallback ruleset (as #792 describes for the SKILL.md lookup) rather than crashing.
2. Emit one actionable line on stderr instead of a Node stack trace, e.g. `caveman: plugin install incomplete (missing caveman-config.js) — run /plugin update caveman`.
3. Optionally verify `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` on SessionStart (cheap, manifest already shipped) so a partial install self-reports instead of failing at a random require.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.233, plugin install path (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` hooks), not standalone `install.sh`
- caveman 2.0.0 @ `27d5a3981a34` ("README: whole-cave table gains status column, Browse row, frozen tier")
- Node v23.11.0 (Homebrew), macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

Related: #801 (same failure class, standalone installer), #792 (missing-file path degrading silently), #78 / #471 (same loader error, different root cause — path resolution / orphaned hooks).

title: fix(hooks): degrade instead of crashing when a sibling hook file is missing
body:
Fixes #848.

`caveman-activate.js`, `caveman-mode-tracker.js` and `caveman-stats.js` require `./caveman-config` at module top level with no guard. An install that is missing that one file therefore produces an uncaught `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — a raw Node stack trace and exit 1 on **every** session start and **every** prompt, which Claude Code surfaces only as:

```
SessionStart:startup hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1408
```

`caveman-parse.js` L43-48 already wraps the identical import in try/catch, and `caveman-activate.js` already treats the *optional* `cavecrew-model-overrides` require as best-effort — "any error is swallowed so SessionStart is never blocked". The risk was already understood; it just was not applied to the mandatory dependency. This is the same failure class as #801, whose copy-list fix landed but left the crash shape intact.

## What changes

A small `requireSibling()` in each of the three entrypoints, plus an explicit degraded path:

| entrypoint | behavior when a sibling will not load |
|---|---|
| `caveman-activate.js` | Emits the built-in fallback ruleset it already uses when `SKILL.md` is unresolvable, and exits 0. A degraded session still gets rules; only flag persistence is lost (no flag write, no mode log, `readFlag()` reports nothing active). `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=off` still opts out — it is the highest-priority source in `getDefaultMode()` and the only one reachable without the config module. |
| `caveman-mode-tracker.js` | Emits nothing, exits 0. Drains stdin before exiting so the parent's payload write does not turn into a broken pipe (#397). |
| `caveman-stats.js` | Prints one actionable line and exits non-zero, instead of a stack trace that the calling hook then reports as an unexplained failure. |

Message shape:

```
caveman: caveman-config.js is missing from /path/to/src/hooks — the install is incomplete.
Run `/plugin update caveman`, or rerun install.sh for standalone hooks. Continuing with
reduced functionality.
```

Two details worth reviewing:

- **Missing vs. broken is distinguished.** A `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` thrown from *inside* a sibling that itself loaded fine is reported as `could not load … — Cannot find module './x'`, not as an incomplete install, so the message never points at the wrong cause. There is a test for exactly this.
- **Only the first line of `error.message` is echoed.** Node appends a multi-line `Require stack:` block to it; echoing that back reprinted the very noise the guard removes. My first cut got this wrong and the new test caught it.

## Deliberate call, open to preference

The loader is **duplicated per entrypoint rather than extracted into a shared module**. It is the guard that makes a missing sibling survivable, so making it a sibling would reintroduce the failure it prevents. That costs ~15 duplicated lines across three files. Happy to fold it into `caveman-config.js` with an inline fallback if you would rather have one copy — say the word.

`src/hooks/checksums.sha256` is regenerated for the three touched files (`tests/verify_repo.py` verifies the manifest).

## Tests

New `tests/test_hook_missing_sibling.js`, in the style of `test_mode_tracker_stdin.js` — builds a temp hook dir holding real copies of every hook file minus the one under test, so the real `src/hooks` siblings can never satisfy a require the test is trying to break. 8 cases: degraded activate / mode-tracker (config and parse) / stats, the missing-vs-broken discrimination, the nested-`MODULE_NOT_FOUND` case, and controls proving the healthy path still writes the flag, still reinforces, and warns about nothing.

Every case asserts the output contains neither `Require stack:` nor `node:internal/modules/cjs/loader` — the exact shape users are reporting.

Full suite, macOS + Node v23.11.0:

```
npm test                                   → 156 pass, 0 fail
for f in tests/test_*.js; do node "$f"; done → 9 files, all pass (new file 8/8)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests      → Ran 62 tests — OK
node --check (all verify_repo.py targets)  → clean
```

## Verified against the real failure

Reproduced from an actual broken install (plugin cache worktree at `27d5a39` with `src/hooks/caveman-config.js` absent): before the patch, exit 1 and the loader stack trace on every session start; after, exit 0 with the ruleset emitted and one stderr line naming the file and the remedy.

title: claude.ai marketplace sync fails since the 2.0.0 restructure
body:
Before 2.0.0 I had caveman installed on claude.ai (web/desktop) via Add marketplace. After removing it and trying to re-add it now, the dialog always fails with **"Marketplace sync failed. Check the repository URL and try again."**

Tried all URL forms:
- `JuliusBrussee/caveman`
- `https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman`
- `https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman.git`

Meanwhile the same repo adds fine with the local Claude Code CLI (`/plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman` → validates and installs), so the manifests look OK — it seems claude.ai's stricter server-side sync rejects something about the new monorepo layout (engine/proxy/SDK dirs, plugin hooks?) introduced in the 2.0.0 restructure.

Workaround I'm using: zipping `skills/caveman/` and uploading it as a skill on claude.ai.

Would be great to have the marketplace path working again for web/desktop users.

@JuliusBrussee

title: Built a complementary skill (plainness dial) on top of Caveman's levels — attribution check
body:
Hi — thanks for Caveman. I've been using it, and it prompted a thought that turned into a
separate skill, so I wanted to check the attribution with you directly rather than just ship it.

**The idea.** Caveman compresses output for a reader who already knows the domain. I kept
wanting the other axis: keep the terseness, but stop assuming I know the specialism. Those turn
out to be orthogonal — terse *and* jargon-free is reachable, and a single verbosity slider
can't get there:

> "Login is broken. The password check compares the wrong two values. Fixing now."

So it ships two dials rather than one:

| Dial | Levels | What it reduces |
|---|---|---|
| Density | `lite` / `full` / `ultra` / `wenyan-*` | words — **this is yours** |
| Plainness | `expert` / `plain` / `zero` | assumed knowledge |

Where they conflict — `ultra` compresses by abbreviating, and abbreviation *is* jargon —
plainness wins.

**Attribution, which is the actual reason I'm opening this.** The density dial is Caveman's
design: I kept your level names and the `wenyan-*` registers deliberately, so anyone moving
between the two projects keeps the same vocabulary. I've read `LICENSING.md` and taken the
`skills/` MIT terms as the ones that apply ("Existing Caveman skill stays MIT and untouched").
Nothing under a BSL-1.1 path — `engine/`, `proxy/`, `rewriter/`, `shrink/` — was copied,
vendored, or reimplemented; the only runtime is a ~40-line POSIX `sh` hook written from
scratch. Your copyright is preserved in `LICENSE`, and `NOTICE` spells out what's derived
versus what's new.

**If any of that is worded wrong, or you'd rather it were framed differently, tell me and I'll
change it.** That's a genuine offer, not a formality.

Two things you're welcome to, no strings:

- **Take the idea.** If a plainness dial belongs inside Caveman rather than beside it, the MIT
  terms already permit that and I'd rather it live where the users are. Happy to open a PR
  instead.
- **A "see also" line**, if you think it's useful to people who land on Caveman and actually
  want the opposite. Entirely your call — no hard feelings if it's noise.

Repo: https://github.com/yevgenyt/layman

One thing I'd flag honestly: you lead with a measured number and I don't have one. Comprehension
is harder to measure than token count, and I'd rather say so than imply a benchmark that doesn't
exist.

title: Plugin payload is the whole repo: agents/CLAUDE.md and agents/AGENTS.md register as agents named CLAUDE and AGENTS, skills register twice
body:
**What happen**

Since 2.x, `claude plugin details caveman@caveman` lists five agents. Two of them — `CLAUDE` and `AGENTS` — are not agents. They are `agents/CLAUDE.md` and `agents/AGENTS.md`, plain maintainer docs with no YAML frontmatter, sitting in the directory Claude Code auto-discovers agents from. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares no explicit `agents` list, so every `.md` file in `agents/` is registered and the agent name falls back to the filename.

At `fcf7663` (v1.10.0) `agents/` held only `cavecrew-builder.md`, `cavecrew-investigator.md`, and `cavecrew-reviewer.md`, so this is new in 2.x.

The root cause is one level up: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` declares `"source": "./"` for the `caveman` plugin, so the installed payload is the whole repository — 21 MB, 28 top-level directories, including `node_modules/`, `engine/`, `proxy/`, `browse/`, `tests/`, and `benchmarks/` — rather than `plugins/caveman/`, which `CLAUDE.md` documents as the "Claude Code plugin distribution (CI-mirrored)". Two more consequences of the same cause:

- Four skills register twice. `commands/` and `skills/` are both auto-discovered by Claude Code, and four names exist in both: `commands/caveman.md`, `commands/caveman-commit.md`, `commands/caveman-review.md`, and `commands/caveman-stats.md` collide with `skills/caveman/`, `skills/caveman-commit/`, `skills/caveman-review/`, and `skills/caveman-stats/`. `plugin details` lists each of the four twice, for 25 entries instead of 21. `CLAUDE.md` describes `commands/` as Codex/Gemini TOML command stubs, but the `.md` halves are picked up by Claude Code as well. This is not new — v1.10.0 showed the same four duplicated.
- The maintainer `CLAUDE.md` (338 lines) ships inside the payload. Any agent that reads a file under the install path picks it up as directory context, including absolute local paths and a reference to a private sibling repository. This happened to me while inspecting the install — it loaded unasked.

Always-on context cost went from ~1,420 to ~2,809 tokens across the same update.

Verified locally, on the installed tree at `766dce6b1394`, by moving files out of it:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| baseline | Skills 25, Agents 5, always-on ~2,809 tok |
| remove `plugins/caveman/` mirror | Skills 25, Agents 5, always-on ~2,752 tok — the mirror does not double-register, it just costs tokens |
| remove `agents/CLAUDE.md` + `agents/AGENTS.md` | Agents 3 |
| remove the four colliding `commands/*.md` | Skills 21, always-on ~2,655 tok |

**Expected**

`plugin details` lists three agents (the cavecrew trio) and each skill once. Docs written for maintainers stay out of the auto-discovered `agents/` directory, and ideally out of the installed payload.

Minimal fix: move `agents/CLAUDE.md` and `agents/AGENTS.md` somewhere not auto-discovered (`docs/`, say), or declare an explicit `agents` array in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. For the collisions, either drop the four `commands/*.md` stubs whose names already exist as skills, or keep the `.toml` stubs Codex and Gemini need and not the `.md` twins.

Fuller fix: point the marketplace entry at `"./plugins/caveman"` and add a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` there — that directory currently has none — so the plugin ships only what a user needs.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: claude plugin details caveman@caveman

Got:   Skills (25)  cavecrew, caveman, caveman, caveman-commit, caveman-commit,
                    caveman-compress, ... caveman-review, caveman-review,
                    caveman-stats, caveman-stats, ...
       Agents (5)   cavecrew-builder, CLAUDE, cavecrew-investigator, AGENTS, cavecrew-reviewer
       Always-on:   ~2,809 tok

Want:  Skills (21)  each name once
       Agents (3)   cavecrew-builder, cavecrew-investigator, cavecrew-reviewer
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

- caveman `766dce6b1394` (marketplace HEAD, one commit past `v2.1.0`), installed with `claude plugin update caveman@caveman -s user` from the `JuliusBrussee/caveman` marketplace
- Previously installed: `fcf7663366c2` (`v1.10.0`), which showed 12 skills and 3 agents
- Claude Code 2.1.233, VS Code extension, Linux

_Drafted by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)._

title: Add command to show current Caveman mode
body:
**What you want**

Add a command to show the currently active Caveman mode.

For example:

```text
/caveman status
```

or:

```text
/caveman:caveman status
```

It could return something simple like:

```text
Caveman mode: full
```

**Before/after example**

```text
Before: No obvious command to check which Caveman mode is currently active. Users have to infer it or inspect the internal state file.

After:  `/caveman status` returns the active mode, e.g. `Caveman mode: full`.
```

**Why good**

Caveman has several modes (`lite`, `full`, `ultra`, Wenyan variants, and `off`), and the mode can persist within a session or come from a configured default.

A status command would make it easy to verify which mode is active, especially after changing modes, returning to a session, or troubleshooting configuration. The mode is already tracked internally, so exposing it through the command interface would improve usability without adding much complexity.

caveman-compress: is_sensitive_path() misses a top-level CREDENTIALS/ directory
body:
`caveman-compress`'s `is_sensitive_path()` guard is a **name-based denylist**. It correctly blocks
`.env`, `credentials.md`, `secrets.txt`, `id_ed25519`, `api_key.md`, and anything under
`.ssh/.aws/.gnupg/.kube/.docker`.

It does **not** block a file that holds credentials but happens to be named innocuously and to sit
in a directory whose name is not on the list.

## Reproduce

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scripts.compress import is_sensitive_path

# blocked, as intended
assert is_sensitive_path(Path("credentials.md"))
assert is_sensitive_path(Path.home() / ".ssh" / "notes.md")

# NOT blocked
assert not is_sensitive_path(Path(r"C:\dev\CREDENTIALS\hetzner\webhosting.md"))
```

The last path is a real-world layout: a top-level `CREDENTIALS/` directory with one file per
service. Neither trips the guard —

- `SENSITIVE_PATH_COMPONENTS` is `{".ssh", ".aws", ".gnupg", ".kube", ".docker"}` and does not
  contain `credentials` or `secrets`;
- the basename `webhosting.md` contains none of the `SENSITIVE_NAME_TOKENS`.

So the file is read and shipped to the API — exactly what the comment above the denylist
("a third-party data boundary that developers on sensitive codebases cannot cross") sets out to
prevent.

## Measured

I ran the guard against 11 paths while evaluating the skill: **10 correct, 1 miss** — and the miss
was the canonical credentials directory of the machine under test. It is a narrow gap, but it is
the one case where the consequence is a leak rather than a bad compression.

## Suggested fix

One line, same shape as the existing check:

```python
SENSITIVE_PATH_COMPONENTS = frozenset({
    ".ssh", ".aws", ".gnupg", ".kube", ".docker",
    "credentials", "secrets",          # added
})
```

Since the comparison already lowercases path parts (`lowered_parts`), this catches `CREDENTIALS/`,
`Credentials/` and `credentials/` alike.

## Worth considering beyond the one-liner

A name-based denylist cannot close this class of problem in general — a file named `notes.md` can
still hold an API token. If you want a stronger boundary, a **content** pre-scan before the API
call would catch what naming never will: private-key headers (`-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----`),
provider token shapes (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `xox[baprs]-…`), and `password|api_key|secret|token`
assignments. Cheap to run, no tokens spent, and it fails closed. Entirely your call whether that
fits the project's scope — the one-liner above already removes the concrete gap.

## Context

Found while evaluating `caveman-compress` as a candidate for a local toolchain; the guard was
otherwise the part I liked most, which is why the gap seemed worth reporting rather than working
around. Version tested: repo state of 2026-08-16 (`766dce6`).

title: wrap-owned proxy self-terminates after 30 min idle while ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL persists, breaking already-running sessions
body:
**What happen**

`caveman enable claude` writes a permanent `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/claude` into the user-scoped Claude settings. But a proxy started with `CAVEMAN_PROXY_OWNER=wrap` shuts itself down after 30 minutes of no session activity (`proxy/cmd/caveman-proxy/main.go:208-225`, via `WaitForIdle`). The autostart that would bring it back is gated on `normalizedEvent === "SessionStart"` (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:11015`) — it does not run on `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, or `SubagentStart`.

So a session that is already running has no way to recover. It idles past 30 minutes, the proxy exits, and the next API call hits a dead port. Nothing supervises the process and nothing reconnects lazily. Every subagent spawned by that session inherits the same dead base URL, so an entire fan-out dies at once.

This is amplified when several agent sessions run concurrently: they all share the single port, so the first one to go idle takes routing down for all of them.

**Expected**

Either the persistent route should be backed by a supervised or lazily-restarted proxy, or the idle shutdown should not apply while a persistent route is installed. A dead endpoint behind a permanent config entry is not recoverable from inside a running session.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: enable native routing, start a session, leave it idle >30 min, resume
Got:   API Error: Connection refused — nothing listening on 127.0.0.1:8787
       (all subagents fail simultaneously; only restarting the host recovers)
Want:  request succeeds — proxy restarted on demand, or never exited while a
       persistent ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is installed
```

**Workaround, and its cost**

Running the proxy as `caveman start` (`CAVEMAN_PROXY_OWNER=start`) skips the idle branch and resolves the crashes. Two caveats worth flagging:

- `caveman start` forces `mode: record` whenever `think.mode` resolves from *default*, and `caveman tools config set think.mode=compress` is rejected as "config key not settable" — the config file has to be edited by hand to keep compression on.
- The `start`-owned proxy sets `recovery_via_mcp: false` by design (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:1990`), while the wrap help text states subscription compression needs MCP recovery. So the workaround appears to trade away part of the feature set.

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

`@caveman-ai/cli@1.1.0` (`binary_release: bin-v1.0.0`), installed via global npm. Claude Code 2.1.234. Windows 11 Pro, build 10.0.26200.

title: Transport errors on large streaming requests collapse into a non-retryable 502 cave_upstream_unavailable, killing the agent
body:
**What happen**

`proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go:315` maps *any* `httpClient.Do` error to a flat `502 cave_upstream_unavailable` with no retry. When a large streaming request hits a transient transport failure, the client receives a 502 — which agent hosts treat as terminal — instead of a retryable stream error. The agent dies rather than retrying.

From a local request log over three days of normal use:

| | |
|---|---|
| Total requests | 12,630 |
| `200` | 12,570 |
| `502 cave_upstream_unavailable` | 44 |
| `429 provider_429` | 14 |
| `400 provider_400` | 5 |

The 502s correlate strictly with payload size:

- Smallest failing request: 127,417 bytes. Largest: 3,767,483 bytes.
- Zero 502s below 127 KB, across ~8,800 smaller requests.
- Failure rate on requests >400 KB: 35 / 3,791 ~ **0.9%**.
- Stream split: 36 streaming, 8 non-streaming. Streaming dominates but does not define it.
- Observed latency at failure: 27 ms to 12.1 s.

Two details that narrow it further: **every** failing row has `response_bytes = 0` and `ttfb_ms = 0`. The failure always happens before a single response byte arrives — consistent with a connection reset or EOF during the request upload, not with a partially-consumed response.

Those latencies also rule out a timeout: `CAVE_GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 900,000 ms (`proxy/internal/gateway/server.go:448`), so nothing came close.

Raw request bodies are not available: the `requests` table stores only `raw_request_sha256` / `transformed_request_sha256`, and body capture (`capture.go`) is off unless `CAVE_CAPTURE_DIR` is set. Since the failure tracks payload size rather than content, a synthetic large body should reproduce it — happy to run a scripted size sweep (128 KB to 4 MB) against the proxy and post the failure curve if that would help.

**Expected**

A transient transport error on the upstream POST should be retried — at minimum for idempotent-in-practice cases, or before the error is surfaced — rather than converted into a terminal 502. Distinguishing "upstream refused/unreachable" from "connection dropped mid-upload" would also let clients react correctly.

```

       agent treats it as terminal and dies
Want:  transparent retry of the transport failure; error surfaced only after
       retries are exhausted, and distinguishable from a genuine upstream outage
```

title: Installing on opencode with a global opencode.jsonc creates a shadow opencode.json that clobbers existing plugins (v2.1.0)
body:
## Summary

Installing caveman v2.1.0 as a native opencode plugin required manual workarounds on a machine whose global opencode config is `opencode.jsonc` (a documented, first-class config format). Three friction points, in order of impact:

1. The installer hardcodes `opencode.json` and never looks for `opencode.jsonc`, so it creates a *shadow* config that clobbers an existing `plugin` array.
2. `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman#v2.1.0 --only opencode` does not run `bin/install.js`; it routes to a different `caveman` entry point that rejects `--only`. The only working path is a local clone + `node bin/install.js`.
3. `install.sh` pins `CAVEMAN_REF` to `v1.10.0` even at the `v2.1.0` tag, so the README's `curl … /v2.1.0/install.sh | bash` one-liner installs v1.10.0, not v2.1.0.

## Environment

- caveman: v2.1.0 (latest tag at time of writing)
- opencode: latest, global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (JSONC, no comments — valid JSON)
- An existing plugin already in the config: `@dietrichgebert/ponytail@4.8.4`
- macOS, Node v22.22.3

## Issue 1 — installer ignores `opencode.jsonc` (highest impact)

`bin/install.js:717` resolves the config path as:

```js
const opencodeJson = path.join(dir, 'opencode.json');
```

…hardcoded, with no `.jsonc` fallback. `bin/install.js:853-886` then does:

```js
let cfg = SETTINGS.readSettings(opencodeJson);  // returns {} when opencode.json is absent
// ...
if (!Array.isArray(cfg.plugin)) cfg.plugin = [];
if (!cfg.plugin.includes(OPENCODE_PLUGIN_REL)) cfg.plugin.push(OPENCODE_PLUGIN_REL);
SETTINGS.writeSettings(opencodeJson, cfg);
```

Because `readSettings` (`bin/lib/settings.js:98`) returns `{}` for a missing file, when the user's real config is `opencode.jsonc` this **creates a new `opencode.json` containing only**:

```json
{ "plugin": ["./plugins/caveman/plugin.js"] }
```

opencode merges config files ("Configuration files are merged together… later configs override earlier ones only for conflicting keys" — https://opencode.ai/docs/config), and both JSON and JSONC are documented first-class formats (the docs' own examples use `opencode.jsonc`). With both `opencode.json` and `opencode.jsonc` now present in the same dir, the conflicting `plugin` key means one plugin array replaces the other — so a user with an existing `plugin` array (e.g. ponytail) **silently loses either their existing plugins or caveman**. (The same-dir `.json` vs `.jsonc` precedence isn't documented, so which one wins is unpredictable to the user.)

The same hardcoded path is used on uninstall (`bin/install.js:1256`), so the uninstall config-prune is a no-op for `.jsonc` users even if they reconcile manually.

Note: `readSettings` already parses JSONC via `stripJsonComments`, so the **read** side is fine — only the **path resolution** at `:717`/`:1256` is the gap.

### Workaround I applied

1. Ran the installer (to get the ownership journal for clean uninstall + AGENTS.md + the file copies).
2. Manually added `"./plugins/caveman/plugin.js"` to the existing `plugin` array in `opencode.jsonc` (after the ponytail entry).
3. Deleted the stray `opencode.json` so `opencode.jsonc` remains the single source of truth.

### Suggested fix

Have the installer resolve the config path the same way opencode does — prefer `opencode.jsonc` if present, fall back to `opencode.json`, and create `opencode.jsonc` for fresh installs only when neither exists (or honor an existing user choice). Minimal change is a small helper around `:717` and `:1256`:

```js
function opencodeConfigPath(dir) {
  const jsonc = path.join(dir, 'opencode.jsonc');
  const json  = path.join(dir, 'opencode.json');
  if (fs.existsSync(jsonc)) return jsonc;
  if (fs.existsSync(json))  return json;
  return jsonc; // create .jsonc for fresh installs (opencode's documented first-class format)
}
```

## Issue 2 — `npx github:…` does not run `bin/install.js` at v2.1.0

The documented opencode install command (INSTALL.md) is:

```
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --only opencode
```

At v2.1.0 this fails:

```
$ npx -y "github:JuliusBrussee/caveman#v2.1.0" --only opencode --dry-run
unknown command "--only" — did you mean `caveman tools toon`?
see: caveman --help
```

That error is **not** from `bin/install.js` (its `parseArgs` would say `error: unknown flag: --only`). There is no global `caveman` binary on this machine (`which -a caveman` → not found; no global npm `caveman`), so npx resolved the package itself but routed `--only` to a different entry point than the installer.

For reference, `package.json` at the v2.1.0 tag reads:

```json
{
  "name": "caveman-installer",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "bin": { "caveman": "./bin/install.js" },
  "type": "module"
}
```

Two oddities worth flagging: the package `version` is `2.0.0` at the `v2.1.0` tag, and the bin is named `caveman` (which collides with the separate `@caveman-ai/cli` `caveman` runtime CLI mentioned in the README). The collision may be why npx lands on the wrong binary.

### Workaround I applied

Cloned v2.1.0 and ran the installer directly, which works perfectly:

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.1.0 https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman.git
cd caveman
node bin/install.js --only opencode --dry-run   # preview
node bin/install.js --only opencode             # install
```

### Suggested fix

Either make the `npx` path reliably invoke `bin/install.js`, or update INSTALL.md to recommend the clone-and-run form as the primary opencode install (it's the only one I could get working at v2.1.0). Renaming the bin away from the overloaded `caveman` (or pinning it to an unambiguous name) would also avoid the `@caveman-ai/cli` collision.

## Issue 3 — `install.sh` pins `v1.10.0` even at the `v2.1.0` tag

The `install.sh` checked into the `v2.1.0` tag still contains:

```sh
PINNED_REF="${CAVEMAN_REF:-v1.10.0}"
# ...
exec npx -y "github:$REPO#$PINNED_REF" "$@"
```

So `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v2.1.0/install.sh | bash` (the README one-liner) installs **v1.10.0**, not v2.1.0. Meanwhile `bin/install.js` at the same tag correctly pins `process.env.CAVEMAN_REF || 'v2.1.0'` — so the shim is stale relative to the installer it wraps.

### Workaround I applied

Set `CAVEMAN_REF=v2.1.0` explicitly — but that still hits Issue 2, so I used the clone form instead.

### Suggested fix

Bump the `PINNED_REF` default in `install.sh` to match the tag at release time (or derive it from the tag the file ships under).

## Net result

The clone-and-run install is clean and the ownership journal + AGENTS.md + file copies all work as intended — only the config-file path resolution and the documented invocation commands need updating. After the manual `.jsonc` merge and stray-`.json` cleanup, caveman + ponytail coexist correctly in one `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
"plugin": [
  "@dietrichgebert/ponytail@4.8.4",
  "./plugins/caveman/plugin.js"
]
```

Thanks for the project — happy to test any fix on a `.jsonc` setup.

title: feat(evals): make the prompt set language-selectable, add French
body:
## What this changes

`evals/llm_run.py` hardcoded `PROMPTS = EVALS / "prompts" / "en.txt"`. Every
published compression number therefore describes English, and nothing in the
repo measures caveman on another language — despite the README's "Speak your
tongue" claim and four open issues about non-English behaviour (#679, #680,
#701, #812).

- `CAVEMAN_EVAL_LANG` selects the prompt set. Defaults to `en` and keeps the
  existing `snapshots/results.json` path, so current invocations and the
  committed snapshot are untouched. Other languages write
  `snapshots/results.<lang>.json`.
- The `__terse__` control arm is now per-language. An English "Answer
  concisely." in front of a French prompt measures a language switch on top of
  terseness, which is not the control the harness isolates.
- `evals/prompts/fr.txt` mirrors `en.txt` line for line — same ten topics, same
  order — so the sets are comparable arm by arm.
- A missing prompt set now fails with the available languages listed rather than
  a bare `FileNotFoundError`.

I did **not** add French examples to `SKILL.md`. Per #812 the named-language
few-shot examples were themselves the attractor tokens driving language drift,
and `710173f` removed them. Adding French ones back would reintroduce that class
of bug for every user, which is why this PR is measurement only.

## Why: a French measurement that the English harness cannot see

Ten French prompts, one independent `claude -p` call each, three arms, plugin at
`766dce6`. Metric is the share of articles (`le/la/les/un/une/des/du`) in prose,
fenced and inline code removed — the most visible marker of French compression.

| Arm | Words | Article rate |
|---|---|---|
| `__baseline__` (`--safe-mode`) | 4478 | 11.84% |
| `__terse__` ("Réponds de façon concise.") | 2443 | 10.32% |
| caveman + a French rule block in user `CLAUDE.md` | 2748 | 5.75% |

Two things the English harness would not surface:

1. **Generic terseness barely touches French style.** `__terse__` cuts words
   45.4% but moves the article rate only −1.52 pt. Ordinary French prose sits
   around 12%. Shortening and compressing are separable in French in a way the
   token-count metric alone cannot show.
2. **On volume, caveman loses to the one-line control.** `__terse__` is −45.4%
   words against baseline; the caveman arm is −38.6%. That is +12.5% words for
   the same questions. This is consistent with `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` and is
   the kind of workload that page invites people to report.

## What is not included

No `snapshots/results.fr.json`. On current `main` that is 10 prompts × (20
skills + 2 control arms) = 220 calls, and you regenerate snapshots as a
reviewable diff anyway. I did verify the write path end to end with `run_claude`
stubbed: `lang: "fr"` and the French `terse_prefix` land in the metadata, all 22
arms are populated, the file goes to `results.fr.json`, and `results.json` is
untouched. Happy to generate the real snapshot if you would rather the PR carry
it.

Environment: Windows 10, Claude Code 2.1.232, plugin `766dce6`, model Opus 5.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Testing

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` on this branch: 67 tests, 2 failures,
  1 skipped. The same two — `test_install_reconfigures_missing_statusline` and
  `test_install_upgrades_old_two_file_install` in `tests/test_hooks.py` — fail
  identically on clean `main` on this machine, so they are pre-existing and
  Windows-specific, not introduced here. No new failures.
- Write path exercised end to end with `run_claude` stubbed, for `en` (default)
  and `fr`: correct prompt file, correct snapshot file, correct per-language
  terse prefix, 22 arms populated, `results.json` untouched by the `fr` run.
- `evals/measure.py` still reads the committed English snapshot unchanged.
- A missing language now exits with `No prompt set at …; CAVEMAN_EVAL_LANG='de';
  available: en, fr` instead of a traceback.

Platform note: Windows 10, so the two installer failures above may not reproduce
for you.

title: fix(cli): keep Claude Code 1M context window behind the local proxy
body:
Claude Code withholds first-party capabilities whenever ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
does not point at api.anthropic.com — most visibly the 1M-token context
window, whose loss silently shrinks the auto-compact window from ~600k to
the 200k default (#865). Both Claude routing doors (session wrap and the
persistent native install) now assert first-party through Claude Code's
own escape hatch (_CLAUDE_CODE_ASSUME_FIRST_PARTY_BASE_URL=1), but only
when the assertion is verifiably true: local proxy mode with an anthropic
upstream of api.anthropic.com (the default, or an explicit
providers.anthropic.base_url naming that host). A user-set value is never
overridden, managed gateways never assert, unverifiable configs
(flow-style YAML, unreadable file) withhold the assertion, and disable
removes the variable only while it still holds exactly the written value.

title: fix(plugin): concat reinforcement onto last system message (fixes vLLM Qwen3 400)
body:
## Problem

The opencode plugin's `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook pushes a **new** system message per turn:

```js
// src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:187 (before)
output.system.push(reinforcementLine(active));
```

vLLM-hosted Qwen3 models use a strict chat template that rejects any system message not at index 0:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: Hosted_vllmException -
{"message":"System message must be at the beginning.","type":"BadRequest","code":400}
```

The fallback chain (Qwen3-6-27b → Qwen3.8-27B) fails identically — both share the strict template.

## Fix

Concat onto the last system entry instead of pushing a new one (same safe pattern [`@dietrichgebert/ponytail`](https://github.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail) already uses):

```js
const line = reinforcementLine(active);
if (output.system.length > 0) {
  output.system[output.system.length - 1] += '\n\n' + line;
} else {
  output.system.push(line);
}
```

Preserves single system message, keeps per-turn reinforcement.

## Verification

Tested with `opencode run "say hi"` per model, caveman in `full` mode (default), no model pinning:

| Model | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-6-27b   | 400 Bad Request | OK |
| Qwen3.8-27B   | 400 Bad Request | OK |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Hangs indefinitely | OK |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-AWQ | OK | OK |
| GLM-5.2 | OK (tolerant) | OK |

## Root cause analysis

The `push()` pattern assumes the model's chat template tolerates multiple system messages interleaved with user/assistant turns. This holds for Anthropic/OpenAI-style APIs and GLM-5.2, but not for vLLM deployments using Qwen3's strict chat template (which enforces system-at-index-0).

The `ponytail` plugin's transform already uses the concat-onto-last pattern and has never triggered this issue — confirming the fix is safe across providers.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows existing style
- [x] Verified across 5 models (4 Qwen3 variants + GLM-5.2)
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] No breaking changes — behavior identical when `output.system` is empty (falls back to `push`)

title: fix(plugin): prefix agent paths with ./ so plugin.json passes validation
body:
## Problem

`claude plugin install caveman@caveman` fails for every user on current Claude Code. The marketplace is added successfully, then the install aborts:

```
✔ Successfully added marketplace: caveman (declared in user settings)
Installing plugin "caveman@caveman"...
✘ Failed to install plugin "caveman@caveman": Plugin temp_local_..._... has an invalid
  manifest file at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/temp_local_..._.../.claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Validation errors: agents: Invalid input
```

Reproducible against upstream `main` (8896fb5) with Claude Code 2.1.234:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman.git && cd caveman
$ claude plugin validate .
Validating marketplace manifest: .../caveman/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json

× Found 1 error:

  ❯ plugins[0] plugin.json → agents: Invalid input

× Validation failed
```

## Cause

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` lists agent paths without the `./` prefix:

```json
"agents": [
  "agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
  ...
]
```

Claude Code's manifest schema requires each entry to be an explicit relative path. I tested every plausible shape against `claude plugin validate`:

| `agents` value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `"./agents"` (string) | FAIL — `agents: Invalid input` |
| `"agents"` (string) | FAIL — `agents: Invalid input` |
| `["./agents"]` (directory in array) | FAIL — `agents: Invalid input` |
| `["agents/cavecrew-builder.md", ...]` (current) | FAIL — `agents: Invalid input` |
| `["./agents/cavecrew-builder.md", ...]` | **PASS** |
| field omitted | PASS (but loses the three cavecrew agents) |

Only the `./`-prefixed file-path array is accepted.

## Fix

Three lines in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```diff
   "agents": [
-    "agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
-    "agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
-    "agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
+    "./agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
+    "./agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
+    "./agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
   ],
```

## Verification

After the change, on the same machine and Claude Code version:

```
$ claude plugin validate .
‼ Found 1 warning:

  ❯ plugins[0] plugin.json → version: No version specified. ...

√ Validation passed with warnings

$ claude plugin marketplace add <local path>
√ Successfully added marketplace: caveman

$ claude plugin install caveman@caveman
√ Successfully installed plugin: caveman@caveman (scope: user)

$ claude plugin list
  ❯ caveman@caveman
    Status: √ enabled
```

Full install path exercised end to end. No other files touched.

Note: the remaining `version` warning is pre-existing and out of scope for this PR — happy to add a semver `version` field in a follow-up if you want it.

title: engine: unwrap agent <file> wrappers before content detection
body:
## Problem

Coding agents wrap file references handed to the model. pi (pi.dev) turns a `@file` argument into `<file name="...">...</file>`; other agents use the same single-element wrapper convention.

Left in place, the wrapper defeats `Detect`: the payload no longer starts with its real first bytes, so Go source never parses (`code_nocgo.go` only accepts files `go/parser` can parse), JSON never validates, and everything falls through to the `text` compressor, which compresses nothing. Result: pass-through at ratio 0 for every wrapped file the agent sends.

Verified on Windows 11 ARM64 with a real agent: pi sends a 142,409-byte `<file>`-wrapped Go payload; the no-cgo build's code compressor returned ratio 0 → the request went upstream unchanged.

## Fix

`unwrapFileWrapper` is deliberately conservative, mirroring the `listing.go` gutter approach:
- wrapper must be the outermost element
- must open with the literal `<file` tag (attributes allowed)
- exactly one `<file` and exactly one `</file>` (a stray tag inside a string literal = not a plain wrapper)
- must contain non-whitespace content
- anything else returns the input unchanged (no-op wrapper, no caller branches)

`Compress` and `Simulate` unwrap before `Detect` and rewrap compressed output so the model still sees the file reference the agent supplied. Original bytes remain in the CCR store unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestUnwrapFileWrapper`: detection + rewrap round-trip, plus negative cases (plain text, bare Go, HTML, multi-element, truncated wrappers).
- Full `go test ./engine/...` passes.

## End-to-end measurement (real agent)

pi coding agent → caveman proxy → DeepSeek, same task A/B:
- record mode (pass-through): 64,310 input tokens
- compress mode with this fix: 18,478 input tokens (**-71.3%**), answer exact-correct

## License

Engine directory change; signed per DCO.

title: pi (pi.dev) support: proven working end-to-end, needs one schema capability
body:
## Summary

We integrated the pi coding agent (pi.dev, `pi` CLI) with the Caveman Proxy on Windows 11 ARM64 and got it working end-to-end: **input tokens 64,310 → 18,478 (-71.3%)**, exact-correct answer, byte-exact recovery via `caveman_retrieve`. This issue documents what it took, and what a native `pi` profile needs. Happy to implement the profile once the approach is confirmed.

Related: #161, #162, #869 (engine fix this integration required).

## What we found (both verified from source + live tests)

1. **MCP gate**: PAYG streaming traffic uses marker-only compression and requires `CAVEMAN_RECOVERY=mcp`. We registered `caveman-mcp.exe` (stdio, no args, shares `~/.caveman/ccr.db`) in pi's `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` and cross-process retrieval is byte-exact.
2. **Engine gap (fixed in PR #869)**: the Windows ARM64 build's pure-Go code compressor (`code_nocgo.go`) only accepts files `go/parser` can parse. pi wraps file content in `<file name="...">...</file>`, which defeats `Detect` → ratio 0 passthrough. With #869, wrapped Go payloads compress.

## What a pi profile needs (current schema can't express it honestly)

- pi reads providers from `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (custom provider: `baseUrl`, `api: "openai-completions"`, `apiKey`, model entries) and MCP servers from `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`.
- pi has **no** env var to relocate `models.json` (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` relocates the whole agent dir — sessions/auth move too, so it's unusable for injection), and it does not read `CUSTOM_BASE_URL`/`CUSTOM_API_KEY`.
- So the existing `config-file` injection can't target pi as-is: its `env_var` must point the agent at a rendered temp config, and pi has no such pointer.

## Options (in order of preference)

1. **Schema: `config-file` without env redirect** — allow a profile to declare a fixed path under `~/.pi/agent/` (pi's real config location) plus a restore-on-stop. `caveman wrap pi` would render `models.json` + `mcp.json` overlays in place (with backup/restore), which is exactly what our manual test did.
2. **pi-side**: an upstream pi PR adding e.g. `PI_MODELS_PATH` so a standard `config-file` profile with `env_var: PI_MODELS_PATH` works. Cleanest long-term, but spans two repos.
3. Manual recipe only (documentation), no profile.

I'm happy to open the profile PR implementing option 1 (schema addition + profile + tests) if that direction is acceptable.

## Draft profile (for reference)

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "id": "pi",
  "display_name": "pi coding agent",
  "vendor": "pi.dev",
  "homepage": "https://pi.dev/",
  "binary_names": ["pi"],
  "install": "npm install -g pi-coding-agent",
  "wire_protocol": "openai-chat",
  "injection": { "method": "config-file", ... },
  "command_hook": { "method": "none" },
  "tested_agent_version": "0.84.2",
  "fallback": "none"
}
```

title: plugin.json agents paths rejected by Claude Code 2.1.235 (agents: Invalid input)
body:
## Summary

`claude plugin install caveman@caveman` fails manifest validation on Claude Code 2.1.235. The `agents` array in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` lists paths without a leading `./`, which the validator rejects. The marketplace itself adds and clones fine; only the install step fails.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.235
- Windows 11 Pro, native PowerShell (no WSL)
- Node 24.19.0

## Reproduction

```
claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman
claude plugin install caveman@caveman
```

## Actual result

```
Installing plugin "caveman@caveman"...
Failed to install plugin "caveman@caveman": Plugin temp_local_... has an invalid manifest file at .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
Validation errors: agents: Invalid input
```

## Cause

Current manifest:

```json
"agents": [
  "agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
  "agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
  "agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
]
```

The Claude Code plugin reference documents array entries as relative paths with an explicit `./` prefix, e.g. `["./custom-agents/reviewer.md", "./custom-agents/tester.md"]`.

## Suggested fix

```json
"agents": [
  "./agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
  "./agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
  "./agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
]
```

Or omit the `agents` key entirely and let the default `agents/` directory be auto-discovered.

title: Claude Code: plugin.json rejected as invalid — "agents" paths need ./ prefix (regression in 902eba34)
body:
## Summary

Since 902eba34 ("fix: opencode .jsonc config, plugin agent discovery, shrink nested descriptions"), Claude Code rejects the plugin manifest outright:

```
caveman @ caveman (user)
Plugin caveman has an invalid manifest file at
C:\Users\hkkchan\.claude\plugins\cache\caveman\caveman\9e4356e717f0\.claude-plugin\plugin.json
```

`/reload-plugins` reports `1 error during load`, and `/plugin` shows caveman as invalid.

## Cause

That commit added the `agents` array to `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with bare relative paths:

```json
"agents": [
  "agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
  "agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
  "agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
]
```

Claude Code appears to require plugin-relative paths to be explicitly relative (`./`-prefixed). Every other plugin in my local cache that declares component paths uses that form — e.g. `"skills": ["./skills/"]` (agentmemory), `"hooks": "./hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json"` (ponytail).

Evidence that the `agents` key is the trigger, not something else in the file:

- The JSON itself is valid — it parses cleanly with `JSON.parse`, no BOM, no trailing commas.
- The previously cached revision (`0d95a81d35a9`) is byte-identical **except** that it has no `agents` key, and it loads without error.
- A missing `version` field is not the problem; several official plugins in the cache omit `version` and load fine.

The three referenced files do exist at `agents/cavecrew-*.md`, so this is purely the path form, not a missing file.

## Fix

Prefix the paths in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
"agents": [
  "./agents/cavecrew-builder.md",
  "./agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
  "./agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
]
```

Patching the cached copy this way clears the error locally, but the next `/plugin update caveman` overwrites it and the plugin breaks again — hence filing upstream.

Possibly related to the path-form problems in #569 (`"skills": "./skills/"` missing) and #792.

## Environment

- Claude Code on Windows 11 (Git Bash shell)
- Plugin cache revision `9e4356e717f0`
- Upstream `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` on `main` still carries the bare paths as of filing

title: fix(xplat): stop hooks stalling on Windows; own only our own config entries
body:
Whole-repo review of every surface that mutates a user's agent config, plus a cross-platform sweep focused on Windows.

## Windows blockers fixed

| | |
|---|---|
| `caveman-mode-tracker` | Finished its work in ~50ms, then blocked until the host killed it at the 5s budget. The `data` listener *references* the stdin handle, so `pause()` alone keeps the loop alive until the host closes the write end — and on Windows that close lags arbitrarily. This is the shape of #819. Fixed with `process.stdin.unref()`. |
| `caveman-activate` | `readFileSync(0)` blocks *inside* the read syscall until EOF; no deadline can interrupt it. The #729/#833 fix was applied to the tracker and never to its sibling. Rewritten event-driven + watchdog. |
| `hookCommand` | Emitted PowerShell call-operator syntax into `settings.json`, but Claude Code's Windows hook shell is **Git Bash**, which rejects it: `syntax error near unexpected token '&'`. Every standalone Windows install had two dead hooks (#835). |
| `install.{sh,ps1}` | Unguarded backup: a `--force` reinstall overwrote the only pre-caveman `settings.json.bak` with the merged file. |

## Config ownership

`src/hooks/uninstall.{sh,ps1}` matched hooks by the substring `caveman` and filtered whole entries — deleting user hooks that merely mention the word, and dropping foreign handlers sharing a matcher group (#593). Verified against real PowerShell: the old code left **zero** user hooks standing.

title: feat(hooks): propagate caveman mode to subagents via SubagentStart
body:
## Problem

SessionStart context is parent-thread only — it never reaches Task-spawned subagents. So in an active caveman session, every subagent (Explore, custom agents, …) runs caveman-unaware and emits full-verbosity output, forfeiting the token savings exactly where output volume is highest.

Closes #672.

## Fix

A SubagentStart hook (`src/hooks/caveman-subagent.js`) that re-reads the active level from the same flag file the other hooks use — via `readFlag`, so it inherits the symlink refusal, size cap, and `VALID_MODES` whitelist — and re-injects the level-filtered SKILL.md ruleset into each spawned subagent as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (raw stdout is silently dropped on SubagentStart). Off/absent/invalid flag → silent exit 0. No stdin read, so there is nothing to stall on spawn.

Pattern ported from ponytail (MIT, [DietrichGebert/ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail)), which closed the same gap for its own mode.

## Relation to #621

#621 proposes the same hook and I'd have been happy to just +1 it, but its SKILL.md lookup is a single `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'skills', …)` — from `src/hooks/` that resolves to `src/skills/`, which doesn't exist, so **plugin installs would always serve the weak inline fallback instead of the real ruleset**. That's the exact bug class #690 reported against caveman-activate.js (fixed in #587/#589 with the 3-candidate order). This PR:

- resolves SKILL.md with the same 3-candidate order as `caveman-activate.js` (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` → `../../` → `../`), so plugin installs get the real ruleset;
- guards the `caveman-config` sibling require (#848): a broken install degrades to inject-nothing, never to a MODULE_NOT_FOUND crash on every subagent spawn;
- skips independent modes (`commit`/`review`/`compress`) — their skill only exists in the parent session, so an activation line pointing at it would be an instruction the subagent can't follow;
- ships tests.

## Changes

- `src/hooks/caveman-subagent.js` — the hook (new)
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — SubagentStart entry
- `bin/install.js`, `src/hooks/install.sh` + `install.ps1`, `uninstall.sh` + `uninstall.ps1`, `checksums.sha256` — wired everywhere the existing hooks are wired, idempotent and marker-guarded like them
- `tests/test_caveman_subagent.js` — 8 cases: active-mode injection with level filtering, wenyan alias, off/absent/invalid flag silence, independent-mode skip, missing-sibling degrade (#848), SKILL.md-unreachable fallback

## Verification

- `node tests/test_caveman_subagent.js` → 8/8; existing `test_hook_missing_sibling.js` (18/18) and `tests/test_hooks.py` (7/7) still green; `bash -n` / `node --check` clean on every touched script.
- e2e: `install.sh` into a temp `$HOME` wires all three hooks and copies the file; `uninstall.sh` removes both again.
- Live on Claude Code 2.1.228 (macOS): with the hook installed, a real Task-spawned subagent reports the injected ruleset in its context — `SubagentStart hook additional context: CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full`.

title: win32 hook commands prefixed with '&' break under Git Bash dispatch
body:
## Bug: win32 hook commands prefixed with `& ` break under Git Bash dispatch

`hookExecutableInvocation()` (`packages/cli/src/index.ts`) unconditionally prefixes every win32 hook command with `& `:

```js
export function hookExecutableInvocation(executable, script, platform = process.platform) {
    const invocation = script
        ? `${quoteHookPath(executable, platform)} ${quoteHookPath(script, platform)}`
        : quoteHookPath(executable, platform);
    // Claude/Codex/Gemini dispatch command hooks through PowerShell on native
    // Windows. A quoted executable is only a string literal there; `&` is the
    // required invocation operator. POSIX hook commands keep their exact shape.
    return platform === "win32" ? `& ${invocation}` : invocation;
}
```

The comment's assumption — that Claude Code always dispatches hook commands through PowerShell on native Windows — doesn't hold for installs where Claude Code (or its Bash tool / hook runner) executes commands via Git Bash / MSYS instead. There, `&` is the background-job operator, not a PowerShell call operator, so every hook using this invocation (`native-hook`, generated via `nativeHookCommand()`/`nativeHookInvocation()`) fails:

```
/usr/bin/bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `&'
/usr/bin/bash: -c: line 1: `& 'C:/.../caveman-proxy.exe' native-hook claude --adapter '...''
```

Symptom in Claude Code: `SessionStart hook error`, `UserPromptSubmit operation blocked by hook`, quoting the syntax error above. This surfaced after upgrading `@caveman-ai/cli` (the `&`-prefix was added by a recent fix for a different, unrelated quoting bug — the prefix logic itself was untested against a Bash-dispatch environment).

**Repro:** Any Claude Code setup on Windows where hooks run through Git Bash rather than PowerShell (e.g. `bash` configured as the shell for the Bash tool / hook execution) — `caveman hooks install claude` or the `caveman claude` wrapper writes the `& '...'` form, and every native-hook lifecycle event (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, etc.) fails with the syntax error above.

**Fix applied locally** (patched `dist/index.js`, reversible, will be overwritten by next upgrade): drop the win32 `& ` prefix entirely — `quoteHookPath()`'s single-quoted, forward-slash form is valid as a plain command invocation under Git Bash without the operator.

```js
return invocation; // no platform-conditional `&` prefix
```

This obviously isn't correct for actual PowerShell-dispatch installs (that's presumably why the prefix was added) — a real fix needs to detect *which* shell is actually invoking the hook command rather than assuming PowerShell whenever `platform === "win32"`. Not obvious from the CLI's own vantage point which shell Claude Code will use to run the command string; may need a Claude Code hook-execution-shell env var/flag to key off of, or documentation telling Windows users which shell to configure Claude Code hooks against.

Version: `@caveman-ai/cli@1.2.1` (npm latest). Platform: Windows 11, Git Bash (MSYS) as Claude Code's hook-execution shell.

title: npx github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- <flag> invokes the wrong caveman bin (collides with @caveman-ai/cli dependency)
body:
\`npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --uninstall\` (and any other flag) fails:
\`\`\`
unknown command "--" — did you mean \`caveman run\`?
see: caveman --help
\`\`\`
That error/help text isn't from \`bin/install.js\` (the installer) — it's from the dependency \`@caveman-ai/cli\`.

**Root cause:** \`package.json\` declares \`"bin": {"caveman": "./bin/install.js"}\`, but \`@caveman-ai/cli\` (listed in \`dependencies\`, v1.2.1) *also* declares \`"bin": {"caveman": "dist/index.js", "cave": "dist/index.js"}\`. When npx installs the temp project, \`node_modules/.bin/caveman\` ends up pointing at \`@caveman-ai/cli\`'s \`dist/index.js\`, not the installer — confirmed by inspecting the npx cache directory directly (both \`.bin/caveman\` and \`.bin/cave\` resolve to \`@caveman-ai/cli\`).

So every documented top-level command in the README/\`--help\` (\`npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman\`, \`-- --all\`, \`-- --uninstall\`, etc.) silently runs the wrong CLI. This isn't Windows-specific — it's a bin-name collision in the dependency tree and should reproduce on macOS/Linux too.

**Repro:**
\`\`\`
npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --uninstall
\`\`\`
**Expected:** runs \`bin/install.js --uninstall\`.
**Actual:** runs \`@caveman-ai/cli\`'s CLI, which rejects bare \`--\`.

**Environment:** Windows, npm 11.17.0, node v24.19.0.

**Workaround:** clone the repo and run \`node bin/install.js --uninstall\` directly (bypasses the npx bin resolution entirely).

**Fix suggestion:** rename the installer's own bin (e.g. \`caveman-install\`) or drop \`@caveman-ai/cli\` from \`dependencies\` (make it an optional/separate install) so the two \`caveman\` bins stop colliding.

title: plugin.json: "agents" field uses file paths, but schema expects directory paths — install fails validation

**Bug:** `claude plugin install caveman@caveman` fails with:

**Cause:** `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares `agents` as an array of individual
markdown files:

    "agents": [

      "agents/cavecrew-investigator.md",
      "agents/cavecrew-reviewer.md"
    ]

Per Claude Code's plugin manifest schema, `agents` must point to a directory
(string or array of directory paths), e.g. `"agents": "./agents"` — not a list

plugins/plugin-dev/skills/plugin-structure/references/manifest-reference.md
in anthropics/claude-plugins-official, which shows `"agents": "./specialized-agents"`.

**Fix:** change plugin.json to:

    "agents": "./agents"

The three files already live correctly under `agents/` — this is a one-line
manifest fix, no file moves needed.

**Repro:**

    claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman
    claude plugin install caveman@caveman
    # → Validation errors: agents: Invalid input

Tested on Claude Code CLI 2.1.236.
