title: SKILL.md wording (self-reference suppression + hard persistence) gets pattern-matched as prompt injection by anti-injection classifiers
body:
**What happen**

Claude (Claude Code, Sonnet 5) repeatedly flags the caveman SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook output as a *prompt injection attempt* and refuses to comply — sometimes surfacing that suspicion directly to the user in its response. This is distinct from #852 (rules delivered but ignored over time): here the rules are delivered but actively distrusted on arrival, on some turns, in some sessions.

Root cause looks like specific wording in `SKILL.md` that structurally matches known injection heuristics:

```
No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think",
no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap.
```

and

```
ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure.
```

Anti-injection training specifically targets two patterns: (1) instructions telling a model to *conceal that it is following injected instructions*, and (2) instructions demanding the model *persist against user pushback / ignore attempts to deactivate it*. Both lines above match those patterns closely, even though the actual intent here is benign (consistent style, not hidden persuasion).

This looks like it got worse specifically on recent Anthropic models — consistent with tightened anti-injection classifiers rather than any plugin-side change (no relevant edits in this version, `0d95a81d35a9`).

**Expected**

Hook-injected ruleset applies without the model treating it as adversarial content, and without flagging it to the user as suspicious.

**Suggested wording changes** (keep the same behavioral intent, remove the injection-shaped phrasing):

- Replace "No self-reference. Never name or announce the style." with something outcome-focused instead of concealment-focused, e.g. "Answer directly in this style — skip a 'Caveman:' prefix or recap, it's redundant with the reply itself."
- Soften "Still active if unsure" / "No revert after many turns" — persistence framed as "default behavior for this session" rather than "resist reversion," e.g. "Default for this session unless the user says 'stop caveman' or 'normal mode'."

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**
- Plugin: `caveman@caveman`, pinned `0d95a81d35a9`
- Level: `full` (default)
- Model: Claude Sonnet 5 (Anthropic)

Related: #852 (drift/ignoring), #468 (closed — recap wording fix, same file)

title: fix(cli): honour HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY for outbound requests
body:
Node's global `fetch` ignores the conventional proxy variables. On a host whose egress only leaves through an HTTP proxy, that means every request the CLI makes fails while `curl` and `npm` — which do read those variables — work fine.

First thing a new user hits:

```
$ caveman setup --install
binary download unreachable — agents still launch; traffic is NOT compressed or metered
fix: caveman setup --install
```

The fix points back at the command that just failed, and nothing in the message suggests a proxy is involved. I lost a while to it before checking whether `fetch` reads the variables at all. The same blind spot affects the npm version check, `login`, and every cloud call.

Node 24 can opt in with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, and 22 has the same switch behind an experimental warning, but it is off by default and a process cannot turn it on for itself after start-up — so the CLI has to implement the variables.

## What this does

New `packages/cli/src/proxy-fetch.ts`, no dependencies added:

- `resolveProxyUrl(target, env)` — `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` by scheme with `ALL_PROXY` as fallback, lower case winning over upper (curl's precedence), bare `host:port` and credentialed forms accepted.
- `shouldBypassProxy(target, noProxy)` — `NO_PROXY` with `*`, exact host, domain suffix with or without leading dot, and optional port pinning.
- `createProxyAwareFetch(baseFetch, env)` — CONNECT tunnel for https so TLS still terminates at the target rather than the proxy, absolute-form for http. Redirects are followed with the proxy re-resolved per hop, so a hop into a `NO_PROXY` host goes direct instead of being forced back through the proxy.
- `installProxyAwareFetch()` — called at the top of `main()`, before any request. No-ops when nothing is configured, and when `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` is set, so a runtime already handling proxying is not proxied twice.

Wrapping `globalThis.fetch` once at start-up rather than editing ~20 call sites keeps proxy semantics in one module and leaves the call sites alone.

## Verification

A/B on a proxy-only host, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` deliberately unset, clean `HOME`:

| | `setup --install` |
|---|---|
| before | `binary download unreachable` |
| after | six binaries downloaded, `checksum verified` each |

`packages/cli/tests/proxy-fetch.runtime.mjs` adds 12 tests: variable precedence and scheme selection, `ALL_PROXY` fallback, bare host and credentials, `NO_PROXY` matching including the suffix false-positive case (`example.test.evil.test` must not match `.example.test`), tunnelling through a real local proxy, bypass, redirect chains with per-hop resolution, POST bodies and methods surviving the hop, abort, and the install guard.

`npm run test:fast` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean.

## Notes for review

- I kept `Response` construction on `Readable.toWeb` so streaming downloads still stream; the release download hashes as it goes and that path is unchanged.
- Redirect cap is 20, matching the fetch spec rather than inventing a number.
- One documented cast (`asBodyInit`) because `BodyInit` in the bundled DOM types predates byte-array bodies.
- Happy to split the module into resolution and transport files if you would rather keep transport separate.

title: fix(caveman): keep procedural safety steps and citations in plain text
body:
## What

Strengthens the Auto-Clarity guard so procedural safety checks and source citations always drop back to plain text instead of being compressed.

## Why

A live benchmark on Hermes (deepseek-v4-pro) found a real failure: on a multi-step nginx cert rotation, the compressed output silently dropped the openssl cert/key modulus match check (a safety verification step that must run before reload), plus the certbot-vs-manual detection step and the source citations. The existing "multi-step sequences" guard did not catch it, because the dropped step was a correctness check, not an order-ambiguity problem.

## Change

Two new drop-conditions in Auto-Clarity:

- Procedural steps that verify safety or correctness (checksum, cert/key modulus match, pre-flight check): keep every step and exact command, in order
- Source citations and reference URLs: keep them so the reader can verify

## Verification

8-case benchmark on Hermes: visible answer text cut 70 percent (24,126 to 7,307 bytes), 7 of 8 cases kept exact commands, flags, ports, and warnings. The one failure was the nginx cert rotation above, which this change addresses.

title: caveman-compress is quarantined as 'dangerous' by Hermes Agent's project-skill scanner (denylist literals, os.environ.get(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), CLAUDE.md mentions) — sibling of #528
body:
## Summary

`caveman-compress` is quarantined as **`dangerous`** by Hermes Agent's project-skill scanner (`tools/skills_guard.py`) when it sits in a repo's `.agents/skills/` — the skill silently disappears from every Hermes session for that repo (no `--force` path for `dangerous` on community/project skills). Sibling of #528 (the `caveman` skill, fixed in v2.1.0); `caveman-compress` has its own distinct triggers, and they are all still present on `main` / v2.2.0.

Hermes Agent v0.20.5 (2026.8.19). Log line:

```
WARNING agent.skill_utils: Project skill quarantined (verdict=dangerous): ...\.agents\skills\caveman-compress — caveman-compress: dangerous — 17 finding(s) in execution, exfiltration, persistence
```

## Findings (reproduced with `scan_skill()`; line numbers from current `main` `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py`)

| pattern | severity | where | what matched |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh_backdoor` | **critical** | `compress.py:64` | `r"\|authorized_keys"` — an entry in `SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX`, i.e. the skill's **own denylist** of files it refuses to read |
| `aws_dir_access` | high | `compress.py:54` | the comment `# … credentials.md / secrets.txt / ~/.aws/credentials would slip through …` explaining that denylist |
| `python_environ_get_secret` | **critical** | `compress.py:281` | `api_key = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` |
| `python_os_environ` | high | same line | bare `os.environ` |
| `python_subprocess` | medium | `compress.py` (the `claude` CLI fallback) + `SECURITY.md:9` (the sentence *describing* it) | `subprocess.run(` |
| `agent_config_mod` ×11 | critical | `README.md`, `SKILL.md` (incl. the `description:` line), `scripts/detect.py:76` | the literal token `CLAUDE.md` |

Any single `critical` → `dangerous`.

## What is being fixed on the Hermes side (so you don't have to)

- `agent_config_mod` on bare `CLAUDE.md` mentions: NousResearch/hermes-agent#92021 → PR #92249 (tiered; bare mention becomes informational).
- `python_environ_get_secret` → medium and comment-line skipping: NousResearch/hermes-agent#60709 → PR #60750.
- The denylist-literal case (`ssh_backdoor` / `aws_dir_access` on a skip-list regex / comment): NousResearch/hermes-agent#92478 (just filed, no PR yet).

## What would make `caveman-compress` install today, regardless of Hermes' timeline

Cheap, no behaviour change:

1. Don't spell the sensitive basenames as literals in the regex source — e.g. build `SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX` from a tuple and `"|".join(...)` it, or assemble the two hot tokens (`"authorized_" "keys"`, `"known_" "hosts"`) so the scanner's token never appears on one line. (Same idea as the #528 fix.)
2. Drop `~/.aws/credentials` from the comment on line 54 (say "cloud credential files").
3. Let the SDK resolve the key: `anthropic.Anthropic()` reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` itself, so the explicit `os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` at :281 can go (keep the "is the SDK usable" branch by catching `anthropic.AuthenticationError` / checking `"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" in os.environ`, which does not match `python_environ_get_secret`).

(Items 1–3 are enough once hermes #92249 lands; until then the `CLAUDE.md` mentions still score critical on their own, which only Hermes can fix.)

## Repro

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tools.skills_guard import scan_skill          # from a hermes-agent checkout
r = scan_skill(Path("<clone>/skills/caveman-compress"))
print(r.verdict); [print(f.pattern_id, f.severity, f.file, f.line) for f in r.findings]
```

Happy to send the 3-line PR for 1–3 if you want it.

title: Proxy: ~1 in 6 concurrent non-streaming responses arrive corrupted — client fails with `ZlibError` (compressed body re-encoding race?)
body:
Under concurrent subagent load, roughly 1 in 6 non-streaming `/v1/messages` requests through caveman-proxy fails **client-side** with:

```
API Error: ZlibError fetching "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/claude/v1/messages?beta=true".
For more information, pass `verbose: true` in the second argument to fetch()
```

`ZlibError` here is Node's `fetch` failing to decompress the response body, so the connection and headers are fine but the compressed payload the proxy served is corrupt. Single sequential main-loop requests never hit it; it only appears when a client fans out several parallel requests (e.g. Claude Code spawning 6+ subagents for a multi-agent code review). The affected subagent dies with "Agent terminated early due to an API error".

## Environment

- caveman CLI **1.2.3** (`binary_release: bin-v1.1.2`); the proxy's own run file reports `"version":"dev"` — happy to pull anything else from it
- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)
- Claude Code 2.1.241 (Node 24.19.0)
- Wrap mode (`caveman claude`), `mode: compress`, `recovery_via_mcp: true`
- Local-only setup, no cloud seat

## Evidence

- Two separate days, consistent rate: proxy counters logged **231 unavailable / 1371 provider_complete** on day one and **296 unavailable / 1765 provider_complete** the next — ~1 in 6 both days.
- Survives a proxy restart **and** a full machine reboot with a fresh session; the rate was unchanged immediately after reboot.
- Only non-streaming requests fail. Streaming turns pass through uncompressed in my configuration (Pro/Max passthrough), which matches: the failure lives on the path where the proxy decodes and re-serves a compressed body.
- The proxy binary's strings include `content_decode_failed/gzip`, `content_decode_failed/zstd`, `content_decode_failed/deflate` and vendored `github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd`, so the proxy is decoding provider gzip/zstd bodies and re-encoding them for the client. My working hypothesis is a race on that re-encode path under concurrency — shared encoder/buffer state producing a corrupted compressed body — since sequential traffic through the exact same code path never fails.

## Repro

1. Run Claude Code through the proxy (wrap mode, compress on).
2. Launch any task that fans out parallel subagents making non-streaming `/v1/messages` calls (a multi-agent code review reproduces it reliably for me).
3. Watch ~1 in 6 of those requests die with the `ZlibError` above; the rest complete normally.

## Not #880

Checked #880 ("connection refused after some time"): different failure. Here the connection succeeds and the response arrives; only the body fails to decompress.

Happy to run a debug build, capture `verbose: true` fetch output, or enable any proxy logging you point me at.

title: chore(skills): shorten skill descriptions to fit the listing budget
body:
Claude Code spends a fixed character budget on the skill listing it puts in the model's context: `contextWindowTokens * 4 * skillListingBudgetFraction`, which is about 6,000 characters at the default fraction of 0.01. Overflow is binary per skill rather than proportional truncation: skills are ranked by recent usage and granted their full description in that order until the budget runs out, and everything past the cutoff renders as a bare name with no description at all.

The 14 caveman skills spent 6,140 characters, more than the entire default budget on their own, so an install that carries caveman alongside other plugins pushes unrelated skills past the cutoff and loses them their discoverability - and, once caveman's own least-used skills fall past it, some of caveman's too.

This rewrites the descriptions to 3,539 characters total. Every trigger phrase and every boundary clause is kept, including the named slash-command and spoken triggers, the level names, and the do-not-use exclusions; what goes is restatement of the body, which the model reads anyway once the skill is selected. No skill body changes.

`skills/compile.mjs` was re-run, so `packages/cli/src/agent-skills.generated.ts` moves with its source.

Signed-off-by: smoochy <34371932+smoochy@users.noreply.github.com>

title: repository-intelligence BM25 index includes .pixi/envs vendored deps, injects irrelevant 'likely implementation path' every turn
body:
## Summary

`repository-intelligence` policy (proxy `mode: compress`, `version: dev`) injects a "Likely implementation path" block into every `UserPromptSubmit` context via BM25 matching, but the index is not scoped to project source — it includes `.pixi/envs/**` (the project's own installed conda/pip dependencies). Result: every turn gets a fabricated-looking "evidence" block pointing at unrelated vendored files, regardless of relevance to the actual user message.

## Environment

- `caveman-proxy` run log (`~/.caveman/run/8787.json`): `"version":"dev"`, `"mode":"compress"`, `"owner":"wrap"`
- Integration pack (`~/.caveman/integrations/claude.json`): `"pack_version":"2.2.0"`, installed via Claude Code settings rewrite (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/claude`)
- Active policies (`~/.caveman/receipts/latest.json`): includes `task-contract`, `repository-intelligence`, `cache-aware-prompt`
- Client: Claude Code, project is a Mojo package using `pixi` (conda-forge) for deps, deps live under `<repo>/.pixi/envs/default/...`

## Repro

Ask the agent anything in a `pixi`-managed repo. Every `UserPromptSubmit` gets an extra system-reminder like:

```
UserPromptSubmit hook additional context: Likely implementation path (observed local metadata):
1. .pixi/envs/default/lib/python3.14/xml/sax/xmlreader.py:107 — symbol matches task terms
Evidence: ccr://ccr_obj_09f4b7e4dd159d2070fb87854ab9b67f. Scout: not_started_no_configured_local_scout.
```

Observed across several turns in one session, matched off single stray keywords in the user prompt (e.g. "proxy" → `site-packages/zmq/devices/proxydevice.py`, generic terms → `dbus-1/system.conf`, `unicode/utfiterator.h`, `email/mime/image.py`). None of these files are part of the project's own source (`src/`, `examples/`) — they're all inside the pixi-managed dependency tree, which should be excluded the same way `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, or `vendor/` would be for other ecosystems.

## Expected

- BM25 candidate index for `repository-intelligence` should exclude known dependency/vendor directories (`.pixi/envs`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `vendor`, etc.), the same exclusion list presumably already applied to `.git`.
- When no local scout is configured (`Scout: not_started_no_configured_local_scout`), consider suppressing the "Likely implementation path" block entirely rather than emitting low-confidence guesses with a `ccr://` evidence handle that reads as authoritative.

## Actual

Irrelevant vendored-dependency file:line guesses injected into every turn's context, with an evidence handle format that looks authoritative but isn't scoped/filtered.

## Impact

Wastes context/tokens each turn (ironic for a token-compression tool) and risks steering the agent toward wrong files if taken at face value.

title: fix(proxy): scope repo intelligence to project source and require direct evidence
body: Fixes #899. `repository-intelligence` walked the whole working tree, ranked BM25 hits, and injected a "Likely implementation path" block into every `UserPromptSubmit`. In pixi-managed repos that included `.pixi/envs/**`, so a generic prompt word like `proxy` pointed at `site-packages/zmq/devices/proxydevice.py` behind a `ccr://` handle that reads as authoritative. Two rounds of adversarial review reshaped this: the first replaced a longer directory-name denylist (too narrow and too wide) with content-based detection, the second found the git listing both unsafe and incomplete. Each regression guard below was verified to fail without its fix. ## Which files may be indexed **Primary: the project's own `.gitignore`.** `listFiles` prefers `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` — an installed dependency tree is ignored by the project that installed it, so git already knows what is source. Two things git is *not* trusted for: - An empty-but-successful listing means the cwd is itself ignored by an enclosing repository. Accepting it silently disabled the whole mechanism while reporting a complete map, so empty falls back to the walk. - Every git-listed path still runs the same content filter as the walk (`directoryFilter`, memoised per directory, one probe per directory rather than per file). Without it an un-ignored conda prefix or a *committed* `vendor/` tree reaches the model precisely because git reported the file. **Detection is by contents, not name.** A directory containing `conda-meta`, `pyvenv.cfg`, or a `site-packages` child is a dependency root under any name — `.pixi`, `envs/py314`, `toolbox` — which also stops the interpreter standard library it carries (`/lib/python3.14/xml/sax/xmlreader.py`, the exact path in the report). Name matching is a narrow, case-folded backstop for names that are never first-party. `build`, `dist`, `target`, `vendor`, `coverage`, and `Pods` are ambiguous and excluded only when a sibling manifest proves the ecosystem, so `internal/build` and a hand-written `vendor/` survive. Symlinked and Windows junction directories are never followed. **`Map.ListingBasis`** discloses which path ran and is folded into `ContentSHA256`, because the two can legitimately disagree (git omits submodule contents). ## Running git against an untrusted repository A repository's `.git/config` names programs git will run, and `core.fsmonitor` runs while the index is read — so plain `git ls-files` in a freshly cloned hostile repo executes attacker code at session start, with no user action. Hardening one call site was not enough. `nativehook.currentRepositoryState` runs `git status` on every hook event and refreshes the index, which triggers `core.fsmonitor` harder than `ls-files` does (verified: the sentinel hook fires), and `store/detect_outcomes` plus two `execFileSync` sites in the CLI were equally raw. The `-c` override list (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, `core.editor`, `core.pager`, `core.alternateRefsCommand`, `diff.external`, `credential.helper`, `protocol.ext.allow`, `uploadpack.packObjectsHook`) now lives in `proxy/internal/gitsafe` and `packages/cli/src/git-safe.ts`, and all five call sites route through it; inherited `GIT_*` is stripped. `tests/verify_repo.py` fails the build on any new raw `git -C ` call site, which is the regression class this belongs to. Listing output is streamed rather than buffered whole, and `gitListBudget` caps git at half the caller's remaining warm budget — taking 2s of a 3s window left the fallback walk, the more expensive path, unable to finish, so the map failed closed in exactly the case the fallback exists for. ## What may be shown to the model - `EvidenceItem.Direct` requires a task term in the file's **own name** or a symbol name. Matching the whole path meant a term naming any ancestor (`src`, `internal`, `lib` — ordinary prompt words) marked every file beneath it, which is no gate at all. `NormalizeTerms` floors terms at three characters to match: direct evidence is a substring test on a file's own name, so `go`/`py`/`js` marked every file of that language a direct hit. - `Bundle.Strength` is `direct_path_or_symbol_match`, `metadata_only`, or `none`. Only `StrengthDirect` is rendered, stored, or given a `ccr://` handle. `Bundle.DirectOnly()` strips metadata-only items *before* the evidence object is written — filtering only at render time left the BM25-proximity guesses stored behind the handle, one retrieval away from the model, which is exactly what the block refuses to render. - A declined turn is silent to the model but records `repository_evidence_declined_no_direct_match` in the ledger, so "declined" stays distinguishable from "broken". - `Scout.Status` is advisory again; gating on it meant a truncated map silenced real hits. The empty-items branch no longer emits a `ccr://` handle either. `FilesScanned` keeps its original meaning; `FilesRanked` is the filtered count. ## Unrelated: the red `engine-ci / windows` check Three pre-existing failures, each hidden behind the previous one, none related to repo intelligence. The Windows job runs `npm test`, then `pnpm -r test`, then `npm run test:windows`, and it has failed at the first step on `main` since Aug 19 — so the later steps had not run at all. **1. `npm test` — `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks keeps a foreign-platform absolute path it cannot judge`.** The guard it covers is POSIX-only by construction: win32's absolute set is a superset of posix's, so `C:\Users\me\.claude\hooks\caveman-activate.js` is *not* a foreign path to a Windows host, which resolves it natively, finds nothing, and prunes — correct behaviour there, and the opposite of what the test asserts. `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks` now takes an explicit `platform` argument defaulting to `process.platform` (same shape as `rewriteLegacyManagedHookCommands`) and selects `path.win32` / `path.posix` from it rather than from the host `path` module, so the POSIX side of the asymmetry is reachable from a Windows runner. Host behaviour is unchanged. A companion test pins the own-platform side: with `platform: 'win32'` the same missing `C:\...` target is a real orphan and is pruned. **2. `npm run test:windows` — all six Pi enable/wrap round trips.** Every stub-backed child process died in its preload: ``` Cannot find module 'C:UsersRUNNER~1AppDataLocalTempcave-pi-enable-7SwNZEbinstub-dispatch.cjs' ``` Node parses `NODE_OPTIONS` itself, and inside a quoted value a backslash is an escape character, so the harness's `--require ""` arrived with every separator consumed. Verified directly on Linux with a file named `a\b.cjs`: quoted-single-backslash fails to resolve, quoted-double-backslash loads. The quotes have to stay (a temp dir under a profile name with spaces), so `stubEnv` now doubles the separators. POSIX is untouched — `stubEnv` returns before that line on non-Windows. Added a Windows-only test that spawns a child under a stub env rooted in a path with a space, so a regression reports the cause instead of six `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`s. **3. `pnpm -r test` — `EBUSY: resource busy or locked` copying `binary-installer.generated.mjs`.** `mcp`, `shrink`, and `browse` each run `gen-wedge-installer.mjs` from their own prepack/pretest, and every run writes all four targets rather than just its own. `pnpm -r` runs those packages in parallel, so several processes copied onto the same file at once and Windows failed the loser. Every writer produces identical bytes and the outputs are committed, so the race was over writes that change nothing: the script now skips when the destination already matches and lands a real change through a temp file plus rename. Verified with a 12-way concurrent storm, and against deliberately corrupted outputs to prove the write path still restores them byte-exact. ## Tests `proxy/internal/repointel`: marker-based detection under non-obvious names, gitignore-driven listing, dependency filtering applied to git output, empty-listing fallback, git command hardening, ambiguous dirs kept without a manifest and dropped with one, case folding, truncated map keeping direct evidence, file-name-vs-whole-path matching, metadata-only and empty bundles rejected, scanned/ranked counts. `proxy/internal/nativeruntime` and `proxy/internal/nativehook`: `.pixi` tree ignored end to end through `Handle`, weak evidence injecting nothing and recording no bundle or `RecoveryRef` (with a positive control in the same session), direct hits still rendered when scout is unconfigured, hook-path `git status` running under the hardened overrides. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass in `proxy/`; `tests/verify_repo.py` passes; `npm test` passes (173 tests, 0 failures); the Pi round trips and `windows-platform` contracts pass locally on Linux; the CLI build and browse pretest chain both run clean after the wedge-generation change.

title: fix: scope caveman mode to the session
body:
## The problem

The mode is applied per session but stored in one file per machine
(`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-active`). Four user-visible bugs follow from
that single fact:

1. **Parallel windows share a mode.** `/caveman ultra` in one window
   retargets the other.
2. **"stop caveman" is undone by auto-compaction.** Deactivation is spelled
   "no flag file", so the next SessionStart re-derives the configured
   default and switches caveman back on.
3. **The statusline badge is machine-wide.** Every window renders whichever
   mode was written last.
4. **`off` cannot survive a SessionStart** — there is nowhere to put it.

Reproducing #2 on current `main`, driving the hooks exactly as Claude Code
does:

```bash
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
echo '{"session_id":"A","source":"startup"}' | node src/hooks/caveman-activate.js >/dev/null
echo '{"session_id":"A","prompt":"stop caveman"}' | node src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js
echo '{"session_id":"A","source":"compact"}'  | node src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
# → CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Why #691 does not close it

#691 branches SessionStart on the payload's source, which correctly
preserves a mid-session level change across a compaction. But it reads
the legacy flag, and in that file "off" is expressed as absence — so a
deactivated session finds nothing stored and falls through to
getDefaultMode() anyway. Bugs 1, 3 and 4 are consequences of the storage
shape rather than of when the hook re-derives: one file cannot hold two
windows' modes, and an absent file cannot express "deliberately off"
distinguishably from "never set".

The change

State moves to $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-sessions/<session_id>.mode,
keyed by the session_id Claude Code already puts in every hook payload
and in the statusline's stdin JSON. .caveman-active stays as a
last-write-wins compat mirror.

Two invariants are load-bearing:

- The mirror never holds the literal off. Deactivation unlinks it.
  off is in VALID_MODES, so an older caveman-mode-tracker.js reading
  it from that path would pass its !INDEPENDENT_MODES.has(...) check and
  inject "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (off)", and an older caveman-statusline.sh
  would render [CAVEMAN:OFF]. Mixed-version installs are real: plugin
  hooks and standalone hooks can both be registered, and statusLine holds
  a path baked in at install time.
- recordModeChange compares against the session's own state, never the
  mirror. Diffing against the mirror would compare one session's
  transition to whatever another session wrote last and spam the log with
  phantom entries. That is why readSessionModeRaw exists alongside
  resolveActiveMode.

Both spellings of off are read everywhere: a missing file (old) and a
literal off (new, durable).

caveman-config.js gains the primitives — validateSessionId (a
whitelist, because a session id becomes part of a path),
resolveActiveMode, readSessionModeRaw, writeSessionMode, per-session
prev for one-shot skills (#599), gcSessionStore (14-day mtime sweep,
startup only — a compaction should not spend the 5s budget walking a
directory), and a session_id-tagged recordModeChange (#601).

caveman-stats filters the transition log on session_id, so a switch in
window B no longer lands inside window A's timeline and skews its estimate.
Both statusline ports take session_id from stdin with bounded,
TTY-guarded reads and render nothing for a deactivated session. Uninstall
(bin/install.js, uninstall.sh, uninstall.ps1) removes the session
store; .caveman-history.jsonl is kept on purpose.

Backward compatibility

Every helper accepts a sessionId that may be null or malformed and
degrades to the previous machine-wide behavior. The old code path is the
fallback branch — which is why the pre-existing suites, none of which send
a session_id, pass unchanged. A session that began before this change,
with only the legacy flag on disk, keeps its mode including across a
compaction.

The three hook entrypoints resolve the new helpers individually
(cfg.writeSessionMode || <legacy stub>) instead of adding them to their
requireSibling shape checks. A caveman-config.js from before this
change satisfies those checks, so hard-failing over the newer exports would
trade "machine-wide mode, as it always worked" for "no state at all" on
exactly the plugin-cache drift #848 exists for.

Decisions worth challenging

- clear re-derives the default; compact/resume/fork do not. This
  differs from #691's comment, which groups clear with the continuations.
  Rationale: /clear is an explicit reset and nothing else in the
  conversation survives it, so neither should a "stop caveman" from before
  it. Per-session storage makes the distinction cheap. Easy to flip if you
  disagree — it is one entry in RESET_SOURCES.
- The payload watchdog's unknown source preserves stored state. If it
  assumed startup, a slow payload on a compaction would drop a
  mid-session ultra (#691 through the timeout door) and re-arm a session
  the user turned off.
- The mirror is kept at all. It costs one extra write per mode change.
  It is there because INSTALL.md tells users to cat it and
  src/hooks/README.md ships a third-party statusline snippet that reads
  it. Dropping it would be a cleaner design and a silent break for those
  readers.

Not touched

- opencode. src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js keeps the machine-wide
  behaviour: it writes its own flag in the opencode config dir and never
  sees a Claude Code session_id. Out of scope here.
- PowerShell badge behaviour. The Windows CI job parses every .ps1 and
  drives install/uninstall, but nothing renders the badge, so
  caveman-statusline.ps1 is covered only by the parity greps added to
  verify_repo.py (SESSIONS_DIRNAME, SESSION_ID_RE, the durable-off
  short-circuit, the stdin guards, and the bash-3.2 fractional-timeout ban).

Tests

New:

- tests/hooks/caveman-config.test.mjs — 25 in-process cases over the
  storage layer: id validation and path containment, durable off, prev
  scoping, mode-log tagging, GC including symlink refusal.
- tests/test_hooks.py::SessionStartSourceTests — source branching, plus
  the stdin hang guard (fails by timing out, not by asserting).
- tests/test_mode_tracker.py::SessionScopedModeTests — two windows,
  independent modes, mirror never holding off, traversal ids.
- 5 statusline cases in tests/test_caveman_stats.js — session badge,
  durable off, legacy fallback, traversal, multiline JSON.
- tests/manual/session-mode-smoke.sh — 22 end-to-end checks driving the
  real hook binaries against a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

package.json and the Node 18 fallback in ci.yml pick up
tests/hooks/*.test.mjs. src/hooks/checksums.sha256 regenerated.

npm test                              197/197
node --test tests/*.js                10 files, 0 failures
python -m unittest discover -s tests  102/102
python tests/verify_repo.py           pass

title: fix(plugin): prefix agents paths with ./ so plugin install works on current Claude Code
body:
## Problem

`claude plugin install caveman@caveman` fails on current Claude Code (2.1.x):

```
✘ Failed to install plugin "caveman@caveman": Plugin temp_local_... has an
  invalid manifest file at .../.claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Validation errors: agents: Invalid input
```

This blocks the plugin install path for every user on current CC. The standalone
hook install (`--with-hooks`) still succeeds, which is why the failure is easy to
miss — hooks work, but the skills and cavecrew agents never load.

## Cause

The CC manifest validator requires plugin-relative paths to start with `./`.
`plugin.json` lists the cavecrew agents as bare relative paths.

The same rule already governs the `skills` field — the repo's own `CLAUDE.md`
documents it under the ClawHub publishing constraints ("all paths must be
relative to the plugin root and start with `./`"; CC returns
`Validation errors: skills: Invalid input` otherwise). `agents` is subject to the
same validator and was missed.

## Fix

Prefix the three `agents` entries with `./`.

## Verification

Tested against a real marketplace copy under
`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/caveman/`, reinstalling between each variant:

| `agents` value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `["agents/cavecrew-builder.md", ...]` (current) | ✘ `agents: Invalid input` |
| `"./agents"` (string dir) | ✘ `agents: Invalid input` |
| `["./agents/cavecrew-builder.md", ...]` (this PR) | ✔ installs cleanly |

After the fix, `claude plugin install caveman@caveman` succeeds and the plugin
loads its skills plus all three cavecrew agents (builder, investigator, reviewer).

Environment: Windows 11, Claude Code 2.1.x, Node v24.19.0.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

wrap: subscription/OAuth requests never become compression-eligible; "MCP recovery missing" persists after a successful `caveman mcp install`
body:
**What happen**
<!-- What caveman do wrong -->

On a Claude Code **subscription (OAuth)** login, `caveman-proxy` meters traffic but never compresses it. `requests` advances, but `requests_eligible_for_compression` does not advance for subscription requests and `compression_tokens_saved` stays `0` in every configuration I could construct.

`caveman mcp install claude --server caveman` reports success and writes its marker, yet `status` and `doctor` continue to report MCP recovery as missing:

- install output: `✓ Claude Code: caveman_retrieve installed` / `→ caveman wrap will now compress streaming requests too (recovered via MCP)`
- marker written: `~/.caveman/mcp/claude.json` → `{"tool":"caveman_retrieve","command":"~/.caveman/bin/caveman-mcp","args":[]}`
- `caveman status` still prints: `MCP recovery missing — streaming turns and Claude Pro/Max sessions pass through uncompressed`
- `caveman doctor claude` → `components.mcp_recovery: false`
- the MCP binary itself answers an `initialize` handshake correctly: `{"result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"caveman","version":"dev"}}}`

Restarting the proxy after `mcp install` (so it re-reads the marker) does not change it.

**Second, related finding:** `caveman claude` (wrap) prints `→ started Caveman proxy on 127.0.0.1:8787 (compress)` but the child does not route through it — `requests` does not advance at all. Explicit `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` *does* route (requests advances), so the proxy is reachable and it is wrap's env injection that has no effect. Adding `_CLAUDE_CODE_ASSUME_FIRST_PARTY_BASE_URL=1` to the wrap invocation did not change this.

Matrix tested, each with an identical ~43,000-token stdin payload:

| proxy mode | routing | first-party flag | Δrequests | Δeligible | saved |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `record` (`caveman start`) | explicit | yes | +3 | +3 | 0 |
| `compress` (wrap-owned) | wrap | no | +0 | +0 | 0 |
| `compress` (wrap-owned) | wrap | yes | +0 | +0 | 0 |
| `compress` (`CAVEMAN_MODE=compress caveman start`) | explicit | yes | +3 | **+0** | 0 |

Final `auth_mode_accounting`: `{"subscription": 9, "unknown": 2}`.

Note the last row: with a compress-mode proxy and traffic demonstrably routed through it, subscription requests are not even counted as *eligible*.

The engine itself is healthy — `caveman compress` on the same payload gives `tokens_before: 43199 → tokens_after: 284` (`ratio: 0.993`) with a working `recovery_handle`. Only the in-flight path never engages.

**Expected**
<!-- What caveman should do -->

Either subscription/OAuth requests should compress once `caveman mcp install` has succeeded — which is what `caveman wrap --help` advertises:

> Subscription logins compress locally too, no account needed (live zone only …; needs MCP recovery; Claude/Codex wrap provide it ephemerally when caveman-mcp is available)

— or `status`/`doctor` should say what the MCP-recovery check requires *beyond* the marker that `mcp install` writes, so it is actionable.

**Before/after example**

```
Input:  caveman mcp install claude --server caveman
        CAVEMAN_MODE=compress caveman start --port 8787 &
        { echo "Reply with one word: OK"; cat big.log; } | \
          ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 \
          _CLAUDE_CODE_ASSUME_FIRST_PARTY_BASE_URL=1 \
          claude -p --max-turns 1
        caveman stats

Got:    requests 8 -> 11, requests_eligible_for_compression 7 -> 7,
        compression_tokens_saved 0
        status: "MCP recovery missing"

Want:   subscription requests counted eligible and compressed, or a status
        message that names the remaining precondition
```

(`big.log` is ~116 KB / ~43k tokens of uniform log lines.)

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

npm global, macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

```
@caveman-ai/cli   1.2.5   (latest at time of filing)
pack_version      2.2.0
Claude Code       2.1.241
doctor claude     tested_version 2.1.226, version_status "newer_unknown", tested: false
auth mode         subscription (OAuth)
```

title: Claude Code: PostCompact hook emits invalid hookSpecificOutput — "Hook JSON output validation failed" on every compaction
body:
**What happen**

On Claude Code, every compaction logs a hook failure:

```
PostCompact ['/Users/yg/.caveman/bin/caveman-proxy' native-hook claude --adapter '.../native-hook-fast.js'] failed:
Hook JSON output validation failed — (root): Invalid input
```

The adapter answers `PostCompact` with a `hookSpecificOutput` envelope:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostCompact","additionalContext":"Build simplest complete system. …"}}
```

Claude Code's hook schema doesn't accept `hookSpecificOutput` for `PostCompact`. Its error enumerates the events that do: `PreToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolBatch`, `Stop`/`SubagentStop`. So the Core text is discarded and an error is surfaced to the user instead.

**Expected**

`PostCompact` returns a shape Claude Code accepts (or returns nothing), so compaction completes without an error.

Worth noting the payload looks redundant: caveman's `SessionStart` entry is registered without a matcher, so it also fires on `source: "compact"` — and emits the *same* 1781-character `additionalContext` under a valid `hookEventName: "SessionStart"`. Core already survives compaction through that path. Dropping `PostCompact` from the Claude lifecycle list may be the whole fix.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: /compact  (Claude Code)
Got:   PreCompact  … completed successfully
       PostCompact … failed: Hook JSON output validation failed — (root): Invalid input
Want:  both hooks complete; Core delivered once via SessionStart(source=compact)
```

Reproduces outside a real compaction:

```bash
echo '{"hook_event_name":"PostCompact","session_id":"x","cwd":"'"$PWD"'","transcript_path":"/dev/null"}' \
  | ~/.caveman/bin/caveman-proxy native-hook claude \
      --adapter /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@caveman-ai/cli/dist/native-hook-fast.js
# -> {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostCompact","additionalContext":"…"}}
```

Same command with `SessionStart` + `"source":"compact"` returns a valid `hookEventName: "SessionStart"` and identical `additionalContext`.

**Where it comes from**

`dist/index.js` hardcodes `PostCompact` into the lifecycle list for non-gemini/non-codex agents, i.e. Claude:

```js
: ["SessionStart", "UserPromptSubmit", "PreToolUse", "PostToolUse", "PostToolUseFailure",
   "PreCompact", "PostCompact", "SubagentStart", "SubagentStop", "Stop", "SessionEnd"];
```

**Knock-on effect: the workaround fights `doctor --fix`**

Removing the `PostCompact` block from `~/.claude/settings.json` fixes the error, but then `caveman doctor claude` reports `state: degraded`, `drifted: true`, and flips every component to `false` (`routing`, `lifecycle_hooks`, `core`, `mcp_recovery`, `tool_rewrite`) with `coding_policy: off`. Running the suggested `caveman doctor claude --fix` re-adds `PostCompact` and the error returns — verified that this is the *only* thing `--fix` changes in the config.

So users get a choice between a clean compaction and a healthy-looking `doctor`. It'd be good if the drift check tolerated a host that has pruned an event its runtime rejects.

(Also, `state: degraded` reads alarming but seems purely a config-match label — `caveman status` output is byte-identical in both states, including `MCP recovery missing — streaming turns and Claude Pro/Max sessions pass through uncompressed`.)

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

- `@caveman-ai/cli` **1.2.3**, global npm install (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@caveman-ai/cli`)
- Also reproduced on **1.2.5** — I ran that release's `dist/native-hook-fast.js` against the payload above and got the same `hookEventName: "PostCompact"` envelope, so upgrading doesn't help.
- Claude Code **2.1.239** (caveman reports `tested_version: 2.1.226`, `version_status: newer_unknown`)
- macOS, Node v26.7.0, `pack_version` 2.2.0

agents/docs/*.md register as subagents caveman:docs:CLAUDE and caveman:docs:AGENTS — agent discovery recurses into subdirectories (sibling of #855)
body:
**What happen**

The two maintainer docs moved out of `agents/` by 0385ad9 landed in `agents/docs/`, which is still inside the auto-discovered tree. On Claude Code 2.1.245 they register as subagents named after their subdirectory:

```
caveman:docs:AGENTS   (Tools: All tools)
caveman:docs:CLAUDE   (Tools: All tools)
```

Both are frontmatter-less maintainer docs — `agents/docs/CLAUDE.md` (7.5 KB, opens with `# agents — the agent-profile registry (caveman wrap data)`) and `agents/docs/AGENTS.md` (626 B). Neither is an agent.

This is the same symptom #855 reported for `agents/CLAUDE.md` and `agents/AGENTS.md`, reappearing one directory level down. It also carries the same severity note FCAR2025 raised there: with no frontmatter there is no `tools:` key, so both register with an unrestricted grant, while the three intentional cavecrew agents are deliberately narrow.

**Why #855 measured this as fixed**

`claude plugin details` and the runtime agent loader disagree. `plugin details` does not see agents in subdirectories; the runtime does.

```
$ claude plugin details caveman@caveman
  Agents (3)  cavecrew-builder, cavecrew-investigator, cavecrew-reviewer
```

But asking a clean non-interactive session to enumerate its own registry returns five:

```
$ claude -p "List EXACTLY the names of every subagent (subagent_type) available to your Agent tool, one per line, no commentary."
caveman:cavecrew-builder
caveman:cavecrew-investigator
caveman:cavecrew-reviewer
caveman:docs:AGENTS
caveman:docs:CLAUDE
claude
Explore
general-purpose
Plan
statusline-setup
```

The `docs:` prefix is the subdirectory name, so discovery is walking the tree and namespacing by relative path. In #855, glen-84 verified the relocation by dropping a frontmatter-less `agents/docs/CLAUDE.md` into the old install tree and reading the count back from `plugin details`, which stayed at 3 and suggested discovery did not recurse. Measured against the runtime instead, it does. Worth noting the check was on Claude Code 2.1.234 and this report is on 2.1.245, so a change in the harness between those two versions is also possible — either way, `plugin details` is not a reliable oracle for what actually registers.

**Expected**

Only the three cavecrew agents register, in `plugin details` and in the runtime alike.

**Fix**

Move the two docs somewhere outside `agents/` entirely — `docs/technical/` would match where the rest of the maintainer documentation already lives. An explicit `agents` array in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` would also work in principle, but that route has its own history in this repo (#871, #872, #882), so relocating the files looks like the lower-risk option.

Removing the two files locally is safe as a stopgap, per FCAR2025's note in #855: nothing reads them at runtime, since `agents/compile.mjs` writes `agents/agents.json` and that JSON is what `caveman wrap` consumes. The plugin cache is overwritten on update, so it does not survive `claude plugin update`.

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

- caveman `81536f57b3303b7de7f5bc5b564cc344f9112d68` (marketplace HEAD, 2026-08-25), installed with `claude plugin update caveman@caveman` from the `JuliusBrussee/caveman` marketplace
- Previously installed: `655b7d9c5431`, which registered the three cavecrew agents only
- Claude Code 2.1.245, CLI in terminal, Arch Linux, Node.js v26.7.0

_Drafted by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)._

title: [Docs/Bug]: caveman codex is persistent despite wrap docs; reinstall can lack rollback journal
body:
## Corrected summary

After inspecting current `main`, the original report conflated two different CLI entrypoints:

```text
caveman codex       # persistent native enable, then launch Codex
caveman wrap codex  # session-only ephemeral CODEX_HOME
```

The explicit `caveman wrap codex` path was retested and **did** leave the real `~/.codex/config.toml`, `hooks.json`, and `AGENTS.md` byte-identical. Therefore the original claim that the explicit wrap itself mutates the real `CODEX_HOME` was incorrect.

Two actionable issues remain:

1. the README's `Wrap any agent` section presents `caveman <agent>` as wrapping and states that Wrap never edits user config, while current CLI source intentionally makes the shorthand a persistent native enable for supported agents;
2. in the reproduced remove → shorthand-enable sequence, persistent writes were present but no native ownership journal was available, so the documented remove command could not restore them.

## Environment

- macOS
- Codex CLI `0.147.0`
- `@caveman-ai/cli` `1.2.5`
- ChatGPT/Codex OAuth
- Caveman telemetry off
- `think.core=false`

## Current source behavior

`packages/cli/src/index.ts::agentShortcut` documents and implements the shorthand as persistent:

```text
caveman <agent>
→ enableNative(...)
→ journaled user-scoped writes
→ launch the host binary directly
```

An explicit leading wrap flag or the `wrap` verb selects the ephemeral path instead.

This behavior is also present in the installed npm `1.2.5` package; it is not only an unreleased `main` change.

## Documentation/UX mismatch

The current README says:

```text
caveman <agent> wraps eight agents natively
Codex: ephemeral CODEX_HOME (ChatGPT login)
Wrap never edits your own config files
```

A user following that section can reasonably expect:

```text
caveman codex ...
```

to be session-only. The CLI instead performs persistent native setup before launching Codex.

The persistent shortcut should either:

- be documented prominently as persistent, with `caveman wrap codex` shown as the session-only form; or
- require an explicit `enable` command and keep the shorthand ephemeral.

At minimum, the first persistent write should show the exact affected files and rollback command before applying changes.

## Journal/rollback reproduction

The machine had previously run a native setup/remove cycle. Before the shorthand test:

```text
caveman doctor codex
state: available
installed: false
routing: false
lifecycle_hooks: false
mcp_recovery: false
tool_rewrite: false
files: []
```

The real Codex config matched pre-Caveman backups byte-for-byte and no process listened on port 8787.

Running:

```text
caveman codex exec ...
```

added persistent blocks to the real `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
# >>> caveman:native-root
model_provider = "caveman"
# <<< caveman:native-root

# >>> caveman:native-tables
[model_providers.caveman]
name = "Caveman"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true

[mcp_servers.caveman]
command = "~/.caveman/bin/caveman-mcp"
# <<< caveman:native-tables
```

and added the native Caveman lifecycle/tool hooks to the real `~/.codex/hooks.json`.

Attempting the documented removal returned:

```text
caveman setup --agent-native codex --remove
⚠ codex: no agent-native bundle journal found
```

The command did not remove the persistent blocks. Manual restoration from the pre-test backup was required.

This is the remaining config-safety bug: current source describes the shortcut writes as journaled, but this state transition produced owned-looking writes without a removable ownership journal.

## Explicit-wrap control test

After restoring both files byte-for-byte and clearing port 8787, I ran:

```text
caveman wrap codex exec ...
```

The session used an ephemeral path such as:

```text
/private/.../T/caveman-wrap-*/config.toml
```

and completed through `provider: caveman`. After exit, the real files retained their exact pre-test hashes.

This confirms the explicit wrap's config-isolation contract works in this environment; the ambiguity is the shorthand semantics plus the missing journal after persistent enable.

## Expected behavior

1. README and CLI help distinguish persistent shorthand from explicit ephemeral wrap.
2. Persistent enable creates the ownership journal before the first config write.
3. Any write failure rolls back prior bytes.
4. Remove works after fresh install, reinstall, remove → reinstall, and existing unrelated hook/config content.
5. If a journal is missing, `doctor --fix` either reconstructs ownership safely from exact Caveman markers or reports a precise manual recovery procedure without guessing at unrelated config.

## Suggested minimal tests

- README/help snapshot: `caveman codex` is labeled persistent; `caveman wrap codex` is labeled ephemeral.
- State transition: setup → remove → shorthand enable → remove restores seeded `config.toml` and `hooks.json` byte-for-byte.
- Explicit wrap: mocked Codex run leaves the real home byte-identical on success and failure.

## Related

- #908 tracks OAuth/subscription compression eligibility. A follow-up Codex analysis there now identifies `custom_tool_call_output` parser incompatibility as the direct Codex no-compression cause; it is separate from the command-semantics/journal problem here.

title: feat: add dnd mode — silent while working, report once done

Adds `dnd` ("do not disturb") as a seventh intensity level: the agent emits no prose while working — no preamble, no plan, no progress notes, no narration between tool calls. Thinking is unrestricted. It speaks only to deliver a final report when the job is done, to ask a question when the request is ambiguous, or to request confirmation when an action needs approval. The existing auto-clarity rule still overrides, so security warnings and irreversible-action confirmations are always spoken.

Implemented as a flat level rather than a modifier on lite/full/ultra: the flag file, statusline whitelist, stats attribution, and mode parser all key off a single mode string, so no format change is needed. The behavior lives in one intensity-table row in skills/caveman/SKILL.md, which the activate hook already filters to the active level — other levels pay no extra tokens.
