title: pi extension re-points local/custom OpenAI-compatible providers named "openai" at api.openai.com
body:
**What happen**

The pi extension routes providers by name. The names `anthropic`, `openai`, and `google` pass the allowlist in `routeForApi` (`packages/pi-extension/src/protocol.ts`). The allowlist does not examine the original base URL of the provider. A user can register a local proxy (litellm, ollama, llama.cpp) or a custom remote endpoint (Azure) under the provider name `openai`. Then the extension replaces the base URL of that provider with the gateway route. The gateway sends the request to `api.openai.com`. The local proxy gets no request, and the request fails with a 401 error or gets to the wrong service.

**Expected**

The extension must replace the base URL of a provider only when the host of the original base URL is the upstream host of the proxy route. These hosts are `api.openai.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, and `opencode.ai` for the compat mount. One host comparison covers loopback proxies, Azure under the name `openai`, and other custom endpoints. For a mismatch, the extension must keep direct mode and show the pass-through warning with the endpoint in the reason. The same rule protects the `opencode-go` route. If the pi catalog moves the endpoint to another host, the request passes through and does not get to the stale built-in URL in the proxy.

Two facts constrain the fix. After `pi.registerProvider(name, { baseUrl })`, each `ctx.modelRegistry` surface (`find`, `getAll`, `getProvider`, `getRegisteredProviderConfig`) returns the gateway route. Thus the extension must read the original from `model.baseUrl` before the first override and cache it per provider. The integration fixture `tests/fixtures/stub-provider-extension.mjs` registers the provider `openai` with the base URL `http://127.0.0.1:1`. This is the shape of this bug, and the routed test asserts that it routes. The fixture needs a rework: the routed arm uses the default host, and the closed-gate arms keep a dead loopback port.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: pi with the provider "openai" and the baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1 (litellm), wrapped with caveman pi
Got:   the request goes to api.openai.com, and the litellm key causes a 401 error
Want:  pass-through to http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1 with the "no compression" warning
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Pi

**Version / install method**

Current `main` after PR #948 (v2.5.0, CLI 1.3.2). This behavior existed before #946. The provider allowlist from #948 documents this behavior but does not fix it. The fix from the #946 plan (a gate on the original base URL of the provider) was not implemented. #952 is the neighboring case: a provider with a custom name passes through after #948.

title: test: no end-to-end coverage for the pi extension to proxy compat-mount seam
body:
**What you want**

An integration test that drives an opencode-go model through the full path: the pi extension route, the gateway prefix strip, the named compat adapter, and a stub upstream.

The unit tests cover the two halves separately. `protocol.runtime.mjs` asserts the route string `/w/pi/compat/opencode-go/v1`. The Go test asserts that `/compat/opencode-go/v1/responses` resolves to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`. The contract between the halves (the `/w/pi` prefix strip and the mount name) is a convention only. A rename on one side passes both suites and breaks production.

`packages/pi-extension/tests/integration.runtime.mjs` has the harness for this test. Its stub gateway answers each path except `GET /health/live` with an OpenAI chat-completions body. Thus an `openai-completions` arm needs no new response shape. The stub provider fixture registers only the provider `openai`. The test needs a new fixture arm that registers an `opencode-go` provider with the base URL `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, `api: "openai-completions"`, and an `apiKey`. The test asserts that the first request lands on the stub at `/w/pi/compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions`. PR #969 adds a Go end-to-end test in `proxy/internal/standalone` for the `anthropic-messages` arm (`/w/pi/compat/opencode-go/v1/messages`), because the stub would need an Anthropic SSE shape for it.

**Before/after example**

```
Before: the reported path of #946 has no automated end-to-end test
After:  an integration test fails when one side of the compat-mount contract drifts
```

title: fix(pi): route only default provider endpoints
body:
## Summary

- The extension routes a provider only when the host of its original base URL is the upstream host of the proxy route (fixes #970). The hosts are `api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, and `opencode.ai`. A provider with the name `openai` that points at a local relay (litellm, ollama) or at Azure now stays direct, with one notice that names the endpoint.
- The router caches the original base URL before the first override. After an override, every `ctx.modelRegistry` surface reports the gateway route, so the registry cannot give the original.
- A new integration test drives an `opencode-go` model through the stub gateway and asserts the path `/w/pi/compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions` (fixes #971). This is the seam of #946.
- The stub provider fixture declares three providers: `openai` on the real host, `opencode-go` on the real host, and `anthropic` on a dead loopback port. The closed-gate tests use the loopback provider, so direct traffic still fast-fails on the machine.

## Proof

- `npm test` in `packages/pi-extension`: 28 tests pass, 0 skipped. The pinned pi 0.84.2 CLI drives the six integration cases.
- Regression proof: with the tests and the fixture from this branch and the source from `main`, exactly two tests fail: `route gate compares the original provider host with the proxy upstream host` and `open gate: a provider with a custom endpoint stays direct with a notice`.
- `node scripts/bundle-pi-extension.mjs` in `packages/cli` bundles the new source. `node --test tests/pi-wrap.runtime.mjs tests/pi-enable.runtime.mjs`: 6 tests pass.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` passes.
- Not run: a live `caveman pi` session against a real proxy. The installed CLI 1.3.1 ships a proxy from before #948. The stub-gateway integration test and the Go end-to-end test in #969 cover the same seam.

## Known limits

- A user who points both the pi `openai` provider and the proxy `providers.openai.base_url` at the same custom relay gets pass-through with a notice instead of routed compression. Before this change, such a setup routed through the proxy.
- Pi supports a separate `baseUrl` for each model in one provider. The router still stores one original URL for each provider.
- After Caveman routes one default model, a same-provider switch can route a custom-endpoint model to the wrong service. This bug exists on `main`.
- PR #972 fixes the provider-level case only. Issue #973 tracks the model-level follow-up.
- The routed integration tests are not hermetic. If routing regresses, a dummy key reaches `api.openai.com` or `opencode.ai`.
- The provider returns a 401 error, or the request fails because DNS is unavailable. The fixture comment states this risk.
- The `anthropic-messages` arm of the seam is covered by the protocol unit test here and by the Go end-to-end test in #969. The stub gateway does not answer Anthropic SSE.

title: pi extension reuses one original base URL across models in the same provider
body:
**What happen**

Pi supports a separate `baseUrl` for each model in one provider.

`ProviderRouter` stores one original base URL for each provider. This sequence can route a custom model to the wrong endpoint:

1. The user selects an `openai` model that uses `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
2. Caveman stores that URL and applies a provider-wide gateway override.
3. Pi reports the gateway URL for all `openai` models.
4. The user selects another `openai` model with a custom model-level `baseUrl`.
5. Caveman reuses the first model URL and routes the custom model to the OpenAI proxy route.

The second model can target a local relay, Azure, or another custom endpoint. Its request can reach the wrong service.

This behavior exists on `main`. PR #972 fixes provider-level custom endpoints, but it does not fix this model-level case.

**Expected**

Caveman must preserve the original URL for each model before it applies a provider-wide override. The registry cannot supply these URLs after the override.

If a model has a custom endpoint, Caveman must keep that model direct and show the pass-through notice.

The regression test must register two models under the same provider. One model uses the default endpoint, and one uses a custom endpoint.

The test must route the default model first. Then it must select the custom model and make sure that the model stays direct.

The test must select the default model again and make sure that routing resumes.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: pi provider "openai" has one default model and one model with a custom baseUrl
Got:   after the default model routes, the custom model also routes to api.openai.com
Want:  the custom model stays direct, and the default model routes through Caveman
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Pi

**Version / install method**

Current `main` with `@caveman-ai/pi`, pinned to Pi 0.84.2. This behavior exists before PR #972.

PR #972 fixes provider-level custom endpoints. It does not fix model-level custom endpoints in the same provider.

title: Mid-session level switch updates the banner but never injects the new level's rules
body:
**What happen**
<!-- What caveman do wrong -->

Switching intensity mid-session updates the mode state and the per-turn banner, but never delivers the new level's rules to the model. The banner claims a level the model has no instructions for.

The two hooks are asymmetric:

- `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart) reads `SKILL.md`, filters the intensity table down to the active level's row, and injects the whole ruleset. It runs **once**.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` (UserPromptSubmit) parses `/caveman <level>`, calls `recordModeChange` + `writeSessionMode`, then emits only:

  ```js
  `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (${activeMode}) — session ruleset applies.`
  ```

"session ruleset" refers to whatever SessionStart injected. If the session started at `full` and the user then runs `/caveman ultra`, the model's context still holds the **full** row — including the literal line `Default: **full**` — while every subsequent turn asserts `(ultra)`. The ultra row's actual directives (`Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous`, `One word when one word enough`, `State each fact once`) are never sent.

The comment at `caveman-mode-tracker.js:273` states the intent, and is accurate about what the code does:

> The SessionStart hook injects the full ruleset once, but models lose it when other plugins inject competing style instructions every turn. This keeps caveman visible in the model's attention on every user message.

It is a visibility reminder. It was not written to carry a level change, and it does not. The consequence is that `/caveman ultra`, `/caveman lite`, and `/caveman wenyan-full` are all no-ops on behavior within a session — only the label moves.

This is easy to miss because the failure is silent and self-confirming: the banner says `ultra`, so both the user and the model believe ultra is active, and the model keeps producing `full`-level output. The user in our case correctly identified that something was wrong only from the output being far too verbose for `ultra`, and initially suspected another plugin was intercepting the hook. It is not — both hook chains fire normally.

Worth noting the `/caveman` slash command cannot compensate. `commands/caveman.toml` is a prompt, not a state write:

```
prompt = "Switch to caveman {{args}} mode. If no level specified, use full. Respond terse like smart caveman — drop articles, filler, pleasantries. Fragments OK. Technical terms exact. Code unchanged. Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]. [next step]."
```

That text paraphrases the `full` level regardless of the argument. So on `/caveman ultra` the model receives (a) a prompt describing `full`, (b) a banner saying `ultra`, and (c) a ruleset in context describing `full`. Two of the three actively point at the wrong level.

**Expected**
<!-- What caveman should do -->

When `caveman-mode-tracker.js` detects an actual level *change* (previous mode ≠ new mode, both non-null and neither an independent mode), it should re-inject the filtered ruleset for the new level, not just the banner. The unchanged-mode case should keep emitting the cheap one-line reminder as it does today, so the per-turn cost is unchanged.

The mechanism already exists — `caveman-activate.js` reads `SKILL.md` and filters the intensity table to the active row. Extracting that into a shared sibling that both hooks call looks like the smallest correct fix. `caveman-config.js` is documented as the home for state primitives shared across the loaders, so a `caveman-ruleset.js` alongside it would match the existing layout.

A cheaper variant, if re-injecting the whole ruleset per switch is unwanted: emit just the new level's intensity-table row plus the one-line banner. That is a few hundred bytes and would fix the behavioral gap, though it leaves the stale `Default: **full**` line and the stale row from SessionStart in context alongside it, which is why full re-injection seems safer.

Either way the fix should be gated on a change, so that a session that never switches pays nothing extra.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: /caveman ultra
       (session had started at level `full`)

Got:   CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra) — session ruleset applies.
       ...and nothing else. Context still holds the SessionStart injection:
         "Default: **full**."
         "| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. ... |"
       The `ultra` row was never sent. Model continues producing full-level
       output while every turn's banner asserts ultra.

Want:  CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: ultra

       <ruleset re-injected, intensity table filtered to:>
       | **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous.
       One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose
       abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) measured zero
       token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function
       names, API names, error strings: never touch |
```

Reproduction, no repo needed:

1. Start a session with no `defaultMode` configured anywhere, so it resolves to `full`.
2. Run `/caveman ultra`.
3. Observe the banner on the next turn reads `(ultra)` while output length and style stay at `full`.

Confirmed the two halves independently:

```console
$ cat ~/.claude/.caveman-sessions/<session-id>.mode
ultra                                  # state write is correct

$ echo '{"session_id":"probe","cwd":"/some/repo"}' \
    | node .../src/hooks/caveman-activate.js | head -1
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: ultra      # activate.js emits the right thing
```

So `writeSessionMode` works and `caveman-activate.js` works. Only the path between them is missing: nothing re-runs the injection when the level changes.

Setting `defaultMode` in the user config is a workaround, but it only takes effect at the *next* SessionStart, so the in-session switch remains broken:

```jsonc
// %APPDATA%\caveman\config.json   (Windows)
{ "defaultMode": "ultra" }
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

The same asymmetry appears reachable from the opencode loader, since `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` evaluates the same hook sources, but this was only observed and verified on Claude Code.

**Version / install method**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| caveman plugin | 2.5.0 (`/plugin`, marketplace `JuliusBrussee/caveman`) |
| `@caveman-ai/cli` | 1.3.1 (npm, global) |
| native pack | 2.2.0 (`caveman-proxy.exe native-hook claude`) |
| Claude Code | 2.1.259 |
| OS | Windows 10 Pro 19045 |

Both integrations were installed and active: the plugin's own `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit` hooks from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, plus the native pack's hooks written into `~/.claude/settings.json`. The native-pack hooks are not implicated — the gap is entirely within the plugin's two hook scripts.

title: fix(install): gemini extension install must not wait for input (#400)
body:
## Summary

A `curl | bash` install hangs at the Gemini CLI step. This change makes `gemini extensions install` finish without input on Gemini CLI v0.41.0 and later. It does not add any directory to the permanent trust file. On an older Gemini CLI it runs the same command as `main`.

Fixes #400
Fixes #676
Refs #460
Refs #993

## Problem

The shell pipe uses stdin for the installer script. The Gemini CLI child process inherits that stdin. Gemini CLI asks a workspace-trust question and an extension-consent question on stdin. It reads no answer, and the install waits without an end. The user sees the prompts but cannot answer them.

## Root cause

Gemini CLI reads both answers with `readline` on stdin. Commit ed1fbb7 added `--consent` for #676 on 2026-07-21. Commit 82864c8 moved the installer back to `bin/` on 2026-08-11 and dropped the flag. The current `main` passes no flag.

## Change

Two commits.

### Commit 1: session-only trust, consent flag, scratch directory

`installGemini` in `bin/install.js` runs:

```text
GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true gemini extensions install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman --consent
```

The two parts have separate purposes:

- `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` trusts the current directory for this process only. It is the variable that `--skip-trust` sets. Gemini CLI documents it for headless use. The trust prompt then does not run, and `trustedFolders.json` stays unchanged.
- `--consent` answers the extension-install warning.

The installer does not use `--skip-trust`. The root chat command owns that flag. After the subcommand, Gemini CLI rejects it as an unknown argument. Before the subcommand, Gemini CLI reads the other words as a chat prompt.

The installer does not use `--consent` alone. The trust prompt uses the same consent callback. Its yes-branch writes the current directory into `trustedFolders.json` permanently.

The installer runs the command in a new empty directory below `~/.caveman/tmp`. A trusted directory lets Gemini CLI load `.gemini/` config and `.env` files from the directory and from every parent. Below the user home, every parent belongs to the user or to root, so the trust covers nothing. A directory below `/tmp` is not safe, because any local user can plant `/tmp/.env`. A directory below `~/.gemini/tmp` is not safe, because Gemini CLI keeps project state there. The directory comes from `mkdtemp`, and the installer removes only that directory. If the installer cannot create it, it reports a failure and does not start Gemini CLI.

### Commit 2: capability probe for older CLIs

The review found that commit 1 passed both parts always. That fails or grants trust on an older Gemini CLI. Upstream source shows this:

| Tags | Untrusted directory on `extensions install` | `--consent` | `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE` |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.10.0 to v0.12.0 | Hard reject | From v0.11.0 | Ignored |
| v0.13.0 to v0.28.0 | Trust prompt. `--consent` answers yes and writes the directory to `trustedFolders.json`. | Yes | Ignored |
| v0.29.0 to v0.40.0 | Same prompt on a TTY. Headless mode auto-trusts, upstream PR #18407. | Yes | Ignored |
| v0.41.0 and later | Prompt on a TTY. Headless mode needs `--skip-trust` or the variable, upstream PR #25814. | Yes | Honored |

`--skip-trust` and the variable come from the same upstream commit, dba9b9a0ff. So the installer now runs `gemini --help` one time and looks for `--skip-trust`:

- Flag present: the installer keeps the variable, the scratch directory, and `--consent`. No prompt, no wait, no write to `trustedFolders.json`.
- Flag absent, or probe failed: the installer runs the same command as `main`, from the caller directory, with no variable and no `--consent`. It prints one note line that names the case. Existing trust stays in effect. The installer grants no new trust. The CLI can prompt or wait, as on `main`.

`--consent` (v0.11.0) is older than `--skip-trust` (v0.41.0). So a CLI with `--skip-trust` also has `--consent`. The code comment states this assumption about the upstream release order.

The dry run prints the command for the installed CLI, and on the modern path the variable.

## Compatibility

The no-prompt guarantee holds only when the probe succeeds and finds `--skip-trust`. On every other version the installer sends the `main` command and leaves the CLI's own prompts in place. On no version does the installer make a directory trusted.

## Tests

`tests/installer/gemini-install.test.mjs`. A fake `gemini` on `PATH` answers `extensions list` and a bare `--help`, and records the trust variable, its cwd, and each argument for the install call. Twelve cases:

1. Piped stdin with `--non-interactive`: the variable is `true`, and `--consent` follows the URL.
2. Piped stdin without `--non-interactive`: the same result, so no TTY branch is necessary.
3. Dry run: the output shows the variable and the command, and Gemini CLI does not start.
4. A CLI with `--skip-trust` exits 1: the installer reports `gemini extensions install failed`.
5. Default path without `--force`: the `extensions list` preflight runs, then the same command.
6. The scratch directory cannot be made: the installer reports a failure, does not start Gemini CLI, and exits 1.
7. Existing files below `~/.caveman/tmp` keep their content, and no scratch directory remains.
8. A CLI without `--skip-trust`: the plain command runs in the caller directory, with no variable, no `--consent`, and no scratch directory.
9. Dry run on that CLI: the output shows the plain command and no variable.
10. The help probe exits 1 with `--skip-trust` in its text: the plain command runs, and the note says `could not read`.
11. The help text comes on stderr with exit 0: the modern command runs.
12. The user sets `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` before the install, on a CLI without `--skip-trust`: the legacy path keeps the inherited variable and still passes no `--consent`.

The test helper removes `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE` from the child environment before it starts the installer. Without that removal, an inherited value looks like an installer-added value.

Results:

```text
node --test --test-force-exit tests/installer/gemini-install.test.mjs   12 pass, 0 fail
npm test                                                                 257 pass, 0 fail
python3 tests/verify_repo.py                                             all checks pass
```

## Manual test

Environment: Gemini CLI 0.58.0, Linux, a throwaway `HOME`, stdin from `/dev/null`.

| Case | Result | `trustedFolders.json` |
|---|---|---|
| Current command, no flags | Prompt shown, hung until a 60 s timeout | Not written |
| Installer with the probe (commit 2) | `--consent` command shown, exit 0, no prompt, extension listed, no scratch directory left | Not written |
| Bare `--consent`, no variable | Exit 0, no prompt, extension listed | Current directory written as `TRUST_FOLDER` |

The third row is why the modern path does not use `--consent` alone, and why the legacy path does not use `--consent` at all.

No Gemini CLI before v0.41.0 was available. The legacy path is proven by the fake only.

To repeat the second row:

```sh
TEST_HOME="$(mktemp -d)/home"; mkdir -p "$TEST_HOME"; cd "$TEST_HOME"
HOME="$TEST_HOME" USERPROFILE="$TEST_HOME" \
  bash /path/to/caveman/install.sh --only gemini --minimal --non-interactive --no-mcp-shrink \
  --config-dir "$TEST_HOME/.claude" </dev/null
HOME="$TEST_HOME" gemini extensions list          # expect: caveman
cat "$TEST_HOME/.gemini/trustedFolders.json"      # expect: no such file
```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(hooks): carry the new level's ruleset on a mid-session switch
body:
Fixes #975.

## What was wrong

`/caveman ultra` mid-session moved the label and nothing else.

`caveman-activate.js` (SessionStart) reads `SKILL.md`, filters the intensity table to the active level's row, injects it — **once**. `caveman-mode-tracker.js` (UserPromptSubmit) wrote the new mode and emitted only its per-turn reminder. So the model kept whatever level SessionStart had given it — that level's intensity row and its literal `Default: **full**` line still sitting in context — while every following banner asserted the new level.

Reproduced on `main` before the fix:

```console
$ echo '{"session_id":"probe","source":"startup",...}' | node src/hooks/caveman-activate.js
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full
... Default: **full**.
... | **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. ... |

$ echo '{"session_id":"probe","prompt":"<command-name>/caveman</command-name><command-args>ultra</command-args>"}' \
    | node src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js
{"hookSpecificOutput":{...,"additionalContext":"CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra). Enforce this reply: ..."}}
```

State write correct, banner correct, the `ultra` row never sent. #951's per-level reminder narrowed this but does not close it: it is a hand-maintained paraphrase, and it carries none of ultra's actual directives (`NO prose abbreviations`, `NO arrows`, `State each fact once`).

The failure is silent and self-confirming — the banner agrees with the user, so both sides believe the switch took, and only the output disagrees.

## The fix

**Shared loader.** `caveman-activate.js` already had the mechanism. Moved to `caveman-config.js` as `loadFilteredRuleset` / `canonicalModeLabel` / `rulesetBanner`, used by both loaders, so the two can no longer disagree about what a level means.

`caveman-config.js` rather than the `caveman-ruleset.js` sibling the issue suggests: the hook file set is pinned in `checksums.sha256`, `verify_repo.py` and the install lists, and `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` can only evaluate files it knows by name — a second shared sibling is standing drift risk, which is what the *"Keep mode-state logic in `caveman-config.js`"* rule in `CLAUDE.md` is about. SessionStart output is byte-identical after the move (diffed).

**Re-injection, gated on an actual change.** The tracker compares the new level against the mode read *before* the write:

- Compared through `canonicalModeLabel` — both spellings of wenyan-full reach storage (`parseModeChange` writes the `wenyan` alias, `getDefaultMode` accepts either), so a raw compare would read that no-op as a switch.
- A `null` previous mode counts as a change: caveman was off, so the model holds no ruleset at all — the strongest case for sending one.
- Independent modes (commit/review/compress) keep their own skills and get no prose ruleset.
- `reinforce` is the gate as well as the reminder, so the #634 repo opt-out suppresses both.

A session that never switches pays nothing extra — one reminder line, one state read, exactly as before:

```
/caveman ultra   → 5490 bytes (banner + ultra row + rules, full row absent)
next turn        →  278 bytes (unchanged)
```

**Degrade paths.** A `caveman-config.js` from before this change passes the tracker's shape check, so the new exports are resolved individually against stand-ins that reproduce the previous behavior — same pattern the per-session helpers already use. An unreadable `SKILL.md` degrades the same way (standalone install, no skills dir). Both are asserted.

## Second commit: `commands/caveman.toml`

The command prompt paraphrased the `full` row regardless of its argument, so `/caveman ultra` handed the model a prompt describing full *alongside* the ultra ruleset — conflicting instructions that would partly undo the fix. It also contradicted `lite`, which keeps articles and full sentences. Now states only what holds at every level and defers the rest to the injected rules.

## Tests

New `tests/test_mode_tracker_ruleset.js` (10 cases, picked up by the existing `for f in tests/test_*.js` CI step): switch injects the new row / drops the stale one, activation from off injects, same-level re-issue does **not**, the wenyan alias is not a switch, an ordinary turn still costs one line, independent modes get no prose ruleset, and the version-skew degrade — with a control case so that assertion cannot pass for the wrong reason.

Full suite green locally:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/verify_repo.py` | all checks passed |
| `tests/test_*.js` | 12 files, all passed |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | 130 passed |
| `node --test tests/installer/*.test.mjs tests/hooks/*.test.mjs` | 245 passed |

`src/hooks/checksums.sha256` regenerated (same file set).

Note: the re-injected ruleset still carries SKILL.md's own `Default: **full**` line, since that describes the configured default rather than the active level and is what SessionStart already sends. Left as-is — changing it means editing SKILL.md and its synced copies.

title: fix(hooks): convert MSYS-style CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT to a Windows drive path
body:
On Windows with Git Bash as the shell, Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`
as an MSYS-style path (`/c/Users/...`). Both hook commands in
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` pass that string straight to `node.exe`, which
treats a leading `/c/` as a relative path on the current drive rather than a
drive root, so module resolution fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and
`SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit` silently no-op with no user-visible error.

The fix converts the path to a Windows drive form (`c:/Users/...`) before
invoking `node`, using the same sed transform from the issue's own
suggested workaround. It only matches a single-letter drive segment
(`^/[a-zA-Z]/`), so a POSIX-style root on macOS, Linux, or native Windows
shells passes through unchanged.

This is the same transform as the MSYS/Git Bash portion of #583, isolated
into a small, focused change now that #583 no longer applies cleanly.

Verified:
- New regression test (`tests/hooks/plugin-json-windows-hook-path.test.mjs`)
  reads the actual command strings from `plugin.json` and runs them under
  `bash -c` with a stub `node` on PATH, asserting the MSYS root gets
  converted and an ordinary POSIX root passes through untouched. Fails on
  main (2/4), passes on this branch (4/4).
- `npm test`, the standalone `tests/test_*.js` suite, `python -m unittest
  discover -s tests`, and `python tests/verify_repo.py` all pass in a clean
  Docker container against this branch.
- I have not run this on an actual Windows host with Git Bash and node.exe.
  I did replicate the CI `windows-powershell` job's own bash-parse check
  (`bash -n -c $h.command`) locally, and it passes.

title: opencode plugin never sends level-specific ruleset content: /caveman ultra|lite|wenyan-* changes only the banner label
body:
**What happen**

`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`'s `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook only ever pushes the generic label below into the system prompt:

```
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (<mode>) — session ruleset applies.
```

It never reads `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, so every intensity level (lite/full/ultra/wenyan-*) runs on identical, empty instructions. The SessionStart hook (`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js:325-404`) does the real work there: it reads SKILL.md, strips frontmatter, and keeps only the active level's intensity-table row and examples. `plugin.js` has no equivalent code path anywhere in its 215 lines, so an opencode session gets zero differentiated instructions even on its first turn, before any level switch.

Verified live on HEAD (367fdb7) by driving the plugin's real `chat.message` and `experimental.chat.system.transform` hooks against an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` sandbox: `/caveman ultra` and `/caveman lite` produce system-prompt content that differs only in the banner's mode name, with no rules behind either.

This is the opencode side of the asymmetry #975 already reported for the other integration's mid-session switch, and it is worse here: opencode never had the rules in the first place, so there is no working baseline to drift from.

**Expected**

`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman lite` should inject that level's actual filtered SKILL.md rules, the way SessionStart already does for that other integration, not only a differently-labeled banner.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: /caveman ultra
Got:   CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra) — session ruleset applies.
Want:  CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra) — session ruleset applies.

       [ultra's filtered SKILL.md row, e.g. "Strip conjunctions when
       cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough."]
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [x] Other: opencode

main @ 367fdb7.

title: fix(opencode): inject the active level's filtered SKILL.md rules, not just the banner
body:
Fixes #983.

`experimental.chat.system.transform` in the opencode plugin only ever pushed the generic label `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (<mode>)`. It never read `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, so every intensity level ran on identical, empty instructions. The SessionStart hook already does the real work for another integration (`src/hooks/caveman-activate.js:325-404`): read SKILL.md, strip frontmatter, keep only the active level's intensity-table row and examples.

This mirrors that filter locally in `plugin.js` (not bridged through `caveman-config.js`, since `loadConfig()`/`loadParse()` above already exist purely because the compiled Bun runtime can't `require()`/`import()` a CJS sibling, and a third bridge isn't worth it for a ~15-line filter) and appends the result after the banner. The stale-block replace in `experimental.chat.system.transform` now matches to end of string instead of just the banner line, so a mid-session level switch swaps in the new level's rules rather than stacking behind the old ones.

Also derived the stale-block regex from `reinforcementBanner()` itself (splitting on a sentinel and escaping) rather than duplicating the banner text as a second literal, so the two can't drift.

**Verification**
- New regression test (`tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs`) confirmed failing against unpatched `main` (ultra's row absent, only the generic banner present) and passing on this branch, run in Docker on Node 18/20/22 (the CI matrix).
- Full `npm test` + `node --test tests/*.js` + `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, in Docker: same 16 pre-existing failures on `main` and on this branch (unrelated `profile scope` tests), no new failures.
- `competing-prs.sh` re-run at submission against `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`: one candidate, #740 (adds `recordModeChange` calls to `applyModeChange`/`handleSessionCreated`), confirmed by patch to not touch `reinforcementBanner`, `loadFilteredRuleset`, or the `system.transform` handler.
- I have not run this against opencode's own runtime, only against the plugin's exported hooks driven directly, the same way the existing test in this file already does.

title: fix(mcp-servers): forward SIGTERM/SIGINT from caveman-shrink to its upstream child
body:
## Summary

Fixes #742. `caveman-shrink` (the MCP proxy that wraps an upstream MCP server) only reacted to the spawned child's own `error`/`close` events — it never listened for signals sent to the wrapper itself. If something tears the wrapper down directly with SIGTERM/SIGINT (an MCP host ending a session, disabling a tool, reloading config) instead of killing a whole process group, the upstream child was left running, reparented to PID 1.

- Add `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)` / `process.on('SIGINT', ...)` handlers that forward the received signal to `upstream` via `upstream.kill(signal)`.
- The existing `upstream.on('close', ...)` handler already sets the correct exit code (`128 + signal number`) once the child actually stops, so no change needed there — the parent's event loop drains naturally after `close` removes the stdin listeners.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the issue's own repro against unpatched `main`: after `kill -TERM` on the wrapper, the fake upstream process survived with `PPID 1`.
- [x] Added two regression tests to `tests/installer/mcp-shrink.runtime.test.mjs` (SIGTERM and SIGINT) that spawn the wrapper around a long-running child, record the child's real PID, signal the wrapper, and assert the child process no longer exists. Confirmed both fail against unpatched `index.js` and pass with the fix.
- [x] Full suite: `npm test` — 247/247 passing (245 pre-existing + 2 new).

title: fix(caveman-compress): reject a compressed body that is not smaller than the input
body:
## Summary

Fixes #776. `compress_file()` only rejected a compressed body when it was *exactly identical* to the input, and `validate()` checks structural invariants only (headings, code blocks, URLs, paths, bullets, inline code) — nothing compares length. A rewrite that is structurally faithful but **longer** than the input (or the same length with different content) passed every check, got written over the original, and was reported as a successful compression, defeating the tool's entire purpose.

- Added a length gate right after the existing identical-output guard in `compress_file()`: aborts before any backup or write when `len(compressed_body.strip()) >= len(body.strip())`.
- Message matches the issue's expected format: `❌ Compression aborted: output is not smaller than input (69 >= 26 chars).`

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the issue's exact repro against unpatched `main`: a 26-char body regressed to 69 chars, `compress_file()` returned `True`, and the larger file was written with a backup created.
- [x] Added two regression tests to `tests/test_compress_safety.py`, mirroring `test_identical_compressed_output_does_not_touch_disk`'s style:
  - `test_expanded_compressed_output_does_not_touch_disk` — output longer than input
  - `test_same_length_compressed_output_does_not_touch_disk` — output same length, different content
  Confirmed both fail against unpatched `compress.py` and pass with the fix.
- [x] Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 132/132 passing. `npm test` (Node suite) — 245/245 passing, unaffected by this change.

title: feat(hooks): add mode status command
body:
Fixes #856.

## What was wrong

There was no read-only command for checking the active Caveman mode. Users had to infer the current mode from state files or issue a mode-changing command, which could mutate flags, append to the transition log, or affect one-shot restoration behavior.

## The fix

Added `/caveman status` and `/caveman:caveman status` handling to `caveman-mode-tracker.js`.

The command reuses the existing session-aware `resolveActiveMode()` resolver and returns `Caveman mode: <mode>` through `additionalContext`. Missing or durable `off` state reports `off`, and the stored `wenyan` alias is presented as `wenyan-full`.

Status is read-only: it does not mutate mode flags, write a transition-log entry, or restore a one-shot mode. User-facing command documentation and generated hook checksums were updated as well.

## Tests

All relevant tests pass locally:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `python -m unittest tests.test_mode_tracker` | 41 passed |
| `node --test tests/installer/slash-commands.test.mjs` | 16 passed |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | 137 passed, 7 skipped |
| `python tests/verify_repo.py` under Git Bash | All checks passed |

The broader explicit Node suite completed with 235 passed and 9 skipped. One unrelated Windows symlink-permission failure (`EPERM`) remains in `tests/hooks/caveman-config.test.mjs`.

title: fix(stats): retire unsourced 0.65 COMPRESSION constant to align with HONEST-NUMBERS.md
body:
There is an internal contradiction between `src/hooks/caveman-stats.js` and `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` regarding counterfactual savings.

### The contradiction

In `src/hooks/caveman-stats.js` (lines 77–81):

```javascript
// Mean per-task savings from benchmarks/results/*.json (avg_savings: 65 across
// 10 tasks, sonnet-4-20250514). Only 'full' has measured data; lite / ultra /
// wenyan modes show no estimate until benchmarked. Add an entry here when a new
// run is committed.
const COMPRESSION = { 'full': 0.65 };
```

Lines 351 (`deriveSavings`) and 528 use this constant to calculate and print `est. N saved` in user-facing stats output.

However:
1. `benchmarks/results/` currently contains only `.gitkeep`. There are no committed raw benchmark result runs in the tree.
2. `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` explicitly promises:
   > "Output reduction vs default verbose replies | **Not published** | Harness exists, but repository has no committed reviewed raw result"
   
   and under *Measure it yourself*:
   > "1. `/caveman-stats` (Claude Code) reads session log and prints actual output/cache counts. **It publishes no counterfactual savings until a reviewed benchmark result is committed.**"

### Community context

Users running real-world workloads have repeatedly flagged this gap when checking their own bills:
- #727 tested 20 prompts across 300 runs on `claude-opus-4-8`: output fell 41–48%, but total cost shifted +0.06% because fresh input and cache reads dominated the invoice.
- #733 noted the divergence between the advertised 65% in terminal output and an actual measured 8.5%.

`docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` is transparent about the economics (input overhead vs output savings). But because `caveman-stats.js` still prints the speculative `0.65` calculation, users see a number in their terminal that the repo's own documentation disowns.

### Proposed fix

1. Remove the `COMPRESSION` object and the counterfactual `est. N saved` calculation from `src/hooks/caveman-stats.js`.
2. Keep all measured counters intact: actual output tokens, cache reads, fresh input, turn counts, and rule-overhead accounting.
3. Replace the estimate line with a pointer to `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` explaining that provider-billed A/B testing outranks counterfactual estimates.
4. Update `tests/test_caveman_stats.js` to assert the measured output counters without the counterfactual estimate.

Happy to open a clean PR with this diff if you'd like it fixed.

title: test(hooks): add reproduction corpus and table test for mode activation (#187)
body:
### Summary

Adds a table-driven test corpus in `tests/fixtures/mode-activation/cases.json` and a runner in `tests/test_mode_activation_corpus.js` covering natural-language activation and deactivation behavior (#187, #672, #975).

### Why

Activation and deactivation bug reports often arrive as narrative anecdotes, making regressions hard to track without an explicit reproduction table.

This PR introduces a pure-data fixture set without modifying any existing production code or regexes:
1. **Intended triggers**: Explicit commands (`/caveman ultra`, `/caveman off`, `activate caveman`, `be brief`, `back to normal mode`).
2. **Negative prose controls**: General text that shouldn't trigger state changes (`"I was reading about caveman art"`, `"switch to a different branch in git"`, `"the ultra-wide monitor setup"`, `"switch from normal mode to debug mode"`).
3. **Documented known failures**: Exact edge cases reported in #187 (e.g. `"I want to start building a caveman game"`, `"don't activate caveman"`, `"fix(caveman): stop caveman being disabled by ordinary prose"`).

### Mechanics

- `tests/fixtures/mode-activation/cases.json` stores prompts, expected outcomes, categories, and references to open issues.
- `tests/test_mode_activation_corpus.js` exercises `parseModeChange` across all cases and validates parity against the hook (`caveman-mode-tracker.js`).
- Known-failing cases are explicitly flagged (`known_failing: true`) and assert current behavior so CI passes while maintaining an honest baseline for future regex improvements.
- Uses standard library only (`fs`, `path`, `assert`, `child_process`). Runs 28 assertions in ~3s.

### Verification

title: daily triage 2026-09-05: level-switch ruleset (both hosts), shrink signals, compress expansion, MSYS hook path
body:
Daily triage run. Five fixes across four root-cause clusters, every one adopted from a contributor PR with authorship preserved and extended where the original missed a sibling host, a sibling signal, or a shell. A sixth commit closes a gap a review bot found in one of them.

Full suite green on this branch: `npm test` 262/262, `node --test tests/*.js` 12/12, `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 133/133, `python tests/verify_repo.py` OK, `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` gate passed. No Go files changed.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #975 | `caveman-mode-tracker.js` answered a mid-session `/caveman <level>` with the per-turn reminder only. SessionStart injects the ruleset once, so the model kept the old level's rules while every banner asserted the new one — silent and self-confirming. | Claude Code, all OS | `tests/test_mode_tracker_ruleset.js` (10 cases) | #981 |
| #983 | Same asymmetry on the opencode side, worse: `plugin.js` never read SKILL.md at all, so every level ran on identical empty instructions from the first turn. | opencode, all OS | `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` (+2 cases) | #984 |
| #742 | `caveman-shrink` registered no termination handling, so a host stopping it with a signal left the spawned upstream MCP server orphaned on PID 1. | any MCP host, POSIX | `tests/installer/mcp-shrink.runtime.test.mjs` (3 signals) | #985, #775 |
| #776 | `validate()` checks structural invariants but not length, so a rewrite that was faithful and *longer* passed every check, overwrote the original and reported success. Guard now holds on the retry path too (see below). | all hosts | `tests/test_compress_safety.py` (+3 cases) | #986, #777 |
| #199 | Under Git Bash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is MSYS-style (`/c/Users/...`), which `node.exe` cannot resolve — both plugin hooks died with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. | Claude Code, Windows + Git Bash | `tests/hooks/plugin-json-windows-hook-path.test.mjs` (12 cases) | #982 |

### What I changed on top of the adopted PRs

**#983 — bridged to the shared loader.** #984 landed its own `canonicalModeLabel` and its own SKILL.md intensity-table parser inside `plugin.js`, duplicating the pair `caveman-config.js` grew for #975. That is the drift CLAUDE.md's "keep it in `caveman-config.js`" rule names opencode as the reason for, and `plugin.js` already evaluates that file through `loadConfig()`, so the shared loader cost no new mechanism. The installed `caveman-config.cjs` is a copy, so a stale plugin dir has no such export — that is resolved per call and degrades to the banner rather than throwing inside a system-prompt hook. Covered by a test that strips the export line from an installed copy.

**#199 — the adopted fix was a bashism.** #982 used a herestring:

```sh
HOOK_ROOT=$(sed '...' <<< "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}")
```

`<<<` is bash-only. On Debian and Ubuntu `/bin/sh` is dash, where it is a syntax error, not a portability nit — verified: `dash: 1: Syntax error: redirection unexpected`. The hook command is a shell snippet and the shell that runs it is not ours to choose, so on any host invoking it through sh this took down SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit together, for every user on that platform, to fix a path format only Windows produces. Trading a Windows-only break for a Linux-wide one is a bad exchange.

`printf %s "$VAR" | sed` does the same conversion and is POSIX. The test harness is the reason this was invisible: it ran the command under `bash -c` explicitly, the one shell where the bug does not reproduce. Every case now runs under sh and bash both, and a spaces-in-path case is added. Confirmed the herestring fails all six sh cases and passes all six bash ones.

**#742 — added SIGHUP.** The gap is that the wrapper registers no termination handling at all, and SIGHUP shares that root cause exactly; it is also the likeliest of the three to be triggered by hand (closing terminal, disconnecting supervisor). Folded into the one forwarding path. SIGKILL stays unregistered because it cannot be trapped.

**#776 — the retry path bypassed the guard** (`c948907`, found by Devin Review on this PR, and a real hole in the fix as first pushed). The adopted guard ran once, on the first candidate. A candidate that fails validation is sent back to Claude for repair and `compressed = fixed` put the repaired text straight into the loop — so a repair that restores the structure `validate()` asked for by padding the prose back out was written over the source and reported as a successful compression. That is the reported bug again, one branch over, and the likelier shape of it: asking a model to restore a dropped heading is exactly what makes output grow. The comparison moved into `_is_smaller_than_body()` and now runs on every candidate; `fixed` is a whole file, so its frontmatter is split off before comparing, or the check would count verbatim-preserved frontmatter on one side only.

`commands/caveman.toml` is also updated, from #981: the stub paraphrased the `full` level regardless of argument, so on `/caveman ultra` two of the three signals the model received pointed at the wrong level. #975 calls this out explicitly as part of the bug.

### Verification beyond the suites

- **Path resolution at all three installed depths.** Both hooks were driven against a real standalone layout (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks/` with skills at `../skills`) and a real plugin layout (`<root>/src/hooks/` with skills at `../../skills`); all four combinations resolve the actual ultra row rather than silently falling back to the hardcoded ruleset. The `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` depth is covered by the control case in `test_mode_tracker_ruleset.js`.
- **opencode both layouts.** Installed tree via the installer test; dev tree driven directly from `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`. Both return the active level's row and no other level's.
- **Nothing new to ship.** The only added files are tests, so no installer file list, `npm` `files` array or plugin layout needed updating — deliberately no new `src/hooks/` sibling, which would have had to be added to `checksums.sha256`, `verify_repo.py` and the install lists.
- **No clobber risk from the opencode idempotent rewrite.** Its `staleBlock` regex matches to end-of-string; confirmed neither `SKILL.md` nor `src/rules/` contains the banner phrase, so it can only ever match an entry this hook itself wrote.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#400 / #980** — reproduced as reported. Not adopting this run: the PR passes `--consent` unconditionally, and its own comment records that Gemini CLI before v0.7.0 rejects that flag with exit 1. That trades a hang on new CLIs for a hard failure on older ones — the same class of regression as the #199 bashism above. Wants a version probe, or the env var alone. The security reasoning about the scratch directory (avoiding a planted `/tmp/.env`, keeping `trustedFolders.json` unchanged) looks right and worth keeping. I could not verify real Gemini CLI flag behavior from this container.
- **#187 / #992** — #992 adds a reproduction corpus and table test, no fix. Useful groundwork; left for a run that can pair it with the parser change.
- **#991, #733, #727** — all turn on a published savings number. Out of scope by standing instruction: this job never publishes or changes a benchmark, savings percentage or token-reduction figure.
- **#976, #977, #978, #979, #988, #989, #990** — `agent-drift:` pin bumps. Root suite passes, so these are eligible, but each needs a conformance run against the newly installed version to be worth anything; batching them with behavioral fixes would make this PR hard to review. Recommend a separate pin-bump PR.
- **Everything else open** — feature requests and design proposals (#638, #637, #629, #743, #571-class agent additions), triaged only, never implemented per standing instruction.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#981** by @akshath-raj — **adopted**, both commits cherry-picked with authorship preserved. The strongest PR in this batch: put the shared loader in `caveman-config.js` exactly where CLAUDE.md says it belongs, gated re-injection on an actual change so an unchanged session pays nothing extra, handled the `wenyan`/`wenyan-full` storage alias, updated `checksums.sha256`, and tested the plugin-cache-drift degradation path.
- **#984** by @AmirF194 — **adopted**, then bridged to the shared loader (see above). Correct diagnosis and a good test; the only issue was the duplicated parser.
- **#985** by @kavish-19 — **adopted**. Minimal, correct, with a real process-level test for both signals. Extended to SIGHUP.
- **#775** by @Dhevenddra — **not cherry-picked, but credited on the commit.** More thorough in scope than #985 (SIGHUP, a grace period, Windows EOF teardown, a separately testable `shutdown.js`), but it sits on a months-old base whose merge commit reverts large parts of current main, so applying it would be destructive. The SIGHUP gap it identified is fixed here. The grace-period and `shutdown.js` ideas are still worth having and would rebase cleanly as a follow-up.
- **#986** by @kavish-19 — **adopted**. Focused, with the same-length reject deliberately tested. The retry-path gap above was in the original issue's fix generally, not something this PR introduced relative to the others.
- **#777** by @divya0795 — **not cherry-picked.** Same fix as #986 and filed first, but on a stale base whose diff against current main deletes workflow files. #986 applied cleanly. Both authors filed a correct diagnosis of #776.
- **#982** by @AmirF194 — **adopted**, bashism corrected and the harness hardened (see above). The MSYS diagnosis was right and is the part that mattered.
- **#992** by @poorvith-mp — reviewed, not adopted this run. See #187 above.

## Needs maintainer decision

- **#980's `--consent` version gate.** Probe `gemini --version` and pass the flag only on >= 0.7.0, or ship the env var alone and accept the consent prompt? I did not want to pick a compatibility floor on your behalf.
- **`commands/caveman.toml`.** CLAUDE.md says behavior changes live in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` only. The change here is inside a Codex/Gemini command stub and is part of what #975 reports, so I kept it, but it is a prose change to a non-SKILL file and is yours to confirm.
- **Agent-drift pin bumps** — seven open, deliberately not batched here. Want them as one PR per run?
- **#775's grace period.** Should a child that ignores SIGTERM be SIGKILLed after a timeout? #775 proposed 2s. Not adopted because it is behavior beyond what #742 reported.

title: fix(stats): drop unsourced output-savings estimate, keep rule overhead
body:
`caveman-stats.js` printed an "Est. tokens saved" figure computed from a hardcoded `COMPRESSION = { full: 0.65 }` ratio. That ratio traces to a benchmark run that was never committed: `benchmarks/results/` holds only `.gitkeep`. `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` explicitly promises no counterfactual savings claim until a reviewed result lands, so the tool contradicted its own honesty doc on every invocation.

Removed `COMPRESSION` and everything downstream that derived a number from it: `deriveSavings`, `deriveNet`/`netLines`, `outputReductionPct`, the per-mode savings breakdown, the USD estimate, and the lifetime output-reduction percentage. The statusline suffix is now always written empty (so a fictional figure left over from before this fix does not linger on disk) rather than carrying a savings string.

Kept the rule-overhead estimate: `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md` separately sources and publishes that number (the per-turn input cost of the injected rules), and it does not depend on which benchmarked mode ran, so it now shows for any active mode rather than only `full`. Kept the `#601` per-mode token-attribution mechanism (`attributeByMode`, `readModeLog`) too: it reports real, already-happened token counts and has uses beyond the removed estimate.

Updated the docs and README passages that described the retired statusline savings example, and regenerated the `caveman-stats.js` entry in `src/hooks/checksums.sha256`.

- The updated `tests/test_caveman_stats.js` catches the bug: 8 of its cases fail against `main` as it stands today, and all 48 pass on this branch. Ran both ways in Docker under Node 18 and Node 22.
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` and `python -m unittest discover -s tests` both pass, which covers the regenerated `checksums.sha256` entry and the Python-side hook tests.
- I only ran this in Linux containers, so I have not tried it on Windows or macOS, and the Go engine suite is untouched by this change so I left it alone.

Fixes #991

title: fix(shrink): escalate to SIGKILL on a stuck upstream
body:
Follow-up to #775, which you reviewed on #993. You kept the SIGHUP gap it found and asked for the two pieces that did not come across: the grace period for a child that ignores the signal, and moving teardown into a testable `shutdown.js`. Both are here, rebuilt on current `main` rather than rebased, so there is no months-old base and no merge commit this time.

## Problem

`forwardSignalToUpstream` on `main` sends the signal and stops there:

```js
function forwardSignalToUpstream(signal) {
  if (!upstream.killed) upstream.kill(signal);
}
```

An upstream that honours SIGTERM exits, and `close` fires. One that traps it and declines to exit keeps running, and since nothing else terminates the wrapper, both processes survive the teardown the host just asked for. That is the same orphan the forwarding was added to prevent, on the subset of servers that install their own handler.

## Fix

`shutdown.forward(signal)` arms a 2s timer when it sends the signal and sends SIGKILL if the child is still alive when it expires. The timer is cleared on `close`, so a server that exits promptly is not delayed by it.

Teardown moves into `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/shutdown.js`: signal forwarding, the escalation, exit-code translation, and the stdin detach. `index.js` keeps the wiring. Timers are injected, so the escalation tests run synchronously and cannot flake on a loaded runner.

`shutdown.js` is added to `package.json` "files". The packaging test from #597 fails without it, which turned out to be a useful guard.

## Evidence

`node tests/test_mcp_shrink.js` gives 26 passed / 0 failed, up from 18 on main.

Each of the eight new tests was run against a variant with the behaviour deliberately removed, so none of them is decorative:

| Variant | Test that catches it |
|---|---|
| escalation removed | escalates to SIGKILL when the upstream ignores the signal |
| SIGKILL sent unconditionally | does not escalate when the upstream exits inside the grace period |
| liveness guard removed | a second signal is a no-op, not a duplicate kill |
| `close` leaves the timer armed | close clears a pending escalation |
| grace period set to 0 | the default grace period is a real duration |
| signal exit code returns 1 | close reports 128+signal |

End to end, wrapping a server that follows stdin EOF, before and after the change:

```
main  : exited code=0 in 27ms | description -> "This is tool that reads file"
branch: exited code=0 in 36ms | description -> "This is tool that reads file"
```

Same output, same exit code, and the grace timer stays out of the normal path.

`python tests/verify_repo.py` passes. `npm test` passes.

## One thing I left out

While building the end-to-end check I hit a separate case that is still open on `main`. It is not what you asked for, so it is not in this PR. An upstream that ignores **stdin EOF** is orphaned, because `endInput()` only ends the child's stdin and nothing follows up:

```
main  : HUNG - wrapper still alive 6s after stdin EOF (upstream orphaned)
branch: HUNG - wrapper still alive 6s after stdin EOF (upstream orphaned)
```

That matters most on Windows, where there are no real signals and the comment in `index.js` points teardown at this exact path. #775 carried a backstop for it inside `endInput()`. Happy to send it as its own PR if you want it.

## Notes

- MIT directory, so inbound = outbound.
- Signed off (DCO).
- The SIGKILL escalation cannot be exercised natively on Windows, where `kill()` terminates the target without running handlers. The logic is covered by the unit tests above; I do not have a Linux node install on this machine to demonstrate it in a real process.

title: caveman-compress: validate_code_blocks cannot detect a fenced/indented block swapping relative position
body:
**What happen**
`extract_code_blocks()` in `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/validate.py` (line 109) collects every fenced code block first, then appends every indented code block after them, regardless of where each block actually sits in the document: `return blocks + extract_indented_code_blocks(text)`.

`validate_code_blocks()` (line 284) compares this list between the original and the compressed file with a plain `c1 != c2`. Because the list is grouped by block TYPE rather than ordered by document position, a compression pass that swaps a fenced block and an indented block's relative position, leaving their content unchanged, produces an identical list on both sides. Validation reports the file unchanged even though the two documents put the blocks in a different order.

**Expected**
A validator that promises code blocks are "preserved exactly" should catch a change in block order, not only a change in block content.

**Before/after example**
Two documents, same fenced Python block and the same indented shell command, only their relative order in the document differs.

~~~
Original:            Intro. <fenced python block> Middle. <indented shell command> End.
"Compressed":         Intro. <indented shell command> Middle. <fenced python block> End.
~~~

Got:   validation passes (`is_valid=True`, no errors)
Want:  validation fails (the two blocks changed relative order)

Reproduced directly against `extract_code_blocks`/`validate_code_blocks` on current `main` (`5184b3d`), in a clean `python:3.11-slim` container:

~~~
extract_code_blocks(orig) == ["<fenced block>", "<indented block>"]
extract_code_blocks(comp) == ["<fenced block>", "<indented block>"]
c1 == c2 (extractor says unchanged): True
is_valid: True errors: []
~~~

**Platform**
- [x] Other: this is a validator-logic bug in the Python script itself, not platform-specific.

**Version / install method**
`main` @ `5184b3d`

title: fix(compress): compare code blocks by document position, not extraction type
body:
`extract_code_blocks()` (`skills/caveman-compress/scripts/validate.py:109`) concatenated all fenced blocks in document order, then appended all indented blocks in document order: `blocks + extract_indented_code_blocks(text)`. That preserves within-type order but throws away cross-type order. `validate_code_blocks()` diffs this list with a plain `c1 != c2`, so a compression pass that swaps a fenced block and an indented block's relative position, content unchanged, produced identical lists on both sides and reported the file unchanged.

Fix: `extract_code_blocks()` and `extract_indented_code_blocks()` now track each block's starting line, and the final list is merged by that position instead of by extraction type. Both extractors still decide block boundaries exactly as before; only the merge order changed.

Fixes #997

**Verification**
- New regression test (`TestCrossTypeBlockOrderIsValidated`): fails on `main`, passes on this branch, run in a clean `python:3.11-slim` container.
- Full `tests/test_validate_inline.py` (23 tests) and `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (136 tests) both pass in `python:3.11-slim` / `node:20-slim`, matching the repo's `python` CI job.
- One existing test's expected block order (`test_lone_indented_marker_does_not_capture_the_real_block`) encoded the old type-grouped order; updated to the correct document-position order.
- Did not check the JS/Node compression paths in `src/` and `mcp-servers/`; this fix is scoped to the Python validator only.

title: caveman-shrink: PROTECTED_PATTERNS function-call regex swallows ordinary parentheticals
body:
**What happen**
`PROTECTED_PATTERNS` in `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js` (line 61) includes `/[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\([^)]*\)/g` to shield real function-call syntax from prose compression. The `\s*` also matches an ordinary word followed by a space and a parenthetical, e.g. `useful (please read carefully)`, not only actual calls like `compress(text)`. The whole span gets sentinel-protected before `compressProse` runs, so filler/hedge/pleasantry stripping never reaches an English parenthetical.

**Expected**
Only real function-call syntax (no space before the paren) should be protected; a word followed by a space and a parenthetical aside should still compress normally.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: "This tool is useful (please read carefully) before continuing."
Got:   "This tool is useful (please read carefully) before continuing."
Want:  "This tool is useful (read carefully) before continuing."
```

Reproduced directly against `compress()` on current `main` (`5184b3d`), in a clean `node:20-slim` container.

title: fix(shrink): require no space before "(" in function-call protection
body:
Fixes #999.

`PROTECTED_PATTERNS`' function-call entry had `\s*` between the identifier and the paren, so it matched "useful (please read carefully)" the same as "compress(text)". The whole span got sentinel-protected before `compressProse` ran, so a pleasantry or filler sitting inside an ordinary parenthetical never got stripped.

Dropped the `\s*`: real function-call syntax never has a space before `(`, so this stops matching English parentheticals without touching actual calls.

Added a test pinning both a pleasantry and a filler word getting stripped out of a parenthetical, plus that `compress(text, opts)` still protects; the new test breaks without the fix. Ran the full `test_mcp_shrink.js` suite on node 18/20/22 (the CI matrix), all green.

title: Redaction never matches a GitHub App installation token (ghs_), and the new stateless JWT format widens the gap
body:
## What

None of the redaction layers carry a `ghs_` pattern, so a GitHub App installation token passes through unredacted. GitHub is currently migrating those tokens to a much longer, more log-prone format, which turns a latent gap into a practical one.

## Where

Four independent sites, all missing the prefix entirely:

- `shared/platform/redact/redact.go` — `credentialPrefixRe` lists `xox`, `sk_live_`, `rk_live_`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `AIza` and `sk-proj-`, but no `ghs_`.
- `shared/platform/redact/payload.go` — the `credential-prefix-token` literal-needle list has the same omission. This one gates whether the regex pass runs at all, so it has to be fixed alongside the regex or the regex is never reached.
- `proxy/internal/repointel/index.go` — the credential-prefix list used to reject secret-shaped values has `ghp-`, `ghp_`, `github_pat-`, `github_pat_`, but no `ghs_`.
- `packages/subagent-tax/lib/sink.mjs` — the key pattern covers `ghp_` and `gho_`, not `ghs_`.

## Why it matters more now

Per GitHub's changelog of 2026-05-15 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-15-github-app-installation-tokens-per-request-override-header/), server-to-server installation tokens — which includes the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` — are moving from a short opaque string to a stateless JWT: `ghs_` followed by roughly 520 base64url characters containing two dots. A 520-character credential is far more likely to end up quoted in a log line, an error body or a CI transcript than the short opaque one was, which is exactly the material these redaction layers see.

The character class matters as much as the prefix. An alphanumeric-only class such as `ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}` does not match a stateless token at all — the JWT's header segment ends at a dot well before 36 alphanumeric characters have gone by — so a pattern written that way fails closed to "no match" rather than matching partially. GitHub's own recommended validation shape is `ghs_[A-Za-z0-9\.\-_]{36,}`.

## Suggested fix

Add a `ghs_[A-Za-z0-9._-]{36,}` branch at each of the four sites. The dash belongs last in the class so it is not read as a range, matching the convention the neighbouring `AIza[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{30,}` pattern already uses.

Over-matching is not a concern in practice. Go's RE2 has no backtracking, and in either engine the class run stops at the first character outside it, so a token followed by prose ends at the space. In `sink.mjs` the surrounding `\b` even trims a trailing sentence period for free, since `.` is a non-word character.

`ghp_`, `gho_` and `github_pat_` are a different token family and are unaffected by the format change; they need no widening.

## Not affected

`shared/platform/githubapp/` needs nothing. `InstallationToken.Token` is a plain string, minted just in time and never persisted, and no `len()` in the package constrains it, so the changelog's advice about sizing storage for 520 characters has no target there.

title: fix(redact): recognize ghs_ GitHub App installation tokens
body:
Added the `ghs_` branch at all four sites, with the character class you specified (letters, digits, dots, hyphens, underscores, dash last in the class) so it matches the stateless JWT shape and not just the old opaque token.

`payload.go`'s needle list needed the same addition since it gates whether the regex pass even runs; without it the regex change alone would never fire.

Tests: a synthetic `ghs_`-prefixed JWT-shaped fixture at each of the four call sites, split mid-token in source so push protection doesn't flag the fixtures themselves. All four show the same failure on main and pass on this branch. Full `go test ./shared/... ./proxy/...` and the `subagent-tax` node suite still pass (50/50).

Left `ghp_`, `gho_` and `github_pat_` untouched per your note, they're a different token family.
Fixes #1002

title: proxy: opencode-go compat mount drops the x-opencode-session header that Pi sends
body:
**What happen**

OpenCode sent this notice on 2026-09-06:

> Some of your requests to OpenCode Go are missing an x-opencode-session header. If we don't have this we cannot properly optimize our service. Starting 09/06 requests missing this header may error.

Pi sends the header. The Caveman proxy removes it.

Pi 0.85.1 adds `x-opencode-session` and `x-opencode-client: pi` to each request that has a session ID. The condition is `model.provider` equal to `opencode` or `opencode-go`, or a base URL host equal to `opencode.ai`. The check uses the provider name, not the base URL. Thus Pi sends the headers after the caveman extension points the base URL at the gateway. Source in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.85.1, `src/core/provider-attribution.ts`:

```ts
function getSessionHeaders(model: Model<Api>, sessionId: string | undefined): Record<string, string> | undefined {
	if (!sessionId) return undefined;
	if (
		model.provider !== "opencode" &&
		model.provider !== "opencode-go" &&
		!matchesHost(model.baseUrl, OPENCODE_HOST)
	) {
		return undefined;
	}
	return { "x-opencode-session": sessionId, "x-opencode-client": "pi" };
}
```

The proxy builds the upstream headers from a fixed allowlist. `Base.SanitizeAndMapHeaders` makes a new header map and copies only the listed names (`proxy/providers/adapter.go:433`). The list has `content-type`, `accept`, `accept-encoding`, `idempotency-key`, the OpenAI headers, the Anthropic headers, and `api-version`. It does not have `x-opencode-*`. The opencode-go compat mount overrides this function (`namedAdapter.SanitizeAndMapHeaders`, `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat.go:184`). The override returns early for each path that is not `/v1/messages` (line 189). On `/v1/messages` it moves the key into `x-api-key`. It does not restore the session headers on any path. The gateway assigns the map to the upstream request (`proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go:348`).

The pi extension routes three OpenCode Go APIs through this mount (`packages/pi-extension/src/protocol.ts:96`): `anthropic-messages` to `/v1/messages`, `openai-completions` to `/v1/chat/completions`, and `openai-responses` to `/v1/responses`. The proxy drops the headers on all three paths.

PR #948 (merged 2026-09-02) added the built-in `/compat/opencode-go` mount and the automatic Pi route. Before #948, the extension sent OpenCode Go models to `/w/pi/openai/v1`, and the proxy sent them to `api.openai.com` (#946). PR #969 fixed the auth scheme on `/v1/messages`, and PR #972 fixed the routing rules. Thus #948 exposed the existing allowlist limit on the new route.

The local proxy database (`~/.caveman/caveman.db`, table `requests`, column `ts` in UTC) shows the traffic from Pi. All rows have `agent_slug=pi`:

| Day (UTC) | Endpoint | Status | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-01 | /compat/opencode-go/v1/responses | 200 | 7 |
| 2026-09-01 | /compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions | 200 | 1 |
| 2026-09-04 | /compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions | 200 | 23 |
| 2026-09-05 | /compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions | 200 | 18 |
| 2026-09-05 | /compat/opencode-go/v1/chat/completions | 502 | 2 |

The rows from 2026-09-01 are before the merge of #948. They most likely came from a local build of the #948 branch. The local reflog shows the first commit of that branch six minutes before the first row. The rows have no build hash, so this is an inference. The two 502 responses have no explanation in the proxy log. No live rejection by OpenCode is claimed from them.

The database stores no headers, and `CAVE_CAPTURE_DIR` stores bodies and metadata only. Thus no local record shows the headers that Pi sent. The evidence for the header loss is the source above.

Not affected:

- Pi in direct mode. The request goes to `opencode.ai` with the headers.
- The OpenCode CLI without `caveman enable opencode`. Its requests do not pass through the proxy.

Not verified: the OpenCode CLI with `caveman enable opencode` and an OpenCode Go model. The `/w/opencode` route uses the same allowlist. Thus it can drop the same headers. The issue text attributes `x-opencode-project` and `x-opencode-request` to the OpenCode CLI. This attribution is not checked against the OpenCode CLI source.

**Expected**

The opencode-go compat mount forwards `x-opencode-session`, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, and `x-opencode-request` to the upstream. The adapter copies the four names before the early return at `openaicompat.go:189`. The copy applies only to the `opencode-go` mount. The shared allowlist does not change, and no `x-opencode-*` wildcard is added.

Two tests pin the behavior:

- An adapter test in `openaicompat_test.go` with a matrix over `/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/responses`. It asserts the exact values when the headers are present. It asserts that the headers stay absent when the inbound request has none. It asserts that a second named mount forwards none of the four.
- An extension of `TestStandaloneOpenCodeGoAuthEndToEnd` in `standalone_test.go`. It puts the headers in the existing `inbound` field and asserts the values at the fake upstream, next to the current auth and body assertions.

The fix lives in the Go proxy binary. Users need a new `bin-v*` release, not only a CLI bump.

Related: #946, #948, #967, #969, #970, #972.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: caveman pi --provider opencode-go --model kimi-k2.6 -p 'Reply with OK'
Got:   the upstream request has no x-opencode-session header; OpenCode may reject it from 2026-09-06
Want:  the upstream request carries x-opencode-session and x-opencode-client, the same as direct mode
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Pi (OpenCode Go provider through the proxy)

**Version / install method**

CLI 1.3.3 on bin-v1.1.6, `caveman enable pi`. Repository at `e0e0253` on `main`, after PR #948, #969, and #972. Pi 0.85.1.

title: fix(proxy): forward OpenCode session headers on the opencode-go mount
body:
## Summary

- The opencode-go compat mount now forwards `x-opencode-session`, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, and `x-opencode-request` to the upstream (fixes #1006). Pi 0.85.1 sends the first two on each request that has a session ID. OpenCode announced that from 2026-09-06 a request without `x-opencode-session` can get an error.
- `Base.SanitizeAndMapHeaders` builds a new header map from a fixed allowlist, thus the proxy dropped every `x-opencode-*` header. The named adapter in `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat.go` now copies the four names after the base call and before the early return for non-Messages paths. Thus the copy runs on `/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/responses`.
- The copy is gated on the mount prefix `/compat/opencode-go`. The shared allowlist, the credential mapping, and the `x-api-key` remap on `/v1/messages` are unchanged. No `x-opencode-*` wildcard is added, so another named mount does not learn the session identity of the caller.
- The four header names live in one package-level slice with a comment that gives the reason.

## Proof

- New adapter test `TestNewNamed_ForwardsOpenCodeSessionHeaders` in `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat_test.go`. It covers the three paths with the headers present and absent. It asserts that the messages path still sets `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version`. It asserts that a second named mount at `/compat/other` forwards none of the four headers.
- `TestStandaloneOpenCodeGoAuthEndToEnd` in `proxy/internal/standalone/standalone_test.go` gets a `wantHeaders` field and three new cases, one per path. Each case sends `x-opencode-session` and `x-opencode-client` through `/w/pi/compat/opencode-go/...` and asserts the exact values at the fake upstream, next to the existing auth and body assertions. The four existing cases now assert that no `x-opencode-session` gets to the upstream.
- Regression proof: with the tests from this branch and `openaicompat.go` from `main`, both tests fail. The adapter test reports four empty headers on each of the three paths. The standalone test reports `upstream x-opencode-session = ""` on all three new cases.
- `go build ./...`, `gofmt -l`, and `go vet` on the changed packages are clean. `go test ./providers/... ./internal/standalone/... ./internal/gateway/...` passes.
- Local end-to-end run on 2026-09-06: a proxy built from this branch, a `compat: opencode-go` override to a loopback fake upstream, and `CAVE_SSRF_ALLOWLIST=127.0.0.1:9999`. The fake upstream received `x-opencode-session` and `x-opencode-client` on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`. The binary from bin-v1.1.6 sent none.
- Not run: `proxy/cmd/caveman-proxy`, `proxy/internal/nativeruntime`, and `proxy/internal/store` fail on this machine because the temp directory is group-writable. They fail the same way on a clean `main` and do not touch the changed code.

## Notes

- The fix lives in the Go proxy binary. Users need a new `bin-v*` release, not only a CLI bump.
- The OpenCode CLI with `caveman enable opencode` and an OpenCode Go model goes through the `/w/opencode` route. That route uses the same allowlist and is not changed here. The attribution of `x-opencode-project` and `x-opencode-request` to the OpenCode CLI comes from #1006 and is not checked against the OpenCode CLI source.
- No local record shows the headers that the installed Pi client sent to the proxy. The database and `CAVE_CAPTURE_DIR` store no headers. The claim about Pi rests on the quoted `getSessionHeaders` source in #1006.
