title: daily triage 2026-09-16: JSON decode-remarshal corruption, revoked-scope capacity leak, nocgo symbol cap, trial silent bypass, shrink stdin EOF
body:
Five fixes, each reproduced with a failing test first. Three adopt contributor PRs by cherry-pick so authorship is preserved; two of those needed work the contributor missed. Two further commits fix issues Devin Review found on this PR — see **Review round** below.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1057 | Decode into `map[string]any` + re-marshal rounds every integer literal above 2^53 anywhere in the body — `encoding/json` decodes untyped numbers as `float64`. Four sites. | Bedrock Converse/Invoke; OpenAI Chat/Responses; gateway recovery loop (all providers). All OS. | `TestCachePointsPreservesLargeIntegersElsewhereInBody`, `TestTransformPreservesLargeIntegersOnRemarshalFallback`, `TestRetrieveRewritesPreserveLargeIntegerLiterals`, `TestAppendArrayElements*`, plus `Test*RejectsTrailingBytes*` | #1058 |
| #1064 | `Delete` writes `expires_at=0`; every `Expire` statement requires `expires_at>0`, so a revoked scope's rows are unreachable forever and revocation traffic alone wedges the shared 100k-row / 64MB cap. | Middleware store, all OS. | `TestMiddlewareRevocationTombstoneSurvivesGraceThenReclaims`, `TestMiddlewareExpiryReclaimsCapacityFromRevokedScopes`, `TestMiddlewareRevokedGrantAnswersDeletedThroughItsGracePeriod` | #1065 |
| #1059 | `ast.Inspect`'s return value only prunes descent into a node's own children. Top-level decls are siblings in `file.Decls`, so the 500-symbol cap stopped nothing after the first declaration that hit it. | repointel under `CGO_ENABLED=0` — which `build-release-binaries.mjs` pins, so it is the path every shipped binary runs. `symbols_cgo.go` was already correct. | `TestScanSymbolsCapsAtFiveHundredAcrossSiblingDeclarations` (verified failing under `CGO_ENABLED=0`, passing under `CGO_ENABLED=1`) | #1060 |
| #1068 | A trial points the child at its own labelled proxy through the environment; native routing pins the base URL in the agent's own config file, which wins. The child talks to the persistent listener, `RecordPayload` drops anything without a `trial:` label, and every counter renders 0 while the trial exits 0. | Every native host (claude/codex/hermes/gemini/opencode/pi/aider). All OS. | `trial refuses to run against an agent whose native routing pins its base URL`, with a control run proving the guard fired on the pin, plus interrupted-install coverage both directions | — |
| — (stdin-EOF half of #995) | `endInput()` did step 1 of the MCP stdio shutdown sequence and stopped; steps 2–3 sat behind the process signal handlers only. Closing stdin is the first thing a host does, and on Windows the only thing. | `caveman-shrink` wrapper; worst on Windows, which has no real signals. | 6 new assertions in `tests/test_mcp_shrink.js` (28 → 35) | #1056 |

### On the decode-remarshal cluster

#1058 fixes Bedrock by splicing. I checked every sibling that runs the same logic and found three more, fixed in a second commit at the decode instead (splicing is unavailable to them — each mutates a nested field no top-level insertion can express). In descending blast radius:

- `appendRetrieveResult` rewrites the **request** re-sent upstream during recovery, so it rewrote the entire conversation history on every round trip.
- `stripRetrieveCall` rewrites the **response** handed back to the agent, so a rounded id landed in a sibling `tool_use`'s arguments that the agent then executes.
- `openai.ApplyProviderNativeTransforms`' documented re-marshal fallback (`stream_options.include_usage`, or `reasoning.effort` on Responses).

Checked and unaffected: `engine/pixel/transform_openai.go` and `engine/cmd/caveman-engine/main.go` decode into `map[string]json.RawMessage`, which preserves raw bytes; `anthropic/cache_breakpoints.go` and the openai preferred path already splice.

Worth noting from the repro output: the old path also **reordered the whole body** (`{"messages":...,"system":...}` → sorted keys), so a cache optimizer was rewriting the very prefix it was trying to make cacheable.

### Two things the contributor PRs missed

**#1065** encodes revocation time as a negative `expires_at` — right idea — but selects revoked scopes into `dead` the moment they are revoked. `dead` drives the choices delete, and `recovery.retrieve` reads the typed `"deleted"` answer off the **choice** row via `Grant`, exactly as `previousPlan` reads it off the scope row. Since `Expire` runs in front of every optimize request, that collapsed the revocation grace to zero on the recovery path (a replayed marker got `"not_found"` — a marker the caller never had — instead of `"deleted"`) while leaving it at a full week on the optimize path. Added a test for the `Grant` path, then made revoked rows wait out the same grace in `dead` that they already wait out in the scope delete. Nothing is collected early by this: `Delete` calls `purge` synchronously, so a revoked scope's payloads are already gone and only its rows remain.

**My own decode fix** widened what two adapters accept, caught in the review pass: `json.Unmarshal` rejects trailing bytes after the top-level value, a `json.Decoder` does not. So `{...}garbage` went from "malformed, pass through byte-identically" to "decode, mutate, re-marshal" — dropping the trailing bytes. Same class of silent caller-byte loss the fix exists to stop. My first attempt at this used `decoder.More()`, which turned out to be insufficient — see **Review round**.

**Operator note on #1064:** a scope revoked *before* this change is stored with `expires_at=0`, so `-expires_at` is 0 and it is past grace for any real clock. Those rows are reclaimed on the first `Expire` pass after upgrade, which is what drains an already-wedged store.

## Review round (Devin Review, both fixed in `72a22fe`)

Both findings were verified against the source before changing anything, and both were real.

1. 🔴 **`decoder.More()` is not a trailing-input check.** It answers "is there another element in the current array or object", which returns FALSE for a trailing *closing* delimiter — so `{...}]` and `{...}}` still got through the guard I had just added, and still lost that byte. Measured against `json.Unmarshal` across eight inputs: `More()` disagrees on `]`, `}` and `]junk`; a second `Decode` requiring `io.EOF` agrees on all eight. Both helpers now use the `io.EOF` form, with test rows for trailing `]`, `}` and `,`. **This was my own regression** — introduced by the commit fixing the first version of the same problem.
2. 🟡 **An interrupted native install still bypassed the trial guard.** My comment claimed a pending journal "has not pinned anything the child would read yet". That is wrong, and `installNativeAgent`'s own comment says so: it writes the pending journal FIRST, then each host file, and publishes the committed journal LAST. Dying in between leaves a fully applied pinned route with only the pending journal on disk. `nativeRoutePinnedFor` now reads both, and reads them differently — a committed journal is taken at its word, a pending one is resolved against the file itself using the `after_sha256` it already records, which stays agent-agnostic and does not refuse a trial over a stale pending journal whose writes never landed.

Both new test groups were mutation-checked by reverting their fix.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1020** (print mode `claude -p` never reaches the engine): not reproduced — needs a live Claude Pro/Max OAuth session and real provider traffic, which this environment has neither of. The reporter's own hypothesis (print mode may present its MCP tool list differently, failing the per-request recovery proof while eligibility still passes) is the right place to look and is consistent with every counter they published. Needs a maintainer with a subscription session, or a captured request pair.
- **#1051** (Codex `config.toml` stops working): already fixed on `main` by #1055 yesterday. Closeable.
- **#575 / #576** (CJK articles): already fixed on `main` by `5506ba8`. I re-verified all four filed rows on current `main` — every one is byte-identical in and out (`before === after`). Closeable; #576 superseded.
- **#1016 / PR #1018** (browse SIGTERM orphans Chrome): `browse/` is a consumer copy here; source of truth is `JuliusBrussee/caveman-browse`. Belongs there.
- **agent-drift #976, #977, #978, #979, #988, #989, #990, #1021, #1054**: in scope per the standing rules and root `npm test` passes (370/0), but I left the pin bumps out — nine bumps across `agents/profiles/*.json` plus `agent-conformance.yml` is a release-shaped change that would dominate the diff of a bug-fix PR and wants its own conformance run. Flagging rather than bundling.
- Feature requests and design proposals (#1001, #1032, #743, #672, #863, #856, #629, #785, #759, #183, #374, #573, #703, #447, #638, #637, #570, #510, #547, #271, #489, …): triaged only, per the standing rules.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1058** by @AmirF194 — **adopted** (cherry-picked, authorship preserved). Correct, minimal, good tests. Extended with the three sibling sites it did not cover.
- **#1065** by @AmirF194 — **adopted with a fix**: right mechanism, but it collapsed the revocation grace to zero on the recovery path. See above.
- **#1060** by @AmirF194 — **adopted** as-is. Matches `symbols_cgo.go`'s already-correct shape.
- **#1056** by @Dhevenddra — **adopted** as-is. Unusually well-evidenced (MCP spec citation, mutation table). Independently re-verified with their own repro both directions: pre-fix hangs past 10s with the upstream orphaned; post-fix exits at 2315ms with code 143. Merges cleanly onto current `main`, as they predicted.
- **#1047** by @g0GobliN — **no action needed from triage; ready for your review.** Already rebased onto current `main` (`ed37ab1`), scope correctly narrowed after #1015/#1055 landed, validation reported in detail. Deliberately not absorbed — it is self-sufficient and the author is actively iterating, so pulling it in here would only duplicate their work. `mergeable_state` is `unstable`; worth a look at the failing check.
- **#576** by @lg320531124 — **superseded** by `5506ba8` on `main`, which settled the design question the other way (mixed-CJK passes through byte-identically rather than selectively compressing). No action needed from the author.
- **#1052** by @SyN-droMe — **superseded**, already adopted into `main` via #1055.
- **#1041** by @Mehael — **superseded**, already adopted into `main` via #1055.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **A third Devin flag I cannot see.** The review says *"1 flag not posted on this PR by your GitHub settings."* I have no access to it, so it is the one part of that review I have **not** checked. Worth opening [the Devin run](https://app.devin.ai/review/juliusbrussee/caveman/pull/1070) before merging.
2. **#1068, the other half.** The reporter offered a second option: have the trial point the child at its own listener anyway. That means temporarily rewriting the user's agent config, which can strand them in a broken state if the trial dies mid-run — a product decision, not a bug fix, so I did not take it. Also still open: a trial that captured nothing should not render its emptiness in the same typography as a measurement (`Requests 0 / Total cost $0.0000` reads as "caveman found nothing to save"). This PR only stops the trial from reaching that state via native routing.
3. **README wording.** Step 5 recommends `caveman trial -- claude` and step 3 is what turns native routing on, so the README walked readers straight into the refusal. Added one sentence in each of the two places the command appears. No numbers touched — please check the voice.
4. **The trial guard fails open.** An unreadable or corrupt install journal reads as "nothing pinned" and the trial proceeds. That degrades to today's behaviour rather than something worse, and failing closed would block legitimate trials, but it is a deliberate choice worth your eyes.
5. **agent-drift batch** — see above; want those as their own PR?

## Verification

All green, on both build configurations, re-run after the review fixes:

```

node --test tests/*.js                       27 tests,  27 pass, 0 fail
python -m unittest discover -s tests        141 tests, OK
python tests/verify_repo.py                 all local verification checks passed

go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...          all ok
CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ...     all ok
node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs        windows compatibility gate passed
```

title: dfffdfdf
fix(hooks): restore "go (back) to normal mode" deactivation
body:
**Problem**
Saying `go back to normal mode` or `go to normal mode` leaves caveman active. The tracker keeps the mode flag and still injects the per-turn `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full)` reminder on that same turn, so the user gets no feedback that the request was dropped. `back to normal mode`, `switch back to normal mode` and `return to normal mode` all work. README and SKILL.md both promise that `normal mode` turns caveman off.

**Reproduce**
```
D=$(mktemp -d); printf full > "$D/.caveman-active"
echo '{"prompt":"go back to normal mode"}' | CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$D" node src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js
cat "$D/.caveman-active"   # before: "full" (still active)   after: file removed
```
Same result with `go to normal mode`.

**Cause**
Regex introduced in #598. The prompt-initial "normal mode" pattern in `caveman-parse.js` lists `go\s+` and `back\s+to\s+` as separate, mutually exclusive prefixes, so `go back to` matches nothing, and `go to` has no alternative at all. This is a regression: running the tracker from the commit before #598, both phrases deactivated caveman.

**Fix**
Make `back` and `to` independently optional after `go`: `go\s+(back\s+)?(to\s+)?`. One regex change. Mid-sentence mentions (`how do I exit vim normal mode`, `switch from normal mode to debug mode`) still do not deactivate. Both Claude Code and the opencode plugin consume this parser, so both get the fix. `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` regenerated.

**Tests**
New case in `tests/test_caveman_parse.js` fails on `main` and passes here. `npm test`, every `tests/test_*.js`, `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and `tests/verify_repo.py` all pass.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); reproduction and test runs were executed locally.

title: caveman-shrink: "make sure" / "be sure" collapse to "make" / "be" — is dropping "sure" inside those collocations intended?
body:
`src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js` lists `sure` in `PLEASANTRIES`, so it is removed wherever it stands alone. That is right for "Sure, this returns the value", but the same rule fires inside "make sure" and "be sure", where "sure" is not a pleasantry but the verb's object. The result is an instruction with a hole in it.

**Reproduce** (current `main`):
```
node -e 'const {compress}=require("./src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js");
for (const t of ["Make sure the file exists.","Make sure to call init before any other tool.","Be sure to pass an absolute path.","Not sure why this fails."]) console.log(JSON.stringify(t),"=>",JSON.stringify(compress(t).compressed));'
```
```
"Make sure the file exists."                    => "Make file exists."
"Make sure to call init before any other tool." => "Make to call init before any other tool."
"Be sure to pass an absolute path."             => "Be to pass absolute path."
"Not sure why this fails."                      => "Not why this fails."
```

In the first case the meaning is inverted, not just weakened: "Make sure the file exists" is a check, while "Make file exists" reads as "create the file".

**Why it matters**
`compressDescriptionsInPlace` rewrites MCP tool descriptions on `tools/list`, so "Make to call init before any other tool" is what the model reads as the tool's contract. "Make sure to X first" is one of the most common phrasings in tool descriptions (the existing test `compresses real MCP-style description` uses "Please make sure to provide the location as a city name" as its sample input, though it only asserts that "city name" survives). This goes against the spirit of CONTRIBUTING's rule that compressors must never silently corrupt a payload, and it has the same shape as the hyphenated-compound corruption fixed in #1055 (`just-in-time` → `-in-time`): a word that is a filler on its own is not a filler inside a fixed collocation.

**Question**
Is removing "sure" inside "make sure" / "be sure" / "not sure" intended, or should the pleasantry rule skip those collocations (e.g. a negative lookbehind for `make|be|not`, or keeping "sure" only when it is sentence-initial and followed by a comma)? Happy to send a PR with a regression test once the intended behaviour is confirmed. The same question applies to the hedge `might` ("might be null" → "be null"), but that one at least drops a hedge rather than the object of a verb, so I am raising only the "sure" case here.

title: learn: subagent_pressure never fires (spawn tool is now Agent, denominator counts every transcript)

`SessionsScanned` counts every transcript opened, not sessions with turns in the window (5,178 vs about 240 for one 7-day run), so pressure rounds to zero even with detection fixed.
Before repairing the count: is a spawn waste? Delegating to a cheaper model saves cost, and over the same month spawns per session fell while spawns per turn rose.
A measure that separates the two cases: the share of subagent tokens on the parent's tier or a more expensive one, plus the receipt size that re-enters the parent.

title: feat(engine): elide GDScript function bodies without a grammar
body:
## Problem

The code compressor has no GDScript. A Godot project's `.gd` reads pass through untouched in both builds: the cgo build has no GDScript grammar in go-tree-sitter, and the pure-Go build (how the release binaries are compiled, `CGO_ENABLED=0`) handles Go only. In a Godot session that is most of the source the agent reads.

## Change

`engine/compressors/code_gdscript.go`: a line scanner elides named function bodies. GDScript is indentation-scoped, so a body is exactly the run of deeper-indented (or blank) lines after a `func name(...):` header. Only whole body lines go, and one `pass # caveman: body elided` line replaces them, so the file stays valid GDScript and the transform is idempotent.

Handled: `static func`, same-line annotations (`@rpc("any_peer") func ping():`), wrapped parameter lists, inner-class methods, `-> Type` returns, `#` comments and quotes inside parameter lists, triple-quoted strings (never a header, never a boundary), trailing blank lines kept as spacing. Left alone: one-line bodies on the header line, bodies that are only `pass`, lambdas.

Detection (`isGDScript`) needs a marker only GDScript has (`extends`, `class_name`, `@tool`, `@export`, `@onready`, `@icon(`, `signal`), no statement from Go, Python or TypeScript (`package`, `def`, `import`, `from … import`), and one complete header on a single line. Both `Compress` paths route GDScript here before grammar sniffing; `looksLikeCode` already classifies `.gd` as code, and the line-numbered Read-tool form goes through `listing.go` and keeps its gutter.

## Measured

Three real Godot files, o200k tokens:

| file | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| editor history layer (UI, many `@export`s) | 1,229 | 465 |
| logic test, long methods | 2,687 | 73 |
| editor test | 2,057 | 230 |

## Tests

Exact-output test of the shapes above, idempotence, space indentation, blank-line and dedent handling, pass-through cases, rejection of Python/Go/TypeScript/prose, routing through `newCode()` in both builds, and a guttered listing reaching the code compressor through the engine. `go test ./engine/...` passes with cgo and with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.

## Docs

`docs/technical/engine.md`: a paragraph on which languages the code compressor covers in each build.

title: fix(engine): parse React components with the TSX grammar
body:
## Problem

`sniffLanguage` routes anything with `function`, `const`, `=>`, `interface` or `class` to the TypeScript grammar. A React component fails that grammar at its first JSX element, `root.HasError()` is true, and the whole `.tsx` file passes through untouched. Plain `.ts` compresses; `.tsx` never did.

## Change

When the TypeScript parse has errors, retry with the TSX grammar, a superset that go-tree-sitter already ships. `parseClean` folds the parse-and-check step so both attempts and the re-parse guard share one rule: code that does not parse cleanly is never edited.

## Measured

o200k tokens: the test component 183 → 71; a real Expo `App.tsx` 1,474 → 804.

## Tests

`TestCodeTSXReactComponent`: bodies elided, the interface and the exported signature kept, no JSX left. `go test ./engine/...` passes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(engine): compress real-world C++ (ifdef sniff, recovered tokens)
body:
Stacked on #1077: the first commit here is that PR's, because both change the same parse gate in `Compress`. Happy to rebase once either lands.

## Problem

Two things kept a Godot GDExtension, and much other C++, out of the code compressor:

1. `#ifdef`, `#ifndef` and `typedef` all contain "def ", and the Python sniff was `has("def ") && has(":")`, so a guarded C or C++ file was parsed as Python and passed through.
2. Class-body macros without a trailing semicolon (`GDCLASS(X, Y)`) and typed anonymous enums (`enum : int64_t {`) make tree-sitter insert a token. `root.HasError()` was true and the whole file passed through with every method body intact.

## Change

1. The Python signal is now a `def name(` that starts a line.
2. `parseAccepted` replaces the `HasError` gate: no ERROR node anywhere, and MISSING nodes are tolerated only when the invented token is a `;` or a name, because the block structure the elision relies on was parsed from real tokens. A MISSING brace or parenthesis still rejects. The re-parse guard holds the output to at most as many MISSING nodes as the input, so an edit can never make the tree worse.

## Measured

o200k tokens on a real GDExtension: the kernel `.cpp` (1,449 lines, `GDCLASS`, two typed anonymous enums) 18,112 → 3,847. Its header is declarations only and stays 1,065. `register_types.cpp` still passes through: `GDE_EXPORT` in declaration position is a real ERROR node, and that rule is unchanged.

## Tests

`TestSniffIfdefIsNotPython`, `TestCodeCppToleratesRecoveredTokens` (macro line, enum and signatures survive, bodies elided), `TestCodeCppRealErrorsStillPassThrough`. `go test ./engine/...` passes.

title: test(ssrf): read the hijacked CONNECT tunnel from Hijack's buffered reader
body:
## Problem

`TestNewHTTPClient_ProxyConnectTunnelsHTTPSWithoutResolvingTarget` fails at random in engine-ci's `go` job with `CONNECT request failed: Get "https://example.com/v1/models": EOF`, while the origin logs `http: TLS handshake error ... first record does not look like a TLS handshake`. Seen twice out of three runs of the identical engine-only diff on #1078 (runs 35130692891 and 35132609922; run 35130604888 passed). It passes locally 600 out of 600, with and without `-race`.

## Cause

The tunnel handler hijacks the connection after `WriteHeader(200)` and copies client bytes from the bare `net.Conn`, discarding the `*bufio.ReadWriter` that `Hijack` returns. `net/http` keeps a one-byte background read pending on the connection while a handler runs. `Hijack` flushes the 200 first and cancels that read second (`hijackLocked` → `abortPendingRead`, then `if c.r.hasByte` hands the byte over in the returned reader). When the client's TLS ClientHello arrives in that window, its first byte sits in the returned reader, and the copy from the bare conn forwards a record that starts one byte late. The origin rejects it and the client sees EOF.

## Change

Copy from the reader `Hijack` returns instead of the bare conn. One test, no production code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(learn): stop overcounting SessionsScanned and undercounting Agent spawns
body:
`sessionEventConsumer.consume()` called `recordSession()` (SessionsScanned++) on every session's `sessionStart` event, before the per-line `since` cutoff in each source's `scanSession` ever runs. A transcript whose real turns all predate the analysis window still got counted as scanned, so `subagent_pressure = TaskSpawns / SessionsScanned / 5.0` divides by a number much larger than the sessions actually in range and the score component stays near zero regardless of real usage.

Moved the increment to the first turn event a source actually emits inside the window; `sessionStart` no longer counts anything. This is the shared path all five sources go through, so one change covers all of them.

Separately, `source_claude.go`'s `TaskSpawns` only matched `"name":"task"`. The subagent-spawn tool_use block is now named `Agent`, not `task`, so real spawns in a recent transcript went uncounted. Added the second name to the same match.

Added two tests in `source_claude_test.go`: one builds a session whose only turn predates `since` and checks it's excluded from `SessionsScanned`, the other checks an `Agent`-named tool_use block counts as a spawn. Both are red on main. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` are clean at the repo root.

I didn't build a fixture for the other four sources (codex, aider, opencode, gemini); they go through the same `consume()`, so the fix should cover them, but I only exercised claude's.

Fixes #1075

title: caveman learn doesn't work on OpenCode 1.18.31
body:
**What happen**
Caveman learn reports only Claude usage. Not OpenCode.

**Expected**
Read my OpenCode session history.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: $ caveman learn
Got:  caveman learn scanned 38 local Claude Code sessions from the last 30 days.
Result: no repeated token-heavy block appeared in at least 3 sessions, so it has no optimization recommendation yet.
Want:  OpenCode usage stats.
```

**Platform**
caveman 1.3.4
opencode 1.18.31
caveman learn --sources opencode --plain finds 0 sessions
OpenCode database exists at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
caveman doctor opencode reports installed components active but version_probe_failed

**Version / install method**
Installed via install.md

Root Cause
Caveman’s OpenCode learner expects the old file-based store:
~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/.../*.json
Your OpenCode 1.18.31 uses a SQLite database instead:
~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
The database has the session data Caveman needs:
- session: session metadata, directory, provider/model and aggregate token counts
- message: per-message payload and timestamps
- part: text and tool-call payloads
Caveman therefore sees no JSON sessions and silently reports zero OpenCode sessions.

title: OpenCode 2: generated native plugin uses incompatible V1 API
body:
## What happened

The native plugin generated by `caveman enable opencode` fails to load in OpenCode 2.0.5. The installed generator still emits a V1 named export returning a Hooks object.

The matching OpenCode server log entry reports:

```text
2026-09-17T09:01:23.371Z
role=server
ref=err_ac6c5897
message="failed to load plugin"
target=~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman-native.js
cause="PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at [\"default\"])))"
```

The installed `@caveman-ai/cli/dist/index.js` generator contains:

```js
// Contract: @opencode-ai/plugin 1.17.8 Hooks (installed local type source).
export const CavemanNative = async () => ({
  // event, chat.message, experimental.chat.system.transform,
  // tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, experimental.session.compacting, dispose
});
```

An isolated import of the generated file succeeds, but its only export is `CavemanNative`; `typeof module.default` is `undefined`. The failure occurs at plugin-definition validation, before native hooks or Caveman subprocesses run. Both Caveman executables exist, the CLI runs, and the separately configured Caveman MCP server connects successfully.

## Expected

Generate a plugin compatible with the detected OpenCode major version, or report unsupported V2 explicitly instead of installing a plugin that cannot load.

V2 requires a default definition with a stable `id` and `setup(ctx)` or `effect`. Adding a default export alone is insufficient: V1 returned hooks must be ported to domain hook registrations, event subscriptions, and cleanup. A no-op setup would hide the load error without restoring functionality.

Official migration documentation: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1

## Reproduction

1. Use OpenCode 2.0.5 and Caveman CLI 1.3.4.
2. Run `caveman enable opencode`.
3. OpenCode discovers `~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman-native.js` automatically.
4. Inspect the server plugin status and matching server log entry.

## Platform

- Other: OpenCode 2.0.5 on macOS
- Caveman CLI: 1.3.4, installed as `@caveman-ai/cli` in Bun's global packages
- Caveman binary release: bin-v1.1.7
- Installed OpenCode plugin packages: `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode/plugin`; their presence does not translate V1 plugin code

## Suggested fix

Port the generator to the V2 API, preserving prompt/context/compaction hooks, before/after tool processing, event handling, and cleanup. Account for changed event payloads, structured system and tool content, and the `bash` to `shell` tool rename. Add a generated-plugin loading test and focused behavior tests against a supported OpenCode V2 release. If retaining V1 support, use separate implementations or the documented dual-version entrypoint.

title: clearSessionPrev deletes through a symlinked parent with a bare unlinkSync
fix(hooks): delete the per-session prev flag through safeDeleteFlag
body:
`clearSessionPrev` deletes the per-session and legacy prev files with a bare `fs.unlinkSync`, so it follows a parent symlink `safeWriteFlag` would refuse to write through. #1055 already fixed this same write/delete asymmetry for `writeSessionMode`'s legacy mirror by routing it through `safeDeleteFlag`; this does the same for `clearSessionPrev`'s two call sites, both of which had the identical gap.

`safeDeleteFlag` is already exported from `caveman-config.js`, so this is a drop-in swap, no new mechanism.

Added a source-code audit test (holds on every runner) plus a behavioral one that stages a symlinked `.caveman-sessions` dir owned by another uid and asserts the file survives (needs chown privileges, skips otherwise, same pattern as the existing `writeSessionMode` symlink test). Ran the full `tests/test_*.js` suite and `npm test` in Docker across node 18/20/22: my new tests fail on the pre-fix code and pass after, nothing else regressed. `npm test` has 11-16 pre-existing failures on main unrelated to hooks (`profile scope ...`), unaffected by this change either way.

Not touched: `caveman-mode-tracker.js`'s own `removeFlag` (bare `unlinkSync`) is a fallback used only when `caveman-config.js` fails to load or lacks these exports, so it can't call `safeDeleteFlag` from the sibling it's standing in for without duplicating the symlink-safety logic. Leaving it as is unless that's wrong.

Fixes #1085

title: fix(opencode): generate a V2 native plugin on OpenCode 2 hosts
body:
Fixes #1083.

`caveman enable opencode` emitted the V1 hook map on every host. OpenCode 2 rejects it at load time (`PluginModule.LoadError`, missing `default`), confirmed against a live 2.0.5 server log (`ref=err_ac6c5897`), so the native integration is dead on arrival there.

This change probes `opencode --version` at enable time (reusing the existing `nativeHostProbe`/`parsedSemver` helpers) and emits the implementation matching the host major:

- OpenCode 1.x keeps the existing V1 template untouched.
- OpenCode 2+ gets a ported `{ id: "caveman-native", setup(ctx) }` plugin preserving every native capability: session lifecycle, prompt profiling, stable/dynamic context injection, pre/post tool observation, shrink rewrite, and compaction hooks, adapted to domain hook registration, structured system parts and tool results, the `session.compaction.ended` event, and both `bash`/`shell` tool names.
- An unreadable version gets the current API rather than a plugin that cannot load.

Verified:

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; full CLI `build` passes.
- `tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs`: existing OpenCode 1.x test now locks the V1 branch; new test drives the generated V2 plugin end to end (setup registration, event lifecycle, prompt profiling with continuation flags, context injection, shell rewrite, output replacement, compaction, cleanup). Both pass.
- The generated V2 file was also validated against a live OpenCode 2.0.5 server: it loads with the plugin reported `active` and zero load failures (local backport; upstream generator output is byte-equivalent in behavior).
- Two `codex` proxy-spawn tests fail in this sandbox both with and without this change (pre-existing, environmental).

Follow-up, out of scope here: `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` (the `bin/install.js --only opencode` path) is V1-only too and will need its own port.

title: fix(opencode): dual V1/V2 entrypoint for the installer plugin
body:
Stacks on #1087 (this branch contains #1087 plus one commit; merge after #1087). Same root cause as #1083, other install path: the `install.js --only opencode` plugin (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`) was V1-only and fails to load on OpenCode 2 (`PluginModule.LoadError`, missing `default`).

The default export now serves both hosts from one file, following the documented dual-entrypoint shape:

- V2 calls `setup()`: prompt/context domain hooks plus an event subscription. Reinforcement injection grew a parts-aware twin for V2 structured system parts with the same idempotency contract.
- V1 (>= 1.18.29, which supports object entrypoints) calls `server()` with the untouched legacy hook map. Older V1 releases only accept a factory function and cannot load this file; no single file serves all three, and this is noted on the export.
- Flag writes, mode parsing, drift degradation, and the createRequire/caveman-config loading trick are shared and unchanged.

The installer also ships `index.js` (same bytes as `plugin.js`): OpenCode 2 auto-discovers package directories by their `index.js` entrypoint and ignores `package.json` `main`, while 1.x keeps loading the explicit `plugin.js` config entry, so one layout serves both hosts with no version detection. The legacy `plugin` config entry is silent on V2; V2 file entries warn, so the entry keeps pointing at `plugin.js`.

Verified:

- `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs`: 16/16 pass. The behavior suite now drives the V2 hooks (prompt/context/subscription); a new compact test locks the dual shape (`id`/`setup`/`server` plus one legacy round-trip); the installer asserts `index.js` ships byte-identical and uninstall removes it.
- `tests/verify_repo.py` passes.
- Live-verified against OpenCode 2.0.7: the directory plugin loads `active` with zero failures, `setup()` writes the mode flag on session init, and the legacy `plugin` file entry stays silent. Verification scaffold removed afterwards; no live-config changes remain.

title: daily triage 2026-09-18 → 09-20: codex trial route, prev-flag delete guard, OpenCode 2 plugin API, pi skills-root scan, seven probed agent pins
body:
> **Still blocked, now for a third run.** One check is red — `profiles` — and fixing it needs a force-push this run is not permitted to make. Cause, fix, and a locally-verified corrected history are in **Blocked** below. One reply from you unblocks it. Every other check is green.
>
> The 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-20 runs appended fixes rather than opening a second PR (one-PR-per-run rule). New material is marked **[09-19]** / **[09-20]**.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[09-20]** #1092 | `caveman trial -- codex …` built its ephemeral `CODEX_HOME` with the **api-key** route `/w/codex/v1` regardless of how Codex was logged in. Which route is correct is a fact about `~/.codex/auth.json`, but it was a defaulted `codexSubscription = false` parameter each caller had to remember to pass — and only `wrap codex` did. Codex then forwarded the ChatGPT OAuth token to the platform Responses API → `401 Missing scopes: api.responses.write`. | Codex on every OS, both affected doors: `caveman trial` and the bare `caveman wrap` interactive picker. The persistent `caveman enable codex` path was never affected — it calls `detectCodexWrapAuthMode()` itself, which is exactly why the reporter's `doctor codex` said `/chatgpt` and `not_needed` while the trial kept failing. | `packages/cli/tests/codex-subscription-wrap.runtime.mjs` — subscription trial gets `/chatgpt`, api-key trial keeps `/w/codex/v1`, plus a source audit pinning the decision at the choke point | — |
| #1085 | `clearSessionPrev` deleted both prev files with a bare `fs.unlinkSync`, following a symlinked parent that `safeWriteFlag` refuses to write through. #1055 fixed the same asymmetry for `writeSessionMode`'s legacy mirror; the two prev sites never got it. | Every Claude Code host (shared `caveman-config.js`; the opencode plugin loads the same file via `new Function`) | `tests/test_symlink_flag.js` — behavioural (foreign-owned symlinked sessions dir) + source audit that both delete sites use `safeDeleteFlag` | #1086 (adopted), #1041 (already on main via #1055) |
| #1083 | `caveman enable opencode` always emitted the V1 `export const CavemanNative` hook map. OpenCode 2 requires a default export with `id` + `setup`, so the plugin fails validation before any hook runs. **And** an install made on 1.x was never regenerated after the host upgraded to 2.x. | OpenCode 2.x, all OS | `packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs` — V1 on major 1, V2 on major 2 with its `setup()` hooks driven end to end, unknown-version regression, host-upgrade drift + `--fix` | #1087 (adopted) |
| **[09-19]** (no issue filed) | `skills/native-core.md` is the native-pack build source, not a skill, but it sat at the root of `skills/` — which **pi scans wholesale**, reading every direct `.md` child as a skill candidate. It has no frontmatter, so pi warned `description is required` for it under **[Skill conflicts]** on every launch. | Every host that installs caveman as a pi package | `tests/verify_repo.py::verify_skills_root_holds_only_skills` — fails on a loose `skills/*.md` and pins `native_pack.core_source` into a subdirectory | #1043 (adopted) |
| #976 #977 #979 #988 #989 #990 #1021 | `tested_agent_version` lagged released upstream versions. | claude, codex, gemini, kilo, opencode, pi, qwen | verified by `node agents/probe-installed.mjs --require <id>` (strict, no `--allow-newer`) passing for all seven | — |

### [09-20] On the Codex trial route

Three details worth a reviewer's eye.

**The guard went to the choke point, not to the call site.** `buildCodexEphemeralWrapEnv` has exactly **one** caller — `spawnWrapped` — so every ephemeral Codex home in the product flows through one function. Two of the three paths into it never passed the flag: `trial()` calls `spawnWrapped` with five positional arguments, and `wrapInteractive()` (bare `caveman wrap`, agent chosen from the menu) calls `runWrapped` without it, where `runWrapped`'s own `= false` default collapsed *unspecified* into *api-key* before `spawnWrapped` could tell the difference. Both parameters are now optional and the mode is resolved inside `spawnWrapped`, so a caller that forgets gets the right route instead of a silent 401. An explicit value still wins, which is what `wrap` passes.

**It follows an idiom the same function already had.** One line below the new code, `routeDecision` uses exactly this contract: `undefined` means *derive it*, a passed value means *use it*. The Codex flag is now consistent with its neighbour rather than being the one input that punishes callers for omitting it.

**Unknown auth keeps the status quo.** `detectCodexWrapAuthMode()` returns `api-key` when `auth.json` is missing or unreadable, so an unreadable login keeps today's behaviour rather than being handed a route it may not be able to use — the same asymmetry argument as the OpenCode V2 gate in this PR. The existing "missing auth.json" test still passes unchanged, and the api-key trial test pins the other direction so the fix cannot over-correct: the `/v1` in `/w/codex/v1` is load-bearing, since Codex appends `/responses` itself and the proxy's allowlist holds only `/v1/responses`.

### Carried over

**The V2 gate defaults *unknown* to V1, not V2.** #1087 as submitted treated an unreadable version as "current" and emitted V2. `nativeHostProbe` returns `version: null` for an empty, non-zero or unspawnable `opencode --version` — and #1081 records exactly that state on a live OpenCode **1.18.31** host. Only a version that positively reads as major >= 2 opts in.

**Doctor now sees the upgrade path.** `nativeIntegrationStatus` compared journaled bytes and pack version only, so a V1 plugin on a V2 host read as `installed`. It now compares the installed plugin's API against the current host major and marks a mismatch degraded, routing into `caveman doctor opencode --fix`.

**The pin bumps also move the `install` string.** kilo and qwen pin the version a second time in the profile's `install` field. `agents/agents.json` and `packages/cli/src/agents.generated.ts` are regenerated by `agents/compile.mjs`.

No README, `INSTALL.md`, benchmark table, savings percentage or token-reduction number was touched.

## Verification

Re-run in full on 2026-09-20 at head `9502fc2`:

- `npm test` — **383 tests, 0 fail** (13 skipped)
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — 27, 0 fail
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 141, OK
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` — all checks passed (hook checksums matching)
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` — gate passed (also runs the Go suites under the Windows target)
- `packages/cli` — **1094 tests, 1075 pass, 1 fail, 18 skipped** — see below

**The one `packages/cli` failure is named this time, and it is not this PR's.** Yesterday's run reported an unnamed `# fail 1` that vanished on re-run; this is it:

```
not ok 229 - native-hook invalid runtime response and timeout fail open without stdout pollution
  error: 'timeout hook exceeded fail-open budget'
  location: 'packages/cli/tests/hooks.runtime.mjs:181:1'
```

It is a hard wall-clock assertion — `assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 1000)` — on how fast the native hook spawns, connects, times out and fails open. Evidence it is environmental rather than mine:

- Run in isolation at this exact commit, `tests/hooks.runtime.mjs` is **68/68 green**, this test included. It only fails under `--test-concurrency=4` on a loaded container.
- Both the test file and the code it exercises (`packages/cli/src/native-hook-fast.ts`) are **outside this PR's diff entirely** — `git diff origin/main...HEAD` touches neither.
- This PR's change is in `spawnWrapped`'s Codex route resolution, which `runNativeHook` never calls.

I did **not** touch it. A 1-second fail-open budget is a real product contract (hooks must never block the host), so loosening it is a maintainer call, not a green-washing edit — and skipping or quarantining it is off the table. Flagged under **Needs maintainer decision** with the options.

## Blocked: the `profile-contract` check needs a force-push I'm not allowed to make

**Unchanged and unanswered since 2026-09-18 08:01 UTC — now three runs.** `profiles` fails at its **first** step, `agents/check-profile-scope.mjs`. Re-reproduced locally today against the current head:

```
$ node agents/check-profile-scope.mjs $(git rev-parse origin/main) $(git rev-parse HEAD)
profile lane rejects out-of-scope path in commit f13faa2: .github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml
exit=1
```

Entirely my mistake, and genuinely this PR's failure — not flake, not the base branch. The gate requires a commit touching `agents/profiles/*.json` to touch *nothing* but those profiles plus the three generated artifacts. My pin-bump commit `f13faa2` also carried `.github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml` and `packages/cli/tests/qwen-wrap.runtime.mjs`, which the lane rejects — correctly.

The check walks **every commit in `base..head`**, so no commit added on top can clear it; only rewriting `f13faa2` can. I re-read the gate's source again today rather than trusting yesterday's summary, and confirmed there is no append-only escape: a revert commit would itself touch `agents/profiles/*.json` plus the workflow file and be rejected by the same rule, and **merging `main` into this branch would make things worse** — `diff-tree -m` takes the union across merge parents, so the merge commit would surface the profiles *and* the out-of-scope paths and add a second violation. The fix is a two-way split of `f13faa2`, built and verified locally: the resulting tree is **byte-identical** to the current head, `check-profile-scope.mjs` returns `profile commit scope valid`, and the generated-artifact step passes.

**Why I stopped, again.** Splitting an existing commit is a history rewrite, so landing it means `git push --force-with-lease` on this branch. The standing instructions for this scheduled run say *never force-push*, unconditionally, and no reply has arrived to change that. title: Regression: Codex trial with ChatGPT OAuth selects /w/codex/v1 and fails api.responses.write
body:
**What happen**

`caveman trial -- codex exec ...` selects the API-key route for a Codex installation authenticated with ChatGPT OAuth. The trial's ephemeral `CODEX_HOME` uses `http://127.0.0.1:<trial-port>/w/codex/v1`, so the OAuth access token is forwarded to the platform Responses API and rejected with `Missing scopes: api.responses.write`.

This appears related to #1045, but it reproduces on the current stable Caveman release after running the documented repair. The persistent native integration is correct and points at `/chatgpt`; only the trial's ephemeral configuration selects `/w/codex/v1`.

Observed during the trial:

```text
provider: caveman
url: http://127.0.0.1:<trial-port>/w/codex/v1/responses
401 Unauthorized: You have insufficient permissions for this operation.
Missing scopes: api.responses.write.
```

The background model refresh also logs:

```text
GET http://127.0.0.1:<trial-port>/w/codex/v1/models
404 Not Found: Proxy path is not recognized.
```

The trial retries five times, exits without a model response, and produces an inferred report with zero input/output tokens and `insufficient_data`.

**Expected**

For `auth_mode: "chatgpt"`, the trial's ephemeral Codex configuration should use the `/chatgpt` route, preserving the OAuth and `ChatGPT-Account-ID` headers and forwarding to `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`, as described in the wrap documentation and #1045.

`caveman trial -- codex exec ...` should complete without requiring an OpenAI API key or the `api.responses.write` scope.

**Before/after example**

```text
Input: caveman trial -- codex exec 'Reply with exactly: OK'
Got:   /w/codex/v1/responses -> 401 Missing scopes: api.responses.write
Want:  /chatgpt/responses -> successful ChatGPT subscription response
```

**Diagnostics**

```text
@caveman-ai/cli: 1.3.4
binary_release: bin-v1.1.7
Codex: codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.9.2
Codex authentication: Logged in using ChatGPT
Caveman tested Codex version: 0.153.0
version_status: newer_unknown
integration pack: 2.2.0
platform: macOS arm64
```

Before reproducing:

```text
caveman doctor codex
state: installed
drifted: false
pack_current: true
~/.codex/hooks.json: exact true
~/.codex/config.toml: exact true
```

The persistent configuration is already correct:

```toml
model_provider = "caveman"

[model_providers.caveman]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
```

Running the maintainer-recommended repair from #1045 does not change anything:

```text
caveman doctor codex --fix
fix.attempted: true
fix.result: not_needed
```

**Reproduction**

```bash
caveman disable codex
caveman trial -- codex exec 'Reply with exactly: OK'
caveman enable codex
```

The failure reproduced twice with separate trial IDs. The normal Codex session works with the same ChatGPT login when not routed through the trial proxy.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [x] Codex
- [ ] Other

**Version / install method**

Installed with:

```bash
npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli@1.3.4
caveman setup --install
caveman setup --agent-native codex
```

title: evals: quality loss not measured; tokenizer mismatch inflates savings numbers
body:
Been running Caveman across a few different session profiles and wanted to flag two things I think are worth closing before the project scales further — both feel like gaps that could undermine trust in the benchmarks long-term.

**1. Quality is currently untested**

The eval framework measures compression (token delta between terse and skill arms), but the README is explicit that it deliberately does not assess answer accuracy. The 18 exact-answer checks in the proxy benchmark are the only quality gate in the repo.

The README references the March 2026 Adobe/JetBrains work on brevity constraints, but those papers test general LLM behavior under brevity pressure — not Caveman's output specifically. I think there's a real opportunity here to close that gap with something like a small correctness eval: a fixed set of prompts with known ground-truth answers, scored pre- and post-skill. Even 30–50 tasks would be meaningful signal. Would be happy to help design or run that if it'd be useful.

**2. tiktoken undercounts Claude savings**

The benchmarks use OpenAI's tiktoken as an approximation. The ratios between arms hold, but the absolute percentages — the ones in the headline — are Claude-tokenizer figures presented using a GPT-4 tokenizer. On typical code content this tends to overcount tokens slightly for Claude, which means reported savings are inflated by an unknown margin.

Swapping in `anthropic-tokenizer` (or even just running a parallel count with both and publishing the delta) would make the numbers defensible to anyone auditing from the Anthropic side.

Neither of these is a blocker on the core approach — the compression is real and the overhead disclosure is honest. Just think these two things are what stands between "interesting project" and "production-credible tool." Happy to contribute on either front if there's appetite.

title: Claude Code interactive: derived cache epoch gate busts at the system component every turn, 0 tokens compressed across 117 requests
body:
Claude Code interactive: `derivedEpochAllows` busts at the `system` component on every request after the first, so compression is skipped session-wide (0.0% reduction)

## Summary

On Claude Code subscription (OAuth) in **interactive** mode, every request after the first in a
session logs `derived cache epoch prefix diverged; forwarding original bytes` with
`diverging_component_index: 1`. Compression is skipped for the whole session. `caveman stats`
reports `before_tokens == after_tokens` and `saved_tokens: 0` over 117 requests.

This looks like the symptom reported in #1066, which was closed on 2026-09-15 as "Retracted by
author. Original diagnosis was incorrect." There are no comments on that issue, so it is not
possible to tell whether the symptom was invalid or only the explanation was. Filing fresh with
measurements.

It is **not** #1020. There the engine is handed nothing and `compression_tokens_before` stays at 0.
Here `before_tokens` advances to 8,984,616, so the engine is reached — it just returns the input
unchanged because the gate refused the request.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Education, x64
- `@caveman-ai/cli` 1.3.4, `binary_release` bin-v1.1.7
- **proxy binary reports `"version":"dev"`** in `~/.caveman/run/8787.json`, not a tagged release.
  Possibly relevant; flagging in case it changes which code is running.
- Claude Code 2.1.278
- Claude subscription OAuth, no API key — `auth_mode: "subscription"` on every request
- `caveman.yaml`: `mode: compress`, `subscription_compress: live_zone`, `breakpoint_plan: frontier`,
  `toolschema_strip: false`
- `caveman status` → `no off-states — everything the layer can do is on`

## Symptom

`caveman stats --json` totals over 30 days:

```json
"requests": 117,
"input_tokens": 10200906,
"cache_read_tokens": 9481087,
"cache_write_tokens": 717897,
"cache_write_1h_tokens": 717897,
"measured_requests": 103,
"before_tokens": 8984616,
"after_tokens": 8984616,
"saved_tokens": 0,
"observe_would_save_tokens": 0
```

`before_tokens` and `after_tokens` are identical to the byte. 103 requests were measured, so the
comparison path runs; it simply never produces a smaller payload.

## Proxy log

One pair of lines per request, on every request after the first in a session:

```
{"level":"WARN","msg":"derived cache epoch prefix diverged; forwarding original bytes",
 "provider":"anthropic","endpoint":"/v1/messages","diverging_component_index":1}
{"level":"WARN","msg":"session frozen-cache prefix did not extend prior request; possible cache bust",
 "request_id":"...","session_id":"claude:...","diverging_component_index":1}
```

77 occurrences in the log window. The index is always 1.

## Where index 1 points

`proxy/providers/anthropic/content_compress.go:17` — `FrozenPrefixComponents` builds the component
list the gate compares:

- index 0: the literal `"cave.anthropic.frozen-prefix.v1"`
- index 1: the top-level `system` field, raw JSON value bytes
- index 2: `tools`
- index 3 and up: frozen messages below the cache floor

So `diverging_component_index: 1` means the `system` field's bytes differ from the stored ones.

`derivedEpochAllows` (`proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go:869`) is documented as append-only tolerant:
growth re-anchors and is allowed, and only a component that "changed, dropped, or reordered" counts
as drift. The `system` field is therefore not growing between turns — it is changing.

## Suspected mechanism

Claude Code appears to mutate `cache_control` annotations on the system blocks between turns as it
re-anchors its cache breakpoints. This session runs a 1-hour cache TTL
(`cache_write_1h_tokens == cache_write_tokens`), and Claude Code documents that the TTL can drop to
5 minutes under usage overage, so those annotations are not fixed for the life of a session.

Because `FrozenPrefixComponents` hashes the raw JSON value bytes of `system`, a moved or retyped
`cache_control` marker is indistinguishable from a content change, and the gate busts even though
the prose content of the system blocks is unchanged.

If that is right, the fix is to normalise `cache_control` (and any other provider-side cache
annotation) out of the component bytes before hashing, so the comparison sees content only.

I have not captured two consecutive raw request bodies to diff the `system` field directly — that is
the obvious next confirmation step, and I am happy to do it if it helps.

## Ruled out, by measurement

Each of these was changed and the divergence count re-measured:

- `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=0` — measured on interactive traffic across a full Claude Code restart
  (process start confirmed by PID start time). Divergence count rose 70 → 77 in the following
  minute; every request still diverged. #1020's author reports the same flag is not the variable.
- Restarting `caveman-proxy` — the log shows 8 proxy restarts in one afternoon, with divergence
  continuing across every one.
- Restarting Claude Code — divergence timestamps all fall after the new process start time.
- Working directory and the presence of a project `CLAUDE.md` — unchanged behaviour.

## Explicitly NOT ruled out

I tested "hooks disabled" (`--settings '{"hooks":{}}'`) and "MCP disabled"
(`--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`) using `claude -p`, and both still showed
divergence. Per #1020, print mode does not exercise the same path as interactive, so I do not
consider those two results valid evidence either way. They would need re-running interactively.

title: fix(engine): stop non-finite values riding the numeric track
body:
**Problem**

A CSV or logfmt export spells a missing measurement `NaN` — pandas, Postgres `numeric`, R — and `strconv.ParseFloat` accepts it, along with `Inf` and `Infinity`. The value parses without error, so the field stays on the numeric track; every comparison against NaN is false, so the unit neither widens the range nor takes the field off that track.

It is elided into a run `summarizeElided` then describes as `range amount=lo..hi` — a bound that unit does not satisfy — and the compressed table comes out **byte-identical** to the same table holding a clean number in that cell:

```
region,status,note,amount
eu,ok,settled invoice for the quarterly subscription renewal,110
eu,ok,settled invoice for the quarterly subscription renewal,111
eu,ok,settled invoice for the quarterly subscription renewal,112
… 56 rows elided (caveman): all region=eu status=ok; range amount=113..168 …,,,
…
"… caveman: elided rows resemble shown rows and match the stated invariants — answer from this view; if you truly cannot, one broad caveman_retrieve …",,,
```

One of those 56 rows had `amount=NaN`. Nothing in the view says a row had no amount at all, under the contract line that tells the agent to answer from this view rather than recover. That is the claim `invariants.go` opens by forbidding — a marker may never imply a fact it did not verify — and the same shape as #1011.

**Reproduce**

```
go test ./engine/compressors -run 'NonFinite|KeepNumericExtremaIgnoresNonFinite'
```

Three tests, all failing before this change. The end-to-end one prints the two byte-identical outputs on failure.

**Cause**

`ParseFloat` is used as the "is this a number" test at all three sites in the package. It is not that test: it accepts the non-finite spellings, and NaN's comparison behaviour then does the rest.

`keepNumericExtrema` has the same root cause and loses more. It latches `minIndex`/`maxIndex` on the first numeric cell and only displaces them on a strict comparison, so the first NaN in a column pins both ends and no later row can ever move them — the column's real extrema stop being kept, which is that pass's whole job (`[NaN 10 70 30]` keeps only the NaN row). End to end the damage is usually masked, because `keepNonRedundant` runs afterwards and independently rescues outlier rows; I could not build a case where the extrema actually disappear from the output. The defense is switched off in silence either way, which is why it is fixed here rather than reported separately.

**Fix**

One `invariantNumber` helper, used by all three sites, that counts only finite values as numbers. A non-finite value leaves the numeric track and the field falls through to enumeration or coverage, which count every unit (`amount: 500×26 NaN×1`), so the NaN becomes visible instead of vanishing. A run whose values are all `NaN` is still constant and still reported as such — that much is verified. Finite numbers are untouched: `range amount=100..400` still renders exactly as before.

Ten lines of logic, at the one choke point the three callers share.

**Tests**

`TestNonFiniteValuesLeaveTheNumericTrack` (NaN mid-run, NaN last, `Infinity`, `-Inf`, and a NaN in an enumerable run, plus the all-NaN-is-still-constant and finite-numbers-unchanged cases), `TestKeepNumericExtremaIgnoresNonFinite`, and `TestTabularNonFiniteCellIsNotAbsorbedIntoARange`, which pins that a NaN row may not compress to the same bytes as a numeric one. All three fail on `main` and pass here.

`go test ./...` (0 failures across the repo), `npm test` (353 pass, 0 fail), `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (141 tests, OK) and `tests/verify_repo.py` all pass. `gofmt` and `go vet` clean.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the reproduction, the fuzzing pass over the TOON round-trip that ruled out neighbouring defects, and every test run above were executed locally.
