title: Add official support for the nanocoder agent
body:
**What you want**
Add official support for the [nanocoder agent](https://github.com/Nano-Collective/nanocoder
). [Their documentation can be found here](https://docs.nanocollective.org/nanocoder/docs/v1.30.0/).

**Before/after example**
Before:
```
$ caveman nanocoder
not a known agent — use `caveman run -- <cmd>`
```

After:
```
$ caveman nanocoder
```

**Why good**
nanocoder is one of the best agents for working with local LLMs via Ollama and llama-server services. OpenCode, by contrast, has lots of bugs with those services. Support has been broken for a long time. [As one example, see here](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/22132).

It is also unclear to me if `caveman run -- nanocoder` even works.

title: daily triage 2026-09-21→10-01: a plugin statusline badge pinned to a prunable cache path, a corrupted ccr.db killing compression in silence, plus the earlier nine runs
body:
This PR now carries ten triage runs. The 2026-10-01 run appended to it rather than opening a second PR, per the one-open-triage-PR rule. Commits from the first nine runs are unchanged, and the push was a fast-forward — no history rewritten.

**Run 10 is the first run that had to merge `main`.** The PR went `mergeable_state: dirty` when Caveman 3.0.0 (#1121), #1145 and #1148 landed. Three files conflicted; resolving them turned up that **`main` has independently superseded three of this branch's fixes** (#1111, #1117, #1116), and the merge then exposed one pre-existing red gate, two stale test fixtures and a 15-minute CI hang. Two new bugs were reproduced and fixed, both on shipped paths.

> **Two follow-ups landed from a concurrent session after this run's push, and both are verified here rather than taken on trust.** `044f07e` fixes the `profiles` gate the mandatory merge commit broke by design (item 23 from earlier runs, finally firing). `21e2cf0` retargets the SDK middleware concurrency tests at 3.0.0's `_pools`, which ends a 15-minute hang in the `sdk` lane. Details in "Profile lane" and "The sdk lane hang" below.

Also: **the npm registry is reachable from this container for the first time**, which unblocked two things nine runs could not do — `scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` ran end to end as a single command (it passed), and the agent-drift versions were probed.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1147 | A plugin install runs the SessionStart hook from the **versioned** plugin cache, and the statusline nudge built its recommended command from `__dirname`. Nothing ever revisited that path: the nudge is one-shot, `bin/install.js` skips hook wiring in plugin mode, and `pruneOrphanedManagedHooks` deletes a dangling entry rather than repointing it. So a plugin update leaves the badge running the old version's script, and once Claude Code prunes that cache version `bash <missing path>` exits 127 — which hides the entire status bar (#711), with the badge never offered again. | Claude Code plugin installs, every OS; the PowerShell branch takes the same resolver. | 7, 4 confirmed red first. | — |
| #1149 | `engineCompressor.CompressSegment` dropped the engine's error and returned `(segment, 0, 0)`. The gateway reads `tb <= 0` as "nothing to compress", so a recovery store that cannot be written stopped compression **silently**: nothing in `proxy.log`, `caveman status` reporting no off-states, `caveman stats` showing 0 saved against 622M compared. All three sibling methods dropped the same error. | caveman-proxy, every OS, compress and pixel modes. | 4, all confirmed red first. | — |
| *(run 10 collateral)* | `verify_repo.py` was **already red on `origin/main`** — three `read_text()` calls without `encoding=`, which is cp1252 on a Windows runner. Plus two telemetry fixtures and five SDK concurrency tests that the merge turned red. | — | — | — |
| *(runs 1–9, unchanged)* | the nvm-dangling hook paths, the Codex hook ignoring a configured `off`, the shrink hook granting permissions and dropping tool input, a regex literal deleting Codex trust records, an uninstall naming no command, `/caveman-compress` truncating large files, Pi publishing elisions without proving recovery, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` honored nowhere in Go, opencode ChatGPT OAuth misrouted, the local-spend duplicate upload, three concurrency races, the repository-evidence leak, the home-dir walk, the MCP key-order compare, and fifteen conformance pins | — | — | #1138 #1139 #1131 #1130 #1126 #1119 #1110 #1114 #1112 #1116 #1117 #1107 |

### #1147 — the recommended path was version-scoped, so it could not survive its own plugin

@marcoamtz filed this from an install audit at 3.0.0 with all four code paths tabulated, the resolved path spelled out, and both halves separated — then said plainly which part was read rather than run. That is most of the work.

Reproduced first, as the literal string the reporter predicted:

```
bash "/tmp/caveman-nudge-pin-xysmk7gs/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.0.0/src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh"
```

One root cause, two symptoms. The nudge now recommends `<claudeDir>/hooks/<script>` — the version-independent path **the standalone installer already owns** — copying the running plugin's script there first. A plugin update refreshes that copy, so a future change to the script reaches users who accepted the nudge (the reporter's point 1). And a configured `statusLine` whose caveman script is already gone is re-offered, because those users are broken on disk *now* and their one-shot marker is already set (point 2); that re-offer is keyed to the broken command in `.caveman-statusline-stale`, so declining is not re-asked every session.

**Ownership before writing.** The copy happens only when the destination is absent, or holds a caveman script that has drifted. The marker is `.caveman-sessions` — chosen because `verify_repo.py` already pins that string in *both* statusline scripts, so it cannot silently stop matching. A foreign or hand-edited script at that path is left untouched and the nudge falls back to the old `__dirname` behavior; there is a test for exactly that.

**Two things the adversarial re-read caught in my own diff**, both fixed before the commit:

- The first draft scanned for the script path with a whitespace-delimited regex. That truncates `C:\Users\Jane Doe\...` at the space, calls a **live** script missing, and re-nudges every user whose home directory contains a space. It now reads the quoted form first — which is what both recommended commands emit — and has its own test with a space in the fixture path.
- `safeWriteFlag` fails silently by design, so recommending the stable path without reading the bytes back would hand the user a command that may not exist. It reads back and falls through to the old behavior if it did not land.

`.caveman-statusline-stale` is added to all four places that enumerate hook state: `uninstall.sh`, `uninstall.ps1`, `bin/install.js` and `INSTALL.md`.

### #1149 — fail-closed, done correctly, then thrown away one layer up

@marcoamtz again, and the diagnosis is exact down to the line numbers. The engine is right: `store.Put` fails, `Compress` returns a pass-through result **plus** the error, so a caller never receives transformed bytes without a durable handle. The proxy then discarded the error, and `tb <= 0` is indistinguishable from "this block had nothing to compress". The only visible signal anywhere was `cave_ccr_unavailable` from a manual `caveman compress`. It went unnoticed for weeks.

Reproduced with a closed CCR store, which fails `Put` the same way a corrupted one does:

```
healthy store:  before=1745 after=254   (real compression)
closed store:   before=0    after=0     and a dropped "ccr: recovery store is closed"
```

The pass-through is unchanged and still correct. What changed is that it is no longer silent. The warning is throttled to one per minute per compressor, because a broken store fails on **every block of every request** — unthrottled this would bury the rest of `proxy.log`, which is where the reporter went looking first.

**All three siblings, not just the one named.** `CompressSegmentType` and `CompressSegmentQuery` run the same engine path and dropped the same error; a guard on `CompressSegment` alone would have left the typed and query-aware routes silent. `engineCompressor` is the only implementation of these three methods (grepped), so there is no fourth. `NewEngineCompressor`'s signature is unchanged — the logger arrives through `NewEngineCompressorWithLogger`, matching the existing `NewWithReceiptsAndUsage` shape — so no existing call site churned, and a nil logger stays a no-op with a test to prove it.

**Deliberately not here:** the other two halves of the report, a `caveman status` off-state and a `PRAGMA quick_check` in `caveman doctor`. Those are in the CLI, and the reporter is right that quarantining a store live sessions still hold open is a maintainer call. Raised below.

### What `main` already fixed — three of this branch's commits are now redundant

Worth knowing before reviewing the diff, because the merge makes them no-ops rather than removing them:

- **#1111** (async `observe()` starving on the shared executor) — `main`'s `_init_workers` now builds a `_pools` dict with a dedicated `receipt` pool at `max_workers=1`. Same fix, better factored, plus a `retrieve` pool and an `_after_fork` this branch did not have. Took `main`'s side whole.
- **#1117** (shutdown-vs-submit TOCTOU) — `main` solves it without a lock: `executor.submit` raising `RuntimeError` is caught, the slot released, and `_local("closed")` raised, with `self._run` re-checking `_closed` **inside** the worker. That last part covers the already-queued job, which this branch's `_lifecycle_lock` did not. Took `main`'s side whole.
- **#1116** (telemetry watermark claim) — `main`'s own `acquireClaimLock` comment names #1116 and #1132 and says it is shared between them deliberately. The implementation is there and correct.

The two Go conflicts went the other way: `claudeConfigDirOverride()` is kept because it `TrimSpace`s, a strict superset of `main`'s bare `os.Getenv`, and whitespace-only would otherwise build a path relative to the process cwd.

### The two telemetry fixtures, and what they were really hiding

`packages/cli/tests/telemetry.runtime.mjs` auto-merged cleanly and then failed two tests, both expecting 1 and getting 0. Neither was a lock failure — instrumenting it showed the watermark advancing to the real total (1500/300) **under a reclaimed stale lock**, exactly as intended. Two separate causes stacked:

1. `main` raised `TELEMETRY_PROMPT_VERSION` 4 → 5, and `telemetrySendable` refuses a config-sourced yes given under older wording. `main`'s own suite asserts 4 is stale, so 5 is the current value, not a workaround.
2. Both tests read `stub.posts` immediately after `runCli`, and `main`'s rewrite sends from a **detached** sender — so the fire-and-forget POST now lands after the CLI exits. Zero posts, not a wrong claim.

The racing test waits for **both** `command_run` posts and then settles, not one: only the winner carries tokens, so waiting for a single post would let "exactly one of the two may claim the delta" pass merely by reading too early — the inverse of what it exists to prove. Green on three consecutive runs.

**One thing for you, not fixed here:** `main` carries three `promptVersion: 4` fixtures of its own (`telemetry.runtime.mjs` at the opt-out-window, deleted-store and restored-store cases). They are green, but they pass **vacuously** — each asserts the *absence* of a token claim, which a stale consent version guarantees regardless of the behavior under test. Left alone because they are passing and pre-existing; flagged because they are no longer testing what they say.

### The sdk lane hang — the merge's third casualty

`sdk (3.11)`, `sdk (3.12)` and `sdk (3.13)` sat in `python -m pytest -q` for ~15 minutes on the pushed head and were cancelled. Not a flake, and not visible to any suite this run had been running: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` covers `tests/`, not `packages/sdk/python/tests/`.

Reproduced locally — `python -m unittest tests.test_middleware` never finished, hanging in `test_observe_burst_does_not_starve_concurrent_optimize`, with `test_aclose_closes_the_receipt_pool_under_the_same_guard` erroring just before it. Cause is the merge, not either side: five tests arrived with this branch's #1111 and #1117 commits and drive internals `main` replaced — `_executor`, `_slots`, `_receipt_executor`, `_receipt_slots`, `_submit_to`, and `_submit`'s old `(function, *args)` signature. The code conflict was resolved in `main`'s favour; the test file auto-merged cleanly and kept driving the removed shape.

`21e2cf0` retargets all five at `_pools` and keeps every assertion, including the one `main`'s own tests do not make — that a refused submit *releases* its slot, which otherwise bleeds pool capacity one failed call at a time. Two details worth crediting: it sets `max_concurrency=4` to match the 4-receipt burst, noting that with the default 16 workers the test would pass without proving anything; and it found why receipts never reached the transport seam (`_receipt()` drops a receipt with no normalizable scope), which is the part that makes the behavioural half work at all.

I checked that those tests still bite, by mutating the implementation rather than trusting them:

- dropping `slots.release()` and the `closed` mapping from `_submit`'s `RuntimeError` branch → **4 errors**, with the bare `RuntimeError` in the traceback, which is #1117 exactly;
- pointing the `receipt` pool at the `optimize` executor → **`test_observe_burst_does_not_starve_concurrent_optimize` fails**, which is #1111 exactly.

Implementation restored byte-identical to `main` afterwards. 15/15 in 0.2s, from an unbounded hang.

### Profile lane — was blocking, now fixed at the gate

`agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` failed on this head, exit 1, caused entirely by the merge commit:

```
profile lane rejects out-of-scope path in commit c16097d: .claude-plugin/plugin.json
```

The gate walked every commit with `diff-tree -m`, which takes the **union across merge parents** — so a merge commit looked like a commit that touched both a concrete profile *and* 570 other files. The branch has carried profile commits since run 2, which made "carries a pin bump" and "is up to date with `main`" mutually exclusive. That is why runs 2–9 appended without merging and flagged the gate instead of using it; this run could not, because the PR was *conflicting*.

I left this for you rather than relax a CI gate on my own authority. **A separate session then fixed it properly in `044f07e`**, switching `-m` to `-c` — what the commit *authored* rather than what it *inherited*. I verified that independently instead of trusting the commit message:

- The real failing CI invocation (`origin/main` → head) now reports `profile commit scope valid`.
- The anti-smuggling property `-m` existed to protect still holds, and the argument checks out: a path arriving through a merge arrives in *some* commit, `rev-list base..head` walks every one of them, and each is scope-checked alone. Parents ancestral to `base` are `main`'s own content, so there is nothing to conceal. A resolution that genuinely edits a profile still appears under `-c` and still faces the full rule.
- `tests/installer/agent-registry-scope.test.mjs` 18/18, including a guard that resolves conflicting profile edits into a third value with an out-of-scope path in the same commit and asserts it is *still* rejected — and that asserts the merge actually conflicted, so it cannot decay into a test of nothing.
- The `profiles` check is green on GitHub on this head, not just locally.

So no squash merge is needed for this reason any more, and the gate is strictly more useful than before.

### Agent drift — probed, not bumped

The registry is reachable this run, so every pin was compared against it:

| Issue | Agent | Pinned | Registry latest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1096 | claude | 2.1.285 | 2.1.286 |
| #1097 | codex | 0.158.0 | 0.159.3 |
| #1118 | gemini | 0.61.0 | 0.62.0 |
| #1100 | qwen | 0.24.6 | 0.24.7 |
| #1099 | pi | 0.87.1 | 0.99.2 |
| #978 | openclaw | 2026.9.5 | 2026.9.7 |
| #1109 | opencode | 1.18.33 | 1.18.34 |
| #1098 | kilo | 7.8.1 | **7.8.1 — already current** |

**Nothing is bumped, and the reason changed mid-run — the honest one is the second.** When the eight issue comments went out, the profile lane was red and a bump could not have been validated by the lane that exists to validate it. `044f07e` then cleared that, so **those comments are superseded on their stated reason** and this is the current position:

A `npm view` comparison is not a probe. Earlier runs on this branch refused to move a pin to a version nothing in the container had actually run, and that standard is right — the probe checks the *surfaces* each profile drives, not just a version string. This run compared versions only, so bumping would be exactly the on-trust move those runs declined. #1098 needs no bump at all: pinned and latest both read `7.8.1`.

Two have blockers beyond probing: **#1099** is a twelve-minor jump (0.87.1 → 0.99.2), the pin least safe to move without surface checks; **#978** needs Node ≥24.16, which neither the conformance lane nor this runner provides, so no automated run can clear it whatever the pin says.

### Sibling-host checks, run 10

- **#1147**: no other host has a statusline to nudge. opencode's TUI exposes no plugin-writable badge, Gemini and OpenClaw load context files with no hook, and the Codex SessionStart hook (added run 9) emits no nudge — grepped. Hooks live only at `src/hooks/`; `plugins/caveman/` ships none, and `plugin.json` wires `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js`. So `__dirname` always has the statusline script as a sibling, at both real depths: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks/` (where source and target are the same path and nothing is copied) and `<plugin root>/src/hooks/`.
- **#1149**: Go only. The engine's own fail-closed behavior is unchanged; the TS and Python middleware do not share this code path.
- `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` **regenerated** for the `caveman-activate.js` change, same file set, recomputed digests.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1150** (@fabcard) — **could not reproduce; not fixed, and I will not guess at a selector.** `claude.ai` is in the `SITES` map with current selectors, the existing Claude specs pass, and the reporter's indicator appearing means the content script loaded and the host matched. My hypothesis was that `document.execCommand("insertText")` fails on claude.ai's ProseMirror, leaving the un-prefixed send path to fire. I tested it against a **real ProseMirror** instance in Chromium: `execCommand` returned `true` and the prefix landed. ProseMirror turns each `\n` into a paragraph, so the draft came back with five newlines rather than two — and the separator check tolerates that by design (`/^\n{2,}$/`). So the hypothesis is disproven and the branch is not reached that way. Exact diagnostics requested on the issue. One finding for you regardless: `test/provider-harness.html` builds the "Claude" editor as a bare `contenteditable` with `class="ProseMirror"`, so the Claude coverage proves the **selector table**, not the editor's input model — which is why a real-world ProseMirror failure would pass CI.
- **#1152** (canary) — **root-caused, not fixed.** `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.131.0 is installed against `supported_range >=0.124.0 <0.129` (tested through 0.128.0), so the anthropic adapter declares itself incompatible and `requirePeers` throws. The canary is working as designed. Not fixed because widening it is a policy call you have already written down: `versions.test.mjs` says "zero-major next minor may break APIs", so 0.129, 0.130 and 0.131 each need testing, and the claim is published in four synced places — `compatibility.ts`, `versions.test.mjs` (including the hardcoded drift sample), `package.json`'s tested list and its peer range — plus the Python twin. Worth noting the user-facing edge: anyone on `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.129+ gets pass-through with a warning, not compression.
- **#1153** (@sbaudet85) — **not a defect; reporter self-resolved, but the confusion is real and yours.** `caveman --version` reported 1.3.4 after following the 3.0.0 instructions because the repo release is tagged 3.0.0 while `@caveman-ai/cli` is at 2.0.0, and a bun-shimmed `npx` had not replaced the old global install. The reporter's own words are the finding: "I understand the CLI version is now the latest, and actually 3.0.0 is set at the repo level. It's quite confusing." Two version lines under one product name, and the install instructions do not say which one `--version` prints. Raised below.
- **#1125**, **#1136**, **#1127**, **#629** — unchanged from run 9, and still one decision: the level machinery is provably correct, so the only lever is ruleset wording, which is product voice. `evals/` can make a candidate wording reviewable; someone has to say which wording ships.
- **#1030 / #1031** — unchanged. `packages/agent/**` is routed to `caveman-agent-sdk` and is byte-identical to `main` across this whole PR.
- **#1146** (OMP in the README install table) — not investigated this run; it is a docs enhancement and #1036 is the native-integration PR behind it.
- **#1137, the fourth path** — the `caveman-cloud` MCP command. Unchanged from run 9: reproduced by reading, not fixed, reasons below.
- **#1134**, **#1133**, **#1121**, **#1105**, **#1036**, **#1130**, **#1132**, **#1129**, **#1123**, **#1120**, **#733**, **#1054**, **#1104**, **#1124**, **#1078**, **#1126**, **#1111**, **#575**, **#1074**, **#1102**, **#863**, **#1093**, **#1020**, **#1090**: carry a verdict from an earlier run with no new information since.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1138** @drakeo338, **#1139** @g0GobliN — adopted in run 9, cherry-picked with authorship preserved, unchanged here.
- **#1131**, **#1126**, **#1119**, **#1117**, **#1116**, **#1110**, **#1114**, **#1112**, **#1107** — adopted in earlier runs. **#1116 and #1117 are now also in `main` independently** (see above), so those two are redundant either way.
- **#1136** @yunus-tuncbilek — still needs a decision, not changes. Right diagnosis (the reinforcement constrains wording, not answer scope), unreviewable as a diff, and `evals/` is the way to make it reviewable.
- **#1031** @zsltg — adopt, wrong repo for this run.
- **#1129**, **#1122**, **#1078**, **#576**, **#1072**, **#1041**, **#839**, **#1095**, **#1121** — verdicts unchanged from earlier runs.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **Cut a CLI release.** Ten runs. Everything in this PR, plus #1105, #1020, #1090 and half of #1134, reaches zero installed users until `@caveman-ai/cli` ships. #1147 sharpens it the same way #1137 did: the fix repairs a broken badge, and the repair ships in the same unreleased CLI.
2. **Confirm `044f07e`'s gate change is the policy you want** (`profiles` lane, item 23 from earlier runs). It fixes the `-m`/`-c` attribution rather than working around it, I verified the anti-smuggling guard still holds, and the whole lane is green — but it is a CI gate, so the call is yours to ratify.
3. **Two version numbers, one product name** (#1153). Repo 3.0.0 vs `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.0, with `caveman --version` printing the latter and the install docs naming neither. A real user hit it and could not tell whether the upgrade worked.
4. **#1149's other two halves** — a `caveman status` off-state and a `doctor` `PRAGMA quick_check` for the CCR store. The reporter is right that auto-quarantining a store live sessions hold open is your call.
5. **#1152 — widen the Anthropic SDK range, or keep failing closed.** Users on 0.129+ get no compression today. Four synced declarations plus the Python twin; the policy ("zero-major next minor may break APIs") is yours.
6. **#1137's option 1 — make the paths stable, not just detectable.** Unchanged, and #1147 is the same genus one layer up: both are a baked path that outlives what it points at. A single `~/.caveman/runtime/` + stable launcher would answer both.
7. **Three vacuously-passing telemetry fixtures on `main`** (see above). They assert an absence that a stale consent version guarantees.
8. **`packages/sdk/python/tests/` and `packages/middleware/python/tests/` are pytest-only, and nothing in the repo's documented local-verification sequence runs them.** `python -m unittest discover -s tests` covers `tests/` alone, which is how a 15-minute hang reached CI unseen. Worth a line in CONTRIBUTING, or a root target that runs both.
9. **The `caveman-cloud` MCP command bakes a versioned path too** (#1137, fourth row). Unchanged.
10. **#1136 / #1125 / #1127 / #629 are one decision.** Unchanged.
11. **Does Claude Code apply `updatedInput` without a `permissionDecision`?** Unchanged; decides whether shrink compresses on Claude Code at all.
12. **#1133's remaining hole** — permission rules evaluate the *rewritten* text, so a `Bash(git push:*)` deny rule stops matching once the command leads with a resolved caveman path. Unchanged.
13. **Ownership policy when a third party writes inside a caveman block** (#1134). Unchanged.
14. **Telemetry default vs. GDPR** (#1134). Unchanged.
15. **Codex 0.158+ ships `--strict-config`**, which errors on unrecognized `config.toml` fields. Unchanged.
16. **The other two sync lanes still have #1132's shape.** `syncLocalPracticeFindings` and `syncPendingLocalScan` want the same `acquireClaimLock` — which `main` now documents as the shared helper, so this got easier.
17. **Does the control-api dedupe imports server-side?** Unchanged.
18. **#1130 turns compression off on old companions.** Wants a release note.
19. **#1129 — a `RegistrySHA256` rotation.** Unchanged.
20. **#1120 — cgo release variants.** Unchanged.
21. **The streaming compress call has no total wall-clock deadline** (#1131). Unchanged and deliberate.
22. **The compress skill's env surface is undocumented.** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CAVEMAN_MODEL`, `CAVEMAN_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` appear in no `.md`.
23. **Twin implementations that drift silently.** Unchanged, and run 10 adds two instances of the genus: `main` and this branch independently fixing #1111/#1116/#1117, and the extension harness mimicking ProseMirror's class name but not its input model. Possibly worth a general guard.
24. **The proxy↔companion `CAVEMAN_CCR_DB` mismatch.** Unchanged — and #1149 makes it louder, since a wrong DB path is now at least logged.
25. **openclaw needs a Node major the conformance lane does not run.** 2026.9.7 requires Node ≥24.16; the lane and this runner top out at 22.
26. **The openclaw compat oracle still proves against 2026.8.2.** Manual-refresh-only.
27. **#1116's stale-lock reclaim is still not atomic.** Unchanged — and it is `main`'s code now.
28. **`npm test` can silently skip tests and still exit 0.** Reconfirmed: 13 skipped this run.
29. **A deterministic savings harness (#733).** @chenhz01 is holding for your yes.

## Verification

Run 10. The four fixes were verified on `c6fd86c`; every suite below was then re-run on the current head `21e2cf0`, after the two concurrent-session commits landed:

- `npm test` (root) — 429 tests, **0 fail**, 13 skipped
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — **28/28**

title: Per-turn reinforcement is level-blind: /caveman ultra compresses one turn, then drifts back to full
body:
## Summary

`/caveman ultra` compresses exactly one response. Every following turn drifts back to `full`-level output, even though `.caveman-active` correctly holds `ultra`.

## Cause

`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` writes the mode correctly, but the per-turn reinforcement it injects is the same string for every level:

```js
additionalContext: "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (" + activeMode + "). " +
  "Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. " +
  "Code/commits/security: write normal."
```

That is the **full**-level ruleset with the active level's *name* interpolated into it. The rules that actually distinguish `ultra` (`SKILL.md`: "Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once.") never appear.

The only place that emits level-specific rules is `caveman-activate.js`, which filters `SKILL.md` to the active level — but it runs once, at `SessionStart`, for whatever level was active *then*. So after `/caveman ultra`:

- Turn 1 compresses, because the `Skill` tool loaded `SKILL.md` (ultra row included) for that turn.
- Turn 2+ sees only the generic reminder plus a stale `level: full` ruleset still sitting in context, and reverts.

The comment above the reinforcement block states its own intent — "keeps caveman visible in the model's attention on every user message" — which holds for on/off but not for intensity.

## Repro

```
$ echo full > ~/.claude/.caveman-active
$ /caveman ultra          # one terse response
$ <any next prompt>       # back to full-level verbosity
$ cat ~/.claude/.caveman-active
ultra
```

Hook output before the fix, at `ultra`:

```
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra). Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. Code/commits/security: write normal.
```

Identical to the `lite` and `full` output apart from the parenthesised name.

## Fix

Branch `fix/per-turn-reinforcement-level-aware`, 3 files, 55 tests pass (`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`).

- `src/hooks/caveman-config.js` — new `readSkillMd(hookDir)` (the 3-candidate resolution already used by `caveman-activate.js`) and `getLevelRules(modeLabel, hookDir)`, which returns the intensity-table description cell for one level, or `null` when `SKILL.md` is unreadable / the level has no row.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` — append `Level <level>: <rules>` to `additionalContext`, resolving the `wenyan` → `wenyan-full` alias the same way `caveman-activate.js` does. Falls back to the current generic text when `getLevelRules` returns `null`, so a standalone hook install without a skills dir is unaffected.
- `tests/test_mode_tracker.py` — three regression tests: reinforcement carries the active level's rules, two levels produce different reinforcement, `wenyan` resolves to the `wenyan-full` row.

After:

```
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra). Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. Code/commits/security: write normal. Level ultra: Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) — measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch
```

Happy to open this as a PR.

## Related: `SessionStart` clobbers a mid-session level change

Separate but compounding. `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` unconditionally does:

```js
const mode = getDefaultMode();
...
safeWriteFlag(flagPath, mode);
```

The hook matches `startup|resume`, so a resume overwrites a mid-session `/caveman ultra` with the configured default. From `~/.claude/.caveman-mode-log.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":1789926403616,"mode":"ultra","prev":"full"}
{"ts":1789935644569,"mode":"full","prev":"ultra"}
```

Nobody ran `/caveman full` in between. `SKILL.md` promises "Level persist until changed or session end", and a resume is neither. On `resume`, reading the existing flag and preferring it over `getDefaultMode()` would match the documented behavior — filed here rather than patched, since it may be intentional.

## Environment

- caveman `main` @ `0d95a81`, marketplace plugin install
- Claude Code 2.1.278, macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), node via plugin runtime

title: feat(cli): managed Claude wrap names repo and branch as x-cave-tags
body:
## Why

Caveman Cloud's Delivery report joins a coding session's spend to the merged change on `tags['repo']` + `tags['branch']`, and no client sent either. The managed wrap knows both at launch and Claude Code honors `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, so this is the smallest change that makes the join live on real wrap traffic, with no server-side state.

## What

- `wrapWorkTags()` reads `origin` and the current branch once at spawn with hardened git (`git-safe.ts`); a launch outside a repo, without an origin, or on a detached HEAD yields what it can and never fails the wrap.
- Values are printable ASCII without comma or equals (a header value must be a ByteString; the tag list is comma/equals delimited). Anything else drops that tag.
- `repoSlugFromRemote` reduces a **github.com** remote to `owner/name`, the key Cloud's Delivery join uses against pull requests imported from GitHub. Other hosts yield no repo tag so a same-named fork or internal mirror cannot collide. Credentials, ports and `.git` are stripped; the URL itself is never sent.
- `buildWrapEnv` merges `x-cave-tags: repo=…,branch=…` into `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` for **managed Claude Code only**. A user's own `x-cave-tags` keeps its keys.
- Local mode untouched: the local proxy strips every `x-cave-*` header before forwarding. Codex has no custom-header env var. Settings-injected Claude Code (`caveman enable`) cannot set a per-session header; those clients use the gateway's owner-scoped session-context registration (Caveman-Cloud #438).
- README: managed wrap sends repo and branch; a branch name can carry a person's name, and how to opt out.

Fixed per process: a branch switch mid-session lands on the next launch.

## Evidence

- `packages/cli/tests/wrap.runtime.mjs`: **45/45** with real git on PATH. The tag tests call `wrapWorkTags()` directly against temp repositories with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, assert the exact header, and fail if the tag is missing; a non-ASCII branch, a non-GitHub remote, a missing remote and a non-repo directory each get their own assertion.
- Note for the reviewer: this machine's `git`/`pnpm` on PATH are a personal disk-budget shim that refuses under 30 GiB free; the run above used the real binaries.

## Review status

Second review round applied: ASCII-only values, github.com-only slug, deterministic test fixture, privacy disclosure. Independent Opus review of this revision not run by the author.

title: fix(caveman-compress): run-aware inline-code pairing survives mid-line backtick runs
body:
## Problem

A backtick run in the middle of a prose line — e.g. `Put the result inside a ```diff fence.` — is matched by neither `FENCE_OPEN_REGEX` (not at line start) nor `FENCE_MARKER_LINE_REGEX` (not a whole-line marker), so its backticks leak into inline-code pairing. The naive `` `([^`]+)` `` pattern opens a span at the run's trailing backtick and closes it at the next real span's opener, shifting every following pair.

On a real ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md containing that sentence, `extract_inline_codes` produced 42 garbage multi-line "spans" of plain prose. The compressor can never reproduce those, so validation failed on every attempt and the file was permanently uncompressible — same failure family as #820, different leak path (mid-line run instead of indented fence marker).

## Fix

Pair spans the CommonMark way: a span opens with a backtick run and closes with an equal-length run.

```python
return [m.group(2) for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!`)(`+)([^`]+)\1(?!`)", text_without_fences)]
```

An unclosed run matches nothing instead of poisoning downstream pairs. Multi-line spans still extract (the #820 fix's contract), fence stripping and marker blanking are untouched, and the change is applied to both copies (`skills/` and `plugins/caveman/skills/`).

## Tests

New `TestMidLineFenceRun` in `tests/test_validate_inline.py`: pairing unaffected by a mid-line run, self-validation passes, and a span dropped after a mid-line run is still an error. Full suite: 144 tests, OK.

Verified end to end: the previously uncompressible CLAUDE.md now compresses and validates cleanly.

title: fix(proxy): match JSON-escaped session markers; skip home dir and .Trash in repo walk
body:
Two proxy fixes found while running the native Claude Code integration on a machine whose agent sessions start in the home directory.

## 1. Session markers never matched, so no request was exactly correlated

`markerPattern` in `proxy/internal/nativeruntime/marker.go` expected `sid="…" sig="…"` with raw quotes. The marker is injected into a user message and reaches the proxy inside a JSON string, where every quote is `\"`. The regex therefore never matched:

- `StripSessionMarkers` returned no session id and the gateway fell back to `unique_recent_session` / `unique_recent_time_model`;
- receipts reported `not_attested_due_approximate_session_correlation`;
- the prefix monitor logged `session frozen-cache prefix did not extend prior request; possible cache bust` on every request (233 of 233 in one run).

The existing test built an invalid JSON body with unescaped quotes, so the escaped form was never exercised.

Fix: accept the raw and the JSON-escaped form as two full alternatives (RE2 has no backreferences, and an optional backslash would let `sid` and `sig` disagree and leave a stray byte). New test embeds a real marker via `encoding/json`, asserts the id is returned, the body is still valid JSON and no longer contains the marker.

Observed after swapping the binary on a live proxy: `session_correlation_basis` went from `unique_recent_time_model` to `signed_marker` and `cache_bust` from 1 to 0 on the next request.

## 2. Repository intelligence walked the whole home directory, including `~/.Trash`

With cwd = home and no git checkout, `listFiles` in `proxy/internal/repointel/index.go` fell back to `walkFiles` over the entire home tree. A discarded `Xcode.app` in `~/.Trash` then produced "Likely implementation path" items pointing at SDK headers in the trash on every prompt, several hundred tokens of noise per turn.

Fix:
- the home directory is treated as not a repository (`ListingHomeSkipped = "home_directory_not_a_repository"`, no files, no walk), consistent with the comment above `listFiles` that an empty answer must not be reported as a complete map;
- `.trash` is added to `dependencyDirectoryNames` (matched case-folded, so `.Trash` is covered).

Tests cover both: a walk over a temp root must not list `.Trash/x.h`, and `listFiles` with root = HOME (via `t.Setenv`) returns zero files with the new reason. After the change the prompt hook reports "no path claims injected".

## Checks

`go test ./proxy/internal/nativeruntime/... ./proxy/internal/repointel/... ./proxy/internal/gateway/...` passes. Commits are DCO signed.

title: AsyncMiddlewareRuntime.observe() shares optimize()'s executor, so a receipt burst can starve it into a false deadline bypass
body:
`AsyncMiddlewareRuntime.observe()` sends receipts through the same 4-worker
executor as `optimize()`/`ready()`/`retrieve()`, instead of the dedicated
single-worker pool `observe_background()` uses. A burst of concurrent
receipts can occupy all 4 workers long enough that a concurrent `optimize()`
call never gets a worker before its own deadline expires, and bypasses with
`reason="deadline"` without ever attempting its capabilities fetch.

The sync API already isolates this correctly: `MiddlewareRuntime.observe_background()`
submits to its own lazily-created `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`, gated by
a separate semaphore, so receipt traffic can never delay `optimize()`. The
async wrapper's `observe()` instead calls `self._submit(self._runtime.observe, receipt)`,
which goes through `self._executor` (the same pool `optimize()` uses) and
`self._slots`, the shared admission semaphore.

Built and ran this from source (HEAD `3ee70a1`), faking only the HTTP boundary:
4 concurrent `observe()` calls with a slow receipts endpoint occupy all 4
shared workers, and a concurrent `optimize()` call started right after them
comes back `reason="deadline"` in about 2s, its capabilities fetch never even
starting. Routing the same 4 receipts through `observe_background()` instead
leaves `optimize()` unaffected.

title: fix(middleware): isolate async observe() to its own receipt pool
body:
Fixes #1111.

`AsyncMiddlewareRuntime.observe()` was routing through `self._submit()`,
the same 4-worker executor and admission semaphore `optimize()`,
`ready()`, `retrieve()` and `delete_session()` share. A receipt burst
could occupy every worker long enough that a concurrent `optimize()`
call sat queued until its own deadline had already passed, so it never
even reached its capabilities fetch.

`MiddlewareRuntime.observe_background()` already solves this on the
sync side with its own lazily-created single-worker pool and a separate
semaphore. `observe()` now delegates to it directly instead of
duplicating the isolation.

Added `test_observe_burst_does_not_starve_concurrent_optimize`, styled
after the existing `test_queued_work_counts_against_one_deadline`: four
concurrent `observe()` calls hold a fake slow receipts endpoint, then a
concurrent `optimize()` is started and given time to miss its deadline
while queued. Without the fix it comes back `reason="deadline"`; with
observe() isolated, it doesn't. Ran the full `packages/sdk/python` suite
(277 tests) on Python 3.13 in Docker, matching the
`python (packages/sdk/python)` CI job's own install and pytest command.

title: nativeruntime: repository-evidence bookkeeping leaks one entry per session forever
body:
`Runtime.repositoryMaps`, `repositoryEnded` and `repositorySessionRefs` in `proxy/internal/nativeruntime/runtime.go` have no removal path. Every `session.start` with a distinct `(CWD, RepositoryState)` key adds a `repositoryMaps` entry, and `markRepositorySessionEnded`, the only thing that runs on `session.end` for this subsystem, prunes `repositoryWarming` but never touches the other three.

`RepositoryState` is a content hash of git status, so it changes on close to every commit or dirty-tree edit. A long-lived proxy process accumulates one entry per session forever, and each `repositoryMaps` entry holds a full `repointel.Map` (the whole repo's file/symbol graph), not a boolean, so this is not a small leak.

Confirmed on `2fd153c` with `go test ./proxy/internal/nativeruntime/... -run TestRepositoryEvidenceMapsGrowUnbounded -v` against a real `ccr.OpenMemory()` store: after 40 sessions with a failing build and 5 with a real repo, all fully ended, `repositoryMaps=45 repositoryEnded=45 repositorySessionRefs=5`, while `repositoryWarming=0`. `activeSessions` elsewhere in the same file already lazily prunes after 30 minutes for the same reason ("a persistent proxy does not retain them forever when a host disappears without session.end"); these three maps have nothing equivalent.

title: fix(proxy): prune repository-evidence bookkeeping on a lazy timer
body:
`repositoryMaps`, `repositoryEnded` and `repositorySessionRefs` had no removal path. `markRepositorySessionEnded` runs on every `session.end` and only prunes `repositoryWarming`; the other three grow by one entry per session for the life of the process. `RepositoryState` is a content hash of git status, so distinct keys pile up fast, and each `repositoryMaps` entry carries a full `repointel.Map`, not a boolean.

Gives these the same lazy prune `activeSessions` already has a few lines up in `Handle`: `repositoryEnded` now stores a timestamp instead of a bool, `repositoryMapEntry` gets a `lastAccess` stamp touched on create and on every read, and `pruneRepositoryState` sweeps anything idle past 30 minutes on each `Handle` call. `lastAccess` is an `atomic.Int64` rather than going through `repositoryMu` because the two read sites (`repositoryEvidenceContext`, `captureTestImpact`) run on the request path and only hold an `RLock`.

One thing worth flagging: `repositoryMaps` entries can be pruned while a session that built them is still alive but idle past 30 minutes without touching that key again. That just means the next read recomputes the map lazily, same as a fresh session would, not a correctness issue.

Added `TestRepositoryStatePrunedAfterIdleWindow`, which backdates one session's bookkeeping past the window and checks it gets swept while a second, recent session's bookkeeping survives the same pass. `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass; `go build ./...` is clean.

title: fix(cli): lock the telemetry token watermark claim across processes
body:
`telemetryTokenDelta()` reads the prior watermark, then hands a compare to `mutateRawConfig()`, which does its own independent `readFileSync` then `writeFileSync` with no locking. Two `caveman` invocations exiting close together (parallel CI steps, a wrapped child invoking `caveman` itself) can both pass the compare before either commits, so both claim and report the same token delta. The existing comment on this function says the opposite ("whoever writes second sees the watermark already moved and reports nothing"), but nothing enforced it across processes, only within one.

Added a lock file around the read-compare-write so only one process can claim a given delta. A process that cannot get the lock within its own budget reports nothing rather than risk a double count, which matches this function's existing undercount-over-doublecount rule. A lock older than 5s is treated as abandoned by a crashed holder and reclaimed, so a killed process cannot wedge telemetry off permanently.

Impact is scoped to the anonymous, opt-outable token-savings metric, not billing or user data.

## Testing

Added a test that races two CLI invocations against a `config.json` whose write is artificially delayed (a `--require` preload, no application code touched), matching the timing the code's own comment describes. On main both processes claim the delta; with the lock, exactly one does. Full `packages/cli` suite (`npm test`, Node 22, Docker): same 5 failures on main and on this branch, all missing native tooling in the container (`git`, two others unrelated to telemetry), none in `tests/telemetry.runtime.mjs`. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: fix(sdk/python): close the shutdown-vs-submit TOCTOU race in AsyncMiddlewareRuntime
body:
`AsyncMiddlewareRuntime._submit` checks `self._closed`, then later calls `self._executor.submit(...)`, with no lock between the two steps. `_shutdown_now` sets `self._closed = True` and shuts the executor down, also as two separate statements with no lock.

`_shutdown_now` runs on whatever thread calls `MiddlewareRuntime.close()`, which need not be the event loop thread running this view's coroutines: `from_sync()` shares one sync runtime's authority with an async view, and `MiddlewareRuntime.close()` already holds its own `self._lock` when it calls `_async_view._shutdown_now()`. The async side had nothing guarding its own `_closed`/executor pair against that.

If a shutdown lands between `_submit`'s check and its `executor.submit()` call, the check sees `_closed` still `False`, then `executor.submit()` raises a bare `RuntimeError` because the executor is already shut down. That escapes uncaught through `optimize()`, `retrieve()`, `ready()`, `observe()` and `delete_session()`, and from there into every framework adapter, each of which only catches `MiddlewareError`.

Fix: a `threading.Lock` shared by `_shutdown_now`'s set-and-shutdown and `_submit`'s recheck-and-submit, so whichever runs first completes before the other proceeds. `_submit` keeps its cheap unlocked check as a fast path and only takes the lock for the recheck immediately before submitting. `aclose()` now goes through `_shutdown_now()` too, since it also wrote `self._closed` directly, unguarded.

## Verification

Docker, `python:3.13-slim` (matches this package's `requires-python`).

* Two new tests force the race deterministically rather than relying on timing: one runs `_shutdown_now` on a real second thread while `_submit` is paused inside its own call to `executor.submit`, the other closes from inside the semaphore acquire to land the shutdown strictly between `_submit`'s two checks. Both fail with the bare `RuntimeError` on today's `main` and pass on this branch.
* Full `packages/sdk/python` suite: 278 passed (was 277), run three times for flake, plus a coverage run scoped to the changed file: every changed line hit.
* `packages/middleware/python[asgi]` suite, the lightest of the framework extras: 64 passed, 35 skipped for frameworks not installed. Confirms the modified SDK still works for a downstream adapter; the other 11 extras were not run individually, since none of them touch `async_runtime.py` and the change does not alter `_submit`'s public exceptions or return values.
* I have not exercised this under real concurrent access through `MiddlewareRuntime.close()` in production; the two tests above reproduce the exact interleaving directly rather than relying on it happening on its own.

One note for the merge queue: #1103 also touches `async_runtime.py` and `tests/test_middleware.py`, adding a second dedicated executor for `observe()`/receipts. It does not touch the `_closed`/`_shutdown_now` pairing this PR guards, and both PRs append a new test after the same existing one, so landing both will want a small textual rebase, nothing semantic.

title: fix(opencode): support ChatGPT OAuth through subscription proxy
body:
# fix(opencode): support ChatGPT OAuth through subscription proxy

## Summary

Fixes two issues with the native OpenCode integration:

1. ChatGPT OAuth requests configured through Caveman's OpenAI provider route were sent to the standard OpenAI upstream instead of the ChatGPT subscription upstream.
2. Native OpenCode MCP registrations were not recognized by the runtime MCP recovery check.

## ChatGPT OAuth routing

The native OpenCode integration configures the OpenAI provider with:

`/w/opencode/openai/v1`

When OpenCode is authenticated with ChatGPT OAuth, Responses requests sent through this route fail with:

> You have insufficient permissions for this operation. Missing scopes: api.responses.write.

OpenCode includes `ChatGPT-Account-ID` on these requests. The proxy now checks for:

* `POST /openai/v1/responses`
* `x-cave-agent: opencode`
* a non-empty `ChatGPT-Account-ID`

Matching requests are rewritten to `/chatgpt/responses` and passed to the existing ChatGPT subscription handler.

The configured OpenCode provider URL remains `/w/opencode/openai/v1`. Requests that do not meet the conditions above continue through the existing OpenAI proxy path.

I initially tested selecting `/chatgpt` during native installation based on OpenCode's stored credential type. I dropped that approach because it depended on OpenCode's credential storage and would only select the route at install time. Doing the check in the proxy keeps it based on the credential metadata present on the current request.

## Native MCP recovery detection

Native OpenCode setup writes the Caveman MCP registration directly to `opencode.json`. The existing `mcpInstalled()` check only recognized the legacy `~/.caveman/mcp/opencode.json` marker, which native setup does not create.

This caused `caveman status` to report MCP recovery as missing even when the native registration was present.

The OpenCode check now reads the native integration journal and compares the current `mcp.caveman` registration with the registration Caveman installed.

This also keeps the check independent from provider routing state. A provider configuration change does not disable recovery as long as the Caveman MCP registration is still present and matches the owned registration.

## Tests

Added coverage for ChatGPT OAuth routing that verifies:

* matching OpenCode Responses requests use the ChatGPT subscription upstream
* `Authorization` is preserved
* `ChatGPT-Account-ID` is preserved
* `x-cave-agent` is not forwarded upstream
* requests without `ChatGPT-Account-ID` do not match
* requests from another agent do not match
* requests to another route do not match
* non-POST requests do not match

Added native OpenCode MCP coverage that verifies:

* the native MCP registration is recognized without a legacy marker
* provider routing drift does not affect MCP detection
* removing the native MCP registration causes detection to return false

## Verification

Tested on an M5 MacBook Air running macOS Tahoe 26.6.2, with OpenCode Desktop 2.0.14 and ChatGPT OAuth using a ChatGPT Plus subscription.

With OpenCode configured to use the normal Caveman provider URL:

`/w/opencode/openai/v1`

Responses requests completed successfully through the ChatGPT subscription handler.

I also ran a longer OpenCode workload to verify the compression path. Once the request became eligible for compression, the proxy logged multiple successful `/responses` requests with `compressed=true`.

Full Go test suite:

`go test ./... -count=1`

passes.

title: Release binaries compress Go only (CGO_ENABLED=0); please consider cgo variants
body:
The release binaries build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. Without cgo the engine links no tree-sitter, so the compressor elides Go only. Python, TypeScript, C, C++, Rust and Java pass through untouched. Go works because the Go standard library carries a Go parser. Every other language needs tree-sitter, which is C.

I measured what a cgo build of the same code does. Build: tag bin-v1.1.7 plus three pull requests (#1076 GDScript, #1077 TSX, #1078 C++), CGO_ENABLED=1, o200k tokens:

| file | before (o200k) | after (o200k) | cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDExtension kernel .cpp, needs #1078 | 18,112 | 3,847 | 79% |
| GDScript file, needs #1076 | 1,229 | 465 | 62% |
| Python module | 1,391 | 802 | 42% |
| React .tsx component, needs #1077 | 183 | 71 | 61% |
| Go file | 9,991 | 1,949 | 80% |

The Go row is a reference. It compresses in the CGO_ENABLED=0 build too.

I run this cgo build instead of the release binaries, so I rebuild after each release. That works, but it keeps multi-language compression out of the default install, and #1076 and #1078 have no effect without a cgo build.

Would you consider shipping cgo variants next to the current binaries, for some or all of the six targets? If the cross-build is the cost, I can contribute the pipeline. The `zig cc` cross-compiler builds static cgo binaries for all six targets from one Linux runner, and the pure binaries with their signed manifest would stay untouched.

title: fix(store): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the Claude root
body:
## Problem

`caveman learn` reports `0 sessions` for anyone who keeps their Claude Code
config outside `~/.claude` via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

`claudeRoot()` in `proxy/internal/store/config_scan.go` was the only place in
the repo that ignored the variable:

- `packages/cli/src/index.ts:6180` (`claudeConfigDir()`) honors it
- `bin/lib/settings.js:377` honors it
- `INSTALL.md:156` documents `--config-dir` as defaulting to `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
- `docs/install-windows.md:6` reads it

That resolver is the single source for the learn session scan
(`learnSessionSources()`), the retro walk (`learn_retro.go:593`), and the
config-tax scan (`config_scan.go:145`). With the override set, all three read a
directory Claude Code is not using, so learn finds nothing and the operator sees
the empty-state message from #1124.

## Fix

One resolver, one new branch, in the documented order:

1. `CAVEMAN_CLAUDE_ROOT` — Caveman's own override, unchanged and still strongest
2. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — the agent's own convention, now honored
3. `~/.claude` — the existing default

`CAVEMAN_CLAUDE_ROOT` keeps top precedence so the existing suite continues to
read its fixtures rather than a real config dir.

## Tests

New `proxy/internal/store/config_scan_test.go`:

- `TestClaudeRootPrefersCavemanOverride` — pins the existing precedence
- `TestClaudeRootHonorsClaudeConfigDir` — override wins over a populated `$HOME`
- `TestClaudeRootDefaultsToHomeClaude` — default still resolves
- `TestLearnSessionSourceReadsClaudeConfigDir` — end-to-end: a learn session
  source reads a transcript from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`

Reverting the one-hunk fix fails the two override tests, the second with the
reported symptom:

```
--- FAIL: TestLearnSessionSourceReadsClaudeConfigDir
    config_scan_test.go:74: claude sessions = 0, want the 1 transcript under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
```

## Checks

```
go build ./proxy/...
go test ./proxy/internal/...
go vet ./proxy/internal/store/
gofmt -l proxy/internal/store/config_scan.go proxy/internal/store/config_scan_test.go
```

All pass. No new dependencies, no generated artifacts, no boundary changes
(`proxy/` internal only).

## Note for the maintainer

`Store.ImportClaude` (`usage_import.go:65`) has its own inline `~/.claude`
fallback for an empty `--path`, reached by `caveman-proxy usage import claude`.
It is the same defect on a sibling path. I left it alone to keep this PR to the
one behavior reported in #1124 — happy to route it through `claudeRoot()` or
leave it, your call.

title: Tool-call silence rule makes newer Claude models go fully silent on long tasks
body:
With caveman `full` active in Claude Code (desktop app, Claude Opus 5.5), the model runs long multi-tool sequences without any user-facing text. In one session the app had to step in with "The user hasn't heard from you in a while" before the model said anything.

The cause is `skills/caveman/SKILL.md:27`:

> Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call.

Newer models (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1) follow this literally, so a long agentic turn gives the user no signal at all.

I understand the intent from #713 (no step-by-step narration eating tokens). Could the rule allow bounded status text instead of none? For example, line 27 could become:

> Tool calls: no narration of routine steps. Before a multi-step run, one line saying what you're about to do; when done, a short recap. Otherwise, text before a call only to clarify, warn about security or irreversible actions, or resolve ambiguity.

The "No tool-call narration" wording on lines 19 and 45 would need the same change. Another option is to keep the strict version for `ultra` only.

Environment: caveman 2.7.0, Claude Code desktop (Windows), Claude Opus 5.5.

title: Add test-report compressor for JUnit/pytest/Jest
body:
Implements S4 (lossy) compressor that normalizes test report formats (JUnit XML, pytest JSON, Jest JSON) into concise text summaries showing only failures and summary stats.

Detection runs before generic JSON check with tightened heuristics requiring both structural keys for pytest/Jest formats to reduce false positives.

Stack traces are filtered to actual stack frames (lines starting with 'at' or containing file:line patterns) and trimmed (keepHead=3, keepTail=2) for stacks longer than 8 frames to reduce noise while preserving context. This fixes a bug where message lines were treated as stack frames and duplicated in output.

Rotates RegistrySHA256 digest (deliberate ABI break requiring Cave Build lock rebuilds).

Comprehensive test coverage includes:
- Format parsing (JUnit XML single/multi-suite, pytest JSON, Jest JSON)
- Detection (true positives, false positive guards)
- Fail-closed behavior (malformed input, non-UTF8, empty)
- Idempotency and edge cases (all-passed, stack trimming)

title: fix(pi): verify recovery before publishing elisions
body:
Focused follow-up to #1034, as suggested when #1015 adopted that PR's first commit (the SQLite lock fix). This PR contains only the second commit: Pi elision verification, rebased onto current `main`.

## Problem

The Pi extension replaces tool output with an elided view plus a `ccr://` recovery handle as soon as compression succeeds. It never confirms that the handle can be recovered by the MCP companion the model will actually call. When the producer and reader disagree (the lock-loss bug fixed in #1015, a different `CAVEMAN_CCR_DB`, or an unavailable companion), the model gets a handle that `caveman_retrieve` rejects as unknown, and the elided content is lost for that session.

## Changes

- **`caveman_retrieve` gains an optional `verify_only` mode.** It returns the normalized handle, the UTF-8 byte length and the SHA-256 of the stored original. It ignores `query`, errors on unknown handles, and is not a delivery. `caveman-mcp version --json` advertises it as the `recovery_verification` capability.
- **The Pi extension publishes an elision only after verification.** The session recovery client must confirm the advertised handle, the exact byte length and the SHA-256. Otherwise the original tool result is kept unchanged, including non-text blocks.

## Compatibility (the protocol question from #1015)

- Verification is capability-gated. With a companion that does not advertise `recovery_verification`, the extension never sends `verify_only`: older servers might ignore the unknown argument and return a real delivery.
- The trade-off is deliberate. With an older companion, the extension keeps the original output instead of eliding it. Compression resumes once the companion is upgraded. It fails toward lossless output, never toward an unrecoverable handle.
- This is a check at publication time, not a promise that the original will be retained indefinitely.

Rebase note: `main` has since removed the per-session retrieval ledger, so the `verify_only` branch no longer interacts with it, and the MCP README and test were adjusted to match.

## Verification

- **Red:** with the new tests on current `main`'s production code: Go `TestVerificationDoesNotConsumeRecovery` fails, and the Pi extension fails 5 of 122 (publication identity, mismatched/malformed publications, missing capability on old companions, invalid proofs, unavailable recovery).
- **Green:** with the change, the Pi extension passes 122/122 (`npm test`, including build and typecheck). `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass for all 71 packages with tests.
- Before rebasing, the same change was used through the installed OMP tools against a shared live producer: exact recovery at startup, after session replacement and after consumer restart. An unavailable recovery store kept the original output.


## Merging together with #1036

This PR and #1036 each pass CI on their own against `main` and can merge in either order. Whichever merges second needs one extra line, because #1130 adds a required `recovery` argument to `shrinkToolResult` and #1036 adds a new call site for it in `packages/pi-extension/src/runtime.ts`:

```diff
-      const result = await shrinkToolResult(state.bridge, state.id, event);
+      const result = await shrinkToolResult(state.bridge, state.id, event, state.recovery);
```

- If #1130 merges first, #1036 no longer typechecks until that line is added.
- If #1036 merges first, #1130 conflicts on that line; resolve it as above.

Without the argument, #1130's verification never runs on the OMP/Pi runtime path, so compression stays off rather than failing silently. Both PRs' tests already pass with or without the other, and the combined result passes the full Pi suite (127/127), `test:omp` (2/2), and the Go tests. I can push the line to whichever PR goes second if that helps.

title: fix(caveman-compress): stream the SDK call so large files aren't truncated
body:
## Problem

`compress_file()` accepts inputs up to `MAX_FILE_SIZE` (500KB, roughly 125k tokens), but the Anthropic SDK path in `call_claude()` used:

```python
msg = client.messages.create(
    model=os.environ.get("CAVEMAN_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-4-5"),
    max_tokens=8192,
    ...
)
```

A compression of a large file does not fit in 8192 output tokens, and `create()` stops at the cap without raising. The failure is quiet and expensive:

1. the compressed body comes back cut off mid-file
2. `validate()` fails on the missing tail (dropped headings, URLs, code blocks)
3. the retry loop spends **two more paid calls** on `build_fix_prompt()`, which cannot succeed, because the tail was never generated
4. after `MAX_RETRIES` the original is restored, so the user pays three calls for nothing

It hits hardest on exactly the files the skill exists for: a large `CLAUDE.md` or a long notes file.

## Fix

- Switch the SDK path to `messages.stream()` + `get_final_message()`, with the ceiling in a named constant: `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 64000` (the max output of the default `claude-sonnet-4-5`). Tokens arrive as they are generated, so a long call does not trip the request timeout.
- If a response still ends with `stop_reason == "max_tokens"`, raise a `RuntimeError` that says the output was capped and suggests splitting the file. A higher cap moves truncation; it does not remove it. Failing at once is cheaper than two repair calls that cannot work.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow:

- **`CAVEMAN_MODEL` default unchanged.** The cap is the bug; the default model is your call, and users can already override it with the env var.
- CLI fallback path untouched.
- `client` construction (including `CLAUDE_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` from #798) untouched.

## Two things worth a look

- **Models with a lower output limit.** A user who pins `CAVEMAN_MODEL` to a model whose max output is below 64000 (for example `claude-opus-4-0`, 32K) now gets a 400 from the API instead of a silently truncated body. It is loud, but it is a behavior change. I can read the cap from an env var if you prefer.
- **What the timeout bounds.** With streaming, the SDK timeout limits the gap between chunks, not the whole call. A healthy call that streams a large body can run longer than `CLAUDE_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, so a second process waiting on the same file lock can reach `LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS` and give up with `LockTimeoutError`. The holder itself is not affected. I left this as it is: a total wall-clock deadline per call would cap output at what fits in 300s and undo most of this fix. Happy to change it if you see it differently.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_call_claude_streaming.py` (3 tests): the SDK path calls `messages.stream()` and never `messages.create()`; the ceiling is above the old 8192; a `max_tokens` stop raises instead of returning a partial body. Each test fails against the code without the matching fix.
- `FirstTextBlockTests` in `tests/test_compress_safety.py` now mocks `messages.stream()` instead of `messages.create()`. The assertions are unchanged.
- Full suite, as CI runs it: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 144 tests OK.

DCO signed off. `skills/` is an MIT directory per LICENSING.md, so this is inbound = outbound.

title: caveman sync's local-spend watermark has no lock, so two overlapping syncs upload the same rows twice
body:
**What happen**

`syncLocalSavings` (packages/cli/src/index.ts) reads the sync watermark, queries the local spend DB for rows past it, POSTs them to `/api/v1/imports`, and only then writes the new watermark. There's no lock around that read-query-post-write sequence, so two processes that both fire it around the same time (two terminals finishing a `cave wrap` session close together, or two `cave sync` runs) can both read the same watermark before either writes it. Both then fetch the same/overlapping row set and both POST successfully, so the same spend/savings rows get uploaded twice.

It's the same shape as the telemetry watermark race fixed in #1116, just with no guard at all, not even the optimistic check `telemetryTokenDelta` had before that fix.

Ran it: built the CLI in a container, wrote a regression test using the same technique #1116's own test uses (a `--require` preload that delays `fs.writeFileSync` on the watermark file, to widen the exit race), pointed it at `sync.json` instead of `config.json`, seeded 2 rows in the local spend DB, and ran two `caveman sync` processes at once against a stub import endpoint. Both exited 0, both printed "synced 2 spans", the stub got 2 separate POSTs, 4 rows uploaded for 2 real spans.

No idea if the control-api backend dedupes imports server-side by span/trace id since that's not in this repo, so I can't say whether this actually double-counts on a real dashboard, only that the client sends the duplicate POST and the stub accepts both.

**Expected**

Each local spend row makes it to the dashboard exactly once, whichever process happens to sync it.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: two `caveman sync` processes racing, 2 unsynced rows
Got:   both POST the same 2 rows, watermark still ends up correct, but 4 rows landed server-side for 2 real spans
Want:  one process wins the race, the other sees the advanced watermark and sends nothing (or the same lock #1116 already uses)
```

**Platform**

Not tied to a particular wrapped agent, any two concurrent `cave wrap`/`cave sync` invocations trigger it.

**Version / install method**

HEAD `2fd153c6`, built from source.

Happy to send a PR using the same lock as #1116 if that's useful, just say the word.

title: Claude shrink hook: `allow` decision, changed command text and lost input fields
body:
**What happen**

In `compress` mode, the Claude Code `PreToolUse` shrink hook rewrites a Bash command to `<caveman> shrink -- <command>`. The source shows three defects:

1. **Approval.** The hook returns `permissionDecision: "allow"` for each command that its filter accepts. The filter accepts commands that change state, for example `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `kubectl delete`, `aws` and `gh`.
2. **Changed command text.** Permission rules evaluate the rewritten input. A rule such as `Bash(git push:*)` can then stop matching the command. Removing `allow` does not fix this defect.
3. **Lost input fields.** `updatedInput` contains only `command`. The hook reference states that `updatedInput` replaces the whole input. Thus the input loses `timeout`, `run_in_background` and `description`.

I verified the source part of this report. I did not verify the host behavior yet. Each host statement below is a prediction from the Claude Code documentation until the host tests run.

#### 1. The hook returns `allow`

The Claude Code output of `shrinkHook` is:

```ts
{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", updatedInput: { command: rewritten } } }
```

`shouldShrink` accepts a command whose first word is in `SHRINK_ALLOW`:

```
git cargo go npm pnpm yarn pip pip3 pytest make jest vitest tsc eslint mypy ruff pylint mvn gradle
dotnet rspec bundle grep rg ag egrep fgrep find ls tree du df ps docker kubectl terraform helm
aws gcloud az gh
```

The filter rejects shell operators and some streaming flags. It excludes a few first-two-token pairs, for example `git commit`, `docker exec` and `terraform apply`. The pair check reads only the first two tokens, so a global option before the subcommand passes the filter:

- `git -C . commit` passes, although the filter excludes `git commit`.
- `docker --context example exec example id` passes, although the filter excludes `docker exec`.

The streaming pattern rejects `-f`, so `git push -f` does not pass. `git push --force` passes.

The hook reference states that deny and ask rules still apply after a hook returns `allow`. Thus the predicted effect is narrower than "every accepted command runs without a prompt". Where no rule covers the command and the permission mode asks, the `allow` decision can remove that prompt.

The code comment above `shrinkHook` describes the same risk for Codex (#1037). The fix for #1037 removed Codex from the hook. The Claude Code branch still returns `allow`.

#### 2. The rewrite changes the text that rules match

The rewritten command is:

```
'<path to caveman>' shrink -- git push --dry-run origin main
```

The hook reference states that permission rules evaluate the rewritten input. A rule for `Bash(git push:*)` can then stop matching the command. This defect stays after the fix removes `allow`. This report makes no claim about other `PreToolUse` hooks. Matching hooks run in parallel, and the reference does not state that one hook receives the output of another.

I saw this problem in one Claude Code session. That session entered a git worktree through the `EnterWorktree` tool. In it, a plain `git status` was refused with this message:

> This session is isolated in the worktree ..., but this command runs caveman with a git command among its operands: what runs it, and from which directory or root, cannot be read here (name git right after the launcher and its options) ... Refusing to run it

Git worked again after I set `think.mode` to `record`. I did not record the Claude Code version. The component that produced the refusal is not known. The host tests below check if the refusal depends on the rewrite.

#### 3. The rewrite loses input fields

`updatedInput` is `{ command: rewritten }`. The hook reference states that `updatedInput` replaces the whole input. An input with `timeout`, `run_in_background` or `description` loses these fields. This changes how the command runs, not only how rules match it.

**Expected**

- The shrink hook returns no permission decision. The normal permission flow of Claude Code decides.
- Permission rules match the original command. If the host cannot match rules against the original command, the hook does not rewrite it.
- The rewrite copies each input field and changes only `command`.
- Two decisions stay separate: which commands have output that the hook can compress, and which permission decision applies. The hook makes only the first decision.

#### Proposed fix

1. Remove `permissionDecision: "allow"` from the Claude Code output of `shrinkHook`. If the host requires a decision together with `updatedInput`, stop the rewrite for Claude Code, as #1037 did for Codex.
2. Copy the original `tool_input` into `updatedInput` and replace only `command`.
3. Keep rule matching on the rewritten text safe. If the hook cannot do this, do not rewrite commands that a permission rule can cover.
4. Make the filter read the subcommand after global options, or remove the exclusion pairs together with the `allow` decision.

Acceptance criteria, one for each defect:

- Approval: with the hook present, a command without a matching rule gives the same prompt as with the hook absent.
- Rule matching: an ask rule and a deny rule for the original command apply with the hook present.
- Input fields: each input field except `command` is equal before and after the rewrite.
- Filter: tests include global options before the subcommand, for example `git -C . commit`, and flags that write, for example `git diff --output=file`.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: git push --force origin main
Got:   {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow",
        "updatedInput": {"command": "'<path to caveman>' shrink -- git push --force origin main"}}}
Want:  {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
        "updatedInput": {<all original input fields>, "command": "<rewritten command>"}}}
       with no permission decision, and permission rules that still match the original command.
       If the host cannot match rules against the original command, no rewrite.
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

caveman v2.7.0: the global npm CLI `@caveman-ai/cli` with the native Claude Code integration, which writes the `caveman shrink-hook` `PreToolUse` entry into `~/.claude/settings.json`. Source details:

- caveman v2.7.0, plugin cache `caveman/caveman/2.7.0`
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, SHA-256 `83d332977a47d3bc281b3780819519ba779409fa41e04964d59c1f1d4a354d35`
- `SHRINK_ALLOW` at line 13864, `shouldShrink` at lines 13877–13893, and the `shrinkHook` output at line 13940
- `main` on 2026-09-28, with the same code (line numbers on `main` can change).

## Reproduction

### Source part (verified)

Run the extracted `shouldShrink` and `shrinkHook` functions of the pinned file above with simulated input, configuration, executable lookup and output. Do not run the command strings. The source part shows:

- the `allow` decision for `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `kubectl delete`, `aws s3 rm` and `gh repo delete`
- the two filter bypasses above
- an `updatedInput` that contains only `command`

### Host part (not run yet)

Fixture:

- A source repository and a bare destination repository, both new, in a temporary directory.
- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so no user or system Git configuration applies.
- In the local configuration of both repositories: `core.hooksPath` set to an empty directory, `protocol.allow=never` and `protocol.file.allow=always`. Thus no Git hook, remote helper or external transport runs. A local `git push --dry-run` can run a `pre-push` hook, so this control is necessary.
- The command text is `git push --dry-run origin main`, with no `-c` option, because a `-c` option changes the tokens that `shouldShrink` reads.
- Before each case, the fixture makes sure that the remote references are unchanged and the hooks directory is empty.

Record for each run: the Claude Code version, the permission mode, the permission rules and the active hooks.

Conditions. Each condition runs in a new session with the same permission mode and the same rules:

- A: no shrink hook.
- B: the hook as released: `allow` and the rewritten `updatedInput`.
- C: the same rewritten `updatedInput` and no `permissionDecision`.
- D: `allow` and an `updatedInput` equal to the original input.

Comparisons. Each pair changes one thing only:

- Approval defect: B against C, and D against A.
- Rewrite defect: C against A, and B against D.
- Rule matching: the rewrite comparisons, in a case with an ask rule and a case with a deny rule. A case without a matching rule gives evidence only for the approval comparisons.
- Input fields: a separate case whose original input has `command`, `timeout`, `run_in_background` and `description`. It compares the input that the tool receives in C with the original input. The permission cases use an input with `command` only.
- Worktree refusal: the rewrite comparisons in a worktree session. A refusal in B and C, and none in A and D, connects the refusal to the rewrite. It does not name the component that refuses.

For each case and condition, record these items:

- The original command
- The rewritten command
- If a prompt appeared
- If the command ran
- The input fields that the tool received

## Workaround

```bash
caveman config set think.shrink false
caveman doctor claude --fix
```

After these commands, `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `shrink-hook` entry, and the other caveman hooks stay. You can also set `think.mode` to `record`, but that setting turns off all compression.

## Related

- #1037: Codex re-prompts for already-approved commands after the shrink rewrite. The fix removed Codex from the hook.
- #1049: the native install always added the shrink hook. The fix made `think.shrink=false` work. That issue notes that the `allow` decision widens the permission grant on Codex.
