title: Caveman 3.1.0: three skills replace six levels, fix stack, maintenance
body:
## Caveman 3.1.0

Three skills replace six intensity levels, the reviewed fix stack lands, and the repo maintenance that piled up since 3.0.0 comes with it. 106 commits over `main`.

### The skill, rethought for current models

`/caveman` is the voice. `/ultracave` strips the grammar. `/megacave` speaks classical Chinese. Each is a self-contained `skills/<id>/SKILL.md` in the same shape: thesis, persistence, why, numbered rules with bad/good pairs, when to break the rules, pre-send check. Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) is the floor under all three instead of a competing register. The tool-call silence ban becomes one status line per phase (#1127, #1154), and the host harness outranks the skill on when to speak (#1125). `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan*` keep working as aliases; stored sessions migrate on read.

Hooks: mode ids are now `caveman`, `ultracave`, `megacave` (+ one-shots, `off`); legacy values map on every read path; the SessionStart hook injects the active skill whole; per-turn reinforcement is derived from the skill's thesis line; statusline renders `[CAVEMAN]`, `[ULTRACAVE]`, `[MEGACAVE]`; an outdated statusline copy pinned to a plugin-cache path now triggers the repair nudge. The always-on rule copies (IDE rules, opencode AGENTS.md, OpenClaw, extension, cavecrew agents, Codex/Gemini stubs, Codex plugin mirror) are regenerated or hand-synced with a drift test. Design record: `docs/technical/three-skills-refactor.md`.

Evals were rerun on `claude-opus-5-5` with host settings isolated: vs a plain `Answer concisely.` control, median output reduction is caveman 3%, ultracave 35%, megacave 9% (n=10, single run, length only). README and HONEST-NUMBERS cite exactly that. **Owner decision:** the default voice adds little over "be concise" on this model; ultracave carries the savings.

### Fix stack (PRs #1163 #1157 #1158 #1159 #1160 #1161 #1162, merged as one)

Proxy session-marker correlation and silent CCR failures (#1105 #1110 #1149 #1113); engine JSON elision, non-finite cells, shrink sentinel (#1151 #1095); CLI dangling hooks, shrink hook permissions, Codex TOML, Remote Control, opencode OAuth, watermark locks (#1137 #1138 #1133 #1134 #1101 #1119 #1116 #1132); statusline nudge path (#1147); Codex SessionStart honors defaultMode (#185 #1139); caveman-compress streaming/ceiling/pairing (#1131 #1107). #1164 (Pi recovery proof, Pi 1.0.0) is **not** here: it must wait for a `caveman-mcp` binary release.

### Maintenance

- `maintenance/2026-09-20`: `/caveman status`, `defaultMode: "manual"`.
- Contributor PRs merged: #1078 (C++ parse gate), #1076 (GDScript elision), #1156 (syslog severities), #1108 (delete dead `proxy/routing`), #1084 (Grok Build install, closes #547), #1062 (eval snapshot contract).
- Daily-triage remnants cherry-picked: Python encoding fixes, merge scope check, the conformance pin-bump chain (#978 #1096 #1097 #1098 #1099 #1100 #1109 #1118).
- Dependabot: #1144 #1143 #1141 #1140 merged. #1142 (TypeScript 7, @types/node 26) reverted: its own CI was red.
- Pins bumped to v3.1.0 everywhere the shim-security test checks, plus the Gemini and Codex plugin manifests.

### Verification on the final head

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` | 186 tests, OK |
| `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` | all checks pass (mirrors, ZIP, generated embeds, checksums, encodings) |

Two independent Opus reviews ran on the diff (hooks/skills; copies/installer/docs); every confirmed finding is fixed in-branch (`c97f4679`, `2ec71944`, `a098adfa`).

### Release order (user-run; tags and publishes are not agent-runnable here)

1. Merge this PR with a merge commit (not squash), so the stack and contributor PR heads become ancestors and GitHub marks them merged.

title: Add a session token-budget intensity ladder
body:
![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/caveman/session-token-budget/preview.gif)

<video src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/caveman/session-token-budget/out.mp4" controls width="720"></video>

Set a numeric output-token ceiling. As the session or the calendar day spends that ceiling, caveman steps its own intensity up so later turns stay shorter. An explicit `/caveman <level>` pins that level until `/caveman release`. If no budget is configured, behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- A `budget` object in the same config files `getDefaultMode()` already reads, or `CAVEMAN_OUTPUT_BUDGET` plus optional `CAVEMAN_BUDGET_WINDOW=session|day`.
- The ladder uses assistant output tokens from the session transcript. Invalid config fails closed to no budget.
- `/caveman hold`, `/caveman release` / `/caveman auto`, and `/caveman budget` pin, release, or show the ceiling. A one-shot mode still restores, then the ladder applies unless a pin is set.
- `/caveman-stats` prints ceiling, window, used, remaining, and hold state when a budget is configured. It does not add a new savings percentage.
- The statusline can show a short remaining badge. Missing the new hook file leaves the current flag alone.

## Tests

Passed: `tests/test_caveman_budget.js`, `tests/test_caveman_parse.js`, `tests/test_mode_tracker_stdin.js`, `tests/test_repo_local_config.js`, `tests/test_caveman_stats.js`, `tests/test_hook_missing_sibling.js`, `tests/test_symlink_flag.js`, `tests/test_hook_stdin_lifecycle.js`, and `tests/verify_repo.py`.

title: Add an install receipt and last-run revert
body:
![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/caveman/install-receipt/preview.gif)

<video src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/caveman/install-receipt/out.mp4" controls width="720"></video>

After a non-dry-run install, caveman writes a receipt of every file that run actually wrote. `--verify-last` checks that receipt. `--revert-last` undoes only that run. `--uninstall` still wipes every known caveman hook. External package commands are listed on the receipt and are not run during revert.

## What changed

- `bin/lib/install-receipt.js` writes `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/caveman/last-install.json` (mode 0600, symlink refused) with write, merge, fence, and command entries.
- `--verify-last` exits 0 when owned entries match, 1 on drift, and 2 when there is no receipt.
- `--revert-last` walks the receipt in reverse. A created file is deleted only when its hash still matches. A settings merge stays marker-scoped. A fence strips only the marked block.
- `--revert-last` together with `--uninstall` is an error. A successful revert renames the receipt so a second revert does not delete twice.
- A failed receipt write prints `receipt: unavailable` and does not fail an install that already succeeded.

## Tests

Passed: `tests/installer/install-receipt.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/e2e.freshinstall.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/uninstall-safety.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/owned-install.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/skills-global-install.test.mjs`, and `tests/verify_repo.py`.

title: daily triage 2026-10-03: opencode one-shot restore, learn agent roots, seven conformance pins
body:
## Commits

```
b91922b fix(opencode): restore the displaced prose mode after a one-shot mode
a39768c chore(agents): bump seven conformance pins after probing each binary
902d802 ci(agents): move the conformance matrix to the seven probed pins
2b52e65 fix(store): honor GEMINI_CLI_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME for learn's agent roots
d185083 fix(install): remove the opencode one-shot prev file on uninstall
4dde735 fix(agents): pin the kilo and qwen install commands to the probed versions
ce22455 test(cli): derive the qwen pin assertion from the profile
```

The pin bump is three commits because `agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` keeps concrete profile-data commits to profiles plus generated artifacts — the workflow matrix and the CLI test each need their own. Two of the seven commits exist because CI caught defects in my own first pass; both are written up in the comments below rather than quietly squashed.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none filed (found this run) | opencode plugin never implemented the #599 one-shot restore. `applyModeChange` wrote `commit`/`review`/`compress` and nothing ever brought the prose mode back; `experimental.chat.system.transform` skips `INDEPENDENT_MODES`, so one `/caveman-commit` stopped per-turn reinforcement for the rest of the session, self-healing only at the next `session.created`. | opencode, all OS | `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` — displaced mode restored, chained one-shots keep the first target, one-shot from off returns to off | — |
| none filed (introduced by the fix above) | opencode uninstall unlinked `.caveman-active` only. Correct while the plugin wrote no prev file; it does now, so uninstall left state behind — and a stale prev is not inert, a reinstall's first one-shot reads it as that session's return target. | opencode, all OS | `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` — uninstall removes both files | — |
| #1081 | `claudeRoot()`/`codexRoot()` honor their agents' relocation variables; `geminiRoot()`/`opencodeRoot()` did not, so `caveman learn` scanned directories those agents never wrote to and reported zero sessions. Same bug as #1124, two hosts further along; the TypeScript CLI already gets both right. | Gemini CLI + opencode users who set `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` or `XDG_DATA_HOME` (common on Linux) | `proxy/internal/store/agent_roots_test.go` — both overrides, both `$HOME` defaults, `CAVEMAN_*` test overrides still win | #1126 (same class, claude root — already in main) |
| #1170 #1171 #1172 #1173 #1174 #1175 #1177 | Nightly drift reports. Seven are real. | all | existing `agents/compile.mjs` pin/matrix equality gate (#135) | — |
| none filed (introduced by the bump above) | A profile pins its version in **two** places — `tested_agent_version` and its own `install` command. The bump moved the first only. Kilo and qwen are the two profiles whose `install` carries a version, so both claimed a version they did not install. `compile.mjs` never looks at `install`, so only the profile-contract job caught it. | all | `packages/cli/tests/qwen-wrap.runtime.mjs` now derives from the profile instead of asserting literals, matching `kilo-wrap.runtime.mjs` — the derived form is what caught kilo | — |

### How the two behavioural fixes were proven

Not inferred from docs — reproduced against the real binaries.

**opencode one-shot**, same prompt sequence on both hosts (`/caveman` → `/caveman-commit` → `"now fix the parser bug"`):

```
Claude Code : caveman → commit → caveman   (reinforced)
opencode    : caveman → commit → commit    (never reinforced again)
```

**Agent roots**, with isolated `HOME`:

```
gemini 0.62.0    + GEMINI_CLI_HOME=X  -> creates X/.gemini,     $HOME untouched
opencode 1.18.34 + XDG_DATA_HOME=Y    -> creates Y/opencode,    ~/.local/share untouched
```

### Pin bumps

Every new version was installed and probed with the repo's own harness — `node agents/probe-installed.mjs --allow-newer --json` on **Node 24.16.0**, the same Node and the same probe the `pinned-upstream-binary` CI job runs. All seven reported `version_ok=true, help_ok=true` in an isolated `HOME`.

```
claude    2.1.285  -> 2.1.288      kilo      7.8.1    -> 7.8.3
codex     0.158.0  -> 0.160.0      openclaw  2026.9.5 -> 2026.9.8
gemini    0.61.0   -> 0.62.0       opencode  1.18.33  -> 1.18.34
qwen      0.24.6   -> 0.24.7
```

Scope of that claim, stated plainly: the probe checks that each binary launches `--version` and `--help` cleanly in an isolated `HOME`. That is what the pinned-binary CI job checks, and what the existing `verified_by` strings mean. It is not an end-to-end wrap test.

## Triaged, not fixed

**Already fixed in main — these can be closed, no code needed.** Verified by reading main, not by assuming:

- **#1176** `agent-drift: pi`: stale report. `pi.json` is already pinned `1.0.0`. The drift run at 04:37Z predated the 06:45Z merge of #1167, which carried the bump.
- **#1124** Read `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: `claudeRoot()` honors it (`config_scan.go:62`). Ships with the next proxy binary release. The sibling gap this left in `geminiRoot`/`opencodeRoot` is fixed in this PR.
- **#1104** level-blind per-turn reinforcement: the three-skill refactor replaced the shared string with `thesisLine(mode, __dirname)`, read per mode from that mode's own `SKILL.md`. The `SessionStart`-clobbers-a-mid-session-change half is fixed too — `RESET_SOURCES` is `{startup, clear}`, everything else reads the stored mode.
- **#856** show current mode: `/caveman status` exists, read-only, in the shared parser.
- **#447** `defaultMode: "manual"`: in `VALID_DEFAULT_MODES`, covered by `tests/hooks/manual-mode.test.mjs`.
- **#575** CJK articles: `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js:165` short-circuits the whole English rule set on a CJK match before `ARTICLES` can run.
- **#403** caveman-stats on Gemini: `caveman-stats.js` gates on `--host` and refuses to read Claude transcripts as another host's usage; `commands/caveman-stats.toml` points Gemini users at native `/stats`.

**Needs the reporter, or a decision:**

- **#1153** can't upgrade to v3.0.0: not reproduced as a bug — two packages, two version lines. `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman` runs `caveman-installer` (3.x); `caveman --version` reports `@caveman-ai/cli` (2.x), which that command does not upgrade. Real UX gap, but whether the installer should detect and upgrade a stale global CLI is a maintainer call, not a bug fix. Left for you.
- **#1123** `/caveman` unrecognized on Codex: reproduced by inspection. `npx skills add -a codex` installs the skill profile only; nothing writes a Codex prompt file, so `/caveman` is not a command there. `.codex/` is repo-local by design and `bin/install.js` never copies it. Shipping Codex prompt files is a feature, not a fix — flagged below.
- **#278** caveman deletes existing code comments: not reproducible with a test (model behaviour). The skill's rule 5 already covers *writing* comments in plain prose, but nothing says *do not delete comments that are already there*. A one-clause addition to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` rule 5 would close it. Skill prose is yours — proposal only, no edit made.
- **#1150** extension not injecting on claude.ai, **#1105** cache-breakpoint planner, **#1152** middleware canary: not investigated this run.
- **#1054** `agent-drift: hermes` (0.19.1 → 0.21.4): not bumped. Hermes installs from a pinned git commit rather than a release, so clearing it means choosing and probing a new commit — a judgement call, not a version bump.
- **#1016** browse SIGTERM cleanup: `browse/` is a consumer copy; source is `caveman-browse`. Out of scope here.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

**Already merged into main — the seven `stack/*` PRs below are all ancestors of `HEAD` but still show open.** They were merged as a chain through the #1167 release PR, so GitHub never auto-closed them. Each can be closed as merged:

- **#1157** `stack/02-engine-compression`, **#1158** `stack/03`, **#1159** `stack/04`, **#1160** `stack/05`, **#1161** `stack/06`, **#1162** `stack/07`, **#1164** `stack/08` — all merged.

**Superseded by that merged work** (each verified present in main, not assumed):

- **#1151** by @JuliusBrussee — superseded by #1157 (`stack/02`). Note: unlike the rest of the chain this branch is **not** an ancestor of main — 3 commits ahead — so worth a glance before closing.
- **#1095** by @pedrohlmelo — non-finite guard is live at `engine/compressors/invariants.go:197`. Superseded by #1157.
- **#1131** by @s4ff0x — streaming SDK call is live at `compress.py:457`. Superseded by #1161.
- **#1107** by @dilchenko — run-aware inline-code pairing is live at `validate.py:243`. Superseded by #1161.
- **#1136** by @yunus-tuncbilek — the answer-scope sentence is live in `reinforcementForMode`, crediting #1136 by number. Superseded by #1162.
- **#1139** by @g0GobliN — `.codex/codex-sessionstart.js` is in main with its own test. Superseded by #1160.
- **#1130** by @andrebrait — superseded by #1164.

**Superseded by earlier merges:**

- **#1043** by @tkoyama010 — **already merged as `8561a3c`, with your authorship preserved**. The PR just never closed. Nothing left to do.
- **#1041** by @Mehael — adopted in the 2026-09-15 triage PR (#1055); the `accessSync(W_OK)` junction check is live in `safeWriteFlag`/`safeDeleteFlag`.
- **#1072** by @pedrohlmelo — the "go (back) to normal mode" branch is live in `caveman-parse.js:255`.
- **#839** by @bb25see-hash — level-aware reinforcement landed differently (per-mode `thesisLine`) in the three-skill refactor.
- **#987** by @MutugiD — `/caveman status` is in the shared parser.
- **#448** by @zirubak — `manual` default mode is in `VALID_DEFAULT_MODES`.
- **#1126** by @Yi-111-a — `claudeRoot()` honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in main. This PR extends the same treatment to the gemini and opencode roots the PR did not reach.
- **#576** by @lg320531124 — the CJK short-circuit is live in `compress.js`.

Not reviewed this run: every other open PR.

## Needs maintainer decision

- **Seven merged-but-open `stack/*` PRs and ~14 superseded contributor PRs** (listed above). Closing them would cut the open-PR count from 69 to roughly 48 and stop re-triaging them nightly. I never close anything.
- **#1153**: should `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman` detect and upgrade a stale global `@caveman-ai/cli`, or should the two version lines be documented more loudly? The user read 3.0.0 release notes and checked a 2.x binary.
- **#1123 / #573**: Codex slash commands. `commands/*.toml` exist but nothing installs them for a `npx skills add -a codex` user. Feature, not triaged further.
- **#278**: proposed one-clause addition to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` rule 5 — "existing comments are payload too: never delete or shorten a comment you were not asked to change." Not written; skill prose is yours.
- **openclaw raised its Node floor**: `npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.8` fails outright on Node 22 ("install Node … upgrade Node, then retry"). CI pins 24.16.0 so conformance is fine, but users on Node 22 will hit it.
- **Suggested guard, not written**: nothing checks that a profile's own `install` string agrees with its `tested_agent_version`. `agents/compile.mjs` compares the CI matrix only, which is why this PR shipped two stale `install` pins until the contract tests caught them. Three lines in `compile.mjs` would make the next drift bump fail closed instead. Out of scope for a triage run, but it will recur.
- **Cosmetic, not changed:** `safeWriteFlag`'s doc header still says Windows "falls back to verifying the resolved path lives under the user's home directory". The #1041 fix replaced that with a writability check, and the inline comment says so — the header above it now contradicts the code.

## Verification

Reproduced the actual CI jobs locally, not just the root suite — the first round taught me that lesson:

```
npm test                                       0 fail
node --test tests/*.js                         28 tests, 0 fail
python -m unittest discover -s tests           186 tests, OK
python tests/verify_repo.py                    all local verification checks passed
go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...  all ok
node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs           windows compatibility gate passed
agents/check-profile-scope.mjs <main> <head>   profile commit scope valid
agents/compile.mjs + generated-artifact diff   clean
profile-contract test set                      306 pass, 0 fail
npm --prefix packages/cli test                 1133 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped
```

Adversarial review of `git diff origin/main...HEAD` against all six classes. Class 4 caught a defect I had introduced — the opencode uninstall litter — fixed in its own commit rather than shipped with a caveat. No new files, so nothing to add to installer file lists; no `../` chains touched; no README or benchmark numbers changed.

One trap worth knowing: `kilo-wrap.runtime.mjs` fails on a machine that has the real `@kilocode/cli` installed, because it shadows the test's shim on `PATH`. Not a defect and not reachable on CI, which installs no agent CLIs.

title: opencode plugin: work on v1 AND v2 now. one file.
body:
## Summary

Added proper opencode v2 support to plugin and installer.

OpenCode 2 no longer runs plugins built against the v1 API, so the caveman
plugin stopped working there. The previous installer layout made it worse: it
registered `plugins/caveman/plugin.js` in `opencode.json`, and v2 rejects that
entry with `configured plugin path must be a directory`, then skips the plugin.

This PR makes the single plugin file speak both the v1 and v2 plugin APIs, and
updates the installer to place and wire it correctly for whichever major
version is installed.

Refs #1083.

## Changes

**`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`** — one default export, `{ id: 'caveman',
setup, server }`:

- v1: the existing `server()` hooks are unchanged — `event`,
  `chat.message`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`.
- v2: `setup(ctx)` registers `ctx.event.subscribe()`,
  `ctx.session.hook('prompt')`, and
  `ctx.session.hook('context' | 'compaction' | 'generate' | 'title')`.
  Reinforcement is pushed into `event.system` as `SystemPart` objects, not
  strings.
- `setup()` returns early when `ctx.session.hook` is absent, because some v1
  builds call both entrypoints and pass the v1 input to `setup()`.

**`bin/install.js`**:

- Writes a flat shim `plugins/caveman.js`
  (`export { default } from './caveman/plugin.js'`). v2 discovers local
  plugins only as flat files under `plugins/` (`plugins/*.{js,ts}`); it does
  not recurse into a subdirectory.
- Probes `opencode --version` to choose the config shape:
  - v1 → a `plugin` entry pointing at the shim.
  - v2 → no config entry (flat auto-discovery), and stale caveman
    `plugin`/`plugins` entries are pruned so upgrades stop emitting the v2
    warning.
- Uninstall removes the shim and both config keys.

**Docs and tests**: `src/plugins/opencode/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and
`INSTALL.md` updated; `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` extended.

## Verification

- `node --test tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs` — 17 pass.
- `tests/verify_repo.py` and the doc-link tests pass.
- Real binaries, isolated config: both OpenCode `1.18.34` (v1) and `2.0.22`
  (v2) load the installed plugin, write `.caveman-active`, and inject the
  ruleset. No `must be a directory` warning after a v2-native install.
- TUI: the user manually ran every scenario in the TUI testing checklist on
  both v1 and v2, and all passed. The checklist is linked from a comment on
  this PR

## Notes

- #1083 tracks the CLI-generated `caveman-native.js` path, which is already
  version-aware. This PR ports the other path: the repo installer
  (`bin/install.js --only opencode`).

title: docs(readme): rewrite the front door around before/after and measured numbers
body:
## What

Rewrites `README.md` from 653 to ~280 lines, modeled on what made the April 2026 README take off: tagline, before/after first, one install command, big claims backed by named research.

- Headline is now **"why many token when few do trick"** (also in the cite block)
- Header: one-line pitch, stat row (proxy 33.2% fewer input tokens, `caveman browse` 129.8× smaller, Adobe 1.4 to 2.4× cheaper), proof line (Adobe CAVEWOMAN, JetBrains, Elasticsearch Labs, #1 HN, #1 Trending, Primeagen)
- Before/after, then the three skills at 20 / 14 / 13 tokens (megacave line is the `useMemo` rendering, counted with tiktoken o200k)
- **How caveman talks**: the reply structure from `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` (answer first, ASD-STE100 sentences, negations kept, payload verbatim, quiet tool runs, when to break the rules, pre-send check)
- **The numbers**: outside labs table (Adobe, Elastic, JetBrains), one proxy table per file type (file alone through today's compressor + whole-session result from the pinned run), skill eval with the terse control arm, browse and compress
- Plain headings; the rock is the only brand emoji
- Dropped: competitor tables, ecosystem table, telemetry essay (kept as three lines with the opt-out), pixel-mode 61% (no committed source), per-type "target savings" ranges (unmeasured)

`docs/WRAP-BENCHMARK.md` gains a **Per-file compression** section: the six corpus files, regenerated byte for byte (corpus SHA-256 matches the published run), through `engine.Simulate` with the case question as query, on today's engine (`aeb45e2f`) and on the engine at the benchmark run (Caveman-Cloud `630e1572`).

## Things to know

- The Elastic post ("elastic-caveman", Elasticsearch Labs, 2026-04-29) never links this repo, so the README says "remade for Elasticsearch", not "cites".
- The session numbers are from the August 2026 run. That engine only got the JSON file to 8,106 tokens; today's gets it to 281. The caption says so, and the session benchmark has not been re-run on today's engine.
- The per-file files hide one record in 61 to 72 KB of noise, a best case for compression. The caption says your files will vary.

## Checks

- `tests/test_benchmark_contract.py`: 6 passed
- `tests/installer/{docs-plugin-commands,shim-security,slash-commands}.test.mjs`: 21 passed
- `tests/verify_repo.py`: all 22 shipped skills documented, Apache-2.0 line present. Its only local failure is file-encoding warnings in the gitignored `tmp-starcharts/`, which CI never sees

title: daily-triage 2026-10-04 → 10-05: npm 12 install break, @anthropic-ai/sdk range, agent pins, proxy models route
body:
> **2026-10-05 run appended.** This PR was still open, so today's fixes are new commits on the same branch rather than a second PR. Branch was already a fast-forward of `main` (no conflict, no rebase, no force-push). New commits: `8446baa`, `24dcf17`, `98d3577`. Everything below the first table is from the 10-04 run and still stands. ## Fixes | Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | #1187 | The gateway route allowlist is POST-only by design, and no adapter listed a models route, so `GET /v1/models` answered 404 `cave_route_not_found` on every mount. Clients that size their context window from `context_length` fell back to a built-in default — Hermes to 256k against a 1M-context upstream. Added a separate GET-only allowlist (`Base.MetadataRoutes`) plus a passthrough that forwards the catalog read unchanged. | caveman-proxy, every host and OS. Declared for `openai`, `anthropic` and `openaicompat` (bare, prefixed, legacy and named mounts) | `proxy/internal/gateway/models_metadata_route_test.go` — 5 forwarding cases, Anthropic sibling, 4 compat mounts, 8 fail-closed cases, 1 auth-ordering case; plus the compression truth table extended to metadata routes | — | | (no issue; PR #1186, commit 1 of 2) | `createSQLiteFile` publishes the CCR database with `os.Link`, and Android/Termux rejects hard links with EPERM, so the store could not be created there at all. Falls back to `O_EXCL` creation, which keeps the atomic no-overwrite property. | caveman-engine CCR store on Android/Termux; POSIX only (Windows has its own `createSQLiteFile`) | `engine/ccr/sqlite_parent_security_posix_test.go` (contributor's, covering both the fallback and the EEXIST case) | #1186 (commit 1 only — see below) | | (found in review, no issue) | My own first commit's one-trailing-segment rule also matched `/v1/models/{model}:generateContent`. Gemini's **inference** routes live under that exact shape, so on a proxy serving both providers an OpenAI metadata route would have claimed a Gemini method call and answered 200 from the wrong upstream. Colon-bearing segments now excluded. | caveman-proxy, any deployment mounting Gemini alongside an OpenAI-compatible provider | 2 cases added to `TestMetadataRouteStaysFailClosed` | — | ### On #1187, two things worth flagging **The reported cause was real but incomplete.** The issue says `openai.go`'s `Routes` is missing `/v1/models`. True, but adding it there fixes nothing: `Base.MatchRoute` hard-gates on `POST`, so no adapter can match a GET on any path. Both gates had to go, which is why this is a new allowlist rather than one more string in an existing one. **It is deliberately not the main proxy path.** Everything that path does — buffer and inspect a body, plan cache breakpoints, compress, parse usage, price the call, write a spend row — presupposes an inference request. A catalog read has no body, no tokens and no cost, so routing it through there would either fault on the missing body or book a zero-token row, which makes the ledger less truthful rather than more. The test asserts zero spend rows for a metadata read. Fail-closed properties kept, each with a test: matched **after** `Authenticate` so the 401/404 split stays unusable as a route oracle; GET only; exactly one trailing id segment; the compat mounts still validate their decoded path spelling first, so an encoded separator cannot claim another mount's credentials. `gemini` is left alone (its catalog is `GET /v1beta/models` with a different response shape), `azure` likewise (`GET /openai/models?api-version=`), and `bedrock`/`vertex` serve no `/v1/models`-shaped catalog at all. Each needs its own verification run; the reporter's case is served by the three that are declared. The compression truth table now covers metadata routes too, so a future one cannot be registered without an explicit compression decision. I verified that guard bites by adding an undeclared `azure` metadata route and watching the test fail with the right message, then reverting. ### Verification (10-05 run, full suite re-run after the last commit) `npm test` 445 pass / 0 fail / 13 skipped (458) · `node --test tests/*.js` 28/28 · `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 186 OK · `tests/verify_repo.py` clean · `go test ./proxy/... ./engine/... ./shared/...` all pass · `go vet` clean · working tree clean after `test-windows-compat.mjs` regeneration (no-op). One caveat reported honestly: `scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` ends with `error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'node'` and `node_modules missing` in a sub-package. The stated motivation does not need it either: SIGSYS kills the process and is never returned as an errno, so the existing `errors.Is(err, unix.EOPNOTSUPP)` check could not have caught it regardless. The narrow fix is to skip `fchmodat2` on Android specifically. Detail on the thread. - **#745 by @vyrus001**: unchanged — adopted in the 10-04 commits. - **#1014 by @AmirF194**, **#1180 by @stone-w4tch3r**: unchanged from below. ## Needs maintainer decision 1. **#1185: what should `/caveman status` say on a host with no hook?** Today `unknown`, which reads as a broken install to the person who filed it. title: proxy: GET /v1/models returns 404 cave_route_not_found, so clients can't discover context_length (Hermes falls back to 256k)
body:
## Summary

The proxy returns `404 cave_route_not_found` for `GET /v1/models` on agent mounts like `/w/hermes/v1/models`. Clients that read model metadata from `/models` cannot get it. For example, Hermes Agent uses `context_length` from `/models` to size its context window. When the request fails, Hermes falls back to its 256k default. In my setup the upstream model advertises a 1M context, so Hermes runs at about a quarter of the real window.

## Reproduce

Upstream is a custom OpenAI-compatible router (`providers.openai.base_url` in `caveman.yaml`). Hermes is routed by `caveman` install through `http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1`.

```
# upstream direct: 200, model entry has "context_length": 1000000
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://<upstream>/v1/models

# through caveman-proxy: 404
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1/models
{"error":{"type":"cave_gateway_error","code":"cave_route_not_found","message":"Proxy path is not recognized.", ...}}
```

The same 404 also comes back for `/v1/models`, `/openai/v1/models`, `/w/hermes/models` and `/w/hermes/v1/models/<id>`.

Hermes log after this:

```
WARNING agent.model_metadata: Could not determine context length for model 'Main' (base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1) — falling back to 256,000 tokens. Set model.context_length in config.yaml to override.
```

## Cause

In `proxy/providers/openai/openai.go` (main @ 6571943), the OpenAI adapter's `Routes` contains only `chat/completions`, `responses`, `responses/input_tokens` and `embeddings`. It does not include `/v1/models`. `Server.proxy` routes fail-closed (`matchAdapter == nil` returns 404). Because of that, a read-only metadata endpoint that every OpenAI-compatible client expects never reaches the upstream.

## Expected

The proxy should pass `GET /v1/models` (and `GET /v1/models/{id}`) through unchanged to the resolved upstream, with no compression, on both the bare and agent (`/w/<agent>/v1`) mounts. The upstream response, including fields like `context_length`, should come back as-is. Other provider adapters (Anthropic `GET /v1/models`) probably have the same gap.

## Workaround

Pin the context window on the Hermes side:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  - name: caveman
    base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1"
    context_length: 1000000
```

This is hardcoded, so it drifts if the upstream changes.

## Environment

- caveman-proxy `bin-v1.1.6` (installed). The route list on current `main` still has no models route, so newer versions are affected too.
- caveman pack 2.2.0, Hermes integration (`native-hermes-routing`)
- Hermes Agent v0.21.5
- Linux x86_64 (Fedora 44)

title: OpenCode with GitHub Copilot provider: proxy receives no traffic (no github-copilot route)
body:
**What you want**

Proxy support for OpenCode's GitHub Copilot provider. The native OpenCode integration only points the openai and anthropic providers at the proxy, so a user signed in only with GitHub Copilot sends nothing through it. Please add a github-copilot route that the Open- Code integration sets up, the way #1119 added one for ChatGPT OAuth. If Copilot is out of scope, please make `caveman doctor`/`status` warn that the active provider isn't proxied, and say so in the docs.

**Before/after example**

Before: OpenCode signed in with GitHub Copilot only. Proxy is healthy, but Copilot requests skip it. caveman stats shows 0 requests, and doctor reports no problem.

After: Copilot requests go through the proxy and show in caveman stats. If Copilot isn't supported, doctor/status says the active provider isn't proxied

**Why good**

Many users get model access through a GitHub Copilot subscription, often through work, and have no direct provider API key. Right now the proxy silently does nothing for them, which is hard to diagnose. A route would let them use the proxy, and a warning would save them time debugging something that isn't supported

title: fix: resolve CodeQL alerts across engine, proxy and JS
body:
Resolves the 51 open CodeQL alerts: 42 by code changes, 9 dismissed as false positives with the reason recorded on each alert.

## Real issues fixed
- **go/unsafe-quoting (#39)**: `engine/pixel/history_anthropic.go`. The opening-turn preview went unescaped inside the model-facing tombstone, so a `"` in the user's first message could fake the end of the "PRIOR CONTEXT ONLY" wrapper. Now `\` and `"` are escaped. Plain previews are byte-identical (the golden fixture passes). New test: `TestDemoteProtectedHeadTextQuotesPreview`.
- **js/polynomial-redos (#6)**: `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js`. On 40 KB adversarial MCP tool descriptions the protected-span regexes took 0.8–8 s; they now take about 1 ms. Fuzzing old vs new found identical `compress()` output. There is a regression test in `tests/test_mcp_shrink.js`. Not fixed: an unclosed `a(a(a(` run is still quadratic, as it was before this PR.
- **js/incomplete-sanitization (#7)**: the version assert in `mcp-version.runtime.mjs` escaped only dots, so a `+` in a version broke the regex. It now uses `includes`.

## Hardening, same behaviour
- **go/request-forgery (#20, #21)**: the Bedrock Mantle base URL now takes its region from the configured host, never from the `x-cave-aws-region` header. `resolveRegion` already rejected a mismatched header in that branch, so the result is the same.
- **go/reflected-xss (#37)**: `countingWriter.Write` is now the unexported `write`, which removes a spurious `io.Writer` call-graph edge. Its only caller is `copyFlush`.
- **go/incorrect-integer-conversion (#22–36)**: the guards are rewritten as `x < 0 || x > math.MaxInt`. This matches the old `uint64` comparison exactly, including on 32-bit.
- **go/allocation-size-overflow (#40–59)**: removed the arithmetic from capacity hints and used `slices.Concat`, which checks for overflow internally. `render.go` now rejects out-of-range dimensions before allocating; its only caller already clamps them.
- **#9, #10**: the conformance stub returns a fixed error body, and the details still go to `errors`. The Firefox e2e script guards its dynamic call with `typeof`.

## Dismissed as false positives
- **#13–19** (js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization): `provider-compat.ts` and `provider.ts` copy how pi-ai 1.0.0 matches provider URLs, using the same substring checks (`openai-completions.js`). Matching on the hostname would make our copy disagree with Pi. In `openclaw-provider-compat.ts` the check is ORed with an exact-host check, and a match means "don't route", which is the safe direction.
- **#60–61** (go/weak-sensitive-data-hashing): one is a SHA-256 lookup key for random 32-byte bearer tokens, the other is a fingerprint of the redaction-rule regex source. Neither hashes a password, and changing either breaks persisted data.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test -count=1 ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` all pass
- `node tests/test_mcp_shrink.js`: 39 passed
- `packages/cli` tests `mcp-version.runtime.mjs` and `agent-compression-conformance.runtime.mjs` pass
- Reviewed by an independent Opus agent: no regressions. Its three low-severity notes are addressed: the quote-only escape replaces the earlier `strconv.Quote`, which escaped CJK spaces and ZWJ; the conformance failure message now includes the stub errors; the shrink test comment is corrected.
- CodeQL on this PR is the final check that the alerts close.

title: daily triage 10-06 → 10-13: Windows npm .cmd→.exe host probe, opencode routed-provider false warning, Claude third-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, compress TypeError, proxy bearer dedup, agent pins
body:
## Fixes

### 2026-10-13 run

Two commits. A previous daily-triage PR (this one) was still open, so this run
appended rather than opening a second. Nothing force-pushed, and no merge was
needed: `origin/main` (`2e08b91`) was already an ancestor of the branch, so the
push was a fast-forward (`423c01b..1992d3e`).

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1252 | npm's `cmd-shim` wraps a package whose `bin` is a native executable in a payload that is one bare `%*`-terminated line with no interpreter: `"%dp0%\…\opencode.exe"   %*`. The shim parser knew two shapes — a Node script, or another `.cmd`/`.bat` to unwrap — so this matched neither and the resolver threw. **On #1215 and the 10-08 decision.** That run root-caused this and deliberately
did *not* fix it, because preferring the bearer globally would change credential
selection for Anthropic, where `x-api-key` IS the native header. That reservation

second principal — exactly what resolving x-api-key first protects against), and

bearer branch on every other path, so OpenAI-protocol mounts are byte-identical;
anthropic and gemini read a bearer as OAuth pass-through and must not treat a
duplicated API key as one. The upstream still receives exactly one credential.

duplicate-credential case is pinned to the mode it had before. It is inert by

- **A price-freshness gate expired today and is blocking `main` and every PR — this is the one item worth acting on first.** `shared/platform/catalog/catalog_test.go:57` fails any catalog row older than 120 days, and `bedrock/anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0` was verified `2026-06-14`, which is exactly 120 days before today. It takes `typescript`, `go` and `macos` red on this PR, and it reproduces on unmodified `origin/main` (`2e08b91`) in a clean worktree with the identical row and message — all three were green on the previous branch head yesterday. This routine did not touch it: clearing it means publishing a real Bedrock price and a new `verified_at`, which it may not do unmeasured, and AWS pricing is outside this runner's egress. `catalog_test.go:90` also pins that row and date as a fixture, so the catalog row and the fixture move together.
- **Gemini's `.env` route, the one sibling of #1247 left unfixed.** `geminiNativeEnv` appends caveman's marker block after whatever the user already has, so a user-set `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` may be shadowed. Whether it is depends on Gemini CLI's dotenv precedence, which this container cannot observe. If it is last-wins, Gemini needs the same refusal Claude just got; if first-wins, caveman's block is the one being ignored and native Gemini routing has been silently inert for those users. Either answer is worth knowing and needs one run on a real `gemini` binary.
- **Does `caveman wrap` deliberately forward a literal `--` to the agent?** It does today, and it is why qwen's route probe could not be completed: `caveman wrap qwen -- "say ok"` hands qwen `--` as its first argument, and qwen's parser then never sees the positional prompt. `CLAUDE.md` says everything after the agent name goes to the agent verbatim, so this may be intended — but if it is, no caveman documentation should show `wrap <agent> -- <args>`, and if it is not, the separator should be consumed. Not changed either way without your call, since the forwarding rule is written down.
- **Where do the middleware quickstart examples live now?** @andrebrait found `/examples/middleware/quickstart.{py,ts}` returning 404; they are the `curl` first step in both middleware READMEs and are not in this repository or its history. Fixing needs a new home for the files or a different first step, and it touches the same lines as #1244.
- **#1242 / #1243 (carried, unchanged)**: whether the Codex marketplace plugin root moves. @AlexCawl's verification stands unchallenged; `plugins/caveman/**` is outside what this routine edits.
- **#1225 (carried)**: whether `pi` bumps past 1.0.2, given that its `verified_by` rests on a suite bound to a 1.0.2 devDependency.
- **#1237 (carried, sharpened)**: whether the conformance lane rather than a triage container should probe the agents whose Node floor is 24.16.0. This run adds a reason to decide it: a bare `npm i -g openclaw` here does not error, it silently installs a version *older* than the pin, which is the kind of thing that could be mistaken for a passing probe.


### 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-09 runs, condensed — all still open

- **The merge commit `844cf85` still trips the profile-contract gate**, and it cannot be cleared without rewriting a pushed commit. `main..HEAD` rejects `844cf85` alone, over `.github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml`; `844cf85..HEAD` is clean, so every commit from 10-09 onward passes the lane. Re-making just that merge clears the check. Your call.
- **The proxy spend store has no busy retry at all** (`proxy/internal/store/store.go`): byte-identical DSN to mem/CCR but it never calls `RetryOnBusy`, and it wraps its `Open` migration in a bare `db.Exec(schema)` while its own comment says lookups and writes "always contend". Flagged, not fixed — no reproduction and a different concurrency discipline (no `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`).
- **`npm test` can still silently under-report.** Pre-existing and unchanged.
- **Whether Node-24-floored agents should be probed by the conformance lane rather than a triage container** (#1237, #1236). The lane already pins `node-version: "24.16.0"`, exactly the floor openclaw requires.
- **#1206** supported-range policy, **#1225** pi pin, **#1242/#1243** Codex plugin root — all superseded by or restated in the newer sections above.

### Earlier runs (10-06 → 10-08), condensed

Still open from those runs: whether the Codex marketplace plugin root moves (#1242/#1243, which this routine may not edit); whether `pi` bumps past 1.0.2 given its devDependency-bound evidence (#1225); whether the conformance lane rather than this container should probe Node-24-floored agents (#1237); and the feature requests listed above.

## Verification

### 2026-10-13 run

Full suite at `1992d3e`, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (the container
starts with no `node_modules`):

- `npm test` — **568 tests, 555 pass, 0 fail, 13 skipped**. Totals drift between runs in this suite because several cases are environment-gated; an earlier run in the same session reported 587/574/0. Zero failures in both.
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — **28/28**.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — **242 tests, OK**.
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` — **all local verification checks passed**. No `src/hooks/` file changed this run, so `checksums.sha256` needed no regeneration, and this confirms it intact.
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` — **windows compatibility gate passed**. Required this run, not optional: the diff is a path/installer change. (This also runs the Go suites, all `ok`.)
- `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` — not run separately: **no Go file changed this run**, and the windows gate exercised them anyway.
- `packages/cli` — **1184 tests, 1166 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped**.
- `packages/pi-extension` — **132/132**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli` — clean.

One failure appeared in the first `packages/cli` run and was chased rather than
retried blind: `cloud MCP telemetry carries only closed tool outcome fields`
(`agent-mcp.runtime.mjs:246`, `telemetry.find(...)` undefined — the detached
telemetry POST had not landed). It passes in isolation, passed on two
subsequent full runs, and nothing in this diff touches telemetry or MCP. Logged
as a concurrency flake, not a result.

Adversarial pass over this run's two commits, by review class:

1. **Path resolution** — no `../` chain and no `path.join(__dirname, …)` added or moved anywhere in the diff (grepped). The shim resolver still resolves a relative target against the shim's own `dirname`, which is pre-existing logic this change does not touch, and it is reached identically from all three installed depths because each copy is resolved by its own package, not by a relative hop.
2. **Referenced but not shipped** — **no new files**, so no installer file list, npm `files` array or plugin layout entry is due. The three changed helpers were already shipped: `installer/lib/` rides the root `files` `installer/` entry, and the two TypeScript copies compile into their packages' own `dist`. The added `parseWindowsExeShim` export is picked up by the pi-extension esbuild bundle (its integration suite passes).
3. **Windows** — this *is* the Windows fix, so the class got the most attention. Reads stay explicit `utf8`. CRLF is handled by splitting on `/\r?\n/` before the per-line anchors, so a `\r` can never defeat the `$`. Backslash targets are split on `/[\\/]+/` as before, and a drive-absolute `C:\Program Files\…` target matches its own alternative. No shell is involved — the target is spawned directly with argv as an array — so a path with spaces and an argument like `unsafe&arg` carry through byte-identically, which the tests assert. The parser is a linear scan over a file already capped at 256KB, so the 5s hook budget is untouched. No PowerShell surface, no rename, no drive-crossing move.
4. **Destructive writes** — none. Both commits are read-only on disk (grepped for `writeFileSync`/`appendFileSync`/`renameSync`/`unlinkSync`/`mkdirSync`/`rmSync` in the changed sources: no hits). Nothing touches `settings.json`, `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md` or a user rule file.
5. **Silent fail-open** — the shim resolver still **fails closed**: an unparseable wrapper throws, and the new form is accepted only on an anchored whole-line match, with a batch-forwarding wrapper explicitly excluded from exe detection so a line is never picked out of the middle of one. The one deliberate open direction is documented in code: `proxyCompatMount` returning `undefined` (unreadable or flow-style `caveman.yaml`) reads as routed rather than as a missing mount, because the baseURL has already proven the requests are not going direct — and the only consequence either way is whether an advisory warning prints. `opencodeBaseUrlRouting` returning `null` on an unparseable URL falls through to the pre-existing warning, not past it.
6. **Claim drift** — nothing changes what ships, so no README "What you get" row or `INSTALL.md` entry moves; grepped both for stale claims about the probe or the routed check and found none. **No benchmark, savings percentage or token-reduction number was touched, and no README benchmark table was opened.**

Two findings from this pass were fixed before pushing rather than shipped with a
caveat. First, an early draft rejected `..` in an exe shim target; npm and pnpm
emit `..` routinely (the bin dir sits beside the package tree) and the Node path
already allows it, so that would have reintroduced the bug for ordinary layouts
— the test now pins `..` as accepted. Second, the per-provider verdict
short-circuited on the first candidate config, so a missing mount named in
`opencode.jsonc` could shadow a genuinely routed endpoint in `opencode.json`;
every candidate is now consulted before answering, and a routed endpoint
anywhere wins.

Both fixes were confirmed to fail first for the right reason: #1252's tests
failed on the absent `parseWindowsExeShim` export, and #1254's reproduced the
reporter's warning string verbatim, including the `(routed: openai, anthropic,
opencode-go)` tail.

Nothing merged, closed or rejected. No force-push — the push was a fast-forward
(`423c01b..1992d3e`).

### 2026-10-12 run

Full gate set, with the branch at `423c01b`, after `npm install` in the repo root
and in `packages/cli`:

- `npm test` — **585 tests, 572 pass, 0 fail, 13 skipped.** Identical to the 10-10 baseline.
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — **28/28**.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — **242 tests, OK** (241 before this run's adopted case).
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` — **all local verification checks passed.** No `src/hooks/` file changed this run, so `checksums.sha256` is untouched and the gate confirms it intact.
- `packages/cli`: `npm test` — **1190 tests, 1172 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 18 skipped.**
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` — **windows compatibility gate passed**, which also ran `./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...`: every package `ok`. No Go file changed in this run's commits; the Go suites are this branch's earlier work being re-confirmed.
- `node agents/compile.mjs` / `packages/cli/scripts/compile-registries.mjs` re-run at HEAD — clean, no stray diff. `agents.json` and `agents.generated.ts` are generated, not hand-edited.

**The 10-10 standing exception is cleared, and the reason is worth recording.**
That run reported `test-windows-compat.mjs` failing identically on unmodified
`origin/main` with `error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'node'`,
and attributed it to sub-packages having no `node_modules` in the container. That
diagnosis was right: with dependencies actually installed the gate passes. The
same missing-`node_modules` state also produced two phantom `#1214` failures in
`native-enable.runtime.mjs` early in this run (`0 windowsHide: true` in a
generated plugin that demonstrably contains two), which vanished after a clean
rebuild — the stale `dist/index.js` from a `tsc` run that had errored on the
missing types was what the tests were spawning. Worth knowing before anyone
chases those as real regressions.

**One honest caveat on the CLI suite.** Its first run here, executed concurrently
with `test-windows-compat.mjs` at load average 33, reported **2 fail / 1
cancelled** out of 1158. That invocation was piped through `tail -40`, so the
failing test names were not captured, and the suite was re-run on its own: 1190
tests, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, exit 0. Contention is the most likely explanation
(these tests spawn real subprocesses and bind ports) but it is an inference, not
something I can prove about two tests I cannot name. Recorded rather than
rounded down to "green".

Adversarial pass over this run's commits (`c99b62c..423c01b`), by review class:

1. **Path resolution** — no `../` chain or `path.join(__dirname, …)` added or moved. The one path constructed is `process.env.CAVEMAN_CONFIG ?? join(cavemanHome(), "caveman.yaml")`, and it is interpolated into an error message only; it reaches no filesystem call, so a wrong answer could at worst misname a file in prose. `cavemanHome()` is the existing helper every other config read uses.
2. **Referenced but not shipped** — no new file in any commit. Nothing to add to an installer list, a `files` array or the plugin layout. The `plugins/caveman/**` mirror of the compress fix was deliberately dropped and is CI's to sync; `tests/verify_repo.py` checks `SKILL.md` and agent parity, not `scripts/*.py`, so the gate does not fail in the interim.
3. **Windows** — no encoding, CRLF, backslash-path, `$Args` or quoting surface in the diff. The new code is URL parsing and a thrown string; the statusline scripts, hooks and installer are untouched. The gate passed on its own.
4. **Destructive writes** — this run makes `enable` strictly *less* destructive. The refusal throws during mutation *planning*, before any mutation is returned, which is why the test can assert `settings.json` byte-identical and no journal written. Nothing writes `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md` or a user rule file.
5. **Silent fail-open** — the class that produced the fifth commit. `claudeForeignRoute` returns `null` (meaning "not a conflict, proceed") for absent, empty and whitespace values, for caveman's own routes, and now for an explicit `api.anthropic.com` when the proxy's upstream is that host; it returns the value (meaning "refuse") for a genuinely foreign endpoint and for an unparseable string. Each of those ten cases was executed end-to-end through `enable claude` rather than reasoned about, and the matrix is in the commit message. A non-string value still falls through to the old overwrite, which loses nothing: a number cannot be a working route.
6. **Claim drift** — `INSTALL.md`'s uninstall entry promised "your own prior value comes back", which now understates the behavior, so it says the route is never taken from a third-party endpoint in the first place and names `providers.anthropic.base_url`. The README "What you get" table needs no row: no feature ships or is removed. **No benchmark, savings percentage or token-reduction number was touched anywhere.**

Guards were checked in both directions, not trusted. The #1247 test fails on the
pre-fix build with `enable must not silently take over a foreign route` and the
settings file rewritten; the shortcut case fails there with an empty stderr where
`providers.anthropic.base_url` is expected. The adopted #1248 cases fail on
`2e08b91` with the genuine `TypeError` from the spread, not as an assertion about
a constant that does not exist yet.

Nothing merged, closed or rejected. No force-push: `origin/main` was already an
ancestor of the branch, so no merge was needed either. The four runtime artifacts
the 10-08 run caught (`packages/cli/backups/` with a `.claude.json.backup.*`,
`policy-limits.json`, its stamp, `remote-settings.json`) were written into the
tree again by the CLI suite; every commit was built from explicit path sets and
`git log --name-only origin/main..HEAD` confirms none of those paths appears in
any of them.


### 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-09 runs, condensed

Both runs green on the full suite and both adversarially reviewed across the six
classes at the time; the detail is in the commits and the per-issue comments.

- 10-10, at `6c5a18f`: `npm test` 585 tests / 572 pass / 0 fail / 13 skipped; `tests/*.js` 28/28; `unittest` 241 OK; `verify_repo.py` all checks passed; `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` all pass (the three new `compat_duplicate_credential_test.go` cases were confirmed red before the fix, green after). `test-windows-compat.mjs` failed identically on unmodified `origin/main` in a throwaway worktree at `2e08b91` (`TS2688`, missing `node_modules` in several sub-packages) — a pre-existing container limitation, and that run touched no path, hook, installer or shell script.
- 10-09, at `bdb0666`: `npm test` 585 / 572 / 0 fail; `tests/*.js` 28/28; `unittest` 241 OK; `verify_repo.py` passed; Go green including `./mem/...` and `TestConcurrentRememberSubprocesses`; `test-windows-compat.mjs` gate passed; `check-profile-scope.mjs` reported `profile commit scope valid`. Both the drift-report guards and #1235's retry budget were mutation-tested (reverting each guard fails exactly the new cases and no others).

Neither run touched `src/hooks/`, so `checksums.sha256` needed no regeneration.
No benchmark, savings percentage or token-reduction number was touched in either.

### Earlier runs (10-06 → 10-08), condensed

Each of those runs recorded the same gate set that the 10-12 section above records, and the one standing exception first noted on 10-08 is restated there.

title: feat(proxy): Caveman Cloud decides model and effort for every routed request
body:
Founder rulings, 2026-10-06:
- "The entire local router system should get its decision from here."
- "Keep the text."
- "Table decides, up or down."

The local runtime now reports facts and applies Cloud's answer. Cloud's `POST /v1/route` decides model AND effort for every routable request class. No routing logic lives in this repo: `tests/test_no_router_internals.js` is unchanged and passes.

**What the route ask sends** (contracts `route-ask-v1`, additive)
- `ask`, sent on a main ask and on a subagent's first request:
  - the latest human turn (an input group with no tool result; the end is kept, ≤128 KiB);
  - the turn before it and the end of the agent's last reply (≤16 KiB each);
  - `turn`, the count of human turns.
- `request`:
  - endpoint;
  - eleven allowlisted agent headers (Claude Code request class / agent ids, Codex thread / subagent / turn metadata, OpenCode agent / parent);
  - declared tool names;
  - the request's own effort and thinking type;
  - the per-message latch.
- `last`: the previous request's served model, effort, age and token counts.
- `state` / `parent_state`: Cloud's opaque signed session token, held in memory only.

**What it applies**
- **Model:** it may now be pricier than the one asked for. The agent still sees the model name it asked for, in JSON and in streams; usage records the served model.
- **Effort:**
  - Responses: `reasoning.effort`.
  - Chat: `reasoning_effort`.
  - Anthropic: top-level `output_config.effort`.
  - When Cloud answers `effort_mode: "message"`, Anthropic per-message effort marks are replayed byte-identically. Cloud ships that mode dark, behind its `routing.perMessageEffort` switch.
  - The proxy never inserts a mark unless Cloud answers "message". A no-effort answer restores the agent's own bytes. A 4,607-request fuzz showed the only byte changes are effort and model.
- **Calls to Cloud:**
  - Tool loops reuse one decision per ask (keyed by session, model, turn and text).
  - Compaction and side requests are asked per request.
  - Subagents are asked per child ask.
- **Recovery:** a thinking-binding 400 on a session routing changed is healed once. It uses Anthropic's documented `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`, with a strip as fallback. It never overrides the agent's own `block_binding`, and latches stop it after a real refusal.

**Disclosure.** README, SECURITY.md, docs, the sign-in line, `caveman on routing` and the setup picker all say what routing sends. That covers the ask together with whatever the agent attaches to it (CLAUDE.md and memory reminders, @-files, `!` output, compaction summaries), plus agent headers, tool names, effort and token counts. They also say that on the Free plan Caveman may keep the ask. Telemetry and runtime events still carry no prompt text. ADR 0083 §7 stands: subscription main-loop traffic isn't routed.

**Release gate.** Don't release a runtime with this until Cloud's `/v1/route` with `request` is deployed (caveman-ai/Caveman-Cloud#786). An older Cloud answers 400, and routing pauses. Traffic is unaffected: routing fails open.

**Checks**
- `go vet` clean.
- `go test -race` passes on gateway and cloudlink. The full race suite timed out in two untouched packages at load average 300–500; both pass without race.
- CLI `test:fast`: 201 pass.
- Contracts and the guard pass.
- Seven independent Opus review rounds, with randomized probes for the dark guarantee and the marked path.

**Known pre-existing failure:** `packages/cli/tests/login-private.runtime.mjs` "private login persists keyless grant…" also fails on `v4` (b37698cc) built clean: login's sign-in lines read `/api/v1/auth/me`, so the test sees one more `/me` than it expects. Not touched here.

title: Caveman 3.2.0: v3 sweep (cache-bust invariant, cgo binaries, new integrations, 30+ issues)
body:
## Summary

This is the Caveman 3.2.0 release sweep: 227 commits on top of `99aafe15`
(origin/main). It merges the 3.2.0 triage queue and the #1105 cache-invariant
hardening into one branch, with release pins already bumped. The artifacts are:

- `v3.2.0`
- `bin-v2.1.0`
- `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.1.0
- `@caveman-ai/pi` 0.3.0
- `@caveman-ai/middleware` 1.0.1
- extension 1.3.0

Headline changes:

- The proxy can no longer change bytes the provider already cached (#1105). A
  runtime tripwire now records any bust caveman causes.
- Release binaries compress TS/JS/Python/Rust/Java/C/C++ (cgo via pinned zig,
  #1020/#1120).
- Bare `/v1/models` is routed by protocol (#1187).
- New always-on integrations: Codex hook, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Antigravity CLI,
  Grok.
- Subagents inherit the session's mode, and headless `claude -p` / Agent SDK
  sessions start off.
- Sessions are recorded for stats when they end, with skill wording fixes.
- The installer moved from `bin/` to `installer/` for Enterprise marketplaces.
- caveman-compress gains the opencode and openai-compat providers.
- Evals gain usage recording and a fidelity eval, plus docs.

User-facing release notes: see the 3.2.0 GitHub Release text (drafted
separately).

## What's in it

### Proxy and engine

- **Cache invariant (#1105).** Commits `b1adbe0f`..`9c8cbde4`, plus `1ae6f9be`
  and `6cbde1fc`.
  - The derived epoch gate is gone. An explicit epoch vetoes only new
    compression.
  - The first decision wins, raw decisions included (`RawDecisionHandle`,
    `rawMemory`, which is consulted only after the store).
  - New rows are remembered only after the splice holds. A late failure sends
    only the new blocks raw.
  - A rate-limit 429 (with `Retry-After`) is passed through and not retried
    raw.
  - Raw pin per conversation lineage. The longest lineage wins, and pin rows
    are never evicted.
  - A PAYG non-MCP conversation stays raw once it streams (`stream_switch`).
  - Pixel mode: decisions are memoised, renders are remembered only once the
    request is sent, the raw pin is honored, the breakpoint is kept, and
    requests to Anthropic are capped at 20 images.
  - The tool-schema strip is memoised.
  - `/chatgpt` reads compress-eligible bodies up to `CAVE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`
    and runs the tripwire.
  - Tripwire `prefix_monitor.go` plus the `requests.cache_bust_cause` column
    (`client`/`raw_retry`/`stream_switch`/`lever_freeze`/`caveman`).
    `caveman status` shows caveman-caused busts.
  - Invariant net: `cache_prefix_invariant_test.go` and
    `FuzzCachePrefixInvariant`.
  - Release binaries are stamped with the pinned tag.
  - Docs: `proxy/CLAUDE.md` and `proxy/AGENTS.md` state the invariant, its two
    exceptions and the known limits.
- **cgo release build (#1020, #1120).** `b3236048`, `99be14a9`, `3c0223c5`,
  `59f77766`.
  - `caveman-proxy` and `caveman-engine` are built for six targets with
    `zig cc`. The build pins zig 0.16.0 and is reproducible.
  - A release-shape CI lane is added.
  - The image and the other four binaries stay pure Go.
- **`/v1/models` routing (#1187, from #1188).** `6802db5c`, `7e389af7`,
  `1de9f90f`.
- **ChatGPT subscription.**
  - #1155: Pi ChatGPT OAuth goes through `/chatgpt`, with zstd decode.
  - #1053 (partial): recovery proven from the request body (`additional_tools`),
    `identity` encoding treated as plain, eligibility counted at the
    compressor, and `body_over_limit` logged for zstd.
- **CCR (#1186).** Works on filesystems without hard links. `fchmodat2` is
  gated on Android, and Android is detected from the system image.
- **Engine (#1129).** Test-report compressor for JUnit, pytest and Jest, with
  detection anchored to top-level shape.
- **Browse (#1018, #1016).** Signal cleanup for Chrome and the temp profile.
  Signals are caught before Chrome launches.

### CLI and native routing

- **Codex.** Auth-lane self-heal with no spawned probes (#1047).
- **OpenCode.**
  - `opencode-go` routed through the proxy's OpenCode Go mount (#1090,
    partial).
  - A warning when the active provider bypasses the proxy (#1190).
- **Hermes.** `HERMES_HOME` is expanded the way Hermes 0.21.5 does.
- **`c3307fe3`.** The local CLI shim is written to `.local-bin/`.

### Hooks and skills

- **Subagents (#621, #672).** SubagentStart hook: `caveman-activate.js
  --subagent`.
- **Headless sessions (#377).** Headless `claude -p` / SDK sessions start off,
  keyed on `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`.
- **Session-end stats (#784, #716).** SessionEnd runs `caveman-stats --record`.
  CWD-scoped session lookup and Claude Code folder encoding (#563).
- **Other hosts.** Shared sessionStart hook for non-Claude hosts. It reads the
  pinned skill first and keeps the mode in the banner only.
- **Skills.**
  - Diff-first (#643, #637).
  - Normal prose for questions the agent asks (#758).
  - Never delete or shorten comments (#278).
  - Hook-less `/caveman status` (#1185).
  - The OpenClaw bootstrap carries the new rules.
- **No Node (#489).** Plugin hooks skip quietly without `node`.

### Installer and host integrations

- **Installer move (#1035).** `bin/` moved to `installer/`. `verify_repo.py`
  guards against a top-level `bin/`.
- **Codex (#573, partial).** Optional always-on SessionStart hook for Codex.
- **Cursor (#405, from #1122).** Cursor plugin and `--only cursor`: user hook
  plus agents. A commented `hooks.json` is left alone.
- **Copilot CLI (#553).** sessionStart hook, gated on the CLI.
- **Antigravity (#183).** Antigravity CLI (`agy`) target.
- **Grok Build (#754).** Grok Build always-on via `~/.grok/AGENTS.md`.
- **CodeBuddy (#408).** CodeBuddy Code target.
- **OpenCode (#725).** Cavecrew agents installed as `mode: subagent`.
- **Detection (#1189).** "No agents detected" wording and Copilot CLI
  detection.
- **#627.** The installer no longer downloads and runs `caveman-init.js`.

title: fix(caveman-compress): require explicit filepath, forbid inline improvisation
body:
## Summary
- `caveman-compress`'s SKILL.md trigger says `/caveman-compress <filepath>`, but nothing tells the model what to do if the user pastes raw text with no filepath instead. Observed in the wild: the model improvised inline compression and wrote its own reasoning about the request straight into the saved file ("User passed text directly, not a filepath. Compress inline per the rules.") instead of asking for a path or refusing.
- Adds an explicit rule under `## Trigger`: require a filepath; if one isn't given, ask for it or offer to save the pasted text first, rather than improvising.

## Test plan
- N/A — SKILL.md instruction change only, no script behavior change.
