Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.60.1
Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-09-30 v1.61.0:

    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

  • 2026-09-01 v1.58.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.4. It carries upstream's own fix for the journal-rollback data-corruption bug, so the local super-journal patch v1.56.0 introduced is dropped; recovery behavior is unchanged. Also bumps the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.6; as always, downstream modules must pin the same version this one does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in support for Linux Open File Description (OFD) locks on database files, off by default; without opting in, locking behavior is byte-for-byte that of previous releases. A POSIX record lock is owned by the (process, inode) pair, so any Close of any descriptor of the database file anywhere in the process silently strips SQLite's locks; OFD locks survive that. Enable it process-wide with MODERNC_SQLITE_OFD_LOCK=1 in the environment, or with the new OFDLocking(true) before the first connection is opened; OFDLockingEnabled reports the mode in effect, and the new ErrOFDLockingTooLate and ErrOFDLockingUnavailable report a switch attempted too late and a platform or filesystem without the feature. Why it is process-wide rather than a DSN parameter, what WAL's -shm coordination still uses, and the /proc/locks measurements behind the design are in [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255).
    • Resolves [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255). See [GitLab merge request #136](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/136), thanks Nathan Herring (@​technosloth), and thanks Gani Georgiev (@​ganigeorgiev) for pressing the opt-in default!

  • 2026-08-19 v1.57.0:

    • Add an opt-in _defensive DSN query parameter turning on SQLite's defensive mode for the connection. On such a connection PRAGMA writable_schema=ON, PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF and PRAGMA schema_version=N become silent no-ops, and writes to a virtual table's shadow tables and to sqlite_dbpage fail. It is a hardening measure, not a sandbox for hostile database files, for which it is only one of the steps SQLite recommends, and it is a property of the connection, not of the file. Absent, or _defensive=0, nothing changes.
    • Reject _defensive=1 together with _journal_mode=OFF (or _journal=OFF) instead of opening a connection in which neither was honoured: SQLite turns that PRAGMA into a no-op that still reports success. Only DSNs using the new parameter can be affected. See [GitHub pull request #6](modernc-org/sqlite#6), thanks wsman!
    • Ship the sqlite-vec license notice this module has been missing since vec/ arrived in v1.47.0. sqlite-vec is Copyright (c) 2024 Alex Garcia, dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT and used here under MIT; the text now ships as LICENSE-SQLITE_VEC, and make vendor fails rather than quietly dropping it.
    • The SQLite notice is renamed from SQLITE-LICENSE to LICENSE-SQLITE; update any direct links to it. Its contents are unchanged. The rename is what makes go mod vendor carry both notices into downstream vendor/ trees: it selects license files by name prefix, so a name merely ending in LICENSE was never propagated.
    • Let a caller-constructed Driver register its own functions, collations and virtual table modules, through new RegisterFunction, RegisterScalarFunction, RegisterDeterministicScalarFunction, RegisterCollationUtf8 and RegisterModule methods plus Must* variants, and let vtab.RegisterModule honour its db argument. Behavior change: vtab.RegisterModule(db, ...) where db was opened on a caller-constructed Driver used to discard db and land on the registered sqlite driver, reaching every connection in the process; it now lands on that Driver alone, so a sql.Open("sqlite") connection that used to resolve such a module gets no such module. Everything else is additive, and the isolating change discussed in [GitLab issue #254](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/254) is deliberately not made here. See [GitLab merge request #135](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/135), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Promote freebsd/386, freebsd/arm and netbsd/amd64 from experimental to fully supported. The package documentation's platform table had carried seventeen entries while this module shipped, cross-built and tested twenty; all three have been in the builder matrix since v1.53.0 and pass the full suite on this release's commit. Documentation only — lib/ is byte-for-byte what v1.56.0 shipped.

  • 2026-08-03 v1.56.0:

Updates `tzdata` from 2026.4 to 2026.5
Release notes

Sourced from tzdata's releases.

2026.5: Release of upstream tzdata 2026e

Version 2026.5

Upstream version 2026e released 2026-09-30T00:14:38+00:00.

Briefly:

Manitoba moves to permanent -05 on 2026-10-31.

Changes to future timestamps

Manitoba’s 2026-03-08 spring forward was its last foreseeable clock change, as it moved to permanent -05 thereafter. Model this with its traditional abbreviation EST. Although the change to permanent -05 legally takes place on 2026-10-31, temporarily model the change to occur on 2026-11-01 at 02:00 for the same reason as other recent temporary hacks. (Caution: see “NOTE FOR 2026b TEMPORARY HACK FOR CLDR AND CANADA” below.)

As the change affects both America/Winnipeg and its backward compatibility link, the obsolescent setting TZ="Canada/Central" will now use the abbreviation EST for affected timestamps, akin to TZ="Canada/Pacific" behavior introduced in 2026b.

Another TZDB release may be needed soon if any of the portions of northwestern Ontario historically aligned with America/Winnipeg do not follow. For now, given the short leadtime with Manitoba’s announcement, assume that they will, to avoid creating new zones that may not be needed if no divergence occurs.

Changes to past timestamps

In 1925 Ireland fell back on 09-20 not 10-04 (thanks to Stan Ulbrych).

Changes to commentary

Discussion on timekeeping practices in northwestern Ontario has been expanded in light of Manitoba’s recent announcement. It is not yet known whether or to what extent these areas may adapt their own timekeeping practices in response.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.55.0 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

title: fix(pi): do not propose a compat mount for a non-URL provider endpoint
body:
## Problem

A Pi provider that answers in-process publishes a sentinel `baseUrl` rather than a URL. [`pi-claude-bridge`](https://github.com/elidickinson/pi-claude-bridge) sets `baseUrl: "claude-bridge"` and gates its own handlers on that exact value, so nothing it sends ever leaves over HTTP.

That provider reaches the unlisted-provider branch in `ProviderRouter.apply` and the operator is told:

```
Caveman: pass-through for claude-bridge/claude-opus-5 (no compat mount named
"claude-bridge" in the local proxy; add compat.claude-bridge.base_url to
caveman.yaml to route it); no compression
```

The advice is not merely useless, it is harmful. Adding that mount makes the extension rewrite `baseUrl` to `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/w/pi/compat/claude-bridge/...`, which no longer equals the sentinel the provider dispatches on — so the provider stops activating. Following the notice disables the provider instead of compressing it.

## Fix

Compute `hostOf(original)` once and branch on it first. An endpoint with no host can never be carried by any mount, so report it plainly and offer no remedy:

```
Caveman: pass-through for claude-bridge/claude-opus-5 (provider endpoint
"claude-bridge" is not an HTTP URL; this provider sends no routable request);
no compression
```

Routing behavior is unchanged — `routeForApi` already returned `undefined` for these models and they already stayed direct. Only the reason string changes. The `hostOf(original) ?? original` fallback in the host-mismatch branch is now dead and removed, since that branch only runs with a host.

Testing `!host` rather than `host === undefined` also covers values that parse as a URL with an empty host (`localhost:8080`), which are equally unroutable.

## Test

`packages/pi-extension/tests/provider.runtime.mjs` gains a case asserting the model stays direct, the notice names the sentinel, and it never mentions `compat.<provider>.base_url`. Verified it fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

```
$ cd packages/pi-extension && npm test
ℹ pass 118
ℹ fail 0
```

## Docs

One paragraph in `docs/technical/proxy-and-providers.md` next to the existing direct-mode rules, recording why this class of provider is never offered a mount.

title: feat(proxy): route across every provider the person set up
body:
Stacked on #1198 (`v4-route-ask`, which already carries the effort work). Retarget to `v4` once #1198 lands.

## What

Routing can leave the harness's own vendor, using what the person has actually set up (ADR 0085, founder rulings 2026-10-06).

- **Provider logins.** `caveman providers add <id> [--key-env NAME|--stdin] | remove <id> | login chatgpt | local`. API keys: anthropic, openai, opencode-go, openrouter, fireworks, deepseek, moonshot, zai, zai-coding-plan, gemini, xai, groq, together. OAuth: Sign in with ChatGPT (experimental, not yet verified against the live service). Keys never go on argv. Secrets are stored in the macOS keychain (`caveman-provider`) or in a 0600 file under `$CAVEMAN_HOME/provider-logins/`. `provider-logins.json` lists only ids and where each secret lives. Every OAuth row carries a terms note.
- **Left out on terms grounds:** Claude Pro/Max logins (Anthropic allows them only in its own apps), Gemini CLI / Antigravity Google logins (Google bans accounts), GitHub Copilot (supported only through OpenCode's own login), and Codex's own `~/.codex/auth.json`. Each of these is refused with the reason.
- **Pool in the ask** (additive to route-ask-v1, hub "v2"): `pool: [{id, model, host, via:"local"}]`, at most 64 entries.
  - The harness's own models come first as `harness/<model>`; each login then adds `<host>/<model>` for the catalog models its host serves.
  - Model lists are static per host for now (`ponytail:` comment).
  - Entries the runtime cannot translate to are excluded.
  - `models` is still sent. A 400 to an ask carrying `pool` is retried without it. If the 400 names `pool`, pool stays off until the next login.
- **Applying the answer:**
  - `pool_id` + `via:"local"` on a harness entry behaves exactly as today.
  - `via:"local"` on a login entry sends the request straight to that host on that login. It is translated when the host speaks another grammar, effort is set top-level, and the agent's copy names the model it asked for.
  - `via:"cloud"` (pool_id `cloud:<provider>:<model>`) sends the agent's own bytes in its grammar to the Cloud gateway (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`) with `x-caveman-route: <pool_id>`, on the project gateway key only. The agent's provider credential is never sent. The gateway URL comes from `cloud.json` `gatewayUrl`, falling back to `baseURL`. With no project key, or after `caveman providers cloud off`, the asked model runs instead. Route asks to the gateway also use the project key now, because the gateway refuses login tokens.
  - Any failure before content reaches the agent falls back to the asked model on the harness's credential. That covers a refused translation, a translator panic, a connect error, any non-2xx (including the gateway's `cave_route_invalid` / `cave_route_unavailable`), and a 2xx that fails or ends before content (the translators hold their output until then). A stream cut after content aborts the connection and never closes a half-finished tool call.
- **Translators** (`proxy/internal/translate`), Apache-2.0 like the rest of the hub. Directions covered: Messages→chat, Messages→Responses, Responses→Messages, Responses→chat, plus same-grammar fitting. Messages→Responses is new code, not a port: it lets a Claude Code session run on the ChatGPT login.
  - Covers streaming, tool calls, thinking/reasoning, images, usage and stop reasons.
  - Thinking signatures are namespaced per host. Later harness requests in a pool-served session drop reasoning another host wrote.
  - Only plumbing was moved. No routing policy, tables, scores, rankings or switch rules exist in the hub; Cloud decides.
- **OpenAI is Responses-only.** An OpenAI host, on an API key or the ChatGPT login, gets only the Responses wire. A Claude Code request reaches it through Messages→Responses. Chat callers get no OpenAI entry in the pool: those entries are left out, so nothing fails. OpenRouter GPT models are removed too.
- **Effort on every path.** The harness path is cleaned on every request and never rewrites per-message effort marks. A local pool target gets the answered effort in its own shape: Messages `output_config`/`thinking`, Responses `reasoning.effort`, or the chat dialect. Responses and OpenAI-style chat clamp `max` to `xhigh`. A via:cloud request carries `x-caveman-effort: <effort>` when the answer has one. A failed target falls back to the asked model at the answered effort, fitted to that model's levels (`translate.FitEffort`; `minimal` becomes `low` on Claude, `max` becomes `xhigh` on OpenAI, `none` is dropped on Claude). The cached reject replays the fitted value.
- **Thinking off per model:** only the exact model or a dated snapshot of it (`claude-opus-5-20260301`) matches. Opus 5.5 never gets `disabled`. Opus 5 gets it only at high or below. Sonnet 5.5 gets `{"type":"between_tools"}` at high or below and nothing above that. Sonnet 5 gets `disabled`. A caller's own `between_tools` stays only for Sonnet 5.5 at high or below, becomes `disabled` for Sonnet 5 and for Opus 5 at high or below, and is dropped elsewhere.
- **Copy:** README, SECURITY.md and the CLI's routing line now say that requests routed to a Caveman Cloud model pass through Caveman Cloud and local ones do not.

## Notes
- **Squash-merge:** the squash message must leave out the line from commit 1fa75b27 that names the private repo and ADR 0085 ("Moved from the private … per ADR 0085; …"). Keep the rest of that commit's message.
- Review round 2, item 4: thinking blocks with an empty signature are dropped on translation. This was accepted as is.
- The gate holds an upstream for at most 10 s, including one that sends only comments or pings (OpenRouter's `: OPENROUTER PROCESSING`). After that the headers go out and pings start, so a failure after that point reaches the agent and does not fall back.
- Reasoning another host wrote is stripped only on Anthropic's or OpenAI's own API. Pass-through requests and other origins are left alone.
- A host's own failure relayed after content is labelled `pool_upstream_failed` and ends the stream cleanly.
- A ping or keepalive goes only between a relayed upstream's events, never inside one. The gate can still commit at any point. Line readers stop when a stream returns early.
- The fallback effort uses the catalog's `effort_levels` for OpenAI models (`catalog.EffortLevels`; the catalog lists `max` for gpt-6-sol). Models the catalog does not list use OpenAI's common set. With thinking off in the body, the fallback effort is capped at high. A caller's own `between_tools` is dropped for non-Claude models.
- A translated Messages stream's `message_start` carries an input-token estimate: chars/4, with a flat 1600 per base64 image or document. It is marked with `x-caveman-input-tokens: estimated`, and `message_delta` carries the host's exact count. Recorded usage stays exact.
- A caller's own `thinking` is fitted to the host's model even when the answer carries no effort. When all input was cached, `message_delta` reports `input_tokens` 1, so the start estimate is never left standing on top of the cache counts. The estimate is counted when `message_start` goes out, not before the upstream send.
- Each failed pool target is logged. The local row stores `route_pool_id`, `route_reason` and `upstream_response_id` (the host's own answer id, e.g. OpenRouter's `gen-…`).
- Locks on `provider-logins.json.lock` carry a token and are removed only by their owner. A stale lock (10 s) is moved aside before it is taken. The CLI's `security` calls time out after 4 s.
- Z.ai Coding Plan is gated on the agent header (`x-cave-agent` of claude/claude-code/codex/opencode) and forwards that agent's own User-Agent. This is left as is on purpose.
- Copy: SECURITY.md and README say that a via:cloud request goes whole (system prompt, tool results, code) through Caveman Cloud, runs on the project's stored provider key and is billed to that project.

## Not covered yet
- chat→Messages and chat→Responses are not translated, so chat callers only reach chat hosts.
- Messages→Responses drops cache_control, stop_sequences, temperature/top_p, document blocks and redacted thinking. A Responses reasoning item without a summary comes back as an empty thinking block that carries its `encrypted_content`.
- Model ids are unverified for Together, Fireworks and OpenRouter. A wrong id gets a 4xx and falls back.
- ChatGPT-login or OpenCode Go Responses reasoning carried back to an OpenAI API key may not decrypt there.

## Tests
- `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` passes, and `go vet ./proxy/...` is clean. Coverage includes translator round trips (streaming and tool calls), pool building from a fake credential store, the ask body with pool, fallback paths (pool 5xx/401, host down, gateway error, untranslatable request, old Cloud 400), the via=cloud request shape, a cut stream aborting, harness-path hygiene, and Messages→Responses (request fields, streamed and assembled answers, tool calls, reasoning round trip, ChatGPT-login fitting, a Claude Code request served by the ChatGPT login end to end, and its fallback).
- Round 2 adds regression tests for: dated-snapshot effort matching, the gate committing after its hold, role-only chat chunks, a relayed response.failed being terminal, a via:cloud 2xx that fails before content, OpenAI login reasoning tagging, an OpenAI API-key target with tools going out on `/v1/responses`, no OpenAI entry on the chat wire, the answered effort on every translator direction, `x-caveman-effort`, effort kept on fallback and after a reject, per-message marks surviving harness cleaning across medium→high→top, lock ownership, stale-lock breaking, the refresh retry, and keychain cleanup under `CAVE_NO_KEYCHAIN`. `-race` passes on the changed packages, and the timing tests pass 30 runs in a row.
- CLI: `tests/provider-logins.runtime.mjs` (9 tests) passes. Root `npm test`: 456 tests, 0 failures.
- Contracts: `validate-schemas.mjs` passes, with new pool vectors. `tests/verify_repo.py`, `node --test tests/*.js`, `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (186 tests) and `npm test` all pass. One installer pwsh test failed once and passed on two reruns.
- Live smoke (2026-10-06, OpenRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, throwaway `CAVEMAN_HOME`, Cloud `/v1/route` and the harness stubbed). All calls returned 200: a Claude Code streamed tool call and its tool_result turn (the replayed thinking was accepted, and `cache_read_input_tokens` 256 appeared on turn 2), the same with a non-streaming caller, and a Codex Responses→chat turn and its function_call_output turn (`cached_tokens` 256 on turn 2). title: feat(proxy): cache follow-ups for Cloud's cache economics (GPT-6 configuration_update, cache_ttl, stickiness, fan-out)
body:
## What this does

These are the hub-side cache follow-ups that Caveman Cloud's new cache-aware routing depends on. The hub only does the mechanics: it applies what Cloud answers and decides nothing about models.

**Record mode** gets none of the cache mechanics this PR adds: no `prompt_cache_key`, no OpenRouter provider pin, no fan-out wait, and host affinity headers keyed on the session itself, as on the base. The routing answer itself (model, effort, per-message marks, `configuration_update`) still applies in record mode, as before.

1. **GPT-6 `configuration_update`.** When Cloud answers `effort_mode: "message"` on OpenAI Responses, the effort now goes in as `{"type":"configuration_update","reasoning":{"effort":…}}` before the newest user message. The top-level `reasoning.effort` is no longer rewritten, so the cached prefix survives. Source: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning, "Change reasoning mid-conversation", read 2026-10-06 ("Keep the original request-level setting; the item updates the conversation", "before the next user message in the input array", "the API rejects adjacent updates"). The Anthropic mark rules carry over unchanged:
   - updates already in history replay byte for byte at their anchors;
   - a later `top` answer becomes one more update once a session has them;
   - an update never goes at the end, never sits next to another one, and never goes before a user message that something already answered (mid tool loop the effort in force holds);
   - none at all where OpenAI forbids it (`truncation: "auto"`, `context_management`, a non-false `multi_agent`); Cloud's effort goes top-level there;
   - a 400 naming a configuration update in any spelling (pro models) retries once at top level and sets `per_message_off` for the session;
   - effort state made on one wire starts afresh on the other.
2. **`request.cache_ttl`** (5m|30m|1h|24h) goes on the route ask. It is read from the body: the longest Anthropic `cache_control` ttl (none counts as 5m), else OpenAI `prompt_cache_options.ttl` or `prompt_cache_retention`. It is an additive field in `route-ask-v1`, with vectors. Cloud refuses an unknown field with its generic `cave_router_request_invalid`, which never names the field. The old retry only matched a 400 containing "pool", so it never fired against the real Cloud. Now a 400 that names a field, or the generic one, is asked again without `cache_ttl`, then without `pool`; a field Cloud has already answered 200 for is never dropped on a generic 400. Only the field whose removal got the 200 stays off until the next login.
3. **Stickiness and affinity.**
   - An OpenAI request the route stage is on for (a `previous_response_id` chain, answered off for a reason, included) gets the session's own hashed `prompt_cache_key` when it carries none. It is added before the effort, so a marks heal keeps it. The original-bytes retry keeps it unless the 4xx names it, which also turns the key off for the rest of the session. A request that was only keyed is never replayed, and a keyed request asks for its answer without brotli so a refusal can be read. Routing off and signed out stay byte for byte.
   - Host affinity headers (`x-session-id` for OpenRouter, `x-session-affinity` for Fireworks, `x-grok-conv-id` for xAI) are keyed on the parent session for a child, so a whole spawn tree lands on one provider.
   - Once a session's OpenRouter entry reports cache reads or writes, it is pinned to the provider OpenRouter named (`provider.order:[p]`, `allow_fallbacks:false`). A pinned failure drops the pin. A pinned non-2xx is sent once more to the same entry unpinned, before the asked model runs. A transport error is never resent, because it may come after the request was written.
   - Checked that `cache_control` survives every translated path to OpenRouter for Claude: Messages→Messages passes it through, Responses→Messages places breakpoints, and the chat wire adds the top-level marker. OpenRouter's catalog rows carry no Gemini or Qwen model, so no path exists yet that would need per-block breakpoints.
4. **Fan-out gate.** Fresh sibling children of one parent with the same model, tools, system prompt and `prompt_cache_key` go one at a time at first: the first is sent, and the others wait until its answer has content (5 s at most, or until their own request is cancelled). They then read that one cache write. Content means a JSON answer's first byte, or an event stream's first event past comments, pings, `message_start` and `response.created`/`in_progress`; an error event releases without warming. A prefix that had content in the last 5 min waits for nobody. The release is idempotent and deferred on every path.
5. **Forked children** keep the `x-caveman-agent` label. `signals.context_tokens` is now the request's bytes times the provider's own tokens per byte, taken from the parent session first, else from the session itself, else bytes/4.

## Live check (measured, not guessed)

`CAVEMAN_LIVE_OPENROUTER_KEY=<key file> go test ./proxy/internal/cloudlink -run TestLiveOpenRouterCache -v` runs the whole proxy with a fake Cloud that answers an OpenRouter pool entry, on a throwaway home with `CAVE_NO_KEYCHAIN`. Spend comes from `usage.cost`, capped at $0.50 per run. Two runs on 2026-10-06:

| Run | First (non-streamed fan-out) | Second (streamed fan-out, after review fixes) |
|---|---|---|
| kimi-k3 session, 4 turns (~5.2k tokens) | turns 2 and 4 read 5120; turn 3 missed on the same pinned provider (InferenceNet's implicit cache) | turns 2, 3 and 4 each read 5120 |
| | `x-session-id` on every turn, pin from turn 3 | same |
| 4 Sonnet 5.5 siblings, gated | 1 write of 6623 + 3 reads: $0.021 | 1 write + 3 reads: $0.021 |
| same shape, ungated | 4 writes of 6623: $0.067 | 4 writes: $0.067 |
| spend | $0.115 | $0.099 |

Total live spend about $0.21, plus a few sub-cent probes of OpenRouter's response shape.

## After release

Until this ships, Cloud's per-message effort switch must stay **off** on any installation serving Codex: today's hub applies a Responses effort at top level whatever the mode. Once a hub with this PR is released, the switch can be turned on for Codex. Cloud must deploy before a hub that sends `cache_ttl`. The retry here covers an older Cloud either way.

## Review

Two independent reviews. The first found two bugs, and both are fixed with regression tests. First, an update could be inserted into history already sent when the effort first changed mid tool loop. Second, adding the cache key made 429s get replayed. It also raised event-level gate release, the retry ladder blaming the wrong field, effort state crossing wires, a per-session `prompt_cache_key`, the heal dropping the key, an update ending the input, `fresh()` gaps and `cache_ttl` lookalikes. All of these were addressed in 4e4a2811. The second review found a regression: the cache key made every keyed OpenAI 4xx get replayed with the original bytes. It also found the key dropped on off and stateful-chain answers, updates sent where OpenAI forbids them, a heal regex too narrow for the actual wording, a fan-out key without `prompt_cache_key`, a pinned failure falling straight back to the asked model, a named 400 dropping an accepted field, and private references. All are fixed with regression tests in 6cc9da5f. A re-review then found three regressions, all fixed with regression tests in a7a0c4ff. First, the key was added in record mode and with routing off. Second, a 4xx naming the key was replayed with it. Third, a pinned transport error was resent. The last re-review is addressed in 2d63b338:
   - record mode gets none of the cache mechanics, with record and compress pool tests, including the OpenAI pool login key;
   - the key no longer blocks the compressed-429 replay;
   - keyed requests drop brotli;
   - a refused key latches off for the session.

## Checks

gofmt; go vet ./proxy/...; `go test -race` on gateway, cloudlink, pool and translate; tests/verify_repo.py; `node --test tests/*.js` (incl. test_no_router_internals.js); `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (186 OK); contracts validate; root `npm test` (454 pass; one flaky failure on a first run, clean on rerun).

title: feat(proxy): the translator covers all nine directions and the known wire gaps, 8-18x faster
body:
Follow-up to #1205 (base `v4-route-pool`). The translator speaks three wire formats: Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and OpenAI chat completions. This PR makes it complete and correct for all three, adds the two missing directions, and makes it fast. Plumbing only: no routing logic.

## What changed

**All nine directions.** chat→Messages and chat→Responses are new, streamed and not: tools, images, files, effort, and reasoning replay. OpenCode, Aider and other chat clients can now reach Claude and the Responses-only GPT models. A chat caller gets another host's reasoning in two fields:
- `reasoning_content`, the text to show;
- one `reasoning_details` entry `{"type":"reasoning.encrypted","data":<envelope>}`. The envelope holds the signed thinking blocks, or a Responses host's `encrypted_content` tagged with its route.

The envelope is replayed only to the host that wrote it. Every chat API strips both the envelope and the text that came with it before sending: chat hosts in the pool, and every `/chat/completions` request on the harness path, whatever the origin and with routing off too (`translate.ChatNative` in `nativeHistory`; a body without an envelope goes byte for byte). The pool now gives chat callers Messages and Responses entries; the old exclusion and its tests are gone.

**The known gaps, with fixtures (`wire_gaps_test.go`):**
1. Documents cross all four cross directions.
   - Messages `document` blocks map to Responses `input_file` and to chat `file` parts, from base64 or URL sources. `responsesPart` now reads `file_data` and `filename`.
   - When the target cannot take a document, the translation is refused, so the pool falls back instead of silently dropping it. That covers a URL or Files API document on chat, an OpenAI `file_id` on Claude, and audio.
   - Images and documents inside tool results are carried as well.
2. Structured output maps in every direction: `output_config.format` (and the beta `output_format`) ↔ `text.format` ↔ `response_format`.
3. `disable_parallel_tool_use` ↔ `parallel_tool_calls` on Messages→chat, Messages→Responses and chat→Messages.
4. A Responses `refusal` (streamed `response.refusal.delta`, or whole in `output_item.done`) reaches a Messages caller as `stop_reason: refusal` with its text kept.
5. `thinking: disabled` becomes effort `"none"` on Responses and chat, clamped to the model's catalog levels. On a model without `none`, it gets the lowest level the model has, not its default. A model the catalog does not list as reasoning (gpt-4.1) gets no reasoning field at all, since it would refuse one. An explicit `max` goes as `max` where the catalog lists it (gpt-6-sol).
6. For a Responses caller:
   - A refusal now ends in `response.incomplete` with reason `content_filter`.
   - A max-tokens stop stays `response.completed`.
   - A non-streamed answer carries `status: incomplete` and the reason for both.
   - Why: Codex accepts `response.incomplete` as the end of a turn only for the reason `interrupted`. `content_filter` goes to its dedicated content-filter path, and every other reason becomes a stream error that it retries up to five times. See [codex-rs codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs L418-L464 @18e28fe1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/18e28fe1b96db7e1d6b13584bec37c41f71b8b0e/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L418-L464).
7. Two directions were missing: chat→Messages and chat→Responses. Both are added (see above).
8. Translated answers carry ids of the runtime's own (`msg_…`, `chatcmpl-…`, `resp_…`). The host's own id stays in `Reply.UpstreamID`, which feeds the row's `upstream_response_id`.

**A relay cut anywhere in an event now surfaces as an API error** (the final review finding on #1205). A cut line is held back and never sent. A cut after a data line ends that event first. All four cut shapes are tested against decoders that mimic `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `openai-node`.

**Upstream failures on translated streams.** Every translated direction stops reading at the upstream's own failure. Before any content, the request falls back at once, even if the upstream keeps the connection open (no heartbeat commits the held error). After content, the stream returns `ErrUpstreamFailed`, as the relay does, so the pool records it as the host's own failure.

**A streamed answer ends at the upstream's terminal event.** Every streamed direction and the relay send their final event (`message_stop`, `[DONE]`, `response.completed`) as soon as the upstream's terminal event arrives, instead of waiting for the upstream to close the connection. After a chat `finish_reason`, only the usage chunk and `[DONE]` are awaited, for 100 ms at most; a relayed chat stream that never sent `[DONE]` gets one. `TestTerminalEventEndsTheStream`: with the upstream lingering 30 s after its terminal event, all nine directions deliver the final event and the usage within 50 ms.

**Text providers refuse.** A body built in another grammar has invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogate escapes (half a pair, as a cut-off long string can leave) replaced with U+FFFD, the way `encoding/json` decodes them. A body in its own grammar goes as written.

**Signature namespaces.** Thinking signatures the runtime mints name their route length-prefixed (`caveman:<n>:<route>:…`, `caveman:r1:<n>:<route>:…`, `caveman:v1:<n>:<route>:<model>`), so route ids holding `:` (`openrouter/x` and `openrouter/x:free`) never share a namespace.

## Performance
Request bodies are now read and written at the byte level (`jsonfast.go`). History is copied as it came and never decoded and re-encoded, tool schemas are canonicalized without decoding, an array is copied only when one of its elements changes, and the stream clocks run in the caller's goroutine. On the 200k bodies every direction runs under 1.3 ms per 100k tokens, even on this loaded machine.

Go benchmarks per direction (`BenchmarkTranslate`), on Claude-Code/Codex/OpenCode-shaped bodies, measured at 2fd96f8d (after every fix below). Before = base `v4-route-pool`, after = this branch, run interleaved on the same machine, best of four or more runs each. The machine was heavily loaded (load average 50 to 70, GC and scheduler time inflate every number), so treat the ratios as the reliable part.

| direction / body | ms per 100k tokens, before → after | speedup | allocs/op before → after | MB/op before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| m>m/2k | 7.72 → **1.08** | 7.1x | 230 → 147 | 0.06 → 0.03 |
| m>m/50k | 7.75 → **0.99** | 7.9x | 2803 → 763 | 1.10 → 0.31 |
| m>m/200k | 7.90 → **0.86** | 9.2x | 12721 → 3098 | 5.29 → 1.19 |
| m>c/2k | 12.46 → **1.99** | 6.3x | 1667 → 258 | 0.23 → 0.11 |
| m>c/50k | 12.72 → **0.99** | 12.8x | 4486 → 699 | 2.89 → 0.51 |
| m>c/200k | 12.25 → **1.05** | 11.7x | 15347 → 2427 | 9.84 → 1.77 |
| m>r/2k | 14.08 → **3.85** | 3.7x | 2078 → 657 | 0.26 → 0.13 |
| m>r/50k | 12.43 → **1.71** | 7.3x | 5730 → 1023 | 2.64 → 0.54 |
| m>r/200k | 12.61 → **1.27** | 10.0x | 19960 → 2500 | 10.32 → 1.78 |

| c>r/2k (new) | **3.63** | | 487 | 0.13 |

| r>m/2k | 13.56 → **5.70** | 2.4x | 2450 → 981 | 0.25 → 0.22 |

Harness-path hygiene on a 200k-token body with nothing to strip (`BenchmarkNative`, ms per request):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic/200k | 1.70 | 0.68 |
| openai/200k | 0.22 | 0.21 |
| chat/200k | (new) | 0.22 |


Cross-grammar bodies include one pass that replaces invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogates (about 0.1 ms per 100k tokens; same-grammar bodies skip it).

A tool or output schema nested 3000 levels deep (`BenchmarkDeepSchema`) costs about 2 ms a request end to end and fails the benchmark above 5 ms: `strictSchema` and `canonicalJSON` read a schema once into a tree, and past 64 levels a schema counts as not strict and keeps its bytes. Responses tools are read at the byte level too, so a schema is never decoded.

## Guarantees kept, and tests for them
- **Byte-stable prefixes.** `TestPrefixStability` grows a session in every direction and checks:
  - every earlier element of the history is byte-identical on every later turn (the runtime's own moving cache breakpoints aside);
  - every other field is unchanged.
- **No forwarded reasoning, no forged signatures.**
  - Foreign reasoning is never forwarded.
  - Signatures are never forged: a fuzz invariant checks that Anthropic never gets a thinking block it did not sign.
  - Signature-only blocks are kept.
- **Stream behaviour.**
  - The hold-until-content gate covers the new directions too.
  - A cut stream never looks complete.
  - Effort is fitted to the model.
- **Fuzz targets, one per direction pair** (`FuzzMessagesToChat` … `FuzzResponsesToResponses`).
  - Each checks: a valid body becomes a valid body or an error, there is no panic, and any answer bytes are served or refused.
  - The seed corpus runs in plain `go test`. The two inputs the fuzzer found (an unescaped prefix, an unclosed `_raw` object) are fixed and kept in `testdata/fuzz`.
  - Every target was fuzzed for 45 s with no further findings.

## Independent review
An Opus reviewer read the diff and ran probes: no JSON-validity, signature-forgery, race or arena-aliasing bugs. Two commits fix all twelve findings from its first rounds, each pinned by a test:
- a non-streaming chat caller's gate no longer opens on a heartbeat;
- a relay tail line is dropped when it does not end the stream;
- a forced tool choice drops thinking on Anthropic;
- thinking off sends `"none"` only to catalog models;
- a message-level `cache_control` is carried over;
- temperature is clamped to 0..1 and never sent with `top_p`;
- envelopes are found by their data, whatever the entry type;
- orphan tool results are sent as text;
- a manual-thinking tool turn without its thinking drops thinking;
- Responses reasoning fields go only to models that reason;
- a malformed array is never rewritten;
- `strict` is set only for schemas that meet OpenAI's strict rules.

A further round found low-severity issues, all fixed in the last commit and pinned by `TestThirdReviewFindings`, `TestFailureWithALingeringUpstream`, `TestHarnessChatCleaningOnEveryOrigin` and `BenchmarkDeepSchema`:
- `strictSchema` and `canonicalJSON` were quadratic in nesting depth; they are linear now, with a depth cap of 64;
- a translated stream that failed before content and then lingered could commit the error instead of falling back; a failure after content now returns `ErrUpstreamFailed`;
- thinking off sent `"none"` to models that do not reason;
- the harness path stripped chat envelopes only on known origins;
- invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogates went through on cross-grammar bodies;
- keys written with escapes did not match; canonical duplicate keys compared raw bytes; a crafted envelope's non-thinking blocks became thinking; a message-level `cache_control` could land on thinking; a malformed nested `reasoning_details` was rewritten; `strictSchema` misread a property named `properties` and objects without properties; route ids holding `:` could share a signature namespace.

A follow-up commit makes every streamed answer end at the upstream's terminal event (above), not at connection close.

One issue predates this PR: `responsesNativeBody` passes a non-envelope `encrypted_content` through to a restoring Responses route. It is out of scope here.

## Checks
- gofmt, go vet
- `go test -race ./proxy/... ./engine/... ./shared/...`
- `tests/verify_repo.py`
- `node --test tests/*.js`, including `test_no_router_internals.js`
- `python -m unittest`
- contracts validate
- root `npm test`

title: pi extension: tool output is shrunk to ccr:// handles in sessions without caveman_retrieve (--tools, subagents)
body:
**What happen**

The Pi extension (`dist/caveman-pi-extension.mjs`) replaces a tool result with a `ccr://` handle even when the session cannot call `caveman_retrieve`. That happens in any Pi session whose tool set is restricted:
- `pi --tools read,bash` (or any `--tools` list without `caveman_retrieve`);
- subagents that run with an agent-specific `tools:` list, which is the common case for Pi subagent extensions.

The model then sees only the handle and the instruction to call `caveman_retrieve`, which it does not have. The original output is lost to that session. In our case, a documentation-review subagent could not read the files it was asked to review, and reported every `read`/`bash` result as an unrecoverable `ccr://` placeholder.

**Expected**

Shrink a tool result only when the session can recover it, that is, when `caveman_retrieve` is in the session's active tool set. Otherwise pass the result through unchanged, like the existing "direct mode" fallback.

**Repro**

macOS, Pi 1.0.4, `@caveman-ai/cli` 1.3.1, local proxy running with `CAVEMAN_RECOVERY=mcp`, extension loaded:

```
pi --no-session --tools read,bash --print \
  "Run: seq 1 3000 | sed 's/^/line /'. Then quote line 2999."
```

```
Got:   tool result = [CommandResult] ... full: ccr://ccr_obj_69bea8c9... 
       recover: call caveman_retrieve with recovery_handle="ccr://..."
       model: "The output was replaced by a placeholder ... I don't have caveman_retrieve."
Want:  the original 3000 lines (or a shrink that only happens when caveman_retrieve is callable)
```

In sessions without `--tools`, `caveman_retrieve` is active, and in our earlier tests the model recovered shrunk output byte-exact (different prompts, same setup).

**Where**

`index.ts` registers the tool, then `pi.on("tool_result", ...)` calls `shrinkToolResult` for every tool except `caveman_retrieve`. Nothing checks whether `caveman_retrieve` is active for this session. Pi's extension API exposes `pi.getActiveTools()` (the set declared to the model), so a guard such as

```ts
pi.on("tool_result", GUARD_tool_result((event) =>
  event.toolName === RECOVERY_TOOL || !pi.getActiveTools().includes(RECOVERY_TOOL)
    ? undefined
    : shrinkToolResult(bridge, sessionId, event)));
```

would keep restricted sessions on direct output. (If you support Pi's codemode exposure, where a tool can be callable without being in the active set, the check may need to include that too. We have not tested that case.)

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Pi (pi.dev) 1.0.4, via the bundled Pi extension

**Version / install method**

`@caveman-ai/cli` 1.3.1 (`npm install -g`), `caveman setup --install`, extension loaded from `dist/caveman-pi-extension.mjs`.

title: pi extension: 'pass-through … no compat mount' warning for a provider whose baseUrl already targets the Caveman proxy (/w/pi)
body:
## Summary

The pi extension in `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.1 warns:

```
Caveman: pass-through for lego-claude/eu.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 (no compat mount named "lego-claude" in the local proxy; add compat.lego-claude.base_url to caveman.yaml to route it); no compression
```

This happens even though the provider's `baseUrl` **already points at the local Caveman proxy wedge** (`http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/pi`), and every request does go through the proxy. In the proxy's `requests` table, these requests are still recorded with `compression_eligible = 1`. So "pass-through … no compression" is misleading. The extension treats its own gateway URL as the provider's "original" upstream, fails the compat-mount lookup for a non-built-in provider name, and warns.

## Setup

Common for upgrades from 1.x, where pointing a custom provider at `/w/pi` was the way to route it.

`~/.pi/agent/models.json`:

```json
{ "providers": { "lego-claude": { "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/pi", "api": "anthropic-messages", "models": [{ "id": "eu.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5" }] } } }
```

`~/.caveman/caveman.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  anthropic:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18788
```

## Expected

Either:

- detect `isLoopbackUrl(original)` plus the gateway's own `/w/pi` prefix, and treat the model as already routed: no warning, or an info message saying "already routed via the Caveman proxy"; or
- if 2.x needs the real upstream in `baseUrl` plus a `compat.<name>.base_url` mount, say so. For example: "provider baseUrl points at the Caveman proxy itself; set it to the real upstream and add compat.lego-claude.base_url". Documenting the 1.x → 2.x migration for custom providers would also help.

## Environment

`@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.1, binaries `bin-v2.0.2`, pi 1.0.4, macOS arm64. Upgraded today from CLI 1.3.1 / `bin-v1.1.4`.
