title: OpenCode plugin (caveman-native.js) flashes console windows on Windows: missing windowsHide
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the OpenCode plugin generated by `caveman enable opencode`
(`~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman-native.js`) opens a visible console window every
time it runs the native hook. The windows pop up and close over and over during a
session. Their title is the node.exe path, for example
`C:\Users\<user>\.nvm\versions\node\v22.x\bin\node.exe`.

## Cause

The plugin calls `execFileSync` to run
`node.exe .../@caveman-ai/cli/dist/index.js native-hook` on every OpenCode event:
prompt submit, tool call and bash command. None of the three `execFileSync` calls sets
`windowsHide: true`.

If the parent process has no console of its own, Windows gives every console child
process a new console window. This is the case when OpenCode runs headless or under a
terminal multiplexer or host app such as Orca or wmux. The result is one flashing window
per hook call.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 with Node installed through nvm-windows.
2. Run `caveman enable opencode`.
3. Start an OpenCode session from a host that does not give OpenCode its own console,
   for example Orca or wmux.
4. Send prompts or run tools. A console window flashes on every event.

## Expected

No visible windows. The hook should run silently.

## Fix

Add `windowsHide: true` to the options of every `execFileSync` call in the generated
plugin:

    execFileSync(nodePath, [cliPath, "native-hook", ...], {
      // ...existing options
      windowsHide: true,
    });

The option is ignored on non-Windows platforms, so the change is safe everywhere.
I patched the three calls by hand and the windows stopped appearing. The patch is lost
whenever `caveman enable opencode` regenerates the file, so it needs to go into the
template.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Node: v22 (nvm-windows)
- Client: OpenCode, run under Orca / wmux

title: proxy forwards x-api-key over Authorization when both arrive, so bearer-only gateways can't be routed (and pi extension rejects the empty x-api-key workaround)
body:
## Summary

With `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.1 / `bin-v2.0.2`, a pi provider for an Anthropic-compatible gateway that accepts **only** `Authorization: Bearer` can't be routed through the Caveman proxy:

1. pi (`authHeader: true`) sends the key both as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and as `x-api-key: <key>`.
2. When both arrive, the proxy forwards only `x-api-key` upstream, so the gateway answers `401 Invalid authentication`.
3. The 1.x workaround was a provider header `"x-api-key": ""`, which made the proxy forward the bearer. In 2.x the pi extension rejects it: `Caveman: pass-through for lego-claude/… (provider headers x-api-key are not forwarded; the proxy cannot preserve this authentication override; keep the provider direct); no compression`.

So such a provider can go direct (works, no compression), or be routed and fail with 401. There's no configuration that both routes and authenticates.

## Measurements

1-token requests to an Anthropic-compatible gateway (Bedrock-backed) that only accepts the bearer:

| Path | Auth headers sent | Result |
|---|---|---|
| upstream direct | bearer + `x-api-key: <key>` | 200 |
| upstream direct | bearer + empty `x-api-key` | 200 |
| proxy `/w/pi/anthropic` | bearer + empty `x-api-key` | 200 |
| proxy `/w/pi/anthropic` | bearer + `x-api-key: <key>` (what pi sends without the override) | **401** |
| proxy `/w/pi/anthropic` | `x-api-key` only | 401 |

`caveman.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  anthropic:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18788   # local proxy chain in front of the gateway
```

Provider: `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:18788`, `api: anthropic-messages`, `authHeader: true`, `headers: {"x-api-key": ""}`.

## Expected

One of:

- When both credentials arrive with the same value, the proxy forwards `Authorization` too, or prefers it, as the provider's `authHeader: true` asks.
- A per-provider or per-mount option, e.g. `providers.anthropic.auth: bearer` or `compat.<name>.auth: bearer`, that forwards the bearer and drops `x-api-key`. The extension's header check would then accept the route.

## Related

- #1212: the misleading "no compat mount" remedy for a provider that already targets `/w/pi`. For bearer-only gateways that remedy can't work either.

## Environment

`@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.1, `bin-v2.0.2`, pi 1.0.4, macOS arm64.

title: Clarify Pixel model defaults and separate request opt-out from skill conversion
body:
## What happens

The current Pixel documentation describes model admission as requiring an explicit allowlist. In the implementation, an unset or empty allowlist selects built-in model bases instead. This makes the documented default difficult to interpret for an operator who wants Pixel disabled while retaining Compress and CCR.

This is a documentation/behavior-contract report. Pixel request mode must still be selected; I am not claiming default Compress mode silently sends images.

## Current source and documentation

Checked against current `main`, commit `99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f`, on 2026-10-07. Documentation and relevant source bytes were matched to the current GitHub Git blobs.

- [Pixel documentation](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/docs/technical/toon-and-pixel.md#pixel-context) describes explicit model allowlisting.
- [Configuration defaults](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/docs/technical/configuration.md#keys-and-defaults) list `think.pixel.models=[]`.
- [AllowedModelBases](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/engine/pixel/applicability.go#L13-L29) returns `claude-fable-5` and `gpt-5.6` when `CAVE_PIXEL_MODELS` is absent or blank. Its disabling sentinel handling accepts `off`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0`.
- [CLI capability parsing](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L3534-L3540) and [runtime mapping](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L3730-L3745) turn an empty model array into no explicit model environment value.

## Expected clarification

If built-in defaults are intentional, document them and the existing durable request opt-out:

```sh
caveman tools config set think.pixel.models off
```

Explain that this persists `["off"]`, higher-priority environment overrides can still change the request allowlist, and this setting does not control file conversion.

Document the independent skill-install path as well. `skills install/add` convert to Pixel unless `--no-pixel` is supplied. Operators currently need that option on each installation; switching request mode to Compress or disabling request model admission does not disable skill-file conversion.

The [skills installer source](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L2213-L2223) shows this separate default.

A supported persistent preference for plain-text skill installations would help Codex users avoid local generated-JS patches that updates overwrite. This is an optional feature request, not a claim that no request opt-out exists. Retaining Pixel code in binaries and YAML limitations caused by custom patches are not reported as upstream bugs.

If explicit operator allowlisting is the intended contract instead, make empty/unset admission deny models and update the current defaults/tests accordingly.

## Verification boundary

Source and documentation inspection only. No provider request, native hook or model-quality benchmark was run for this report. The issue is not specific to Codex, although plain-text skill installation is useful in a Codex workflow. The setup motivating this feedback is Codex Desktop on Windows, with `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.0.1.

title: [Enhancement] Add a unified architecture map with component and data boundaries
body:
## Request

Add one unified architecture map near the start of the README, with a link to the detailed technical documentation.

The existing [architecture page](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f/docs/technical/architecture.md) already explains the local request path. A single broader map would help readers place the other mechanisms relative to the agent, tools and model before reading feature details.

## Why it helps

During a Codex adaptation, several names were easy to conflate:

- Output Shrink reduces finite command output or a saved log before the agent consumes it. Native catalog Shrink reduces MCP tool definitions.
- Proxy Compress transforms eligible content in an outgoing provider request. Record forwards that request without Engine compression.
- Pixel is an optional text-to-image transport path, not a third Engine mode.
- CCR stores recoverable originals. Cavemem provides durable memory. Middleware uses a separate scoped recovery store.
- Browse has its own browser/CDP path. SDK middleware is a separate application integration. Cloud inference routing and Cloud control/metadata sync have different data boundaries.

A diagram can show these distinctions and their conditional connections without requiring the reader to infer architecture from the order of feature sections. This is documentation feedback, not a claim that these paths fail in upstream Codex support.

## Example

![Architecture example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/striges88-bit/filins-stack/bf4e0e1d8d44440ed702526c7af090f4c718b78a/bundles/caveman/assets/architecture.png)

The example has 19 main nodes and 31 selected conditional flow edges. Its inventory contains 125 source-backed component records and 207 typed conditional relationships. The map draws the principal flows; it does not draw all inventory relationships.

It is based on documentation and source at `99aafe151a1be72be783e662858e8a0955add59f`. Source links are included per inventory record. Local exclusion badges reflect our profile, where Cloud, Cavemem and Pixel are disabled. An upstream version should replace those local badges with neutral optional-component labels.

[Editable SVG](https://github.com/striges88-bit/filins-stack/blob/bf4e0e1d8d44440ed702526c7af090f4c718b78a/bundles/caveman/assets/architecture.svg), [source inventory](https://github.com/striges88-bit/filins-stack/blob/bf4e0e1d8d44440ed702526c7af090f4c718b78a/bundles/caveman/assets/components.json), [renderer](https://github.com/striges88-bit/filins-stack/blob/bf4e0e1d8d44440ed702526c7af090f4c718b78a/bundles/caveman/assets/render_architecture.py), and [coverage checks](https://github.com/striges88-bit/filins-stack/blob/bf4e0e1d8d44440ed702526c7af090f4c718b78a/bundles/caveman/assets/coverage.json).

The SVG is editable. The renderer and source inventory are provided with the bundle's license and third-party notices. The example contains no private paths, credentials, transcripts or CCR data. Configuration and availability are explicitly distinguished from runtime activation. No token-saving percentage is asserted.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Place Output Shrink, catalog Shrink, proxy Compress/Record and Pixel at their actual boundaries.
- Show CCR recovery separately from durable memory and middleware recovery.
- Include native hooks/Core, delegation, Browse, SDK/middleware, Learn/accounting, Cloud inference and Cloud control paths.
- Mark optional paths and state what data crosses each boundary.
- Link the diagram to detailed configuration, recovery and component documentation.

title: fix(proxy): support android executable identity
body:
## What happen

`cave wrap <agent>` starts a Caveman proxy, then blames the listener it just started:

```
→ started Caveman proxy on 127.0.0.1:8787 (compress)
caveman · owner: unknown · opencode
something else is listening on 127.0.0.1:8787 — this session is not compressed; caveman will not restart a process it does not own
```

The session then runs direct — no compression, no metering — against a proxy `wrap` spawned seconds earlier. Reproduced on Termux (Android) with opencode; every wrapped agent is affected.

## Expected

`caveman · compress · opencode` and no foreign-process line: the proxy `wrap` starts is certified as its own.

## Before/after example

```
Input: cave wrap opencode
Got:   owner: unknown → foreign-process → direct launch (no compression)
Want:  owner: wrap, mode compress → compressed session
```

## Root cause

`runstate.processExecutable` handled `linux`/`darwin`/`windows` only. A local Termux build carries `runtime.GOOS == "android"`, so the executable-identity probe failed, `caveman-proxy status` always answered `owner: unknown`, and `wrap` read the listener it had just spawned as a foreign process.

Not a double launch: one proxy process, one `→ started` line (checked with a manual e2e, run-state pid counted before/after). Run state is also written before `srv.Serve`, so the port-accept window is not in play either. The repo's own `TestProcessProbes` and `TestRunStatusRequiresThisListenerGeneration` fail on this host without the fix.

## Fix

`processExecutableFor(goos, pid)`: android shares the linux `/proc/<pid>/exe` read, darwin/windows keep their probe, unknown platforms still fail closed.

## Test added

- `proxy/internal/runstate/runstate_test.go` — identity resolves on android and linux and agrees for the same pid; an unknown platform still errors (red on main under Termux)
- `packages/cli/tests/wrap-restart.runtime.mjs` — "a wrap that starts the proxy itself reports it as its own, once": owned banner, exactly one spawn, no foreign-process line, agent env routed through that proxy (red on main)

## Platform

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: opencode (any wrapped agent) on Termux/Android

Hosts: Android/Termux only. linux/darwin/windows behaviour is unchanged.

## Version / install method

Local build from `main` (`scripts/install-local-cli.sh` / `go build`).

## Verification

- `go test ./proxy/...` green except `internal/nativehook` and `internal/nativeruntime`, which hardcode `mkdir /tmp/...` and fail on Termux regardless of this change
- `packages/cli` runtime suite: failure set unchanged (8 pre-existing `#!/usr/bin/env` stub-agent failures on this host), new test passes
- Local runs of both suites also need the fchmodat2 gate from #1186: unmerged `main` SIGSYS-crashes the proxy on Android at SQLite chmod. Gate not included here — it has its own PR.

title: perf(proxy): gateway hot path
body:
The local proxy's request path, made faster without changing anything it stores.

## What changed

- **Rows are finished off the request path** (`gateway.Config.AsyncRecord`, on in `caveman-proxy serve`). `record()` builds the row and returns; the request token count (canonical JSON plus the o200k count), the SQLite write and the Cloud observe run after the handler returns. Neither the client's connection nor a stream's final chunk waits on them any more. Each count runs on its own goroutine, and one writer hands finished rows to the store in record order, batched. Rows that are already finished never wait behind one still being counted. At most 64 rows are in flight: a full queue makes the next record wait and never drops a row. A panic while finishing or writing rows drops those rows, as a panicking handler did, and does not reach the process. `Server.Flush` waits until every recorded row is written; session receipts call it before they read usage, so the last request is counted. `Server.Close` writes the rest; `serve` calls it after the HTTP server shuts down and before the store closes. With `AsyncRecord` off nothing changes. A pass-through request is canonicalized once instead of twice.
- **SQLite**: `Store.RecordBatch` commits with one transaction and one prepared statement, falling back to `Record` per row if the transaction fails. It commits with `synchronous(NORMAL)` on its own connection, under WAL. NORMAL syncs at checkpoints instead of on every commit.
  - **Durability:** a power loss or OS crash can drop the last request-row batches committed before it. A process crash or a clean exit loses none.
  - **Scope:** the connection goes back to the pool at its previous level, so every other table keeps FULL: recovery originals, the prefix-replacement cache and middleware state.
  - **Middleware writes:** the batch takes the middleware writer slot, so they queue instead of sleeping in SQLite's busy handler.
- **Upstream keep-alive**: up to 256 idle connections per provider host (1024 in all) instead of Go's default of 2. The 90 s idle timeout still applies.
- **Usage parsing**: `ParseUsageBytes` skips stream lines that spell none of the keys the usage merge reads (text and tool deltas). Lines with a `\u` escape or under a `message_*` event name are still decoded.
- **Hashing and inspect**: the body is hashed once on a pass-through, and the signing context gets that digest. `InspectRequest` validates the body in one pass that accepts exactly what `json.Valid` accepts, then decodes only the top-level fields it reads; for messages and input it reads only the length. Bodies that could spell a key the nested pricing walk matches, or that hold an out-of-range number, are decoded whole as before. The frozen-prefix scan jumps between quotes with `IndexByte` and stops copying messages.

## Numbers

Medians of 6 rounds that alternate base and this branch round by round, on one machine shared with other work (load average 40–100). The spread is wide; p comes from benchstat.

**Request path** (`BenchmarkProxyHandler`): one record-mode Messages request through the whole handler against an in-process upstream, timed until the handler returns, which is when the client's connection is free again. Each request starts once the previous row is written, like a single agent. GOMAXPROCS=4.

| Request | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2k tokens, non-stream | 1.54 ms | 0.23 ms | −85% (p=0.002) |
| 2k tokens, stream | 1.46 ms | 0.67 ms | −54% (p=0.002) |
| 50k tokens, non-stream | 14.5 ms | 1.86 ms | −87% (p=0.002) |
| 50k tokens, stream | 17.6 ms | 2.48 ms | −86% (p=0.002) |
| 200k tokens, non-stream | 66.2 ms | 4.86 ms | −93% (p=0.002) |
| 200k tokens, stream | 72.5 ms | 7.29 ms | −90% (p=0.002) |
| allocations, 200k | 866k | 9.1k | −99% |

**Each piece** (GOMAXPROCS=1):

| Piece | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `InspectRequest`, 200k | 5.72 ms, 8,193 allocs | 0.81 ms, 263 allocs (p=0.004) |
| `InspectRequest`, 50k | 1.23 ms | 0.25 ms |
| frozen-prefix evidence, 200k | 9.5 ms, 2.1 MB | 2.8 ms, 1.3 MB |
| usage parse, 2,000-delta stream | 6.27 ms, 64k allocs | 3.24 ms, 4.2k allocs |
| request token count, 200k (now off the path) | 96.9 ms | 59.0 ms (one canonicalization) |
| SQLite insert per row | 165 µs (`Record`, FULL) | 13–19 µs (`RecordBatch`, 8–64 rows, NORMAL) |

`InspectRequest` against the alternatives at 200k: this PR takes 0.72 ms, `json.Valid` alone takes 1.71 ms, and `json.Unmarshal` into `map[string]json.RawMessage` takes 2.77 ms. So encoding/json can't produce the same result in less time.

**End to end with the real SQLite store** (`BenchmarkServeRecordMode`). The time per request includes writing every row, because the store is closed inside the timed region.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2k, one caller, 8 cores | 2.24 ms | 0.54 ms (−76%, p=0.002) |
| 50k, one caller, 8 cores | 16.8 ms | 3.16 ms (−81%, p=0.002) |
| 2k, eight callers, 8 cores | 695 µs | 406 µs (not significant, p=0.13) |
| 50k, eight callers, 8 cores | 10.6 ms | 5.95 ms (not significant, p=0.39) |
| 2k, one caller, 1 core | 2.19 ms | 2.37 ms (not significant) |

The token count still costs the same CPU; it just no longer sits on the request path. On a single core it has nowhere else to run, so that last row does not move.

**Upstream pool:** eight concurrent callers over three rounds opened 20 upstream connections before and 8 after. `TestDefaultUpstreamClientKeepsConnectionsForConcurrentCallers` fails on Go's default pool.

## Proof that nothing stored changed

- `TestStoredRowsGolden` pins every column of seven stored rows to the values the previous build wrote: Messages, a Messages stream, Responses, a Responses stream, a chat stream, a provider error and a ChatGPT subscription call. It covers hashes, frozen-prefix evidence, usage, request token counts, prices and dollars, and checks rows finished both inline and async.
- `TestHotPathFactsGolden` pins the body hash, prefix evidence, inspected metadata and request token counts of 2k, 50k and 200k agent requests to the previous build's values.
- `TestAsyncRecordRowsMatchInline` compares async rows with inline rows across record, compress (with booked savings), original-bytes fallback, upstream error and ChatGPT.
- Ordering, batching, drain-on-close, records after close, Flush and panics are covered by `TestAsyncRecordKeepsRequestOrder`, `TestRecorderBatchesFinishedRows`, `TestAsyncRecordCloseDrainsQueuedRows`, `TestAsyncRecordFlushWaitsForRecordedRows`, `TestUsageAfterFlushWritesPendingRowsFirst` and `TestRecorderSurvivesPanics`. `TestRecordBatchStoresWhatRecordStores` checks that a batch stores the same columns as one `Record` per row.
- Differential tests and fuzz targets compare each fast path with the code it replaces: `inspectObject` against `json.Unmarshal` plus the old reads (validity and metadata), the usage line filter against decoding every line, and the `IndexByte` string scan against the byte loop. The fuzz runs: about 7.7M inputs for `FuzzInspectObject`, 10.8M for `FuzzUsageLineFilter` and 3.7M for `FuzzScanJSONString`. None found a difference.
- Mutation check: each new test fails when the value it guards is changed.
- `go test -race -timeout 40m ./...`passes, and `go test -race ./proxy/... ./shared/...` passes again after the review fixes.

## Not in this PR

- The o200k count itself, now off the request path but still the largest CPU cost per row: about 25–45 ms for a 200k request. The stored numbers need it, so it stays. A faster exact pre-tokenizer is the next lever.
- Buffered non-stream responses, which stay as they are. They make a broken body a clean 502.
- A run of the external gateway bench against this branch. The numbers above are Go benchmarks on the shared machine.

title: feat(cli): Cloud commands move to cvm; caveman keeps sign-in
body:
**Do not merge until `@caveman-ai/cloud` is on npm.** Merging first would leave users with no Cloud CLI.

## What changes

Caveman Cloud's commands leave `caveman` for a separate CLI, `cvm` (`npm i -g @caveman-ai/cloud`), built in the Cloud repo so its command list always matches the server. `caveman` keeps `login`, `logout`, `whoami` and everything local.

- A moved command prints one line and exits 2, bare or under `cloud`:
  `caveman traces moved to cvm. Install: npm i -g @caveman-ai/cloud, then run: cvm traces list`
- Commands cvm has no equivalent for (`keys create|revoke`, `billing charges`, `traces export`, `agent run`) say they were removed and point at the dashboard.
- Any other `caveman cloud <verb…>` prints the moved line with the same arguments.
- Kept, because they work on local files: `sync`, `receipts verify`, `audit import`, `audit eval-import`.
- `mcp-serve` / `cloud mcp-serve` run `cvm mcp` when cvm is installed, so agents registered earlier keep working. This is the only forwarding.
- MCP setup (`setup --agent-native`, `tools mcp install --server caveman-cloud`) registers `node <cvm.mjs> mcp`. Without cvm installed, it stops before writing anything and prints the install line.
- Removed: the in-CLI Cloud MCP server (`src/agent-mcp.ts`) and the trace, experiment, plan, billing, key and receipts-export code and tests.

## Two fixes found on the way

- `caveman login --instance` refused every real grant from a private install, because Cloud sends `gateway_url` whenever the install sets a gateway URL. The private path still ignores the gateway and still refuses gateway keys.
- After `logout`, `CAVE_TOKEN` + `CAVE_API_URL` failed with "Invalid URL" (`baseURL: ""` beat the environment).

## Checks

- `pnpm lint`: clean.
- `pnpm test` (with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset): 1149 tests, 1129 pass, 18 skipped, 2 fail. Both failures are `native-enable` tests that need 127.0.0.1:8787 free; they fail the same way on `main` on the machine that ran this.
- Live: this branch's `caveman login --instance` against a local Cloud stack, then `cvm` on the stored credential with no second login.

## Open for the maintainer

- `setup --agent-native` now needs cvm installed. Skipping the Cloud MCP instead would need a bundle journal format change that released CLIs cannot read.
- Windows MCP registration is tested with a stand-in shim on macOS only.
- `init`, bare `doctor`, `dev` and `deploy aws` still call or mention Cloud and were left alone.

title: Lead README install with the proxy; native install ships the voice skills
body:
## README
- `## Install` is now proxy-only (`npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli && caveman setup --install`, then `caveman claude`), with the Node.js 22.13+ requirement.
- The skill moves to its own section, "Small rock: the skill" (output compression alone), with the skills.sh badge and the collapsed "Other ways in" block.

## CLI
`caveman <agent>` (first run) and `caveman enable <agent>` now also write the `output` skill suite (`caveman`, `ultracave`, `megacave`) into the Claude Code / Codex user skills dir.
- Create-only (`wx`): an existing `SKILL.md` is never overwritten or claimed. Codex also skips a skill already in `~/.agents/skills`.
- Ownership is a `~/.caveman/integrations/<agent>.voice-skills.json` sidecar, not native-journal operations, so an edited or deleted skill never reads `degraded`.
- `caveman disable <agent>` removes only regular files still byte-identical to what was written; the record is always dropped.
- Fail-open: a skill write or removal failure never fails enable, disable, repair or the launch.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.55.0 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

title: Proxy-first README install; native install ships the voice skills
body:
Follow-up to #1221, which merged with only its first commit.

## README
- `## Install` is proxy-only (`npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli && caveman setup --install`, then `caveman claude`), with the Node.js 22.13+ requirement.
- The skill moves to its own section, "Small rock: the skill" (output compression alone), with the skills.sh badge and the collapsed "Other ways in" block.
- The README does not yet say the proxy install brings `/caveman`: that needs a CLI release containing this PR (npm is at 2.0.1).

## CLI
- `fix(cli): disable all Claude profiles` (was local-only on main), fixture conflict resolved against the v3 sweep.
- `caveman <agent>` (first run) and `caveman enable <agent>` also write the `output` skill suite (`caveman`, `ultracave`, `megacave`) into the Claude Code / Codex user skills dir.
  - Create-only (`wx`): an existing `SKILL.md` is never overwritten or claimed. Codex also skips a skill already in `~/.agents/skills`.
  - Ownership is a `~/.caveman/integrations/<agent>.voice-skills.json` sidecar, not native-journal operations, so an edited or deleted skill never reads `degraded`.
  - `caveman disable <agent>` removes only regular files still byte-identical to what was written, in both the single-journal and all-Claude-profiles paths; the record is always dropped.
  - Fail-open: a skill write or removal failure never fails enable, disable, repair or the launch.

Capability promotion: byte-safe clause, native enable path. The skill files are inert until invoked and change no request bytes.

## Verification
- `native-enable` 73/73, `agent-native` 10/10, `skills` 14/14, `skills-add` 10/10, `agent-shortcut` 14/14; `tests/installer` 434/434; `tests/verify_repo.py` passes.

## What is in it

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `acad8868` | Merge `origin/main` into `v4` (9 conflicted files) |
| `93f6cc5c` | docs: hosted sign-in is open when the server says so |
| `c51e9a09` | Merge `v4-gateway-speed` (#1198, #1205, #1210, #1219) |
| `dd9a40a3` | Merge `v4-cache` (#1209) |

Each of the five PR heads (`18b6d957`, `5c94f77f`, `abde736a`, `c4a33ee7`, `f052a474`) is an ancestor of the tip, so merging this closes them.

## Sign-in

`caveman login` stays open on hosted: `blockCloudLoginWhileBeta` and the "still in beta" text have zero hits in the merged tree. The server decides; a 403 `cave_device_login_disabled` prints "Sign-in is not open on <host> yet." Two stale lines (`packages/cli/README.md`, `SECURITY.md`) were corrected.

Proven with the built CLI from this branch against a hosted-shaped Caveman Cloud stack (identity on, open sign-up, free personal organization): `login` → browser approval → tokens, then `whoami` returned the person's own organization, plan `free`, deployment `hosted`.

## Conflict resolutions worth a reviewer's eye

- `proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go`: the raw retry is skipped for main's rate-limit 429 and for the stack's 429 on the asked model after a route edit; the retry signs the keyed original's hash; the response stream keeps the stack's served-model reader with main's extra `streamResponse` argument.
- `proxy/internal/gateway/chatgpt.go`: the stack's off-path accounting (`finishRecord`) now works on main's decoded zstd bodies.
- `proxy/internal/store/store.go`: the stack's shared insert plus main's `cache_bust_cause` column (75 placeholders).
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts`: main's OpenCode route helpers with v4's `plan` argument; v4's quiet enable/disable with main's `allClaudeProfiles`; main's OpenCode warnings go into v4's status grid.
- `install.sh` / `install.ps1`: main's `installer/install.js` path, v3.2.0 pin and npm 12 `--allow-git=root`, with v4's first run (`caveman setup`) after it. The PowerShell path was edited by hand and not executed locally.

## Checked locally (macOS)

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...`: 60 packages ok
- `go test -race ./proxy/internal/gateway/...`: ok, 3 runs
- CLI: 1284 tests, 1279 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped; `test:fast` ok
- SDK 276/276, middleware 136/136, root `npm test` 581 pass
- `tests/*.js` 30/30 including `test_no_router_internals.js` and `test_no_unscoped_npx.js`

Not run locally: the `release-shape` job (needs zig), Windows, the Docker image.

## Open before a release from this line

- No test covers main's cache tripwire and raw pin together with the stack's route edits. A raw retry caused by a route edit pins the conversation raw; pool-served requests bypass the tripwire and the pin.
- Main installs the voice skills on every native enable; v4's module apply writes only what its plan showed, so `caveman setup` / `caveman on` do not install them.

- #1198's failing `macos` check was `TestMiddlewareAcceptanceDefaultDeadlineIncludesQueue` running 0.69 ms over its budget, in a package neither side touched.

title: Caveman v4: Auto routing, cache follow-ups, cache warming, gateway hot path
body:
One branch for v4. It carries everything on the `v4` integration line (#1198, #1205, #1209, #1210, #1219, and main at 3.2.0 via #1232) plus the Auto model and cache warming work that was only local (`v4-auto-warm`), merged and reconciled. Supersedes #1232.

## What is new since the stacked PRs

- **Merge of `v4-auto-warm`** (Auto picker model, routing on subscriptions, predictive cache warming, two Anthropic pricing fixes). 11 conflicted files; both sides kept.
- **Cache follow-ups run on Auto.** #1209's tests named a model and expected the route stage to act; routing now runs only on `caveman-auto`, so they send Auto. No assertion loosened. The Auto path on `/chatgpt` now heals a refused `configuration_update`.
- **Rate limits.** The ChatGPT-login Auto path replayed every 4xx, so a plan at its usage limit had each request sent twice. Rate-limit 429, 401 and 403 are returned as they come; a replay that is itself a 429 still rejects the routed decision.
- **Model stickiness** (a model switch re-writes the whole cached prefix). A turn that starts during a Cloud pause keeps its answer for the turn; a transient Cloud failure runs the model the session was last sent on and gives way to the fallback if that model fails; a 4xx the original bytes get too no longer demotes the turn.
- **Cache warming limits.** At most two warms at once, up to 5s early jitter, credential pause on a 5xx.
- **CLI.** A login/logout sync followed by `disable` or a repair replaced `settings.json` / `opencode.json` with the pre-enable backup, dropping what the user added since; it now merges. No Auto under OpenCode Go. `disable` across Claude profiles removes Caveman's Auto keys and a saved choice of Auto from each. Logout clears a saved Auto choice made in a session-only `caveman claude`.
- `caveman-auto[1m]` is read as Auto by the proxy.

## Verification

- Go `./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...`: 52 packages pass. `-race` on `proxy/internal/gateway` and `proxy/internal/cloudlink`: clean.
- CLI suite: 1,300 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. Installer + hooks: 581 pass, 2 skipped. `tests/verify_repo.py`: passes.
- Live, signed out (no `cloud.json`), proxy built from this branch, real Claude Max and ChatGPT logins: Claude Code on a named model and on `caveman-auto[1m]` answers; turn 2 reads the cache (35,543 and 34,328 tokens read); Codex on `/chatgpt` answers.
- Five independent reviews (signed-out passthrough, cache safety, 429/error risk, CLI wiring, translator + hot path) found no P0. The P1s they found are fixed here, each with a test that failed first; the proxy fixes were reviewed again and that review's findings fixed.

## Not in this PR — decisions for the owner

- **Cache warming is on by default, signed out included.** It sends `max_tokens: 0` replays on the user's own key or subscription while a session idles, and continues for a while after the agent closes. Now capped and backed off, but still new background traffic. `CAVEMAN_CACHE_WARM` is read only at proxy start; the live switch is `caveman off waste-fixes`.
- **Auto has no proxy-side floor on model changes between turns.** Cache cost under Auto depends on Cloud's ranker weighing the warm cache.
- ChatGPT-login Auto still has no session `prompt_cache_key` and no fan-out stagger (the API-key path has both).
- The translator drops some Responses state it cannot carry (`conversation`, `prompt`, `local_shell`, `web_search`) when a request is served on another provider, instead of refusing.
- `caveman off routing` does not clear a saved Auto choice in an agent that is not natively wired.
- Version metadata is still 3.2.0 / cli 2.1.0; no bump or tag here.
- CodeQL will report one new alert, `go/weak-sensitive-data-hashing` at `proxy/internal/cloudlink/events.go:123`: an in-memory SHA-256 fingerprint of the login used to tag events, never stored or sent. False positive.

title: fix(mem): retry SQLite contention longer
body:
## Summary

- extend RetryOnBusy's wall-clock budget from 5 to 30 seconds
- document that retry callers must be idempotent
- add a regression test where SQLite consumes its full 5-second busy timeout before returning SQLITE_BUSY
- update the memory concurrency documentation and test comment

## Why

On Windows, TestConcurrentRememberSubprocesses lost 2 of 24 concurrent writes to SQLITE_BUSY. A SQLite call can consume the entire 5-second busy timeout before returning, which also exhausted the old 5-second retry budget and prevented a second attempt.

The affected schema operations and Remember insert are idempotent, so a bounded longer retry window resolves cross-process contention without changing the single-writer or WAL configuration.

## Validation

- The same behavioral fix passed all checks in [francojeferson/caveman#1](https://github.com/francojeferson/caveman/pull/1).
- The merged fork commit passed both [CI](https://github.com/francojeferson/caveman/actions/runs/37876777511) and [engine-ci](https://github.com/francojeferson/caveman/actions/runs/37876777489), including the full Windows job.

title: feat(cli): one-command setup that finds logins, survives npx and a taken port
body:
Draft, opened to get the Windows / macOS / Linux `first-run` CI job on this branch. Not for merge until reviewed.

## What changes for someone installing

- **One command, one key.** `npx @caveman-ai/cli` (or `caveman setup`) opens on a single screen: what was found, what setup will do in a few rows, Enter applies. Customize and Details (the full file plan) are one key away. Before: three Enter screens, a 16-line file plan, a dozen raw download lines.
- **Finds logins.** Every Claude Code config dir Claude Code has signed in from (`~/.claude`, `~/.claude-*`), how Codex signs in, and API keys exported in the shell. `caveman enable claude` wires every Claude profile in one journal; re-running setup wires one that appeared later. Look-alike dirs (`~/.claude-mem`) and profiles that point at their own gateway are left alone.
- **Found API keys are offered, never taken.** `k` ticks them for Auto's pool; off by default because Auto can spend on a key it is given.
- **Sign-in reads as what happened.** A Cloud that is down says so (`api.caveman.so is not answering right now (HTTP 503).`) instead of `device authorization failed: HTTP 503`; setup still finishes and names `caveman login`.
- **Ends by offering to start the agent.**

## Stability fixes found on the way

- **npx cache paths.** Setup run from `npx` (which `install.sh` does) wired the runner's cache path into every agent: the shrink hook, the native-hook adapter, bundled plugins. A cache clean left each session with hooks pointing at nothing. A runner now never wires: it installs this CLI version with npm when it is not installed (globally, or under `~/.caveman/cli` when the prefix is not writable) and has that copy do the wiring. If npm cannot install it, nothing is written.
- **Port 8787 held by something else** (wrangler dev, a container). Setup wired agents to it anyway. A first setup now moves the runtime to the next free port and keeps it in `cloud.json` (`localPort`); wiring, the session hook and `caveman start` read it.
- **Windows: Claude Code read as "wired but not runnable".** Its npm shim forwards to a native `claude.exe`, and the launcher refused every non-Node shim. Found by the new `first-run` job; such a shim now runs its executable directly.
- `install.sh` / `install.ps1` name the Node 22.13 floor instead of handing a Node 18–22.12 user to a first run that cannot start.
- `caveman providers login chatgpt` opens the browser on Windows.

## Behaviour changes to review

- The full file plan is no longer printed before the confirming key; it is behind Details (`d`). The first screen still says what routing sends to Cloud before that key.
- Under npx, setup runs `npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli@<version>` (shown on the first screen and in `--dry-run`).
- `enable claude` touches every signed-in Claude profile, not only the active one.
- A Windows `.cmd` shim that forwards to an `.exe` beside it is now launched (it was refused).
- README install block is now `npx @caveman-ai/cli`. This is only true once a CLI with these changes is published.

## Tests

- `packages/cli` full suite locally: 1324 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (before the last launcher commit; its suites were rerun).
- An independent review of the branch found four P1 defects (profile wiring into look-alike dirs, a deleted or read-only sibling profile blocking disable, npx still wiring from the cache when any install existed, an empty agent list lost in the handoff); all are fixed with a test each.
- New CI job `first-run`: builds the CLI, installs real Claude Code, runs `setup --dry-run`, `setup --yes`, `status`, `doctor claude`, `off --all` in a throwaway home, and checks that every path a written hook names exists. Green on windows-latest, macos-14 and ubuntu-latest.

title: fix(codex): register marketplace plugin lifecycle hooks
body:
Installing Caveman from the Codex marketplace exposes its skills but does not register activation hooks. Move the Codex manifest and its existing icons to the marketplace root and declare inline `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks using the existing handlers and readable Node commands.

Codex stores mode changes per chat in `PLUGIN_DATA`. Startup/clear apply the configured default; resume/compact preserve the selected style or explicit off. Native `$skill` and Markdown skill references use the shared parser. Invalid session ids fail open, and Codex skips Claude statusline setup, model overrides, and usage scripts.

Remove the repository-local hook configuration to prevent duplicate activation. Keep the standalone Codex loader and installer introduced in main. The Claude plugin manifest, launch commands, Windows behavior, standalone installer, and OpenCode behavior are unchanged. No dependencies or version bump are added.

Fixes JuliusBrussee/caveman#1242.

title: v4: stability fixes from the release audit (Windows, macOS, every agent)
body:
Stability pass on the v4 release candidate (stacked on #1238 / `v4-setup`).

## How it was tested
- **Audit:** a 126-agent audit of `v4-setup` @ 308c743b found 95 findings, 93 of them confirmed by an independent re-check (1 P0, 12 P1, ~50 P2, rest P3).
- **Fixes:** eleven fix lanes, followed by four more rounds that came out of independent Opus reviews of the fixes. Every review round found fewer and smaller issues; the last found no P0–P2. Each fix has a regression test that failed before it.
- **Real hosts** on macOS, in throwaway homes, against local stub upstreams:

  | Host | Version |
  |---|---|
  | Claude Code | 2.1.295 |
  | Codex | 0.161.0 |
  | Gemini CLI | 0.53.1 |
  | opencode | 1.18.35 and 2.0.22 |
  | Pi | 1.0.0 |
  | Antigravity CLI (agy) | 1.2.17 |

  Every host loaded what Caveman writes, routed through the proxy, compressed, and restored its config byte-for-byte on `off` / `--uninstall`.
- **Agent conformance:** the workflow (pinned real Codex/Gemini/opencode/Pi/Kilo/Qwen/OpenClaw/aider/Hermes) is green on this branch.
- **Windows CI:** engine-ci's Windows job now runs on PRs that touch Windows code. It had been off for PRs, and main's run hung. `go test ./...` passes on real Windows.
- **CI on 195c2552:** 66 checks pass, including windows (the full `npm run test:windows` lane), windows-powershell and first-run on windows-latest. Three are red:
  - `catalog`: the PR-shape gate (see Known gaps).
  - `govulncheck` and `links`: known red, not from this PR.

## Highlights
- **Windows (P0):** `npx @caveman-ai/cli setup` could not launch Node's own `npm.cmd`/`npx.cmd`. All four copies of the shim launcher now agree (pnpm `.exe` shims, MCP entries written as `node <script>`), and a parity test guards that.
- **Your own endpoint:**
  - Setup and every door (native, `caveman <agent>`, `wrap`) leave an agent alone when it already points at the user's own endpoint (corporate gateway, LiteLLM, own Codex/opencode provider, Gemini base URL) and print how to opt in. Before, the user's token went to the vendor API.
  - A shell endpoint exported after wiring is caught.
- **Codex:**
  - disable, off and doctor survive Codex rewriting config.toml, and the user's own `model_provider` comes back.
  - BOM handling, and ChatGPT-vs-API-key detection from auth.json.
  - Exact Codex hook-trust hash; doctor says when `/hooks` trust is missing.
  - One voice owner.
  - No unsupported hook events, and no wasted shrink hook.
- **Runtime:**
  - status and doctor detect a stopped runtime, and `doctor <agent> --fix` restarts it.
  - A port counts as Caveman's only when its listener proves it with the instance token.
  - Every wiring path moves off a port another program holds, including Windows excluded ranges.
  - The runtime starts from home, not the project directory.
  - Install lock.
  - A stale runtime restarts only when idle.
- **Upgrades:**
  - 3.2.0 binaries are refreshed to the pinned release.
  - A running Windows `.exe` is moved aside.
  - Graceful Windows stop with a private shutdown token.
  - The old telemetry opt-out is honored.
  - A broken `cloud.json` is never overwritten.
- **Installer:**
  - npx uninstall runs a v4-aware CLI. The dependency was `^1.1.0`, which installed 1.3.4.
  - OpenClaw keeps the user's skill files; opencode 2.x works.
  - Gemini detection, plus `--force` with backup and restore.
  - settings.json is untouched when caveman never wrote it.
  - BOM, CRLF and JSONC handling.
  - Stale hook repair.
  - Delegated skill installs pinned; Cline, Continue and Augment detection.
  - Installer tests no longer touch the developer's real agents.
- **Hooks:**
  - defaultMode is honored in BOM/UTF-16/JSONC configs.
  - Windows reads `~/.config/caveman/config.json`.
  - Hooks run under a recorded stable node path, so a Homebrew/nvm upgrade no longer breaks them.
- **Proxy:**
  - Auto gives way when the routed model is rate-limited or overloaded (both login kinds).
  - Gemini 3 thought signatures.
  - id-less tool calls.
  - A late usage chunk is no longer dropped.
- **Engine:** compressed line-numbered listings keep their true line numbers (bug present since 2.0.0).
- **Python SDK:** the transport deadline now covers every read, not just the connect, and `close()` aborts a blocked stream within ~100 ms. Before, a stalled stream on Windows could hang past its timeout.
- **Price catalog:** three retired Claude rows were removed (Bedrock 3.5 Haiku, Bedrock 3.5 Sonnet v2, `claude-opus-4-1`). Their 2026-06-15 `verified_at` would have tripped the 120-day staleness test on 2026-10-12 and turned every PR red. The oldest-row pin moves to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` (2026-07-10). No new dated snapshot was minted, because no price was re-checked. `main` needs the same fix before 2026-10-12.
- **Memory:** concurrent `caveman mem remember` no longer loses a write when several processes open a fresh database at once (WAL switch retried on SQLITE_BUSY).
- **Windows:**
  - git runs without console windows.
  - Go and Node agree on the pipe name.
  - CAVEMAN_HOME ACL tightening only on a Caveman-owned folder.
  - System tools are resolved from System32.
  - The statusline repair and re-offer now work when the configured path contains `~`, as in 8.3 short names like `RUNNER~1`.

## Release gates (not code)
- [ ] Cut the v4 binary release and pin it (BINARY_RELEASE and the mcp/shrink/browse launcher pins). The Go fixes and Auto routing only reach users then; bin-v2.1.0 cannot route Auto.
- [ ] Bump the root `@caveman-ai/cli` range to the v4 CLI. Publish the CLI before tagging the repo if it is a new major; otherwise `npx github:` fails with ETARGET.
- [ ] Bump `CLI_VERSION` in install.sh/install.ps1 and `PINNED_REF` in installer/install.js, install.sh and install.ps1 (still v3.2.0) to the v4 tag. Delegated `npx skills add …#ref` now pins to it.
- [ ] Bump `@caveman-ai/pi` (0.3.0) and tag `pi-v*` (localPort and shim parity).
- [ ] Tag contracts-v2.1.0 (local 2.1.0 vs npm 2.0.0).
- [ ] Bump the Codex `tested_agent_version` (0.160.1 → 0.161.x).
- [ ] Cloud (api/app.caveman.so) answered 503 throughout, so Auto routing and sign-in were not exercised end to end.
- [ ] Price catalog: 13 rows go stale on 2026-11-07 and 23 more on 2026-11-20 unless their prices are re-checked against the vendor pages. `claude-sonnet-4-5` (both rows) retires on the Claude API on 2026-11-30.
- [ ] Known red, not from this PR: govulncheck (Go 1.26.9 + golang.org/x/net 0.60.0), and docs links (docs.caveman.so 404s).

## Open product questions
- Start the runtime on login (launchd/systemd/login item)? Without it, Codex users who never trust Caveman's hooks via `/hooks` (`codex exec`, CI) hang after a reboot until they run `caveman doctor codex --fix`.
- Should `off --all` also stop the background runtime?
- Should installer `--uninstall` remove the Claude Code marketplace entry? It is kept today so a project-scoped install isn't broken.
- Should the Claude marketplace be pinned to the release tag? Claude Code 2.1.296 supports it, but it breaks existing unpinned marketplaces and freezes `claude plugin update`.

## Known gaps left
- **Not testable here:** Windows interactive terminals (mintty, conhost); Smart App Control with the unsigned binaries; macOS Intel, Windows ARM and Linux arm64 runtime; corporate HTTP_PROXY; Node 24/26; bun/pnpm global installs; live model turns.
- **Wrap and installer:**
  - The wrap door does not read project-level opencode/Gemini config.
  - Hermes and aider wrap have no own-endpoint check.
  - Installer `--with-mcp-shrink` writes bare `npx`.
  - Gemini extension install is unpinned.
  - kilocode and jetbrains-augment detection are substring matches.
- **Windows:**
  - Native wiring can write a `caveman-mcp.cmd` path when an npm-global caveman-mcp precedes `~/.caveman/bin`.
  - Windows `caveman stop` cannot drain a wildcard-bound runtime.
- **Codex:** a user's own SessionStart hooks after a removed installer hook shift position and need `/hooks` re-trust.
- **Engine:** for prose with blank lines, elision counts paragraphs, so a repeated paragraph inside a skipped run can still get an earlier number (never a later one).
- **Flaky under heavy local load:** pwsh 60 s spawn timeouts. CI windows-powershell is green.
- **Catalog PR gate:** `provider-catalog.yml` accepts only `current.yaml` plus one new dated snapshot. The catalog fix also has to change tests, so this PR (and the matching fix for main) needs an owner override.

title: opencode plugin targets the v1 plugin API — broken on OpenCode v2.x (verified breakdown + port spec)
body:
## Summary

The official `opencode` plugin (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`) targets the **OpenCode v1 plugin API** and fails to load on **OpenCode v2.0.x**. Tested against **v2.0.26** (Bun-compiled single binary, Linux x64): the loader rejects the module with a hard schema error and the plugin never runs. Each incompatibility below was verified directly against the v2.0.26 binary, and I've included a concrete port plan.

## How to reproduce

1. Run the caveman installer (installs the plugin under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman/`).
2. Start OpenCode v2 and load the plugin.
3. Observed failure:

```
Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
```

Note: with the v1 installer layout the plugin is usually **not picked up at all** (see breaking change #2), so to get past that step I registered the plugin directory explicitly via a v2 `plugins` entry, which surfaced the schema error above.

## Breaking change #1 — module contract: function export → definition object

Current code:

```js
export const CavemanPlugin = async (_ctx) => { ... };
export default CavemanPlugin;
```

OpenCode v2 requires the default export to be an **object** with an `id` and an `effect` or `setup` function:

```js
export default { id: 'caveman', setup(ctx) { ... } };
```

A bare function is rejected with the schema error quoted above.

## Breaking change #2 — config key: `plugins` (plural) + directory entries

- v1: singular `plugin` key pointing at a relative `.js` file path.
- v2 config (`opencode.json(c)` or a managed config via `OPENCODE_CONFIG`) takes a **plural `plugins` array of absolute directory paths**; the directory becomes the module root, resolved through its `exports["."]` / `main`.
- A relative `.js` path under a singular `plugin` key does **not** load on v2.
- Auto-discovery of subdirectories under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` is **not effective** on v2 — the plugin must be listed explicitly in the config.

The installer therefore needs to write/merge a `plugins` entry into the v2 config rather than relying on the v1 layout.

## Breaking change #3 — `chat.message` and `experimental.chat.system.transform` no longer exist

Verified hook surface present in v2.0.26 (all found in the binary):

```
compaction, context, experimental.ws.handshake, generate, http.request,
http.response, model.request, retry, title
```

Verified absent (0 hits in the binary): `chat.message`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`, `tool.execute.*`.

The event dispatcher (`event`) **does** survive, including `session.created`, `message.updated`, `session.idle` — so the existing `event`-based session-init flag write (the pattern from #418/#421) ports over as-is.

## Port plan (what I'd do for a PR)

1. Export a definition object (`{ id: 'caveman', setup(ctx) { ... } }`) and register everything through the v2 hook/event API.
2. Keep the `event`-based `session.created` flag write unchanged — it survives v2.
3. `chat.message` parsing: mode toggling is already handled model-side via `/caveman` slash commands, which work on v2 today. Recommend having the plugin subscribe to `message.updated` (or drop parsing entirely and let the commands own it — simpler and v2-native).
4. `experimental.chat.system.transform` (per-turn reinforcement injection): no direct v2 equivalent. Nearest options are the `context` hook (system-prompt assembly) or documented AGENTS.md injection. The plugin's idempotent banner-append logic already exists and can be preserved in whichever path we pick.
5. Installer: emit the plural `plugins` array (absolute directory path) into the v2 config instead of the v1 `plugin` key / `plugins/` auto-discovery expectation.

## Workaround that works today (no plugin required)

Mode tracking already works without the plugin: `/caveman*` slash-command files plus the default-mode chain (`CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE` env → repo `.caveman/config.json` → `~/.config/caveman/config.json`). The plugin only adds session-start flag writes / telemetry, so this is not blocking — but on v2 the plugin currently fails to load, so installs are broken rather than degraded.

## Environment

- OpenCode v2.0.26 (Bun-compiled single binary), Linux x64
- caveman 3.2.0 (HEAD `2e08b917`)
- Verified via an explicit `plugins` config entry + `opencode run --standalone --print-logs`

Happy to submit the port PR if it's wanted.

title: fix(cli): login and logout drop the old account's refresh outcome, so status stops saying refresh offline
body:
## Bug

`caveman status` says "account refresh offline — cloud sync and seat state may be stale" whenever `cloud.json` has `wrapEntitlementRefresh.ok === false` (`refreshOffline()`). Only `refreshWrapEntitlementInBackground()` writes that flag, and it runs only on the local-proxy wrap path (`gateApplies`).

Seen 2026-10-11: a failure recorded under an earlier login (a dead local-dev Cloud, September) survived `caveman login` to prod. `caveman claude` with native wiring launches directly, so nothing ever ran the refresh again and the warning never cleared.

## Fix

The refresh outcome (`wrapEntitlementRefresh`) and the weekly run claim (`wrapEntitlementRunRefreshWeek`) belong to the credential they ran under. `login()` (right after saving the new credential) and `logout()` (after clearing it) now drop both keys.

- No extra background refresh after login: login already fetches the entitlement in the foreground (`fetchAndStoreWrapEntitlement`).
- Token rotation (`refreshCLIConfig`) keeps both keys, since the account doesn't change.
- Every sign-in path (porcelain, first-run UI, onboarding, `init`, private instance) goes through `login()`.
- Dropping the weekly claim lets the new account's first wrapped run report that week. Cloud only uses `wrapped_run` to update `last_wrapped_run_at`, so a second report is harmless.

## Proof

- New runtime test in `packages/cli/tests/login.runtime.mjs`:
  - plants the stale flag and checks `status` shows the warning;
  - logs in and checks both keys are gone and `status` is clean;
  - plants it again, logs out, and checks both keys are gone.
- The test fails without the fix (at the post-login assertion) and passes with it. It fails if either the login call or the logout call is removed.
- Full CLI suite on this branch: 1238 passed, 7 failed, 5 skipped. All 7 failures also fail on untouched `v4` on this machine, and none involve login, logout or the refresh flag: engine recovery conformance, `~/.caveman/bin` resolution, private-login `/auth/me` count, two `enable codex` proxy-spawn tests, the session recovery gate, and the record-policy hook test (flaky on untouched `v4`).
- An independent review found no blocking issues.

## Not in this PR

- A temporary refresh failure under the *current* credential on the wrap path, followed by a switch to native wiring, still leaves the flag stuck. The weekly claim blocks a retry that week, and native wiring never retries. One option: `refreshOffline()` ignores a flag older than about 8 days. That's a product call.
- `logout` keeps `wrapEntitlement` and `wrapEntitlementState`. A login to a different account whose entitlement check comes back unavailable keeps the previous account's cached entitlement. Same reasoning, separate change.
- The same bug is on `release/v4`, `v4-setup`, `v4-stability` and `main`. On the release stack, `logout` also calls `syncAutoEntries()`; the change is otherwise identical.

title: feat(telemetry): receiver for Caveman Blocks usage counts
body:
Adds the Supabase receiver for the `blocks/v1` usage-telemetry contract that the `scripts` module (`caveman-blocks`) sends. Client side: caveman-ai/blocks `feat/telemetry`.

- `supabase/functions/blocks-telemetry`: Edge Function plus allowlist validator. It keeps first-party block names only, drops unknown map keys and caps counters at what one install's day can produce.
- `public.blocks_events` uses the same access model, retention and rate-limit counters as `cli_events`, so both products share one global ceiling. One `daily_usage` row per install per day; the first write wins.
- Nine analytics views (`blocks_summary`, `blocks_daily`, funnel, retention, block and harness usage, scan, product overlap). `bytes_withheld` is block output kept out of the agent's context.

Cherry-picked unchanged from `feat/blocks-telemetry` (2026-10-04) onto `v4`. The migrations sort after the last one on `v4`.

**Verification**
- `node --test supabase/functions/blocks-telemetry/ingest.test.ts supabase/functions/cli-telemetry/ingest.test.ts`: 16/16 pass.
- An independent review checked that client and receiver agree on the contract (endpoint, field rules, first-party list, batch size, SQL). No blocking defects.

**Known tradeoff:** the per-IP limit (30 events/min, shared with `cli_events`) can drop `daily_usage` rows behind a shared NAT. The endpoint always answers 202, so the client marks those days sent and doesn't retry.

title: caveman doctor opencode reports version_probe_failed on Windows when OpenCode is installed via npm (.cmd shim → native .exe)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `caveman doctor opencode` reports OpenCode as `unavailable` (`version_probe_failed`), even though `opencode --version` works from PowerShell. This blocks `caveman enable opencode` and `caveman doctor opencode --fix` ("opencode is unavailable; repair host installation first"), so the generated OpenCode V2 plugin cannot be regenerated.

## Root cause

- npm installs `opencode.cmd`, which forwards to a native binary:
  ```bat
  "%dp0%\node_modules\@opencode\cli\bin\opencode.exe"   %*
  ```
- `nativeHostProbe()` → `portableInvocation("opencode", ["--version"])` (`dist/portable-command.js`) resolves the `.cmd` via `resolveWindowsCommand`, then calls `resolveWindowsNodeShim()`.
- `resolveWindowsNodeShim()` only understands shims that forward to a Node script (`.js`/`.cjs`/`.mjs`) or to another `.cmd`/`.bat`. For this shim it throws:
  ```
  cannot safely launch non-Node Windows command shim: ...\opencode.CMD; install a native .exe
  ```
- `nativeHostProbe()` catches the error and returns `error: "version_probe_failed"`, `version: null`. The doctor then reports `state: unavailable`, `launchable: false`.

The error message suggests installing a native `.exe`, but the tool already is one. It is just reached through a `.cmd` shim, which the parser does not handle.

## Reproduction

Windows 11, PowerShell 7.6.6, Node (system), npm global prefix `%APPDATA%\npm`.

```powershell
npm i -g @opencode/cli@2.0.27      # provides opencode.cmd -> bin\opencode.exe
npm i -g @caveman-ai/cli@2.1.0

opencode --version                  # opencode v2.0.27  (works)
caveman doctor opencode             # state: unavailable, version_probe_failed
```

Direct check of the helper:

```js
import { portableInvocation } from ".../@caveman-ai/cli/dist/portable-command.js";
portableInvocation("opencode", ["--version"]);
// throws: cannot safely launch non-Node Windows command shim: ...\opencode.CMD; install a native .exe
```

Running the native binary directly works:

```powershell
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\node_modules\@opencode\cli\bin\opencode.exe" --version
# opencode v2.0.27, exit 0
```

## Expected

The probe should resolve the `.cmd` shim to the `.exe` it forwards to and run it directly (same as `.js` shims are handled), returning `launchable: true` and `version: "opencode v2.0.27"`.

## Suggested fix

In `resolveWindowsNodeShim` / `parseWindowsNestedShim`, recognize a single forwarding line to a native executable:

```js
const exe = source.match(/^(?:@echo[ \t]+off[ \t]*\r?\n)?[ \t]*(?:CALL[^\r\n]*\r?\n[^\r\n]*)?"%(?:dp0%|~dp0)\\?([^"\r\n]+\.exe)"[ \t]+%\*/im);
```

(or simpler: detect `"%dp0%\...\.exe" %*` and return that path). Keep the existing rule that rejects arbitrary batch syntax; only the exact forwarding form should match. Then `portableInvocation` returns `{ command: exePath, args }` without `process.execPath`.

## Impact

- `caveman doctor opencode` is unusable on Windows for any npm-installed OpenCode.
- `caveman enable opencode` is blocked, so the native plugin cannot be regenerated after an OpenCode major change (V1 → V2).
- Affects anyone using the npm distribution of OpenCode on Windows.

## Environment

- caveman CLI: 2.1.0
- OpenCode: 2.0.27 (npm `@opencode/cli`)
- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.6

title: opencode doctor: 'not routed through Caveman' warning for a provider whose baseURL already targets a proxy compat mount
body:
## Summary

`caveman doctor opencode` warns:

```
OpenCode's active provider "ollama-cloud" is not routed through Caveman; its requests go direct and are not compressed or counted (routed: openai, anthropic, opencode-go)
```

That isn't true. `ollama-cloud` goes through the proxy via a user-defined compat mount, and the proxy records every request. The check added for #1190 (`opencodeUnroutedActiveProvider`) treats a provider as routed only if it appears in the journal's `owned.routes`, which holds just the three routes `caveman enable opencode` writes. It never looks at the provider's `baseURL`, or at the `compat` mounts in `caveman.yaml`.

This is the OpenCode version of #1212, where the pi extension warns about a provider whose `baseUrl` already targets the proxy.

## Setup

`~/.caveman/caveman.yaml`:

```yaml
compat:
  ollama-cloud:
    base_url: https://ollama.com/v1
```

`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (excerpt; no top-level `model`):

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "ollama-cloud": {
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/opencode/compat/ollama-cloud/v1"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` has one entry, `ollama-cloud` (`type: api`). With no `model` pinned, the check falls back to the signed-in providers. None of them is in `owned.routes`, so it names `ollama-cloud`.

## Evidence the traffic is routed

- `GET http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/opencode/compat/ollama-cloud/v1/models` returns 200. An unknown mount (`/w/opencode/compat/nope/v1/models`) returns 404.
- The proxy's `requests` table has 32 opencode requests with `endpoint = /compat/ollama-cloud/v1/chat/completions` and status 200, totalling about 905k input tokens. They come from both OpenCode 1.19.0 and 2.0.27.

## Expected

Treat a provider as routed when its global-config `baseURL` already points at the gateway's `/w/opencode` prefix. For a `/compat/<name>/` path, also check that `compat.<name>` exists in `caveman.yaml`. Keep warning when the `baseURL` is missing or points somewhere else, which is the #1190 case.

## Environment

- `@caveman-ai/cli` 2.1.0, binaries `bin-v2.1.0`, pack 2.2.0
- OpenCode 2.0.27, installed via mise (`npm:@opencode/cli`); the check doesn't depend on the OpenCode version
- Linux x86_64 (Arch / Omarchy)

title: release: Caveman v4
body:
Merges `v4` into `main` for Caveman 4.0.0. `main` is 0 commits ahead of `v4`, so this merge adds nothing from main. **Do not merge before the release window (Tue 2026-10-13, 07:00 PT).** It supersedes #1233, whose head `release/v4` is an ancestor of `v4`.

## What ships

- **One install:** `npx @caveman-ai/cli` (CLI 4.0.0) opens a one-screen setup that finds your agents and logins, plus `caveman on|off` modules from a signed module index.
- **Auto routing** through Caveman Cloud, including Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT logins.
- **Grammar translators** between Messages, Chat Completions and Responses.
- **Cache warming.**
- **Caveman Blocks** mirrored into the signed binary release.

The full release notes are below; they become the `v4.0.0` GitHub Release body.

## Release pins in this branch

`9e8ee229` sets these pins:

- `packages/cli/BINARY_RELEASE` is `bin-v4.0.0`.
- `@caveman-ai/cli` is `4.0.0`.
- The product is `v4.0.0`: `install.sh`, `install.ps1`, `installer/install.js`, the README and INSTALL one-liners, root `package.json` and the plugin manifests.
- Both shims' first-run CLI is `4.0.0`.

The tags these pins name are created after this PR merges, in this order:

1. `bin-v4.0.0`
2. `cli-v4.0.0`
3. One commit on `main` that bumps the root installer's `@caveman-ai/cli` range to `^4.0.0` and relocks it.
4. `v4.0.0`

## Expected red checks (none blocks the release)

- **`node` / `root-surfaces` / `macos` / `windows`**: one test, *installer package depends on the CLI major this repo releases*. A `^4.0.0` range can't be locked before 4.0.0 is on npm, and the test's own comment says to publish the new CLI major before the tag that bumps the range. Fixed by the morning commit after the CLI publish.
- **`first-run` (3 OS)**: downloads the pinned `bin-v4.0.0`, which only exists after the merge, because release tags must be on `main`. Re-run after the binary release.
- **`catalog`**: the provider-catalog lane's scope gate rejects any non-catalog path, so a release PR always trips it (#1233 did too). The catalog validator passes.
- **`links`**: docs.caveman.so pages 404 since the docs-site restructure. Also red on `main`'s schedule; #1244 fixes most of them.
- **`CodeQL`**: 7 alerts, triaged as false positives or code already on `main`:
  - SHA-256 fingerprints of API keys
  - the proxy relaying upstream bytes
  - the upstream URL in `retrieve_tool.go`, there since 2.0.0
  - an int conversion that already has its bound check
  - an allocation already capped by `maxSpliceBytes`

`9193c6d5` moves Go to 1.26.9 and `golang.org/x/net` to 0.60.0 (GO-2026-6617), so `govulncheck` is green and the release binaries don't ship the vulnerable stdlib.

<details><summary>Release notes (draft for the v4.0.0 GitHub Release)</summary>

Caveman 4.0.0 makes `npx @caveman-ai/cli` the one install, adds Auto routing through Caveman Cloud on top of the local proxy, and ships Caveman Blocks as a module.

### One command to install

- `npx @caveman-ai/cli` opens a one-screen setup. It finds your coding agents and their logins (every Claude Code profile), shows what it will change, applies on Enter, then offers to start the agent. Without a terminal it applies only with `--yes`.
- `install.sh` and `install.ps1` end in the same setup, pinned to the CLI this release ships.
- `caveman on|off` switches modules from a registry. The module index (`modules.json`) is listed in the signed checksum manifest of the binary release, and the CLI refuses an index that manifest does not list. A module lockfile records what is installed.
- New commands: `caveman stop`, a status grid, an offline `caveman doctor`, `caveman providers add|remove|login|local` and `caveman providers cloud on|off`.
- One config home: `~/.caveman/cloud.json`. Older config migrates once, without races, and the telemetry opt-out carries over.
- Sign-in uses the shared device flow. It refuses plain-HTTP Clouds other than this machine.

### Auto routing (signed in to Caveman Cloud)

- `caveman-auto` shows up in the Claude Code and OpenCode model pickers with a 1M context window. Routing applies only to Auto, and that includes Claude Pro/Max logins and ChatGPT logins (Codex, OpenCode).
- For each routable request the proxy asks Cloud's route stage for a model and effort (contracts `route-ask-v1`) and picks from the providers you set up. If the key is refused or a billing limit is hit, the request goes through unrouted and `caveman status` says why.
- Translators between Messages, Chat Completions and Responses cover all nine directions, so Claude Code can run on Responses hosts such as the ChatGPT plan.
- A signed-in runtime sends `runtime/v1` event batches to Cloud and respects the telemetry opt-out.

### Cache

- The proxy keeps the Anthropic prompt cache warm while a session is paused. Warm timing comes from measured return times, at most two warms run at once, and `caveman stats` lists every warm.
- A session stays on its model across Cloud pauses and transient failures, so a model switch doesn't rewrite the cached prefix.

### Caveman Blocks

- The binary release mirrors `caveman-ai/blocks` v0.1.0-rc.4 (pinned by the digest of its checksum list). Each Blocks binary is republished under the same signed manifest as the other binaries. Blocks usage counts fall under the same telemetry notice and opt-out as Caveman's.

### Catalog

- Adds Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

### Versions

- `@caveman-ai/cli` goes from 2.1.0 to 4.0.0 to match the product version. Binaries move from `bin-v2.1.0` to `bin-v4.0.0`.
- The `npx github:JuliusBrussee/caveman` installer depends on CLI `^4.0.0`, so `-- --uninstall` runs a CLI that understands what 4.0 wrote.

### Companion releases

- [Signed binaries, module index and container: `bin-v4.0.0`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/releases/tag/bin-v4.0.0)
- [npm CLI: `@caveman-ai/cli@4.0.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@caveman-ai/cli/v/4.0.0)

Full changes: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/compare/v3.2.0...v4.0.0

</details>

Updates `github.com/chromedp/chromedp` from 0.16.0 to 0.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/chromedp/chromedp's releases.

v0.21.0

The package remote has its own WebSocket client, and it is a package of the core module now. The nested module remote and the dependency github.com/gobwas/ws are gone. The core module still needs only the standard library and cdproto.

The import path is the same: github.com/chromedp/chromedp/remote. The public API of the package is the same.

Upgrade: if your go.mod has a line for github.com/chromedp/chromedp/remote, remove it (go mod tidy does that). Go reports an ambiguous import while both the old nested module and the core module provide the package. The tag remote/v0.2.0 is the last version of the nested module.

The client follows RFC 6455: it checks the handshake, joins fragmented messages, checks UTF-8 and the size of a message, answers pings, and does the close handshake. It does not support extensions such as permessage-deflate. Go 1.25 and later are supported.

v0.20.1

Documentation only. The README, the package documentation and the docs have the current versions (chromedp v0.20.0, cdproto v0.157.8, remote v0.2.0), the CI matrix and the release history. The README describes termcast and the 43 programs of chromedp/examples.

v0.20.0

chromedp supports Go 1.25 and later. Before this release, the module needed Go 1.27 (see #1536).

  • The JSON types come from github.com/chromedp/cdproto/cdp/jsonv2. With Go 1.27 or GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 they are aliases of the types of the standard encoding/json/v2 and jsontext, so the public API is the same. With Go 1.25 and 1.26 they come from github.com/go-json-experiment/json.
  • The modules chromedp, remote and test use go 1.25 and cdproto v0.157.8.
  • The CI runs Go 1.25, 1.26 and stable on Linux, stable on Windows and macOS, and the experiment and the compatibility tag.

v0.19.1

Documentation only. The README and the package documentation describe termcast, which draws the screen of a page in a terminal, and the 43 programs of chromedp/examples.

v0.19.0

This release adds new actions and options, fixes bugs, and works on Linux, Windows and macOS in CI. See docs/MIGRATION.md for every change.

New

  • Tap and TapXY send a touch tap.
  • DragAndDrop and DragAndDropXY drag and drop with the mouse and with HTML5 drag and drop.
  • Console reads the console, the uncaught exceptions and the browser log of a page as one iterator.
  • ExposeFunc calls a Go function from the page, like exposeFunction in Puppeteer.
  • PrintToPDF takes options for the paper, the margins, the scale, the page ranges, the header and the footer, the outline and a stream.
  • WithNewWindow chooses a window or a tab for a new target. NoInheritEnv starts the browser with only the given variables. WithDetachOnCancel leaves the tab open when the context ends.
  • EvalAwaitPromise waits for a promise that an expression returns.

Fixed

  • Call on a Target or a Browser returns an error when the connection to the browser is lost, and does not hang.
  • The exec allocator keeps the order of the flags.
  • WaitNotPresent works with a JSPath that gives null or an empty list.
  • Evaluate returns ErrJSNull for null when the type cannot be nil, and Text works on a text node.
  • The pipe transport, the allocator and the tests work on Windows and macOS, and the default browser lookup on Windows falls back to Microsoft Edge.

Notes
