Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.60.1
Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-09-30 v1.61.0:

    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

  • 2026-09-01 v1.58.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.4. It carries upstream's own fix for the journal-rollback data-corruption bug, so the local super-journal patch v1.56.0 introduced is dropped; recovery behavior is unchanged. Also bumps the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.6; as always, downstream modules must pin the same version this one does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in support for Linux Open File Description (OFD) locks on database files, off by default; without opting in, locking behavior is byte-for-byte that of previous releases. A POSIX record lock is owned by the (process, inode) pair, so any Close of any descriptor of the database file anywhere in the process silently strips SQLite's locks; OFD locks survive that. Enable it process-wide with MODERNC_SQLITE_OFD_LOCK=1 in the environment, or with the new OFDLocking(true) before the first connection is opened; OFDLockingEnabled reports the mode in effect, and the new ErrOFDLockingTooLate and ErrOFDLockingUnavailable report a switch attempted too late and a platform or filesystem without the feature. Why it is process-wide rather than a DSN parameter, what WAL's -shm coordination still uses, and the /proc/locks measurements behind the design are in [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255).
    • Resolves [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255). See [GitLab merge request #136](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/136), thanks Nathan Herring (@​technosloth), and thanks Gani Georgiev (@​ganigeorgiev) for pressing the opt-in default!

  • 2026-08-19 v1.57.0:

    • Add an opt-in _defensive DSN query parameter turning on SQLite's defensive mode for the connection. On such a connection PRAGMA writable_schema=ON, PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF and PRAGMA schema_version=N become silent no-ops, and writes to a virtual table's shadow tables and to sqlite_dbpage fail. It is a hardening measure, not a sandbox for hostile database files, for which it is only one of the steps SQLite recommends, and it is a property of the connection, not of the file. Absent, or _defensive=0, nothing changes.
    • Reject _defensive=1 together with _journal_mode=OFF (or _journal=OFF) instead of opening a connection in which neither was honoured: SQLite turns that PRAGMA into a no-op that still reports success. Only DSNs using the new parameter can be affected. See [GitHub pull request #6](modernc-org/sqlite#6), thanks wsman!
    • Ship the sqlite-vec license notice this module has been missing since vec/ arrived in v1.47.0. sqlite-vec is Copyright (c) 2024 Alex Garcia, dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT and used here under MIT; the text now ships as LICENSE-SQLITE_VEC, and make vendor fails rather than quietly dropping it.
    • The SQLite notice is renamed from SQLITE-LICENSE to LICENSE-SQLITE; update any direct links to it. Its contents are unchanged. The rename is what makes go mod vendor carry both notices into downstream vendor/ trees: it selects license files by name prefix, so a name merely ending in LICENSE was never propagated.
    • Let a caller-constructed Driver register its own functions, collations and virtual table modules, through new RegisterFunction, RegisterScalarFunction, RegisterDeterministicScalarFunction, RegisterCollationUtf8 and RegisterModule methods plus Must* variants, and let vtab.RegisterModule honour its db argument. Behavior change: vtab.RegisterModule(db, ...) where db was opened on a caller-constructed Driver used to discard db and land on the registered sqlite driver, reaching every connection in the process; it now lands on that Driver alone, so a sql.Open("sqlite") connection that used to resolve such a module gets no such module. Everything else is additive, and the isolating change discussed in [GitLab issue #254](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/254) is deliberately not made here. See [GitLab merge request #135](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/135), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Promote freebsd/386, freebsd/arm and netbsd/amd64 from experimental to fully supported. The package documentation's platform table had carried seventeen entries while this module shipped, cross-built and tested twenty; all three have been in the builder matrix since v1.53.0 and pass the full suite on this release's commit. Documentation only — lib/ is byte-for-byte what v1.56.0 shipped.

  • 2026-08-03 v1.56.0:

    • Re-vendor the transpiled sources, picking up modernc.org/libsqlite3's patch for an upstream data-corruption bug in SQLite 3.53.3's journal rollback. A crash during the commit of a multi-database (ATTACH) transaction can leave a hot journal whose zeroed super-journal name still validates, so pager_playback() deletes it without playing it back and leaves the database corrupted. Not a transpilation artifact: a plain gcc build of stock 3.53.3 fails on the same bytes. The SQLite version is unchanged at 3.53.3, every supported target carries the patch, and it will be dropped once upstream ships its own fix.

title: Caveman 4.0.1: fixes found after the 4.0.0 launch (sync, OpenCode, Pi, hooks) and the open fix PRs
body:
Patch release on top of 4.0.0. Draft until the pin bump lands and the Windows question below is settled.

## Merged in

- #1249 login and logout drop the old account's refresh outcome
- #1196 daily triage 10-06 → 10-13 (35 fix commits; conflicts with v4 resolved, see below)
- #1248 compress: name a non-object opencode `agent` config
- #1218 proxy: executable identity on Android/Termux
- #1244 dead doc links
- #1200, #1234 caveman-compress: require a filepath, say the file goes to the model provider

## New fixes

- **sync**: a large unsynced span backlog failed forever with "Request body exceeds configured limit". Spans now upload in batches under the 16 MiB cap and the watermark moves per batch. The SQLite `ExperimentalWarning` no longer prints.
- **OpenCode 2**: a subagent spawn emitted `session.created` and reset the mode for every session, undoing "stop caveman" and `/ultracave`. Child sessions are ignored and their model-written prompts no longer switch the mode.
- **Pi**: `caveman wrap pi` after `caveman enable pi` loaded the extension twice and Pi exited 1. Routing reset the thinking level (`--thinking high` became the settings default). Pi 1.1+ promptless `before_agent_start` events threw. `@caveman-ai/pi` goes to 0.3.1 because the npm 0.3.0 build predates Caveman 4's config home.
- **Claude Code hooks**: the prompt hook had no stdin deadline and could hold a prompt for the whole hook timeout.
- **tests**: `tests/test_hooks.py` dropped an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` so it cannot aim at a real config.

## #1196 merge notes

v4 already fixed two triage items a different way, so v4's code was kept and the triage tests retained: the Windows `.exe`-forwarding npm shim (#1252) and the third-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` guard (#1247). Two #1247 tests were adapted to v4's behavior (`caveman claude` on a foreign endpoint launches directly and exits 0, rather than failing), and one INSTALL.md sentence was reworded to match.

## Known and not fixed here

- `first-run (windows-latest)` is red on main and will stay red on this PR: the pinned caveman-blocks v0.1.0-rc.4 writes its hook command without `.exe` but only recognises entries ending in `.exe`, so `off --all` leaves the hook and each `setup` adds a duplicate. The fix is in caveman-ai/blocks (branch `fix/windows-hook-ownership`, not yet pushed) and needs an rc.5, then `BLOCKS_RELEASE` and a new `bin-v*`.
- `caveman sync` practice findings are rejected by Cloud ("Request rejected."): control-api validates `practice_id` against optimizer families rather than the practices registry. Needs a Cloud fix and deploy.
- #1243 (Codex marketplace plugin hooks) is held back: with the installer hook also present it injects the ruleset twice.
- Version pins are still 4.0.0; the bump is a follow-up commit on this branch.

## Verification

Locally on macOS: CLI suites for sync, login, pi-wrap, pi-enable, native-enable; pi-extension 143/143; installer + hooks 638/638; `tests/*.js` 30/30; `verify_repo.py`; compress safety 58/58; Go `proxy`, `mem`, `shared`, `engine/ccr`. Four CLI tests fail identically on main on this machine (a live proxy on :8787). Nothing here was run on Windows.

title: cavecrew: tell the orchestrator to spot-check "No match." / "No issues." / "unchanged" claims before acting on them
body:
**What you want**

Add a bullet to `skills/cavecrew/SKILL.md` under "What NOT to do": do not act on or reject a subagent's absence claim (`No match.`, `No issues.`, "section missing", "unchanged") without one spot-check (a single grep or `sed -n` on the cited path). Optionally, `agents/cavecrew-investigator.md` Output could state which patterns and paths were searched on a zero-hit result, so a negative is checkable. Range-check any cited `file:line` against the file's length.

**Before / after**

Before: SKILL.md defines `No match.` and `No issues.` as terminal outputs and says nothing about how far the main thread should trust them.
After: SKILL.md tells the main thread to verify a negative with one grep before skipping or redoing work.

**Why good**

1. A missed search looks identical to a true negative, so absence is the claim a subagent is worst placed to get right.
2. Observed: a docs subagent reported that a how-to file had no text on a topic when it did (about line 195); a review subagent reported a section absent from a reference file when it existed (about line 1555). Both were wrong, in opposite directions. One nearly skipped a needed edit, the other nearly caused a redundant one.
3. Related: a subagent cited `file:line` ranges beyond a 99-line file's length. It was caught only because a `wc -l` range check was run.
4. Upstream `skills/cavecrew/SKILL.md` and the three agent definitions have no such guidance (checked on `main`).
5. Cost is one or two lines and no change to the agents.

Caveat: these failures were seen with general docs and review subagents, not only cavecrew agents. The rule transfers because cavecrew uses the same `No match.` / `No issues.` hand-back contract; that is my inference. Happy to open a PR with this wording if you prefer.

title: `shrink-hook` rewrite breaks `bash` tool calls under PowerShell
body:
> <!-- caveman-daily-triage -->
> **Reproduced and fixed in #1196.** Thank you for a report that located the cause and the exact shim line — that is what made this a one-sitting fix.
> 
> Your reading was right: `parseWindowsNodeShim` wants a `.cjs`/`.mjs`/`.js` target and `parseWindowsNestedShim` wants a `.cmd`/`.bat`, so npm's bare `"%dp0%\…\opencode.exe"   %*` payload matched neither, the resolver threw, and `nativeHostProbe` turned that into `version_probe_failed`. The advice it printed was the sting: the tool already *was* a native `.exe`.
> 
> `parseWindowsExeShim` now recognizes that one form. It is anchored to the whole line, which is what keeps every existing Node shim on the Node path — those name interpreter and script on the same line (`"%~dp0\node.exe" "%~dp0\..\cli.js" %*`), so `node.exe` can never be mistaken for the target. Arbitrary batch syntax still fails closed (trailing `& echo`, a `.ps1` target, an `.exe` line inside a batch-forwarding wrapper), and a recognized forward whose target is missing now says *that* instead of a parse failure.
> 
> Fixed in all three copies that launch third-party hosts and are documented to stay in sync: `packages/cli` (your probe), `packages/pi-extension`, `installer/lib`. Seven regression cases across the three suites, driven with an explicit `platform: "win32"` so they run on the POSIX CI too.
> 
> ---
> _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ 

 _Originally posted by @JuliusBrussee in [#1252](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/1252#issuecomment-6141153504)_
## Summary

The `shrink-hook` rewrite used by the generated OpenCode native plugin (`plugins/caveman-native.js`, `tool.execute.before`) produces a command that PowerShell cannot parse. On Windows, when the host shell is PowerShell, every rewritable `bash` tool call fails with a parser error before it runs.

## Reproduction

Windows 11, PowerShell 7.6.6, `@caveman-ai/cli@4.0.1`, OpenCode 2.0.28.

Ask `shrink-hook` to rewrite a command:

```powershell
'{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git status"}}' | node "$env:APPDATA\npm\node_modules\@caveman-ai\cli\dist\index.js" shrink-hook
```

Output:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"command":"'C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm/caveman.CMD' shrink -- git status"}}}
```

Run the rewritten command in PowerShell:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -Command "'C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm/caveman.CMD' shrink -- git --version"
# ParserError: Unexpected token 'shrink' in expression or statement.
```

A quoted string at the start of a PowerShell statement is an expression, not a command. It needs the call operator `&`.

## Expected

The rewritten command should run under the host shell. Either prefix the quoted path with `&` for PowerShell, or emit a form that works for both cmd and PowerShell (e.g. no quoting of the executable, or invoke `node` with the script path).

## Impact

- Any `bash` tool call that `shrink` rewrites fails on Windows when the shell is PowerShell.
- Affects the generated native plugin on OpenCode 2.x; the rewrite happens in `tool.execute.before`, before execution, so the failure is not recoverable by the agent.
- Not verified end-to-end inside a live OpenCode session. The parser failure is reproduced deterministically.

## Environment

- caveman CLI: 4.0.1 (`@caveman-ai/cli`)
- OpenCode: 2.0.28 (npm `@opencode/cli`)
- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.6

title: fix(installer): bound and pin hook downloads to https
body:
## Summary

`downloadTo` in `installer/install.js` downloads hook files from the pinned release ref during a detached (curl|bash) install. Before this change it had no limits on redirects, protocols, time, or body size.

**curl path** — added four flags:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--proto-redir =https` | Reject any redirect that downgrades off HTTPS |
| `--max-redirs 5` | Cap redirect chain length |
| `--max-time 60` | Hard 60 s wall-clock limit |
| `--max-filesize 8388608` | Refuse responses larger than 8 MiB |

**Node https fallback** (used when curl is absent) — four matching guards:

| Guard | Limit |
|---|---|
| URL check before each fetch | Reject `http://` redirect targets |
| Redirect counter | Abort after 5 redirects |
| `req.setTimeout` | Abort after 60 000 ms |
| Byte accumulator | Abort when body exceeds 8 MiB |

## Testing

Added `tests/installer/download-hardening.test.mjs` (9 tests):

- curl path: verifies all four flags appear in the args passed to curl
- Node fallback: non-https redirect rejected, redirect-count cap, oversized body rejected, timeout fires, successful download resolves

Full installer + hooks suite: **648 pass, 0 fail** (2 skipped, Windows-only).

## Scope

Only `installer/install.js` and the new test file are touched. No behaviour change for the local-clone install path — `downloadTo` is only called when hook files are fetched from the remote ref.

title: fix(hooks): write cavecrew model overrides safely
body:
## Summary

`applyOverrides` in `src/hooks/cavecrew-model-overrides.js` patches installed agent frontmatter on every `SessionStart`. It used a plain `fs.writeFileSync` with no symlink check, and the model-value guard missed Unicode line-break characters.

Three fixes:

**1. Symlink refusal**
`lstatSync` is checked before writing. A symlinked agent file is silently skipped, so the write cannot be redirected outside the plugin directory.

**2. Atomic write**
Replaced `writeFileSync(agentPath, ...)` with write-to-temp + `renameSync`. The temp file is `agentPath + '.caveman-tmp-<pid>'` and is cleaned up by the rename. On POSIX, `rename` is atomic, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a half-written agent file. The original file's mode bits are preserved.

**3. Unicode line-break rejection in `patchFrontmatterModel`**
The existing guard `/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/` misses U+0085 (NEL), U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) — all treated as line endings by YAML parsers but not caught by the ASCII range. Extended to `/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]|[\^E  ]/`.

`src/hooks/checksums.sha256` is regenerated for the changed hook file.

## Testing

Five new tests added to `tests/test_cavecrew_model_overrides.js`:

- U+2028 / U+2029 / U+0085 each rejected by `patchFrontmatterModel`
- `applyOverrides` skips a symlinked agent file (POSIX only)
- No `.caveman-tmp-*` file left after a successful write

Suite grows from 27 to **32 tests, all passing**.

Full installer + hooks suite: **639 pass, 0 fail** (2 skipped, Windows-only).
`tests/test_symlink_flag.js`: **20 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped**.
`python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: **all checks passed**.

## Scope

Only `src/hooks/cavecrew-model-overrides.js`, `src/hooks/checksums.sha256`, and `tests/test_cavecrew_model_overrides.js` are touched. No API or behaviour change visible to callers.

title: daily triage 2026-10-14 + 10-15: HTML misroute, cavecrew override write, two compress data-loss fixes (3 pin bumps still pending your call)
body:
> **Note on authorship of this description.** Two daily-triage runs have written to this PR (2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15), and both edited this body. This revision is a **merge** of the two, not a replacement of either: the 10-14 run's CI analysis and its clean-worktree verification numbers are kept (they are better than the 10-15 run's), and the 10-15 run's per-fix detail, triage verdicts and contributor reviews are restored after being dropped. Please don't read the shifting "I" as one agent contradicting itself. Every fix is attributed below.

## Fixes

### From the 2026-10-14 run

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1263 | The `shrink` rewrite is a command handed **back** to the host for the host's own shell, but it was rendered with `quoteHookPath`. A quoted path at the start of a PowerShell statement is an expression, not a command; single quotes are literal characters in cmd.exe. Only a bash-family host ever accepted it. | Windows: opencode plugin (PowerShell), Gemini CLI (cmd.exe). Claude Code's Git Bash was the one host it worked on. POSIX byte-identical. | `packages/cli/tests/windows-platform.runtime.mjs` — `hostShellInvocation` driven with explicit `platform: "win32"`, so it runs on POSIX CI |
| #1264 | Not the adapter and not the supported range — the oracle. `TS-2/#1206` deep-compared every call option across two independent calls, and an `AbortSignal` is a live EventTarget whose hidden listener table holds anonymous closures that compare by reference, so two calls' signals can never be `deepStrictEqual`-equal once anything listens. Vacuous at the pinned 1.65.0 (the option is `undefined` there unless the caller passes one); impossible at 1.77.0, which mints one per call. | `@caveman-ai/middleware` TypeScript, Mastra adapter; nightly canary only — the engine-ci merge gate was green | the failing assertion itself, rewritten: presence parity, state parity, and caller-cancellation propagation |

**#1263 known tradeoff, still yours to call:** on Windows a caveman path containing a space now silently gets no command rewrite. A hook cannot warn — stdout is the protocol — so this is the one degraded path that cannot print its own line. `caveman setup`/doctor is the place to surface it, if it should be.

#### #1264 — reproduced, then settled

Reproduced locally at `@mastra/core` 1.77.0: the same single failure, `call option abortSignal reached the native model unchanged`, both signals carrying exactly one listener and differing only in closure identity. `prepare()` forwards params by shallow spread, so the signal object is the caller's own — the verbatim claim holds.

- full suite **137/137** at the pinned 1.65.0
- full suite **137/137** with `node_modules` at 1.77.0 and the manifest at its committed pins — the canary's own configuration, which was 136/137 before this change
- `scripts/check-latest-in-range.mjs` → `26/26 latest releases inside their supported range`, so **no range widening is needed**; the devDependency, lockfile and `testedFrameworkVersions` are untouched.

### From the 2026-10-15 run

Four adopted from contributors (authorship preserved in each commit), one follow-up of its own, one ported docs fix. Every one was verified failing on `main` first.

| Commit | Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `15ebd61` | #1272 (part) | `Detect` ran the terminal check before HTML, and that check treats ≥3 bare carriage returns as a progress-bar redraw. A page served with CRLF line ends and a few stray CRs (githubstatus.com) opens with `<!DOCTYPE html>` and still routed to the terminal compressor, which saved 14 of its 47,607 tokens. Second bug in the same function: the declaration test was a bare prefix match, so `<htmlReport>` counted as an `<html>` tag. | Every engine caller — proxy, CLI, MCP, WASM — shares one `Detect`; no sibling host copy exists. OS-independent. | `TestDetectHTMLDocumentWithStrayCarriageReturns`, `TestDetectHTMLDeclarationNeedsATagBoundary` (fail on `main` as `"terminal"` and `"html"`) | first commit of #1273 |
| `106ec34` | — (security) | `patchFrontmatterModel`'s guard `/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/` missed U+0085 NEL, U+2028 LS and U+2029 PS, which YAML treats as line endings, so a model value could inject a second frontmatter line. `applyOverrides` also wrote with a plain `writeFileSync` and no symlink check, so a symlinked agent file redirected the write. | Claude Code `SessionStart` (plugin + standalone). | 5 tests; 4 fail on `main`, including `symlink target was overwritten` and `model: son\x85net` splitting the frontmatter | #1270 |
| `5f332af` | — (hardening, found reviewing #1270) | That atomic write stages `<agent>.md.caveman-tmp-<pid>` and renames it into place. The rename is the step most likely to fail for a reason the hook cannot control (EPERM from an open handle on Windows, EACCES on a read-only parent), and the hook swallows every error there by design. The staged file was left behind, and the hook runs on **every** SessionStart, so it accumulated one copy per pid in the user's plugin directory. | Claude Code `SessionStart`; Windows most exposed. No sibling host: `cavecrew-model-overrides.js` is required only by `caveman-activate.js`, and `installer/lib/cursor-native.js` drops the Claude `model:` key for Cursor instead of overriding it. | `applyOverrides removes the staged temp file when the rename fails` | — |
| `8e0e22b` | — (data loss) | The first compression pass splits frontmatter off before the model sees the file and masks code / `<!-- nocompress -->` regions, refusing to write if a marker changed. The fix/retry pass gave both up: `build_fix_prompt` sends the whole file unmasked and with frontmatter, checked only by `validate()`, which never compares frontmatter and cannot see a fence indented under a list item. A repair could rewrite a destructive command or rewrite `name:`/`description:`, pass validation, and be written over the user's source file. | `caveman-compress` on every host. | 2 tests, both fail on `main`: the `-n prod` → `-n dev` rewrite and the `description:` rewrite are each accepted and written out | #1274 |
| `edd228e` | — (data loss) | `_compress_file_locked` wrote the backup and staged candidates in `<file>.caveman-staged`, but only cleaned up on the normal "failed after retries" branch. `call_claude` can raise during the fix call (300 s timeout, auth/CLI failure, `openai-compat` HTTP error) and the user can Ctrl-C it. Nothing caught either, so the staging file was left next to the source where it can get committed, and the backup was left behind — making every later `/caveman-compress <file>` abort with "Backup file already exists" until the user hunts it down. | `caveman-compress` on every host. | 3 tests, all fail on `main`, including the `KeyboardInterrupt` case leaving the backup in place | #1276 |
| `e7ecd67` | — (dead docs link) | Both middleware READMEs told the reader to `curl` a quickstart script from `docs.caveman.so/examples/middleware/quickstart.{py,ts}`. Neither is published, so the **first command** of the documented getting-started path fails for every reader. | `@caveman-ai/middleware` TS and Python READMEs — both packages' npm/PyPI landing pages. | this repo's own `docs-links` CI, which reports both as HTTP 404 | #1268 |

Credit: `15ebd61` @u7k4rs6 · `106ec34` @tejgokani · `8e0e22b`, `edd228e` @jwcastillo · `e7ecd67` @minhhung2556.

`src/hooks/checksums.sha256` was regenerated for the hook change (`verify_repo.py` passes).

#### Why two adopted commits dropped their `plugins/caveman/` hunk

#1274 and #1276 each also hand-edited `plugins/caveman/skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py`. Those hunks are dropped, **not rejected**: the triage routine may not write under `plugins/caveman/**`, and `.github/workflows/sync-skill.yml` already copies `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/` into that mirror on push to `main`. Checked before dropping: `tests/test_compress_safety.py` imports the `skills/` copy, and `verify_synced_files` asserts byte-equality for `SKILL.md` and `agents/*.md` only — nothing pins the script mirror.

### The one CI failure, and why it was not this PR's

`links` failed on `edd228e` with two dead URLs in `packages/middleware/{python,typescript}/README.md` — files no commit on this branch touches, and still dead on `main`. `docs-links.yml` triggers on `docs/technical/**`, so `15ebd61` surfaced a pre-existing failure. The fix existed as #1268 and is now on the branch as `e7ecd67`. Resolved; the whole head is green.

That run also **settled #1268's open question**: both URLs are `HTTP 404` from a runner that is not proxy-blocked, so the premise two runs could only call unverifiable is now evidence.

## Verified but dropped from this PR — three agent pins, needing two commits from you

The pin bumps were made, verified, and then **reverted out of this PR** (`311b505`) because the commit *shape* was wrong, not the content. `profile-contract` rejected them:

```
profile lane rejects out-of-scope path in commit 2dccb02:
  .github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml
```

`agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` keeps concrete profile-data commits atomic — only profile JSONs plus the three generated artifacts — and each commit also carried its conformance install line. The gate walks every commit in `base..head` individually, so no forward-only commit clears it; the fix is a history where the workflow pin sits in its own commit, and this routine does not force-push. Say the word and it will be force-pushed instead.

- **claude 2.1.299** (#1265) — `agents/probe-installed.mjs --require claude` → `ok`; isolated-home `--version`/`--help` both exit 0. Route probe: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at a local stub in a throwaway HOME, redirection observed reaching `POST /v1/messages?beta=true`.
- **gemini 0.64.0** (#1266) — probe `ok`. Route probe: `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` redirection observed reaching `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`. 0.64.0 also now requires `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` headless. The record should name that route, not the 0.63.0 record's `:streamGenerateContent` — the headless `-p` door is non-streaming.
- **openclaw 2026.10.3** (#1237) — the three-run blocker was the container, not the release: openclaw's preinstall gate needs Node ≥24.16.0 and this image ships 22.22.0. Under a fetched official v24.16.0 build, probe `ok`. Its `verified_by` should also state what was **not** re-observed: OpenClaw is reached through `SOUL.md` + a workspace skill rather than env injection, and confirming that bootstrap loads needs a live credentialed session.

Re-landing is two commits: (1) the three profile JSONs + `node agents/compile.mjs` output; (2) `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.299`, `@google/gemini-cli@0.64.0`, `openclaw@2026.10.3` in the conformance workflow.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1272 (table half)** — reproduced, not implemented. The detection misroute is fixed above; the other half (a dashboard or Istanbul index has no `<article>` so it passes through whole, and a coverage.py report puts every table cell on its own line) is a feature, which this routine triages rather than builds. #1273 implements it and is the right vehicle. The issue is deliberately **not** closed by `15ebd61`.
- **#1150** (extension not injecting on claude.ai) — probably already fixed; needs one retest. `c9edc29f` ("snapshot the rich draft after the editor settles", extension 1.3.0, `Refs #1150`) fixes exactly this shape on Claude's tiptap editor. The reporter is on 1.2.0. Before closing: that commit's own message records 1.2.0 as *sending* in the Chromium harness, so if 1.3.0 still fails for them the cause is a third thing (Brave Shields, or the per-site toggle). No browser here to verify.
- **#1246** (opencode v1 plugin API) — **already fixed on `main`**, pending release: `be80f1b3` (loads on 2.x), `3840ea02` (installer names the directory both majors load), `e46ef1d0` (a subagent session no longer switches the user's mode). `src/plugins/opencode/server.js` adapts `plugin.js`'s 1.x hooks rather than forking them.
- **#1278** and **#1262** (cavecrew briefing guidance; spot-check absence claims) — both reproduced as documentation gaps, not bugs. `skills/cavecrew/SKILL.md` says nothing about the delegating brief's working directory, hook-trigger text or git identity, and defines `No match.`/`No issues.` as terminal outputs (lines 39, 53) without asking for a negative to be verified; neither it nor the three `agents/cavecrew-*.md` files cover either. Both are SKILL.md behaviour changes, yours by policy. #1262's reporter offered a PR.
- **#1258** (Copilot: ultra recognized, not used) — needs info, with a likely cause. The per-repo rule body (`src/rules/caveman-activate.md`) *names* `/ultracave` but carries only the base ruleset; the ultra rules live in `skills/ultracave/SKILL.md`, which nothing injects on a host with no session hook. VS Code / Visual Studio Copilot Chat has no hook and no per-turn reinforcement (Copilot drops `userPromptSubmitted` output), so an "I'll keep using ultra" promise has nothing holding it after the next turn. Needs: which Copilot surface, and whether the install was `--only copilot` or `--with-init`.
- **#1279** (native runtime closes every `native.sock` request empty after a 2.0.1 → 4.0.1 upgrade) — belongs to `caveman-coding-agent`. The report's own evidence points at state in the upgraded `CAVEMAN_HOME` (93 MB `ccr.db` with a 33 MB WAL; a fresh home on the same binary replies in ~10 ms), and the Pebble native runtime, sessions and `caveman doctor` live in that repo. One part *is* in scope here and wants its own issue: the fail-open direction — the pi extension silently stores no recovery copy and does no shrinking.
- **#1236** (agent-drift: hermes) — not reproduced. The latest-drift lane resolves hermes from a GitHub release tag, and `releases/latest` is 403 through this environment's proxy; PyPI stops at 0.19.0, so 0.22.0 cannot be installed or probed here. Worth knowing: the body now renders the corrected single-cause sentence, so the `drift-report.mjs` fix from #1196 is confirmed working in production. The captured `help_error` in the `agent-probe-hermes` artifact is still the one thing that settles whether 0.22.0 broke `--help` upstream or trips over the probe's isolated environment.
- **#1240** (api.caveman.so 503) — cannot verify: this environment returns `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` for every `*.caveman.so` host, so 503-versus-blocked and up-versus-down are indistinguishable. No repo change available either way.
- **#1225**, **#1242** — skipped; triaged 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-10 with no activity since, verdicts unchanged.
- Not re-investigated, no new verdict: #1217, #1216, #1115, #1102, #1093, #1090, #1053, #1028, #1020, #863, #573, #570, #374, #271, #186.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1273 by @u7k4rs6** — first commit adopted as `15ebd61` (credit preserved; supersedes that commit only, not the PR). The table work is a real improvement and the right fix for #1272's other half, not adopted only because this routine doesn't implement features. For your decision: ~900 new lines in `html_structural.go`, and the PR is honest that pages whose tables used to be flattened can come out **larger**. Rebasing on this PR drops its first commit cleanly.
- **#1270 by @tejgokani** — **adopted** as `106ec34`, plus `5f332af` for the one gap. Four of five tests fail on `main` for the right reasons. `checksums.sha256` correctly regenerated. Worth noting: the atomic rename also defeats the symlink redirect on its own, since `rename` replaces the link rather than following it — the explicit `lstatSync` is good defence in depth on top.
- **#1269 by @tejgokani** — needs changes; the hardening itself is good. Of its nine tests, only the four curl-flag ones fail on `main`. The five Node-fallback tests pass unchanged there, because they exercise an **inline reimplementation** of `downloadTo` declared in the test file, not the real function. The header says the copy must stay "structurally identical" but nothing enforces it, so those five prove nothing today and will rot. `installer/install.js` has no exports and calls `main()` at load, which is why — the honest fixes are a `require.main === module` guard plus `module.exports`, or spawning the real installer with `curl` off PATH the way the curl tests already do. For priority: the remote-hook path already verifies every download against the pinned checksum manifest, so the real win is the time/size bounds rather than redirect substitution.
- **#1274 by @jwcastillo** — **adopted** as `8e0e22b`. The most serious bug triaged: the fix pass could write a model-rewritten destructive command over the user's source file.
- **#1276 by @jwcastillo** — **adopted** as `edd228e`. Verified the paths its cleanup recomputes match the locked body's exactly, and that `backup_dir_for`/`_state_base_dir` are pure, so the call site adds no new failure mode. One cosmetic note passed to the author, left as written rather than edited inside an adopted commit: the cleanup's `unlink(missing_ok=True)` isn't itself guarded, so a `PermissionError` there would replace the original exception on the way out (exit code still nonzero).
- **#1277 by @jwcastillo** — correct, and a genuine command-execution bug: `caveman mem remember -- "<block>"` runs backticks and expands `$VAR` in a block whose `content_sha256` the skill just verified, then the skill trims the real block from the source on the strength of that hash. Not adopted, for one logistical reason: verifying it means building `packages/cli`, which perturbs the installer suite's baseline (see verification note). Reviewed statically — `stdio[0] = "inherit"` hands the bytes through undecoded, and temp-file-over-heredoc is right because `cavemem` stores bytes exactly and a heredoc appends a newline. Confirmed independently that `agent-skills.generated.ts` is a true generated artifact (`compile-registries.mjs` on a clean tree produces no churn). **Recommend merging on its own.**
- **#1275 by @peppekerstens** — sound, and its test does fail on `main` (verified). Explicitly defensive: the PR states opencode 2.0.29 calls `setup()` once because it drops a duplicate plugin id, so no installed user is hitting a double activation. Your call on carrying the `globalThis` registry. The design reads right either way — keying on `directory` + `workspaceID`, and the no-op disposer not releasing the active entry, are both correct.
- **#1284 by @ab-gad-leadliaison** — looks right; `go test ./proxy/internal/store/` is green with it (its test can't be checked against `main` alone, as it depends on the PR's `readSkillFrontmatter` signature change). The `disable-model-invocation` half is the valuable one: counting a skill Claude Code keeps out of context means a re-measure never shows the drop, so the net-token-negative gate rejects the least destructive fix for its own `dead_load:skills` finding. `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` with a fallback to the old key scan on invalid YAML is the right shape. **Recommend merging as-is.**
- **#1268 by @minhhung2556** — **confirmed correct, by CI**, and ported as `e7ecd67` with authorship preserved. Both removed URLs are `HTTP 404`; every other `docs.caveman.so` link in the checked set, including the `integrations/frameworks` guide it keeps, passes. Their PR still stands on its own and no-ops once either lands.
- **#1243 by @AlexCawl** — not adopted; verdict unchanged from 2026-10-10 (three product decisions above a triage routine). Now `mergeable_state: dirty` against a `main` that has since landed the user-level `.codex/codex-sessionstart.js` always-on path (#573), which its removal of the repo-local Codex hook config overlaps directly. Needs a rebase and a reconciliation with that path before the design questions are answerable.
- **#1267, #1220** — drafts, left alone. **#1239, #1036, #1191** — not reviewed. **#1259, #1280, #1281, #1282, #1283** (dependabot) — not reviewed; version-bump PRs are outside this routine's remit.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **The three pin bumps above** — two commits, or a word and the corrected history gets force-pushed onto this branch.
2. **Windows silent decline (#1263)** — surface it in `caveman setup`/doctor, or accept the silence?
3. **#1273's table work** — ~900 new lines in the engine, and some pages get larger. Worth it for #1272's other half, or narrower?
4. **#1262 / #1278 SKILL.md wording** — both reporters are waiting on a yes/no; #1262's offered a PR.
5. **Node-24-floored agents (#1237)** — the 10-14 run worked around it by downloading a Node 24 build, which is a triage container doing the lane's job. Should Node-24-floored agents be probed by a lane job instead? OpenClaw's bootstrap surface still has no automated check at all.
6. **`testedFrameworkVersions` ceiling for `@mastra/core`** — 1.77.0 passes the whole suite and the execution range already admits it, so nothing is broken; moving the tested ceiling off 1.70.0 is a release-surface call.
7. **`docs-links` is red on `main` right now**, and has been since those URLs were documented. Two triage runs treated its subject as unverifiable while CI was answering it on every PR. Worth deciding whether that check should gate `main` rather than only fail on PRs that happen to touch `docs/technical/**`.
8. **Two triage sessions are both awake and both editing this PR.** The 10-14 session is still subscribed and rewrote this body once; the 10-15 session merged the two rather than clobber it. Worth knowing in case the description shifts again under you — the per-issue comments, not this body, are the durable record of each verdict.

## Verification on the whole current head

Run in a **clean worktree**, so no local build state colours the numbers:

`npm test` **626 pass / 15 skipped / 0 fail** · `node --test tests/*.js` 30/0 · `python -m unittest discover -s tests` **251 OK** (up from 244: the new compress-safety tests) · `python tests/verify_repo.py` all passed, including the `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` manifest · `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` all ok · `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` gate passed · `packages/cli` windows-platform + hooks + native-enable + agent-registry + porcelain suites 252/0 · middleware 137/137 at both Mastra versions · compress suites `test_compress_safety.py` 65 OK plus `test_compress_cli.py`, `test_compress_concurrency.py`, `test_validate_inline.py` all OK.

CI on `e7ecd67`: **all seven workflows green** — `CI`, `engine-ci`, `codeql`, `docs-links`, `supply-chain`, `middleware-conformance`, `middleware-python`. No open review threads. `mergeable_state: clean`.

Two measurement notes, both resolved:

title: HTML data pages pass through or lose their table structure
body: The HTML compressor only looks for an article, so pages that are mostly data don't get much out of it. A dashboard or an Istanbul coverage index has no article to find and goes through whole, and on a coverage.py report every table cell ends up on its own line, so you can't tell which number belongs to which column and nothing gets trimmed. Also, githubstatus.com gets detected as terminal output instead of HTML, because it has a few stray carriage returns.

title: feat(engine): keep tables in HTML articles as tables
body:
The article extractor put every table cell on its own line and dropped the empty ones, so on a coverage.py report you couldn't tell which number belonged to which column, and none of the rows were trimmed. Tables that form a plain grid are now kept as Markdown tables and trimmed the same way CSV already is. The coverage.py function index I tested went from 115k to 72k tokens. Articles without tables come out exactly as before, while pages whose tables used to be flattened can come out a few percent larger, since every value now keeps its column.

The first commit makes percentages count as numbers when picking which rows to keep. The dashboard part is now split out into #1288, which builds on this one.

title: fix(compress): hold the fix pass to the first pass's code and frontmatter guards
body:
### Problem

The first compression pass protects two things from the model:

- **Frontmatter.** It is split off before the model sees the file and added back verbatim afterwards.
- **Code and `<!-- nocompress -->` regions.** `mask_code_blocks` replaces them with markers, and `restore_code_blocks` refuses to write if any marker changed. This also covers fences indented under a list item.

The fix/retry pass gives up both protections. `build_fix_prompt(original_text, compressed, …)` sends the whole file, unmasked and with its frontmatter. The result is then checked only by `validate()`, plus a verbatim check of `<!-- nocompress -->` regions. `validate()` misses both cases:

- It never compares the frontmatter.
- It cannot see a fence indented under a list item, because `FENCE_OPEN_REGEX` allows at most 3 leading spaces and `extract_indented_code_blocks` skips runs inside lists.

So the repair can change a destructive command or rewrite `name:`/`description:`, pass validation, and be written over the source.

### Repro

Use a file with frontmatter and a fence nested under a list item. The first candidate drops the URL, so `validate()` rejects it and the fix pass runs:

````markdown
---
name: deploy-notes
description: Notes for deploying the service to production safely.
---

# Deploy

Some prose about the deploy process that is fairly verbose and wordy.

- Deploy:

      ```bash
      kubectl delete pod --all -n prod
      ```

See https://example.com/docs for more.
````

On `main`, the fix response can restore the URL and also do either of these:

- **(a)** Change `-n prod` to `-n dev`.
- **(b)** Rewrite `description:` as `deploy notes prod.`

The log shows `Validation attempt 2` / `Validation passed`, and the changed file is written.

### Fix

After the fix call, the candidate must now:

- Keep the frontmatter byte for byte (`split_frontmatter(fixed)[0] == frontmatter`).
- Contain every masked block from the first pass verbatim: fenced code, indented code (including list-nested fences) and `<!-- nocompress -->` regions.

The old check covered only nocompress regions. This change widens it to all masked blocks, so `nocompress_regions` is gone. If a check fails, the attempt is skipped, as the existing preamble and size guards already do. If no attempt passes, the original stays untouched and the backup and staging file are removed. The plugin mirror (`plugins/caveman/skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py`) is updated byte for byte.

### Tests

New tests in `tests/test_compress_safety.py` run the real `validate()` with a stubbed `call_claude`:

- `test_fix_pass_cannot_change_list_nested_code`: the repair changes `-n prod` to `-n dev`.
  - Fails on `main` because the file is written.
  - Passes with this change: the source is unchanged, and no backup or staging file is left.
- `test_fix_pass_cannot_rewrite_frontmatter`: the repair rewrites `description:`.
  - Fails on `main`.
  - Passes with this change.
- `test_fix_pass_that_only_restores_the_url_is_written`: a faithful repair is still accepted and written. This is a control: it passes both before and after.

Results (Linux, Python 3, node 24):

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 247 tests, OK.
- `python -m pytest -q tests`: 247 passed, 163 subtests passed.
- `python tests/verify_repo.py`: "All local verification checks passed". This includes the skills/plugin sync check.

title: fix(opencode): activate the 2.x plugin one time for each location
body:
## Summary

This change makes the opencode 2 entry point (`src/plugins/opencode/server.js`) activate one time for each location. A second `setup()` for the same location registers no hooks.

This change is defensive. opencode 2.0.29 does not show a double activation today.

## Why

opencode 2 can find `plugins/caveman/` two times:

1. The `plugin` entry in `opencode.json`. opencode 1.x needs this entry.
2. The auto-discovery of `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`.

opencode 2.0.29 logs `loading plugin` two times for this directory. But it calls `setup()` one time only, because it drops a duplicate plugin id. I traced this with a temporary log line in a test copy.

Before this change, nothing in `server.js` stopped a second `setup()`. If a host or a later opencode 2 calls `setup()` two times, caveman registers a second event subscriber, a second prompt hook and a second context hook. The result is two banners in each request, and each `/caveman` command runs two times.

## What changed

- `server.js` keeps a set of active locations on `globalThis` under `Symbol.for('caveman.opencode.setup')`. A second module instance of the file uses the same set.
- The key is `ctx.location.directory` plus `ctx.location.workspaceID`. One opencode 2 service can run the plugin for several projects, so each project still gets its own setup.
- A second `setup()` for the same location registers nothing and returns a no-op disposer.
- The disposer of the first setup stops the event subscription and releases the location. A reload (dispose, then setup) activates again. opencode 2.0.29 closes the old plugin scope before it loads the new one.
- If `setup()` fails, it releases the location.
- `plugin.js` (opencode 1.x) does not change.

## Tests

- New test in `tests/installer/opencode.test.mjs`. It calls `setup()` two times with a fake `ctx` for the same location, from one module instance and from a second one. It checks that the hooks register one time, that a no-op disposer does not release the active copy, that a second location still loads, and that setup after dispose registers again. The test fails on current `main` and passes with this change.
- `npm test`: 627 pass, 14 skipped, 1 fail. The fail is `standalone hooks keep a stable PATH node symlink`. It fails on my machine with `EXDEV` because `/tmp` and `/usr/bin` are on different filesystems. This change does not touch it.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: all checks pass.

Real binaries, Linux x64, with a throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and the repo installer (`--only opencode --minimal`). A logging proxy recorded each model request:

| Binary | Prompt | Flag after the run | Model requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| opencode 2.0.29 | a normal question | `caveman` | 1 system message, 1 banner `(caveman)` |
| opencode 2.0.29 | `/caveman off` | removed | 1 system message, no banner |
| opencode 2.0.29 | `/ultracave` | `ultracave` | 1 system message, 1 banner `(ultracave)` |
| opencode 1.18.31 | `/caveman megacave` | `megacave` | 1 system message, 1 banner `(megacave)` |

opencode 2.0.29 showed no `WARN` log lines for these runs.

## Not tested

- The opencode 2 TUI. I used `opencode run --standalone` only.
- A host that calls the new `setup()` before it disposes the old one. With this change, that order would leave the plugin inactive after the old copy is disposed. opencode 2.0.29 does not use that order.

title: fix(compress): remove the backup and staging file when the run dies before the live write
body:
## Problem

`_compress_file_locked` writes the backup (`~/.local/share/caveman-compress/backups/<parent>/<stem>.original.md`) and stages each candidate in `<file>.caveman-staged` next to the source. It only removes them on the normal "failed after retries" branch.

`call_claude(...)` can raise during the fix call:

- `RuntimeError` on a 300 s timeout
- a CLI or auth failure
- an HTTP error from `openai-compat`

The user can also press Ctrl-C (`KeyboardInterrupt`) during that call. Nothing in the function catches either one, and `cli.py` only calls `sys.exit`. The original file is untouched, but two files are left behind:

- `<file>.caveman-staged` stays in the repo, where it can get committed.
- The backup stays, so every later `/caveman-compress <file>` prints "Backup file already exists ... Aborting". The user has to find the backup and delete it by hand.

## Repro

1. Pick a file whose first compression fails validation. For example, the model drops a heading.
2. Make the fix call raise, either with a provider timeout or by pressing Ctrl-C while it runs.
3. Run `/caveman-compress <file>` again. It prints "Backup file already exists" and aborts. `<file>.caveman-staged` is still next to the source.

In tests: stub `call_claude` with `side_effect=[first_candidate, RuntimeError(...)]` and make `validate` fail.

## Fix

`compress_file` now wraps the call to `_compress_file_locked` in `try/except BaseException`. When anything is raised, KeyboardInterrupt included:

- It always removes the staging file.
- It removes the backup only if both hold:
  - The backup did not exist before this run. A backup from an earlier run, or from another file that maps to the same backup slot, is never touched.
  - The live write never started. `_compress_file_locked` sets `run["live_write_started"] = True` on the line just before the live `_write_target(filepath, ...)`. A failure in that write therefore keeps the backup, which is what the existing `test_forced_primary_write_failure_leaves_original_and_backup_intact` expects.
- It then re-raises, so `cli.py` still reports the error and sets the exit code.

The cleanup is at the call site, not in a `try/finally` around the validate/fix loop. That keeps the loop body unchanged, so this PR does not conflict with #1274, which edits the fix-pass guard block. A trial merge of both branches went through with no conflicts.

The script and its plugin mirror (`plugins/caveman/skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py`) are changed together.

## Tests

New tests in `tests/test_compress_safety.py`:

- `test_fix_call_exception_leaves_no_backup_or_staging`: the fix call raises `RuntimeError`. Afterwards the source is unchanged, there is no backup and no staging file, and a second run compresses normally.
- `test_fix_call_keyboard_interrupt_leaves_no_backup_or_staging`: the same with `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- `test_error_after_live_write_keeps_the_backup`: the run is interrupted right after the live file is replaced. The backup must survive.
- `test_error_before_backup_check_keeps_an_existing_backup`: the run is interrupted before the backup check. The backup from an earlier run must survive.

Against unpatched `compress.py`, the first three fail and the fourth passes.

| `python -m pytest -q tests` | 248 passed, 163 subtests passed |
| `python tests/verify_repo.py` | All local verification checks passed |
| `python -m pytest -q tests/test_compress_safety.py` | 62 passed |

title: fix(learn): store offloaded blocks from stdin, not a quoted shell argument
body:
## Problem

In the `cavemem_offload` step, `skills/caveman-learn/SKILL.md` tells the agent to run:

    caveman mem remember -- "<the real block>"

The block is a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md section, or text the user pastes into every session. Text like that usually holds backtick code spans, shell variables, quotes and `!`. Inside double quotes:

- The shell runs the backticks.
- The shell expands the variables.
- The first `"` in the block ends the argument early.

So the stored memory is not the block whose `content_sha256` the skill has just checked. The skill then trims the real block from the source. After that, the "byte-exact" `caveman mem recover` returns the altered text. This is the "make the agent dumber" result the skill exists to prevent. The block's content can also run commands.

`cavemem remember --stdin` already exists (`mem/cmd/cavemem/main.go`, `cmdRemember`). The CLI wrapper could not reach it: `caveman mem remember --stdin` dropped every argument that starts with `--` and printed the usage message.

## Repro

Take a block that contains:

    Before committing run `make clean` and check "$HOME/.config"

The agent follows the skill and runs `caveman mem remember -- "Before committing run `make clean` and check "$HOME/.config""`. Bash runs `make clean` and expands `$HOME`. The quote before `$HOME` ends the argument. The stored text is different from the block the skill verified.

## Fix

- `packages/cli/src/index.ts`
  - `caveman mem remember --stdin` (the only argument) now calls `cavemem remember --stdin`. The wrapper passes its own stdin to cavemem unchanged (`stdio[0] = "inherit"`), so the bytes are never decoded or re-encoded on the way.
  - `cavememRun` takes a new `stdin` option for this. Every existing call keeps the old piped stdin.
  - The usage line and `caveman mem` help now list `--stdin`.
  - `remember <text>` and `remember -- <text>` behave as before.
- `skills/caveman-learn/SKILL.md`
  - The agent now writes the block to a temp file with its file tool, then runs `caveman mem remember --stdin < <temp file>`.
  - The skill now says why the block must never go on the command line.
  - The new text contains no `$`, as `skill-file.test.mjs` requires.
- I chose a temp file over a quoted heredoc. A heredoc always appends a newline, and cavemem stores the text exactly as it arrives. With a heredoc, `recover` would return the block plus one byte, so it would not be byte-exact. A file written with the file tool holds exactly the verified bytes. It also cannot collide with a heredoc delimiter that appears inside the block.
- `packages/cli/src/agent-skills.generated.ts` is regenerated with `node packages/cli/scripts/compile-registries.mjs`. The copy embedded in the CLI stays byte-identical to `SKILL.md`, and `skills.runtime.mjs` checks this.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/tests/mem.runtime.mjs`, new test "mem remember --stdin passes the block to cavemem byte for byte":
  - A fake cavemem echoes what it reads on stdin.
  - The test sends a block with a leading `---` rule, backticks, `"$HOME"`, `!` and no trailing newline.
  - The block must come back unchanged.
  - Before the fix, the wrapper exits 2 with the usage message.
- `skills/caveman-learn/tests/skill-file.test.mjs`: SKILL.md must name `caveman mem remember --stdin` and must not contain `mem remember -- "`.

Results on this branch:

|---|---|
| `node --test skills/caveman-learn/tests/skill-file.test.mjs` | 6 / 6 pass |
| `node --test tests/mem.runtime.mjs tests/skills.runtime.mjs tests/learn-v2.runtime.mjs tests/verbs-gate.runtime.mjs tests/learn-implement.runtime.mjs` (in `packages/cli`) | 48 / 48 pass |
| `pnpm test` (in `packages/cli`) | FULL_SUITE_RESULT |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | Ran 244 tests, OK |
| `python -m pytest -q tests` | 244 passed, 163 subtests passed |

title: cavecrew: add brief guidance on working directory, hook triggers and git identity
body:
**What you want**

The `cavecrew` skill documents when to delegate and what each agent returns, but gives no guidance on what the delegating brief should carry. Add a short "Briefing builders and reviewers" section with two rules for any subagent that runs commands:

1. Set an explicit working directory outside live, hook-enabled trees. Do not put text that matches a lifecycle-hook trigger in command text run inside such a repo.
2. Fresh clones may lack a git identity, so set repo-local `user.name`/`user.email` before delegating commits.

**Before/after example**

```
Before: Brief to cavecrew-builder: "Fix X in repo Y and commit."
        Builder pasted text containing a hook trigger string into a command run in the live project; the harness hook matched it and rewrote a tracked file. Reverted only because the builder noticed and reported it. In parallel runs over several fresh clones, every first commit failed for lack of a git identity and builders improvised or asked.
After:  Brief states the cwd, forbids trigger phrases in command text, and the lead sets the git identity first.
```

**Why good**

The subagent cannot discover these hazards before they fire, while the lead usually already knows them. Observed in one session running parallel builders against several local clones.

title: Native runtime closes every native.sock request with an empty reply after a 2.0.1 → 4.0.1 upgrade (pi shrink silently off)
body:
## Summary

After an upgrade from 2.0.1 to 4.0.1, the native runtime accepts each connection on `~/.caveman/run/native.sock`, then closes it with an **empty reply**. It does this for every request, `session.start` included. `caveman native-hook pi PostToolUse` then prints nothing, so the pi extension fails open: it stores no recovery copy and does no shrinking, with no warning. `caveman doctor pi` does not flag it.

The same binary and environment with a fresh `CAVEMAN_HOME` reply in about 10 ms. That points at state in the upgraded home. This could be a sibling of #1149.

## Steps

1. Run Caveman 2.0.1 with pi sessions for some days.
2. Upgrade: `npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli@4.0.1`, `caveman setup --install` (bin-v4.0.1, checksums verified), `caveman setup --yes --agents none --skip routing,scripts`.
3. Restart the proxy. Here it is a launchd job: `caveman-proxy serve` with `CAVEMAN_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8787 CAVEMAN_PROXY_OWNER=start CAVEMAN_MODE=compress CAVEMAN_RECOVERY=mcp CAVE_ENGINE_TOON=best-of`. The run state shows `bin-v4.0.1`, `owner: start`, `recovery_via_mcp: true`.
4. Send the request that `native-hook pi PostToolUse` builds (protocol_version 1, `tool.after`) to `native.sock`, terminated with a newline.

## Result

| `CAVEMAN_HOME` | `session.start` | `tool.after` (37 KB tool output) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| upgraded `~/.caveman` | 0 bytes, closed after 0.3 s | 0 bytes, closed after 1.9 s |
| fresh home (symlinked `bin/`, copied `cloud.json`), same env, with `serve` and without it | `{"action":"allow",…}`, under 10 ms | `{"action":"allow","recovery_ref":"ccr://ccr_obj_…",…}`, about 10 ms |

The upgraded home holds a 93 MB `ccr.db` with a 33 MB WAL, and a 25 MB `caveman.db`. Five `caveman-mcp` processes from older 2.x pi sessions still hold `ccr.db` open next to the new proxy. I did not stop them, because they belong to other running sessions. That makes contention or a blocked migration my best guess, but I have not confirmed it.

## A second observation

Even the healthy runtime proposes no `output_replacement` for that 37 KB tool output, which is a uniform JSON array of 47 objects, in `compress` mode (`policy_mode: safe`, `profile: full-safe`). It returns only `recovery_ref`. `caveman doctor pi` lists `post_tool_rewrite` as supported. Does pi get output rewrites in 4.0.1, and if so, which outputs qualify?

## Environment

macOS 27 (arm64), pi 1.2.0 (doctor: `tested_version` 1.0.4, `newer_unknown`), `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1, `bin-v4.0.1`. The pi extension is loaded from `dist/caveman-pi-extension.mjs` through a small loader, not through `caveman enable pi`. A test with `caveman setup --agents pi` in a fresh home behaved the same.

Updates `tzdata` from 2026.4 to 2026.5
Release notes

Sourced from tzdata's releases.

2026.5: Release of upstream tzdata 2026e

Version 2026.5

Upstream version 2026e released 2026-09-30T00:14:38+00:00.

Briefly:

Manitoba moves to permanent -05 on 2026-10-31.

Changes to future timestamps

Manitoba’s 2026-03-08 spring forward was its last foreseeable clock change, as it moved to permanent -05 thereafter. Model this with its traditional abbreviation EST. Although the change to permanent -05 legally takes place on 2026-10-31, temporarily model the change to occur on 2026-11-01 at 02:00 for the same reason as other recent temporary hacks. (Caution: see “NOTE FOR 2026b TEMPORARY HACK FOR CLDR AND CANADA” below.)

As the change affects both America/Winnipeg and its backward compatibility link, the obsolescent setting TZ="Canada/Central" will now use the abbreviation EST for affected timestamps, akin to TZ="Canada/Pacific" behavior introduced in 2026b.

Another TZDB release may be needed soon if any of the portions of northwestern Ontario historically aligned with America/Winnipeg do not follow. For now, given the short leadtime with Manitoba’s announcement, assume that they will, to avoid creating new zones that may not be needed if no divergence occurs.

Changes to past timestamps

In 1925 Ireland fell back on 09-20 not 10-04 (thanks to Stan Ulbrych).

Changes to commentary

Discussion on timekeeping practices in northwestern Ontario has been expanded in light of Manitoba’s recent announcement. It is not yet known whether or to what extent these areas may adapt their own timekeeping practices in response.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

New Features

  • Claude Haiku 5.5: anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5, with adaptive thinking up to xhigh/max effort.
  • Adjust default tools with +name/-name: --tools entries like pi -t +codemode,-write change the default selection instead of replacing it. See Tools.
  • GPT-6 Luna and image classification: OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna is available as a classifier model through the Decisions API, and codemode's models.classify() accepts images for classifiers that support them. See Use classifier models.
  • Native llama.cpp decision models: Julia-1, Laya, Kev, lev, and OpenJev served by llama.cpp 0.6.0 or later run natively as classifiers through /v1/systemone. See Classification.

Added

  • Added +name and -name entries to --tools, which change the default tool selection instead of replacing it, for example pi -t +codemode
  • Added durationMs to the tool render context and to tool_execution_end extension events: the recorded execution time of a final tool result (#10549)
  • Added outputPad to the tool render context (#10557 by @​rwachtler)
  • Added OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna as a classifier model through the Decisions API, available with OPENAI_API_KEY (see Use classifier models)
  • Added images to codemode's models.classify() context, so classifiers that accept images, such as GPT-6 Luna, can judge them
  • Added program status reporting with OSC 7501: terminals and agent dashboards that support it see whether Pi is working, blocked on a dialog or login, done, or failed. PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1|0 overrides detection (see Terminal setup) (#10607)
  • Added aborted to agent_settled session, extension, and JSON events, so integrations can tell a cancelled run from a finished one (#10607)
  • Added Claude Haiku 5.5 (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5), with adaptive thinking up to xhigh/max effort and prompt caching on Bedrock
  • Added native llama.cpp decision models: Julia-1, Laya, Kev, lev, and OpenJev served by llama.cpp 0.6.0 or later are listed only as classifiers through /v1/systemone instead of as chat models (see Classification) (#10382)

Changed

  • Changed outputPad to also apply to ! command output, tool output, and summary blocks (#9946, #10557 by @​rwachtler)
  • Changed pi mcp login --timeout to limit the whole sign-in, including requests to the authorization server, instead of only the wait for the browser (#10565)

Fixed

  • Fixed bash and PowerShell results losing Took after reloading a session, and the live Took including wall-clock steps; both now show the recorded execution time (#10549)
  • Fixed managed installs keeping every old release; pi update now keeps only the new release and the one it updated from (#10392, #10511 by @​davidbrai)
  • Fixed standalone binaries loading .env, .env.local, and .env.development from the launch directory into Pi's environment (#10473)
  • Fixed !! command headers losing their dim color once output arrives (#10557 by @​rwachtler)
  • Fixed the codemode description not marking searchTools(), describeTool(), and describeNamespace() as async, which led models to serialize the unawaited promise as {} (#10555)
  • Fixed codemode output items running together, so models could not tell where one text() or console.log() output ended and the next began. With several text items, each now starts with a ==> text N/M <== line, and console calls follow the other output in one <console_output> block with one line per call
  • Fixed /mcp waiting for all servers to connect before opening; the manager now updates live and remains usable while enabling, reconnecting, or disabling servers (#10562)
  • Fixed images being dropped as "could not be resized" when running under node --watch on Node 24.19+ and 26.x, where Node posts its own messages on the image resize worker channel (#10527)
  • Fixed clipboard paste doing nothing in Termux, and failed copies there omitting the Termux:API install hint (#10391)
  • Fixed ! and RPC bash output keeping fragments of color codes, such as a stray m, when a code was split across output chunks (#10504)
  • Fixed MCP OAuth sign-ins that could not be cancelled while waiting on the authorization server and kept running after the session ended. The sign-in screen now cancels with Esc at every step, session shutdown aborts a running sign-in, and each request to the authorization server times out after 15 seconds (#10565)
  • Fixed shutdown waiting up to 15 seconds to refresh an MCP OAuth token that was about to expire, only to close the server's session (#10565)
  • Fixed the fullscreen text selection surviving session switches and other transcript rebuilds, which highlighted unrelated text in the new transcript (#9311, #10567 by @​christianklotz)
  • Fixed OpenAI models on Bedrock ignoring the thinking level and always running at Bedrock's default reasoning effort (#9331, #10142 by @​jsanter27)
  • Fixed model headers in models.json not overriding the originator and User-Agent headers of Codex requests (#10429 by @​lucasmeijer)
  • Fixed server_busy and servers are currently busy provider errors ending the turn instead of being retried (#10543)
  • Fixed Mistral responses that end with finish_reason: "error" not being retried (#10487)
  • Reduced context-limit request failures by estimating input at 3.5 characters per token instead of 4 when calculating output limits (#10497)
  • Fixed Radius models disabled by an organization owner still being listed
  • Fixed Anthropic browser login failing with "localhost refused to connect" when port 53692 is reserved or in use, for example by Hyper-V/WSL port exclusions on Windows: login now falls back to a free loopback port (#10571)
  • Fixed session costs undercounting long prompts on models with prompt-length pricing tiers, such as Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, through OpenCode, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Google, MiniMax, and other providers
  • Fixed Markdown links not being clickable in Herdr (#10573)
