title: fix(learn): skip disable-model-invocation skills, read multi-line descriptions
body:
## Problem

`caveman learn` overstates the skill catalog tax (`config_tax`, `dead_load:skills`) in two cases, both in `proxy/internal/store/config_scan.go`:

1. **`disable-model-invocation: true` is ignored.** `scanSkills` counts every `SKILL.md`, but Claude Code keeps a skill with this flag out of the model's context until the user invokes it (`/name`). Hiding an unused skill this way is the least destructive fix for a `dead_load:skills` finding, yet the re-measure never shows the drop, so the net-token-negative gate rejects it. The only change the gate accepts is removing the skill folder.
2. **Multi-line descriptions count as empty.** `readSkillFrontmatter` keeps only the text on the `description:` line itself, so a plain multi-line or block-scalar (`>`, `|`) description counts as just the skill name. `vercel-composition-patterns` is one example.

## Fix

- Parse frontmatter with `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`, which is already a module dependency. If the YAML is invalid, fall back to the old single-line key scan. Hand-written frontmatter often has an unquoted `: ` in a description.
- Skip skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` in `scanSkills`.

## Tests

- `TestScanSkillsSkipsModelInvocationDisabledSkills`
- `TestReadSkillFrontmatterDescriptionForms`: single-line, plain multi-line, folded `>-`, quoted, and loose (non-strict) YAML.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/store/`, and `go test ./internal/store/` pass.
- Checked by hand against a real `~/.claude/skills`: the flagged skill was skipped, and `vercel-composition-patterns` went from 7 to 57 tokens.

title: Routing: offer Auto (caveman-auto) in pi
body:
## Request

Offer Auto (`caveman-auto`) in [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi).

In 4.0.1, the routing module adds Auto to the model pickers of Claude Code and OpenCode only. `dist/caveman-pi-extension.mjs` has no reference to `caveman-auto`, so a pi user cannot select Auto. This is true even with the routing module on and the user signed in.

## What a pi integration needs

- **A model entry.** pi has its own model registry. The extension can already re-point a model with `pi.setModel`, and an extension can also register a provider. A `caveman-auto` model on a provider that points at the local proxy would make Auto selectable with `/model`.
- **Bearer-only gateways.** pi sends a provider key as `Authorization: Bearer` and as `x-api-key`. On the built-in `anthropic` upstream, the bin-v4.0.1 proxy forwards only `x-api-key`, and a bearer-only gateway answers 401. I measured this on 2026-10-14. The #1215 fix keeps the bearer on named compat mounts only. Auto for pi needs the bearer kept on whichever path it uses.
- **Prompt cache.** pi documents that a switch to another model between turns loses the prompt cache. An Auto decision that changes the model mid-session therefore makes the provider write the conversation to the cache again. The 4.0 note "a session stays on its model across Cloud pauses" helps. A short note on how often Auto changes models inside one session would help users estimate the cost.

## A related option

`route-ask-v1` sends `ask.text` (the latest human turn, up to 128 KiB), `ask.prev_text` and `ask.reply_tail` to Cloud. Some companies do not let prompt text leave their network. In those companies, Auto is usable only with an option to route on the on-machine signals alone (`signals`, `request`, `models`), without the `ask` texts. Is such an option planned?

Environment: `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1, `bin-v4.0.1`, pi 1.2.0, macOS 27.

title: pi: tool-output shrinking stops silently when the native runtime returns an empty reply
body:
## Summary

When the native runtime returns an empty reply, pi's tool-output shrinking stops with no sign. `caveman native-hook pi PostToolUse` prints nothing and exits 0. `shrinkToolResult` in the pi extension then returns `undefined`, so Pi keeps the full output, stores no recovery copy, and shows no warning. `caveman doctor pi` reports no problem either. Split out of #1279, as suggested there.

## Why it matters

A user turns on the `input` module to save tokens. If the runtime fails, the saving goes away and nothing tells the user. On the machine in #1279, this lasted from the upgrade until I probed `native.sock` by hand.

## Steps

1. Make the runtime return an empty reply. In my test, a held write transaction on `ccr.db` does it: the runtime closes the request after about 5 s. The live runtime in #1279 does it for every request.
2. Run a pi session and produce a large tool output.
3. The output reaches the model unchanged. No notification appears, and stderr shows nothing.

## Suggestion

- In the pi extension, when `PostToolUse` gets no reply, notify once per session, for example: "Caveman: tool-output shrinking is off this session (the native runtime gave no reply)". The `SessionStart` path already notifies "caveman native runtime unreachable" when it gets no reply.
- In `native-hook`, write one line to stderr when the runtime reply is empty, instead of printing nothing.
- In `caveman doctor <agent>`, send a `session.start` to `native.sock` and report a runtime that answers with an empty reply.

Environment: `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1, `bin-v4.0.1`, pi 1.2.0, macOS 27.

title: fix(antigravity-cli): declare contextFileName in agy plugin.json
body:
## Problem

agy 1.3.5 stopped auto-discovering `rules/AGENTS.md` (agy 1.2.17 did). Installing caveman via antigravity-cli staged a plugin.json without `contextFileName`, so the always-on caveman ruleset was not loaded. New agy sessions started in verbose mode and `/caveman status` reported `(not tracked by this host)`.

## Change

- `installer/install.js`: declare `contextFileName: 'rules/AGENTS.md'` in the staged plugin.json; switch hardcoded version to `packageVersion(repoRoot)` (matching OMP plugin path); run `agy plugin enable caveman` after install.
- `skills/activation-rule.mjs`, `src/rules/caveman-activate.md`, `src/tools/caveman-init.js`: update caveman skill docs with persistence note, expanded switch aliases (`/caveman:caveman`, `/caveman:ultracave`, `/caveman:megacave`), and `/caveman status` command.
- `tests/installer/antigravity-cli.test.mjs`: add assertion that installed `plugin.json` contains `contextFileName: 'rules/AGENTS.md'`.

## Validation

- `node --test tests/installer/antigravity-cli.test.mjs`: 4/4 pass (was 3/4 fail on contextFileName assertion)
- `node --test tests/installer/rule-copies.test.mjs`: 4/4 pass
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: all local checks pass

## Limitations

- Only verified against the project's stubbed `agy` test double; real agy 1.3.5 integration not exercised in CI (no agy in CI environment).
- Documentation updates in three files are duplicative but each serves a distinct runtime entrypoint (skill loader, hook bootstrap, CLI init).

title: fix(nativeruntime): honor the hook deadline inside Handle
body:
Fixes #1279

## Problem

After a 2.0.1 → 4.0.1 upgrade, every request to `~/.caveman/run/native.sock` is closed with an empty reply, so the pi hook fails open silently — no recovery copy, no shrinking, and `caveman doctor pi` flags nothing. The report's trigger: stale 2.x `caveman-mcp` processes still hold `ccr.db` open, so their cross-process write lock turns every store call the runtime makes into a wait on the store's own `busy_timeout` (5000 ms, `engine/ccr/store_sqlite.go:81`), serialized behind `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` (`engine/ccr/store_sqlite.go:203`).

`Runtime.Handle` (`proxy/internal/nativeruntime/runtime.go`) discarded its `context`, so the 250 ms hook deadline the caller applies (`hookDeadline`, `proxy/internal/nativeruntime/server_common.go:70`) could not interrupt a store call wedged on that lock: each request waited out the full 5 s and failed with `database is locked (5)` (SQLITE_BUSY), and `serveConn` then closed the connection with 0 bytes, seconds after the hook had already failed open (`server_common.go:84-89` closes without a synthetic decision by design). Queued same-session events waited out another full busy timeout each.

## Change

`Handle` now honors its context and returns fail-open at the deadline:

- the session stripe is acquired with a bounded `TryLock` wait instead of an unbounded lock;
- the store-backed half of the decision drains on a goroutine, so `Handle` stops waiting at the deadline while the in-flight statement finishes or fails on its own;
- store work not yet started after the deadline is skipped instead of queued;
- the stripe moves with the drain, preserving per-session event order.

The socket protocol is unchanged: an undeliverable decision still closes the connection without a synthetic response (`TestServeConnRuntimeErrorReturnsNoSyntheticDecision` stays green), and a fresh home still answers with a real decision well under the budget.

Test-fixture note: the lock holder is a second connection on the same `ccr.db` (`BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`) — the same SQLite lock state as the stale 2.x processes, without external process dependencies; the fresh-home case goes through `ServeUnix` and an in-test socket client speaking the same protocol as `Call`.

## Tests

New `proxy/internal/nativeruntime/hook_budget_test.go` (4 tests), asserting the budget with a held write lock. On the pre-fix tree the same tests measured `Handle` at 5.09 s (asserted < 1.5 s), a queued same-session event at 5.11 s, the empty-reply close at 5.10 s, and the store error `ccr typed object put: database is locked (5)`; after the fix, this session re-ran all four (`go test -v -count=1 -run 'TestHandleReturnsBeforeStoreBusyTimeout…|TestQueuedSessionEvent…|TestServeConnClosesWithinBudget…|TestFreshStoreSocketAnswers…' ./proxy/internal/nativeruntime/`):

- `Handle` fails open at **250.7 ms** (250 ms deadline), queued event at **250.0 ms**, empty-reply close at **250.6 ms**, fresh-home decision in **361 µs** (< 50 ms budget).

Regression, this session, go1.26.9 darwin/arm64 (`GOPROXY=https://goproxy.cn,direct` — proxy.golang.org unreachable on this machine):

```
timeout 300 go test -count=1 ./proxy/... ./engine/ccr/...   → 28 packages ok, 0 FAIL
go test -race -count=1 ./proxy/internal/nativeruntime/      → ok 5.783s
timeout 300 go build ./...                                  → ok
go vet ./proxy/... ./engine/ccr/...                         → clean
gofmt -l proxy/internal/nativeruntime/                      → 0 files
```

Signed off (DCO). Written with Claude Code (AI-assisted); every number above was run against the final commit.

title: fix(pi): tell the session when the native runtime goes quiet
body:
Fixes #1287.

## Problem

`shrinkToolResult` returns `undefined` for two different situations:

1. the runtime answered and decided not to shrink this result, and
2. the runtime gave no reply at all — `caveman native-hook pi PostToolUse` printed nothing and exited 0.

Both fall out of the same `undefined`, so when a runtime stops answering mid-session (as in #1279) tool-output shrinking quietly stops for the rest of the session. The user pays full token cost, Pi stores no recovery copy, nothing is shown, and `caveman doctor pi` is happy. That is the first bullet of this issue's suggestion list:

> In the pi extension, when `PostToolUse` gets no reply, notify once per session.

## Change

- `shrinkToolResult` takes an optional `onNoReply` callback, invoked **only** on the empty-reply path. The other skip paths (no text, over `MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`, an unusable/absent replacement, a handle that does not verify) are ordinary per-result decisions and deliberately stay silent.
- `index.ts` wires it to the existing `notify` helper, once per session:

  > Caveman: tool-output shrinking is off this session (the native runtime gave no reply)

  It is gated on `runtimeReachable`, which is set when `SessionStart` came back. A session that never reached a runtime already got the *"native runtime unreachable"* notice, so the two can never both fire; a replacement/resumed session resets both flags.

Fail-open behaviour is unchanged — the shrink is still skipped, the original bytes still survive, the callback only reports.

## Tests

`tests/recovery.runtime.mjs` gains a case covering: an empty reply raises the signal (and every empty reply does, the caller rate-limits), a real reply never raises it however the reply is judged (accepted, no handle, unresolvable handle), and a result that is skipped before the bridge is ever asked raises nothing.

```
node --test --test-force-exit tests/recovery.runtime.mjs   # 13/13 pass
npm run build                                             # tsc --noEmit + esbuild, clean
```

`tests/portable-command.runtime.mjs` fails in my sandbox on `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION: ".ts"` — it imports a `.ts` source directly and needs the Node >= 22.13 type-stripping this box's Node 20.19.2 does not have. Pre-existing and unrelated to this diff.

## Not in this PR

The other two suggestions (a stderr line from `native-hook` on an empty runtime reply, and a `session.start` probe in `caveman doctor`) live outside the pi extension, and the pi bridge currently discards the hook child's stderr, so they would not surface here. Happy to split them off if you want them.

title: diff compressor elides "\ No newline at end of file" markers and pure-rename "rename to" headers as if they were context
body:
## What happens

`diffCompressor` (engine/compressors/diff.go) treats two kinds of git-diff lines that are *not* context as elidable context, because `isDiffStructuralLine` (diff.go:71) only recognizes `diff --git `, `index `, `--- `, `+++ `, `@@ ` and `+`/`-` lines. Everything else falls to the elide path whenever it sits more than `keepContext=2` lines away from a structural line (diff.go:40-46):

1. **`\ No newline at end of file`** — git emits this immediately after the line it annotates. When ≥3 context lines separate that line from the last changed line, the marker is dropped and replaced by `… N context lines elided (caveman) …`.
2. **Extended headers of rename/copy blocks** — `rename from`/`rename to` (and `copy from`/`copy to`). A 100%-similarity pure-rename block is `diff --git` + `similarity index` + `rename from` + `rename to`; the ±2 keep-window around `diff --git` covers lines 0-2, so `rename to` (the 4th line) is dropped whenever the block is the last file section of a multi-file diff.

## Before/after example

Example A — `\ No newline at end of file` lost (change near the top of a file whose last line has no trailing newline; 21-line hunk, so the compressor fires):

```
Input (last lines of a >12-line git diff):
@@ -1,20 +1,20 @@
 ...
 import collections
-old_value = 1
+new_value = 2
 import os
 import sys
 import json
 import logging
 import hashlib
 import datetime
final_line = compute()
\ No newline at end of file

Output:
 ...
 import collections
-old_value = 1
+new_value = 2
 import os
 import sys
… 6 context lines elided (caveman) …

=> the "\ No newline at end of file" marker is gone
```

Example B — `rename to` lost (rename block is the last section of a multi-file diff, ≥12 lines total):

```
Input (last file section):
diff --git a/old_name.py b/new_name.py
similarity index 100%
rename from old_name.py
rename to new_name.py

Output:
diff --git a/old_name.py b/new_name.py
similarity index 100%
rename from old_name.py
… 1 context lines elided (caveman) …

=> the diff now says the file was renamed away but never says what it was renamed to
```

(Both outputs produced by walking diff.go's keep/elide loop line by line against commit d262ab3.)

## Impact

- The compressed diff now misstates the file: a model reconstructing the file from Example A adds a trailing newline that the original does not have; Example B loses the rename destination entirely, so `git apply`/review conclusions are wrong even before considering the legitimately elided context.
- Both are dropped under a marker claiming only "context lines" were elided — the exact invariant the `isChangedDiffLine` comment (diff.go:84-91) defends for `+`/`-` lines.

## Suggested fix

In `isDiffStructuralLine`, also keep:
- lines starting with `\` (git's `\ No newline at end of file`), and
- the extended headers by prefix: `old mode`, `new mode`, `deleted file mode`, `new file mode`, `copy from`, `copy to`, `rename from`, `rename to`, `similarity index`, `dissimilarity index`, `Binary files`, `GIT binary patch`.

These lines are short, appear at most a handful per file section, and are exactly the ones whose absence is invisible to the re-parse/elision accounting while changing patch semantics.

title: CR-terminated (classic-Mac) payloads detected as terminal output: whole document silently collapses to its last line
body:
## What happens

A payload whose lines end with bare CR (classic-Mac line endings) is detected as **terminal output** and silently collapses to its **last line**, with no elision marker and no pass-through.

Chain (commit d262ab3):

1. `looksLikeTerminal` (engine/detect.go:100-105): any payload with ≥3 bare CRs (`\r` not part of `\r\n`) is classified `terminal`, even with no ANSI escape anywhere.
2. `terminalCompressor.Compress` (engine/compressors/terminal.go:58) splits on **LF only** (lineends.go:14), so a CR-only document is a single "line".
3. `collapseCarriageReturns` (terminal.go:100) keeps only the **last non-empty `\r` segment** of a line (terminal.go:109-112) — correct for a progress-bar redraw, catastrophic for CR-as-line-terminator.
4. `len(lines) < 4` so `elideMiddle` never runs; `Compress` returns `ok=true` as long as the result differs from the input (terminal.go:142-144). The whole document is replaced by one line and the compression is claimed as a clean success.

## Before/after example

```
Input  (84-byte file, CR-only line endings, no ANSI):
Quarterly Report\rRevenue: $12,400\rExpenses: $9,100\rNet: $3,300\rSignatures: CEO, CFO\r

Output (21 bytes):
Signatures: CEO, CFO\r
```

Detect → `terminal`; `ok=true`; nothing in the output says anything was elided.

Secondary effect of the same root cause: any non-ANSI payload that merely contains ≥3 stray bare CRs (a text file with a few CR paste artifacts) routes to the terminal compressor, and every line containing a bare CR is truncated at its last CR — e.g. `Hello \rWorld` becomes `World`, silently.

## Expected

- A document with no ANSI escapes and CR line endings should not be treated as terminal-progress output (the "final visible state" argument doesn't hold when the CRs are the document's line terminators — the user saw every line, not a redraw), or
- the terminal compressor should recognize CR-only documents and treat `\r` as the line terminator (or at minimum emit an elision marker for what it drops).

## Suggested fix

Options, in increasing strength:
- In `collapseCarriageReturns` / `Compress`: when the payload contains no `\n` at all but multiple `\r`, split on `\r` instead of collapsing to one segment (same idea as lineends.go's per-line CR handling).
- In `looksLikeTerminal`: require an ANSI escape for the terminal classification, or exclude payloads where CRs are line terminators (e.g. zero `\n` but ≥2 `\r`).
- Weaker stopgap: emit an elision marker for dropped `\r` segments so the loss is at least disclosed.

Note: this is the engine's `terminal` compressor, a different component from the `caveman-compress` CRLF problems in #762/#533 (those are the skill's file rewriter on Windows).

Verified by porting `looksLikeTerminal` + `Compress`'s cleanup loop line-by-line against d262ab3 and running the 84-byte input above through it.

title: fix(diff): preserve patch metadata
body:
The diff compressor treated extended Git headers and `\ No newline at end of file` markers as ordinary context. In a long diff, this could remove a pure rename's destination or the final newline annotation while reporting that only context was elided.

Recognize newline markers, rename/copy headers, mode and similarity headers, and binary-diff headers as structural lines. The existing context window also retains the line annotated by a newline marker. Add regression cases for LF and CRLF payloads that check metadata remains verbatim while ordinary context still compresses.

Closes #1293

Validation:
- Reproduced the metadata loss with the regression test before applying the fix.
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./engine/... -count=1` passed on Windows with Go 1.26.9 and Zig 0.16.0.
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./...` passed.
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet ./...` passed.
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./...` passed.

title: fix(diff): keep git's extended headers out of the elided context
body:
Fixes #1293.

## What was wrong

`isDiffStructuralLine` (`engine/compressors/diff.go`) recognized only `diff --git `, `index `, `--- `, `+++ `, `@@ ` and `+`/`-` lines. Every other line fell to the elide path whenever it sat more than `keepContext=2` lines away from a structural line — so two kinds of git metadata were dropped and replaced by `… N context lines elided (caveman) …`:

1. **`\ No newline at end of file`** — git emits it right after the line it annotates, so it vanishes whenever ≥3 context lines separate it from the last changed line.
2. **Extended headers of rename/copy blocks** — a pure rename is `diff --git` + `similarity index 100%` + `rename from` + `rename to`. The ±2 window around `diff --git` covers lines 0–2, so `rename to` — the new path, the entire point of the block — is dropped whenever the block is the last file section of a multi-file diff.

The marker in both cases claims only context was dropped, which is what makes the loss silent.

## The fix

Treat git's extended headers as structural. Added `isDiffExtendedHeaderLine` with the column-0 prefixes git emits between `diff --git` and the first hunk (`similarity`/`dissimilarity index`, `rename`/`copy from|to`, `old`/`new`/`new file`/`deleted file mode`, `Binary files `, `GIT binary patch`) plus the `\ No newline at end of file` marker.

None of them can be context, so the column-0 match is unambiguous: inside a hunk every context line carries a leading space and every changed line a leading `+` or `-`. `TestDiffCompressorKeepsHunkLinesThatLookLikeHeaders` pins that down with a `+rename from old` / `-new file mode gone` hunk.

## Before / after

Example A — unterminated file, change near the top:

```
@@ -1,20 +1,20 @@
 import collections
-old_value = 1
+new_value = 2
 import os
 import sys
 import json
 import logging
 import hashlib
 import datetime
-final_line = compute()
\ No newline at end of file
```

Before, the last three lines collapsed to `… 6 context lines elided (caveman) …` and the marker was gone. Now `\ No newline at end of file` survives, along with the ±2 context lines around it.

Example B — pure rename as the last section of a multi-file diff:

```
diff --git a/old_name.py b/new_name.py
similarity index 100%
rename from old_name.py
rename to new_name.py
```

Before, `rename to new_name.py` was elided. Now the whole rename block is kept.

## Tests

Three new tests in `engine/compressors/breadth_test.go`, following the existing `TestDiffCompressorKeepsBlankLineChanges` precedent. The two bug tests fail on `d262ab3` and pass here; the third is a regression guard.

```
go test ./engine/...   # all packages ok
go vet ./engine/compressors/
gofmt -l engine/compressors/   # clean
```

Cost: marking ~13 more prefixes structural widens the keep window slightly for diffs that carry rename/binary headers. Those lines are metadata the reader needs in order to read the hunk, so the trade goes the right way, and CCR still holds the full original either way (S4).

Signed-off-by: Yi-111-a <98324547+Yi-111-a@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Dev agents dashboard merges different machines that share the same caveman home path
body:
**What happen**

On https://app.caveman.so/dev/agents, three separate Linux machines show up as one "machine". The `install_id` reported for a machine is `sha256(<caveman home path>)`, so every Linux host where the user has the same username gets the same id, and their requests are added together in one row.

- `printf %s /home/<user>/.caveman | sha256sum` equals the `install_id` that `reports.dev_agents` returns for all three Linux hosts.
- On Windows, `sha256("C:\Users\<user>\.caveman")` equals that host's `install_id`.
- `telemetry.anonymousId` in `~/.caveman/cloud.json` is different on every host, so it is not what keys the dashboard.
- The macOS host does not fit the pattern: its proxy runs with `HOME=/Users/<user>` and uses `/Users/<user>/.caveman`, but `sha256` of that path (or variants with a trailing slash, a `/private` prefix, the hostname, or the db/bin paths under it) does not match its `install_id`. I could not find what the macOS id comes from.

**Expected**

One row per machine: the three Linux hosts appear as three machines. Derive `install_id` from something unique per install (for example a random id generated once and kept in the caveman home, like `anonymousId` or `deviceId`), not from the path.

**Before/after example**

Five hosts (3 Linux, 1 macOS, 1 Windows), same account and project. Each ran:

    npx -y @caveman-ai/cloud@rc setup --project <id> --no-launch
    npm i -g @caveman-ai/cli
    caveman setup --install
    caveman claude

Got:  Machines = 3 (all three Linux hosts in one row, plus macOS and Windows)
Want: Machines = 5

Possibly related: some hosts upload only part of their traffic. One host has 28 requests in its local `caveman.db` for an hour but the dashboard shows 9 for the same window; another has about 2,200 local requests over 30 days and 30 in the dashboard. I can open a separate issue if useful.

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

caveman 4.0.1 via `npm i -g @caveman-ai/cli` (proxy `bin-v4.0.1`); cloud via `npx -y @caveman-ai/cloud@rc setup`; Claude Code 2.1.301. Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 container, Ubuntu on WSL), macOS, Windows 11.

title: Claude Code skips the caveman dependencies because the root uses a pnpm lockfile
body:
## What I see

I installed the plugin with `claude plugin install caveman@caveman`. Then `claude plugin list` showed this note:

> The packages it lists were not installed, because it uses a yarn or pnpm lockfile, which plugin installs do not support
> If it needs those packages, parts of it may not work. Updating or reinstalling this version of the plugin will not install them while that is still true

## Why the note appears

The plugin installer in Claude Code runs a dependency install only when the plugin root
holds a `package.json` and a supported lockfile. The installer accepts three lockfiles:
`bun.lock`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, and `package-lock.json`. The installer rejects
`pnpm-lock.yaml` and `yarn.lock`.

The note appears when the cached copy has all three of these properties:

- a lockfile
- runtime `dependencies` in the root `package.json`
- no `node_modules` directory

The caveman repository root has all three:

- The root `package.json` declares `"dependencies": { "@caveman-ai/cli": "^4.0.0" }`.
- The root ships `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- The installed copy has no `node_modules`.

I reproduced this behavior on 3.1.0. The `main` branch at 4.0.1 shows the same behavior.

## Why an update cannot remove the note

The documentation gives one instruction for this branch of the note. It says that an
update does not install the packages while the reason stands, and that the plugin
author must replace the lockfile.

A new npm lockfile alone is not sufficient. `@caveman-ai/cli` is a pnpm workspace
package in `packages/cli`. The automatic install also rejects `workspace:`, `file:`,
`link:`, and git dependencies.

## Suggested direction

The root `package.json` serves the npm package `caveman-installer`. The plugin does not
use that package. Two options:

1. Point the `source` field in the marketplace entry at a subdirectory. Put only the
   plugin files in that subdirectory: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `src/hooks/`,
   `skills/`, `commands/`, and `agents/`. Put no `package.json` and no lockfile at its
   root. This action clears the note. It does not change the npm package.
2. Keep the plugin root. Remove the runtime `dependencies` field there. Check first that
   `installer/install.js` can find the CLI in another way.

## The note does not break the plugin

Each hook that the plugin declares requires only Node built-in modules and sibling
files. The code reaches `@caveman-ai/cli` only from `installer/install.js` through
`require.resolve('@caveman-ai/cli/package.json')`. The note is cosmetic for the plugin
path.

Docs:

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading#node-js-package-dependencies
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/troubleshooting#the-packages-it-lists-are-not-installed

title: chore(agents): bump the Pi pin to 1.3.0
body:
Fixes #1225.

Moves the Pi pin from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.0.4 to **1.3.0** (current `latest`). The commit layout follows what `agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` requires:

1. `chore(pi)`: pi-extension devDependency, both lockfiles, README pin, and the compat tripwire literal
2. `ci(agents)`: conformance matrix pin only
3. `chore(agents)`: `agents/profiles/pi.json` plus the `node agents/compile.mjs` output only

## Compat review (the tripwire in `provider-compat.runtime.mjs`)

I diffed pi-ai 1.0.4 against pi-ai 1.3.0 (the copy nested under pi-coding-agent 1.3.0), in isolated prefixes:

- `detectCompat`/`getCompat` (openai-completions), `detectSessionAffinityFormat` (openai-responses) and `getAnthropicCompat` are textually identical. The one addition is `supportsMidConvoEffort` in the Responses `getCompat`. It comes from `model.compat`, not the URL, so there is nothing to freeze.
- **Helpers:** every `baseUrl` / `openrouter.ai` / `api.openai.com` line in pi-ai's `api/`, `utils/` and `providers/` code is unchanged. The only exceptions are the new `openai-decisions` API (not routed) and catalog data.
- The bundled chunks that the `pi` binary actually runs carry the same compat logic as `dist/api`. `core/provider-attribution.js` (the oracle for `unpreservedAttributionHeaders`) is byte-identical.
- 1.3.0 now drops thinking blocks from a different model. That check keys on provider/api/id. The router only swaps `baseUrl` and `compat`, so a routed turn still counts as the same model.
- Pi 1.2.0's `before_agent_start` union (custom-message runs carry no `prompt`) is already handled on main by 0f4643c8. At 1.3.0 the types also enforce it: the old `prompt: string` handler signature fails tsc with TS2769.
- **`--tools +name`/`-name` (1.1.0)**, probed with real Pi 1.3.0 through the stub gateway:

  | Flags | Tools sent to the model |
  |---|---|
  | (default) | `read, bash, edit, write, caveman_retrieve` |
  | `-t -write` | `read, bash, edit, caveman_retrieve` |
  | `-t +grep` | default plus `grep`, still with `caveman_retrieve` |
  | `-t read,bash` | `read, bash` only, still routed through `/w/pi` |

  The last row behaves the same on Pi 1.0.4 (re-probed from the old lockfile), so it is not a regression. It is listed under follow-ups.

## Lockfiles

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` (engine-ci `--frozen-lockfile`) and `packages/pi-extension/package-lock.json` (release job `npm ci`) both move. Both were deduped so that the extension's own `pi-ai` peer resolves to 1.3.0 and not a stale hoisted 1.0.4.
- `@earendil-works/chord` and its esbuild 0.28.2 drop out, because Pi 1.2.0 removed that dependency. Nothing outside Pi changed.

## Verification

- `node agents/probe-installed.mjs --require pi` with no `--allow-newer`, against 1.3.0 installed with `--ignore-scripts` into a temp prefix under a temp HOME: `ok` (version_ok, help_ok, version_matches)

- `node agents/check-profile-scope.mjs origin/main HEAD`: valid. `node agents/compile.mjs --check`: ok
- Root `npm test`: 638 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (two Windows-only, one skipped because a real CLI is installed alongside)
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: all checks passed

- **OpenCode Go endpoint moved.** Pi 1.3.0's catalog moved opencode-go from `https://opencode.ai/zen/go` to `https://opencode.ai/inference/go`. The proxy's built-in compat mount (`proxy/internal/config/config.go`) still publishes `/zen/go`, so `verifiedProviderRoute`'s path proof fails and stock OpenCode Go models on Pi ≥1.3.0 now stay direct (no compression). This fails closed and never misroutes, and it already affects anyone running Pi 1.3.0 whatever our pin says. Moving the mount is a proxy change with its own tests.

title: fix(cli): pin Gemini API-key auth when routed (exit 41)
body:
## Problem

When Caveman routes Gemini CLI, a user whose Gemini settings name no `security.auth.selectedType` (headless or CI, never ran the auth picker) gets `Invalid auth method selected.` and exit 41 before any request is sent.

Cause, read from the gemini-cli bundle and confirmed by live probes: `getAuthTypeFromEnv` checks `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_GCA`, then `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI`, then `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` → `gateway`, and only after that `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The CLI's `validateAuthMethod` has no `gateway` case. Both Caveman doors set `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`: wrap through env, native through `~/.gemini/.env`. So even a user with `GEMINI_API_KEY` set fails. Reproduced on 0.63.0, 0.64.0 and 0.65.0-preview.0. Upstream google-gemini/gemini-cli#27550 was closed not planned, and fix PR #27558 was closed without merging.

**Why not a system-settings overlay:** Gemini 0.63+ loads system and system-defaults files only when the file and every parent directory are root-owned (`isFileAndDirectorySecureSync`). A temp overlay is skipped with "not owned by root (uid 0)". No CLI flag or env var selects the auth type.

## Change

- **Native door** (`caveman enable gemini`, also reached by the `caveman gemini` shortcut):
  - Writes `security.auth.selectedType = gemini-api-key` into `~/.gemini/settings.json`, but only when the value is unset (or empty) and no GCA, Vertex, Cloud Shell or compute-ADC switch is on. The check reads the shell first, then `~/.gemini/.env` with the last line winning, as Gemini does.
  - The write is journaled (`owned.selected_auth`). Disable removes it only while it still holds that value, and keeps any containers the user already had.
  - The enable plan prints one line naming the setting.
  - An install from before this change journals no `selected_auth`, so `enable` and `doctor gemini --fix` re-wire it once. The shortcut still never mutates a journaled install.
- **Wrap door:** writes no user config, as before. A headless launch prints one line naming the setting to add, when no auth type is set in user or workspace settings and no switch is on. "Headless" follows Gemini's own `isHeadlessMode`. Interactive, ACP, version/help and subcommand runs skip the line.

No profile or schema change. Wrap routing stays declarative, so the registry's builder manifest is unchanged.

## Verification

- New tests in `packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs` and `wrap.runtime.mjs` failed before the fix and pass after. They cover: write only if unset; a user re-choice outliving disable; an existing OAuth choice; Vertex, Cloud Shell and dotenv GCA switches; a re-wire to a moved gateway; the old-install upgrade; empty containers kept; and the headless hint with its negatives.
- Full CLI suite (`env -u FORCE_COLOR -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, sanitize-host-env fixture): 1420/1432 pass. The 6 failures also fail on unmodified `main` in this environment: agent-compression-conformance (pi), caveman-bin-resolution, hooks record policy, two opencode-wrap Auto picker tests, wrap-restart. None involve Gemini.
- Live, real gemini-cli 0.64.0 in an isolated npm prefix, temp HOME, loopback stub, dummy key:
  - Native door before the fix (route in `.env` only): exit 41.
  - After `enable`: exit 0, `POST /w/gemini/v1beta/models/…:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` reached the stub with `x-goog-api-key`. `disable` restored the settings file.
  - Wrap door with no auth type: the hint, then Gemini's exit 41. With `selectedType` set: no hint, exit 0, routed.
- An independent Opus review found no blockers. Its medium findings (no upgrade path; Cloud Shell/ADC; silent pin) are fixed here.

## Known limits

- An interactive user who has never picked an auth type no longer sees Gemini's first-run picker after `enable`; `/auth` in Gemini changes the type.
- The env-switch check runs at enable time. A Vertex switch exported only per project, or set only in a project `.env`, is not seen.

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

  • 2026-09-01 v1.58.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.4. It carries upstream's own fix for the journal-rollback data-corruption bug, so the local super-journal patch v1.56.0 introduced is dropped; recovery behavior is unchanged. Also bumps the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.6; as always, downstream modules must pin the same version this one does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in support for Linux Open File Description (OFD) locks on database files, off by default; without opting in, locking behavior is byte-for-byte that of previous releases. A POSIX record lock is owned by the (process, inode) pair, so any Close of any descriptor of the database file anywhere in the process silently strips SQLite's locks; OFD locks survive that. Why it is process-wide rather than a DSN parameter, what WAL's -shm coordination still uses, and the /proc/locks measurements behind the design are in [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255).
    • Resolves [GitLab issue #255](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/255). See [GitLab merge request #136](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/136), thanks Nathan Herring (@​technosloth), and thanks Gani Georgiev (@​ganigeorgiev) for pressing the opt-in default!

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

title: Daily triage 2026-10-17 -> 24: pi extension cost regressions (prompt-cache rewrite, 1.8 KB outputs masked, retrieve promise), ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH default, CCR returns damaged bytes, stats ledger scan, caveman-compress cluster, agent pins
body:
Daily triage, seven runs on one branch (the 2026-10-17 PR was still open on each later run, so per the run's own rules this appends rather than opening a second). Nothing merged, closed or rejected.

**Run 7 (2026-10-24)** ships six fixes across three clusters, every one adopted from a contributor PR with authorship preserved. Each was reproduced with a failing test first.

- **The pi extension cost more than it saved** (#1364, #1365, #1368 — PRs #1376, #1378, #1377). Per-prompt runtime context was appended to the **system prompt**, so the provider rewrote its cache from the system prompt onward at every prompt; it now rides a hidden custom message, which pi documents as participating in LLM context, and the system prompt stays byte-stable. Tool outputs as small as 1.8 KB were replaced by a content-free handle the agent then paid a whole extra model request to redeem; a 4096-byte floor matches the Hermes shrink floor. And the mask promised "one call returns the entire original" while `caveman_retrieve` with a `query` returns a gap-marked excerpt — the MCP server's own schema was already honest, only pi's re-declared tool was not. The mask fix lands in the shared native runtime, so Claude Code, Codex and pi move together.
- **`caveman enable claude` changed the host's own default** (#1361 — PR #1362). With `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` unset Claude Code defaults to always-on tool search; caveman wrote `auto`, silently moving users to threshold mode, and hosts that connect MCP servers after the first request cross the threshold mid-session and bust the cache. One constant feeds both Claude routing doors (the persistent native install and the ephemeral `wrap` env), so both moved together; `disable` still withdraws a legacy `auto` as ours. Added the test the PR was missing for the `wrap` door.
- **The CCR store returned damaged bytes; stats scanned the whole ledger** (#1369, #1371 — PRs #1373, #1372). A `recoveries` row whose bytes no longer matched its content-addressed handle was handed back as a recovery; `Get`, `GetObject` and dedup resolution now verify the hash and fail with a distinct `ErrCorruptRecovery` (and `cave_corrupt_recovery` rather than `cave_unknown_handle`, so an agent stops retrying in vain). The stats window gets its `(julianday(ts), id)` expression index.

Both store issues are only **partly** addressed, so their commits say `Refs`, not `Fixes` — matching what @zsltg explicitly asked for. The expiry, consolidation-trigger and display questions in #1369/#1370/#1371 still need your decision, and #1370's own building-block PR #1374 is reviewed and recommended but held by this run's six-fix cap.

**New finding, not fixed:** `b4531df` moved `packages/cli/BINARY_RELEASE` to `bin-v4.0.2` without regenerating the five `*.generated.*` files, which still say `bin-v4.0.1`. `release-packages.yml` runs `gen-binaries.mjs --check` and exits 1 on exactly that drift, so this is what blocks #1366. Your own #1321 already carries the regeneration. `engine-ci.yml` checks `gen-device-auth.mjs` but not `gen-binaries.mjs`, which is why the half-bump reached `main` unnoticed — see the Run 7 comment.

Run 7 on `2833027`: root `npm test` (652, 635 pass / 0 fail), `node --test tests/*.js` (30/30), `unittest discover` (280 OK), `verify_repo.py` (all), `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/... ./mem/... ./mcp/... ./shrink/...` (ok), `packages/cli` (1439, 1424 pass / 0 fail), `packages/pi-extension` (146/146, nothing skipped), and `test-windows-compat.mjs` **passed** this run. Fast-forward `8c674f6..2833027`; **nothing force-pushed**; `main` merged cleanly (`fa7c75b`).

> **Full Run 7 report — fixes table, what I changed on top of each contributor PR, what was triaged without fixing, and the items needing your decision — is in [the Run 7 comment](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1315#issuecomment-6381609150).** Runs 1 and 2 are summarised below; their detail is in the branch history and in this PR's earlier comments.

**Run 6 (2026-10-23)** ships six fixes in one cluster: the seven `caveman-compress` issues @Warcren filed on 2026-10-22 (#1349-#1355) and the four contributor PRs that followed (#1356-#1359, all adopted with authorship preserved). Shared shape: `scripts/compress.py` guards the *fix* path but not the *first* path, and keys shared state on a name rather than a path. Headline bugs: a first-pass reply carrying model commentary and a second frontmatter block is written **and passes validation** (#1349); credential dotfiles reach the provider (#1354); and a backup key collision whose own abort message told users to delete another project's only uncompressed original (#1351). Also fixes a test file that ran 27 of its 34 tests and exited 0. #1352 reproduced as **already fixed** on `main` since `edd228e`.

> **Full Run 6 report — fixes table, changes made on top of each contributor PR, what was triaged without fixing, and three items needing your decision — is in [this comment](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1315#issuecomment-6359735940)**, not inline: this body is ~1.5KB from GitHub's 65,536-char cap.

Run 6 on `8c674f6`: `npm test` (647, 630 pass / 0 fail), `node --test tests/*.js` (30/30), `unittest discover` (**280 OK**, +29), `verify_repo.py` (all, incl. new `verify_test_entrypoints`), `go test` (ok). `test-windows-compat.mjs` fails identically on unmodified `main` (missing `node_modules` here) — environment, not regression. Fast-forward `58bec5e..8c674f6`; **nothing force-pushed**; `main` merged cleanly (`cfe1784`). Runs 1-5 unchanged below.

**Run 5 (2026-10-22)** ships two fixes. The first is the same `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gate as runs 2 and 4 — but this time it is **not another number bump, and it retires decision 14**: Anthropic shipped a coordinated major across *both* SDKs on 2026-10-21 (npm 1.0.0/1.1.0, PyPI 2.0.0/2.1.0), hours after run 4 committed. The npm bound was the only one in the table still carrying a next-*minor* bound, which is what made it go stale three times in five days; with upstream's 0.x line closed it becomes a next-*major* bound like every sibling, and the treadmill ends with the line rather than with another minor. The same release broke the **Python** sibling too, which run 4 checked and correctly cleared at the time — so both hosts move in one commit. The second fix bumps the `claude` pin after re-running its observed route probe, which also confirms run 4's decision 16 (the drift lane *is* verifiable from here — the probe worked first try). `main` is already an ancestor, so no rebase was needed and **nothing was force-pushed** (fast-forward `5b03f66..19cebb5`). Runs 1–4 are unchanged below.

Full suite green on `HEAD` (`19cebb5`): `npm test` (647 tests, 629 pass / 0 fail / 18 skipped), `node --test tests/*.js` (30/30), `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (251 OK), `python tests/verify_repo.py` (all checks), `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` (**gate passed, exit 0**), the TypeScript middleware conformance suite (137/137 under `CAVEMAN_REQUIRE_FRAMEWORKS=1`, run separately against three SDK releases) and the Python middleware suite (137 passed under `CAVEMAN_REQUIRED_ADAPTERS=anthropic`, against four releases). No Go file changed this run, so `go test` was not re-run; run 4's cgo note below still applies to anyone who does.

**Run 4 (2026-10-21)** adds three fixes and clears the whole agent-drift backlog. Two are adopted contributor PRs completed on top (an engine honesty invariant, a JSON determinism bug); the third is **not new work but a correction to run 2's own fix, which had gone stale and would have shipped broken** — see the first row below. Five agent pins moved after re-running the route probes they claim, which resolves run 3's decision 12 rather than deferring it again. `main` is already an ancestor, so no rebase was needed and **nothing was force-pushed** (fast-forward `e649529..5b03f66`). Runs 1–3 are unchanged below.

Full suite green on `HEAD` (`5b03f66`): `npm test` (647 tests, 629 pass / 0 fail / 18 skipped), `node --test tests/*.js` (30/30), `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (251 OK), `python tests/verify_repo.py` (all checks), `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/... ./shrink/...` under **cgo** (no failures), `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` (**gate passed, exit 0**), and the middleware conformance suite (137/137 under `CAVEMAN_REQUIRE_FRAMEWORKS=1`).

Two notes on reading that, because both bit me this run:

- **`CGO_ENABLED=0` is not a clean Go run here.** `TestReleaseShape*` carry no build tag on purpose and fail without tree-sitter, so a cgo-free `go test ./engine/...` reports three failures that mean nothing. cgo is available in this environment and every Go number above is a cgo run.
- **`node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` fails identically on `main` when the pnpm workspace is not installed** (`error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'node'`, exit 2). I confirmed that against a clean `main` worktree before trusting it, then ran `pnpm install` and got a real `gate passed`. A red windows gate in a fresh container is probably missing `node_modules`, not a regression.

## Fixes

### Run 5 — 2026-10-22

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1322 | **One upstream event, two hosts.** Anthropic shipped a coordinated major across both SDKs on 2026-10-21 — npm `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 1.0.0 at 16:00Z and 1.1.0 at 22:03Z, PyPI `anthropic` 2.0.0 at 15:51Z and 2.1.0 at 22:00Z — hours after run 4 moved the npm bound. Both certified adapters refuse the current latest in their own ecosystem, so anyone installing either SDK today gets fail-open pass-through with one warning and **no compression at all**. The npm bound moves `0.138` → `2` and the PyPI one `2` → `3`. The npm half is the structural end of decision 14, not a fourth widening: it was the only framework still carrying a next-minor bound (the zero-major caution), and that caution cannot apply to a line upstream has closed at 0.137.0. Upstream's only breaking change in either major is the default API version; the adapter surface was **verified intact rather than assumed** (`getUserAgent()` still returns `Anthropic/JS 1.1.0`, so the `/JS (\S+)$` read in `versions.ts` still resolves; `baseURL`, `withOptions` and `beta.messages.toolRunner` all present). | `@caveman-ai/middleware` (npm) **and** `caveman-middleware` (PyPI), all OS | existing conformance suites re-run against each release. TS: 137/137 on 1.1.0, 137/137 on 1.0.0, 137/137 at the 0.124.0 floor, under `CAVEMAN_REQUIRE_FRAMEWORKS=1`; the 12 pre-widening failures were all `reason: "unsupported_version"`. Python: 137 passed on 2.1.0, 2.0.0, 1.8.0 and 1.0.0 under `CAVEMAN_REQUIRED_ADAPTERS=anthropic`; the 28 pre-widening failures all read `anthropic requires anthropic<2,>=1.0`. Plus three new boundary assertions in `versions.test.mjs` (1.0.0 and 1.1.0 admitted, 2.0.0 refused) and `check-latest-in-range.mjs` 25/26 → 26/26 — that script is what surfaced the PyPI half. | — |
