The substantive finding (output shrinks ~36% in their pilot, the plugin's own instructions add ~19% input, net −3% with a 90% range of −12%..+2%) is a claim about this project's headline numbers, so it goes to you untouched — see decision 9. Worth noting `--plugin-dir` loads every `skills/*/SKILL.md`, so their measured input includes the bundled skills, not only the voice.
- **#1285** (Antigravity CLI 1.3.5) — **new evidence this run; likely an upstream agy bug already fixed in 1.3.6, and #1289's hypothesis now looks wrong.** The reporter posted `/skills` output showing agy loading all nine caveman skills *from the plugin directory*, so the plugin is installed, enabled and being read — only `rules/AGENTS.md` is not reaching the rule set. Antigravity CLI's own changelog for **1.3.6** reads: "Fixed skills, rules, and Markdown agents failing on **unquoted colons**." The reporter is on 1.3.5, and the staged `rules/AGENTS.md` is a byte-copy of `src/rules/caveman-activate.md`, which carries several two-colon lines (`- One idea per sentence: ASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, …`, `- Tool runs: bounded status: …`). That matches the symptom and explains why 1.2.17 worked. Separately, `contextFileName` appears nowhere in agy's changelog, and **1.4.1** adds a validator warning for an `AGENTS.md` at the plugin **root instead of in `rules/`** — which is where caveman already puts it, so our layout is right. I asked the reporter to try 1.3.6+ and, failing that, `agy plugin validate --strict --json`. Not reproduced here (no `agy` binary) and nothing changed in the installer. This largely answers decision 4.
- **#1246** (opencode plugin on OpenCode v2.x) — unchanged from run 1 and still entirely unfixed on main. Note this is a *different* code path from #1316: that was the generated `caveman-native.js`, this is the repo's own `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`. See decision 1.
- **#1307** (pnpm lockfile blocks plugin dependency install) — accurately diagnosed, cosmetic for the plugin path by the reporter's own analysis; both remedies are a packaging decision. See decision 2.
- **#1258** (VS Code Copilot drops caveman ultra) — not reproducible as filed: no extension version, no caveman version, no install method. Likely the same class as #1318.
- **#1225** (agent-drift: pi 1.3.0) — real, handled by your own #1311. Not duplicated.
- **#1236** (agent-drift: hermes 0.22.2) — still unverifiable from this environment; `releases/latest` returns 403 and PyPI stops at 0.19.0. No new comment; the prior triage comments already say exactly this. See decision 6.
- **#1272 / #1150 / #863 / #1093 / #1020 / #1053 / #1090 / #1278 / #1262 / #1286 / #1279 / #1217 / #1216 / #1240** and the remaining open issues — not investigated this run, and not commented on.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

### Run 5 (2026-10-22)

- **#1346 by @jafin01 — content looks right; blocked on a repo rule I can't resolve, and on #1262 being yours.** It adds one "What NOT to do" bullet telling the cavecrew orchestrator to spot-check absence claims (`No match.`, `No issues.`, "unchanged") and range-check cited line numbers — which is exactly what #1262 asked for, and a previous run already confirmed the gap is real and unaddressed. Two reasons I did not adopt it. (1) #1262 is a **product decision about skill wording**, which this routine triages rather than implements. (2) It edits `plugins/caveman/skills/cavecrew/SKILL.md` as well as the source — and that is not a contributor mistake, it is **forced**: `tests/verify_repo.py` requires the mirror to be byte-identical to the source, while `CLAUDE.md` says never to edit the mirror. So the PR cannot be made rule-compliant and green at the same time. Raised as decision 18. The change itself needs only your yes.

### Run 4 (2026-10-21)

- **#1332 by @AlSh007 — adopted.** Cherry-picked with `-x`. Real honesty-invariant bug, confirmed red for the right reason before the fix. Completed on top because the guard exempted `.eE` literals and the same float64 collision is reachable with decimals; see the fixes note. Credited as co-author. Nothing they could reasonably have caught — their scope was the reported case and it was right.
- **#1343 by @CHLIN0 — adopted.** Cherry-picked with `-x`. Clean diagnosis of a genuine nondeterminism bug, and the test is the right shape: it asserts the canonical location on each of 32 attempts rather than diffing two outputs that could happen to share a map order. I verified the single-file scope rather than assuming it (see the fixes note) and found nothing missing.
- **#1338 by @estebanmunchjones2019 — recommend merge as-is, not adopted here.** Accurate on every point I checked against the code, fills a real gap, and reads well. Docs-only, so it is better merged standalone with their credit than cherry-picked into a fix PR. One optional improvement if you want it: it says Codex API-key mode uses `providers.openai`, which is right, but `openai-codex` is a separate upstream in `ProviderUpstreams` — a reader on ChatGPT-auth Codex might over-apply the advice.
- **#1306 by @ysntony — unchanged from run 3: sound, with one test inconsistency.** Still not adopted, still did not fit the fix budget. The specific flaw is still there: `TestPoolMoonshotK3TargetSendsFittedChatRequest` hand-builds a target URL with no `/v1` and asserts against it, so it passes while exercising a path the real pool never produces.
- **#1341, #1321, #1311, #1312 (yours), #1340, #1339, #1313, #1314 (dependabot), #1329 (draft), #1319, #1267, #1288, #1273, #1036, #1220, #1308, #1289, #1243, #1269, #1290, #1317, #1325, #1330, #1331** — not reviewed this run. Runs 1–3 verdicts on the last ten of those still stand.

- **#1330 by @AlSh007 — adopted (run 3).** Cherry-picked with `-x`. A genuinely good catch: the deletion was load-bearing-looking (`# Clean up backup file left by installer`) and had been there long enough to read as intentional. Their shape is right — track whether *this run* made the file, and keep even their own `.bak` when it is the only copy of comments the rewrite dropped. Tests cover both surfaces. Completed on top: the sibling audit of `installer/install.js --uninstall` (not affected), and the four `.ps1` commits above, three of which were the Windows 5.1 hunt. Nothing they could reasonably have caught.
- **#1331 by @AlSh007 — adopted (run 3).** Cherry-picked with `-x`. Small, correct, and the test is the good kind: it asserts the `input_schema` profile equals the `inputSchema` profile rather than hardcoding an expectation, so it cannot drift from the baseline it is pinning. Confirmed red before the fix for the right reason (empty `Params`/`Required`). I checked the other two implementations of the same lookup rather than taking the single-file scope on trust; both are already correct, for different reasons. Noted in the fixes section.
- **#1325 by @szsunyuan — adopted (run 3).** Cherry-picked with `-x`. Fixes #1324 at the routing layer rather than special-casing DeepSeek: the `/v1`-then-bare loop covers Z.ai's `/paas/v4` base in the same change, and the test asserts both. Verified all three new cases red before the fix (2 in the CLI suite, 1 in the pi-extension suite) and the full 1437-test CLI suite plus the 145-test pi-extension suite green after. The negative case they kept — a mount that would put `/v1` back on the way out still returns `undefined` — is what makes this a widening rather than a loosening.
- **#1306 by @ysntony — reviewed, not adopted; sound, with one test inconsistency.** I checked its central provider claim against Kimi's own API docs rather than trusting it: K3 does accept exactly `low | high | max`, reasoning is always on with no off switch, and `max_completion_tokens` is the documented cap field. So the `kimi` dialect, the none/minimal→`low` collapse and the `max_tokens_field` switch are right, and unmapped efforts emitting nothing is correctly fail-closed. The flaw: `providers.json` sets `"path": "/v1/chat/completions"` and `pool_test.go` asserts that URL, but `TestPoolMoonshotK3TargetSendsFittedChatRequest` hand-builds `URL: ".../chat/completions"` with no `/v1` and asserts `last("/chat/completions")` — a target constructed in the test rather than derived from the provider entry, so it passes while exercising a path the real pool never produces. Left for you; it did not fit this run's fix budget.
- **#1329 by @ysntony** (draft, Moonshot Responses routing) — not reviewed this run. **#1319 by @1TRUDEV** has one new commit since run 2, but it is a merge of `main` into their branch (`0cafd44`), not a change to the proposed text; run 2's four blockers below all still stand.
- **#1317 by @tranducquy0 — adopted.** Cherry-picked with `-x` so their commit and authorship stand as written. Clean PR: it traces `getAgentDir`/`getSessionsDir` through `expandTildePath` rather than guessing the precedence, keeps `CAVEMAN_PI_ROOT` on top, and ships tests for all three cases. Verified their tests are meaningful (they do not compile against main). One gap filled in a follow-up commit credited to them: every relocation test builds `piSessionSource` directly, but `learnSessionSources()` is the only construction the real scanner performs — restoring that one line left their whole suite green with the bug back. Checked the sibling too: `piRoot()` had exactly one caller, which their change replaces.
- **#1319 by @1TRUDEV — needs changes.** The problem in #1318 is real, but four things block this shape. (1) It overrides the auto-clarity rule: `skills/ultracave/SKILL.md:59` deliberately drops to plain prose for security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, ambiguous fragments and questions to the user, and this text lands *after* the skill body, so "Output exclusively code, technical facts, or single-line bullet points" is the last thing the model reads. CLAUDE.md calls that carve-out load-bearing. (2) Wrong layer — behaviour belongs in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and the three skills map 1:1 to the stored modes. (3) No `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` regeneration, so `tests/verify_repo.py` fails the build as filed. (4) No test, and the constant says `ULTRA_CAVE` while also applying to `megacave`.
- **#1290 by @ketpatil77 — adopted (run 1).** Cherry-picked, then completed: the diagnostic now distinguishes a non-object root from a parse failure (`[]` *is* valid JSON), and the documented `readSettings` contract covers the new null case. Checked the sibling reader; Claude Code's SessionStart hook parses the same file independently and is unaffected.
- **#1269 by @tejgokani — needs changes, core is sound (run 1).** Bounding the hook download fixes a real hang. Two blockers: it makes `installer/install.js` requireable and threads an `_https` test seam through production code (new pattern, your call — decision 3); and the oversized-body branch rejects without unlinking the partial `dest`.
- **#1289 by @ALANDVO — needs changes (run 1), and new evidence this run argues its premise is wrong.** See the #1285 entry above: `contextFileName` is absent from agy's changelog, and 1.4.1 confirms `rules/AGENTS.md` is the expected location. The earlier points stand independently — it changes "every technical fact kept" to "every technical **factor** kept" (copy regression), bundles unrelated rule-body edits across generated files, and adds an unrequested `agy plugin enable`.
- **#1243 by @AlexCawl — maintainer decision, not a code review (run 1).** It relocates the Codex plugin manifest and deletes `.codex/hooks.json` / `.codex/config.toml`, and replaces the mode-resolving sessionstart script with a direct `caveman-activate.js` call — dropping the `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE` / `.caveman.json` / `defaultMode: "off"` resolution that script exists for. Out of bounds here: `plugins/caveman/**` is off-limits to this run.
- **#1321, #1311, #1312 (yours), #1313, #1314 (dependabot), #1267, #1288, #1273, #1036, #1220, #1308** — not reviewed.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **#1246 — accept the offered OpenCode v2 port, and pick where per-turn reinforcement lives.** `experimental.chat.system.transform` is gone in v2; the options are the `context` hook or documented AGENTS.md injection. Also needs a call on v1 compatibility: v2 wants an object with `id`, v1 wants a function. Right now v2 installs fail to load rather than degrade. Note #1316's fix does **not** cover this file.
2. **#1307 — which remedy for the pnpm lockfile note:** point the marketplace `source` at a plugin-only subdirectory, or drop the root runtime `dependencies`.
3. **#1269 — is `installer/install.js` allowed to become a requireable module?** The only blocking question on an otherwise sound security PR.
4. **#1289 / #1285 — largely answered this run, and probably needs no caveman change.** `contextFileName` is not in agy's changelog at all, and 1.4.1 confirms `rules/AGENTS.md` is the expected location, so #1289's premise looks wrong. The live hypothesis is now agy 1.3.5's unquoted-colon bug, fixed upstream in 1.3.6. Awaiting the reporter's upgrade result. If you want caveman to be robust against it regardless, the change would be to the rule body's two double-colon lines — but that is a voice edit to `src/rules/`, so it is your call, not mine.
5. **#1305 — should `ensureDeviceId()` become eager?** It already writes a durable per-install random id into `cloud.json`, but only on entitlement flows, which is the actual root cause. Eager at install needs no new identity store and no dependence on the revocable telemetry id. Plus the install-id discontinuity above, in case the dashboard needs a backfill.
6. **#1236 — the hermes probe cannot be run from this environment at all** (403, four runs running). Either the drift lane needs a reachable install path, or this agent's drift reports should say they are unverifiable from CI rather than reopening each release.
7. **DCO — enforce it or correct the doc.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires sign-offs that main's own recent commits don't carry. I won't make that certification on anyone's behalf, so sign-offs here would need to come from you.
8. **Pi under `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`: does Pi read `<agent dir>/extensions`?** `caveman enable pi` writes to `~/.pi/agent/extensions` unconditionally, so on a relocated install the persistent door silently does nothing — `buildPiWrapArgs` already withholds the owned copy whenever that var is set, which is the repo's own belief that Pi stops reading there. I wrote the fix and its two failing tests, confirmed them red, and then dropped both: I could not verify the extensions path from a primary source, and the current behaviour at least degrades to the session copy. One confirmation turns this into a two-line change.
9. **#1323 — how to answer an independent measurement that finds no net saving.** Their method looks sound and their setup is the one we document. The honest reply probably involves the `evals/` three-arm harness rather than the benchmark table, and possibly a note in INSTALL.md that `--plugin-dir` loads every bundled skill. I changed no number and made no claim on your behalf.
10. **Should the middleware range widening carry a CHANGELOG entry?** `packages/middleware/typescript/CHANGELOG.md` has a 1.0.1 entry for the 0.129–0.131 widening, but 0.132 and 0.133 were added later with none, and the package is still at 1.0.1. I left it alone rather than guess the release convention.
11. **#1326 — litellm 1.106.0 needs `mcp` installed and does not depend on it. Which remedy?** Three options, and the choice is a packaging-policy one `pyproject.toml` already has a standing comment about. (a) Add `mcp>=2.0,<3` to the `litellm` extra, so `pip install caveman-middleware[litellm]` yields a working litellm — satisfiable alongside the strands/crewai `mcp<2.2` ceiling, but it takes on a dependency no caveman code imports. (b) Leave the package alone, add `mcp` to the litellm CI lane so the canary stops failing — honest about whose bug it is, but it masks a break real users will hit. (c) Leave both and report upstream. I did not pick one, and I deliberately did not narrow the COMPATIBILITY range, which would turn compression off on a litellm that is fine once `mcp` is present.
12. **#1327 / #1328 — the agent pins need a verification this environment cannot perform.** `claude@2.1.303` is launchable (probe run, `version_ok`/`help_ok` true), but `claude.json`'s `verified_by` asserts an observed `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` route probe that I could not get a single request out of in three attempts. Either someone with a working headless `claude -p` runs it and the pin moves with its claim intact, or the drift lane needs a probe whose claim matches what CI can actually check. Separately, `openclaw.json`'s `verified_by` cites a `config_overlay.local` the profile no longer has.
13. **The `.ps1` surface has no honest test signal below Windows CI, and this run cost four commits proving it.** Every `.ps1` case *skips* where pwsh is absent, so a green POSIX run says nothing about them — and installing pwsh is not enough either, because Linux pwsh is 7.x and the bug that bit us is specific to Windows PowerShell 5.1 (native stderr as terminating error records under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`). Options: run the `.ps1` cases in the `windows` lane earlier/faster so the feedback loop is not 7 minutes per guess; add a 5.1-semantics lint for native calls inside a `Stop` scope; or accept it and write `.ps1` defensively by rule. `verify_repo.py`'s greps now guard two specific instances of this, which is not the same as a signal.

14. **~~The `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gate needs a keep-up mechanism, not another manual widening.~~ — RESOLVED by run 5, structurally rather than by policy.** Upstream closed the 0.x line (1.0.0 on 2026-10-21), so the bound is now a next-*major* bound like every sibling in the table and there is no next-minor left to go stale. The treadmill described below was a property of gating a zero-major dependency per minor; it ends with the line. The underlying policy question — whether the canary should widen-and-PR on a green suite — is still worth answering for the *next* zero-major framework, but nothing is pending on `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. Original text follows.

14b. **The `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gate needs a keep-up mechanism, not another manual widening.** This is the second run in a row to move the same bound, and it went stale inside two days while the PR carrying the previous widening sat open. It is a zero-major dependency that ships a minor every few days, and the rule ("the next untested minor is refused") means every release is a fail-open no-compression event for anyone on it until someone runs the suite. The suite passes unmodified each time, which is the real signal. Options: let the nightly canary widen-and-PR automatically when the suite passes against the new release; relax the zero-major rule to trust patch/minor within a tested major and keep the explicit gate for majors only; or accept the treadmill and merge these PRs faster. I widened it again rather than change the policy, because the policy is yours.
15. **#1337's second half: should the wrap 401 path carry a hint?** The docs PR (#1338) fixes the discoverability gap. The reporter also suggests detecting the actual misconfiguration — resolved upstream is `api.openai.com` while the key is not an OpenAI key or the agent's `model.base_url` is non-default — and saying so instead of relaying a bare `HTTP 401: Incorrect API key provided`. That is a genuinely good error-message improvement and a feature request, so I triaged it rather than building it.
16. **The agent-drift lane is verifiable from CI after all — worth deciding whether to make it so.** Run 3 concluded the `claude` route probe could not be performed here and escalated it; it can, and four of the other five went the same way on the first attempt. Which means these issues can be cleared automatically rather than accumulating: the probes are a stub HTTP recorder plus the profile's own overlay, and every claim in all five `verified_by` texts is machine-checkable. Two caveats if you want that: `openclaw` needs its own Node (≥24.16, and it refuses 22 outright), and two probes still render the overlay by hand rather than through `buildWrapEnv`, so the base-config merge stays unexercised either way.

17. **#1225 — Pi 1.4.0 removed the oracle that keeps `src/provider-compat.ts` honest. What replaces it?** Detail in "Triaged, not fixed" above. The short version: caveman hand-copies Pi's provider-attribution rules in production to warn when the compat mount would drop them, and the private host helper the test compared that copy against is gone in 1.4.0 — attribution moved into pi-ai behind `ClientIdentity`. Three ways out, all yours: re-express the oracle against `getClientIdentity`/pi-ai's `identity?` path; drop the oracle and pin the expectations by hand (cheaper, loses the property that caught drift); or ask upstream for a supported export. Until one is chosen the pi pin cannot move with its claim intact, so #1225 stays open and #1311 stays stale. Worth noting the general shape: a drift report that says "it launches" can hide an upstream API removal that only a non-obvious test reaches.
18. **`CLAUDE.md` and `tests/verify_repo.py` disagree about the `plugins/caveman/` mirrors, and it blocks contributors.** `verify_repo.py` (lines ~231–252) asserts byte equality between `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and its `plugins/caveman/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` mirror; `CLAUDE.md` says "Never edit synced copies under `plugins/caveman/skills/`". `sync-skill.yml` only runs on push to `main`, so a PR that edits just the source fails the check, and a PR that edits both violates the documented rule — which is exactly the position #1346 is in. Either have `verify_repo.py` skip the mirror check when only the source changed, or amend `CLAUDE.md` to say "edit both in a PR; CI keeps them in sync after merge". I did not change either, since both are yours.
19. **Decision 10 is still open and the 1.0.1 CHANGELOG entry is now visibly behind.** `packages/middleware/typescript/CHANGELOG.md` documents the 0.129–0.131 widening under 1.0.1 and nothing since, while this branch has moved that gate three times and has now crossed a major. There is no `Unreleased` heading and neither run 2 nor run 4 added one, so I followed the branch's practice and added nothing — but whatever ships this branch needs one entry covering all of it, and the Python CHANGELOG needs its first gate entry too.

### Minor, no action taken

The CLI runtime suite leaves `packages/cli/{backups/,policy-limits.json,policy-limits.json.stamp.json,remote-settings.json,remote-settings.json.synced-at}` behind, untracked and not gitignored. I deleted them rather than commit them; worth a `.gitignore` line or a temp dir in the suite so they cannot be committed by accident.

title: opencode profile probes only `opencode` — official `opencode2` bin (V2) is missed, so V2 users still get the V1 native plugin
body:
## Summary

The native plugin generator is correctly major-gated since #1087/#1089, but the gate can never see OpenCode 2 on hosts that run it via the official `opencode2` bin. `agents/agents.json` lists `binary_names: ["opencode"]` only, and `binOf()` returns the first `which()` hit. Any leftover `opencode` 1.x earlier on PATH wins, `opencodePluginMajor()` returns 1, and `caveman enable opencode` / `caveman doctor opencode --fix` write the V1 `export const CavemanNative` file — which the OpenCode 2 server then rejects with `PluginModule.LoadError: ... Missing key at ["default"]`.

Verified against `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1 (npm dist) and `main`: zero occurrences of `opencode2`.

## Repro (Linux x64)

- `@opencode/cli@2.0.26` publishes both bins: `{ "opencode": "./bin/opencode.exe", "opencode2": "./bin/opencode.exe" }` (bun global install).
- This host: `which opencode` -> a mise install of 1.19.3; `opencode2 --version` -> `opencode v2.0.26`.
- `caveman doctor opencode` reports `"version": "1.19.3"`, so `opencodeNativePluginSource()` emits V1 and OpenCode 2 logs:
  `failed to load plugin target=~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman-native.js cause="PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at [\"default\"]))"`
- Workaround that proves the fix path: with a PATH shim where `opencode` resolves to the 2.0.26 binary, `caveman doctor opencode --fix` emits the V2 `caveman-native.js` (`export default { id: "caveman-native", async setup(ctx) ... }`), which loads and runs cleanly on 2.0.26.

## Suggestion

- Add `opencode2` to the opencode profile's `binary_names`, and when several candidates exist prefer the one whose `--version` parses as major >= 2 (fall back to the current first-found behavior).
- This affects both the native probe and the `caveman run opencode` target, so "prefer highest major" may be safer than simply reordering.

Related: #1246 covers the repo's own `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` port. This report is only about host detection for the generated `caveman-native.js`.

title: fix(learn): honor Pi's PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR
body:
Follow-up to the #1309 Pi learn adoption (per the review comment): Pi honours
`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, but the Go learn
scanner only read `CAVEMAN_PI_ROOT/agent/sessions`, so it reported zero sessions
for anyone who relocated Pi.

- `piRoots()` resolves the sessions dir: `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` (outright
  override), then `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (`<agent dir>/sessions`), both
  tilde-expanded via a new `expandTilde` mirroring Pi's `expandTildePath`;
  `CAVEMAN_PI_ROOT` keeps top precedence, like the sibling roots.
- `piSessionSource` carries the resolved `sessionsDir`; the default layout and
  existing `rel_path` values are unchanged.
- `docs/technical/learn.md` reads table documents both variables.
- Tests: `TestPiRootsHonorRelocationVariables`, `TestExpandTildeMirrorsPi`,
  `TestPiSessionSourceHonorsRelocatedSessionsDirs`; `TestMain` unsets the two Pi
  vars for isolation.

Verified: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/store/`, `go test ./internal/store/`
all pass.

title: Ultracave ignored on Opus 5.5 despite #929, hooks fire every turn
body:
**What happens:** Caveman (ultracave) is active and the SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks inject the banner every turn. Replies are still full prose from the first response on, in every session. A custom `outputStyle` set to ultracave didn't help either.

**Env:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), macOS, caveman `81958ad`.

**Expected:** Ultracave output from the first reply to the last, per #852.

**Repro:** Install caveman with ultracave as the default, start a session, ask any multi-part question.

title: fix(hooks): enforce strict persona override for ultracave mode (#575)
body:
Problem:
In ultracave and megacave modes, competing system instructions, user settings, or CLAUDE.md files would occasionally override the persona, causing Claude to revert back to verbose conversational prose.

Fix:

Added a STRICT_OVERRIDE system directive constant inside src/hooks/caveman-activate.js.

Dynamically appended the strict enforcement override to the ruleset whenever ultracave or megacave is active, locking down the response constraints against conflicting system prompts.

title: fix(engine): compress Codex code-mode command output inside its JSON line
body:
Codex 0.161 in code mode returns each `exec_command` result as one JSON line (`{"chunk_id":…,"exit_code":0,…,"output":"…"}`) after a few header lines. The whole tool result then reads as text with one long line, and the proxy logged `nothing_compressible` on every Codex tool turn.

The engine now unwraps the largest `output` string of such a line (next to the file and listing wrappers in `unwrapInput`), compresses the real lines, and writes the JSON string back byte-valid. `caveman_retrieve` still returns the original segment. A line that Codex cut in the middle still qualifies when its string decodes. Anything else passes through unchanged.

title: fix(pi): verify the compat route for an OpenAI base without /v1
body:
Fixes #1324

## What happens today

Pi's built-in `deepseek` provider sends to `https://api.deepseek.com`, with no `/v1` (pi-ai 0.99.2 through 1.3.0). With the proxy running, the Pi extension says:

```text
Caveman: pass-through for deepseek/deepseek-flash (no compat mount named "deepseek" in the local proxy; add compat.deepseek.base_url to caveman.yaml to route it); no compression
```

After the user adds that mount and restarts the proxy, it says:

```text
Caveman: pass-through for deepseek/deepseek-flash (provider endpoint path or API "deepseek/openai-completions" is not verified by the running proxy); no compression
```

## Why

For the OpenAI family, `verifiedProviderRoute` only tried the `/v1` compat route. The URL the proxy would forward on that route always has `/v1` before `/chat/completions`, and Pi's DeepSeek URL has none, so no `compat.deepseek.base_url` value can ever verify. The same is true of every OpenAI-family base that doesn't end in `/v1`, including Pi's built-in `zai` and `zai-coding-cn` (`.../api/coding/paas/v4`).

## Fix

A named mount is a subtree route. The proxy joins whatever follows `/compat/{name}` onto the mount's base (`joinCompatPath`, which `compatTarget` mirrors), and the OpenAI grammar picks chat or responses from the endpoint. So `/compat/deepseek/chat/completions` already forwards to `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions` and is compressed. No proxy change is needed.

The proof now tries `/v1` first, then no suffix:

- **Same test as before:** the route must match the URL the host SDK would request, exactly.
- **Existing routes unchanged:** every route that verified before keeps its `/v1` path.
- **Still refused:** a mount that would add `/v1` to an unversioned base.
- **OpenClaw:** it shares this proof, and the compat and header checks it runs afterwards are unchanged.

After this lands, the reporter's setup works with:

```yaml
compat:
  deepseek:
    base_url: https://api.deepseek.com
```

## Tests

- `packages/cli/tests/provider-routing.runtime.mjs`:
  - DeepSeek and Z.ai bases route to `/compat/{provider}` for both chat and responses.
  - A `/v1` mount on an unversioned base stays unverified.
- `packages/pi-extension/tests/provider.runtime.mjs`:
  - Selecting `deepseek/deepseek-flash` with the mount routes to `/w/pi/compat/deepseek` with no notice.
  - Closing the gate restores the model's own endpoint.
- Both new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. The Pi test fails on `main` with the exact notice from the issue.
- Run locally on Node 24.16.0:
  - CLI routing, OpenClaw and OpenCode suites: 112/112 pass.
  - `@caveman-ai/pi` `npm test`, including the real-Pi integration test: 145/145 pass.
  - Full CLI suite (`tests/*.runtime.mjs`): 1410 pass, 23 skipped, 1 fail. The failure is `onboard-setup.runtime.mjs`, "under npx … setup without npm writes nothing". It fails the same way on unmodified `main` here: this machine has a system npm at `/usr/bin/npm`, which is on the fixture's `PATH` (`{bin}:/usr/bin:/bin`). It's unrelated to this change.
- Go: not run, since there's no toolchain on this machine; this PR changes no Go code.

title: fix(hooks): uninstall no longer deletes a settings.json.bak it did not make
body:
## What

`src/hooks/uninstall.sh` and `uninstall.ps1` delete `settings.json.bak` unconditionally ("backup file left by installer"). But both scripts only create the backup when none exists, and their own comment says an existing one is "the only pre-caveman copy the user has". So an uninstall can destroy:

- a `settings.json.bak` the user made themselves, and
- the only copy of the `//` comments that the settings rewrite drops (`install.sh` tells the user "Comments are preserved in settings.json.bak").

## Reproduction (on main)

`settings.json` has `// my model choice`, `"model":"opus"` and a caveman SessionStart hook. A `settings.json.bak` holding `{"model":"my-own-manual-backup"}` already exists.

```
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> bash src/hooks/uninstall.sh
  Removed: <dir>/settings.json.bak
```

Afterwards `settings.json` is `{"model":"opus"}` and both the user's backup and the comment are gone.

## Fix

Remove the backup only if this run created it and it is plain JSON (nothing is lost). A pre-existing `.bak` stays. So does a backup of a commented file. The PowerShell twin gets the same change.

## Tests

Two new cases in `tests/hooks/standalone-install-safety.test.mjs`, run for both the bash and pwsh surfaces. Both fail on main and pass with the change. `node --test tests/hooks/*.test.mjs`: 136 pass.

Note: `pwsh` isn't available on my machine, so the `.ps1` change and its test cases haven't been run locally. I mirrored the bash logic by hand.

One behaviour change worth a look: the `.bak` that `install` makes (the pre-caveman copy) is now left in place by uninstall instead of being deleted, since the script can't tell it from a user's own backup. `installer/install.js --uninstall` already treats it this way.

title: fix(shrink): read the schema of Anthropic input_schema tools
fix(engine): keep integers above 2^53 off the numeric range track
body:
## What

The elision marker's `range col=lo..hi` is meant to hold for every elided row. For integers above 2^53 it doesn't: `invariantNumber` parses with `strconv.ParseFloat`, so distinct integers that land in the same float64 compare equal, `value > maxVal` never replaces the first one seen, and the marker prints a bound that an elided row exceeds. `keepNumericExtrema` uses the same compare. This hits snowflake IDs and nanosecond timestamps.

## Reproduction (on main)

CSV `id,status` with 30 rows `1234567890123456000+i*100,ok`:

```
… 24 rows elided (caveman): all status=ok; range id=1234567890123456300..1234567890123458500 …
```

The elided rows run to `1234567890123458600`, which is outside the stated range.

## Fix

`invariantNumber` no longer treats an integer literal with magnitude >= 2^53 as a number (decimals and exponent forms are unchanged). The column falls through to the exact-string coverage path, the same route a non-finite value already takes. The same case now prints `id: 25 distinct, 1234567890123456300..1234567890123458700`, which covers every elided row.

## Tests

`TestTabularLargeIntegerRangeCoversEveryElidedRow` fails on main and passes with the change. `go test ./engine/... ./shrink/... ./mcp/...` is clean.

title: docs: Hermes behind a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway needs providers.openai.base_url (otherwise a confusing 401)
body:
**Setup**
Hermes Agent configured with a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway (`model.provider: custom`, `model.base_url: https://gateway.example/litellm`). The existing docs show `providers.anthropic` style overrides for Claude Code only.

**What happens**
`caveman wrap hermes chat -q hi` with only `providers.anthropic.base_url` set in caveman.yaml:
- Hermes traffic uses the OpenAI wire, so the proxy forwards it to the default `https://api.openai.com`.
- The gateway key is sent to api.openai.com and the user sees `HTTP 401: Incorrect API key provided ... platform.openai.com/account/api-keys`, which looks like a bad key rather than a routing/config gap.
- `caveman enable hermes` instead refuses with "sends its requests to its own endpoint ... remove model.base_url there", which doesn't mention that wrap works with a `providers.openai` override.

**Fix that works (verified, wrap + proxy `provider_upstreams.openai` + stats request count)**
```yaml
providers:
  anthropic: {base_url: https://gateway.example/litellm}
  openai:    {base_url: https://gateway.example/litellm}
```
(plus `CAVE_SSRF_ALLOWLIST=<gateway host>` if it resolves to a private address, and `OPENAI_API_KEY=<gateway key>` in the wrap env.)

**Docs gap**
docs/technical/configuration.md "Provider overrides" lists only bedrock/azure_openai/compat examples, and docs/technical/agent-wrapping.md lists Hermes as "OpenAI Chat Completions" without saying which `providers.*` key applies. Suggest: a short "Self-hosted gateway for Hermes / Codex / Aider" example showing `providers.openai.base_url`, and a hint in the wrap 401 path when the resolved upstream is api.openai.com but the key isn't an OpenAI key / `model.base_url` is non-default.

Environment: caveman bin-v4.0.1, Hermes Agent v0.22.2, Linux.

title: docs(config): document providers.openai.base_url for OpenAI-wire agents behind a gateway
body:

Adds a short section to docs/technical/configuration.md explaining that OpenAI-wire agents (Hermes, Codex API-key, Aider) use `providers.openai.base_url`, that omitting it forwards a gateway key to api.openai.com (HTTP 401), and the related `CAVE_SSRF_ALLOWLIST` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `caveman enable hermes` caveats.

body:
Updates the requirements on [pluggy](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy) and [anthropic](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python) to permit the latest version. Updates `pluggy` from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0
Changelog

Sourced from pluggy's changelog.

pluggy 1.7.0 (2026-10-14)

Deprecations and Removals

  • [#632](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632>_: Hookspec methods defined without self as the first parameter now emit a :class:DeprecationWarning. Add self as the first parameter or use @staticmethod.

Features

  • [#170](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170>_: Hookspecs can now declare default values for arguments, using the usual def myhook(myarg="default") syntax. This is mainly a backward compatibility feature, to allow a hookspec to add new parameters to an existing hook without breaking existing callers. See :ref:hookspec_arg_default for details.

  • [#729](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729>_: Tracing now adds detail where str() is ambiguous: empty strings and strings containing whitespace are quoted, and enums and paths show their repr().

    A value spanning several lines is now displayed as a block instead of running into the surrounding trace.

Bug Fixes

  • [#629](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629>_: Fix hooks failing to register on Python 3.14+ when type annotations use forward references.

  • [#315](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315>_: Source archives created by git archive (including GitHub's "Source code" downloads) now carry version information, so building pluggy from them no longer fails with a missing version.

  • [#442](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442>_: With the addition of default values for hookspec arguments, we also changed the precedence of default values for hookimpl arguments. Previously, if a hookimpl function declared a default for an argument, it was always used, even if the hook call passed an explicit value. Now the precedence is changed to: hook call passed value > hookspec default value > hookimpl default value. See :ref:hookimpl_arg_defaults.

  • [#701](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701>_: Hookimpls and hookspecs are now discovered via :func:inspect.getattr_static, so properties, cached_property and other descriptors are no longer executed while scanning a plugin. Hooks declared through such a descriptor are not supported.

    As a side effect, @hookimpl/@hookspec applied above @classmethod or @staticmethod is now picked up; previously the marker sat on the wrapper where getattr() never saw it. Callables stored directly on a plugin instance -- in its __dict__ or in a __slots__ slot -- keep being called exactly as getattr() returned them, i.e. without an implicit self.

title: fix(proxy): relay Claude OAuth token refresh
body:
## Problem

Claude Code signed in with a Claude Platform profile (`user_oauth` in `~/.config/anthropic/configs/<profile>.json`) refreshes its access token at `{ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL}/v1/oauth/token`. Under `caveman wrap`, that URL is `/w/claude/v1/oauth/token` on the local proxy. The proxy rejects any path it doesn't know, so once the token expired every session failed with:

```
API Error: User OAuth refresh failed (HTTP 404): {"error":{"type":"cave_gateway_error","code":"cave_route_not_found","message":"Proxy path is not recognized."}}
```

## Fix

- The `anthropic` adapter now declares `POST /v1/oauth/token` and `/anthropic/v1/oauth/token` in a new `Base.OAuthTokenRoutes` allowlist. Matching is exact and POST only.
- The gateway relays the grant and the provider's answer byte-for-byte. The check runs after the authenticator, like the `/v1/models` route.
  - It attaches no provider credential: the grant carries its own refresh token or assertion, so the operator's key never goes along.
  - Neither body is logged.
  - It writes no spend row.
  - Provider errors such as `invalid_grant` pass through unchanged. Claude Code reads that body to clear a dead refresh token.
- `anthropic-workspace-id` is now forwarded. Claude Code sends it on every request in this mode; a user OAuth token is scoped to the org, so dropping the header ran calls against a workspace the user didn't pick.

## Proof

- `go test ./...` in `proxy/` passes (27 packages).
- New tests in `oauth_token_route_test.go`:
  - The grant is relayed on `/w/claude`, bare and `/anthropic` paths.
  - No credential goes upstream and no spend row is written.
  - A 400 rejection comes back unchanged.
  - Requests that should not match still don't: GET, subtree, prefix collision, encoded separator, other oauth paths. The authenticator still runs before route matching. Oversized bodies get 413.
- With the route declaration removed, the relay test fails with the exact `cave_route_not_found` body from the report.

title: fix(json): stabilize elision note placement
body:
# Fix JSON elision note placement determinism

JSON payloads with multiple large repetitive arrays could place `__caveman_note__` in different sibling arrays on repeated compression of identical bytes. Object traversal used Go map iteration while the first elision shared a payload-wide flag, so sorting keys only during final JSON encoding did not stabilize the note location.

Sort object keys before recursive transformation and document canonical lexicographic traversal. Array order and the existing note eligibility rules remain unchanged. Regression coverage checks the exact note location for single arrays, reversed-order siblings, nested objects, and protected error subtrees, together with byte stability, empty-query equivalence, and idempotence.

Validation (Go 1.26.9, CGO_ENABLED=0):

- The new canonical-location regression fails on the original implementation and passes with the fix.
- Compressor, context-window, safety, and CCR package suites pass, along with focused Engine compression/recovery/Simulate tests.
- `go vet ./engine/compressors ./engine`, `gofmt`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- A synthetic two-array fixture produces one output variant across 512 direct and 256 Engine calls after the fix (two variants before). All 256 Engine recovery checks return the exact original bytes. These are bounded local checks, not provider-cache, cost, quality, or performance measurements.

Full repository and CGO/release-shape suites were not run.

title: fix(installer): fall back to Bun when Node is absent
body:
## Summary

Addresses #570, following the automatic fallback approach requested in https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/656#issuecomment-6014034026.

- Keep Node first in both shell shims. Use Bun only when Node is absent, preserving the release pin, arguments and exit status. Existing Node version checks and npm 12 handling stay intact.
- Use one shared package runner for both nested skill-install paths. Bun invokes `x --bun` with its own executable, so Node shebangs do not require a missing Node or a separate `bunx` binary.
- Keep the runtime boundary explicit: skip automatic Node hooks under Bun, reject explicit Node-only hook/MCP/Claude-plugin requests before changes, and do not launch the Node-only CLI during first run or uninstall. Incomplete native-routing cleanup still reports failure.
- Add focused runtime/argument/error-path regressions and document experimental installer support.

## Validation

- Full installer/hooks suite: 650 passed, 22 skipped, zero failures (`node --test --test-force-exit --test-concurrency=2 tests/installer/*.test.mjs tests/hooks/*.test.mjs`, with isolated HOME and `CAVEMAN_TEST_BUN` set). One earlier run hit the existing MCP final-response timing test; its isolated rerun and the complete rerun both passed.
- Linux, Node 24.19.0 and official Bun 1.4.3: 22 focused Bun tests passed, including four actual-Bun smoke tests with Node absent from PATH. These cover native skill installation, nested skills dry-run, a real Node-shebang skills fixture forced through Bun, and the local shell shim.
- Python: 251 tests passed; `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` passed.
- `bash -n`, JS syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two new shell fallback regressions fail against the unmodified base with the original Node-required error.

PowerShell contracts run under both available PowerShell editions but were skipped locally because neither is installed. They cover shim control flow and argument construction, not native Windows `bun.exe` quoting. Networked GitHub package bootstrap and native Windows Bun execution were not exercised locally.

AI-assisted implementation, with a separate review that caught and fixed unsupported-Claude skip accounting masking failed installs. No dependency, generated-hook, or release changes.

title: fix(proxy): keep the percent-encoded slash of a Bedrock ARN model id upstream
body:
## What

`bedrock.Adapter.ResolveUpstreamURL` builds the upstream path from `req.URL.Path`, which is the decoded path, and never sets `RawPath`. A model id that is an ARN with a `/` in it (inference profiles, provisioned and custom models, which the allowlist accepts on purpose) arrives with that slash percent-encoded, because it is part of one path segment. Upstream it becomes a literal separator, so the path gains a segment and no longer has the `/model/{modelId}/{action}` shape.

## Reproduction (on main)

```
POST /bedrock/model/arn%3Aaws%3Abedrock%3Aus-east-1%3A123456789012%3Aapplication-inference-profile%2Fabc123/converse
-> https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:application-inference-profile/abc123/converse
```

`%2F` is gone. `parseModelPath` and the allowlist already treat the ARN as one id, and the SigV4 signer builds its canonical URI from `EscapedPath()`, so the resolver was the one place that dropped the encoding.

## Fix

Also join the escaped paths into `RawPath` for the runtime endpoint. Go uses `RawPath` only when it decodes to `Path`, which it does here. Non-ARN model ids resolve exactly as before.

## Tests

`TestResolveUpstreamURLKeepsEncodedSlashInARN` fails on main and passes with the change. `go test ./providers/... ./shared/platform/awssig` is clean.

Note: I haven't called AWS. That an unencoded ARN slash is rejected there is inferred from the route shape and from how the AWS SDKs encode this path parameter. The path change itself is verified.

I left `vertex` and `Base.ResolveUpstreamURL` alone: they have the same join but I have no case where their paths carry an encoded slash.

title: fix(claude): separate plugin payload from installer dependencies
body:
## Problem

Claude’s marketplace currently installs the repository root, which also
contains the npm installer’s package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml. Claude Code
therefore reports that the declared dependencies were not installed because
the lockfile is unsupported.

The plugin hooks use Node built-in modules and bundled sibling files.
The root @caveman-ai/cli dependency belongs to the installer, including its
native-integration cleanup path.

This PR implements the plugin-only-directory option proposed in #1307,
while retaining the installer dependency.

Refs #1307
Related: packaging decision 2 and mirror-maintenance decision 18 in #1315.

## Changes

- Point the Claude marketplace source at ./plugins/claude.
- Generate that payload from canonical repository sources using
  scripts/build-claude-plugin.mjs.
- Preserve all 22 canonical skills, the caveman-init command, three cavecrew
  agents, the plugin manifest, hooks, supporting scripts, and license notices.
- Exclude the root installer package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml from the plugin.
- Exclude plugins/claude from the npm installer tarball.
- Add a dedicated plugin README and adapt specific human-documentation links
  whose repository-relative targets are outside the standalone payload.
- Add generated-payload verification, release-version parity checks, and
  synchronization-workflow integration.
- Document how contributors regenerate and include the payload in their PRs.

Skill instructions and runtime files remain byte-identical to their canonical
sources. Documentation transformations are limited to the dedicated README
and explicitly mapped human-documentation links.

The existing plugins/caveman distribution remains separate. Repointing Claude
there without completing it would omit existing skills and hook files.

## Why the diff is large

Of the 88 changed files, 78 are generated distribution files. Most added lines
are existing canonical content copied into the standalone Claude payload.

Suggested review order:

1. Marketplace source and npm package exclusion.
2. scripts/build-claude-plugin.mjs.
3. Packaging tests and tests/verify_repo.py.
4. Synchronization workflow and contributor documentation.
5. Generated output, checked against its canonical sources.

## Generation and regression protection

The generator selects tracked canonical inputs and provides a read-only
--check mode that detects missing, modified, or unexpected payload files.

Regression coverage includes:

- Excluding installer dependencies and unsupported root lockfiles.
- Preserving the skill inventory and required plugin components.
- Detecting drift without modifying output.
- Repairing missing, changed, and obsolete files.
- Avoiding rewrites of unchanged files.
- Including newly staged skills and removing deleted skills.
- Handling a directory replaced by a file.
- Adapting documentation links without changing skill instructions.

The generator also rejects symlink inputs/output entries and preserves
executable permissions.

## Installation verification

Manual experiments ran on macOS with Node.js 22.21.1 and Claude Code 2.1.306,
using isolated HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR directories.

A direct local-folder install did not expose the warning, so it was not used
as proof of the fix.

The original GitHub marketplace installation reproduced the
dependencies-refused warning. A Git-backed control using the original
repository layout reproduced it as well.

For the candidate and final implementation, temporary Git fixtures were
installed through Claude’s marketplace clone path using a test-only Git URL
rewrite. No public fixture repository was required.

The final fixture was exported from the staged tree now committed in this PR.

Results:

- Installation succeeded and the plugin was enabled.
- No dependencies-refused note appeared.
- No readFromFolder override appeared.
- All 78 installed files matched the generated payload.
- The installed root contained neither package.json nor pnpm-lock.yaml.
- claude plugin details discovered 23 skills: the 22 canonical skills plus
  caveman-init.
- It also discovered all three cavecrew agents and all four hook events:
  SessionStart, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, and SessionEnd.

title: caveman-compress: First-pass output is written with model commentary and a second frontmatter block, and validation passes
body:
**Repro.** File with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `updated: 2026-09-30`). Provider reply: `Here is the compressed version of your file, …:` then its own `---` block with `updated: 2026-10-21`, then the compressed body. Result: exit 0, "Validation passed"; the file holds the original frontmatter, the commentary line, a second frontmatter block with the changed date, then the body.

**Cause.** The preamble guard (output must start with the original's first line) runs on the fix path only. The verbatim frontmatter is prepended to whatever the model returned. On the fix path, the model receives the whole file, frontmatter included, and its rewrite is kept as is.

**Suggested fix.** Apply the same guards to the first pass and the fix pass: strip or reject leading text before the first heading or `---`; reject a reply that contains a frontmatter block; send and accept the body only on both paths.

Related: #588 (closed) fixed the preamble leak on the fix-retry path; the first pass still has no guard.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: Validation checks structure only: a changed number passes, and a prose-only file passes anything shorter
body:
**Repro.** `- retry … at most 3 attempts` compressed to `- retry … max 5 attempts`, every heading, URL, path and inline code span kept: exit 0, "Validation passed". A todo list with no headings, code, URLs or paths passes any shorter reply. A column-0 `<!-- … -->` comment is not masked (`mask_code_blocks` returns it unchanged with no blocks), and deleting it, or joining two bullets of one section, passes `validate.py`.

**Cause.** README's "What Is Preserved" promises numbers, dates, versions and terms are never touched; nothing checks them. HTML comments are neither masked nor counted; bullet loss is a warning that is never shown.

**Suggested fix.** Mask HTML comments like `nocompress` regions; count numbers/dates/versions and per-section bullets as errors; show warnings in the CLI output.

Also: `should_compress()` (`scripts/detect.py`) compresses generated files. Return False when line 1 contains `generated by` (case-insensitive); the generator overwrites the result anyway.

Related: #112 and #776 (closed) were earlier "Validation passed" gaps; these cases still pass on v4.0.1.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: Backup key collides across projects, and the abort's remedy deletes another file's original
body:
**Repro.** Compress `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, then `/some/repo/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Both map to `backups/.claude/CLAUDE.original.md`; the second aborts with "Please remove or rename the backup file if you want to proceed." Following that deletes the first file's only uncompressed original. Separately: after a successful run, a second run aborts the same way; removing the backup and re-running stores the compressed text as the new "original".

**Cause.** `backup_dir_for` keys on `filepath.parent.name`, the file on `stem + ".original.md"`. README's "edit `.original.md` there, then run skill again to re-compress" cannot work: the live file aborts on the existing backup and `.original.md` targets are skipped.

**Suggested fix.** Key the backup on the full resolved path (hash or mirrored tree); replace the remove/rename advice with a restore/rotate command that never discards the only original; document a working edit-and-recompress loop.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: A failed fix call leaves the backup and `<name>.caveman-staged`, and every rerun aborts
body:
**Repro.** First reply drops a URL (validation error); the fix call returns a truncated reply (`finish_reason: length`). Run 1 exits 1 ("hit the server's token cap"). Run 2 aborts "Backup file already exists … Aborting to prevent data loss", exit 2. A `CLAUDE.md.caveman-staged` with partial text sits beside the source.

**Cause.** No `try/finally` around the steps after the backup write; cleanup runs only on paths that return False.

**Suggested fix.** Wrap everything after the backup write in `try/finally` that removes the backup (when the source is unchanged) and the staged file.

Related: #544 and #766 (closed) covered interrupted writes; the leftover backup and staged file still block reruns on v4.0.1.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: Punctuation right after a URL or path fails validation
body:
**Repro.** Reply keeps `https://docs.example.com/billing/v2` and `docs/runbook.md` but writes `…/v2,` and `docs/runbook.md.`: "URL mismatch: lost={…/v2}, added={…/v2,}" and "File paths lost: ['docs/runbook.md']" on both attempts, exit 2.

**Cause.** `URL_REGEX = https?://[^\s)`]+` and `PATH_REGEX`'s `[\w\-/\\.]+` include trailing `,` and `.`.

**Suggested fix.** Trim trailing `.,;:!?` from extracted URLs and paths before comparing.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: Credential dotfiles pass the sensitive-name check
body:
**Repro (code read, not run).** `.npmrc` (`//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=…`), `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`: empty `suffix`, not in `SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX`, content sniff falls through to `natural_language`, so the content is sent. Conversely, any path component containing `token`/`secret` (`tokenizer/`, `design-tokens/`) is refused. Extensionless files are read by `detect_file_type` before the sensitivity check, though SKILL.md says "refused before they are read".

**Suggested fix.** Check the sensitive name before detection; test the basename only; never classify a dotfile as natural language by sniffing; add common credential dotfiles to the list.

Related: #858 (closed) added a directory name to `is_sensitive_path()`; dotfile credentials are still sent.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: caveman-compress: Messages and docs disagree with the code (retry count, failure message, rules, extension lists)
body:
- Docs say "retry up to 2 times"; the code makes one fix call (`range(MAX_RETRIES)` with `MAX_RETRIES = 2`).
- Every False return prints "Compression failed after retries", exit 2, including refusals where no retry ran (backup exists, empty file, not smaller).
- SKILL.md's Compression Rules never reach the provider and contradict `build_compress_prompt` ("Never restructure…" vs "Merge redundant bullets").
- Three different extension lists (SKILL.md, README, `detect.py`); SECURITY.md's file-I/O list omits lock files, the staged file and temp files.

Seen on v4.0.1 (`2a6b9a9`). Repros used a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=openai-compat`) returning a fixed reply, so they show what the code accepts, not how often a real model does it.

title: fix(compress): ignore trailing punctuation on URLs and paths in validation
body:
Fixes #1353

`URL_REGEX` and `PATH_REGEX` both include trailing `.` and `,`, so if the compressed text writes `…/v2,` or `docs/runbook.md.` where the original had no punctuation right after, validation reports the URL/path as lost and the compress run exits after both attempts.

`extract_urls()` / `extract_paths()` now strip trailing `.,;:!?` from each match before comparing. Dots inside a path (`src/app.config.ts`) are untouched. Both sides go through the same functions, so the comparison stays symmetric.

Tests: added `TestTrailingPunctuation` to `tests/test_validate_inline.py`, including an end-to-end `validate()` case with the repro from the issue (3 of the new tests fail without the change). Only the source under `skills/` is changed; `sync-skill.yml` updates the plugin mirror. `test_validate_inline.py`, `test_compress_safety.py`, `test_compress_cli.py`, `test_detect.py` and `verify_repo.py` pass, and the fixtures in `tests/caveman-compress/` still validate.

title: fix(compress): refuse credential dotfiles before reading them
body:
Fixes #1354

Credential dotfiles such as `.npmrc` (`_authToken=…`), `.pypirc` and `.pgpass` have an empty `Path.suffix`. They aren't in `SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX`, so `detect_file_type()` sniffs their content, classifies them as `natural_language`, and the contents get sent to the provider.

Changes:
- added `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.s3cfg` and `.boto` to `SENSITIVE_BASENAME_REGEX` (`.git-credentials` and `.htpasswd` were already caught by the name tokens; the test covers them too)
- `cli.py` now calls `is_sensitive_path()` before `detect_file_type()`, so a refused file isn't read first, matching what SKILL.md says ("refused before they are read"). `compress_file()` keeps its own check.

I left out two of the issue's suggestions on purpose:
- Never classifying a dotfile as natural language would also block legitimate prose dotfiles like `.cursorrules`.
- Only testing the basename would loosen the current directory-level blocking (`secrets/`, `api-keys/`). That's a policy call, so better as its own change if you want it.

Tests: `test_credential_dotfiles_are_blocked` in `test_compress_safety.py`, plus a CLI test checking that a `.npmrc` is refused before the `Detected:` line, with the file left untouched. Both fail without the change. `test_compress_safety.py`, `test_compress_cli.py`, `test_detect.py`, `test_validate_inline.py` and `verify_repo.py` pass. Only the sources under `skills/` are changed; `sync-skill.yml` updates the plugin mirror.

title: fix(compress): match the retry docs and failure message to what the CLI does
body:
Addresses the first two points of #1355.

- SKILL.md and the caveman-compress README said "retry up to 2 times", but `MAX_RETRIES = 2` means two validation passes with at most one fix call between them. The docs now say that.
- `cli.py` printed `Compression failed after retries` for every `False` from `compress_file()`, including runs that stopped before any attempt (backup already exists, empty file, output not smaller). It now prints `Compression did not complete (see above). Original file is untouched.`, which holds on every path because the live file is only written on success. The exit code is still 2.

I didn't touch the other two points (SKILL.md's compression rules vs `build_compress_prompt`, and the extension lists). Those need a decision on which side is right, not just a wording fix.

The plugin SKILL.md mirror is updated in the same commit since `verify_repo.py` checks it. The `cli.py` mirror is left to `sync-skill.yml`.

Tests: added a CLI test with a whitespace-only `.md`, which exits 2 without claiming retries. `test_compress_cli.py`, `test_compress_safety.py` and `verify_repo.py` pass.

title: fix(compress): keep frontmatter local on compress and fix passes
body:
This PR fixes [issue #1349](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/1349).

Keep YAML frontmatter local on both the initial compression and fix retry. Apply the same body guards to both responses: preserve a leading heading or code block and reject added frontmatter-shaped blocks outside preserved code. Rejected responses leave the source unchanged.

The fix prompt now carries the body only, and a fix reply that includes frontmatter is rejected, so replies must return the body only.

`plugins/caveman/` is not edited; the sync workflow regenerates it from `skills/`.

The regression tests cover both reported paths, body-only repairs, nested/list-valued YAML, thematic breaks, fenced YAML, code preservation and CRLF. Arbitrary commentary before plain prose without a structural anchor or frontmatter shape remains ambiguous; this change does not attempt to classify or strip that prose.

Validation in offline ARM64 Docker with Python 3.12.15:
- 102 targeted tests passed, zero skips.
- The 18 new checks on the base produced the declared eight bug failures, two body-only contract failures and eight passing preservation controls.
- All 12 scripted OpenAI-compatible adapter cases matched their expectations. These exercise real compression/validation with synthetic replies, without a provider call; they do not measure model behavior.

`tests/verify_repo.py` and full GitHub CI were not run locally; the broader verification runner requires Node, git, bash and installer hooks beyond this Python-only environment.

![Caveman validation results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9ea22f4-4b73-4cec-b24f-d4c02f043270)

AI assistance was used to implement, test and review this change.

Closes #1349.

title: `caveman enable claude` sets ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto: ~2.5x token usage in Agent SDK hosts (T3 Code) from inlined MCP schemas and a broken prompt cache
body:
**What happened**
After `caveman enable claude`, `~/.claude/settings.json` got `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto`. In T3 Code (Claude Agent SDK, sdk-ts 2.1.308/309), MCP servers connect after the session starts, so the first calls fall under the `auto` threshold and every MCP schema is sent in full. When the late servers connect, the tool list grows and then flips to deferred, so the prompt changes and the cache misses. The same task cost about 2.5x the plain CLI.

**Evidence (one session)**
| call | tools sent | cache write | cache read |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 117 | 92,823 | 0 |
| 2 | 129 | 101,549 | 0 |
| 4 | 16 (deferred) | 38,326 | 0 |

Before enabling caveman, sessions of the same kind sent 13 tools on call 1 (about 13k cache write, 15k read). The CLI is less affected because its MCP servers are connected before the first call, so it is already over the threshold.

**Cause**
When `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` is not set, Claude Code itself defaults to always-on tool search (the same as `true`). Caveman replaces that default with `auto`. From the Claude Code 2.1.309 binary:
```js
if(O(e))  return "tst-auto";  // "auto" / "auto:N" → threshold mode
if(Ne(e)) return "tst";       // truthy → always on
if(ls(e)) return "standard";  // falsy → off
return "tst";                 // not set → always on (default)
```
Caveman, `packages/cli`:
```js
const TOOL_SEARCH_DEFAULT = "auto";
if (env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH === undefined)
    env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH = TOOL_SEARCH_DEFAULT;
```
So enabling caveman silently moves users from Claude Code's default (always on) to threshold mode.

**Suggested fix**
Set `TOOL_SEARCH_DEFAULT = "true"`. That keeps Claude Code's own default when the base URL goes through the proxy. The cost is one ToolSearch round-trip the first time each MCP tool is used. Happy to send a PR.

**Workaround**
Set `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Caveman only writes the value when it is missing.

**Environment**
caveman CLI 4.0.1, Claude Code 2.1.308/2.1.309, T3 Code desktop 0.1.1/0.1.2, Linux x64.

*Diagnosed and drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code).*

title: fix(cli): default ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH to "true" to match Claude Code
body:
Fixes #1361.

Claude Code defaults to always-on tool search when `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` is unset. `enable claude` and `wrap` wrote `auto` instead, which uses a threshold. Agent SDK hosts (T3 Code) connect MCP servers after the first request, so early turns send every schema in full and the switch to deferred later breaks the prompt cache. That's about 2.5x token usage; see the issue for numbers.

- `TOOL_SEARCH_DEFAULT` is now `"true"`.
- `disable` also removes the legacy `"auto"` written by earlier releases.
- Tests: updated the enable assertion and added a test for the legacy withdraw. `native-enable.runtime.mjs` passes 117/117.

Existing installs keep `"auto"` until they disable and enable again, since `enable` never overwrites a value that's already set.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(compress): treat a .env file as config, not prose
body:
## Problem

`detect.py` lists `.env` in `SKIP_EXTENSIONS`, but that entry never matches a file named `.env`. In pathlib a dotfile without another dot has no suffix (`Path(".env").suffix == ""`), so `detect_file_type()` sends `.env` to the content sniffing for extensionless files. `KEY=value` lines match no code pattern unless the value starts with a quote or bracket, so a typical `.env` comes back as `natural_language`:

```
DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@localhost:5432/app
API_KEY=sk-test-123
DEBUG=true
```

`caveman-compress .env` then prints `Detected: natural_language`, sends the file, keys included, to the model and rewrites it. #606 closed the same gap for `Dockerfile`, `Makefile` and shebang scripts.

## Fix

- When a file has no suffix, its whole name is matched against `SKIP_EXTENSIONS`, so `.env` is classified as `config` and skipped.
- Other dotfiles are sniffed as before, so a prose dotfile such as `.cursorrules` stays compressible.
- The plugin copy of `detect.py` is updated in the same PR, as in #606.

## Tests

- `test_dotenv_is_config_not_compressible` fails on `main` (`natural_language`) and passes with the fix.
- `test_prose_dotfile_still_compressible` pins that `.cursorrules` prose is still compressible.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 253 tests OK. `python tests/verify_repo.py`: all checks pass.

title: pi: per-prompt runtime context is appended to the system prompt, so the provider prompt cache is re-written at each prompt
body:
## Summary

When the native runtime returns context for a prompt, the pi extension appends that context to the **system prompt** (`packages/pi-extension/src/index.ts`, `before_agent_start`, around lines 234-256 on `main`):

```ts
const dynamic = [additionalContextOf(response), ...pendingContext].filter(Boolean);
...
const parts = [event.systemPrompt, coreContext, ...dynamic].filter(Boolean) as string[];
return { systemPrompt: parts.join("\n\n") };
```

The dynamic part changes from prompt to prompt. Examples from our sessions: `Likely implementation path (observed local metadata): 1. docs/guides/upgrade-headroom.md — file name matches task terms Evidence: ccr://…` and `Current observation already exists: docs/reference/token-toolchain.md; …`. The provider caches the request prefix in the order tools, then system, then messages. So each change re-writes the prompt cache for everything after the tool definitions: the system prompt and the whole conversation. It happens again when the context disappears.

## Evidence

pi 1.3.0, the `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1 pi extension, and the `bin-v4.0.2` `caveman-proxy` serving `native.sock`. I verified the binary against `checksums.txt` and its signature. The installed `bin-v4.0.1` runtime does not answer on this machine (#1279), Signet's pi extension, context-mode and RTK. Claude Haiku 4.5 through an Anthropic-compatible gateway, with **no proxy in between**. The run is one session of 8 prompts against the same working tree. A recording forwarder between pi and the gateway kept every request body, and I diffed consecutive requests in cache order:

| Request | Prompt | First difference from the previous request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 009 | 4 (first request) | none, it extends the previous request |
| 011 | 5 (first request) | `system[0]`: `…\n\nLikely implementation path (observed local metadata):\n1. docs/guides/upgrade-headroom.md …` appended |
| 014 | 6 (first request) | `system[0]`: that list changes to `1. docs/reference/token-toolchain.md …` |
| 018 | 7 (first request) | `system[0]`: changes to `Current observation already exists: docs/reference/token-toolchain.md; …` |
| 020 | 8 (first request) | `system[0]`: the dynamic context is gone again |

Provider usage for those first requests (pi session file):

| Prompt | Cache read | Cache write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 (system unchanged) | 28,645 | 249 |
| 5 | **10,683** | **18,735** |
| 6 | **10,683** | **20,102** |
| 7 | **10,683** | **20,815** |
| 8 | 24,900 | 6,739 |

10,683 tokens is the tool definitions alone. The same 8 prompts cost $0.112 when the native runtime was quiet (no dynamic context), and $0.171 to $0.208 when it answered. Cache writes went from 38k to 78k–86k tokens. In a long session on an Opus-class model, each such prompt re-writes the whole conversation. A cache write costs 25 times a cache read, so this outweighs what the compression saves.

## Expected

The system prompt stays byte-stable across prompts, so `coreContext` only. Per-prompt context reaches the model after the cached prefix: for example as a message that pi's `context` event appends after the new user turn, or as a prefix on that turn. Either way, only the new tail is written to the cache.

## Notes

- The same happens through Headroom 0.41.0 in `cache` mode, so this is not a proxy effect. Direct to the gateway with the runtime quiet, the system prompt never changed in 8 prompts.
- Related: #1279. With the `bin-v4.0.1` runtime quiet, there is no context and so no cache loss. The bug shows once the runtime answers, here with `bin-v4.0.2`.

title: pi: short tool outputs (~1.8 KB) are replaced by a content-free handle, so every needed output costs a caveman_retrieve round trip
body:
## Summary

With the `bin-v4.0.2` native runtime answering on our machine (the installed `bin-v4.0.1` one does not, #1279), the pi extension replaces even short tool outputs with a recovery handle that carries no content. When the agent needs the output, which is the normal case for a command result or a file it just read, it has to call `caveman_retrieve`. That costs one extra model request, so it costs more tokens than the shrink saves.

## Examples (pi 1.3.0, `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1 pi extension, `bin-v4.0.2` `caveman-proxy`, `CAVEMAN_MODE=compress`, policy `safe`, profile `full-safe`)

`seq 1 200 | sed 's/^/line /'` (200 lines, about 1.8 KB) came back as:

```text
[CommandResult]
status: current
source: seq 1 200 | sed 's/^/line /'
full: ccr://ccr_obj_715d44adc3860c4d6adb17dcb2a3bca9
recover: call caveman_retrieve with recovery_handle="ccr://…" to get these bytes back in full — one call returns the entire original.
```

A `read` of a 20-line file (about 4 KB) came back as `[FileObservation]` with only `status: current`, `source:` and the handle. The 800-byte and 1,600-byte outputs that we tested were passed through. `status: current` also appears for a command that was never run before, so it does not mean "you have already seen this".

## Cost

In an 8-prompt pi session on Claude Haiku 4.5, the model called `caveman_retrieve` 3 times. Each call was a full extra request. It read 27k to 31k cached tokens and wrote 0.5k to 1.6k tokens, and the retrieved bytes then entered the context anyway. On an Opus-class model, each round trip costs more than writing the original output into the context once. A handle-only replacement saves tokens only when the agent never needs the content. For a command result or a fresh `read`, the agent almost always needs it.

## Suggestions

- A minimum size below which the output passes through unchanged. In our tests, about 1.8 KB was enough to trigger a replacement.
- When the output is replaced, keep an inline excerpt or summary (head, tail, error lines), so that most outputs need no round trip.
- Or count the cost of a `caveman_retrieve` round trip when the runtime decides to replace an output.

Related: #1364 (per-prompt context in the system prompt), #1279.

title: Release a CLI that installs bin-v4.0.2: setup --install still gets the bin-v4.0.1 runtime (#1279)
body:
## Request

Please publish an `@caveman-ai/cli` release that installs `bin-v4.0.2`.

## Why

- `bin-v4.0.2` (2026-10-23) has the native runtime changes from #1309: `Handle` honors the hook deadline, and each stripe gets a one-slot queue.
- The npm `latest` tag is still `4.0.1`. Its `dist/binaries.generated.js` pins `BINARY_RELEASE = "bin-v4.0.1"`, so `caveman setup --install` installs the 4.0.1 runtime. Users cannot get the fix through a supported path.
- On our machine, `bin-v4.0.2` is the fix for #1279. In the same Caveman home, with the same environment, `session.start` on `native.sock` behaves like this:
  - `bin-v4.0.1` times out every time, including right after a restart.
  - `bin-v4.0.2` answers in 61 to 87 ms.

  Details: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/1279#issuecomment-6362449054. I checked the `bin-v4.0.2` binary against `checksums.txt`, and the signature against the key pinned in CLI 4.0.1 (`openssl dgst -sha256 -verify`: `Verified OK`).
- The release would also ship #1292 (the pi extension tells the session when the runtime goes quiet), which is merged but not on npm.

## Note

When shrinking works in pi, two issues show up, and they cost more tokens than shrinking saves in our tests: #1364 (per-prompt context in the system prompt re-writes the prompt cache) and #1365 (outputs of about 2 KB become content-free handles). If those can go into the same release, pi users get the fix for #1279 without the extra cost.

title: fix(middleware): do not mark a response over the limit at a quarter of it
body:
## What

`UsageReader.feed` (`packages/middleware/python/caveman_middleware/_usage.py`) rejects a chunk early when `len(self.text) * 4 + len(chunk) > self.max_buffer`. But `self.text` is already decoded text, not bytes, so the `* 4` makes the reader give up at a quarter of its configured limit once a response arrives in more than one chunk. In the ASGI adapter (`max_buffer=65536`), a non-streaming JSON response of about 16 KB or more is marked `overflow`, `finish()` returns `None`, and the receipt carries no usage.

## Reproduction (on main)

A 20,129-byte chat-completion JSON with a valid `usage` block fed to `UsageReader(sse=False, max_buffer=65536)`:

```
chunks 1  overflow False  usage {'input_tokens': 5, 'output_tokens': 7, ...}
chunks 2  overflow False  usage {...}
chunks 8  overflow True   usage None
```

20 KB is well under the 64 KB limit.

## Fix

Compare `len(self.text) + len(chunk)` instead. The check after decoding (`len(self.text) > self.max_buffer`) still enforces the real limit, and a single chunk larger than the limit is still refused up front.

## Tests

New `tests/test_usage_reader.py`: the 20 KB body in 1, 2, 8 and 40 chunks must read its usage (the 8 and 40 chunk cases fail on main), and a body over a small limit must still overflow.

I ran the new file with `python3 -m unittest`. I could not run the rest of the middleware suite here: it needs `pytest`, which isn't installed in my environment.
