title: fix(middleware): require patched filelock
body:
## Problem and correction

A fresh `caveman-middleware[litellm]` install resolves LiteLLM 1.106.2 and filelock 3.32.7. That filelock version has GHSA-v4x8-3wr5-3wq8, GHSA-9vhv-jxww-xfm5 and GHSA-567q-5qvw-pf92, causing the certified-extra supply-chain gate on main to fail. This establishes a vulnerable dependency graph, not a demonstrated exploit in a Caveman request path.

Publish `filelock>=4.2.1` in the LiteLLM extra's wheel metadata. The resolver honors both packages' requirements and backtracks past LiteLLM releases requiring filelock below 4. Today both pip and uv select LiteLLM 1.103.7 with filelock 4.2.4. Other extras do not gain this dependency. No audit exceptions or weakened checks.

## Validation

- Built the original wheel: new metadata regressions failed (3 failed, 5 passed).
- Built the corrected wheel: all 8 metadata regressions passed, including vulnerable boundary versions and isolation from other extras.
- Actual installed-wheel LiteLLM suite, macOS/Python 3.14.2: 179 passed, 244 other-adapter skips, for both resolved 1.103.7 and existing latest pin 1.102.1.
- Actual pip dry-run of the built wheel and local SDK wheel, followed by pip-audit 2.10.1 over all resolved third-party pins: no known vulnerabilities found.
- Local floor 1.95.0 runtime check remains unavailable: upstream publishes no macOS wheel for that version. The Linux floor and all three latest LiteLLM CI lanes have now passed at `73ca60885ffae3c92bb03f36f36e80e920983cd1`.
- `git diff --check` passed. Supply-chain CI passed; remaining engine-ci jobs are pending. No production or live-provider validation claimed.

## Related work

PR #1379 addresses separate LiteLLM tool-call import failures and version exclusions. This patch does not depend on or modify that human branch; both PRs touch the LiteLLM extra and need reconciliation if both land. No release or deployment is included.

title: feat(evals): add Spanish (es) prompt set
body:
## What this changes

- `evals/prompts/es.txt`: the ten `en.txt` questions in Spanish (Spain), same topics, same order.
- `TERSE_PREFIXES["es"] = "Responde de forma concisa."`, so the control arm stays in the prompt's language (same reasoning as #862).
- README: lists the new set. `tests/test_eval_llm_run.py`: the unknown-language message now includes `es`.

No snapshot is committed, following the README ("none is committed yet") and #1380. The numbers are below so the set can be judged without a run.

Tests: `uv run --with pytest --with tiktoken pytest tests/test_eval_*.py` passes (31 tests, 142 subtests).

## Does caveman transfer to Spanish?

The README asks this as an open question. Two same-day runs on the same setup: `claude-opus-5-5`, CLI 2.1.310, `CAVEMAN_EVAL_SKILLS=caveman,ultracave,megacave`, one run per arm, n = 10. The English run uses the unchanged `en.txt`. The committed `results.json` is from CLI 2.1.288, so it is not used here.

Reduction over the terse control (median, with the mean in brackets):

| Skill | es, tiktoken | en, tiktoken | es, billed output | en, billed output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| caveman | +3% (+8%) | +15% (+14%) | +7% (+10%) | +10% (+10%) |
| ultracave | +41% (+36%) | +35% (+32%) | +38% (+35%) | +4% (+6%) |
| megacave | not comparable | not comparable | | |

- **caveman gains less on Spanish than on English.** On tiktoken the median is +3% against +15%; on billed output, +7% against +10%. With n = 10, a single run and a stdev of about 13%, this points in a direction but is not a significant result. It fits the README's guess: the rules target English function words.
- **The terse control is similar in both languages:** −20% vs baseline in es, −21% in en.
- **ultracave's billed-output gap (+38% es vs +4% en) is not explained here.** The tiktoken numbers for the same arm are close (+41% vs +35%). It may be thinking tokens, which billed output includes. I would not read anything into it without more runs.
- **megacave answers in Classical Chinese in both languages**, as its SKILL.md says. Its delta is a script change, not compression, and the skill says not to claim savings, so it is left out.

## Language fidelity

This bears on #665 and #812. The `caveman` and `ultracave` Spanish answers stayed in Spanish on all 10 prompts. A heuristic count of English function words (the, is, and, of, to, …) gives 0 or 1 per answer, against 15 to 66 Spanish ones. Technical terms stayed verbatim.

Each call ran with `--setting-sources project` from an empty temp dir, so no user hook, CLAUDE.md or plugin reached any arm.

Reproduce:

```bash
CAVEMAN_EVAL_LANG=es CAVEMAN_EVAL_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 CAVEMAN_EVAL_SKILLS=caveman,ultracave,megacave uv run python evals/llm_run.py
CAVEMAN_EVAL_LANG=es uv run --with tiktoken python evals/measure.py
```

## Context, not part of this change: uncontrolled field data

I use caveman in Spanish every day, with a local hook (not in this PR) that adds Spanish-specific rules on top of the skill: Spanish filler words, no chat abbreviations, keep articles and ¿ ¡. This compares my own sessions before and after I installed the hook, `claude-opus-5-5` turns only, as aggregates:

| | Before (30 days, 729 turns) | After (19 days, 405 turns) |
|---|---|---|
| Median characters per turn | 1,110 | 902 (−19%) |
| p90 characters per turn | 2,490 | 2,212 (−11%) |
| Spanish filler words per 1,000 words | 0.16 | 0.04 |
| Wordy phrases per 1,000 words | 0.07 | 0.01 |
| Turns opening with a courtesy phrase | 4.7% | 1.5% |

This is not a controlled comparison. Over the same period the plugin moved to 3.2.0, my own instructions changed, and the mix of tasks is different. I include it only as the reason I think an **opt-in** Spanish mode could be worth measuring later. Such a mode would be loaded only by an explicit setting and never in the canonical rules, which is why #118 was closed. This PR proposes no rules. If an `es` mode ever gets proposed, this prompt set is what it would be measured with.

title: cavemem: a memory cannot be reverted to an earlier value (supersede and remember reject the expired row's text)
body:
**What happen**
`cavemem` cannot store a revert to an earlier value. Memory ids are `sha256(text)`, so A -> B -> A hashes back to A's expired row.

- `Supersede(B, "A")` fails with `replacement memory mem_... already exists` (`mem/store.go`, the `exists > 0` check counts expired rows).
- `Remember("A")` fails with `memory ... exists only as an expired historical version and cannot be re-remembered as current`.

The only way out is `Forget` on A's old row, which deletes its history.

**Expected**
Superseding the current memory with the text of an earlier, expired version succeeds. History stays a straight line (A -> B -> A'), and recall returns only the current version.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: remember "database host is db-a"; supersede it with "database host is db-b"; supersede that with "database host is db-a"
Got:   supersede: replacement memory mem_9d7af57ea8bfb74b already exists
Want:  new current version "database host is db-a", history A -> B -> A'
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: cavemem CLI / MCP / JS and Python clients

**Version / install method**
main, built from source (`go build ./mem/cmd/cavemem`)

title: cavemem supersede: no --stdin and no exit 65, so texts over ~128 KB (Linux) or ~32 KB (Windows) fail in the clients
body:
**What happen**
`cavemem supersede <id> <text>` takes the new text as a command-line argument, and `remember` has `--stdin` for this. The size cap is 256 KB (`MaxMemoryBytes`), but one argument is limited to about 128 KB on Linux (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) and the whole command line to about 32 K characters on Windows. The JS and Python clients pass the text as an argument, so a replacement `remember` accepts fails to spawn.

Also, `cmdSupersede` returns exit code 1 for every error. `cmdRemember` maps `ErrMemoryTooLarge` to exit 65. Both clients export `MEMORY_TOO_LARGE_EXIT_CODE = 65` as the contract, so for supersede a caller cannot tell "too large" from any other failure.

**Expected**
`supersede <id> --stdin` exists, the clients use it, and an oversized replacement exits 65.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: supersede(id, <200 KB text>) from the Python or JS client on Linux
Got:   OSError / E2BIG before the binary runs
Want:  stored, or exit 65 if over 256 KB
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: cavemem CLI, JS and Python clients

**Version / install method**
main, built from source (`go build ./mem/cmd/cavemem`)

title: mem: allow reverting a memory to an earlier value; add supersede --stdin
body:
Fixes #1384
Fixes #1385

**Revert to an earlier value (#1384)**
`Supersede` counted expired rows when checking whether the replacement already exists, so A -> B -> A always failed. When the replacement text matches an expired row, the new version now gets its own id (hash of the text plus the id it replaces). History stays linear and recall returns only the current version.

**`supersede --stdin` (#1385)**
- `cavemem supersede <id> --stdin` reads the text from stdin, capped at `MaxMemoryBytes`, like `remember`.
- An oversized replacement exits 65, matching `remember` and the exported `MEMORY_TOO_LARGE_EXIT_CODE`.
- The JS and Python clients now send the text over stdin, so they stop hitting argv size limits.

**Tests**
- `TestSupersedeCanRevertToAnEarlierValue` fails on `main` with "replacement memory ... already exists" and passes with this change.
- New CLI test for `--stdin` and exit 65.
- `go test ./mem/...`, `node --test mem/js/tests/client.test.mjs` and `pytest mem/py/tests` pass.

A literal replacement text of `--stdin` is now read as the flag, as `remember` already does.

title: Hermes native enable rewrites openai-codex to custom and loses provider-specific routing
body:
## What happened

On a Hermes configuration already using the named OAuth provider `openai-codex`, native enable unconditionally writes `provider: custom` and the generic proxy route `/w/hermes/v1`, while preserving the model and the text of `api_mode: codex_responses`.

`custom` is an intentional generic provider, not inherently invalid. The bug is applying that generic route/provider rewrite to an existing Codex OAuth integration without preserving its credential and transport selection. Existing custom endpoint refusal and restoration protections must remain.

## Before / generated / expected for Codex

```yaml
# Existing
model:
  provider: openai-codex
  default: gpt-6.1-sol
  api_mode: codex_responses

# Generated provider/base URL
  provider: "custom"
  base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1"

# Expected for this named OAuth provider
  provider: openai-codex
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt
```

The expected existing proxy base is `/chatgpt`; the Responses operation is `/chatgpt/responses`, not `/chatgpt/v1/responses`.

## Reproduction and evidence levels

1. In a disposable HOME/HERMES_HOME, seed the working model block above, with the agent executable and compatible Caveman binaries available.
2. Run `caveman enable hermes`, inspect the installed YAML, then run `caveman doctor hermes`.
3. Enable again and disable, retaining the output/config snapshots and checking restoration separately.

The **published npm CLI 4.0.1** reproduces the rewrite and doctor acceptance without any credential or inference. Full-source entrypoints on frozen main `1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9`, `v4.0.1` and `cli-v4.0.1` also reproduce when run with Bun; these are not newly built tsc/npm packages. A control using a pre-existing custom user endpoint is refused without modifying its configuration. Restore assertions passed for the seed tested; they do not cover all YAML forms.

An isolated execution of the installed Hermes resolver, with no production secrets or network, resolves the generated configuration to `custom`, `chat_completions` and `no-key-required`. Its Codex branch with an explicitly supplied test credential retains `codex_responses` and `/chatgpt`. This proves selection behavior, not live OAuth authentication or token refresh.

**Historical observation, not replayed in the cross-audit:** the original environment returned HTTP 401 with `no-key-required`; restoring `openai-codex` and `/chatgpt` subsequently produced a real response without fallback. The installation-time journal separately records the original provider and the generated generic route. New fixture journals are removed by normal disable and were not retained as snapshots; their absence must not be described as an additional failure.

Three existing Go proxy tests passed: path/query preservation, exact credential-header forwarding and no credential fallback. They use test HTTP servers, not a ChatGPT login. No claim is made that every native lifecycle surface or a complete Hermes fix was validated; one ancillary tag fixture had an unavailable native socket while its HTTP proxy remained up.

## Cause / source

At main `1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9`:

- [Generator](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L10144-L10161): unconditional `custom` + `/w/hermes/v1`.
- [Existing endpoint guard](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L10209-L10216): already refuses protected user endpoints for absent/custom/auto providers; preserve it.
- [Doctor](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L11384-L11387): expects the generic Hermes route.
- [Current test](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs#L1549-L1593): starts with Codex but asserts that generic result.
- [Existing ChatGPT handler](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/proxy/internal/gateway/chatgpt.go#L24-L44): transport need not be invented.

## Expected / regression tests

Preserve the named Codex provider and its credential handling, choose the existing ChatGPT proxy base, and align doctor with the original provider retained in the journal. Preserve non-Codex behavior, model, API mode, user endpoints/credentials and exact restoration protections. Add regression cases for Codex vs non-Codex, repeat enable/doctor/disable, existing custom endpoints and user-modified blocks.

## Related report / environment

[The August 27, 2026 comment on #706](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/706#issuecomment-5435449291) reports precisely this incompatibility and an unpushed local fix. The closed native-Hermes feature request is precedent, not proof the fix landed. The mechanism remains in the inspected source.

Linux/Fedora 44; Home Manager; Caveman CLI/runtime 4.0.1, native pack 2.2.0. The rewrite is reproduced with the public npm CLI, independently of the downstream Nix managed-install patch.

title: doctor opencode reports MCP recovery healthy when the registered executable is missing
body:
## What happened

The native doctor can report `state: installed` and `components.mcp_recovery: true` when OpenCode's registered MCP executable is absent or non-executable. It successfully probes another compatible MCP binary globally instead of validating the command OpenCode will launch.

This is independent of Nix. The reproduction uses two copies A and B of the **same real runtime/version**; B need not be a newer release.

## Reproduction

In an isolated HOME with a real local proxy and compatible agent/runtime executables:

1. Set `CAVEMAN_MCP_BIN` to executable A and run `caveman enable opencode`; let the CLI generate both the host registration and its ownership journal.
2. Confirm doctor reports installed with A available.
3. Make A unavailable, leaving another compatible executable B resolved through `CAVEMAN_MCP_BIN`; do not change the registration or its journal.
4. Run `caveman doctor opencode`: it returns success, `installed` and recovery=true, although launching the registered A raises FileNotFoundError.
5. Repeat with A present but chmod 0644: doctor still reports recovery=true, while a real launch raises PermissionError.
6. Negative control: without a valid globally resolved binary, recovery becomes false.

This was reproduced with the integrity-checked **public npm CLI 4.0.1**, frozen main `1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9` and release source entrypoints. Source entrypoints were run with Bun, not newly built tsc/npm packages. The primary npm/main/v4.0.1 scenarios used real proxies without the native-runtime warning. The ancillary cli-v4.0.1 scenario produced the same MCP result but logged an unavailable native Unix socket; it is not evidence of working native lifecycle hooks.

Journals come from real enable commands, not synthetic journal doubles. A real MCP initialize/tools-list against B exposes five tools. That proves B speaks MCP, not that the host can launch missing A or that a full OpenCode session is healthy. No model inference was needed.

## Cause / source

At the main SHA above:

- [OpenCode registration/journal comparison](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L11345-L11354) accepts the unchanged entry without validating its executable.
- [Global MCP probe](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L13710-L13714) resolves the current companion binary, independent of the host command.
- [State/component calculation](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/1f951fb4ad40ba63302c6e7f987147e034d599d9/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L11428-L11473) derives recovery from that probe and ownership.

## Expected / safety constraints

- For recognized owned local registrations, check the actual registered command's existence/executability before attesting recovery. Global companion availability is a different property.
- Do not run arbitrary user-modified commands simply to probe them, and do not adopt them as owned automatically.
- Preserve existing refusal to destructively restore/disable user-modified entries.
- Tests: missing A with valid B; non-executable A with valid B; unchanged working registration; negative global-probe control; user-edited registration preserved by disable/repair.

**Not a separate bug:** manually replacing the registered command A with B breaks ownership equality, legitimately yields `degraded`, and blocks destructive disable. Component flags derived from aggregate ownership are not proof that each component physically stopped working. Separating ownership drift, launch validity and global availability would improve diagnostics, but must not weaken those safeguards.

## Related reports / environment

[#1137](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/1137) covers disappearing hook/plugin targets; the registered MCP command is a remaining distinct surface. [#926](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/926) concerns hook identity, not this MCP target check. No exact dedicated duplicate was identified in scoped all-state searches.

Original observation: OpenCode on Fedora 44/Home Manager, CLI/runtime 4.0.1 and native pack 2.2.0. The old store path exposed the problem, but the public npm reproduction uses ordinary disposable paths.

title: daily triage 2026-10-25: cavemem revert + argv limits, Hermes OAuth provider, MCP recovery honesty, two agent pins
body:
## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1384, #1385 | Memory ids are `sha256(text)`, so `Supersede` counting expired rows made A→B→A impossible; and `supersede` took its text as one argv element with no `--stdin` and no exit 65, unlike `remember` | cavemem CLI + MCP, JS and Python clients; argv limit hits Linux (~128 KB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) and Windows (~32 KB command line) | `TestSupersedeCanRevertToAnEarlierValue`, `TestSupersedeReadsReplacementFromStdinAndMapsTooLargeExit`, JS + Python client cases | #1386 |
| #1385 (sibling) | `caveman mem supersede` joined the replacement into one argv element and filtered `--stdin` away as flag-looking, so the npm CLI kept hitting the same limit the contributor fixed everywhere else | `caveman`/`cave` npm CLI; same two OS limits | `mem supersede --stdin passes the replacement to cavemem byte for byte (issue #1385)` | — |
| #1391 | `hermesNativeConfig` wrote `provider: "custom"` + `/w/hermes/v1` unconditionally, dropping a named OAuth provider's credential and transport; `api_mode: codex_responses` survived in text, so the resolver picked `chat_completions` with `no-key-required` → 401 | `caveman enable hermes` on any config using `openai-codex`; all OS | existing hermes enable/disable case now asserts the preserved provider (it previously pinned the bug), plus a new non-Codex case — Hermes had no generic-provider coverage at all | — |
| #1392 | `doctor`/`status` attested MCP recovery from `probeMcpBinary()`, which answers "is some compatible caveman-mcp resolvable", not "can the registered command launch" | claude, gemini, opencode journaled registrations; all OS | `doctor stops attesting MCP recovery when the registered binary cannot launch (#1392)` — covers both missing and `chmod 0644` | — |
| #1381 | codex pin stale at 0.163.0 | conformance matrix + profile | re-ran `agents/probe-installed.mjs` (see below) | #1388 |
| #1360 | opencode pin stale at 1.19.3 | conformance matrix + profile | re-ran `agents/probe-installed.mjs` (see below) | #1389 |

### Review round — Devin Review found a data-loss bug I had introduced

Worth reading even if you skim the rest. **`3304023`** fixes silent data loss in the adopted #1386 change.

A cavemem build predating `supersede --stdin` reads supersede's *second argument* as the replacement text. The clients and the `caveman mem` CLI shell out to a **separately installed** binary, so client-newer-than-binary skew is ordinary. I built cavemem from `afb5d18~1` and ran the new client against it:

```
supersede returned: {"id":"mem_06cc…","supersedes":"mem_a66a…"}   # exit 0, success
recall "deploy key"  -> []                                        # the fact is GONE
history              -> 'the deploy key lives in vault…'  EXPIRED
                        '--stdin'                          CURRENT
```

Exit 0, the real memory expired, the literal `--stdin` stored as the current fact — against `mem/CLAUDE.md`'s own "a memory is never lost" invariant. `version --json` now advertises `supersede-stdin`, and every caller checks it first: the clients use the **argv form for anything that fits in one argument** (96 KiB, 24 KiB on Windows — platform-aware so Linux texts between 24 KB and 128 KB don't regress), and only use stdin above that; `caveman mem supersede <id> --stdin` probes and refuses with an upgrade message. Both probes fail **closed**. Verified on both sides: the old binary now stores small replacements correctly and refuses a 200 KB one with the memory intact; a current binary still stores 200 KB over stdin, so #1385's real case survives. Invariant written up in `mem/CLAUDE.md`.

**`bf1982f`** fixes a second regression from the same adopted change: after A→B→A, `Remember(A)` failed with "exists only as an expired historical version" — a message that is *false* in that state, since a current row holds the text and Recall returns it. `Remember` now returns that current row without reviving the expired one. Treated as blocking despite its yellow label, because my own branch created the state.

**`45a1bfe`** aligns `journaledMcpTargetsExist` with the `claudeProfileGone` filter every sibling check applies. **Not a reproduced fix** — both `enable` and `doctor --fix` drop a gone profile's operations, so I could not construct a sequence where it changes the verdict (probe output is on the thread). Kept because it cannot mask a real failure and leaving one helper inconsistent is a trap; say the word and I'll drop it.

The fourth finding (codex/hermes registrations stay uninspected) is the limitation already documented below — no code change, reasoning on the thread.

### Notes on the two fixes I extended

**#1391** keeps the named provider and points `base_url` at the proxy's existing `/chatgpt` handler, which takes its suffix verbatim — the Responses operation is `/chatgpt/responses`, so it must not gain a `/v1`. That is the convention `codexGatewayBase()` already documents for the `codex` agent, and `proxy/internal/gateway/chatgpt.go` already serves it, so no transport was invented. The route written is journaled and `doctor` now expects that route instead of always the generic one; a journal from before this change carries no `provider` and still reads as generic, so existing installs stay healthy. Preserved unchanged: every non-OAuth provider still gets the generic route, the refusal to touch a user's own `custom`/`auto` endpoint, and `disable`'s verbatim restore. The ephemeral `wrap` door is a different mechanism (`applyHermesAuthEnv` sets a base URL in a temp `HERMES_HOME` and never rewrites `provider`), so it carries no equivalent rewrite — its 7 tests pass untouched.

**#1392** reuses `invocationTargetsExist`, the helper the hook and plugin surfaces of this same bug class already use (#1137, which the reporter correctly identifies as the sibling). Existence and executability only — a registration the user may have edited is never run to probe it and never adopted as owned, which the test asserts. One shared `mcpLaunchable` term now feeds both the component and the state verdict, so they cannot disagree. Codex tables and the hermes `mcp_servers` block journal their registration as config text with no structured command; those stay uninspected rather than gaining a second YAML/TOML parser in a doctor path, where a mis-parse would call a healthy install degraded. **That is a remaining surface, not a closed one.**

### What I actually verified for the two pin bumps

I installed each pinned release and re-ran the repo's own probe here (Node 22.22.0): `codex` 0.164.0 and `opencode` 1.19.4 both report `version_ok: true, help_ok: true`, with `status: broken` **solely** because `version_matches` was false against the old pin. `node agents/compile.mjs` compiles 10 profiles and leaves the tree clean (so the contributors' generated files match the generator exactly), and `agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` reports scope valid across the branch.

I did **not** reproduce the route probe that `opencode`'s `verified_by` asserts (it needs a loopback recorder and a live `opencode run`); that line rests on @danieldutu's reported run, which is specific and carries its own limitations. Both PRs were based on a stale main — their workflow hunks carried `openclaw@2026.10.4`, `claude-code@2.1.302` and `gemini-cli@0.64.0` — so I confirmed after cherry-picking that only codex and opencode moved and main's other pins (`claude-code@2.1.308`, `gemini-cli@0.65.0`, `openclaw@2026.10.5`) are intact.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1390** (MiniMax `mcode`): feature request, not implemented per routine scope. Investigated and left a note on the likely shape — the reporter's own evidence (rules present in `CLAUDE.md` and visible in `/context`, opener unchanged) points at adherence rather than a delivery failure, which is the same wall #1318 is at, so a profile addition alone would not deliver what they are asking for. Needs a maintainer decision.
- **#1318** (ultracave adherence), **#1307** (pnpm lockfile note), **#1242** (Codex marketplace hooks), **#1285** (Antigravity CLI), **#1350**/**#1352** (compress validation): all carry a `<!-- caveman-daily-triage -->` comment with no new activity since, so skipped per the marker rule. #1307 and #1242 additionally need decisions outside this routine, and #1242's remedy touches `plugins/caveman/**`, which this routine may not edit.
- **#1236** (hermes drift): *not* a simple pin bump — the issue says 0.22.5 **fails** the latest probe, unlike #1381/#1360 where the new release probes clean. Re-checked the blocker this run: `github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/latest` still returns **403** here and PyPI `hermes-agent` still stops at **0.19.0**, so the 0.21.x/0.22.x line is unreachable and I could not verify a working 0.22.5 wrap. Structurally unchanged from the five previous runs, so I did not post a sixth identical comment.
- **#1225** (pi drift): installed is 1.4.0 while the open PR #1311 bumps only to 1.3.0; the profile pin is 1.0.4. Left alone rather than landing a pin for a version nobody probed.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1386 by @PARTHDESHMUKH2005** — **adopted**, cherry-picked with authorship preserved. I reproduced both bugs first: the revert failure returns the exact hash the reporter quoted (`mem_9d7af57ea8bfb74b`), and `cmdSupersede` had no `--stdin` and returned 1 for every error. Their judgement to fix only `Supersede` and leave `Remember` rejecting expired text is correct — that rejection is deliberate and documented in `store.go`. They missed one sibling (the npm CLI's own `mem supersede`), and the review round above found two further consequences of the change that neither of us caught: the version-skew data loss and the `Remember` regression. Both are fixed here; none of it detracts from a well-built PR.
- **#1388 by @danieldutu** — **adopted** (both commits, in order). The commit message is unusually honest about scope ("Launchability only… I ran no route probe"), and my re-run agrees with it exactly.
- **#1389 by @danieldutu** — **adopted** (both commits, in order). Route-probe attestation not re-run here; see above.
- **#1387 by @danieldutu** — **not landed this run**, no criticism implied. It closes #1336, which is already closed, and there is no open `agent-drift: qwen` issue, so it falls outside the "pin bumps for drift issues" scope this routine works under. The verification write-up looks as careful as the other two. Maintainer's call.
- **#1311 by @JuliusBrussee** — **stale**: bumps Pi to 1.3.0 while #1225 reports 1.4.0 installed. Needs a decision plus a fresh probe.
- **#1330 by @AlSh007** — **already landed**; no action needed. The change is on main as `e186906` (2026-10-19), and main's PowerShell twin is actually *stronger* than the PR's: it adds a `$BackupIsPlainJson = $false # unreadable probe: keep the backup` branch the PR lacked. Worth closing as merged-in-substance.

## Needs maintainer decision

- **#1392's remaining surface**: codex and hermes journal their MCP registration as config text. Extending the launchability check there means parsing TOML/YAML in a doctor path; I judged a mis-parse (calling a healthy install degraded) worse than the current gap, but that is a call to confirm.
- **`45a1bfe`**: an unreproduced consistency change. Drop it if you'd rather not carry those.
- **#1391's provider allowlist**: `HERMES_CHATGPT_OAUTH_PROVIDERS` currently holds only `openai-codex`. If Hermes gains other named OAuth providers that carry their own transport, they belong in that set.
- **Pre-existing, unrelated to this branch**: `packages/cli/src/binaries.generated.ts` is committed at `bin-v4.0.1` while `scripts/gen-binaries.mjs` generates `bin-v4.0.2`, so `tests/binary-pin.runtime.mjs` passes only when the generator runs first. I reproduced both failures on clean `origin/main` and changed nothing — PR #1321 looks like the intended fix.
- **#1390**, **#1387**, **#1311**, **#1236**, **#1225** as described above.

## Verification

All green on this branch, with the full root suite confirmed to run an **identical test set** to `origin/main` (name-by-name diff, after an earlier concurrent run under-reported by 26 tests and turned out to be runner variance, not a missing file):

- root `npm test` — 652 tests, 0 fail
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — 30, 0 fail
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 280, OK
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` — all checks passed
- `go test ./mem/... ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` — 55 packages ok, 0 fail
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` — gate passed
- `packages/cli` full runtime suite — 1443 tests, 0 fail
- `mem/js` (6) and `mem/py` (7) client tests — 0 fail

One failure in an early run (`enable opencode finds a host installed only as opencode2`) was my own environment pollution — I had installed `opencode` globally to probe the pin, and that test asserts a host present *only* as `opencode2`. It passes once removed; worth knowing that this test is sensitive to a real `opencode` on PATH.

No benchmark, savings, or token-reduction number was touched. `src/hooks/` was not modified, so `checksums.sha256` needed no regeneration (the manifest covers hook files, not the uninstall scripts).

title: daily triage: advisor-tool declaration left every Claude Code request unpriced (#1465); the Mastra canary pinned a framework assumption, not the adapter (#1463); plus earlier runs
body:
# Daily triage — 2026-11-05

Tenth run on this branch. A `daily-triage/` PR was still open, so today appended to it. **Nothing was force-pushed** — two new commits in one fast-forward push (`fe6b12f..e7bd471`). `origin/main` is unchanged at `2e068f73` and `git merge-tree` reports this head merges clean into it, so no rebase was taken.

**Two fixes, both from the only two actionable items filed or re-fired since the last run.** The new-items list was small today: two issues, one new contributor PR, one reply on an older one, and the two bots re-firing. Both fixes are closed out with a test that was seen to fail first; nothing was dropped from the PR during review.

**The `2026-11-03` and `2026-11-02` run sections were condensed into the shared condensed block below**, continuing the pattern (`2026-10-27`/`2026-10-26` on 10-31, `2026-10-29`/`2026-10-28` on 11-03, `2026-10-31` on 11-04). Two were taken rather than one on purpose: the body was at 54,908 of GitHub's 65,536 characters, and condensing only the oldest would have left this description at roughly 66,900 — over the cap — and condensing only enough to fit would have left the next run with no room at all. It now stands at 52,019, with 13,517 characters of headroom. Nothing is lost: every commit is still on the branch with its full reasoning in its commit message (`git log origin/main..HEAD`), each issue carries that run's own triage comment, and the previous full text is in this description's edit history.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1465 | `requestPricingUnsupportedReason` refuses to price any request whose `tools[]` declares a provider-hosted type outside `tokenOnlyProviderTool`, because such a tool can carry per-call or storage charges token rates cannot reconstruct. Claude Code now declares the server-side advisor (`advisor_20260301`) on **every** agent turn once the account flag is on, so each request was stamped `unsupported_provider_tool_charge` at inspect time; `standalonePriceForUsage` zeroes the price for any non-empty reason, the row lands `pricing_known = 0`, and `caveman stats` can only say "Unknown". The declaration is not a charge, and this repo already knew it — an advisor that *runs* reports its own model as a non-`message` `usage.iterations` entry, which `mergeProviderOutcomeQualifiers` has failed closed on since it was written | `caveman-proxy` / `caveman stats` on every host and OS, for any Anthropic account the advisor flag is on for (the reporter's store: 23,980 of 24,129 rows) | `adapter_contract_test.go` — the declaration prices, a later date stamp prices, an advisor beside a function tool prices, and a bare `advisor`, a non-date revision, an `advisory` lookalike and the same type on `openai` all still fail closed | — |
| #1463 | Not the adapter. `tests/hardening.test.mjs:81` asserted that cancelling the caller still aborts the signal the native model was handed — a claim about `@mastra/core`, not about caveman, since `native()` is a type assertion with no runtime effect and `prepare()` spreads the params. That framework behaviour has now moved three times (1.65.0 left the option unset unless the caller passed a signal; 1.77.0 began minting one per call, #1264; 1.82.0 stopped linking the minted one to the caller), so the nightly canary failed on an upstream release with the adapter unchanged | the nightly `middleware-canary` lane only; the pinned merge gate was green throughout, and no shipped adapter behaviour changes | same test, restated as the claim the adapter can make: the wrapped call's signal stands in the same relation to the **caller** as the bare call's, before and after cancellation, measured as `(is it the caller's own signal, is it aborted)` | — |

### #1463 is measured now, not argued

The 11-04 run reached the right diagnosis but could not run the canary and said so. It runs here. With `@mastra/core@latest` (1.82.0) and everything else at its pin the failure reproduces exactly — 136/137, that one assertion, `actual: false` — and so does the canary's own condition (every framework in `testedFrameworkVersions` at `@latest`, then `package.json` and the lockfile restored to their pins as the workflow does), at 137 tests.

The one line the last run asked for: on the **bare, unwrapped** `Agent` under 1.82.0, `options.abortSignal !== caller.signal` and `caller.abort()` leaves it unaborted. So it is `bare` that is `false`, the test's framework assumption was the wrong thing to pin, and widening is the correct call. The restatement is *stronger* than the old check on the identity axis — a clone of the caller's signal now fails where propagation alone would have passed it — and regime-independent on the propagation axis. Which regime the installed release implements is reported with `t.diagnostic` rather than asserted, so a passing canary still says which one it saw: pinned 1.65.0 prints `true`, 1.82.0 prints `false`, and the whole middleware suite is **137/137 under each**.

Deliberately **not** done: the tested-version lists are unchanged. The supported range already admits 1.82.0 (`>=1.65.0 <2`), so `check-latest-in-range.mjs` passes; claiming a new tested release is a published compatibility statement for you to make, not a triage run.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1465's first cause (@robin-ede) — reproduced in source, left to you on purpose.** `classifyHeaderAuthMode` returns `AuthModeSubscription` on a `claude-cli/` User-Agent *before* the credential is looked at, and `ListPriceEligible` admits only `payg`/`api_key`/Vertex `oauth`, so an API-billed Claude Code install can never reach the API-cost line however the second cause goes. The reporter is right about the mechanism. Both directions they offer invert a **deliberately pinned contract** — `authmode_test.go:16` is literally named *"ua subscription wins over payg token"* with `Bearer sk-ant-api123` as its input — so it is a policy change with a blast radius across every host, not a bug fix a triage run may take. Listed below for your call; the reporter offered to send the PR once you pick a direction.
- **#1464 (@otxboc, skills.sh `skills-guard-v10` DANGEROUS, 28 findings) — believed, and still not fixable here under this run's own rules.** The reporter did the work: they checked every finding against the live source and report them all as pattern matches on the skill's *intended* function (compressing and overwriting `CLAUDE.md` through an external model CLI, excluding secret-file patterns, reading a token-cap env var). Nothing in the finding list contradicts that. Why no fix: there is no failing test in `tests/` for "a third-party scanner returns a verdict", so the no-fix-without-a-failing-test rule binds; and the two CRITICALs are **README prose**, where this repo's own instructions make the README a product artifact with a deliberate voice and a 60-second install test — rewording `cp "$BACKUP" CLAUDE.md` and the overwrite description to please a scanner regex is exactly the kind of change that needs your sign-off, not mine. The `|authorized_keys` hypothesis (`compress.py:80`) is plausible and the narrowest of the three: it is one alternation branch in a refuse-list, so splitting the literal would not weaken the exclusion — but it is still a change made to satisfy an unseen regex, verifiable only by re-running the scanner, which I cannot do. The registry-allowlist route touches nothing in this repo at all. **What would settle it:** the reporter has offered the full raw scan output and to test any proposed change — that, plus your call on whether the README may move, turns this into a one-commit fix.
- **#1418 / #1408 / #1406 / #1236 / #1455 / #1417 / #1407 / #1423 / #1225 (agent-drift) — the nightly re-fired #1418 on 11-05 at the same versions; nothing changed but the timestamp.** Not re-commented, for the same reason as the last two runs: each already carries two or three triage comments and they all clear together on one unanswered question — whether a **liveness** probe may move a pin. Installing an agent at `@latest` would also replace the binary this session runs under, so the probe still needs a clean runner.
- **#1246, #1454** — unchanged since 11-04 and both waiting only on a close, which this run never does. No new activity on either.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1466 by @sudip28122812-creator — the premise checks out and the diff is internally consistent; one scoping question is yours.** The advisory is real: [GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw / CVE-2026-111769](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw), the MCP TypeScript SDK followed redirects to any origin and handed the new origin custom headers (`X-API-Key`, `mcp-session-id`) plus, on 307/308, the request body including OAuth token requests carrying `refresh_token` and `client_secret`; fixed in 1.32.0. Verified here rather than trusted: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is imported **only** by `packages/middleware/typescript` (`src/mcp.ts`, `src/compatibility.ts` and three test files — nothing else in the repo consumes it), so the blast radius is exactly the package they touched; `package.json` and `compatibility.ts` stay in step, which is what `versions.test.mjs:48`/`:51` check; and no test requires a floor to appear in `tested` or requires two tested entries, so the single-entry `tested: ['1.32.0']` is legal. **The question:** the PR raises `supportedFrameworkVersions` from `>=1.30.0` to `>=1.32.0`, and `frameworkGate` responds to an out-of-range version by *declining* — a user still on 1.30.x keeps their vulnerable SDK and additionally loses MCP compression, pass-through and silent except for the one-time warning. The decline message is the useful half (`Use @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0, or set acceptFrameworkVersion after testing …`), so this is arguable either way and I have not taken it: bumping the **pin** is unambiguously right, raising the **supported floor** is a published support decision. Two small notes: npm latest is already 1.32.2, so the canary's `@latest` install tests a release this PR does not name (harmless — the range admits it); and **no CI has run on this PR at all** (`get_status` → `pending`, zero statuses, zero check runs), so the author's "136 tests passed" is their local run, unverified by the repo's own lane.
- **#1427 by @danez — verdict unchanged, and their new evidence is worth having on the record.** The 10-31 review's one gap was live authenticated Codex execution; @danez has since run it against a real `AGENTS.md` outside a Git repository, with the initial validation catching a dropped inline-code occurrence and the targeted repair restoring it, and checked `--output-last-message` against installed Codex CLI help. That closes the part this container cannot reach. It is still a **feature** (a new compress provider), which the standing rule keeps out of a triage PR, so it remains recommended to you unchanged — not blocked on anything I found.
- **#1462 / #1461 / #1460 / #1415 / #1314 (dependabot) — in scope by the activity rule, not commented, one real overlap to flag.** No triage comment has ever been left on these, so they are formally in scope; they are bot PRs rather than volunteers, so the one thing worth saying goes here instead of in five notifications. The overlap: **#1462 bumps `golang.org/x/net` 0.60.0 → 0.62.0**, which is exactly what `2cb5e69` on this branch and @JuliusBrussee's own **#1426** both do — three changes to one module. Whichever of the three lands first, the other two conflict in `go.mod`/`go.sum`; #1462's remaining value after that is its other five bumps (`go-winio` 0.6.2→0.6.4, `pgx/v5` 5.11.0→5.12.0, `klauspost/compress` 1.20.1→1.20.3, `tiktoken-go/tokenizer` 0.8.1→0.10.0, `x/sys` 0.48.0→0.49.0). The tokenizer bump is two minors and sits under the engine's token accounting, so it is the one in that group I would not wave through without a run. None of the five was individually verified here.

## Needs maintainer decision

- **#1465, cause 1: may the billing class stop being guessed from the User-Agent?** The two shapes the reporter offers are a declared `billing = api` setting, or checking the credential before falling back to the UA. Either inverts `authmode_test.go`'s named contract. Worth noting that the test's own input — a `codex-cli/` UA carrying `Bearer sk-ant-api123` — is precisely the case the reporter says is misclassified, so the decision is whether that line was a considered trade or has simply never been revisited.
- **#1464: may the README move to satisfy the hub scanner, and do you want the registry-allowlist route instead?** The two CRITICAL findings are README prose under rules that treat it as product copy with a protected voice.
- **A type-level incompatibility between two *supported* versions, found while reproducing #1463 and not fixed blind.** `@mastra/core` 1.82.0 together with `@ai-sdk/provider` pinned at 4.0.11 — both inside the declared ranges (`>=1.65.0 <2`, `>=4.0.11 <5`) — fails our own `tsc` at `src/mastra.ts:272` with `TS2379`: 1.82.0 vendors `@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.35 types whose `JSONObject` values are `Readonly`, which `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` rejects against 4.0.11's. The canary never sees it because it moves every framework at once, and users consuming the shipped `dist` are unaffected at run time; a consumer that typechecks against our `.d.ts` with that combination is not. Fixing it means touching `src/mastra.ts`'s types, with no failing test in `tests/` to anchor it, so it is reported rather than attempted.
- **The `check-latest-in-range.mjs` lane and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`:** if #1466's floor raise lands, that script's range check is the only thing keeping the MCP tested list honest, and the PR leaves `tested` at a single release that is already behind npm latest.
- **Pre-existing `BINARY_RELEASE` drift, unchanged and again left alone.** Any build in this repo still rewrites `binaries.generated.ts`, `browse/bin/release.generated.mjs`, `mcp/bin/release.generated.mjs`, `shrink/bin/release.generated.mjs` and `packages/shared/binary-installer/release.generated.mjs` from `bin-v4.0.1` to `bin-v4.0.2`, because `packages/cli/BINARY_RELEASE` already says `bin-v4.0.2`. All five were reverted after today's runs — checked explicitly this time, given that `8c805e5` swept them in on 11-04 — and the final tree is clean. It belongs to #1366 / #1321.

## Verification

Full suite on `e7bd471`, after the review pass and after reverting the build drift, not before:

- `npm test` (root) — 661 tests, **0 fail**, 19 skipped
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` — 30/30
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 292 tests, **OK**
- `python tests/verify_repo.py` — **all local verification checks passed**
- `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` — 53 packages `ok`, 0 fail
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` — **windows compatibility gate passed**
- `pnpm --filter @caveman-ai/middleware test` with `CAVEMAN_REQUIRE_FRAMEWORKS=1` — 137/137 at the pins **and** 137/137 with every framework at `@latest`

Both fixes were seen to fail first for the stated reason: the pricing cases at `reason = "unsupported_provider_tool_charge", want ""`, and the Mastra assertion at `cancelling the caller still cancels the signal the native model was handed`, `actual: false`.

Adversarial review of today's diff (`fe6b12f..e7bd471`, 3 files, +60/−4) against the six classes. **Path resolution** — no `../` chain, no `path.join(__dirname, …)`, nothing under `src/hooks/`, so no installed-depth question and no `checksums.sha256` regeneration; `verify_repo.py` agrees. **Referenced but not shipped** — no new file at all; both changes are to files already in their packages, so there is nothing to add to an installer list, an npm `files` array or the plugin layout. **Windows** — no shell or PowerShell script touched, so statusline `SESSIONS_DIRNAME`/`SESSION_ID_RE` parity is untouched; the new matcher is byte-length-then-ASCII-digit, so a multi-byte rune cannot false-match (it fails the `len == 8` byte check or the digit range) and there is no encoding, CRLF or path handling in either file; `t.diagnostic` has existed since Node 16.17, below every version this repo runs. **Destructive writes** — nothing writes `settings.json`, `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md` or a user rule file; the Go change only reads a decoded body. **Silent fail-open** — the pricing gate is the direction that matters here and it still fails *closed*: `tokenOnlyProviderTool` returns true only for `advisor_` plus an eight-digit stamp on `anthropic`, so every unrecognised shape stays unpriced rather than mispriced, which is why the dated-stamp bound was chosen over a bare `advisor` prefix. The test change cannot pass vacuously: `linkage` dereferences `.aborted` on both calls, so a dropped signal on one side throws rather than comparing equal, and the pre-existing `instanceof` equality assertion above it still runs. **Claim drift** — nothing shipped changed, no README, `INSTALL.md`, benchmark, eval or percentage touched (checked by grep); grepped `docs/`, `README.md` and `INSTALL.md` for `unsupported_provider_tool_charge`, `tokenOnlyProviderTool` and `pricing_known` and found no documentation stating the old behaviour, so there is nothing to correct.

# Daily triage — 2026-11-04

Ninth run on this branch. A `daily-triage/` PR was still open, so today appended to it. **Nothing was force-pushed** — seven new commits on top of `4f4c856`, in two fast-forward pushes (`4f4c856..8c805e5`, then `8c805e5..fe6b12f`). `origin/main` is unchanged at `2e068f73` and `git merge-tree` reports this head merges clean into it, so no rebase was taken.

**Four fixes, three of them from issues filed since the last run, one adopted from a contributor.** Every genuinely new actionable item was closed out; what is left on the new-items list is one canary needing a framework install this container does not have, one claim the reporter withdrew themselves, and the drift bot re-firing against a decision that is still yours.

**The `2026-10-31` run section was condensed into the shared condensed block below**, the same way `2026-10-29`/`2026-10-28` were on 11-03 and `2026-10-27`/`2026-10-26` were on 10-31. The body was at 53,855 of GitHub's 65,536 characters; today's section fits without condensing anything, but leaving it at ~60k would force the next run to condense under pressure. Nothing is lost: every commit is still on the branch with its full reasoning in its commit message (`git log origin/main..HEAD`), each issue carries that run's own triage comment, and the previous full text is in this description's edit history.

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1457 | `proxyYamlMode()` read the proxy's mode with `/^\s*mode\s*:/m`. Under `/m`, `^` matches the start of **every** line and `\s*` eats the indentation, so the pattern meant "`mode:` at any depth", not "the top-level key". `caveman.yaml` legitimately carries a second, nested one — `middleware.mode` — and the proxy resolves keys by **name** (yaml.v3), so the two read one file differently in both directions: a nested-only mode was adopted as the proxy's, and a nested key written *above* a real top-level one won on textual order | `caveman start` / `wrapRuntimeConfig` on every host and OS, for any `caveman.yaml` carrying a `middleware:` block | `capability-config.runtime.mjs` — all three spellings, observed through `CAVE_ENGINE_TOON` | — |
| #1459 | The repaste miner segmented **every** text payload in a transcript turn, so context the host and caveman's own hook re-inject each session (Claude Code's `CLAUDE.md`/auto-memory system-reminder, the SessionStart ruleset) came back as `recurring_context:repaste:*` findings telling the user they had pasted it again in N sessions, with `fix_kind` `cavemem_offload` | `caveman learn` on every source (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, pi, aider); reported on Claude Code / macOS | new `proxy/internal/store/recurring_test.go` — exclusion, the locator-index contract, a human block that *quotes* injected text, plus a predicate table | — |
| #1458 | `forward_headers` is a **compat-mount** contract (`CompatConfig`, validated by `openaicompat.ValidateForwardHeaders`). `ProviderConfig` never declared it and yaml.v3 drops keys a struct does not declare, so `providers.<name>.forward_headers` parsed into nothing: no error, no log line, no forwarding — the operator saw only upstream 401s while the file on disk said otherwise | `caveman-proxy` config load, every host and OS | `config_test.go` — refusal across three providers, the remedy it points at loads, an ordinary `base_url`-only override still loads | — |
| *(no issue filed)* | A GFM cell writes a literal pipe as `\|`. `parseMarkdownTable` split rows on every pipe, giving that row an extra cell, so the table failed the column check. `LooksTabular` calls the same parser, so the real symptom was one step earlier than "uncompressed": `Detect` returned **`text`** and handed the payload to the prose compressor | `caveman-engine` on every host and OS, WASM build included | adopted author's `tabular_test.go` case, plus a new `engine/detect_test.go` case pinning the routing | **#1456** (adopted, authorship preserved) |

A fifth commit is review fallout, not a new fix: adversarial review of the #1459 guard found that its hook-result rule (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\s+hook\s+(success|…)`, case-insensitive, no trailing colon) also matched an ordinary English sentence whose first word happens to precede the words "hook success" — *"The hook success path is the one I care about"* was classed as injected and silenced. That is exactly the trade the anchoring exists to avoid, so the rule now requires the host's own spelling: capitalised event name, lower-case verb, trailing colon. The table test states the contract and pins both spellings that must not match.

### Scope note on #1457, stated rather than quietly skipped

Anchoring the regex makes the CLI read the key the proxy reads. It does **not** close the reporter's scenario A, and the commit says so. That divergence has a different cause: `think.mode` defaults to `compress` in the CLI (`CAPABILITY_DEFAULTS`) while `config.Load()` normalizes a file with no top-level mode to `record`. Making them agree is a default change with its own blast radius — it would turn toon off for every `caveman start` with no `caveman.yaml` — and is listed below as yours.

# Original description (mem/supersede follow-ups to #1394) — unchanged, still needs review

## Why this is a separate PR

#1394 was merged at 07:57Z. Devin Review's findings on it landed at 07:56Z and I had not finished verifying them, so **main now carries a silent data-loss bug** and these fixes never reached it. A merged PR cannot track follow-up work, so this is a new PR rather than more commits on the old branch.

**Main is affected right now**, not just in theory:

```
$ git show origin/main:mem/js/index.mjs | sed -n '44,45p'
export function supersede(id, text) {
  return call(["supersede", id, "--stdin"], text);     # unconditional
$ git show origin/main:mem/cmd/cavemem/main.go | grep -c supersede-stdin
0                                                       # no capability to check
```

## The bug

A cavemem build predating `supersede --stdin` reads supersede's **second argument as the replacement text**. The JS/Python clients and `caveman mem` shell out to a *separately installed* binary, so a client newer than the binary on PATH is an ordinary state, not an exotic one. I built cavemem from `afb5d18~1` and ran main's client against it:

```
supersede returned: {"id":"mem_06cc…","supersedes":"mem_a66a…"}   # exit 0, reported success
recall "deploy key"  -> []                                        # the fact is GONE
history -> 'the deploy key lives in vault…'  EXPIRED
           '--stdin'                          CURRENT
```

Exit 0, the real memory expired, the literal string `--stdin` stored as the current fact. That breaks `mem/CLAUDE.md`'s own **"byte-safe write — a memory is never lost"** invariant.

## The fix, in two rounds

**It took two review rounds to get right, and the second round found more data loss — worth knowing before merging.** `777bb73` introduced the capability gate; `b30e90b` fixes two regressions that gate itself introduced.

`version --json` now advertises `supersede-stdin`. A replacement goes over stdin — and therefore requires that capability, refusing before any write without it — when **any** of three things holds, because each makes argv unsafe for a different reason:

| Condition | Why argv cannot carry it |
| --- | --- |
| over the platform argv limit (96 KiB; 24 KiB on Windows) | Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, Windows whole-command-line cap — the original #1385 case |
| exactly `--stdin` | the binary reads it as the **flag** and fills the text from *its* stdin, which `subprocess` lets it inherit from the caller |
| contains a NUL | no OS can pass a NUL in an argument at all |

Everything else takes the argv form, which every build reads correctly. The size threshold is platform-aware on purpose: one conservative number would have regressed Linux texts between ~24 KB and ~128 KB that work today.

**What round two caught (`b30e90b`), both regressions of my own round-one fix:**

```
$ printf 'TOTALLY UNRELATED PIPED DATA' | python3 repro.py    # supersede(id, "--stdin")
  text='the deploy key lives in vault under ops/deploy'  EXPIRED
  text='TOTALLY UNRELATED PIPED DATA'                     CURRENT     # ← stored the piped bytes

JS FAILED on NUL: ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE | args[2] must be a string without null bytes
PY FAILED on NUL: ValueError | embedded null byte
```

The first is silent wrong-data storage (JS closed stdin and failed loudly instead); the second made `supersede` the one operation unable to store what `remember` accepts, since `remember` always pipes. Both probes **fail closed** — an unreadable `version` answers "no".

Verified against binaries built either side of the change: the old one stores small replacements correctly and refuses what it cannot carry with the memory intact; a current one stores a 200 KB replacement, a literal `--stdin`, and NUL-bearing bytes over stdin. Invariant documented in `mem/CLAUDE.md`.

**Checked and deliberately unchanged:** `caveman mem supersede <id> -- --stdin` is safe. `execFileSync` pipes an empty stdin rather than inheriting, so the binary refuses with `cannot supersede with empty text` and the memory is left intact — verified, the original was still CURRENT afterwards.

## Also here

**`2c7c4a9` — `Remember` stayed broken for a reverted fact.** After A→B→A, `memID(A)` names A's expired row, so `Remember(A)` failed with *"exists only as an expired historical version"* — false once a current row holds that text, since Recall returns it. Only reachable because #1394 made the revert storable, so it is a regression that shipped with it. `Remember` now returns the current row with identical text without reviving the expired one; a fact that really exists only as history is still refused.

**`230648e` — consistency only, and not reproduced.** `journaledMcpTargetsExist` walked every journaled operation while the ownership checks beside it filter `claudeProfileGone` first. I could not construct a sequence where that changes the verdict (both `enable` and `doctor --fix` drop a gone profile's operations — probe output is on the #1394 thread), so this is an alignment, not a fix. Kept because it cannot mask a real failure and leaving one helper inconsistent is a trap; **drop this commit if you'd rather not carry unreproduced changes** — the other three stand alone.

## Worth a separate decision

This repo already institutionalises exactly this bug class — `middleware-conformance.yml` runs **skew / HEAD clients vs published runtime** and **skew / published clients vs HEAD runtime**, and both passed on #1394 *and* on this PR's first head while the bug was live. They cover the middleware clients against the proxy runtime; there is no equivalent for the **cavemem client ↔ binary** pair, which is the one that broke.

My own verification has the same shape of hole: I tested against a real pre-change binary, which is how round one's bug surfaced, but only with ordinary replacement text — never with an input that collides with the flag, which is the one value the design makes special. That is why round two existed.

The cheapest honest CI version: build `cavemem` at the previous release tag, run the current `mem/js` and `mem/py` suites against it, and assert every command either behaves or refuses — never silently misreads an argument. Not building that lane here (new job, maintainer's call, and this PR already carries four fixes); the new `supersede-stdin` capability at least gives it something concrete to assert.

title: fix: protect provider cache and runtime lifecycle
body:
Provider cache prefixes and active requests could change or disappear during cache pressure, configuration changes, transient OpenCode hints, and process shutdown. This patch preserves tested cache decisions, forwards supported provider traffic, fixes recovery-store races and limits, and makes release publication depend on a native-platform reliability matrix.

Changes are split into focused, DCO-signed commits:

- Keep warm raw/compressed/Pixel decisions for the documented retention window; replay existing TOON decisions after disabling new compression; preserve signed Gemini parts and opaque provider metadata.
- Relay Anthropic token exchange and workspace selection, escaped Bedrock ARN paths, and native OpenAI Responses WebSockets. Abort truncated responses visibly, close upgraded peers on shutdown, and drain accepted HTTP requests on first stop.
- Reapply SQLite budgets on replacement connections, guard failed-migration cleanup, and serialize deduplication/budget decisions. Twelve concurrent writers now retain one map payload.
- Persist OpenCode prompt guidance in admitted history. Disable its two ephemeral per-tool advisory hints with an explicit decision reason; execution, compression, and recovery stay available. Fix launcher signal forwarding and mixed-version plugin selection.
- Bound installer downloads and Python usage buffers; exclude documented bad LiteLLM versions from fresh extra installs; regenerate runtime pins.
- Add a reusable macOS/Linux/Windows reliability workflow and require it before binary/package release builds.

Validation (local fixtures, including subtests):
- Integrated Engine/proxy/provider/store/runtime: 2,967 passed, 24 documented skips.
- Gateway/provider race suite: 1,682 passed; CCR race: 97 passed; native-runtime race: 80 passed.
- CLI: 1,469 passed, 6 skips on the frozen source.
- Pi extension: 147 passed.
- Installer: 511 passed, 3 skips.
- Installed Python middleware wheel: 188 passed, 264 optional-framework skips; focused usage/dependency tests: 37 passed with no skips.
- Go vet, repository verification, generators, and actionlint passed.

[Full audit, official provider/host sources, and 44-issue/52-PR inventory](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/codex/runtime-maintenance/docs/technical/maintenance-audit-2026-10-25.md) records proof and remaining leads. The inventory was complete for open items at audit time; this does not approve every existing PR diff.

All eight pull-request workflows passed at `e31ddbe749a55749cd938c1274885b4af1c84695`, including [the new Ubuntu/macOS/Windows reliability gate](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/actions/runs/40180538795) and [the full Engine workflow with its Windows job](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/actions/runs/40180538742). This remains a draft for review. Native Windows console execution, actual OpenCode persisted replay, live provider cache hits, and completed-task savings remain unproven. HTTP/WebSocket history transitions are not cache-equivalent; warm cache retention can increase disk use; pre-existing corrupt/full stores and #1279's long-lived runtime report remain open. No release, merge, paid provider call, or issue closure is included.

title: Codex analytics: completed SSE cancellation loses counters; fresh practice findings return HTTP 500
body:
## Summary

Two independently reproduced problems prevent useful numeric analytics for an existing Codex desktop installation:

1. Cloud rejects a freshly computed practice finding with HTTP 500.
2. The local 4.0.1 subscription proxy drops usage/compression counters after Codex receives a complete `response.completed` event and closes the stream.

Environment: Windows, Codex desktop (Store/MSIX), Caveman CLI/proxy 4.0.1; Cloud CLI updated from 0.1.0-rc.29 to 0.1.0-rc.35. The updated CLI passes the server-contract compatibility check. OpenAI subscription identity and local compression must remain unchanged; no paid gateway migration is requested.

## Cloud: minimal failure with current typed client

After recomputing a fresh local report with `caveman learn --since 1d --sources codex --repo <local-repository-filter> --json`, both the standard `caveman sync` and the current typed `fixes.submit_practice_findings` operation fail.

The typed operation was reduced to **one real finding** with:
- registered practice ID `prompt-prefix-stability`;
- basis `inferred`;
- integer tokens_per_turn, tokens_per_day_rate, sessions_scanned;
- a valid observed_at timestamp from the fresh report;
- the original generated sink_id.

Actual: HTTP 500, `cave_practice_findings_write_failed`.
- server request ID: `01a17282-6820-783f-9edf-127608a19f9f`
- typed operation envelope request ID: `ba2043bd-99ca-409f-9528-b4e136c4e4d8`
- another fresh standard-sync request ID: `01a1726f-7401-7f03-9c89-a7496b30576c`

Expected: metadata accepted, or a specific validation error if a field is invalid. No model/eval execution was involved in this reproduction. Historical numeric span import succeeded separately; that is not evidence that this lane works.

## Local proxy: completed Codex stream classified as cancellation

In pinned tag `v4.0.1`, `proxy/internal/gateway/chatgpt.go` installs `chatGPTSSECompletionReader` only for `rc.AgentSlug == "pi"`. Codex follows the same Responses protocol, but does not get the terminal-delivery check.

An isolated full-handler regression uses:
- POST `/chatgpt/responses`, x-cave-agent: codex, stream:true;
- a fixture upstream that supplies:
```
event: response.completed
data: {"type":"response.completed","response":{"usage":{"input_tokens":111,"output_tokens":22}}}

```
- a ResponseWriter which cancels the request context **after successfully writing the complete frame**;
- the upstream reader then returns context.Canceled.

On the original 4.0.1 source:
```
SSE_canceled_after_delivery:
  completed usage lost: code=cave_client_canceled tokens=0/0
mislabeled_SSE_canceled_after_delivery:
  completed usage lost: code=cave_client_canceled tokens=0/0
```

The second case uses application/json Content-Type for the actual SSE payload. Both cases lose compression before/after counters too. These are deterministic fixtures, not an inference from a similar issue or a claimed production root cause for every missing row.

## Candidate fix and safeguards verified locally

Reuse the existing terminal-delivery tracker for explicitly requested Responses streams, including Codex. For a successful stream request with a non-SSE header, inspect a bounded, non-consuming body prefix (`event:`, `data:`, or SSE comment `:`) before classifying it as SSE. Do not treat a genuine JSON response as SSE solely because stream:true was requested.

Preserve existing passthrough of unknown events on requests without a stream flag; making every SSE-header response enforce a terminal event broke the existing `TestProviderStreamsFlushBeforeCompletion/chatgpt` test, so that broader change was rejected.

Verified after the scoped change:
- completed terminal frame followed by cancellation retains 111/22 usage and compression counts;
- early cancellation, partial terminal write, and provider error do not claim successful compression savings;
- genuine JSON response remains byte-exact;
- OAuth header remains unchanged;
- subscription USD cost/savings remain zero, never guessed from catalog prices;
- full `go test ./proxy/internal/gateway ./proxy/providers/openai -count=1` passes with **CGO enabled**, including the TypeScript compression release-shape test;
- separate-port startup, compression, exact MCP recovery, duplicate-listener refusal and graceful shutdown pass.

The candidate is prepared but **not deployed to the working proxy**: installation refused to interrupt active connections. No historical records were rewritten.

Please investigate the Cloud persistence failure and advise on accepting the protocol-level accounting fix upstream. No end-user prompts, source code, keys, organization IDs or local paths are attached.

title: Native Unix IPC fails when CAVEMAN_HOME makes native.sock too long
body:
**What happen**

The native runtime uses `<CAVEMAN_HOME>/run/native.sock` directly. A valid, long data-directory path exceeds the Unix socket pathname limit: the HTTP proxy starts, but native IPC does not. Native hooks exit successfully without a runtime response.

The proxy logs `native runtime unavailable; hooks remain fail-open`, with `native runtime listen: ... bind: invalid argument` on the tested Linux host. This is not a claim that provider routing stops.

Source: [`SocketPath` / `ServeUnix`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/proxy/internal/nativeruntime/server_unix.go#L15-L56), [fast hook endpoint](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/native-hook-fast.ts#L369-L398).

**Expected**

Keep native IPC usable with long data-directory paths, or report the unsupported socket-path length explicitly with an actionable diagnostic. Preserve hook fail-open behavior, private socket permissions and isolation between homes.

**Before/after example**

1. Start `caveman-proxy serve` with a fresh writable `CAVEMAN_HOME`, a free loopback `CAVEMAN_LISTEN`, and `CAVEMAN_MODE=compress`.
2. Set `CAVEMAN_NATIVE_MODE=safe`, `CAVEMAN_NATIVE_PROFILE=full-safe` and `CAVEMAN_CORE=true`. Pass a Pi `PostToolUse` event (`session_id: "path-probe"`, `tool_name: "Read"`, `cwd` set to the working directory) to `bun packages/cli/src/native-hook-fast.ts pi`. Use `tool_input.file_path` pointing to `sample.txt` in that directory and `tool_response.content` containing 1,000 newline-terminated `repeated output` lines.
3. Repeat with a longer physical `CAVEMAN_HOME`, keeping the mode, profile, binaries and event unchanged. Allocate a free loopback port for each run. Measure the complete socket path in bytes.

| Socket path | HTTP listener | Native socket | Native hook response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 bytes | Available | Created | Protocol JSON with `recovery_ref` |
| 182 bytes | Available | Absent | Empty stdout, exit 0 |

Both cases used fresh stores; loopback ports were allocated independently. No host session or provider API call was needed.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Linux x86_64; native runtime / Pi hook transport. Darwin not executed.

**Version / install method**

Published proxy `bin-v4.0.1`, invoked directly without a package wrapper; artifact SHA256 `ix3A6buol6uox0ma/7djmY6apYKR3EuqbOqBi/GDnVk=`. CLI source at `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, run with Bun 1.4.2. No downstream patches.

Related: [#1279](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/issues/1279) concerns an existing socket accepting requests and returning empty replies. Here the socket cannot bind at all.

AI-assisted investigation and drafting; reproductions executed locally.

title: Statusline setup suggestion expands literal dollar signs in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
body:
**What happen**

The SessionStart hook emits a statusline setup command as `bash "${scriptPath}"`. A literal `$NAME` in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is expanded when the suggested command runs, even though the copied script exists at the literal path. The suggested badge setup therefore fails.

Source: [`caveman-activate.js:590–595`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js#L590-L595). `JSON.stringify(command)` escapes JSON, not shell interpolation.

**Expected**

Shell-quote the literal script path before serializing the suggested command. Keep detection of user-authored shell-expanded statusline commands unchanged. Normal installer registrations are not implicated.

**Before/after example**

1. Use a fresh physical `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` containing the literal directory component `$CAVEMAN_PATH_SEGMENT`; leave that environment variable unset.
2. Set `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=caveman`. Run the unmodified `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` with a SessionStart payload (`source: "startup"`, a valid `session_id`), no configured statusline and no existing nudge marker.
3. Parse the emitted `statusLine.command` JSON and run that exact command through `/bin/sh -c`, passing the same session ID on stdin.

```text
Input: suggested command containing /.../$CAVEMAN_PATH_SEGMENT/claude/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh
Got:   variable segment disappears; bash reports No such file or directory; exit 127
Want:  execute the existing literal-path script and display [CAVEMAN]
```

Control: an ordinary config path displays the badge. Invoking the same copied dollar-path script directly as a Bash argument also succeeds. All SessionStart invocations exit 0; the failure is the emitted setup command, not activation.

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

Unmodified checkout at `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, Linux x86_64, Node v26.12.1. Executed the real SessionStart hook and emitted command in isolated profiles; no live Claude session or downstream patch used.

AI-assisted investigation and drafting; reproductions executed locally.
