title: Support safe, optional cooperation with TokenSave
body:
## Problem

When both projects are used, Caveman instructions can overlap with semantic code
research, while input and catalog compression may alter information TokenSave
provides. Users need optional cooperation that preserves exact tool results and
keeps installation, session availability, and activation distinct.

## Proposed scope

1. Pin both upstream revisions. Inspect Caveman skills, behavior modifiers,
   Cavecrew, agent integrations, compression entrypoints, catalog shrinking, and
   routing alongside TokenSave instructions, schemas, responses, and indexing
   readiness. Record supported interfaces and gaps before changing behavior.
2. Update Caveman-owned instructions to prefer targeted semantic queries when
   appropriate tools are available in the session and the project is indexed.
   Avoid redundant broad exploration or Cavecrew research after sufficient
   evidence. Explicit user instructions take precedence. Preserve exact code,
   identifiers, paths, signatures, errors, numbers, and semantic relationships.
3. Add a configurable general tool-result preservation policy using existing
   configuration and CLI conventions. Resolve identity from protocol tool calls
   and results, including verified agent naming formats. Never match result prose
   or infer server identity from an ambiguous name.
4. Apply preservation before every applicable lossy transformation, including
   downstream compression or elision paths discovered during the audit. Define
   exact content preservation separately from transport JSON serialization.
   Recovery handles alone do not satisfy this requirement.
5. Audit catalog shrinking separately. Provide description preservation where
   selection or argument guidance could be lost. Preserve names, schemas,
   parameters, constraints, and defaults; structural equality alone does not
   establish equivalent tool selection.
6. Report enabled mechanisms, protected identities, unsupported protocols,
   ambiguous identities, invalid settings, and conflicts without logging payloads.
   Document conservative behavior when identity cannot be established; never
   claim protection for such cases without a tested safe fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Source-pinned interface matrix distinguishes verified support from gaps.
- [ ] TokenSave absent, unavailable, unindexed, and removed retain normal behavior.
- [ ] Available indexed tools receive suitable targeted queries; unrelated
      delegation, models, providers, and routing remain unchanged.
- [ ] Interleaved tool calls resolve to the correct results for each supported
      protocol; ambiguous, malformed, and unsupported cases have diagnostics.
- [ ] Mixed requests preserve protected content exactly while unrelated content
      still receives normal compression. Test every applicable lossy path.
- [ ] Fixtures include JSON, source snippets, identifiers, paths, signatures,
      errors, numbers, and semantic relationships, including nested content.
- [ ] Catalog tests cover preserved descriptions and unchanged schemas,
      constraints, defaults, and tool names.
- [ ] Configuration examples use implemented options, with reproducible commands
      and relevant passing tests, lint, and formatting checks recorded.
- [ ] Correctness evidence is separate from reproducible A/B measurements:
      TokenSave alone versus TokenSave plus Caveman, using input/output tokens,
      MCP calls, redundant reads, independently verified task success, latency,
      and cost per successful task. Missing telemetry or billing is explicit.

## Boundaries

No automatic TokenSave installation, mandatory dependency, TokenSave-owned
configuration edits, extra proxy, endpoint replacement, model/provider switching,
or TokenSave public MCP contract changes. TokenSave cannot be assumed to set
headers on an agent's model requests. Begin with the smallest verified protocol
and expand only with evidence. No synthetic savings or unsupported percentages.

Companion: TokenSave issue https://github.com/aovestdipaperino/tokensave/issues/797
and draft PR https://github.com/aovestdipaperino/tokensave/pull/800. Caveman owns
the proxy and catalog preservation controls; TokenSave remains independently managed.

title: feat: preserve configured semantic tool results and catalogs
body:
## Problem and behavior

Tool-result compression can elide semantic information already retrieved by
TokenSave. Configured tools now bypass adapter rewrite candidates, including
cached substitutions, while unrelated results retain ordinary compression.
Caveman also prefers suitable semantic queries when session tools and an indexed
project are available, and reuses sufficient findings before repeating research.

## Changes

- Add `preserve_tools` to existing proxy YAML and the JSON-array environment
  override `CAVEMAN_PRESERVE_TOOLS`. Validate exact-name and final-prefix wildcard
  rules. Empty arrays disable the policy; malformed rules refuse startup.
- Correlate Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, and OpenAI Responses/custom-tool results using
  protocol call IDs. Gemini uses the response's protocol tool name. Configured
  results and unresolved identities bypass compression and replacement lookup.
- Report configured rules and per-request matched names, protected/unresolved
  counts, ambiguity, and unsupported protocols without payloads.
- Add catalog-shrinker library/CLI policy preserving complete matching MCP/OpenAI
  tool envelopes, descriptions, and schemas. Lint applies the same policy.
- Disable pixel rendering and proxy catalog annotation stripping while policy is
  configured; these paths lack the general identity-aware preservation mechanism.
- Update voice/Cavecrew/investigation instructions and regenerate delivery files
  from canonical sources. Document configuration, scope, and verification.

Example:

```yaml
preserve_tools: ['mcp__tokensave__*', 'tokensave_*']
```

Tools are not automatically discovered or installed. The integration does not
change endpoints, models, providers, unrelated delegation, or MCP contracts.

## Validation

Passed Go tests and vet across the policy, all provider adapters, compressor,
shrinker, config, gateway, and standalone packages. Tests include interleaving,
mixed payloads, both bare and qualified names, custom calls, malformed rules,
exact serialized payload preservation, and a cached-elision regression.

Registry compilation, rule-copy tests, full local repository verification,
formatting, and whitespace checks passed. The repository verification included
regenerated plugin mirrors and the skill archive. See the
[consolidated validation record](https://github.com/atontini/caveman/blob/feat/tokensave-cooperation/docs/drafts/tokensave-cooperation/README.md) for commands and related PR status.

## Limits

Policy applies to supported model protocol envelopes, not arbitrary raw Engine
inputs. Unknown naming formats require explicit rules and verification. Start a
fresh session after changing policy. Pixel mode conservatively passes through;
Gemini catalog shrinking is unsupported and currently leaves its envelope alone.

No live A/B performance trials were run. TokenSave's existing benchmark runner
supplies a protocol, but actual telemetry, independently scored agent tasks, and
billing remain pending. Recovery is not unchanged delivery, and schema equality
does not prove equivalent tool selection. This PR is prepared for draft review and remains unmerged.

Refs #1403

Companion: https://github.com/aovestdipaperino/tokensave/pull/800 (Refs its issue #797).

title: Hermes native enable writes invalid YAML (model block above %YAML, plugin list indented 4 spaces)
body:
**What happen**

`caveman setup --agents hermes` (native wiring, CLI 4.0.1) rewrites `~/.hermes/config.yaml` into a document no YAML parser accepts. Two independent defects in the bundled `dist/index.js`:

1. `hermesNativeConfig` inserts a new section with `lines.unshift("model:")` (~line 10034). When the config starts with `%YAML 1.1` / `---` — which is what Hermes itself writes — the block lands **before** the directive:

```
model:
  # >>> caveman:native-hermes-routing
  provider: "custom"
  base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1"
  # <<< caveman:native-hermes-routing
%YAML 1.1
---
```

`yaml.safe_load` then fails with `ComposerError: expected a single document in the stream`.

2. The plugin entry is inserted with a fixed four-space indent (~line 10072) inside an `enabled:` list whose siblings use two spaces:

```
plugins:
  enabled:
    # >>> caveman:native-hermes-plugin
    - caveman_native
    # <<< caveman:native-hermes-plugin
  - herdr-agent-state
```

`ParserError: expected <block end>, but found -`.

After the file is broken, caveman cannot repair it: `caveman doctor hermes --fix` answers `Hermes routing block changed after enable; refusing destructive disable`. Deleting the journal and re-running setup reports `existing Hermes Caveman native block is unjournaled` or `plugins/caveman_native/plugin.yaml already exists`. The only way out is hand-editing the YAML.

**Expected**

- A new section is inserted after the document start markers (`%YAML`, `---`).
- A list entry takes the indentation of its siblings.
- `doctor --fix` re-adds a block that disappeared instead of refusing: there is nothing destructive to protect when the block is gone.

**Before/after example**

```
Input:  %YAML 1.1\n---\nplatforms:\n  telegram:\n    enabled: false\nplugins:\n  enabled:\n  - herdr-agent-state\n_config_version: 52\n
Got:    model: …prepended above %YAML… ; plugin entry at 4 spaces  -> unparsable
Want:   model: inserted after --- ; plugin entry at 2 spaces        -> parses
```

Patched writer (insert after the markers, reuse the sibling indent) produces a document that parses, with `model: {provider: custom, base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/hermes/v1}` and `plugins: [caveman_native, herdr-agent-state]`.

**Platform**

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Hermes Agent (native routing + plugin + MCP wiring)

**Version / install method**

`@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1, installed through the Nix package (absolute store paths resolved to profile paths). The two writer defects are not Nix-specific: they depend only on the config shape Hermes generates (`%YAML` directive plus two-space list items).

title: Wrap support for Mistral Vibe
body:
**What you want**

I want `caveman wrap vibe` to send Mistral Vibe traffic through the proxy, so that the proxy can compress it, and Vibe keeps the Mistral models.

Issue #264 asked for Mistral Vibe support. It was closed as complete with the `mistral-vibe` row in the installer (`installer/install.js:285`). That row detects the `vibe` or `mistral` command and installs the Caveman skills through `npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -a mistral-vibe`. The skills work, but the proxy does not see Vibe traffic. `caveman wrap` has no `vibe` profile, and `caveman run -- vibe` passes the traffic through to `api.mistral.ai` without changes.

A pure profile pull request cannot add this support. Three small core changes are necessary. I propose them below. I can send the pull request after a maintainer decides the points in "Decisions for the maintainers".

Versions: caveman 4.0.1, Mistral Vibe 3.0.2 on Linux. The line references are for `main` at `b4531dfc`.

**Before/after example**

```
Before: caveman wrap vibe    -> no such agent
        caveman run -- vibe  -> requests go direct to api.mistral.ai
After:  caveman wrap vibe    -> requests go to /w/vibe/compat/mistral/v1
```

**Why good**

This change lets the proxy route Vibe traffic, as it routes the traffic of the other agents. Vibe keeps its own models, so this is not a model swap like the Qwen profile.

This proposal does not prove compression or savings for Vibe. The recorder test below proves that Vibe accepts the provider override and sends a chat request. It does not prove that the proxy keeps the full Mistral request, or that Vibe can recover compressed content. The tests in the "Tests" section must show that before the feature claims savings.

## Decisions for the maintainers

I need a decision from a Caveman maintainer on these four points before I write code. Under `docs/CONTRIBUTING_PROFILES.md`, changes 1 to 3 are core changes, not profile changes. Decision 1 changes a compiler allowlist, so it needs founder review.

1. Array root in `config-env-content` (change 1). Can `config_content.local` and `config_content.managed` be a non-empty array? If not, tell me which method you prefer for `VIBE_PROVIDERS`.
2. Built-in `mistral` compat mount (change 2). Can the proxy ship this mount, as it ships `opencode-go`? If not, each user must add the mount in `~/.caveman/caveman.yaml`, and the profile cannot depend on it.
3. Refusal of managed routing (change 3). If a `config-env-content` profile has no `managed` content, can `buildWrapEnv` refuse managed routing? Today it falls back to `local`. No shipped profile changes, but the meaning of an absent `managed` value changes for future profiles.
4. Shape of the pull request. Do you want one pull request, or one pull request for each change and one for the profile? The profile depends on all three changes.

## How Vibe can point at the proxy

Vibe has no `*_BASE_URL` variable. But Vibe reads its configuration from `VIBE_*` environment variables through pydantic-settings, with JSON values for complex fields (`vibe/core/config/layers/environment.py`). Thus `VIBE_PROVIDERS` can replace the list of providers for one run.

I tested this with Vibe 3.0.2 and a recorder on `127.0.0.1`:

```shell
MISTRAL_API_KEY=fake \
VIBE_PROVIDERS='[{"name":"mistral","api_base":"http://127.0.0.1:18787/compat/mistral/v1","api_key_env_var":"MISTRAL_API_KEY","backend":"mistral"}]' \
vibe --trust -p "say hi" --max-turns 1
```

The recorder received this chat request:

```
POST /compat/mistral/v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer ...
body keys: messages, metadata, model, parallel_tool_calls, reasoning_effort, stream, temperature, tools
```

The request uses the OpenAI chat shape, so the profile can use `wire_protocol: openai-chat`.

Vibe also sends telemetry to `POST /v1/datalake/events` on the same host. It keeps the scheme and the host of `api_base`, but not the path. Thus the proxy receives these requests at its root. In my test, the recorder rejected them, and Vibe still sent the chat request.

The proxy already rejects these requests. `MatchRoute` in `proxy/providers/adapter.go:485` accepts only listed routes, and no provider lists this path. Thus the proxy does not forward the Mistral key to another upstream.

## Change 1: allow a list as the inline configuration

`config-env-content` is the correct method. `VIBE_PROVIDERS` passes `validateEnvVariableName`. But the compiler rejects a list as the root value (`agents/compile.mjs:320`):

```js
need(inj.config_content.local && typeof inj.config_content.local === "object" && !Array.isArray(inj.config_content.local), "injection.config_content.local is required");
```

The schema has the same limit (`agents/profiles/schema.json:64`, `"local": { "type": "object" }`). The compiler applies the same rule to `managed`.

The proposed change:

- Let `config_content.local` and `config_content.managed` be an object or a non-empty array, in the compiler and in the schema.
- Change only the validation of the root value. `validateConfigStrings` already reads arrays and validates each item.

In the schema, this form is sufficient:

```json
"local": { "type": ["object", "array"], "minItems": 1, "description": "..." }
```

JSON Schema applies `minItems` only to arrays. Thus the form accepts any object and any non-empty array, and it rejects an empty array and a scalar. The compiler check in `agents/compile.mjs` stays the gate that the build enforces.

`renderDeep` in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` already renders arrays, and `buildWrapEnv` serializes the result into the environment variable. The type in `agents.generated.ts` is already `unknown`. `collectInjectionModelIds` already reads arrays, and the Vibe profile pins no model. Thus I expect no change to the runtime. The existing profiles do not change.

## Change 2: a built-in compat mount for Mistral

The proxy has no Mistral upstream. Without one, a Vibe profile can only send Vibe to OpenAI models.

The proposed change adds one entry to `builtinCompat` in `proxy/internal/config/config.go`, next to `opencode-go`. Pull request #948 added `builtinCompat` and the `opencode-go` entry. This change uses the same pattern:

```go
"mistral": {BaseURL: "https://api.mistral.ai/v1", APIKeyEnv: "MISTRAL_API_KEY"},
```

The base URL does not double the `/v1` segment. `joinCompatPath` in `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat.go:104` removes the segments that the base path and the request path share. Thus the proxy sends `/compat/mistral/v1/chat/completions` to `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions`.

The proxy forwards the key of Vibe. Vibe sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and the proxy uses this inbound bearer token first (`proxy/internal/standalone/standalone.go:220`). The proxy reads `APIKeyEnv` only for a request without an `Authorization` header. Thus the proxy process does not need `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. The user sets `MISTRAL_API_KEY` for Vibe, because the profile names it in `api_key_env_var`.

Change 2 adds no entry to `packages/cli/src/modules/provider-logins.ts`. `packages/cli/tests/provider-logins.runtime.mjs:110` requires the CLI list to match `proxy/internal/pool/providers.json`. A saved Mistral login needs an entry in both registries and a test of the full route. That work can follow in a separate change.

A user can already add the same mount in `~/.caveman/caveman.yaml`. The built-in entry removes that manual step and lets the profile depend on the mount.

## Change 3: refuse managed routing when a profile has no managed configuration

Vibe has no provider field for an extra header such as `x-cave-upstream-key`. Thus the profile has no `managed` content and supports only local mode.

The current code does not enforce this. If `managed` is absent, `buildWrapEnv` uses `local` in managed mode too (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:12290`). The Vibe profile then points Vibe at a remote gateway, and Vibe sends `MISTRAL_API_KEY` to that gateway as its bearer token.

The proposed change is a data rule, not a check on the agent ID: if a `config-env-content` profile has no `managed` content, `buildWrapEnv` refuses managed routing. The Vibe profile stays declarative. Only two profiles use `config-env-content`, `kilo` and `opencode`, and both declare `managed`. Thus no shipped profile changes. But the rule changes the meaning of an absent `managed` value from a fallback to `local` into a refusal.

The error goes to the `catch` block in the caller (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:6854`). That block launches the agent directly with a warning. Thus Caveman does not inject a managed route that Vibe cannot use. The direct launch keeps the original routing of the user. It does not guarantee that Vibe sends traffic to `api.mistral.ai`. The cleanup at `packages/cli/src/index.ts:6869` removes only the variables in `WRAP_BASE_URL_ENV_VARS`, so an existing `VIBE_PROVIDERS` value stays active.

Change 3 also documents the rule in two places:

- The `managed` description in `agents/profiles/schema.json:65`.
- The `config-env-content` entry in `docs/technical/agent-profile-registry.md:61`.

## The profile

After changes 1, 2, and 3, the profile `agents/profiles/vibe.json` is pure JSON:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "id": "vibe",
  "display_name": "Mistral Vibe",
  "vendor": "Mistral AI",
  "homepage": "https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe",
  "binary_names": ["vibe"],
  "install": "uv tool install mistral-vibe==3.0.2",
  "wire_protocol": "openai-chat",
  "tested_agent_version": "3.0.2",
  "injection": {
    "method": "config-env-content",
    "env_var": "VIBE_PROVIDERS",
    "config_content": {
      "local": [
        {
          "name": "mistral",
          "api_base": "{{cave_base_url}}/compat/mistral/v1",
          "api_key_env_var": "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
          "backend": "mistral"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "injection_completeness": "declarative",
  "fallback": "generic-env",
  "maintainer": null
}
```

The provider keeps the name `mistral`, so the default Vibe models stay valid.

The proxy accepts the `/w/vibe/` prefix without a change. `SplitAgentPath` in `proxy/providers/agentpath.go:6` checks only the shape of the slug, and no list of known agents exists. The compiler requires `injection_completeness` (`agents/compile.mjs:398`).

The compiler also checks the version pin. A pinned `install` command must equal `tested_agent_version` (`checkProfileInstallPins` in `agents/compile.mjs`). Each shipped profile must have an entry in the `pinned-upstream-binary` matrix of `.github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml` (`checkConformancePins`). That job runs `node agents/probe-installed.mjs --require vibe`. The probe runs `vibe --version` and `vibe --help` in an isolated home, and both must exit with code 0. I did not yet run this probe for Vibe.

## Other files to change

The pull request will also change these files:

- `agents/agents.json` and `packages/cli/src/agents.generated.ts`, regenerated with `node agents/compile.mjs`, as `docs/CONTRIBUTING_PROFILES.md` requires.
- `.github/workflows/agent-conformance.yml`: a `vibe` entry in `pinned-upstream-binary` with `python -m pip install mistral-vibe==3.0.2`, and a `vibe` entry in `latest-drift-probe`, as for the other profiles.
- `docs/technical/agent-wrapping.md`: a row for Mistral Vibe in the table of wrapped agents.
- `README.md:259`: `vibe` in the list of agents for `caveman <agent>`.
- The schema and registry documentation from change 3.

Each commit of the pull request will carry a DCO sign-off.

## Tests

The pull request will add these tests:

- Profile compiler: accept an object root and a non-empty array root. Reject an empty array, a scalar root, an unknown template token, and a literal upstream URL inside an array. Also reject `{{cave_optional_openai_key_env}}` as an item of an array root. `renderDeep` throws for an array item that renders to nothing (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:7239`). The compiler already prevents this, because `optionalOpenAIKeyEnvPathAllowed` (`agents/compile.mjs:130`) accepts the template only at two object keys for Qwen and Kilo. The test makes sure that the new array root keeps this protection.
- Rendering: render the array into valid `VIBE_PROVIDERS` JSON with the attributed `/w/vibe/compat/mistral/v1` URL.
- Managed mode: refuse managed routing for a synthetic profile without `managed`, and keep its local behavior. Put this test next to the OpenCode managed test at `packages/cli/tests/wrap.runtime.mjs:689`. Keep the existing managed tests for OpenCode and Kilo (`packages/cli/tests/kilo-wrap.runtime.mjs:290`) unchanged.
- Direct fallback: when `VIBE_PROVIDERS` is not set, the direct launch sets no `VIBE_PROVIDERS`. When the user set `VIBE_PROVIDERS`, the direct launch keeps that value unchanged.
- Telemetry: the proxy rejects `POST /v1/datalake/events`. This test protects against a future catch-all route.
- Full route: send requests through the real proxy to a local test upstream, with the bearer token that Vibe sends. Make sure that the path, the model, the credentials, the Mistral-specific fields, streamed responses, and tool calls stay correct.
- Compression: send a large tool result and prove that Vibe can recover any content that the proxy removes. Until the full-route test and this test pass, the README and the docs describe the feature as routing support only.

## Limits

- Managed mode is not supported. Change 3 refuses it, and Vibe then starts directly with its own configuration.
- The mount works only with an API key. The browser login of Vibe does not use `api_base`.
- During a wrapped run, `VIBE_PROVIDERS` replaces the providers in `~/.vibe/config.toml`. Other providers of the user are not available in that run.
- If the user already set `VIBE_PROVIDERS`, the wrapped run replaces that value. The `opencode` profile merges an existing value, but the Vibe profile does not.
- I did not run `agents/probe-installed.mjs` for Vibe. If `vibe --version` or `vibe --help` needs a configuration or a login, the conformance job fails, and the probe needs a change.
- I did not test the full route through the proxy. My test used a recorder in place of the proxy. Compression and savings for Vibe are not proven.

title: Hermes: YAML reserialization loses native ownership despite unchanged routing, plugin and MCP values
body:
**What happen**

Native Hermes ownership depends on the exact comment-delimited YAML strings saved in the integration journal. Reserializing a valid configuration removes those comments and changes quoting/indentation, without changing its values. `caveman doctor hermes` then reports `degraded`; `doctor hermes --fix` and `disable hermes` refuse restoration. Native MCP registration detection also relies on the literal journaled block.

Observed on a live installation: YAML parses; provider, gateway URL, enabled `caveman_native` membership and enabled `caveman-native` MCP command still match the journal. All three marker blocks disappeared. The process which rewrote that live file is not established; PyYAML reserialization reproduces the layout change deterministically.

Source at `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, `packages/cli/src/index.ts`: `nativeIntegrationStatus`, `restoreNativeOperation` and `nativeMcpRegistered` compare Hermes blocks with `text.includes(...)`.

**Expected**

Recognize unchanged owned values after YAML normalization. Restore only the owned provider/base_url fields, plugin membership and MCP entry, preserving unrelated siblings and the journal's original values. Actual changes to owned values, duplicate keys and ambiguous shapes must still refuse destructive restoration. This is not a request to bypass the refusal for missing or user-edited routing.

**Before/after example**

After enabling native Hermes integration in an isolated home:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
p = Path(hermes_home) / "config.yaml"
before = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())
p.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(before))
assert yaml.safe_load(p.read_text()) == before
```

```text
Before reserialization: native configuration recognized.
After reserialization: values unchanged, markers gone; doctor reports degraded.
Want: unchanged ownership; safe disable restores only owned settings.
```

Normalization can also emit YAML-only escapes (`"caf\xE9"`) and fold a long executable path across lines. A JSON-string-only decoder or literal line matching is insufficient. Original `base_url: null` / empty endpoints must remain restorable.

A downstream fix was exercised on the real installed configuration without modifying its YAML or journal: ownership/routing/MCP recovery become healthy. Isolated probes also cover nullable endpoints, Unicode escapes and wrapped command paths. The downstream installed-runtime contract now passes: 19 Node tests plus three Python suites, including normalization, refusal of changed/ambiguous owned values, restoration and real MCP retrieval. The final Home Manager profile is activated; Hermes is recognized without modifying its configuration or journal. No real provider request or full Hermes session is claimed. Downstream PR: https://github.com/jerome-benoit/dotfiles/pull/271.

Separate from #1405 / #1395: those address writing invalid YAML, not ownership after a valid document is normalized.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Hermes Agent native integration

**Version / install method**

CLI 4.0.1 built from upstream commit `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, Nix packaging; companion runtime `bin-v4.0.2`. The literal-YAML ownership checks are upstream, not Nix-specific. Report and downstream investigation assisted by an AI coding agent.

title: fix(cursor): stop always injecting skill files from AGENTS.md
body:
## Summary

Cursor inlined four skill files from `AGENTS.md` on every turn in this repo. Commit, review, and compress are one-shot skills. Caveman is only needed while the mode is on. That input arrived before the task started, so a shorter reply could not pay it back.

## AS-IS

- `@` lines pulled `skills/caveman/SKILL.md`, `caveman-commit`, `caveman-review`, and `caveman-compress` on every turn: **3,747** tokens (`o200k_base` estimate).
- One controlled reply that also carried the full caveman skill plus the hook banner added **1,203** input tokens. Output fell **931 → 736** (**−195**, −20.9%). Net for that reply: **+1,008**.

Counts are tiktoken `o200k_base` estimates, not provider-billed tokens. The two prose replies used for the output comparison are not in this branch.

## TO-BE

- `AGENTS.md` no longer inlines those files. It tells the agent to load caveman only while the mode is on, and commit, review, or compress only when that task is asked.
- The file itself is **219** tokens (`o200k_base`).
- Claude Code already works this way: full ruleset once at session start or mode switch, then a **~90**-token `reinforcementForMode` reminder. The same reply under that billing model was **−105** net.

## Verified

- Diff is `AGENTS.md` only. No test referenced the old `@` lines. No hook checksum, changelog, or generated rule regen required.
- Token counts from one local `o200k_base` pass over the four skill files and the two prose replies (temporary test artifacts, not committed).

## Final result

Always-on injection of those four skills cost about **3,747** tokens per turn in this repo. Removing the `@` lines drops that cost. A **195**-token shorter reply did not offset always injecting the skill text on a single reply.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open this repo in Cursor with the new `AGENTS.md` and confirm the four skill bodies are not inlined from the rules file on ordinary turns.
- [ ] Invoke `/caveman-commit`, `/caveman-review`, or `/caveman-compress` when needed and confirm the matching skill still loads on demand.

title: Questions about ultracave (hello@caveman.so bounces)
body:
I sent these to hello@caveman.so, the address in TRADEMARKS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, and it bounced: "550 5.1.1 The email account that you tried to reach does not exist."

I use the ultracave voice with Claude Code on long math research projects. I only want the voice, not the rest of the package.

1. With the skill alone, the voice fades: answers start short and get longer after a few messages. Is there a recommended way to keep just the voice for a whole session?
2. Since I didn't know of one, I made ultracave into a Claude Code output style, which is sent with every request. Is that a sound approach, or would you expect it to fade too?
3. The style is in a small plugin I share with a few friends. It ships your Apache license and copyright notice and says it isn't affiliated with caveman. Following TRADEMARKS.md, I named it "terse". May I call it "ultracave"?

Thanks for caveman.

Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.61.0
Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

  • 2026-09-01 v1.58.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.53.4. It carries upstream's own fix for the journal-rollback data-corruption bug, so the local super-journal patch v1.56.0 introduced is dropped; recovery behavior is unchanged. Also bumps the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.6; as always, downstream modules must pin the same version this one does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).

body:
Updates the requirements on [chardet](https://github.com/chardet/chardet), [jsonpointer](https://github.com/stefankoegl/python-json-pointer), [pluggy](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy), [python-dateutil](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil), [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools) and [anthropic](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python) to permit the latest version. Updates `chardet` from 7.6.0 to 7.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from chardet's releases.

7.7.0

Big release: raising max_bytes to cover a huge input no longer makes detect() slow, every answer now decodes the window it was detected from, and markup declarations are read the way browsers read them. A lot of this came from new contributors, so thank you all!

Performance

  • Raising max_bytes on large inputs no longer gets slow. On compiled wheels, detect(data, max_bytes=len(data)) on 272 MiB takes about 0.2s for cp1252 and 0.5s for Shift_JIS, down from several seconds. UTF-8 validation and a final decode of the winner still read the whole window, and the other stages stop at a 256 KiB evidence cap (ADR-0006). The default 200 KB cap is still the fastest path, and default calls are unchanged.
  • The pure-Python wheel on CPython scores bigram models through operator.itemgetter instead of a Python loop, making detect() about 1.25x faster and detect_all() about 1.35x faster. (#404, thanks @​deadstrobe5)
  • Fixed three scans that went quadratic on hostile input: the UTF-7 + scan on line-wrapped base64 (128 KiB went from 5.4s to 1.2ms), unclosed <meta and <?xml tags in the markup scan, and the EBCDIC charset-declaration regex. (#403, thanks @​Samin061)

Bug Fixes

  • Every answer now decodes the examined window under the name you get back. BOMs, BOM-less UTF-16/32 null patterns, ISO-2022/HZ escapes, and <meta charset> declarations used to be trusted without decoding the rest of the window, so a confident answer could still raise further in. The 5.x/6.x display names (EUC-JP, SHIFT_JIS, Big5, ISO-2022-JP) are only used when those narrower codecs decode it too. (#394 and #396, thanks @​Samin061)
  • Markup declarations follow the WHATWG prescan: declarations inside comments are ignored, a charset= inside another attribute (like a refresh URL) no longer beats a real <meta charset>, quoted or spaced content charsets work, and an ASCII page declaring utf-16le no longer comes back as UTF-16-LE. (#389 and #398, thanks @​SashaMIT and @​xiehuanyi)
  • PEP 263 cookies resolve the way tokenize.detect_encoding resolves them, including only counting a line-2 cookie when line 1 is blank or a comment. (#391, thanks @​xiehuanyi)
  • Fixed BOM-bearing UTF-32 coming back as UTF-16 when max_bytes cuts a code unit. (#405, thanks @​AryanRG)
  • Fixed language labels on Unicode text tilting toward accent-heavy languages, so a French paragraph with a few accents no longer comes back as Hungarian. Mislabels on the test corpus's Unicode files dropped from 140 to 104.
  • Fixed a mostly-ASCII Windows-1252 file with a single Ö detecting as HP-Roman8, and English with a lone É detecting as MacRoman. (#383, thanks @​aadsm)
  • Fixed null-separated records like find -print0 output coming back as UTF-16-LE with Chinese as the language.
  • prefer_superset=True no longer swaps in a code page that can't decode the data, and now respects include_encodings/exclude_encodings. (#393, thanks @​00200200)
  • chardetect and UniversalDetector no longer mistake input cut exactly at the byte cap for the whole stream. (#392, thanks @​00200200)
  • lookup_encoding's cache is capped at 1024 entries, since charset names come from untrusted markup. (#390, thanks @​Samin061)
  • Plus smaller fixes to detect_all() ranking, EBCDIC XML MIME types, and the deprecated chardet.equivalences shim. The changelog has the full list.

Improvements

  • New -m/--mime-type flag for chardetect shows the MIME type next to the encoding, like file -i. (#384, thanks @​smi11 for the request)
  • Visual-order Hebrew is now detected, and cp864 Arabic is trained on contextually shaped text in visual order, the way real cp864 systems stored it.
  • EncodingInfo.is_multibyte is now is_multibyte_cjk. The old name still works with a DeprecationWarning and goes away in 8.0.
  • pipeline/markup.py is now compiled by mypyc (15 modules total), and CI enforces 100% test coverage.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/chardet/chardet/compare/7.6.0...7.7.0

Changelog

Sourced from chardet's changelog.

7.7.0 (2026-10-17)

Features:

  • Added a -m/--mime-type flag to the chardetect CLI, which shows the detected MIME type next to the encoding, like file -i. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude, [#384](https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/384) <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/384>_)

Accuracy:

  • Visual-order Hebrew is now detected. The ISO-8859-8 model trains on both bidi conventions, so 1990s visual-order pages come back as ISO-8859-8 while logical-order text still prefers Windows-1255. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • cp864 Arabic now trains on contextually shaped text in visual order, the way real cp864 systems stored it, instead of isolated letter forms in logical order. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)

Performance:

  • Raising max_bytes on large inputs no longer gets slow. On the compiled build, detect(data, max_bytes=len(data)) on 272 MiB takes about 0.23s for cp1252 and 0.56s for Shift_JIS, down from several seconds. UTF-8 validation and a final decode of the winner still read the whole window, so the answer still decodes it. The other stages stop at a 256 KB evidence cap, which sits above the default max_bytes, so default calls are unchanged, and the default 200 KB cap is still the fastest path. ADR-0006 has the design. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • The UTF-7 + scan is no longer quadratic on line-wrapped base64 like PEM certificates, MIME attachments, and JWTs. 128 KiB of it went from 5.4 seconds to 1.2 milliseconds. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • A head full of unclosed <meta or <?xml tags no longer makes the markup scan quadratic, taking it from about 5 ms to about 20 µs. A literal < inside an attribute value now hides that one tag. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • An EBCDIC charset= or encoding= followed by whitespace and no value no longer makes the declaration scan backtrack quadratically. A crafted 4 KB document used to cost detect() about 60 ms. (Samina <https://github.com/Samin061>, [#403](https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/403) <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/403>)
  • The pure-Python install on CPython scores bigram models with operator.itemgetter instead of a Python loop, making detect() about 1.25x faster and detect_all() about 1.35x faster across the test corpus. Compiled builds and PyPy keep their existing paths. (Afonso Ribeiro <https://github.com/deadstrobe5>_)

Updates `pluggy` from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0
Changelog

Sourced from pluggy's changelog.

pluggy 1.7.0 (2026-10-14)

Deprecations and Removals

  • [#632](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632>_: Hookspec methods defined without self as the first parameter now emit a :class:DeprecationWarning. Add self as the first parameter or use @staticmethod.

Features

    A value spanning several lines is now displayed as a block instead of running into the surrounding trace.

Bug Fixes

  • [#629](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629>_: Fix hooks failing to register on Python 3.14+ when type annotations use forward references.

  • [#442](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442>_: With the addition of default values for hookspec arguments, we also changed the precedence of default values for hookimpl arguments. Callables stored directly on a plugin instance -- in its __dict__ or in a __slots__ slot -- keep being called exactly as getattr() returned them, i.e. without an implicit self.

Updates `python-dateutil` from 2.9.0.post0 to 3.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from python-dateutil's releases.

3.0.0

This is the last major version of dateutil that will support any version of Python older than 3.11. The next release will be the 4.x series, which will support Python 3.11 and later. We may release fixes for serious bugs in the 3.0.x series, but there are no plans for new features there.

The biggest change in this release is a rewrite of tz.tzfile, which affects nearly every user of dateutil.tz and changes the UTC offset of nonexistent times (see below). dateutil also now depends on the tzdata package, and no longer ships its own time zone database.

Data updates

  • dateutil no longer bundles a copy of the IANA time zone database. Time zone data now comes from the system (see dateutil.tz.TZPATH) or, failing that, from the new tzdata dependency, so the data version is whatever version of tzdata is installed. (gh pr #1130)

Features

  • Rewrote tz.tzfile based on a backport of the zoneinfo module's pure-Python implementation. This adds support for Version 2 and Version 3 tzfile(5) binaries, resolving issues with timestamps beyond 2038 and "slim" format binaries. (gh issues #462, #1059, gh pr #1130)
  • Added dateutil.tz.TZPATH and dateutil.tz.reset_tzpath to allow for runtime configuration of the IANA time zone data search path. These replace the mutable dateutil.tz.TZPATHS list, which has been removed. (gh pr #1130)
  • dateutil now depends on the tzdata package, which gettz consults after the search path and before the Windows registry. On Windows this means that names that are both IANA keys and Windows time zone names, such as "UTC", now return a tzfile rather than a tzwin. (gh pr #1130)

Bugfixes

  • tz.tzfile now follows PEP 495 for times that fall in a gap: with fold=0 it uses the offset from before the transition, and with fold=1 the offset from after it. Previously it always used the offset from after the transition, so for example datetime(2003, 4, 6, 2, 30, tzinfo=tz.gettz("America/New_York")) had a UTC offset of -04:00, where it now has -05:00, the same as with zoneinfo. (gh pr #1130)
  • tz.tzfile objects for fixed-offset zones, such as tz.gettz("UTC"), now return their offset, DST offset and abbreviation when utcoffset, dst and tzname are called with None, as tz.tzutc, tz.tzoffset and zoneinfo.ZoneInfo do. This means that datetime.time objects with such a zone attached are now aware: time(12, tzinfo=tz.gettz("UTC")).isoformat() is now "12:00:00+00:00" rather than "12:00:00". (gh pr #1130)
  • tz.tzfile now infers dst() from the standard time on both sides of each DST period, rather than only the one before it, and does so for each transition rather than for each local time type. This fixes dst() for double summer time (e.g. in Europe/London in the 1940s), for half-hour DST (e.g. in Pacific/Rarotonga) and where the standard offset changed at the same time as a DST transition (e.g. in America/Bahia_Banderas in 2010). Against the standard offsets in the tz database source, the only remaining errors are in Europe/Paris in 1944 and 1945. (gh pr #1130)
  • Fixed rrulestr raising ValueError on experimental X- parameters in an RRULE line (such as GNOME Evolution's X-EVOLUTION-ENDDATE); these are now ignored as RFC 5545 permits. Fixed by @​yajo (gh pr #1374)
  • Enabled pickling and deepcopy of cached rrule and rruleset instances. The cache setting is preserved, and cached results are regenerated on demand without copying locks or generators. Reported by @​niccokunzmann (gh issue #1369). Fixed by @​Jay1023CN (gh pr #1600).
  • Fixed relativedelta.__ne__ raising TypeError when comparing against an unsupported type such as None; it now returns True. Reported and fixed by @​kevinkt1 (gh issue #1157, gh pr #1158)
  • Raised the minimum version of six to 1.6, fixing No module named 'six.moves' errors with older versions. Reported by @​skytreader (gh issue #1415), fixed by @​jdarias3 (gh pr #1424).

Deprecations

  • Deprecated the dateutil.zoneinfo module. The module now acts as a wrapper around the tzdata package and will be removed in a future version. Users are encouraged to migrate to dateutil.tz.gettz or the standard library's zoneinfo module. dateutil.zoneinfo.rebuild.rebuild no longer does anything, and by default raises RebuildDeprecationWarning as an error; filter the warning to call it as a no-op. (gh pr #1130)
  • Deprecated passing gettz a relative key that refers to a file outside of every directory on TZPATH, such as "../../etc/localtime". By default this now raises dateutil.tz.DeprecatedTzKeyWarning as an error; filter the warning to keep the old behavior for now, or pass an absolute path instead. (gh pr #1130)

Documentation changes

  • Added intersphinx to the docs build and cleaned up some broken links. (gh pr #1463)

Misc

  • Releases are now uploaded to PyPI using trusted publishing, and the built sdist and wheel are tested on all supported platforms before upload. (gh pr #1619, #1622)
  • Changes to CI, tests and release tooling that do not affect users of the package: gh pr #1417, #1462, #1464, #1465, #1466, #1467, #1468, #1469, #1470, #1499, #1501, #1504, #1576, #1577, #1578, #1581, #1585.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

title: chore(agents): verify and pin Kilo 7.8.18
body:
## Summary

Refs #1407.

Update Kilo's tested and installation pins from **7.8.15 to 7.8.18**, backed by real routing probes rather than version/help checks alone.

- Update `agents/profiles/kilo.json`, including `last_verified_at` and the observed evidence in `verified_by`.
- Regenerate `agents/agents.json` and `packages/cli/src/agents.generated.ts`.
- Match the pinned-binary conformance workflow to 7.8.18.

Two DCO-signed-off commits keep the profile/generated data separate from the workflow change, as required by the profile commit-scope gate. Routing configuration, runtime code, dependencies, and binary-release pins are unchanged.

## Routing evidence

Tested the real npm-installed `@kilocode/cli@7.8.18` on Linux x86_64 with Node 24.16.0. Two runs used separate scratch homes, different loopback ports, dummy credentials, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible SSE endpoint.

Both runs verified:

- The profile's own `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` local overlay was accepted.
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` reached the injected base URL.
- `X-Cave-Agent: kilo` and the expected dummy bearer credential arrived.
- The profile selected `gpt-5.5` without a CLI model override, with `stream: true`.
- Kilo received the complete scripted reply and exited **0**.

The overlay was rendered directly from the canonical profile, not through Caveman's `buildWrapEnv`, so the real-binary probes do **not** establish the wrapper's base-config merge behavior. External plugins were disabled with `--pure`. No live provider, paid model call, compression, or task-quality measurement was involved.

## Validation

- CLI build and `tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Profile CI runtime suites (`agent-registry`, `agent-shortcut`, `kilo-wrap`, `qwen-wrap`, `porcelain`): **312 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Registry compiler and commit-scope regression suites: **26 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `node agents/probe-installed.mjs --require kilo --json`, without `--allow-newer`: **status `ok`**, tested and observed versions both **7.8.18**, version/help checks passed.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: passed.
- Actual two-commit `agents/check-profile-scope.mjs` gate: passed.
- Registry regeneration consistency and `git diff --check`: passed.

The initial runtime-suite run inherited `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, which overrode the telemetry test's explicit opt-in to its loopback fixture. Removing that test-process override made the focused test and then the entire suite pass; no repository-code workaround was added.

Not run: full Go/engine suite, full monorepo test matrix, live-provider calls, or macOS/Windows execution.

title: fix(learn): separate cold resumes from cache churn
body:
Large cache writes after idle periods currently produce the same `cache_churn` finding as real invalidations, including a suggestion that early prompt content changes every message. Two synthetic sessions with three post-initial writes each reproduce the false positive despite every miss following the one-hour TTL.

Carry timestamps, model, reported 5-minute/one-hour cache lifetime, and Claude provider miss diagnostics into the detector. Separate likely cold resumes (`previous_message_not_found` after the known TTL), confirmed tool invalidations (`tools_changed`), and unknown transitions. Read-only cache hits retain the last known lifetime because they refresh the cache without reporting new writes; model changes and missing metadata remain conservative.

Preserve the existing recurrence threshold and measured spike cohort, but count a session toward churn only if it has an invalidation or unknown spike. Cold-only sessions cannot trigger the finding. Keep all observed creation tokens in separate attribution buckets, with session path, current/prior line, gap, TTL, model, diagnostic, and creation/read counts. Suggestions explain the observed causes and do not claim that all writes were avoidable. The cache-efficiency suggestion also avoids diagnosing prompt mutation from the billing mix alone.

`caveman.learn.v1` and existing evidence fields remain intact. `attribution`, `sessions_with_spikes`, and `locators` are additive; CLI text uses the updated title/suggestion and `--json` forwards the full evidence. No generated artifacts are affected.

Validation:
- `go test ./...` in `proxy` passes.
- Regression coverage includes long-gap cold resumes, short-gap tool changes, unknown reasons, mixed sessions, TTL boundaries, read-only refreshes, model changes, missing metadata, deduplication, locators, and JSON serialization.
- Scratch end-to-end scans reproduce the baseline false positive and confirm cold-only suppression; CLI text and JSON were checked with the rebuilt proxy and isolated `CAVEMAN_HOME`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

title: fix(cli): ignore managed hook object key order
body:
Equivalent managed hook objects can be serialized with different JSON key order, such as `{command, type}` instead of `{type, command}`. The ownership comparison treats them as changed, causing `caveman doctor codex` to report degraded components. With stale managed entries present, repair can also refuse with "Caveman hook changed after enable; refusing destructive disable".

Use the existing recursive `canonicalize` helper after normalizing the command identity. This ignores object key order while preserving hook fields and array order.

Regression coverage exercises the isolated CLI:
- Reordered managed Codex hook handlers remain healthy.
- Timeout, matcher, and added permission-bearing field changes still report drift and refuse destructive removal of altered legacy shrink hooks.
- Repair reconciles reordered stale shrink and unsupported Codex event entries while preserving an unrelated hook.

Validation: the key-order health and stale-hook repair regressions failed before the source change, then all five targeted cases passed. Package build and TypeScript lint passed.

The full CLI package suite ran: 1,438 passed, 6 skipped, 2 failed. The Claude setup test passed on rerun. The remaining failure, `setup-from-runner.runtime.mjs` / "an npm install that never finishes is stopped once and named", expects one npm call but sees zero. The same command reproduces the identical failure on clean upstream `main` at `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, without this change.

title: fix(proxy): recognize completed Codex subscription streams
body:
Codex can close a ChatGPT subscription response immediately after consuming `response.completed`. The `/chatgpt/responses` route only installs its terminal-delivery tracker for Pi, so completed Codex responses can be recorded as `cave_client_canceled`, suppressing usage and request-compression accounting even though the client received the answer.

Extend the existing Pi stream-request detection and completion tracking to Codex. A cancellation is accepted only after the terminal frame has been fully written; early cancellation and partial terminal writes remain failures. Add a route-level regression covering all three cases with an `application/json` response header, including byte preservation and usage accounting.

Validation:
- The new completion regression fails on the original implementation and passes with this change.
- `go test ./proxy/internal/gateway ./proxy/internal/store ./proxy/providers/openai` passes against current main.
- Live Codex subscription testing with the rebuilt proxy returned the expected diagnostic result, recorded both responses with HTTP 200 and no error, preserved provider usage, and recorded the compressed request comparison. Local request-token estimates remain inferred.

Historical database rows are not rewritten.

Adopts @zsltg's #1374 onto current `main`, authorship preserved (3 commits cherry-picked cleanly). Refs #1370, Refs #1369, Refs #1371. Not `Fixes`: the policy parts stay open.

## Where the three issues stand

- **#1369 (corrupt `recoveries`)**: hash-on-read already landed in #1315. The likely cause is the pre-#1015 lock loss (#1008); damage written before that fix persists. Detection, post-upgrade check and a repair command still need your decision.
- **#1370 (page cap)**: this PR. The cap/payload mismatch is the root cause of compression stopping: `max_page_count` counts every page while the budget counts payload, and the cap was set only on one connection.
- **#1371 (`caveman stats` timeout)**: this is `caveman.db`, not `ccr.db`. The `julianday(ts)` index landed in #1315. Moving the digest lists needs your decision.

## What this changes

- `max_page_count` is set by a connection hook on a store-private `sqlite.Driver`, so a connection that `database/sql` replaces keeps the cap. `mem/` and other SQLite DBs in the process are unaffected (`TestMemoriesDatabaseHasNoPageCap`).
- `SQLITE_FULL` refusals are recorded, and `Stats` gains `storage_full_reason`: `payload_budget`, `page_cap` or `disk_full`. `StorageFull` no longer reports false when the page cap refused the write.

It does not unwedge a store that is already at the cap. That needs consolidation (#1375) and expiry (#1370 part C).

## Tests

`go test -race ./engine/... ./mem/...` passes. The exception is `TestProcfsChmodFallbackRefusesSymlink`, which fails on `main` too under `umask 077` and passes under `umask 022`, so it's an environment artifact.

title: Standalone hook installers overwrite JSONC settings on idempotent re-run, and OpenCode plugin ignores repo-level defaultMode=off
body:
I ran a 4-pass [Ponder](https://github.com/Quinnod345/ponder) architecture audit on the standalone hook installers (`src/hooks/install.sh`, `src/hooks/install.ps1`) and the OpenCode plugin (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`) and found 3 reproducible issues around JSONC settings idempotency and repo-level `.caveman.json` opt-out (`#634` parity):

### 1. `src/hooks/install.sh` omits `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER` in `ALREADY_INSTALLED` check (`src/hooks/install.sh:93-114`)
- Both the JSONC preflight (`src/hooks/install.sh:54-75`) and the merge step (`src/hooks/install.sh:173-181`) pass `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER="$SETTINGS_HELPER"` (`installer/lib/settings.js`) so `settings.json` files with `//` comments, `/* */` comments, or trailing commas are parsed safely.
- However, the `ALREADY_INSTALLED` probe at `src/hooks/install.sh:93-114` omits `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER` and calls bare `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.CAVEMAN_SETTINGS, 'utf8'))`.
- **Impact**: If a user already has caveman hooks installed, adds a `//` comment or trailing comma to `~/.claude/settings.json`, and re-runs `bash src/hooks/install.sh` without `--force`, `JSON.parse` throws inside the silenced `>/dev/null 2>&1` block. `ALREADY_INSTALLED` evaluates to `0`, and `install.sh` proceeds to the merge step and rewrites `settings.json` via `JSON.stringify`, stripping the user's comments (and without updating `settings.json.bak` if `.bak` already exists from the initial install).

### 2. `src/hooks/install.ps1` uses `ConvertFrom-Json` instead of `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER` in `ALREADY_INSTALLED` check (`src/hooks/install.ps1:80-112`)
- Like `install.sh`, `src/hooks/install.ps1` uses `node` + `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER` for the preflight (`lines 36-64`) and the merge step (`lines 167-180`), but uses `Get-Content $Settings -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json` for the `ALREADY_INSTALLED` probe (`lines 80-112`).
- **Impact**: In Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`), `ConvertFrom-Json` rejects `//` comments and trailing commas, throwing into `catch` so `$HooksWired` becomes `$false` and an idempotent re-run without `-Force` overwrites `settings.json`.

### 3. `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` ignores `ctx` directory and does not honor repo-level `defaultMode: "off"` (`src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:276-378`)
- `CavemanPlugin = async (_ctx) =>` discards the OpenCode plugin context instead of extracting the workspace directory (`ctx?.location?.directory || ctx?.directory || ctx?.worktree`), calling `getDefaultMode()` with no `startDir` at lines `280` and `332`.
- Furthermore, because OpenCode's `.caveman-active` flag is stored globally at `~/.config/opencode/.caveman-active`, `experimental.chat.system.transform` (`lines 351-378`) checks `readFlag(flagPath)` without checking `getDefaultMode(projectDir) === 'off'`. If another session set the global flag (or if a repo has `.caveman.json` with `{"defaultMode": "off"}`), OpenCode still injects the caveman system prompt into that repo's requests, unlike `caveman-activate.js:305` and `caveman-mode-tracker.js:372` (`#634`).

### Full Audit Trail
- Report: https://github.com/Quinnod345/ponder/blob/main/studies/ecosystem-audits/caveman/report.md
- Apply plan: https://github.com/Quinnod345/ponder/blob/main/studies/ecosystem-audits/caveman/apply-plan.md

title: fix(hooks,opencode): use JSONC parser in ALREADY_INSTALLED probe and honor repo defaultMode=off in OpenCode
body:
Fixes #1430

### Summary
I ran a 4-pass [Ponder](https://github.com/Quinnod345/ponder) architecture audit on the standalone hook installers and the OpenCode plugin and found three edge cases around JSONC settings idempotency and repo-level `.caveman.json` opt-out:

1. **`src/hooks/install.sh` (`lines 93-118`)**: Pass `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER="$SETTINGS_HELPER"` to the `ALREADY_INSTALLED` probe and use `require(helper).readSettings(...)` when available (matching preflight at line 66 and merge at line 180) so re-running `install.sh` without `--force` on an already-installed JSONC `settings.json` short-circuits cleanly instead of falling through and stripping comments.
2. **`src/hooks/install.ps1` (`lines 80-118`)**: Replace the `ConvertFrom-Json` `ALREADY_INSTALLED` probe with the same `node` + `CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER` probe used by `install.sh`, avoiding `ConvertFrom-Json` failures on JSONC comments and trailing commas in Windows PowerShell 5.1.

### Validation
