title: wrap claude: caveman_retrieve results are recompressed because the ephemeral plugin tool name is not a recovery tool name
body:
## Summary

Under `caveman wrap claude`, a `caveman_retrieve` result is compressed again on the next request, so elided content can never be recovered. The agent gets back the same stub and the same `<<ccr:…>>` handle it asked to expand. For code this means an agent can't see the function bodies of files it reads.

This is the "Same truncation" failure that `TestRecoveryResultIsNeverRecompressed` guards against, but for the tool name that `wrap claude` itself produces.

## Cause

`caveman wrap claude` registers the MCP server inside its ephemeral plugin (`buildClaudeEphemeralPlugin`, plugin name `caveman-wrap`, passed with `--plugin-dir`). Claude Code namespaces plugin tools, so the tool the model calls is:

```
mcp__plugin_caveman-wrap_caveman__caveman_retrieve
```

`providers.IsRecoveryToolName` (`proxy/providers/adapter.go`) used to accept any `__caveman_retrieve` suffix. 381331354 ("fix(proxy): close recovery tool namespace", 2026-08-30) replaced that with a closed list (`caveman_retrieve`, `mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve`, `caveman_caveman_retrieve`) that doesn't include the wrap plugin's spelling. The Anthropic adapter's `recoveryToolUseIDs` therefore doesn't exempt the result, and the prefix cache substitutes the original compressed replacement.

The list is unchanged at `bin-v4.0.2` and on `main`.

## Observed (CLI 4.0.1 / bin 4.0.1, Claude Code, subscription login, default `think.*` config)

1. `Read` of a 207-line Python file reaches the model with function bodies replaced by `...`, ending in `<<ccr:ccr_939bf742…>>`.
2. `~/.caveman/ccr.db` `recoveries` holds the full original for that handle (`code`, 10004 bytes).
3. `caveman_retrieve` with `verify_only: true` → correct `byte_length` and `sha256`.
4. `caveman_retrieve` without `query` → the model receives the identical stub and the same handle.

## Reproduction test (fails at `bin-v4.0.1`)

Same setup as `TestRecoveryResultIsNeverRecompressed`, parameterised on the tool name. Added as `proxy/internal/gateway/zz_wrap_plugin_name_test.go`:

```go
func TestWrapPluginRetrieveResultIsNeverRecompressed(t *testing.T) {
	for _, name := range []string{
		"mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve",
		"mcp__plugin_caveman-wrap_caveman__caveman_retrieve",
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rt := &captureTransport{responses: []string{subMessageRespBody, subMessageRespBody}}
			comp := &liveZoneCompressor{outputs: [][]byte{[]byte("ELIDED"), []byte("ELIDED")}}
			srv := newSocketFreeCompressServerWithConfig(
				anthropic.New("https://upstream.test"), comp, rt, passthroughTestCreds{},
				Config{SubscriptionCompress: "live_zone", RecoveryViaMCP: true, PrefixCache: newTestPrefixCache()},
			)
			headers := map[string]string{
				"user-agent": "claude-cli/2.1", "authorization": "Bearer sk-ant-oat-test",
				"anthropic-beta": "oauth-2025-04-20", "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
			}
			serveBody(t, srv, "/v1/messages", `{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","messages":[`+anthropicReadTurn(true)+`]}`, headers)
			if !strings.Contains(string(rt.bodies[0]), "ELIDED") {
				t.Fatalf("precondition: first read should have been compressed")
			}
			retrieve := strings.Replace(anthropicRetrieveTurn(), "mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve", name, 1)
			serveBody(t, srv, "/v1/messages", `{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","messages":[`+anthropicReadTurn(true)+`,`+retrieve+`]}`, headers)
			tail := string(rt.bodies[1])[strings.Index(string(rt.bodies[1]), "toolu_ret"):]
			if !strings.Contains(tail, recoveredBlock) {
				t.Fatalf("recovered bytes were recompressed for %s", name)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

At `bin-v4.0.1`: the `mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve` case passes and the `mcp__plugin_caveman-wrap_caveman__caveman_retrieve` case fails with "recovered bytes were recompressed".

## Fix (verified)

Add the wrap plugin's spelling to the closed list. The namespace stays closed:

```diff
 	recoveryToolName     = "caveman_retrieve"
 	mcpRecoveryToolName  = "mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve"
 	kiloRecoveryToolName = "caveman_caveman_retrieve"
+	// `caveman wrap claude` registers the MCP server inside its ephemeral
+	// `caveman-wrap` plugin, and Claude Code namespaces plugin tools.
+	claudeWrapRecoveryToolName = "mcp__plugin_caveman-wrap_caveman__caveman_retrieve"
 )
@@
 func IsRecoveryToolName(name string) bool {
-	return name == recoveryToolName || name == mcpRecoveryToolName || name == kiloRecoveryToolName
+	return name == recoveryToolName || name == mcpRecoveryToolName || name == kiloRecoveryToolName || name == claudeWrapRecoveryToolName
 }
```

With it, both cases pass, along with `TestRecoveryResultIsNeverRecompressed` and `go test ./proxy/providers/...`. In `./proxy/internal/gateway/`, the only failure is `TestReleaseShapeSubscriptionReadOfTypeScriptCompresses` ("this build has no tree-sitter code compressor"). It fails identically without the change, so it comes from my local build, not the fix.

A contract test asserting that the name the wrap plugin yields is a recovery tool name would stop the two from drifting apart again, for example if the plugin or server name in `buildClaudeEphemeralPlugin` changes.

## Workaround

`caveman enable claude` (registers the server with `claude mcp add --scope user caveman`, giving `mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve`) and start plain `claude`, not `wrap`. Or `caveman wrap --off claude`.

title: caveman-compress: a trailing commentary section after the body passes validation
body:
**Repro.** File `AGENTS.md`, no frontmatter, first line `# Working on this repo`, compressed with this pool's copy of `skills/caveman-compress` (synced 2026-10-26, after #1315 merged `_body_candidate_error`) via `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=opencode`. The reply is the compressed body, then `\n\n---\n\nUntouched: the shared/skills/ directory structure (whether add.py, install.sh, update.sh, doctor.sh, global-skills, sources.json, SKILL.md actually exist in this working tree). Risk: compression removed polite filler but preserved all instructions intact.` Result: exit 0, "Validation passed", trailer written into the file.

**Cause.** `_body_candidate_error()` guards the head only: it compares the anchor line and counts added frontmatter-shaped `---` blocks. A trailing `---` has no closing delimiter, so `_frontmatter_block_count` sees no block and the anchor still matches. Nothing inspects the tail. Verified against the shipped functions: `_frontmatter_block_count` returns 0 both for a plain body and for that body plus `\n---\n\nUntouched: …`, and `_body_candidate_error(body, body + trailer)` returns `''` (accepted). That reading is from the code, independent of which model produced the reply.

**Suggested fix.** One bullet in the STRICT RULES block of `build_compress_prompt`: `- Output ends where the input ends: no appended summary, notes, or "untouched" section.` A rejection heuristic would have to tell `---` plus closing notes from a legitimate trailing section, which #1359 explicitly declines to classify, so the rule belongs in the prompt.

**Related.** #1349 (closed as fixed): leading preamble and added frontmatter are guarded now, this is the tail.

**Related.** #1434 is the sibling case: no prompt rule keeps the verb that carries an instruction.

**Seen on** `main` as of 2026-10-26 (`scripts/compress.py`, 51313 bytes). #1359 (open) touches the same guard area, so a patch would rebase onto it.

**AI disclosure.** Drafted with the pi coding agent (pi.dev). The repro commands were run on my machine by the agent, and I reviewed the output, the cited code, and this text before filing.

title: caveman-compress: no prompt rule keeps the verb that carries an instruction, so orders come back as labels
body:
**Repro.** File `AGENTS.md`, no frontmatter, compressed with this pool's copy of `skills/caveman-compress` (synced 2026-10-26, after #1315 merged `_body_candidate_error`) via `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_PROVIDER=opencode`. `Do out-of-repo temp work (downloads, throwaway copies) in a fresh 0700 dir from mktemp -d /tmp/pi-XXXXXX: carry the path it prints, and remove that path when done.` came back as `Out-of-repo temp work (downloads, throwaway copies) in a fresh 0700 dir from mktemp -d /tmp/pi-XXXXXX: carry the printed path, remove it when done.` Every protected span — the path, `mktemp -d /tmp/pi-XXXXXX`, the inline-code spans — survived, so validation passed and the line is now a topic label. The same run turned `Deleting is the irreversible half, so it runs on the literal path …` into `Deletion is the irreversible half: runs on the literal path …`, which has lost its subject.

**Cause.** `build_compress_prompt()`'s STRICT RULES protect spans only (fenced and indented code, inline backticks, headings, XML tags, URLs, paths, commands) and say nothing about the prose it asks the model to cut, so a leading imperative is free to be dropped as filler. SKILL.md's "Drop "you should", "make sure to", "remember to" — just state the action" reads as permission, and "Fragments OK: "Run tests before commit"" has no counterweight saying the verb must survive. The same gap is why #1355's note — SKILL.md's compression rules never reach the provider — still holds on `main`.

**Suggested fix.** One bullet in the same STRICT RULES block: `- Keep the verb that carries each instruction: "Do X", "Run Y", "Never Z" stay orders. A fragment is fine, a verbless noun phrase is not.` Scoped to sentences whose only instruction is that verb: the goldens under `tests/caveman-compress` show label-style output (`No class components`, `State local as possible`) is intended for preference files, and that stays fine.

**Related.** #1350 (open): validation is structure-only, which is why a dropped verb passes. #1355 (closed): the prompt still carries no prose rules. #1433 (open) is the sibling case: a trailing commentary section that also passes validation.

**Seen on** `main` as of 2026-10-26 (`scripts/compress.py`, 51313 bytes; `validate.py` 16284 bytes, identical to this pool copy). No existing issue or PR mentions dropped imperative verbs.

**AI disclosure.** Drafted with the pi coding agent (pi.dev). The repro commands were run on my machine by the agent, and I reviewed the output, the cited code, and this text before filing.

title: caveman-shrink exits on a list response with a null entry
body:
**What happen**

The `caveman-shrink` MCP wrapper exits when the upstream server sends a list response that has a `null` (or other non-object) entry in `tools`, `prompts`, `resources` or `resourceTemplates`.

`transformResponse` in `src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js` reads `item[field]` (line 158) and `item.inputSchema` (line 182) without checking that `item` is an object. The line callback only guards `JSON.parse`; `transformResponse` runs outside that try/catch, so the `TypeError` is uncaught and the wrapper process dies. The MCP host loses the upstream server, including every message after the bad one.

**Expected**

A malformed entry should not take the wrapper down. Skip entries that are not objects, and if the transform fails for any reason, pass the original line through unchanged, the same way unparseable lines are already passed through.

**Reproduction** (on `main` at 9b68f7e)

```sh
node src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js node -e \
  'console.log(JSON.stringify({jsonrpc:"2.0",id:1,result:{tools:[null]}}))' < /dev/null
```

Output, exit status 1, nothing on stdout:

```
src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js:158
          if (typeof item[field] === 'string') {
                         ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'description')
    at transformResponse (src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/index.js:158:26)
```

**Version / install method**

`main` at 9b68f7e, run from a clone with Node 26.0.0. I have a small PR with a regression test ready.

title: fix(shrink): skip non-object list entries instead of exiting
body:
Fixes #1435

**What:** `transformResponse` now skips entries in `tools` / `prompts` / `resources` / `resourceTemplates` that are not objects. The upstream line callback also wraps the transform in a try/catch and passes the original line through on error, matching how unparseable lines are already handled.

**Why:** a `null` entry made `item[field]` throw outside the `JSON.parse` guard. The exception was uncaught, so the wrapper exited and the host lost the upstream server.

**How tested:**

- New test in `tests/installer/mcp-shrink.runtime.test.mjs`: the upstream sends `{"tools":[null,{"name":"t"}]}` and then a second message. The test expects exit 0, the list passed through, and the second message delivered. On `main` it fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'description')`; with this change it passes (6/6 in that file).
- With the `continue` guard removed by hand, the try/catch alone also passes both messages through unchanged.
- `node tests/test_mcp_shrink.js`: 39 passed.
- `npm test`: 636 pass, 1 fail, 16 skipped. The one failure, `standalone hooks keep a stable PATH node symlink` in `e2e.freshinstall.test.mjs`, also fails on unmodified `main` on my machine (macOS, Node 26) and is unrelated to this change.

title: Claude: reordered keys in the shrink-hook entry lock doctor --fix and enable out
body:
**What happens**

If any other tool rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` and changes the key order inside caveman's PreToolUse shrink-hook entry, caveman treats that entry as foreign. The values don't change. After that:

- `caveman doctor claude` reports `degraded` with `drifted: true`
- `caveman doctor claude --fix` fails with `claude PreToolUse Caveman hook changed after enable; refusing destructive disable`
- `caveman enable claude` fails with `Claude Code integration is degraded; run caveman doctor claude --fix before changing it`

So each command waits on the other and nothing repairs it. `caveman status` stays `degraded` for output, input and waste-fixes.

In my case the entry caveman wrote had this order:

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "& '.../caveman.CMD' shrink-hook", "timeout": 30, "shell": "powershell" }
```

Something else on the machine rewrote settings.json about a minute after `caveman enable claude` and left it as:

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "& '.../caveman.CMD' shrink-hook", "shell": "powershell", "timeout": 30 }
```

I have several hook installers (ECC, rtk, token-optimizer, lean-ctx at the time), and I haven't pinned down which one did the rewrite. All 10 native-hook entries and the env block were still intact.

**Why**

`removeNativeHookEntries` checks each managed entry against `canonicalManagedHookEntry`, which swaps the command for its identity and then calls `JSON.stringify` on the entry. `JSON.stringify` keeps insertion order, so `{timeout, shell}` and `{shell, timeout}` give different strings and the entry falls outside `allowedManaged`. In the 4.0.1 bundle that's `dist/index.js` around line 7816 (`canonicalManagedHookEntry`) and the throw at line 10709. Native-hook entries skip this because of the `ownedNative` short circuit, which is why only the shrink-hook entry trips it.

**Repro**

1. `caveman enable claude` on Windows (the `shell: "powershell"` key is only added on win32).
2. Swap `timeout` and `shell` in the PreToolUse shrink-hook entry of `~/.claude/settings.json`. Nothing else.
3. `caveman doctor claude --fix` refuses.

The reverse also holds. I put the two keys back in caveman's order, changing nothing else, and `doctor claude --fix` reported `repaired`. After that `doctor claude` showed `installed`, `drifted: false`, and `status` showed `wired`.

**Expected**

Compare entries as data, not as key-ordered strings. Sorting keys before stringifying (or a deep-equal) in `canonicalManagedHookEntry` would do it. Real changes to the command, matcher, timeout or shell should still refuse, as they do now. The health check that flags `drifted` probably needs the same change, though I haven't traced it.

**Related**

#1410 is the same kind of problem for Hermes, where YAML reserialization breaks ownership. #926 was another way `doctor` could get stuck at `degraded` with `--fix` refusing.

**Environment**

- caveman CLI 4.0.1 (`@caveman-ai/cli`), native pack 2.2.0
- Claude Code 2.1.316
- Windows 11, PowerShell hooks

title: fix(cli): compare managed hook entries independent of key order
body:
## Why

If another tool rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` and reorders the keys in Caveman's shrink-hook entry, Caveman should still recognise that entry as its own. Today it doesn't. `doctor claude` reports `degraded`, `doctor claude --fix` refuses with `PreToolUse Caveman hook changed after enable; refusing destructive disable`, and `enable claude` refuses because the install is degraded. Each command points at the other, and nothing repairs it.

Fixes #1437.

## What changed

`canonicalManagedHookEntry` swapped the command for its identity and then called `JSON.stringify` on the entry. `JSON.stringify` keeps insertion order, so `{timeout, shell}` and `{shell, timeout}` produced different strings. The entry then fell outside the owned set in both places that compare through this helper:

- `nativeHookEntriesHealthy` (doctor ownership, which decides `degraded`)
- `removeNativeHookEntries` (the ownership guard in disable and `--fix`)

The helper now sorts object keys before stringifying. Arrays keep their order, and the command identity, matcher, timeout and shell values still have to match exactly. A real change to any of them is still refused.

## Not changed

`drifted` in `doctor` output still reads `true` after a reorder. It is a raw byte-hash comparison of the whole settings file, and any edit sets it, including the existing test's unrelated `theme` change. It doesn't feed the `state` that blocks `--fix` and `enable`, so I left it alone.

## Tests

- New test `reordered keys in an owned hook entry stay owned (#1437)` in `packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs`. It enables Claude, reverses the key order of every PreToolUse entry and its hook object, then asserts that `doctor claude` reports `installed` and `disable claude` exits 0 and removes the hooks.
- That suite uses `/bin/sh` stub binaries and can't run on native Windows, so I haven't run the new test locally. It first runs in CI here.
- Instead I reproduced the bug end to end on Windows 11 with Node 22, against the built `dist/index.js`. I used an isolated home and npm-style `.cmd` stubs, so the `shell: "powershell"` key from the report was present.
  - Before the fix: after the key swap, `doctor --fix` and `disable` both failed with the error above.
  - After the fix: `doctor --fix` printed `native Caveman repaired` and `disable` exited 0. `lifecycle_hooks` and `tool_rewrite` matched the pre-reorder baseline.
- I started the full CLI suite on Windows and stopped it partway through. Many of its tests fail on native Windows with or without this change because of the POSIX stubs, so it doesn't tell us anything about this fix.

title: Compat mount to a loopback upstream fails with a generic 502 cave_upstream_unavailable and no log line
body:
**Version:** caveman-proxy bin-v4.0.2 (darwin/arm64), self-hosted, `caveman-proxy serve`.

**`caveman.yaml`:**

```yaml
compat:
  legohr:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28787   # a local proxy (Headroom) in front of the provider
    wire_dialect: anthropic
```

Every request to `/compat/legohr/v1/messages` returns:

```
502 {"error":{"type":"cave_gateway_error","code":"cave_upstream_unavailable","message":"Upstream service error.", ...}}
```

The upstream never gets a connection, and the proxy log (default level) has no line for these requests. The cause is the SSRF guard: in self-hosted mode it blocks loopback unless the host is allow-listed (#841). Setting `CAVE_SSRF_ALLOWLIST=127.0.0.1` fixes it.

**Ask:** when the guard blocks a mount's upstream, say so, either in the error body or in a WARN log line that names the host and `CAVE_SSRF_ALLOWLIST`. Today it looks the same as an upstream outage.

title: OpenCode CLI, installer and copied plugin ignore OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
body:
**What happen**

With a nonempty absolute `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, three Caveman paths still use `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`: CLI hook installation, the unified installer, and the copied mode plugin's `.caveman-active` file. They report success while leaving the selected directory untouched.

OpenCode 2.2.5 selects this variable as its global config directory ([CLI wiring](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L138-L140), [global service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/util/src/global.ts#L74-L84)). This report concerns that configuration, not whether older OpenCode releases also scan an additional directory.

**Expected**

Use nonempty `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` consistently; otherwise retain `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` and `~/.config/opencode` fallbacks. Installation and plugin runtime state must agree with the host's selected root.

**Before/after example**

From the Caveman checkout at the revision below, with `caveman` already installed:

```sh
t=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$t/home" "$t/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh
exit 0
' > "$t/bin/opencode"
chmod +x "$t/bin/opencode"
# The fake command supplies discovery only; no OpenCode session runs.
probe() {
  env -i PATH="$t/bin:$PATH" HOME="$t/home" USERPROFILE="$t/home" \
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$t/xdg" XDG_DATA_HOME="$t/data" \
    XDG_STATE_HOME="$t/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$t/cache" \
    CAVEMAN_HOME="$t/caveman" OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR="$t/selected" "$@"
}
probe caveman tools hooks install opencode
probe node installer/install.js --only opencode --non-interactive --no-color
probe node --input-type=module -e \
  'const m=await import(process.argv[1]); await m.CavemanPlugin({})' \
  "$t/xdg/opencode/plugins/caveman/plugin.js"
find "$t/xdg/opencode" -name '*shrink*' -o -name '.caveman-active'
test ! -e "$t/selected"
```

Observed: all three commands exit 0. The hook is `xdg/opencode/plugins/caveman-shrink.js`; installer copies under `xdg/opencode`; plugin factory writes `xdg/opencode/.caveman-active`. Nothing reaches `selected`.

Cause: separate root helpers omit the variable in [CLI](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9028-L9033), [installer](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/installer/install.js#L1490-L1495), and [plugin](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js#L132-L144).

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode, Linux x86_64

**Version / install method**

CLI 4.0.1, source `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`; Node v22.23.4, Linux 7.2.13-200.fc44.x86_64. CLI used the existing unfixed Nix build through a disposable profile; installer used raw upstream source. Relevant compiled CLI root helper matches upstream. Plugin factory was invoked directly, not through a host session. No provider/model requests. AI-assisted report and reproduction.

title: Hermes plugin membership matcher reports installed for disabled, wrong-field and prefix matches
body:
**What happen**

`caveman tools hooks install hermes` reports success and writes an installed marker even when Hermes rejects `caveman_shrink` as disabled or not enabled. Valid YAML remains unchanged. The shared membership matcher accepts list items outside `plugins.enabled` and prefix matches inside flow lists.

**Expected**

Read exact scalar membership under `plugins.enabled`; apply `plugins.disabled` first. Explicitly disabled plugins must remain disabled without a successful installation claim. A name such as `caveman_shrink_extra` is not `caveman_shrink` and must not disable it either.

**Before/after example**

With an installed CLI, this disposable example covers the deny case:

```sh
t=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$t/home" "$t/hermes" "$t/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh
exit 0
' > "$t/bin/hermes"
chmod +x "$t/bin/hermes"
cat > "$t/hermes/config.yaml" <<'YAML'
plugins:
  enabled: []
  disabled:
    - caveman_shrink
YAML
env -i PATH="$t/bin:$PATH" HOME="$t/home" USERPROFILE="$t/home" \
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$t/xdg" XDG_DATA_HOME="$t/data" \
  XDG_CACHE_HOME="$t/cache" XDG_STATE_HOME="$t/state" \
  CAVEMAN_HOME="$t/caveman" HERMES_HOME="$t/hermes" \
  caveman tools hooks install hermes
cat "$t/caveman/hooks/hermes.json"
```

Observed: exit 0, `Hermes Agent: command-output rewrite hook installed`, marker `{"installed":true}`; deny entry remains.

The real Hermes YAML parser and `scan_directory`/`gate_manifest` also checked the generated manifest:

| Valid input | Caveman install | Hermes gate |
|---|---|---|
| Block `plugins.disabled: [caveman_shrink]`, enabled empty | Success, unchanged YAML | Disabled |
| Exact name in both flow lists | Success, unchanged YAML | Disabled wins |
| Enabled empty; `other: [caveman_shrink]` as a block list | Success, unchanged YAML | Not enabled |
| `plugins.enabled: [caveman_shrink_extra]` | Success, unchanged YAML | Not enabled |
| Exact enabled name; disabled only `caveman_shrink_extra` | Success | Load (control) |

Cause: [unscoped/prefix regex and early return](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L18375-L18399); [installer](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L18491-L18503) and [marker-only status](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L18569-L18578). Hermes [gate](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/c419cf7c864ac0ee511dbd9f7091a8bba0b567ee/hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py#L269-L324) applies exact memberships and disabled precedence. Same matcher serves native enable too; that path was source-inspected, not executed here. Unlike #1405/#1410, no invalid YAML or normalization is involved.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Hermes Agent

**Version / install method**

CLI 4.0.1 at `9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`, existing unfixed Nix build through a disposable profile; relevant compiled matcher matches upstream. Node v22.23.4, Linux x86_64; Hermes `c419cf7c864ac0ee511dbd9f7091a8bba0b567ee`, Python 3.14.8 / ruamel.yaml 0.19.1. Fake Hermes executable supplies CLI discovery only. Real host parser/discovery code evaluates generated files without loading plugin callbacks or starting a session. No provider/model requests. AI-assisted report and reproduction.

title: Generated OpenCode native hooks lose the host project cwd in both V1 and V2
body:
**What happen**

The generated native OpenCode adapters omit the host's project directory in both the lifecycle payload and subprocess working directory. V1 discards its factory context; V2 receives `ctx.location.directory` but never uses it when calling Caveman.

When a host process serves a project different from its own launch directory, `native-hook` therefore receives no project cwd and inherits the launch directory. [`nativeRuntimeRequest`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L17207-L17218) falls back to that subprocess's `process.cwd()`. The resulting wrong native session cwd is source-backed; no native runtime was started in this probe.

This concerns native session/repository context, not the shell tool's own workdir or command execution directory. #1430/#1431 concern a different file, `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js`, and its default-mode lookup.

**Expected**

Propagate the authoritative host project directory to native-hook payloads and subprocess options. Keep V1/V2 behavior aligned, including generated shrink-hook subprocesses.

**Before/after example**

Focused probe executed against the unchanged upstream `opencodeNativePluginSourceV1` and `opencodeNativePluginSourceV2` generator bodies:

1. Create separate disposable `launcher`, `project`, and HOME directories.
2. Point only the generator's `cavemanInvocation` dependency at a Node recorder that logs its cwd and stdin JSON.
3. Run from `launcher`; initialize V1 with `{ directory: project }` and V2 with `ctx.location.directory = project`.
4. Deliver `session.created`, then invoke each before-tool hook with `bash` (V1) or `shell` (V2). The recorder does not execute the supplied command.

Observed in both versions:

```text
host project: .../project
SessionStart child cwd: .../launcher; payload.cwd: absent
PreToolUse child cwd:  .../launcher; payload.cwd: absent
shrink-hook child cwd: .../launcher; payload.cwd: absent
```

Want: native calls identify `.../project`, regardless of host launch cwd.

Source: [V1 native call](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9096-L9123), [V1 shrink call](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9225-L9244), [V2 native call](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9273-L9299), [V2 shrink call](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9432-L9455). None supplies `cwd`.

**Platform**

- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode V1 and V2 adapters; probe on Linux x64, Node v22.23.4.

**Version / install method**

Generated JavaScript was imported directly; only subprocess destination was replaced with the recorder.

title: OpenCode 2 native plugin drops owner-routed locationless session.deleted events
body:
**What happen**

The generated V2 native plugin drops a legitimate `session.deleted` event when its public envelope has no `location`. [`sameLocation`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9377-L9400) returns false before the deletion branch can send `SessionEnd` and clear `contexts`/`pending`.

OpenCode keeps routing metadata separate from the public event. [Its bus resolves locationless session events through their owner](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/core/src/bus.ts#L210-L265), then [filters each location subscription using that routing snapshot](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/core/src/bus.ts#L729-L744). [The plugin host subscribes through this bus](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts#L266-L282). Therefore, absent public `event.location` does not mean the event belongs elsewhere. This is missed cleanup, not cross-project event leakage.

**Expected**

Handle locationless deletion events already routed to this plugin instance. Send `SessionEnd` and clear that session's local maps immediately, rather than waiting for plugin disposal.

**Before/after example**

A focused generated-plugin probe used an isolated HOME and a local subprocess recorder. It evaluated the unchanged V2 generator with only `cavemanInvocation` pointing at that recorder, then:

1. Called `setup(ctx)` for one project and supplied an async event stream.
2. Delivered a located `session.created` for `v2-project-session`; the recorder returned stable context.
3. Delivered this event through the same stream:

```json
{"type":"session.deleted","data":{"sessionID":"v2-project-session"}}
```

4. Requested context for that same ID to observe whether cached context was removed.
5. As a control, delivered the same deletion with the matching `location` attached.

Observed before plugin disposal:

```text
locationless deletion: SessionEnd calls = 0
context afterward:    new SessionStart calls = 0 (cached context retained)
located control:     SessionEnd calls = 1
```

The callback/subprocess behavior above was executed. The host delivery rationale is source-backed, not a claimed full-server execution. [OpenCode's session removal publishes `Deleted` with only `sessionID` in its data](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/core/src/session.ts#L391-L401); routing need not add a public location.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode V2 native adapter; Linux x64, Node v22.23.4 probe.

**Version / install method**

Caveman source [`9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/9b68f7ed12b05e7efaff18e65c5a3fc2849fd0a4/packages/cli/src/index.ts) (CLI package version 4.0.1), also current main when checked. OpenCode source contract [`977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/977f5c695c2b4a254560743432d20f622cbe1233/packages/core/package.json#L1-L4), package version 2.2.5.

AI-assisted report. No model, proxy, native runtime, or host service was started.

title: Standalone hooks install opencode still generates a V1-only CavemanShrink plugin on OpenCode 2
body:
**What happen**

The standalone `caveman tools hooks install opencode` path still writes a V1-only `caveman-shrink.js`. Its only export is `CavemanShrink`; there is no default definition. The installer nevertheless reports that command-output rewriting is installed.

This is separate from closed #1083, which covered `caveman enable opencode` and `caveman-native.js`. It is also separate from #1246 and #1180, which concern the installer plugin under `src/plugins/opencode/`.

**Expected**

**Before/after example**

home="$(mktemp -d)"
HOME="$home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$home/.config" caveman tools hooks install opencode

exports: ["CavemanShrink"]

The upstream generator remains V1-only. title: fix(cli): honor Hermes plugin membership lists

title: pi extension: warns 'not an HTTP URL' for pi-virtual models (router/auto) and host-subprocess bridges
body:
**What happen**

The pi extension warns once per model per session for a model that is not an HTTP provider at all:

```
Caveman: pass-through for router/auto (provider endpoint "" is not an HTTP URL; this provider sends no routable request); no compression
```

`router/auto` is a pi **virtual** model (`api: "pi-virtual"`, empty `baseUrl`). It never sends an HTTP request: pi resolves it to a physical model before any transport. So the warning is not actionable — there is no upstream to mount, and no `compat.router.base_url` that could make it routable.

Same class of noise for host-subprocess bridges such as `grok-pi`, which publishes the sentinel baseUrl `cli:grok-single`:

```
Caveman: pass-through for grok-cli/grok-4.7-build-fast (provider endpoint "cli:grok-single" is not an HTTP URL; this provider sends no routable request); no compression
```

`provider.ts` already has the right instinct for the sentinel case (the `!host` branch, and the comment "Never offer that remedy for an endpoint with no host"), but it still emits a `warning` for a provider that cannot be routed by design.

**Expected**

A model whose `api` is `pi-virtual`, or whose `baseUrl` has no host, should be skipped silently (or reported at `info`/debug level), because no configuration change can route it. The extension should not claim "no compression" for a request that never leaves the process.

Concretely, in `packages/pi-extension/src/provider.ts` `apply()`, next to the existing `openai-completions` / `api.openai.com` carve-out:

```ts
// pi-virtual never sends HTTP: pi resolves it to a physical model before any
// transport. An empty baseUrl must not be compared with a compat mount that
// shares the provider name (router/auto vs compat.router).
if (model.api === "pi-virtual") {
  if (!(await this.restoreCurrentModel(ctx))) return;
  return;
}
```

`router` is also a legitimately mountable compat name in `caveman.yaml` (`compat.router.base_url`), so a provider named `router` with a real HTTP baseUrl must keep routing as it does today — the guard has to key on the virtual API, not the provider name.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: select model router/auto with the Caveman pi extension enabled
Got:   Caveman: pass-through for router/auto (provider endpoint "" is not an HTTP URL; this provider sends no routable request); no compression
Want:  no warning (nothing to route, nothing to compress)
```

**Platform**

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: pi (pi-coding-agent 1.4.0)

**Version / install method**

- `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1 (npm global), bundled extension reports `clientInfo.version` 0.3.0; upstream `packages/pi-extension` is 0.3.1 and has the same behaviour
- binaries `bin-v4.0.1`, proxy mode `compress`, `~/.caveman/caveman.yaml` with `compat.mistral` and `providers.openai-codex`
- Linux x86_64

Note: the locally generated `~/.pi/agent/extensions/caveman-native.js` had this guard added by hand, which is why `caveman doctor pi` reports `exact: false` and `caveman enable pi` refuses to re-run ("changed after enable; refusing destructive disable"). Landing the guard upstream would let that file stay generated.

title: Codex style hook pins installation-time Node path; allow PATH-based runtime resolution
body:
The standalone Codex style installer persists an absolute Node executable in `hooks.json`, rather than resolving the default Node runtime when the hook runs.

Observed with caveman-installer 4.0.1 on Linux using mise. Installed SessionStart command (home path anonymized):

```text
"/home/user/.local/share/mise/installs/node/latest/bin/node" "/home/user/.codex/caveman/hooks/codex-sessionstart.js"
```

Current main still generates this through `installCodexHook()`:

```js
PLATFORM_PATHS.hookCommand(absoluteNodePath(), [script])
```

`absoluteNodePath()` probes `command -v node` and persists the absolute candidate, falling back to `process.execPath`. A deployment wrapper in our dotfiles only invokes the upstream installer with `--only codex --non-interactive --no-mcp-shrink`; it does not generate or rewrite this command.

Expected: offer a portable mode that resolves Node through the hook process's PATH, such as `node "/absolute/path/to/codex-sessionstart.js"`, or executable direct invocation on POSIX using the script's existing `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang. Please document the tradeoff if absolute paths are intentional for GUI clients with limited PATH. An explicit runtime override would also make this choice controllable.

The observed mise `latest` alias currently exists and may survive upgrades; no hook failure is claimed here. The issue is that the integration is coupled to the installation-time runtime manager instead of following the runtime available through the hook's PATH. Versioned candidates can additionally become stale after pruning.

Related: #805 addressed Homebrew stable paths; #1137 covers versioned native CLI/proxy integration paths. This report concerns the standalone style-only Codex SessionStart hook in `installer/install.js`.

title: Anthropic outcome qualifiers (iterations) never read message_start's message.usage — dead on streaming responses
body:
### What happens

`mergeUsage` merges Anthropic outcome qualifiers (notably `usage.iterations`) only from the **outer** `obj["usage"]` and `obj["response"]["usage"]` positions (`mergeProviderOutcomeQualifiers` at `proxy/providers/adapter.go:1940`, call sites at `:1204-1213`). But the counter parser explicitly knows that on a streaming `message_start` event the usage object lives at **`message.usage`** — `usageObjects()` (`:1668-1685`) has a dedicated `add(msg["usage"])` branch for exactly that shape, without which streaming Anthropic `input_tokens` (which only appears on `message_start`; `message_delta` doesn't repeat it) would never parse.

So the same field has two consumers reading two different positions: counters see `message.usage`, the outcome-qualifier guard does not. If `iterations` rides `message_start.message.usage` — the only streaming shape where that usage object appears — the qualifier guard never inspects it, `PricingUnsupportedReason` stays empty, and a response with a separately-billed dimension (compaction/advisor iterations, which the code's own comment at `:1944-1947` says are "billed apart from the top-level counts") is priced as a precise token-catalog subtotal. That is exactly what the `mergePricingQualifiers` comment (`:1900-1903`) forbids: presenting "a token-only subtotal as the exact bill".

### Steps to reproduce

Logic-level, via the existing parser surface:

```go
u := UsageObservation{}
ParseUsageBytes("anthropic",
  []byte("event: message_start\ndata: {\"type\":\"message_start\",\"message\":{\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":2,\"output_tokens\":1,\"iterations\":[{\"type\":\"compaction\"}]}}}\n\n"),
  &u)
// u.PricingUnsupportedReason == "" today; counters DO pick up input_tokens=2
// from message.usage, proving this object reaches the parser.
```

### Expected behavior

The iterations guard should see the same objects the counter parser sees — including `message.usage` on `message_start`.

### Suggested fix

In `mergeUsage`, mirror the counters' reach for the message sub-object:

```go
if msg, ok := obj["message"].(map[string]any); ok {
    mergeProviderOutcomeQualifiers(provider, msg, usage)
}
```

(`message_start`'s message carries no `stop_reason`, so the refusal check inside is a no-op for it.)

### Honest caveat

There is no fixture in the repo showing `iterations` on `message_start`; if Anthropic only ever emits it on the terminal `message_delta.usage` (top-level `usage`), the existing `obj`-level check already covers streams and this reduces to defense-in-depth. But the split-brain between the two consumers of the same field is present regardless — this report is primarily about that inconsistency.

### Environment

- caveman main @ `2e068f73`, `proxy/providers/adapter.go`
- Desktop JVM-free (pure Go parser path); no live traffic involved

title: CLI: routedAiderArgs misses argparse abbreviations of --model (--mod=...), silently defeating routed model with no warning
body:
### What happens

`routedAiderArgs` (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:6560-6592`) detects a user-supplied model by exact match on `--model` and the `--model=` prefix only. Aider's CLI is built on `configargparse`, which by default accepts unambiguous abbreviations of long options — so on the pinned aider version (`tested_agent_version: "0.86.2"` in `agents.generated.ts`, whose `args.py` parser does not set `allow_abbrev=False`), a user can pass the model as `--mod=<model>` and it still resolves to `--model` inside aider.

The routing wrapper then sees `sawModel == false`, silently prepends its own `--model <routed-default>`, and prints **no bypass warning**. Aider parses both as the same `--model` store action, and argparse's last-wins semantics mean the user's abbreviation — later in argv — wins. The result is byte-for-byte the situation the function already warns about for `--model=<non-openai>` ("traffic may bypass Caveman", `:6586`), except with **zero warning and a defeated route**: same class of input, two opposite treatments.

(Note: `-m` is not part of this gap — it is aider's short alias for `--message`, which the wrapper correctly ignores.)

### Steps to reproduce

```text
caveman wrap aider --mod=anthropic/claude-x …
# → routedAiderArgs prepends "--model openai/gpt-5.5", prints nothing,
#   aider resolves --mod as --model and uses anthropic/claude-x: traffic
#   bypasses Caveman with no diagnostic.
# Compare: caveman wrap aider --model=anthropic/claude-x … → warning printed.
```

### Expected behavior

Abbreviated spellings that argparse will resolve to `--model` should be detected the same as the exact flag — at least the common `--mod=` form — so the existing bypass warning fires instead of the route being silently overridden.

### Suggested fix direction

In the same loop, additionally recognize `=`-style args whose name is an unambiguous prefix of `--model` (length > 2, `"--model".startsWith(name)`), treating them like the `--model=` branch. A conservative variant is to cover only prefixes that cannot resolve to any other aider option; the maintainer knows the full flag list.

### Environment

- caveman main @ `2e068f73`, `packages/cli/src/index.ts`
- aider behavior per its pinned `0.86.2` (`configargparse` default `allow_abbrev=True`); if the maintainer knows otherwise for this version, the report reduces to the `--mod=`-spelling case only

title: CLI: proxyYamlMode() matches nested middleware.mode — start and the proxy disagree on the same caveman.yaml
body:
### What happens

`proxyYamlMode()` (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:4551-4560`, main @ `2e068f73`) reads the proxy's top-level mode from `caveman.yaml` with:

```js
const match = raw.match(/^\s*mode\s*:\s*["']?([^#\s"']+)/m);
```

With the `/m` flag, `^` matches the start of **every** line, and `\s*` also consumes newlines — so `^\s*mode\s*:` does not mean "a top-level `mode:` key", it means "`mode:` at any indentation on any line". `caveman.yaml` legitimately contains a second, nested `mode:` key: `middleware.mode` (`proxy/internal/config/middleware.go:56`, whose comment documents "the proxy can record while the middleware compresses" as a supported configuration). The nested key is picked up as if it were the proxy's mode.

Two consequences, both from real spellings:

**A. Middleware-only mode makes `caveman start` describe a different mode than the proxy runs.**

```yaml
listen: 127.0.0.1:8787
middleware:
  mode: compress
```

- Go side: `config.Load()` sees no top-level mode → normalizes to **record** (`config.go:424-426`, `!knownModes[c.Mode]`).
- CLI side: `proxyYamlMode()` returns **"compress"** → `start` reports compress (subscription hints, `CAVE_ENGINE_TOON="best-of"` injected at `:2745`) while the proxy itself runs record.

**B. Key order flips the CLI's answer.**

```yaml
middleware:
  mode: record
mode: compress
```

- Go side: yaml.v3 resolves keys by name → the proxy runs **compress**.
- CLI side: the regex takes the first textual match → **"record"** → `think.mode=record`, `CAVE_ENGINE_TOON` becomes empty (compress mode with toon silently off), and `caveman status` reports a `runningModeMismatch` that is not real (`:20954-20955`).

Both scenarios are the same defect: `wrapRuntimeConfig({ forStart: true })` applies `proxyYamlMode()` as `think.mode` with source `proxy-yaml` (`:4670`), while the CLI's own comment above the start path (`:2708-2714`) says start and the proxy resolve the same mode decision — for these inputs they disagree.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point `CAVEMAN_CONFIG` at a file containing only:
   ```yaml
   listen: 127.0.0.1:8787
   middleware:
     mode: compress
   ```
2. Run `caveman start` (or any path that calls `proxyYamlMode()`).
3. Observe: the CLI treats the mode as `compress` (toon on, compress-flavored subscription hints) while the proxy normalizes its own mode to `record`.

For scenario B, put `middleware:\n  mode: record` **above** a top-level `mode: compress` and watch `caveman status` report a mismatch between a running compress proxy and a "record" gate.

### Expected behavior

`proxyYamlMode()` should read only the top-level key, so for every input it agrees with `config.Load()` (`proxy/internal/config/config.go`).

### Suggested fix

Anchor the pattern to column 0 — drop the whitespace run:

```js
const match = raw.match(/^mode\s*:\s*["']?([^#\s"']+)/m);
```

`yamlScopedBaseUrl()` (`:4580-4608`) is unaffected: it tracks indentation deliberately and requires the nesting.

### Tests

`proxyYamlMode()` currently has zero coverage (no test references it; the Go side's own test only pins a top-level key, `config_test.go:174`). Four cases, written test-first:

1. `middleware:\n  mode: compress` with no top-level key → expect `undefined` (fails today: returns "compress").
2. `middleware:\n  mode: record` above `mode: compress` → expect `"compress"` (fails today: returns "record").
3. Cross-check vs the Go loader for both inputs: `config.Load().Mode` must equal the CLI's reading (scenario A fails today: "compress" vs "record").
4. Guard: `mode: compress` with a nested `mode: record` still returns `"compress"` (must keep passing after the fix, so the fix cannot regress to "first indented key wins").

Verified against `origin/main` @ `2e068f73`; PR #1395's diff (41 commits) does not touch `proxyYamlMode`, and a repo-wide issue/PR search found no prior report.

title: learn: repaste findings flag Caveman's own SessionStart ruleset and CLAUDE.md injection as pasted text
body:
## What happened

`caveman learn --all` on Claude Code reports 17 `recurring_context:repaste:*` findings ("The same text … was pasted again in N sessions", `fix_kind=cavemem_offload`), recommending moving each block to cavemem.

None of the flagged blocks were pasted by the user. Following each finding's first locator back to its transcript line:

- ~half are Caveman's own SessionStart hook output (`SessionStart:startup hook success: CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full … Respond terse like smart caveman …`), including the largest ones (~7.5k tokens, 12–24 sessions each).
- the rest are Claude Code's own injection of CLAUDE.md / auto-memory (`Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior …`), seen in 74–184 sessions each.

## Why it matters

The suggested fix can't save anything for this text: the hook and the host re-inject it every session regardless of what's stored in cavemem. Acting on it the other way (deleting the source after offloading) would silently stop the agent from receiving its instructions, especially with auto-recall off (the default). The findings also crowd out genuine repeated pastes in the report.

## Expected

The repaste detector should exclude host- and hook-injected context: hook `additionalContext` / `hook success` text, Claude Code's CLAUDE.md / memory system-reminder blocks, and Caveman's own ruleset. Those are already covered by the "always-loaded setup" accounting.

## Repro

1. Claude Code with the Caveman native hooks installed and a project CLAUDE.md.
2. Run several sessions.
3. `caveman learn --all`: the repeated-text findings point at the SessionStart ruleset and the CLAUDE.md injection.

## Environment

- `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.1, integration pack 2.2.0
- Claude Code 2.1.317, macOS
- 240 Claude sessions over 30 days

title: chore(deps): bump the pip group across 2 directories with 9 updates
body:
Updates the requirements on [chardet](https://github.com/chardet/chardet), [cyclonedx-bom](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-python), [jsonpointer](https://github.com/stefankoegl/python-json-pointer), [pluggy](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy), [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest), [python-dateutil](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil), [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools), [tzdata](https://github.com/python/tzdata) and [anthropic](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python) to permit the latest version. Updates `chardet` from 7.6.0 to 7.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from chardet's releases.

7.7.0

Big release: raising max_bytes to cover a huge input no longer makes detect() slow, every answer now decodes the window it was detected from, and markup declarations are read the way browsers read them. A lot of this came from new contributors, so thank you all!

Performance

  • Raising max_bytes on large inputs no longer gets slow. On compiled wheels, detect(data, max_bytes=len(data)) on 272 MiB takes about 0.2s for cp1252 and 0.5s for Shift_JIS, down from several seconds. UTF-8 validation and a final decode of the winner still read the whole window, and the other stages stop at a 256 KiB evidence cap (ADR-0006). The default 200 KB cap is still the fastest path, and default calls are unchanged.
  • The pure-Python wheel on CPython scores bigram models through operator.itemgetter instead of a Python loop, making detect() about 1.25x faster and detect_all() about 1.35x faster. (#404, thanks @​deadstrobe5)
  • Fixed three scans that went quadratic on hostile input: the UTF-7 + scan on line-wrapped base64 (128 KiB went from 5.4s to 1.2ms), unclosed <meta and <?xml tags in the markup scan, and the EBCDIC charset-declaration regex. (#403, thanks @​Samin061)

Bug Fixes

  • Every answer now decodes the examined window under the name you get back. BOMs, BOM-less UTF-16/32 null patterns, ISO-2022/HZ escapes, and <meta charset> declarations used to be trusted without decoding the rest of the window, so a confident answer could still raise further in. The 5.x/6.x display names (EUC-JP, SHIFT_JIS, Big5, ISO-2022-JP) are only used when those narrower codecs decode it too. (#394 and #396, thanks @​Samin061)
  • Markup declarations follow the WHATWG prescan: declarations inside comments are ignored, a charset= inside another attribute (like a refresh URL) no longer beats a real <meta charset>, quoted or spaced content charsets work, and an ASCII page declaring utf-16le no longer comes back as UTF-16-LE. (#389 and #398, thanks @​SashaMIT and @​xiehuanyi)
  • PEP 263 cookies resolve the way tokenize.detect_encoding resolves them, including only counting a line-2 cookie when line 1 is blank or a comment. (#391, thanks @​xiehuanyi)
  • Fixed BOM-bearing UTF-32 coming back as UTF-16 when max_bytes cuts a code unit. (#405, thanks @​AryanRG)
  • Fixed language labels on Unicode text tilting toward accent-heavy languages, so a French paragraph with a few accents no longer comes back as Hungarian. Mislabels on the test corpus's Unicode files dropped from 140 to 104.
  • Fixed a mostly-ASCII Windows-1252 file with a single Ö detecting as HP-Roman8, and English with a lone É detecting as MacRoman. (#383, thanks @​aadsm)
  • Fixed null-separated records like find -print0 output coming back as UTF-16-LE with Chinese as the language.
  • prefer_superset=True no longer swaps in a code page that can't decode the data, and now respects include_encodings/exclude_encodings. (#393, thanks @​00200200)
  • chardetect and UniversalDetector no longer mistake input cut exactly at the byte cap for the whole stream. (#392, thanks @​00200200)
  • lookup_encoding's cache is capped at 1024 entries, since charset names come from untrusted markup. (#390, thanks @​Samin061)
  • Plus smaller fixes to detect_all() ranking, EBCDIC XML MIME types, and the deprecated chardet.equivalences shim. The changelog has the full list.

Improvements

  • New -m/--mime-type flag for chardetect shows the MIME type next to the encoding, like file -i. (#384, thanks @​smi11 for the request)
  • Visual-order Hebrew is now detected, and cp864 Arabic is trained on contextually shaped text in visual order, the way real cp864 systems stored it.
  • EncodingInfo.is_multibyte is now is_multibyte_cjk. The old name still works with a DeprecationWarning and goes away in 8.0.
  • pipeline/markup.py is now compiled by mypyc (15 modules total), and CI enforces 100% test coverage.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/chardet/chardet/compare/7.6.0...7.7.0

Changelog

Sourced from chardet's changelog.

7.7.0 (2026-10-17)

Features:

  • Added a -m/--mime-type flag to the chardetect CLI, which shows the detected MIME type next to the encoding, like file -i. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude, [#384](https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/384) <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/384>_)

Accuracy:

  • Visual-order Hebrew is now detected. The ISO-8859-8 model trains on both bidi conventions, so 1990s visual-order pages come back as ISO-8859-8 while logical-order text still prefers Windows-1255. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • cp864 Arabic now trains on contextually shaped text in visual order, the way real cp864 systems stored it, instead of isolated letter forms in logical order. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)

Performance:

  • Raising max_bytes on large inputs no longer gets slow. On the compiled build, detect(data, max_bytes=len(data)) on 272 MiB takes about 0.23s for cp1252 and 0.56s for Shift_JIS, down from several seconds. UTF-8 validation and a final decode of the winner still read the whole window, so the answer still decodes it. The other stages stop at a 256 KB evidence cap, which sits above the default max_bytes, so default calls are unchanged, and the default 200 KB cap is still the fastest path. ADR-0006 has the design. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • The UTF-7 + scan is no longer quadratic on line-wrapped base64 like PEM certificates, MIME attachments, and JWTs. 128 KiB of it went from 5.4 seconds to 1.2 milliseconds. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • A head full of unclosed <meta or <?xml tags no longer makes the markup scan quadratic, taking it from about 5 ms to about 20 µs. A literal < inside an attribute value now hides that one tag. (Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>_ via Claude)
  • An EBCDIC charset= or encoding= followed by whitespace and no value no longer makes the declaration scan backtrack quadratically. A crafted 4 KB document used to cost detect() about 60 ms. (Samina <https://github.com/Samin061>, [#403](https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/403) <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/403>)
  • The pure-Python install on CPython scores bigram models with operator.itemgetter instead of a Python loop, making detect() about 1.25x faster and detect_all() about 1.35x faster across the test corpus. Compiled builds and PyPy keep their existing paths. (Afonso Ribeiro <https://github.com/deadstrobe5>_)

Updates `pluggy` from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0
Changelog

Sourced from pluggy's changelog.

pluggy 1.7.0 (2026-10-14)

Deprecations and Removals

  • [#632](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632>_: Hookspec methods defined without self as the first parameter now emit a :class:DeprecationWarning. Add self as the first parameter or use @staticmethod.

Features

  • [#170](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170>_: Hookspecs can now declare default values for arguments, using the usual def myhook(myarg="default") syntax. This is mainly a backward compatibility feature, to allow a hookspec to add new parameters to an existing hook without breaking existing callers. See :ref:hookspec_arg_default for details.

  • [#729](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729>_: Tracing now adds detail where str() is ambiguous: empty strings and strings containing whitespace are quoted, and enums and paths show their repr().

    A value spanning several lines is now displayed as a block instead of running into the surrounding trace.

Bug Fixes

  • [#629](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629>_: Fix hooks failing to register on Python 3.14+ when type annotations use forward references.

  • [#315](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315>_: Source archives created by git archive (including GitHub's "Source code" downloads) now carry version information, so building pluggy from them no longer fails with a missing version.

  • [#442](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442>_: With the addition of default values for hookspec arguments, we also changed the precedence of default values for hookimpl arguments. Previously, if a hookimpl function declared a default for an argument, it was always used, even if the hook call passed an explicit value. Now the precedence is changed to: hook call passed value > hookspec default value > hookimpl default value. See :ref:hookimpl_arg_defaults.

  • [#701](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701>_: Hookimpls and hookspecs are now discovered via :func:inspect.getattr_static, so properties, cached_property and other descriptors are no longer executed while scanning a plugin. Hooks declared through such a descriptor are not supported.

    As a side effect, @hookimpl/@hookspec applied above @classmethod or @staticmethod is now picked up; previously the marker sat on the wrapper where getattr() never saw it. Callables stored directly on a plugin instance -- in its __dict__ or in a __slots__ slot -- keep being called exactly as getattr() returned them, i.e. without an implicit self.

Updates `pytest` from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates `python-dateutil` from 2.9.0.post0 to 3.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from python-dateutil's releases.

3.0.0

This is the last major version of dateutil that will support any version of Python older than 3.11. The next release will be the 4.x series, which will support Python 3.11 and later. We may release fixes for serious bugs in the 3.0.x series, but there are no plans for new features there.

The biggest change in this release is a rewrite of tz.tzfile, which affects nearly every user of dateutil.tz and changes the UTC offset of nonexistent times (see below). dateutil also now depends on the tzdata package, and no longer ships its own time zone database.

Data updates

  • dateutil no longer bundles a copy of the IANA time zone database. Time zone data now comes from the system (see dateutil.tz.TZPATH) or, failing that, from the new tzdata dependency, so the data version is whatever version of tzdata is installed. (gh pr #1130)

Features

  • Rewrote tz.tzfile based on a backport of the zoneinfo module's pure-Python implementation. This adds support for Version 2 and Version 3 tzfile(5) binaries, resolving issues with timestamps beyond 2038 and "slim" format binaries. (gh issues #462, #1059, gh pr #1130)
  • Added dateutil.tz.TZPATH and dateutil.tz.reset_tzpath to allow for runtime configuration of the IANA time zone data search path. These replace the mutable dateutil.tz.TZPATHS list, which has been removed. (gh pr #1130)
  • dateutil now depends on the tzdata package, which gettz consults after the search path and before the Windows registry. On Windows this means that names that are both IANA keys and Windows time zone names, such as "UTC", now return a tzfile rather than a tzwin. (gh pr #1130)

Bugfixes

  • tz.tzfile now follows PEP 495 for times that fall in a gap: with fold=0 it uses the offset from before the transition, and with fold=1 the offset from after it. Previously it always used the offset from after the transition, so for example datetime(2003, 4, 6, 2, 30, tzinfo=tz.gettz("America/New_York")) had a UTC offset of -04:00, where it now has -05:00, the same as with zoneinfo. (gh pr #1130)
  • tz.tzfile objects for fixed-offset zones, such as tz.gettz("UTC"), now return their offset, DST offset and abbreviation when utcoffset, dst and tzname are called with None, as tz.tzutc, tz.tzoffset and zoneinfo.ZoneInfo do. This means that datetime.time objects with such a zone attached are now aware: time(12, tzinfo=tz.gettz("UTC")).isoformat() is now "12:00:00+00:00" rather than "12:00:00". (gh pr #1130)
  • tz.tzfile now infers dst() from the standard time on both sides of each DST period, rather than only the one before it, and does so for each transition rather than for each local time type. This fixes dst() for double summer time (e.g. in Europe/London in the 1940s), for half-hour DST (e.g. in Pacific/Rarotonga) and where the standard offset changed at the same time as a DST transition (e.g. in America/Bahia_Banderas in 2010). Against the standard offsets in the tz database source, the only remaining errors are in Europe/Paris in 1944 and 1945. (gh pr #1130)
  • Fixed rrulestr raising ValueError on experimental X- parameters in an RRULE line (such as GNOME Evolution's X-EVOLUTION-ENDDATE); these are now ignored as RFC 5545 permits. Fixed by @​yajo (gh pr #1374)
  • Enabled pickling and deepcopy of cached rrule and rruleset instances. The cache setting is preserved, and cached results are regenerated on demand without copying locks or generators. Reported by @​niccokunzmann (gh issue #1369). Fixed by @​Jay1023CN (gh pr #1600).
  • Fixed relativedelta.__ne__ raising TypeError when comparing against an unsupported type such as None; it now returns True. Reported and fixed by @​kevinkt1 (gh issue #1157, gh pr #1158)
  • Raised the minimum version of six to 1.6, fixing No module named 'six.moves' errors with older versions. Reported by @​skytreader (gh issue #1415), fixed by @​jdarias3 (gh pr #1424).

Deprecations

  • Deprecated the dateutil.zoneinfo module. The module now acts as a wrapper around the tzdata package and will be removed in a future version. Users are encouraged to migrate to dateutil.tz.gettz or the standard library's zoneinfo module. dateutil.zoneinfo.rebuild.rebuild no longer does anything, and by default raises RebuildDeprecationWarning as an error; filter the warning to call it as a no-op. (gh pr #1130)
  • Deprecated passing gettz a relative key that refers to a file outside of every directory on TZPATH, such as "../../etc/localtime". By default this now raises dateutil.tz.DeprecatedTzKeyWarning as an error; filter the warning to keep the old behavior for now, or pass an absolute path instead. (gh pr #1130)

Documentation changes

  • Added intersphinx to the docs build and cleaned up some broken links. (gh pr #1463)

Misc

  • Releases are now uploaded to PyPI using trusted publishing, and the built sdist and wheel are tested on all supported platforms before upload. (gh pr #1619, #1622)
  • Changes to CI, tests and release tooling that do not affect users of the package: gh pr #1417, #1462, #1464, #1465, #1466, #1467, #1468, #1469, #1470, #1499, #1501, #1504, #1576, #1577, #1578, #1581, #1585.

Updates `tzdata` from 2026.5 to 2026.6
Release notes

Sourced from tzdata's releases.

2026.6: Release of upstream tzdata 2026f

Version 2026.6

Upstream version 2026f released 2026-10-28T06:16:49+00:00

Briefly:

Cuba will not fall back 2026-11-01; stays on -04 through 2027-11-07. No more leap seconds, and leap second tables no longer expire. Improve 1965/1966 data for Brazil.

Changes to future timestamps

Cuba will not fall back to -05 on 2026-11-01 and instead plans to maintain -04 through 2027-11-07.

Changes to past timestamps

In 1965 Brazil ended DST on 03-31 at 24:00 not 00:00, and in 1966 it ended DST on 03-01 at 01:00 not 00:00. (Thanks to Daniel Dias Rodrigues.)

Changes to documentation and commentary

Documentation and commentary now reflect leap seconds’ demise.

Changes to commentary

Discussion on timekeeping in northwestern Ontario has been updated to reflect that provincial regulation has been issued to allow these areas to stay aligned with America/Winnipeg and follow Manitoba’s adoption of year-round -05 after all. (Thanks to Aoun Khan, Chris Walton, and Heitor David Pinto.)

Discussion on timekeeping in Saskatchewan has been updated to document its new Time Act, 2026 which comes into force on 2026-10-30. (Thanks to Heitor David Pinto.) No change is expected.

Updates `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` from 5.11.0 to 5.12.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.12.0 (October 30, 2026)

This release fixes two security vulnerabilities with narrow triggering conditions but serious impact. Affected applications should upgrade to v5.12.0; see Security Fixes below.

It also adds batched transaction startup, client certificate policy controls, and per-query batch timing, and improves connection pool cancellation and type handling. Custom implementations of BatchResults, including mocks, must add the new Tx method.

Security Fixes

  • SQL injection in simple-protocol batches (GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq, high severity). In pgx v5 before v5.12.0, SendBatch using the non-default simple protocol could allow arbitrary SQL execution with the application's database privileges when a queued query ends in a -- comment without a newline and the next query has an attacker-controlled string argument on its first line. Batched queries are now separated by a newline to end such comments. Extended-protocol modes are unaffected. Reported by Igor Kupczyński (@​igor-kupczynski).
  • Bypass of require_auth and channel_binding=require (GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g, high severity). In pgx v5.9.0 through v5.11.0, applications relying on these settings without verifying the server's identity with sslmode=verify-full (or equivalent TLS verification) could accept an impersonating server that skips authentication. The attacker could read queries and parameters and return fabricated results. pgx now enforces authentication completion and required channel binding before accepting the connection. This vulnerability does not bypass TLS server certificate verification. Reported by @​president-xd.

Features

  • Add Batch.BeginTx and BatchResults.Tx to begin a transaction as the first query of a batch, saving the round trip for BeginTx. Call Batch.BeginTx before queuing any queries, consume the begin query's result first, and close the batch before using the transaction. With pgxpool.Pool.SendBatch, the connection remains acquired until the transaction is committed or rolled back. Add FailedBatchResults for wrappers that fail before sending a batch (Timo Furrer)
  • Add TraceBatchQueryData.ReadStartTime and per-query durations to tracelog batch query entries. These measure result consumption, including application time spent reading rows, rather than server execution alone (Yasser-Ameur)
  • pgconn: support the sslcertmode connection parameter, PGSSLCERTMODE environment variable, and Config.SSLCertMode. The default, allow, sends an available client certificate when requested; disable prevents sending one and skips loading certificate/key files; require fails unless the server requests and receives a certificate. require does not guarantee server-side certificate validation, disables TLS session resumption, and stops further host or TLS fallbacks when the certificate requirement fails (k-zshiba)
  • pgtype: add support for PostgreSQL 19's oid8 and oid8[] (k-zshiba)

Changes

  • pgxpool: background attempts to satisfy MinConns and MinIdleConns now have a 60-second timeout, including connection hooks. Initial background connections preserve the constructor context's values but ignore its cancellation and deadline.
  • pgxpool: canceling Acquire during a health-check ping now returns promptly and lets a successful ping return

... (truncated)
