title: fix: hook, installer and agent-integration sweep (#1468, #1452; adopts 5 PRs)
body:
Sweep of the open hook, installer and agent-integration work: two issues fixed, five contributor PRs adopted (cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept), four declined.

## Issues fixed

**#1468: option to turn off the per-turn reinforcement** (`af560e19`)
- Root cause: `caveman-mode-tracker.js` emitted `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (...)` on every prompt whenever a prose mode was active. The only off switch was `defaultMode: "off"`, which turns caveman off entirely.
- Fix: a `reinforce` setting read by `getReinforce()` in `caveman-config.js`. It resolves through the same sources in the same order as `defaultMode`: `CAVEMAN_REINFORCE`, then the nearest repo config that names it, then the user config, then on. Both settings now go through one `resolveSetting()`. Turning it off drops only the reminder. SessionStart's ruleset still injects, and so does a mid-session switch's ruleset, so #975 cannot come back. The tracker resolves `getReinforce` the same way it resolves the other newer exports, so a stale `caveman-config.js` keeps reinforcing. `checksums.sha256` is regenerated. opencode is unchanged because its system-prompt transform is how the ruleset gets delivered there, not a repeat.
- Docs: INSTALL.md (next to `defaultMode`) and CLAUDE.md.
- Tests, all seen failing first: 7 resolution cases in `tests/test_repo_local_config.js` and 4 tracker cases in `tests/test_mode_tracker_ruleset.js`. The tracker cases check that an ordinary prompt emits nothing, that a switch still injects the ruleset without the reminder, that activation from off still injects, and that a repo `.caveman.json` in the session cwd turns it off.

**#1452: Codex hook pins the install-time Node path** (`a4050f6f`)
- Root cause: every hook writer (Codex SessionStart, Claude standalone hooks, Cursor and Copilot CLI sessionStart) persists `absoluteNodePath()`, so the hook stays tied to the runtime manager that was active at install time.
- Fix: a new `--hook-node <node|path>` flag. The default is unchanged: an absolute path, because GUI-launched hosts start without the shell PATH (#249, #805). `node` writes bare `node`, which the shell resolves through the hook's PATH on each run. An absolute path pins that node. A pinned path that does not run as Node ≥ 18 is refused before any write. Bare `node` missing from the installer's PATH only produces a warning, since the agent's PATH is what counts. Values are limited to `node`/`node.exe` so that `installerHookShape` keeps replacing entries in place on re-install. Windows Codex, Cursor and Copilot hooks already write bare `node`, so nothing changes there.
- Docs: `--help`, the INSTALL.md flags table, and the INSTALL.md Codex section, which states the trade-off.
- Tests, all seen failing first: 3 in `tests/installer/codex-hooks.test.mjs` and 1 in `e2e.freshinstall.test.mjs`. They check that the PATH command actually runs the hook through `/bin/sh`, that a plain re-run restores the pin with exactly one entry per event, that an absolute pin works, and that invalid values write nothing.

## Contributor PRs adopted (close as landed)

- **#1467** (@mauhpr) codex: avoid invalid PostCompact hook output (`0ad8e60a`). I checked the claim against Codex's hook docs: PostCompact JSON supports only the common fields (`continue`, `stopReason`, `systemMessage`, `suppressOutput`), so `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is invalid there. The bug is still present on main. The fast hook delegates PostCompact to the same handler. The regression test failed with the line reverted and passed with it.
- **#1411** (@minhhung2556) Root `AGENTS.md` no longer inlines four skill files on every turn (`e45976c7`). Maintainer-only file: not in the npm `files` list and read by no test.
- **#1346** (@jafin01) cavecrew: spot-check subagent absence claims and range-check cited lines (`f692a3d0`). Covers #1262 only; #1278 stays open. The mirror is byte-equal and `compile-registries.mjs` is a no-op.
- **#1269** (@tejgokani) installer: bound hook downloads with an https-only redirect policy, 5 redirects, 60 s, 8 MiB, and partial-file cleanup (5 commits). This decides #1315 question 3 as yes: `install.js` now runs `main()` only under `require.main === module`. I checked that every entry still runs it as main: `node installer/install.js`, a symlinked npm-style bin, `bun installer/install.js`, and both shims (whole suite). This complements the checksum manifest rather than duplicating it; the real gain is the time and size bounds.
- **#1344** (@cyrus-za) installer: fall back to Bun only when Node is absent (#570) (`8576b819`). Node stays first along with its version check. Under Bun the installer is skills-only: `--with-hooks`, `--with-mcp-shrink` and `--only claude` are refused before any write, and automatic hooks are skipped. With real Bun 1.3.7 and PowerShell 7.6.5, all 30 Bun and PowerShell tests passed. Seven of them fail against the base `install.sh`.
- Follow-up `7c8db06e` records both decisions (runtime choice in the shims; requireable installer) in CLAUDE.md.

## Contributor PRs declined

- **#1243** (@AlexCawl): #1242 is real, but this shape is too wide. It moves the Codex manifest to the repo root, which changes the marketplace payload from 6 skills to every `skills/*`. It deletes the repo `.codex/hooks.json`/`config.toml`, and it swaps the mode-resolving `codex-sessionstart.js` for direct `caveman-activate.js` calls. It also adds a third mode-state store (`PLUGIN_DATA`) in `src/hooks`, with no guard against double injection next to the installer-owned Codex hook (#573) or the CLI's native Codex wiring. It now conflicts on CLAUDE.md and the hook checksums. A narrower fix would ship `codex-sessionstart.js` and its payload inside `plugins/caveman/` and declare the hook there.
- **#1348** (@jafin01): By #1307's own analysis the warning is cosmetic, because the plugin hooks use no dependencies. The fix commits a second generated mirror of 78 files and roughly 10k lines (every skill, hook and agent) that each skill or hook PR would have to regenerate. It also changes the marketplace `source`, and existing installs pick that up only after a version bump. That cost is high for a cosmetic note; #1307 stays open as a packaging decision.
- **#1289** (@ALANDVO): The title's premise has been dropped, since `contextFileName` is not an agy plugin field. The remaining diff still bundles rule-body edits the description says were removed: Persistence/Status lines and `/caveman:*` aliases, sent to rule-only hosts and to generated files, while dropping the mode descriptors. #1285 points to agy 1.3.5's unquoted-colon bug, fixed in agy 1.3.6. The `version` field on its own fixes nothing.
- **#1319** (@1TRUDEV): It appends an override after the ultracave/megacave skill body that defeats the load-bearing auto-clarity rule ("Output exclusively code, technical facts, or single-line bullet points"). It puts a prompt change in the hook instead of `SKILL.md`, labels megacave sessions `ULTRA_CAVE`, has no test, and skips the `checksums.sha256` regeneration, so `verify_repo` fails. It cites #575, an unrelated closed compress bug. #1318's own measurements show that a host-level output style re-sent every turn does not move Opus 5.5 either.

## Verification (macOS, Node 22.22.2)

- Root `npm test` (installer + hooks): 709 tests, 702 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped.
- `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js`: 30/30. Each `tests/test_*.js` run directly: all pass.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 293 tests, OK.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: all checks passed, after the rebase onto `ca3a5240` too.
- `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs`: 243 tests, 238 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. Two `opencode-wrap.runtime.mjs` cases fail only when the host session's `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION*` leaks into the env; that is environmental and unrelated.
- packages/cli (`env -u FORCE_COLOR -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, sanitized env): `post-compact.runtime.mjs` failed without #1467's line and passed with it. The hooks/native/codex batch (253 tests) has opencode failures that come from a real `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` on the host PATH; they reproduce with #1467's line reverted. `record policy keeps native hooks…` is a pre-existing timing flake (2 of 3 isolated runs pass; it is Claude-only and never sends PostCompact).
- The five build-rewritten `*.generated` release files were reverted and are not in this branch.

title: fix(ccr): free room in a full recovery store, refuse and repair damage, move stats digests out of request rows
body:
Fixes #1369
Fixes #1370
Fixes #1371

The recovery store (`ccr.db`) and the stats store (`caveman.db`) had three open bugs that all ended the same way: compression or `caveman stats` stopped working, and nothing said why. This PR fixes each one at its root cause and makes the state visible in `caveman status` and `caveman doctor`.

## #1370: a full `ccr.db` refused every compression forever

**Root cause.** `PRAGMA max_page_count` counts every page (rows, indexes, overflow, slack) while the payload budget counts payload bytes, so the reporter's store hit its page cap at ~384 MiB of a 512 MiB budget. The cap was also set on one pooled connection only. Nothing in the store ever deleted a typed object, so from that point every recovery write failed and every input was forwarded uncompressed.

**Fix.**
- Adopted @zsltg's #1374 (page cap on every connection through a store-private driver hook, plus `storage_full_reason`: `payload_budget` / `page_cap` / `disk_full`) and #1375 (lookup + budget check + insert in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, read snapshots for `data_ref` resolution, deterministic owner tie-break, hash-checked fallback copy). Authorship is preserved by cherry-pick.
- New (`b7fd2f5a`): a write refused for capacity runs one reclaim and is tried once more.
  1. **Consolidate** duplicate `RepositoryMap` full copies stored before #1023. Every full copy that nothing points at becomes a reference to one copy whose bytes verify. A copy something already reads stays full, so no existing reference is re-pointed and no reference ever names another reference. Old and new readers get the same bytes before and after. No object is deleted.
  2. **Expire** typed objects past the retention policy, oldest first, until used pages and payload are at 80% of their limits. Archived objects expire once their session's last write is 14+ days old (the hooks' session TTL). Objects of a session that never reached `session.end` expire once it has been idle 30+ days. A full row that a kept row reads through `data_ref` is never deleted. Blob recoveries (`ccr_…`) never expire.
- Each expired id keeps a tombstone (180 days), so retrieval returns `ErrExpired` (wraps `ErrNotFound`) and the MCP tool answers `cave_expired_recovery` ("do not retry") instead of `cave_unknown_handle`.
- Every expiry logs one proxy.log WARN line with counts, sessions and age range, and is recorded in `ccr_meta` for `recovery-store status`.
- Nothing is reclaimed on a store that fails `PRAGMA quick_check`. A reclaim that frees nothing backs off for 10 minutes, and the write passes through as before.
- #1375's owner index is narrowed to `RepositoryMap` rows. Over every full row it cost ~24 MiB on a 160k-object store, all of it counted under the cap.
- A partial `data_ref` index makes "does anything read this owner" a lookup. The lookups repeat `data_ref != ''` so the planner can prove the partial index applies. Without that, each lookup walked every large row's overflow chain to reach `data_ref`, the last column. `TestReclaimLookupsUseIndexes` pins the plans.

**Tests** (each failed on the code before `b7fd2f5a`, run in a scratch worktree with stubs for the new symbols):
- `TestFullStoreExpiresEndedSessionsAndAcceptsNewRecovery`: before: `ccr put: ccr: storage budget exceeded`.
- `TestIdleSessionExpiresOnlyAfterIdleRetention`: before: the object of a 40-day idle session was never expired.
- `TestExpiryKeepsAnOwnerThatAKeptReferenceReads`: before: storage budget exceeded.
- `TestFullStoreConsolidatesDuplicateRepositoryMaps`: before: `ccr typed object put: ccr: storage budget exceeded`.
- `TestConsolidationOwnerMustVerify`: before: consolidated 0 objects.
- Guards that pass both before and after: `TestFullStoreWithNothingExpirableStaysRefusedAndKeepsEverything`, `TestExpiredObjectAnswersExpiredThroughEveryReadPath`, `TestReclaimLookupsUseIndexes`, `TestRetrieveReportsExpiredObjectDistinctly` (mcp).
- #1374's `TestConsolidatedRepositoryMapsLeaveRoom` ran the consolidation SQL by hand. The store now does it itself, so `TestFullStoreConsolidatesDuplicateRepositoryMaps` replaces it.

## #1369: a damaged `ccr.db` stayed damaged, and kept taking writes

**Root cause.** Damage written before the #1008 lock-loss fix (`bd739e15`) persists across upgrades. Nothing ran `quick_check`, so every new write kept landing in the damaged b-tree, where a page with two parents can spread the damage. #1373 stopped wrong bytes reaching a reader, but nothing stopped the writes or offered a repair.

**Fix.**
- `15119e85`: `CheckIntegrity` runs `quick_check` on its own read-only connection, so the store's single connection keeps serving.
  - `CheckIntegrityOnce(version)` skips the full read when the same build already found the store intact.
  - A damaged result, or SQLite reporting `malformed` mid-operation, makes every later write fail with `ErrStoreDamaged`, and the caller passes the original through. Reads go on, hash-checked.
- `bdf80bf3`:
  - `serve` runs the check once per release, off the request path, and wires the proxy logger into the store.
  - `caveman-proxy recovery-store status|check|repair [--force]`:
    - `status` never creates or writes the file. It reports page and payload use, whether the store is full and why, what the next write may expire, the last passing check and the last reclaim.
    - `check` adds `quick_check` and exits 1 when the store is damaged.
  - `repair`:
    - It opens the store with `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE`, so it refuses (exit 3) while any other process has the store open, and nothing else can write during the swap.
    - It copies every row whose bytes match their handle or content hash into a new file. It reads each table three ways: forward scan, reverse scan, then every key the table's index lists.
    - A reference whose owner did not survive is re-pointed to any verified copy.
    - The new file must pass `quick_check` before the swap.
    - The damaged database and its `-wal`/`-shm` are renamed to `ccr.db.damaged-<UTC time>`. They are never edited or deleted.
    - Rows it could not carry over are listed by id.
  - Damage found by the serve-time check or `check` is kept in `run/ccr-integrity.json`, outside the damaged file, so `status` shows it without re-reading 500 MB. A passing check or a repair clears it.

**Tests:**
- `TestDamagedStoreRefusesWritesAfterIntegrityCheck`: before: `put into a damaged store = <nil>`.
- `TestSQLiteCorruptionMidOperationStopsWrites`: before: the next put tried the damaged tree again.
- `TestReclaimNeverWritesToADamagedStore` and `TestCheckIntegrityOnce*`.
- `TestRepairRebuildsDamagedStoreAndKeepsEveryVerifiedRow` covers the #1149/#1369 page-with-two-parents damage plus one row whose bytes do not match its handle. It asserts the backup is byte-identical, every handle is accounted for, the result passes `quick_check`, and writes work again.
- `TestRepairRefusesAStoreAnotherConnectionHolds`, `TestRepairLeavesAnIntactStoreAlone`, `TestRepairResolvesReferencesThroughAnyVerifiedCopy`, `TestInspectStore*`.
- `TestDamageFoundAtServeReachesStatusUntilRepaired` (proxy) runs serve check → status → repair → status.

## #1371: `caveman stats` timed out on a large `caveman.db`

**Root cause.** Each `requests` row kept up to 1,024 cache component digests (66 KB) in `provider_cache_component_sha256`, which sits before the accounting columns. SQLite stores a row's columns in order, so every report read walked that list's overflow pages to reach the token and price columns: about 930 MB for the default 30-day report.

**Fix** (`0d39ede8`):
- A new `request_cache_components(request_id, digests)` table, written in the same transaction as the request row on all three write paths. New rows leave the legacy column NULL.
- `AgentEvidenceForBuild` reads the side row (falling back to a legacy value) and emits `provider_cache_components_available` on every request.
- The running proxy moves legacy lists in the background in 500-row transactions with a pause between them. The progress mark is kept in `store_maintenance`, so a restart resumes, and rows an older proxy writes after a downgrade are still moved.
- Lists older than 14 days expire every 6 h. Request rows, tokens, prices and reports never change. No `DROP COLUMN`, no `VACUUM`.
- CLI: a stats report that runs out of time now says so, names the size of `caveman.db` and suggests `--days 7`, instead of a bare `spawnSync ETIMEDOUT`.

**Tests:**
- `TestRecord*StoresCacheComponentsOutsideRequestsRow` (3 write paths) and `TestRefusedComponentListIsUnavailable` failed on main ("request b3 keeps 66559 digest bytes in its requests row").
- `TestMigrateMovesLegacyComponentListsOutOfRequestsRows`: interrupted and resumed, idempotent, outside-retention cleared without a copy, an older proxy's later rows moved, Summary and 0/7/30-day reports byte-identical.
- `TestExpireCacheComponentsKeepsAccounting`.
- CLI `stats names a timed-out report and a shorter window` failed before.

## `caveman status` and `caveman doctor` (`a52cd754`)

- `status`: a new `recovery-store` off-state appears when the store refuses writes (damaged, or full with nothing old enough to expire), with the proxy's fix and the installed binary spelled out. Only proxies that advertise `recovery_store_v1` are asked.
- `doctor`: runs `recovery-store check` and fails with the reason and the fix.
- Both CLI tests failed before the change.

## Adopted / superseded PRs

- #1374 (@zsltg): adopted as `4c6cc73b`, `c464460b`, `dea549e3`. These are the same trees as the rebased copies in #1375 and #1425.
- #1375 (@zsltg): adopted as `8c32cffc`. `b7fd2f5a` narrows its owner index and changes `ownerLookupSQL` to a literal type.
- #1425 (owner): its three ccr commits are the same as #1374's, and its fourth (`fix(deps): bump golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0`) is already on main as `2cb5e696`.
- #1372 and #1373 were already on main via #1315 (`7a320e59`, `5e91c000`). Verified.

## Not done

- Automatic `VACUUM` of either file: it needs free disk for a full copy and blocks writers. Freed pages are reused, and `recovery-store repair --force` rebuilds `ccr.db` compactly on request.
- Raw-page salvage like sqlite `.recover`: repair recovers every row reachable through any b-tree path or the key index. Rows only on an orphaned page stay in the backup, and their ids are listed when the index still names them.
- Expiry knobs (env vars for the retention floors): the 14/30-day floors are constants matching the hooks' session TTL.

## Verification

- Go: `go test ./proxy/... ./engine/... ./shared/... ./mcp/... ./mem/... -count=1` (umask 022, private `TMPDIR`) passed in 57 packages. One timing test in an untouched package, `TestOIDCKnownKidDoesNotWaitForARefetch` (`proxy/internal/identity`, "after 66ms" under load), failed once and passed on rerun.
- `gofmt -l` is clean on every touched package. `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go vet ./engine ./engine/ccr ./mcp` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./engine/ccr ./proxy/cmd/caveman-proxy` are clean.
- Fail-first:
  - Every test quoted above with a `before:` result was run against the commit before its fix, in a scratch worktree with stubs for the new symbols, and failed as quoted. The repair and inspect tests exercise new API and have no earlier state to fail against.
  - The three new CLI tests were run against `origin/main`'s CLI sources and all three failed.
- CLI suite (`packages/cli`, `env -u FORCE_COLOR -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `--import ./tests/fixtures/sanitize-host-env.mjs`, four batches): 1469 tests, 1455 pass, 14 fail.
  - 13 of the 14 also fail on this machine with `origin/main`'s CLI sources. The causes are a host `caveman-proxy` and `opencode` on `PATH`: bin resolution, the opencode plugin and enable tests, routing pickers, wrap-restart, and agent conformance.
  - The 14th is `binary-pin`: the build rewrites the five `*.generated` release files to bin-v4.0.2, and I reverted them before committing.
  - An `agent-shortcut` flake changed name between runs. A rerun of `agent-shortcut`, `status`, `stats` and `modules-status` passed 46/46.

Updates `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` from 5.11.0 to 5.12.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.12.0 (October 30, 2026)

This release fixes two security vulnerabilities with narrow triggering conditions but serious impact. Affected applications should upgrade to v5.12.0; see Security Fixes below.

It also adds batched transaction startup, client certificate policy controls, and per-query batch timing, and improves connection pool cancellation and type handling. Custom implementations of BatchResults, including mocks, must add the new Tx method.

Security Fixes

  • SQL injection in simple-protocol batches (GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq, high severity). In pgx v5 before v5.12.0, SendBatch using the non-default simple protocol could allow arbitrary SQL execution with the application's database privileges when a queued query ends in a -- comment without a newline and the next query has an attacker-controlled string argument on its first line. Batched queries are now separated by a newline to end such comments. Extended-protocol modes are unaffected. Reported by Igor Kupczyński (@​igor-kupczynski).
  • Bypass of require_auth and channel_binding=require (GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g, high severity). In pgx v5.9.0 through v5.11.0, applications relying on these settings without verifying the server's identity with sslmode=verify-full (or equivalent TLS verification) could accept an impersonating server that skips authentication. The attacker could read queries and parameters and return fabricated results. pgx now enforces authentication completion and required channel binding before accepting the connection. This vulnerability does not bypass TLS server certificate verification. Reported by @​president-xd.

Features

  • Add Batch.BeginTx and BatchResults.Tx to begin a transaction as the first query of a batch, saving the round trip for BeginTx. Call Batch.BeginTx before queuing any queries, consume the begin query's result first, and close the batch before using the transaction. With pgxpool.Pool.SendBatch, the connection remains acquired until the transaction is committed or rolled back. Add FailedBatchResults for wrappers that fail before sending a batch (Timo Furrer)
  • Add TraceBatchQueryData.ReadStartTime and per-query durations to tracelog batch query entries. These measure result consumption, including application time spent reading rows, rather than server execution alone (Yasser-Ameur)
  • pgconn: support the sslcertmode connection parameter, PGSSLCERTMODE environment variable, and Config.SSLCertMode. The default, allow, sends an available client certificate when requested; disable prevents sending one and skips loading certificate/key files; require fails unless the server requests and receives a certificate. require does not guarantee server-side certificate validation, disables TLS session resumption, and stops further host or TLS fallbacks when the certificate requirement fails (k-zshiba)
  • pgtype: add support for PostgreSQL 19's oid8 and oid8[] (k-zshiba)

Changes

  • pgxpool: background attempts to satisfy MinConns and MinIdleConns now have a 60-second timeout, including connection hooks. Initial background connections preserve the constructor context's values but ignore its cancellation and deadline.
  • pgxpool: canceling Acquire during a health-check ping now returns promptly and lets a successful ping return

... (truncated)

Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.61.1
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-02 v1.61.2:

    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

title: Keep generated OpenCode V1 plugin state inside each factory
body:
**What happen**

The generated V1 native plugin keeps `projectDir`, `contexts`, `pending`, and `hostHooks` at module scope. Creating a factory for project B changes the directory used by project A's existing callbacks. Both factories also return the same hook map, so disposing A also ends and clears B's sessions when SessionStart has populated the shared context map.

This is a concurrent-instance residual of closed #1443, not the original missing-cwd case. A single initialized factory now forwards its directory correctly. V2 already keeps its directory and session maps inside `setup()`.

Sources: [shared state and subprocess options](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts), [shared disposal and factory](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts). OpenCode V1 [creates plugin hooks per directory](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts) and [dispatches and disposes each instance's hooks](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts).

**Expected**

Each V1 factory should own its hook map, session maps, and project directory. Creating or disposing another project must not change its callbacks.

**Before/after example**

Source-level reproduction, using one import of the generated V1 module:

1. Create A with `{ directory: "/tmp/project-a" }` and B with `{ directory: "/tmp/project-b" }`.
2. Deliver `session.created` for distinct session IDs through A and B, using a child recorder that returns nonempty SessionStart `additionalContext` so both contexts are cached.
3. Invoke A's `tool.execute.before` callback.
4. Dispose A.

Derived from the current source: A's native calls carry B as both child cwd and payload cwd; its shrink child also uses B. A's disposal iterates both sessions in the shared map. Expected: A keeps project A and disposal touches only A's sessions. Session-ID reuse is not required.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode V1 adapter; source review on Linux x86_64.

**Version / install method**

Caveman main `4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2`, CLI package version 4.0.1. AI-assisted source inspection, not a fresh installed-CLI or OpenCode-session reproduction. No native runtime, model request, or user session was started.

**Isolated verification**

Fresh isolated check: one generated V1 module, two factories and distinct session IDs returned the same hook map. Both recorded SessionStart calls used /audit/project-B, including project A. Only child execution was replaced by a harmless recorder; no OpenCode host was started.

title: Preserve trailing spaces in OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR on all three surfaces
body:
**What happen**

The CLI, unified installer, and copied mode plugin trim `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` before resolving it. On Linux, an absolute directory ending in a space is valid and distinct from the trimmed path. Caveman therefore installs files and writes `.caveman-active` outside the root selected by OpenCode.

This is a byte-preservation residual of closed #1441. The variable's precedence is now fixed; the remaining problem is altering a nonempty path. It does not require changing the whitespace-only fallback policy or rejecting relative roots.

Sources: [CLI](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L9116-L9120), [installer](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/installer/install.js), and [copied plugin](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js). OpenCode's [global service uses the raw environment value](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3ec9b3b0a6936ac38360004870024028c1cc0c71/packages/util/src/global.ts).

**Expected**

Preserve the selected nonempty path's bytes consistently across all three helpers. A directory ending in a space must remain that directory.

**Before/after example**

Source-level input and result, with the trailing space shown inside JSON strings:

```
Input: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR="/tmp/caveman-config "
Got:   "/tmp/caveman-config"
Want:  "/tmp/caveman-config "
```

Every helper computes `selected = value.trim()` and then resolves `selected`. The CLI uses the result for generated plugin/config paths; the installer uses it for its OpenCode payload; the copied plugin uses it for its mode flag. OpenCode selects the untrimmed directory instead.

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: OpenCode integration on Linux x86_64; source-inspected POSIX path case.

**Version / install method**

Caveman main `4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2`, CLI package version 4.0.1. Host selection checked against OpenCode source `3ec9b3b0a6936ac38360004870024028c1cc0c71`. AI-assisted source inspection, not a fresh installer or OpenCode execution. No installation into a real home, model request, or user session was performed.

**Isolated verification**

Fresh isolated check: each of the three actual root helpers resolved "/audit/config with trailing space " to "/audit/config with trailing space". No installer main or OpenCode host was executed.

title: Hermes native route writer corrupts unhandled valid mapping shapes
body:
**What happen**

Native Hermes enable still writes malformed YAML for a valid model mapping whose fields use four-space indentation. This is a residual after #1405, not its fixed document-header or list-item indentation cases.

**Expected**

Either edit the existing route fields with their actual structure, or refuse before writing any integration files. General YAML support is not required.

**Before/after example**


The old provider is then indented below the new scalar `base_url`, rather than remaining a sibling field. The result is not the original valid mapping. Quoted route keys and multiline route values reach the same lexical-writer problem; these should not become separate tickets.

title: Hermes disable removes an edited MCP entry after checking only two fields
body:
**What happen**

After native enable, a normalized `caveman-native` MCP entry can gain a user `cwd` without losing Caveman's ownership proof. Disable then deletes the entire edited entry, including that field. This is a changed-value residual of #1410, not a request to weaken its refusal contract.

**Expected**

Reject destructive restoration when the installed MCP entry has changed, including added fields. Preserve the entry and journal on refusal.

**Before/after example**

In a disposable fixture, enable with an existing `mcp_servers` mapping, remove integration marker comments through normalization, and add `cwd`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  caveman-native:
    command: /fixture/caveman-mcp
    enabled: true
    cwd: /fixture/custom-workdir
```

Keep routing and plugin membership as installed. With their original journal, [`hermesMcpOwned`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14481-L14490) still returns true: it compares only `command` and `enabled`, ignoring the decoded extra `cwd`. [`hermesRestoreOwnedByValue`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14528-L14598) then removes the complete server span. Hermes [uses cwd for stdio launch](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/90d6b98fd86d20981ee06ddd5b7d93e4320f26a4/tools/mcp_tool_transport.py), so this is a semantic user edit, not formatting.

**Isolated verification**

title: Hermes disable removes created parents that now contain foreign siblings
body:
**What happen**

Native disable removes `plugins:` or `mcp_servers:` when enable originally created that parent, even if the user later added unrelated children. Those children survive as text but lose their parent and can move into another section or become invalid YAML.

**Expected**

Remove only the owned plugin/MCP entry. Remove a created parent only when it is still empty. Preserve later foreign siblings at their original parsed paths.

**Before/after example**

Start a disposable config with `model` but no `plugins` or `mcp_servers`; enable native Hermes. After the plugin block's closing marker, add this sibling before `mcp_servers`:

```yaml
  disabled:
    - foreign_plugin
```

The routing and all installed marker blocks remain byte-identical. [`restoreNativeOperation`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L10975-L11189) replaces the journaled plugin block with an empty string. That block includes `plugins:`, so the new `disabled` list loses its parent.

The [normalized fallback](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14528-L14598) has the same cause: it removes created `enabled`, `plugins` and `mcp_servers` rows without checking remaining children. Adding a second enabled plugin or another MCP server reaches the same defect. Related: #1410 and [the preservation contract discussed in #1395](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1395#issuecomment-6446471814). This is not its fixed unchanged-normalization or folded-command case.

title: Hermes plugin membership misses decoded disabled keys and scalar escapes
body:
**What happen**

The #1442 fix still reports a plugin enabled when the deny-list uses a quoted key or an escaped plugin name. Hermes decodes both and refuses to load that plugin; Caveman can still install its files and claim success.

**Expected**

Use the same decoded exact membership and disabled precedence as Hermes, or reject unhandled shapes before any install write. This does not require accepting every YAML form.

**Before/after example**

Source-level fixture:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - caveman_shrink
  "disabled": [caveman_shrink]
```

`hermesNamedPluginMembership(text, "caveman_shrink")` returns `enabled`: the [reader](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L19045-L19080) matches only literal two-space `enabled:`/`disabled:`. With an unquoted disabled key, `["caveman_\x73hrink"]` reaches the same mismatch because [configValue](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L8755-L8757) removes quotes without decoding YAML escapes. Hermes [loads decoded lists and applies disabled first](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/90d6b98fd86d20981ee06ddd5b7d93e4320f26a4/hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py), so both fixtures deny the exact plugin.

These are new decoded-value cases, not #1442's five fixed block/flow, wrong-field and prefix examples. The shared reader also serves `caveman_native`.

title: Hermes MCP presence stays true after a pre-existing server is removed
body:
**What happen**

If native enable finds an existing `mcp_servers.caveman-native`, its journal records `mcp_block: null`. Removing that server later does not clear the native registration check: null is treated as proof that the server is still present.

**Expected**

Keep null as the non-ownership sentinel for disable, but check current server presence separately for recovery status. Do not remove or adopt a foreign registration.

**Before/after example**

Source-level sequence in an isolated fixture:

1. Start with an existing `mcp_servers.caveman-native` entry and enable native Hermes.
2. Keep the resulting journal, then remove only that MCP entry from config.yaml.
3. Evaluate `nativeMcpRegistered("hermes")`.

The [caller](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14046-L14064) calls `hermesMcpOwned`; that helper [returns true immediately for null](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14481-L14490), without reading current MCP config. With no other MCP installation, `anyMcpInstalled()` therefore remains true and the [mcp-missing off-state](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts) is suppressed. Hermes has no such configured server to load.

Related to #1410 and [the non-ownership versus health contract](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1395#issuecomment-6446471814); this is deletion after enable, not unchanged YAML normalization.

title: Hermes hook install succeeds when the second membership list is invalid
body:
**What happen**

An enabled plugin match allows Hermes hook install to write plugin files and an installed marker even when `plugins.disabled` is syntactically invalid. The membership reader treats an unreadable deny-list as no deny, then accepts the enabled item.

**Expected**

Validate both relevant lists before install side effects. Reject syntactically malformed relevant membership lists with a nonzero result and no new payload or success marker. No general YAML support is required.

**Before/after example**

Source-level fixture for `caveman tools hooks install hermes`:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - caveman_shrink
  disabled: [foreign_plugin
```

The disabled flow list never closes, so Hermes cannot parse this config. In Caveman, [`hermesPluginListContains`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L19045-L19080) turns its null parse result into false; the enabled scan returns true. Both install preflight and `enableHermesPluginInConfig` then accept membership, and `installShrinkPluginHermes` writes files before returning success. The hook command consequently writes its success marker.

This is distinct from #1442's corrected five valid-input membership cases. It also does not claim that every duplicate-key spelling is accepted.

title: Hermes native status marks lifecycle hooks healthy for a disabled plugin
body:
**What happen**

After a healthy native install, adding `caveman_native` to Hermes's deny-list leaves Caveman's lifecycle health true. Hermes refuses to load the plugin, so its lifecycle hooks cannot run.

**Expected**

Keep enabled-only membership for ownership and safe disable, but use effective disabled-first membership for native health. Report inactive hooks without removing the user's deny entry.

**Before/after example**

Keep native routing, payloads, journal and MCP intact. Add the plugin to both lists:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - caveman_native
  disabled:
    - caveman_native
```

[`hermesPluginOwned`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L14501-L14506) correctly returns true for safe removal: the installed enabled entry still exists. However, [`nativeIntegrationStatus`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L11729-L11735) uses that same ownership result to report `lifecycle_hooks: true`, without checking effective membership. Hermes's [gate](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/90d6b98fd86d20981ee06ddd5b7d93e4320f26a4/hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py) applies disabled first and does not load it. Other healthy dependencies remaining unchanged is the only prerequisite for the false lifecycle component.

This is a residual after #1442, not its fixed initial-install deny case. Please preserve [the ownership/loadability distinction made when adopting #1446](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1395#issuecomment-6571935359); only the health consumer needs the additional check.

Source review of Caveman main `4bf8898b31c93326a5e5d90999241a1c15b52ed2` (CLI package metadata 4.0.1), Linux x86_64. No current installed binary or Hermes session was run. AI-assisted source inspection and drafting.

title: Bricked with claude code?
body:
**What happen**
No show skill on `/`, no autowrap.

**Expected**
Show skill on `/` and/or autowrap.

**Before/after example**
```
Input:  I just installed a skill called caveman but it doesn't show when I press "/". What's up with that?
Got: 
Let me look at where it got installed.

  Listed 4 directories

The skill never got installed into Claude Code. What you have is the Caveman CLI (@caveman-ai/cli v4.0.1, plus ~/.caveman/), and that's a separate tool. Claude Code only shows / skills that exist as SKILL.md files in ~/.claude/skills/ (or a project's .claude/skills/ or a plugin), and ~/.claude/skills/ doesn't exist on your machine. ~/.caveman/integrations/ is empty too, so it hasn't been hooked up to any agent yet.

Its README says the caveman, ultracave and megacave skills are only written into Claude's skills directory when you do one of these:

caveman claude           # first run of the wrapper writes the skills
# or
caveman enable claude    # writes them without launching through the wrapper

After that, restart Claude Code (or open a new session) and /caveman should appear. If it still doesn't, caveman doctor claude reports what it set up.

Be aware that caveman claude doesn't just add a skill. It runs Claude Code through Caveman's wrapper, which compresses context and meters usage. If all you want is the /caveman command, caveman enable claude is probably the better choice. I haven't run either one, since both change your Claude config. I can run one if you want.

✻ Churned for 25s · done 3:57 PM
```

title: fix(verify-and-stop): preserve quiet verification attempts
body:
## Summary

Keep one verification attempt active until its outcome is known. Treat quiet output as pending, use deadlines and recent successful durations to assess progress, and inspect an existing process before retrying after a lost session handle. A restricted process listing is unavailable evidence, not proof that the old attempt exited.

Add three evaluation scenarios covering a quiet run within its observed duration, a lost elevated session with a restricted process view, and an explicit heap-memory failure. These are evaluation fixtures; no model-based evaluation was run.

## Came from

Came from /retro: yes

Learning-Id: retro-20261107-quiet-verification

- Symptom: a quiet test suite was repeatedly canceled and a duplicate commit attempt was launched. A later run passed after 278.64 seconds.
- Cause: the verification guidance did not distinguish absent output from evidence of a stall or unavailable process visibility.
- Required behavior: preserve one active attempt, poll at useful intervals, and justify a restart with observed failure, a deadline, or evidence that progress is impossible.
- Verification: `skills/verify-and-stop/evals/evals.json` records the expected decisions.

## Validation

- `python -X utf8 tests/verify_repo.py`: passed with Git Bash on PATH.
- Retro evaluation-sample validator and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Root `npm test` on Windows: 615 passed, 36 failed, 57 skipped. This is not a green full-suite result. Failures were in `tests/hooks/caveman-config.test.mjs`, `tests/hooks/plugin-json-windows-hook-path.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/platform-paths.test.mjs`, `tests/installer/shim-security.test.mjs`, and `tests/installer/wedge-release-entry.test.mjs`; these files are unchanged.
- Rechecking the shell-related files with Git Bash resolved the WSL/missing-shell failures. The two hook/path files then had 29 passed and 8 failed; all eight remaining failures were EPERM while creating test symlinks. The shim/release files had 8 passed, 6 skipped, and no failures.
- The initial config failure was also EPERM creating a symlink. No changes to machine permissions or unrelated installer code are included.

title: fix(sdk-python): restore TLS budget after CONNECT reads
body:
A successful HTTP CONNECT reply left the socket's 100 ms read-poll timeout in place for the following TLS handshake. HTTPS middleware requests through a proxy could therefore fail with `deadline` despite a five-second exchange budget. Restore the remaining exchange budget after each successful response read. The new local TLS regression preserves trusted/untrusted certificate and connection-reuse assertions.

The required Windows job also exposed a preexisting timeout-fixture bug: the native-stub preload exits immediately after loading its body, so the slow proxy's timer never runs. Make that fixture wait synchronously. Its five-second delay, 300 ms parent timeout, and timeout-message assertions are unchanged.

Validation:
- Original SDK source fails with a 250 ms server handshake delay and a captured 0.1-second client timeout; corrected source passes with the remaining exchange budget.
- Python SDK: 345 tests passed; wheel build passed.

title: ECONNREFUSED when direct Claude launch uses an unavailable local proxy
Reduce Windows CI latency without weakening coverage — suggestions using OPT
body:
Hi! 👋 I noticed the failed Windows run and wanted to suggest a small CI optimization experiment.

The SDK test test_https_proxy_connect_tunnel_with_custom_ca hit its five-second deadline:

MiddlewareError: Caveman middleware: deadline
This happened roughly seven minutes into the job, and subsequent middleware, extension and workspace checks were skipped. The timeout needs its own diagnosis; optimizing CI would not automatically fix it.

I maintain OPT, a catalog of optimization patterns focused on preserving correctness. A few principles could be useful here:

Remove an unnecessary scheduling dependency. At the failing revision, Windows depends on the entire root-surfaces job, although its scheduling decision uses only that job’s changed-path output. Moving path detection into a small dedicated job could let Windows start earlier while keeping root-surfaces independently required.

Separate independent Windows checks. The Windows lane runs suites serially. Applying OPT’s bounded-parallelism principles, experiment with a few independent jobs, retaining each suite’s prerequisites and required checks. A Python failure should not prevent unrelated suites from reporting. Measure duplicated setup costs: shorter elapsed time does not necessarily mean fewer billed minutes.

Profile before trimming work. Following OPT’s deterministic-test guidance, collect pytest --durations=20 and per-step timings before optimizing fixtures or repeated setup. Preserve assertions, isolation and platform coverage; the Python commands in different working directories are not automatically duplicate coverage.

The existing cancellation of superseded runs and pnpm caching are already useful foundations. Success would mean the same required coverage, faster feedback, and measured runner-minute costs across repeated comparable runs—not a promised speedup or retries that hide the timeout. 🙂

title: fix(opencode): preserve whitespace in configured paths
body:
Fixes #1485.

With `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR="/tmp/config  "`, Caveman installed plugins and wrote mode state under `/tmp/config`. The CLI, unified installer, and copied mode plugin each resolved a trimmed value. OpenCode's [global service at ed0171f](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/ed0171f08ac4018ae648fcca7315b3d717989d50/packages/util/src/global.ts) selects the raw environment value, so those writes could land outside the host-selected directory. Reproduced independently against Caveman main 3dc497a7f858c774d6e15b25e8c6120ef3a0eda8; no equivalent PR found.

Use `.trim()` only to recognize an empty/whitespace-only value, then resolve the original string on all three surfaces. Preserve #1441 precedence and fallback policy, including the intentional treatment of blank values as unset. OpenCode itself uses a nullish fallback; this PR does not broaden scope to change Caveman's existing blank-value policy.

Add production-path regressions for ordinary, leading-space relative, trailing-space absolute, empty, whitespace-only, and unset values with and without XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Tests invoke the built CLI, run the actual installer/uninstaller, and execute a genuinely installed copy of the mode plugin in isolated child processes. Sentinels ensure trimmed/unselected roots remain untouched and uninstall preserves user files. Correct the existing OpenCode CLI fixture to set USERPROFILE as well as HOME on Windows, and register the new suite in the existing Windows compatibility gate.

Validation, entirely on GitHub runners for builds and tests:

- [Before](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/42638039570): the harness confirmed exactly 12 expected production-path failures on Linux and six on Windows, covering all three surfaces. Ordinary paths and existing fallback cases passed.
- [After](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/42638766725): Linux 36/36 new fixtures; Windows 30 passed, six trailing-space filename cases skipped because normal Win32 paths normalize those names. CLI build and TypeScript checks passed on both platforms.
- Existing #1441 regressions passed on both platforms. Full OpenCode installer suites: 50/50 on each. Full CLI hook suite: 86/86 on Linux; that existing POSIX-shell suite was not run wholesale on Windows.
- Final commit only removes the temporary fork verification workflow; tested source and test files are unchanged. Permanent coverage uses the existing CLI and Windows CI gates. All commits are DCO signed.

No dependencies added, real user configurations touched, or build artifacts committed/downloaded locally. Verification exercises Caveman integrations and the copied plugin factory; it does not claim a live OpenCode host session or model request. title: Engine panics on numbered listings with empty lines; proxy drops the request and the conversation can't recover
body:
**Version:** bin-v4.1.0 (`filewrap.go` panic path unchanged since v4.0.1), macOS arm64

**Minimal repro:**
```
seq 1 10 | ~/.caveman/bin/caveman-engine compress
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [10:0]
engine.unwrapFileWrapper  engine/filewrap.go:35
engine.unwrapInput        engine/filewrap.go:133
```
Any input of 9 or more numbered lines with nothing after the number triggers it, for example `seq 2 12`, or `printf '%6d\t\n'` for 1..12. Random integers don't trigger it.

**Cause:** `unwrapListing` strips the line numbers and leaves a body that is only whitespace. `unwrapFileWrapper` then computes `start = len(input)` from `TrimLeftFunc` and `end = 0` from `TrimRightFunc` on the whole input, so `input[start:end]` panics. Computing `end` from `leftTrimmed`, or returning early when `start >= end`, fixes it.

**Impact through the proxy** (`CAVEMAN_RECOVERY=mcp`, Anthropic `/v1/messages`): a tool_result of this shape of at least 512 bytes makes `rewriteRequest` panic inside `CompressSegmentQuery`. `net/http` recovers, so the process survives, but the client connection closes with no response and nothing is sent upstream. No `proxy.log` entry or `requests` row is written, and under `caveman wrap` stderr goes to `/dev/null`, so the failure is invisible. Retries fail the same way, and so does the next request after the user types again, because the block is still in the live zone. The conversation stays stuck. Suggest a per-block `recover` in the proxy's compress loop that keeps the original bytes, plus a log line, in addition to the engine fix.

**Also:** `caveman tools shrink` reports this crash as `"engine unavailable; passthrough — run caveman setup"`, which sends users the wrong way.

Updates `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` from 5.11.0 to 5.12.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.12.0 (October 30, 2026)

This release fixes two security vulnerabilities with narrow triggering conditions but serious impact. Affected applications should upgrade to v5.12.0; see Security Fixes below.

It also adds batched transaction startup, client certificate policy controls, and per-query batch timing, and improves connection pool cancellation and type handling. Custom implementations of BatchResults, including mocks, must add the new Tx method.

Security Fixes

  • SQL injection in simple-protocol batches (GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq, high severity). In pgx v5 before v5.12.0, SendBatch using the non-default simple protocol could allow arbitrary SQL execution with the application's database privileges when a queued query ends in a -- comment without a newline and the next query has an attacker-controlled string argument on its first line. Batched queries are now separated by a newline to end such comments. Extended-protocol modes are unaffected. Reported by Igor Kupczyński (@​igor-kupczynski).
  • Bypass of require_auth and channel_binding=require (GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g, high severity). In pgx v5.9.0 through v5.11.0, applications relying on these settings without verifying the server's identity with sslmode=verify-full (or equivalent TLS verification) could accept an impersonating server that skips authentication. The attacker could read queries and parameters and return fabricated results. pgx now enforces authentication completion and required channel binding before accepting the connection. This vulnerability does not bypass TLS server certificate verification. Reported by @​president-xd.

Features

  • Add Batch.BeginTx and BatchResults.Tx to begin a transaction as the first query of a batch, saving the round trip for BeginTx. Call Batch.BeginTx before queuing any queries, consume the begin query's result first, and close the batch before using the transaction. With pgxpool.Pool.SendBatch, the connection remains acquired until the transaction is committed or rolled back. Add FailedBatchResults for wrappers that fail before sending a batch (Timo Furrer)
  • Add TraceBatchQueryData.ReadStartTime and per-query durations to tracelog batch query entries. These measure result consumption, including application time spent reading rows, rather than server execution alone (Yasser-Ameur)
  • pgconn: support the sslcertmode connection parameter, PGSSLCERTMODE environment variable, and Config.SSLCertMode. The default, allow, sends an available client certificate when requested; disable prevents sending one and skips loading certificate/key files; require fails unless the server requests and receives a certificate. require does not guarantee server-side certificate validation, disables TLS session resumption, and stops further host or TLS fallbacks when the certificate requirement fails (k-zshiba)
  • pgtype: add support for PostgreSQL 19's oid8 and oid8[] (k-zshiba)

Changes

  • pgxpool: background attempts to satisfy MinConns and MinIdleConns now have a 60-second timeout, including connection hooks. Initial background connections preserve the constructor context's values but ignore its cancellation and deadline.
  • pgxpool: canceling Acquire during a health-check ping now returns promptly and lets a successful ping return
