Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.62.0

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-07 v1.62.0:

    • Add illumos/amd64, tested on an OmniOS builder. Resolves [GitLab issue #210](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/210), thanks Jasper Siepkes (@​siepkes), who also started the modernc.org/libc port!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.16.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.8.0; SQLite stays 3.54.1 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.80.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in syncing with fdatasync(2), off by default: Fdatasync(true) makes commits sync with fdatasync instead of fsync, process-wide, which skips the timestamp update fsync forces and keeps a commit just as durable. FdatasyncEnabled reports the setting; on macOS and Windows Fdatasync returns ErrFdatasyncUnavailable. Resolves [GitHub issue #10](modernc-org/sqlite#10), thanks aibeshkov!
    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).

body:
Bumps the npm group with 1 update in the /extension directory: [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright). Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.64.1 to 1.65.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.1

Bug Fixes

  • #43936 [Regression]: decorated class with a static field fails to load in 1.65 ("_initClass is not a function") with useDefineForClassFields: false
  • #43934 [Bug]: Test locations are one column off under Bun 1.4.4+

Browser Versions

  • Chromium 159.0.8154.6
  • Mozilla Firefox 159.0
  • WebKit 27.2

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.39.2 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.3 - 04 Nov 2026

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

Updates `python-dateutil` from 3.0.0 to 4.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from python-dateutil's releases.

4.0.0

dateutil 4.0 requires Python 3.11 or later and no longer depends on six. Apart from that, the changes in this release are bug fixes, but note that isoparse is now stricter about the numeric fields it accepts (see below).

Deprecations

  • Dropped support for Python versions older than 3.11 and removed the dependency on six, along with Python 2 compatibility helpers that were never part of the public API, such as dateutil.tz.tzname_in_python2. (gh pr #1625)

Bugfixes

  • parser.isoparse, and the isoparser methods parse_isodate, parse_isotime and parse_tzstr, now require each numeric field to be exactly the expected number of ASCII digits. Strings that were previously accepted, such as 20200728121240 (read as 21:24), 2014- 4-21 and 2_14-04-21, and offsets such as +-1:00, now raise ValueError. tzical applies the same check to TZOFFSETFROM and TZOFFSETTO. Reported by @​janos-gonye (gh issue #1074). Fixed by @​varun3257 (gh pr #1617).
  • Fixed an issue where iterating over a cached rrule or rruleset could hang forever if another iterator over the same rule had already completed the cache, for example when a cached rrule was included twice in an rruleset. Reported by @​bysiber (gh pr #1455). Fixed by @​pganssle (gh pr #1655).
  • Unpickling a tzutc now gives the dateutil.tz.UTC singleton, and unpickling a tzoffset gives the same object as calling tzoffset(name, offset). Previously unpickling bypassed the singleton-generation logic. Reported and fixed by @​masipcat (gh issue #1051, gh pr #1053).
  • relativedelta(yearday=366) now resolves to December 31 in leap years. Previously it gave December 30, the same date as yearday=365. Reported and fixed by @​Master-Norna (gh pr #1583).

Misc

  • The build backend is now Hatchling, and the package metadata is in pyproject.toml. Versions are still derived from Git tags and exposed as dateutil.__version__. This mainly affects people building dateutil from source. (gh pr #1637, #1638)
  • Changes to CI, tests and release tooling that do not affect users of the package: gh pr #1636, #1644, #1645, #1646, #1648, #1649, #1650.

title: fix(engine): guard unwrapFileWrapper against whitespace-only input
body:
Closes #1508

## Problem

`seq 1 10 | caveman-engine compress` panics:

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [10:0]
engine.unwrapFileWrapper
	engine/filewrap.go:35
```

`unwrapListing` strips the bare-number gutters from a numbered listing
whose lines are empty, leaving a body that is only whitespace. `unwrapFileWrapper`
then computes `start = len(input)` from the left trim but `end = 0` from
the right trim, and `input[start:end]` panics. The proxy drops the request
and the conversation can't recover.

## Fix

Derive `end` from the already left-trimmed slice instead of from the whole
input (`engine/filewrap.go`):

```go
end := start + len(bytes.TrimRightFunc(leftTrimmed, unicode.IsSpace))
```

This gives the same `end` for every non-whitespace-only input, and
`start <= end` by construction, so a whitespace-only body now passes
through untouched (fail-closed, per the engine's conventions).

## Tests

- New `TestUnwrapInputNumberedListingEmptyLines` reproduces the exact
  `#1508` input (`1\n2\n...\n10\n` through `unwrapInput`); it panicked
  before the fix and passes after. Whitespace-only inputs
  (`""`, `" "`, `"   \n\t  \n"`) added to the `TestUnwrapFileWrapper`
  no-op table.
- `go test ./engine/...`: all packages pass except `engine/ccr`, where
  `TestPersistentStoreBudgetRefusesNewRecoveryAndPreservesExisting` fails
  because my local `GOTMPDIR` is group-writable (`2770`); it fails
  identically on clean `main`, so it is unrelated to this change.
- End-to-end with the built binary: both repro forms from the issue
  (`seq 1 10` and `printf '%6d\t\n'`) now exit 0 and pass the input
  through unchanged.

title: fix: daily triage 2026-11-12 — engine panic fail-open + OpenCode configured path bytes
body:
Daily triage run for 2026-11-12. 57 open issues and 25 open PRs reviewed; no prior `daily-triage/` PR was open.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not merge as-is — this branch violates the DCO policy, and it is my fault.**
> `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires a `Signed-off-by` on every commit (line 15) and says to *"retain commit authorship and DCO sign-off"* (line 37). Both contributors **did** sign their work; I destroyed those trailers by rewriting the engine commit message and squashing the OpenCode series. My own two commits were never signed.
> The remedy needs a force-push, which this run is instructed never to do. Recommended fix, which requires nobody to re-sign anything — rebuild from the contributors' original signed commits and re-apply mine with `-s`:
> ```
> git cherry-pick 79a56fe                            # zichen0116/caveman fix/filewrap-whitespace-panic, signed
> git cherry-pick d8305f8 d34b06c 158a435 aa772de    # anirudhqwerty/caveman fix/opencode-config-path-whitespace, signed
> # then re-apply the two proxy commits with git commit -s
> ```
> The code and tests below are unaffected and fully verified; this is purely commit metadata. Caught by Devin Review — details in [that thread](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/pull/1518#discussion_r4547576604).

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1508 | `unwrapFileWrapper` took `start` from `TrimLeftFunc` over the whole input and `end` from `TrimRightFunc` over the whole input. A numbered listing whose lines carry nothing after the number leaves a whitespace-only body after `unwrapListing`, so `start = len(input)` and `end = 0` and `input[start:end]` panicked. | Every engine consumer (CLI `caveman-engine compress`, proxy, MCP, SDKs); all OS | `engine/filewrap_test.go` — `TestUnwrapInputNumberedListingEmptyLines` + 3 whitespace cases | #1517 |
| #1508 | A panic in the `Compressor` seam unwound the whole handler. `net/http` recovered so the process lived, but the client connection closed with no response, nothing went upstream, and no `requests` row or `proxy.log` line was written — invisible under `caveman wrap`, where stderr goes to `/dev/null`. Every retry failed identically because the block stayed in the live zone. | Proxy compress + observe-estimate paths, all providers; all OS | `proxy/internal/gateway/compress_panic_test.go` — 3 tests (compress, estimate, `ErrAbortHandler` passthrough) | — |
| #1485 | All three OpenCode root helpers computed `selected = value.trim()` and then resolved the **trimmed** string. A nonempty path keeping its own bytes is what the host reads, so caveman installed its payload and wrote `.caveman-active` outside the selected root while reporting success. Byte-preservation residual of #1441. | OpenCode on Linux/POSIX (CLI, unified installer, copied mode plugin) | `packages/cli/tests/opencode-config-dir.runtime.mjs` — 36 cases, all three surfaces × 6 value shapes × XDG/home | #1507 |

### Verification notes

- **#1508 engine** reproduced on this tree before the fix: `panic: slice bounds out of range [10:0]` at `engine/filewrap.go:35`, matching the reporter's trace exactly.
- **#1508 proxy** the new tests fail for the right reason without the guard (panic unwinds at `proxy.go:443`). The guard is **per segment**, so one bad block does not cost the rest of the request its compression, and a decline is already a first-class outcome on both loops (`out == nil` keeps the block raw, `tb <= 0` skips the estimate) — so recovering lands the request on the documented byte-safe fail-open path rather than dropping it. The panic is logged at **error** with its stack, so a defect behind it stays findable rather than silently absorbed. `http.ErrAbortHandler` is re-raised untouched, since absorbing net/http's control-flow sentinel would turn an intended abort into a silent success.
- **#1485** adopted test verified failing without the fix (6/6 trailing-space cases) and passing with it (36/36). Fixed on all three surfaces in one commit because they cannot share a function (compiled Bun plugin, dependency-free installer) and a fix in one leaves the other two writing elsewhere. The test asserts the roots that must **not** be written stay untouched, and that uninstall preserves a user file.
- One migration edge worth knowing: a user who previously installed under the trimmed path gets a fresh install under the untrimmed one, leaving the old payload orphaned. No data loss, and the old location was never read by the host — that was the bug.

### Full suite

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | 709 tests, **15 failures identical to `origin/main`** (test-name sets diffed, byte-identical) — pre-existing, environment-dependent: curl flag paths, gemini extension, hook integrity manifest, `caveman-shrink` signal forwarding, OMP |
| `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` | 30/30 pass |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | 304 tests, OK |
| `python tests/verify_repo.py` | all checks passed |
| `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` | 0 failures |
| `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` | 281 tests, 0 failures (includes the newly registered OpenCode test) |

Nothing under `src/hooks/` changed, so `src/hooks/checksums.sha256` needs no regeneration — confirmed by `verify_repo.py`.

**CI:** the one red check, `govulncheck`, is a Go **standard-library** advisory and not from this PR — this branch touches no `go.mod`/`go.sum`, and 50 of its 51 call sites are in files this branch never opens (the 51st is pre-existing code outside its edited ranges). Evidence in a separate comment. Everything else completed green.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1489, #1486–#1492 (Hermes cluster, 7 issues)**: not fixed. Reproduction requires executing a test file from an external fork, which this environment's sandbox denied (`Code from External`), and the hard rule here is no fix without a failing test first. I will not adopt ~200 lines of new YAML-decoding logic in the installer path unverified. See the PR review below — the fix looks right and needs one maintainer test run.
- **#1495 claude, #1496 codex, #1497 qwen, #1516 gemini, #1225 pi (agent-drift)**: reproduced and probed, deliberately **not** bumped. I installed each newer version and ran the real gate, `node agents/probe-installed.mjs`: `version_ok` and `help_ok` are **true** for claude 2.1.322, codex 0.167.2, gemini 0.68.0, qwen 0.27.2 and pi 1.5.2. I reverted the bumps because each profile's `verified_by` field attests *which lane* verified the pin ("CI pinned-binary probe … ubuntu-latest with Node 24.16.0 … route check last run on X"). My probe ran on Linux/Node 22.23.4 locally and I did not re-run any route check, so writing that attestation would have been a fabricated verification claim. See "Needs maintainer decision".
- **#1506 openclaw**: could not verify. `openclaw@2026.11.3` refuses to install on Node 22.23.4 (requires `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`); the CI lane runs Node 24.16.0 and would install it.
- **#1510 hermes**: not probed — needs a git clone plus `uv` and Python 3.14.
- **#1318 (ultracave ignored on Opus 5.5)**: not a reproducible code defect. The hooks inject the ruleset correctly and the reporter confirms the banner fires every turn; the model is not following the injected rules. That is prompt/model-adherence work in `skills/ultracave/SKILL.md`, not a hook bug, and no test in `tests/` can pin it. Needs a design decision.
- **#1503 (ECONNREFUSED on direct `claude` launch)**: reproduced by inspection and it is a question of intended behaviour — whether `setup` should auto-start the proxy or warn when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a dead local port. Design decision, not a bug fix.
- **#1504 (Windows CI latency)**, **#1484**, **#1093**, **#1350**, **#1272**, **#1278**, **#1217**, **#1216**: design proposals and feature requests — triaged only, per the run's rules.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1517 by @zichen0116** — **adopted**, cherry-picked with authorship preserved. The diagnosis and the fix are both right: deriving `end` from `leftTrimmed` is the minimal correct change and `start <= end` holds by construction. Its test additions are good; I kept them as written. *(Their DCO sign-off was intact on the original and I dropped it — see the note at the top.)*
- **#1507 by @anirudhqwerty** — **adopted**, cherry-picked (4 commits squashed to one, author preserved). Correctly keeps the whitespace-only fallback policy and the relative-root behaviour, changing only the bytes of a nonempty selected path, and fixes all three surfaces rather than one. The runtime test is unusually thorough — it drives real install/uninstall on each surface and asserts the wrong roots stay clean. I also kept its `USERPROFILE` fixture isolation, and dropped the temporary `.github/workflows/verify-1485.yml` the PR itself removed. *(The squash is what destroyed their four sign-offs — see the note at the top. Squashing was unnecessary and I should not have done it.)*
- **#1501 by @Ha1baraA11** — **needs one maintainer test run, then likely adopt.** Addresses #1489 and incidentally hardens #1491. The approach is right and fails closed in the direction this repo wants: it adds an explicit `"unhandled"` membership state and refuses to write config on YAML shapes it cannot decode, instead of guessing. I could not execute its tests here (sandbox denied running an external fork's test file), so I did not adopt it unverified. Worth noting for review: it widens the key regexes to quoted forms, adds a YAML scalar decoder that rejects unknown escapes, and makes `hermesFlowSequenceItems` return `false` on nested flow collections rather than descending — that last one is a behaviour narrowing, so please confirm no existing valid config relied on nesting.
- **#1311 by @JuliusBrussee** — **stale.** Bumps the Pi pin to 1.3.0; installed Pi is now 1.5.2 (#1225), so this pin is already behind. Either refresh it or close in favour of a 1.5.2 bump.
- Dependabot **#1511–#1515** — not reviewed; routine dependency bumps, left for the maintainer.
- **#1427, #1404, #1393, #1329, #1288, #1273, #1267, #1036, #1421, #1424, #1338, #1396, #1220, #1498, #1499** — feature work and docs, out of scope for a bug-fix triage run.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **The DCO breakage at the top of this body.** It needs a force-push to repair and this run is instructed never to force-push. Either grant that for the next run, or rebuild the branch with the commands above.
2. **Can a triage run bump agent pins at all?** The blocker is `verified_by`, not the probe. I have clean probe evidence for five agents (above) but cannot honestly write "CI pinned-binary probe … Node 24.16.0". Options: (a) let `agent-conformance` bump its own pins and write the attestation, (b) define a weaker honest form of `verified_by` for a local probe, or (c) have triage bump the pin and leave `verified_by` untouched until the lane reruns. I did not choose on your behalf — this is a claim-honesty policy call.
3. **Pi 1.0.4 → 1.5.2 (#1225)** deserves a human look regardless. `packages/pi-extension` is bundled into the CLI and published on `pi-v*` tags, and the probe only exercises `--version`/`--help`; a five-minor jump could move the extension API without the probe noticing.
4. **#1501's flow-sequence narrowing** (nested `[`/`{` now rejected outright) — intentional per the issue, but it is a compatibility decision.
5. **#1318** needs a call on whether ultracave adherence on Opus 5.5 is a skill-wording problem to iterate on, or should be documented as a model limitation.
6. **Sandbox permission**: verifying contributor PRs properly means running their tests. This run was blocked from doing that for #1501. If you want daily triage to adopt contributor fixes reliably, that capability needs granting.
7. **`govulncheck`** flags a Go stdlib advisory on `main` as well as here. Fixing it means a toolchain bump — out of scope for triage, but worth a look on its own.

title: Independent benchmark of caveman v4.0.1 in Claude Code, and a SessionStart side effect worth knowing about
body:
Hi, and thanks for caveman. I've been building **TokenTrial** (https://github.com/bishtashish708/tokentrial), an open benchmark that runs coding-agent tasks with and without a token-saving tool and reports cost per correctly solved task. caveman v4.0.1 was one of the first tools tested. The results and raw data are public in the repo, but I'm sharing them with you before announcing them anywhere, so you can check the setup and push back if anything's off.

**Setup**
- Claude Code 2.1.252, headless (`claude -p`), model `claude-haiku-5-5`.
- 10 tasks × 8 repeats per arm. Answers are checked with hidden tests.
- Cost covers every API call, priced by token type.

**A Claude Code side effect you may want to know about.** In a smaller pilot, caveman looked 29% cheaper per solved task. Most of that came from Claude Code, not from caveman's compression:
- Claude Code 2.1.252 makes a small background `claude-haiku-4-5` call to generate a session title (about 940 input and 11 output tokens). It **skips that call whenever any `SessionStart` hook is configured**.
- caveman's SessionStart hook triggers the skip. So does a project hook that only runs `true`, and so does caveman with its mode set to `off`.
- An empty plugin or a `UserPromptSubmit` hook does not trigger the skip.

So caveman users really do avoid that call. But any SessionStart hook would avoid it too, which is why I compared caveman with a do-nothing SessionStart hook.

**Result**
- **−9% vs baseline (95% CI −21% to +5%), and −0% vs the do-nothing-hook control (CI −10% to +11%).** That's no measurable cost effect in this setup.
- Mean output fell about 11% against the control (5,185 vs 5,796 tokens).
- Output was only about 40% of a run's cost here; cache reads and writes make up most of the rest. So the output saving didn't show up in the total.
- Solve rate was 77/80 (2 misses on a DST-aware cron task, 1 on a git forensics task), against 79–80/80 for the other arms. That's too few failures to read anything into.

**How caveman was set up.** Please tell me if this differs from how you'd recommend running it.
- caveman v4.0.1 at commit `d262ab3`, loaded with `--plugin-dir` and `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=caveman`. It was confirmed active in 80/80 runs.
- The "nudge already shown" marker was pre-seeded, so runs model a returning user rather than a first session.
- caveman's state files were removed after each run.
- I didn't test a marketplace install directly, to avoid modifying my global config. It registers the same SessionStart hook, so I'd expect the same behavior.

**Caveats.** One model (Haiku already writes fairly concise output), one Claude Code version, synthetic small-to-medium tasks, and a single caveman version. v4.1.0 came out shortly before the runs were pinned and wasn't tested. Larger tasks with longer answers could well show a different result.

**Links**
- Leaderboard: https://bishtashish708.github.io/tokentrial/
- Write-up: https://github.com/bishtashish708/tokentrial/blob/main/results/v0.2/FINDINGS.md (see "Why caveman's pilot saving disappeared")
- Raw records and scrubbed transcripts: https://github.com/bishtashish708/tokentrial/tree/main/results/v0.2/raw
- The caveman adapter: `src/tokentrial/arms.py` (`_setup_caveman`)
- Reproduce: `uv run tokentrial install-arms`, then `uv run tokentrial run --repeats 8 --arm baseline --arm noop-hook --arm caveman`

I'd welcome a critique of the method, or a configuration you think represents caveman better. I'll include your response, or a rerun, in the published results. Feel free to close this if it isn't useful here.

title: Same filewrap.go:35 panic from a second trigger: a tool result `{"exit_code":N,"output":"\n"}` silently kills the proxy and the session never recovers
body:
## Summary

A tool result whose text is a compact JSON object with an `exit_code` key and a **whitespace-only `output` value, where `output` is the last key**, makes `engine.unwrapFileWrapper` panic (`slice bounds out of range [1:0]`). This is the same panic site as #1508 (`engine/filewrap.go:35`) reached from a much more common input shape.

Through the proxy the failure is invisible: the connection is closed with no response, nothing is written to `proxy.log`, no `requests` row is created, and the upstream is never contacted. The client retries, every retry fails the same way, and the conversation stays permanently broken because the block remains in the live context.

Because the poison block enters the history at an arbitrary point in a session, it looks like a size/context problem ("requests stop going through at ~45% of context") rather than a content bug.

## Environment

- caveman 4.1.0 / `bin-v4.1.0` (npm `@caveman-ai/cli@4.1.0`, which is current)
- macOS 26.6.2, x86_64, proxy binary `caveman-proxy` (Mach-O x86_64)
- proxy env: `CAVEMAN_MODE=compress`, `CAVEMAN_RECOVERY=mcp`, `CAVEMAN_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8787`, `CAVEMAN_PROXY_OWNER=wrap`, `CAVE_ENGINE_TOON=best-of`
- client: codex-cli 0.167.2, provider `base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt`, `wire_api=responses`, `requires_openai_auth=true`

## Repro 1 — engine only (no agent, no account)

```bash
printf '{"exit_code":0,"output":"\n"}' | ~/.caveman/bin/caveman-engine compress
```

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [1:0]

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine.unwrapFileWrapper({0x..., 0x1, 0x8})
	github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine/filewrap.go:35 +0x554
github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine.unwrapInput({0x..., 0x1d, 0x200})
	github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine/filewrap.go:133 +0x37b
github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine.(*Engine).Compress(0x..., {0x..., 0x1d, 0x200}, ...)
	github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine/engine.go:73 +0x7f
main.runCompress(...)
	github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/engine/cmd/caveman-engine/main.go:127 +0x2e5
```

Exit code 2. `caveman compress < same input` produces the identical panic.

## Repro 2 — through the proxy (deterministic, no credentials needed)

```bash
cat > /tmp/poison.json <<'JSON'
{"input":[{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"c1","output":"{\"exit_code\":0,\"output\":\"\\n\"}"}]}
JSON

curl -sS -m 10 -o /dev/null -w 'http=%{http_code}\n' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer probe' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/poison.json \
  http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt/responses
```

Observed:

```
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
http=000
```

in 0.00–0.03 s. No `proxy.log` line, no new `requests` row.

**The upstream is never contacted.** With the same bogus bearer token, any non-poison request returns the upstream `401` (the proxy forwards and upstream answers); the poison request dies locally before that. `net/http` recovers the panic, so the process survives and keeps serving other traffic — only the offending connection closes, with an empty reply.

The same happens for `type: "custom_tool_call_output"` (`output: [{type: "input_text", text: ...}]`). The identical text inside a `message` item does **not** trigger it — the unwrap only runs for tool results.

## Trigger rule

The text of a tool result must be compact JSON (no spaces) with `exit_code`, a non-empty whitespace-only `output`, and nothing after the `output` value:

| tool result text | result |
|---|---|
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\n"}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":137,"output":"\n"}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\t"}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\r\n"}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":" \t\n "}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":0,` + newline + `"output":"\n"}` | **panic** |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\n"}` + trailing newline | ok (401) |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\n" }` (space before `}`) | ok (401) |
| `{"exit_code": 0, "output": "\n"}` (spaces in JSON) | ok (401) |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"\n","x":1}` (output not last) | ok (401) |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":""}` (empty, not whitespace) | ok (401) |
| `{"exit_code":0,"output":"x"}` | ok (401) |

Reads like `end` is computed from the right-trimmed wrapper while the value body trims to nothing, so `input[start:end]` gets `start > end` — the same shape as #1508 (there `[10:0]`, here `[1:0]`).

## How it looks in a real agent session (codex)

Observed real payload block (106 bytes), produced by codex unified-exec for a command that printed only a newline:

```json
{"chunk_id":"0efd58","wall_time_seconds":0.000014707,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1,"output":"\n"}
```

Once such a block is in the request history, every following request from that session fails:

```
ERROR: Reconnecting... 1/5
...
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
ERROR: stream disconnected before completion: error sending request
```

client-side log:

```
Request failed method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt/responses is_timeout=false is_connect=false
```

`is_connect=false` / `is_timeout=false` plus a sub-100 ms failure matches "connection accepted, then closed without a response". Retries never help, because the block is still in the context; the session has to be forked/trimmed or the proxy bypassed.

## Control: the same conversation works without the proxy

Same codex session (`codex exec fork <thread>`, 446 872 input tokens — 94% of the 475 000-token window), same prompt:

- through caveman (`127.0.0.1:8787/chatgpt`): 5 reconnects, `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request`
- directly against `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (`wire_api="responses"`, `requires_openai_auth=true`): completes normally

So this is not payload size, not the network, not account limits. For reference, the same proxy served requests up to 3 198 590 bytes successfully earlier that day.

## Suggested fix

1. In `unwrapFileWrapper`, return early when `start >= end` (or compute `end` from `leftTrimmed`), as suggested in #1508.
2. In the proxy's per-block/per-segment compress loop, add `recover()` that keeps the original bytes and continues — a single poison block should degrade to "not compressed", not to a dropped request.
3. Log the recovered panic with the block size and a request id, and write a `requests` row, so this stops being invisible.
4. Same for `caveman-engine compress`: exit non-zero with a readable error instead of a Go panic (and `caveman tools shrink` currently reports engine panics as `"engine unavailable; passthrough — run caveman setup"`, which misdirects).

A one-line guard on the trim bounds plus a `recover` in the proxy loop would make all of #1508, this report, and any future engine edge case non-fatal.

title: Default proxy port 8787 is also wrangler dev's default
body:
`caveman-proxy` listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default. `wrangler dev` (Cloudflare Workers) uses the same port by default.

- #1238 handles this at first setup: when 8787 is taken, Caveman moves to the next free port.
- When Caveman is set up first, it keeps 8787, and `wrangler dev` fails to start afterwards.
- Many projects hardcode 8787 in their configs, READMEs and CI files. Caveman writes its own URL into each agent's config, so its port is rarely typed by hand.

Would a default port that common dev tools don't use be an option?

**Repro:** run `caveman setup` while nothing listens on 8787, then run `wrangler dev` in a Workers project.

Caveman 4.0.1, Linux.

Thanks!

title: fix(middleware-python): keep Bedrock clones working on anthropic 2.6+
body:
Refs #1494.

## Summary

Stop passing `aws_profile` to `AnthropicBedrock.copy()` twice on **anthropic 2.6.0 and later**, where it raises `TypeError` for any Bedrock client created with a profile, and move the tested latest pin to **anthropic 2.8.0**.

- Pass `aws_profile` through `_extra_kwargs` only when the SDK's `copy()` has no `aws_profile` parameter. Earlier releases still need it.
- Stub the SigV4 signer in the contract test where anthropic 2.7+ binds it, as well as at the old module path.
- Set `constraints/latest.txt` to tested **anthropic 2.8.0** (was 2.1.0).
- Correct the README's `anthropic` row, which still showed `1.0–<2` and `1.8.0`, to the gate's `<3` and the new pin.

`COMPATIBILITY`, the `anthropic` extra, CHANGELOG and package versions are unchanged: 2.8.0 is already inside `>=1.0,<3`. This PR changes four middleware files in one commit, which carries a DCO sign-off.

## Why

#1494 has reported the nightly canary red since November 7. The failing lane is `canary / anthropic`, on `test_anthropic_cloud_clients_keep_the_callers_credentials`; #1474 noted the same `TypeError` when anthropic 2.6.0 came out. Two SDK changes are behind it.

**anthropic 2.6.0** made `AnthropicBedrock.copy()`, sync and async, take `aws_profile` and keep it, along with a custom `http_client`, on the clone. `_append()` still passed the profile through `_extra_kwargs`, so `copy()` received it twice:

```text
TypeError: anthropic.lib._platform_client.copy_platform_client() got multiple values for keyword argument 'aws_profile'
```

`with_caveman_anthropic()` raises this for any Bedrock client created with a profile, not only in the test. Before 2.6, `_extra_kwargs` is still the only way to keep the profile, so the workaround stays for those releases. The adapter reads `copy()`'s signature rather than comparing version numbers, as `agno.py` already does with `inspect.signature`.

| anthropic | plain `copy()` keeps `aws_profile` / `http_client` | `aws_profile` through `_extra_kwargs` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0.0, 2.5.0 | no / no | accepted |
| 2.6.0, 2.7.0, 2.8.0 | yes / yes | `TypeError` |

**anthropic 2.7.0** removed `anthropic.lib.bedrock._auth`. The Bedrock client module now imports `get_auth_headers` from `anthropic.lib.aws._auth` once, at import. The test stubbed the old module, so on 2.7+ the real signer ran and asked for `botocore`. The test now also patches the name in `anthropic.lib.bedrock._client`, with `raising=False` so older SDKs are unaffected. This half is test-only.

## Validation

Tests used built wheels installed into fresh environments, ran from outside the checkout, and required the Anthropic adapter through `CAVEMAN_REQUIRED_ADAPTERS=anthropic`. They used local fixtures and dummy credentials, with no live-provider calls and no `botocore`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Current-`main` wheel, anthropic 2.1.0 and 2.5.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** each |
| Current-`main` wheel, anthropic 2.6.0, 2.7.0 and 2.8.0 | **1 failed, 157 passed** each: the credentials test |
| Latest lane with only the adapter change reverted | **1 failed**: the `TypeError` above |
| Latest lane with only the test change reverted | **1 failed**: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'botocore'` |
| Python 3.11.18, floor constraints, anthropic 1.0.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Python 3.13.18, latest constraints, anthropic 2.8.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Python 3.12.3, latest constraints, anthropic 2.8.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Python 3.14.6, latest constraints, anthropic 2.8.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Python 3.13.18, unconstrained extra (canary), anthropic 2.8.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Python 3.13.18, anthropic 2.1.0, 2.5.0, 2.6.0 and 2.7.0 | **158 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** each |
| All 13 extras resolved against the updated `constraints/latest.txt` | Resolved; only `[anthropic]` installs the anthropic SDK |
| `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` on the final tree | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

Every environment imported `caveman_middleware` from `site-packages`. The 278 skips in each are for unavailable optional adapters. The resolution check used `uv pip install --dry-run`, not pip.

Not run locally: the other isolated adapter-family environments, full Go/engine and Node suites, macOS/Windows execution, or live-provider calls, including Bedrock. These results do not claim that the full hosted CI matrix is green; current CI results are in the PR's Checks tab.

title: Question: does `/caveman:caveman-init` (plugin) still fetch caveman-init.js from main?
body:
Hi, and thanks for caveman and for the care that clearly goes into its security: the integrity checks on hook downloads, removing the remote fallback from the installer in #627, the symlink-safe writes. That care is what made me look at this one more closely.

I'm not sure I'm reading this correctly, so I'd really appreciate your view before treating it as a bug.

## What I'm seeing

As far as I can tell, in the Claude Code plugin, `/caveman:caveman-init` may still download and run `src/tools/caveman-init.js` from `main`, even though the plugin ships its own copy of that file.

`commands/caveman-init.md:11` (same on `main` and in `v4.1.0`, `1e91f13`):

```
2. Otherwise download and run the standalone script (it is self-contained and supports stdin execution): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/src/tools/caveman-init.js | node - $ARGUMENTS`
```

Step 1 looks for `src/tools/caveman-init.js` in the user's current repo, so outside a caveman checkout I'd expect plugin users to reach step 2. `commands/caveman-init.toml` seems to follow the same pattern.

## Why I'm asking

We're evaluating caveman for our team through our own marketplace, pinned to a commit SHA we've reviewed. If I understand correctly, this command would run whatever is on `main` at call time, rather than the reviewed code, so the pin wouldn't fully cover it.

## What I may be missing

I saw that #803 proposed using `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/tools/caveman-init.js` first, and that it was closed as implemented, and that #627 removed the remote fallback from `installer/install.js`. I couldn't find where the plugin command itself was changed:

- `commands/caveman-init.md` seems to have only one commit (`5f079ab7`, 2026-07-02), and `commands/caveman-init.toml` last changed in `51e19903` (2026-07-02).
- I couldn't find a hook that intercepts `/caveman-init` the way `caveman-mode-tracker.js` does for `/caveman-stats`.

It's quite possible the fix lives somewhere I didn't look, or that I'm misunderstanding how the plugin resolves this command. If so, a pointer would be very helpful and I'll happily close this.

## A possible change, if useful

If it does turn out to be a gap, something along the lines of #803 might work:

```
1. If `src/tools/caveman-init.js` exists in the current repo (a caveman checkout), run: `node src/tools/caveman-init.js $ARGUMENTS`
2. Otherwise, if `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/tools/caveman-init.js` exists (plugin install), run: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/tools/caveman-init.js" $ARGUMENTS`
3. Otherwise …
```

For the last step, you're in a much better position than I am to judge: dropping the curl pipe as you did in #627 (pointing to `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --with-init`), or keeping it for some setups I'm not aware of. I'd be glad to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer.

## Environment

- caveman `v4.1.0` (`1e91f1306d602d4ca23618701b1185575ae1869b`), reviewed as a Claude Code plugin through a marketplace entry pinned by SHA
- Compared with `main` on 2026-11-12

Thanks again for your time!

title: fix(readme): stop GitHub clipping the Caveman Code banner
body:
Follow-up to #1526. On github.com the banner's right edge was cut off ("Same model, same work, small…", "Read the launch …").

Cause: GitHub renders every table at its widest unwrapped line and scrolls the overflow. The banner wrapped a nested table and long lines inside an outer table, so the box grew past the README column.

Fix:
- Drop the outer box and the nested table. The banner is now a heading, one stat table and the links, followed by a rule above the logo.
- Make the three stat cells parallel and short ("than Codex" / "than Claude Code"). The same-model detail (GPT-6.1 Sol against Codex, Opus 5.5 against Claude Code) moves to the source line under the table.
- Remove the fixed `width="33%"` so each cell sizes to its caption.

Numbers are unchanged from #1526 (sourced from caveman.so/code and the launch post).

Checked on the real GitHub renderer with headless Chrome screenshots of this branch: nothing clipped at 1400px or 700px. On desktop every caption fits on one line; at 700px the table wraps evenly.

Tests: `tests/test_benchmark_contract.py`, `tests/test_detect.py` pass.

title: fix(codex): ship native manifest at marketplace root
body:
# fix(codex): ship native manifest at marketplace plugin root

Codex loads Caveman from the repository root declared by marketplace `source: "./"`. Only `plugins/caveman/` currently has a native Codex manifest, so root installs fall back to the Claude manifest and warn: `ignoring hooks: expected a string, string array, object, or object array; found object`.

Add a root native Codex manifest pointing at the existing `skills/` directory, include it in the npm package, and extend manifest/version guards. This covers both marketplace-checkout discovery and installed-cache discovery. Claude hooks and existing user-level Codex hooks remain unchanged; the new manifest adds no hook registrations.

## Validation

- Regression before fix: 3 failures (missing root manifest, missing release-version entry target, missing npm package inclusion).
- Focused manifest/version/SessionStart checks: 25 passed.
- `npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts`: root `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` included.
- `npm test`: 679 passed, 29 skipped, 2 failed under sandbox. Failures: temporary Node hard-link permission and localhost listen permission.
- Permission-enabled recheck: all 3 localhost signed-manifest checks passed; Node-symlink fixture still fails with missing temporary `claude-config/settings.json`. The same Node-symlink failure reproduced on unmodified upstream HEAD.
- Identical root manifest applied to actual marketplace and installed-cache paths: fresh Codex session (CLI 0.166.0) exited 0, emitted zero hook-manifest warnings, and received both Caveman activation/reinforcement markers as lite.
- `git diff --check`, clean-base patch application, and reverse-application checks passed.

Base: `ad473752bdc86ca96d7289443228d4c53ec119a8`, verified upstream HEAD during preparation.

## Related work and scope

Related: #1243 (closed) and its review in #1477. This is a warning-only packaging correction for the existing repository-root marketplace source, not the lifecycle integration proposed there. It adds no plugin hooks, removes no repository hook configuration, changes no mode-state handling, and leaves the nested distribution manifest intact. Fresh installs still require the existing standalone/user-level activation setup; this PR does not claim to solve #1242.

## Environment and limits

Validated on macOS Apple Silicon, Node 26.3.0, Codex CLI 0.166.0. Windows and the full supported Node matrix were not run locally. Full `npm test` is not claimed green: the remaining temporary Node-symlink fixture failure reproduces on the unmodified base. Upstream CI has not executed jobs: CI, engine-ci, and CodeQL currently report `action_required` for this fork PR (zero check runs). This appears to require maintainer approval; no CI result is claimed. Prepared with OpenAI Codex; commit carries DCO sign-off.

title: daily-triage 2026-11-13 → 11-20: the OpenCode V2 adapter listened for an event its host does not have, and the standing root-suite blocker turns out to be a broken /dev/null
body:
> **2026-11-20 run appended.** This daily-triage PR was still open, so this run added two commits rather than opening a second PR. Nothing was force-pushed, rebased, merged or closed; the branch was pushed as a fast-forward (`b58ae37..b154c4c`). `git merge-tree` against `main` reports **no conflict**, so no rebase was needed. Each run's section is kept in full only while it is the newest; older ones are preserved verbatim in this description's **edit history** (click the "edited" marker) and summarised here, because appending in full passed GitHub's 65,536-character body limit. Nothing has been removed from the record.

# 2026-11-20 run

One cluster fixed, and one four-run-old mystery finally has an answer.

The cluster is this PR's recurring shape once more — **the adapter listened for an event its host does not have.** #1539 reported that the generated OpenCode **V2** plugin registers no handler for `experimental.idle`, the hook a V2 host actually calls when model work completes. Reading the producer closed the question the 11-17 triage could not: OpenCode V2 has **no `session.idle` bus event at all** — its session-event schema names 54 session events and not one of them is idle. So the adapter's only Stop branch was dead code on that host, and nothing downstream ever saw a turn end there.

The answer is to the **14 root-suite failures this PR has carried as a standing blocker since 2026-11-16** ("identical on unmodified `main`, so environmental or genuinely broken"). They are environmental, and the mechanism is now pinned: **`/dev/null` in the daily-triage container is an ordinary root-owned regular file, not a character device.** Details under "Needs maintainer decision".

## Fixes

| Issue(s) | Root cause | Hosts/OS affected | Test added | Supersedes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fixes #1539 | **The V2 adapter reported a turn boundary only from an event-bus branch keyed on `session.idle`, an event V2 does not publish.** Completed model work reaches a V2 plugin through the session `experimental.idle` hook, which the host triggers at the point the session *would* go idle and [deliberately skips for control-only drains](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/d432a06b9c07bab0be4e8d642173b1cb14137f11/packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts#L177-L189) such as a manual compaction. With no handler, a V2 host emitted **no Stop at all**. What blocked this fix on 11-17 was the double-emit risk — if a 2.x host published the bus event *and* called the hook, adding the handler would count one turn twice, and inflated accounting is worse than a missing boundary. The producer settles it both ways: the schema has no idle event, and the hook is triggered *before* the drain returns `Complete`, so for any one boundary the hook always arrives first. The bus branch is therefore kept for any host that does publish idle but stays quiet once the hook has spoken. Continuation turns are unaffected: when a plugin admits input the drain loop keeps going and calls the hook again, and each of those calls is a real completed-model boundary. | The CLI-generated native **OpenCode V2** adapter (`caveman enable opencode` on a 2.x host), every OS — the change is a flag, a condition and one hook registration inside the generated plugin, with no path, encoding or shell handling. The **V1** generator is deliberately untouched: V1 is a different host major whose bus does carry `session.idle`. | 1 new test, 4 boundary cases plus the ordering guard (`packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs`) | #1557 |

### Reproduced failing first

- The new test fails on `main` for the right reason: *"the V2 adapter must handle the hook the host actually calls at a completed-model boundary"* — `sessionHooks` holds only `compaction`, `context`, `prompt`.
- The ordering guard is load-bearing, not decoration: with `&& !idleHookSpoke` reverted and everything else in place, the test fails on *"a bus session.idle after the hook has spoken is the same boundary, not a second turn"*. It was re-applied and the test goes green again.
- The three no-session-id cases (`{background}`, `{sessionID: ""}`, `undefined`) emit nothing, and a second hook call for the same session still emits its own Stop, so a continuation turn is not swallowed by the guard.
- `packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs` + `tests/opencode-factory-isolation.runtime.mjs`: **166 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped.**

### Sibling check

- `src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js` (the standalone plugin) emits **no** turn-boundary events at all — it handles mode state, slash-command parsing and per-turn reinforcement — so it has no twin of this defect.
- The Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, OpenClaw and Pi paths each get Stop from their own host's named hook; `session.idle` appears nowhere else in the tree (`packages/cli/src/index.ts:9345` is the V1 generator, and the two test references are fixtures).

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#1548** (scope the SubagentStart ruleset by agent type): **a feature request, so triaged only** — this run implements feature requests never. The measurement is credible and the ask is modest (a `CAVEMAN_SUBAGENT_MATCHER`-style knob). @DrSkyle has implemented it in **#1556**. Maintainer decision; the second half of the issue (whether `SessionStart` still needs the `compact` matcher) is a behaviour question I did not change.
- **#1554** (`mahasiswa`): not a caveman bug report. The body is an unrelated prompt pasted inside the template's HTML comment, with no caveman behaviour described. Asked the reporter for the actual before/after, and flagged that the paste carries their own personal details. Nothing closed.
- **#1494** (middleware-python nightly canary): verdict **unchanged from 11-19, and the 11-20 failure is byte-identical** — `TypeError: copy_platform_client() got multiple values for keyword argument 'aws_profile'`, `1 failed, 157 passed, 278 skipped` ([run 44673909366](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/actions/runs/44673909366)). Already fixed on this branch (`3205058`, adopted from @szsunyuan's #1524). Needs this merge, not a new patch. No new comment: the only new activity was the bot's own daily ping.
- **#1482** (middleware-canary, TypeScript): same — **identical failure**, `@google/genai` 3.6.1 against `supported_range ">=2.21.0 <3"`, 6 failures all from `requirePeers` ([run 44669513252](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/actions/runs/44669513252)). This branch's `c7cf4b8` widens the bound to `high: '4'`. Fixed here, failing on `main`.
- **#1546, #1495, #1496, #1497, #1506, #1510, #1516, #1225** (`agent-drift:` pin bumps): precondition still unmet — `AGENTS.md` allows these only after the root `npm test` passes, and it does not (**14 failures**, the same families every run). Now explained rather than merely recorded; see below. No pin bumped, and no host agent is installed in this container to confirm one against.
- **#1522**: latest comment is this run's marker with no new activity since. Skipped by the run's own rule.
- **Skipped as already triaged with no new activity since**: #1536, #1307, #1318, #1503, #1493 and the rest of the 67 open issues. #1536's routing decision and #1318's adherence question both remain maintainer calls, unchanged.

## Contributor PRs reviewed

- **#1557 by @DrSkyle — adopted, with credit.** Its `experimental.idle` registration is the half that was missing, and its commit is cherry-picked onto this branch as the parent of the fix so authorship is preserved. What it did not carry is the reason the 11-17 triage declined to merge a handler at all: it leaves the bus `session.idle` branch unguarded, so on any host that publishes both, one turn would be reported twice. This branch adds that guard, the producer evidence for why the hook wins the race, and the regression test for it. Thank you for picking up a blocked issue.
- **#1556 by @DrSkyle — not evaluated as a fix; maintainer decision.** It implements #1548's agent-type matcher. The implementation looked reasonable on a read, but a knob that changes which agents receive the ruleset is a behaviour decision, not a bug fix, and this run does not land feature requests.
- **#1555 by @JuliusBrussee — the maintainer's own draft** (Bun workspace, related to #570). Left alone.
- **#1553, #1552, #1551, #1550, #1549**: reviewed on 11-19 (see edit history), unchanged since. #1553's whitespace guard is in this branch with credit; #1550 and #1551 still cannot both merge, because #1551 contains #1550's `engine/edge_cases_test.go` byte-identically; #1549 still edits only the CI-generated `dist/caveman.skill` mirror.

## Needs maintainer decision

1. **A release — still this PR's most load-bearing item.** Nothing new changes this: #1522's panic fixes, #1543, #1484, both canary fixes and now #1539 are all unreleased, and the newest tags remain `v4.1.0` / `bin-v4.1.0` (tagged 2026-11-07). `git tag --contains` is empty for every one of these commits. The fixes exist; users cannot get them.
2. **The 14 root-suite failures are environmental, and here is the proof.** They are not a repo defect and never were:
   - `/dev/null` in this container is `-rw-r--r-- 1 root root` — a **regular file**, not the `crw-rw-rw-` character device every program assumes. The session runs as uid 0, so anything redirecting to it **writes real bytes into a shared file** instead of discarding them.
   - That breaks two things at once. `spawnSync(..., { stdio: 'ignore' })` opens `/dev/null` and intermittently fails `ENOENT` while the file is being replaced: in `installer/install.js`, **every** `hasCmd()` call in a failing run returns false (184/184, including `/bin/sh` by absolute path while `fs.existsSync('/bin/sh')` is `true` and the same process spawns it fine with `stdio: 'inherit'`). With no `sh`, `hasCmd('curl')` is false, the installer takes the Node https path, and the fake curl the test planted is never invoked — which is exactly the four `curl path:` assertions, and the same mechanism behind the `gemini install`, hook-integrity, `caveman-shrink` signal and `OMP` families.
   - The second half is visible directly: `tests/wrap.runtime.mjs` sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, and git dies with **`fatal: bad config line 1 in file /dev/null`** — it is reading another test's stderr back out of it. Measured across one run of those two tests: `/dev/null` went from `regular empty file 0` to `regular file 69`, holding that git error plus `parent directories): .git`.
   - **Nothing in the repository can fix this**, and the installer's behaviour is provably correct: run by hand with a working `/bin/sh`, it passes exactly the argv the tests expect — `-fsSL --proto-redir =https --max-redirs 5 --max-time 60 --max-filesize 8388608`.
   - So the decision is yours: **the `agent-drift:` gate as `AGENTS.md` writes it ("after the root `npm test` passes") cannot be satisfied in this container for a reason unrelated to the code.** Either the gate should be read against a CI run rather than the triage container, or `/dev/null` needs fixing wherever this runs. I did not bump a pin on the strength of an environment diagnosis, and I did not alter the container: repairing `/dev/null` with `mknod` was correctly refused as a destructive system change, and I did not retry it.
   - Two CLI runtime tests fail for the same reason and are **not** this PR's doing: `wrapWorkTags reads the launch repository deterministically…` and `managed claude wrap names repo and branch as x-cave-tags`. Neither `tests/wrap.runtime.mjs` nor `wrapWorkTags` appears anywhere in `git diff origin/main...HEAD`.
3. **`constraints/latest.txt` pins.** Unchanged from 11-19: `anthropic==2.8.0` while 2.10.0 is out, so the pinned lane never exercises the 2.6+ `copy()` path that broke. Verified green for the anthropic family and **deliberately not bumped** — the file's own header says to bump "after it passes", which needs this merge first.
4. **#1493's onboarding path.** Unchanged: if pressing Enter at the first-run page can leave a user with nothing installed and no hint, that is a UX trap on the primary install door — but it needs the reporter's answers before anyone writes a test.
5. **PR closures.** #1517, #1547, #1542, #1524, #1498, #1538, #1541, #1501, part of #1553 and now #1557 are represented in this branch; #1550/#1551 overlap each other. **I never close anything.**
6. **Where the new proxy reliability bound gets documented**, unchanged: `docs/technical/proxy-reliability.md` was deleted on `main` and `proxy/AGENTS.md` rewritten, so the edit is unlandable from this branch.

### Verification (2026-11-20, full gate)

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| root `npm test` | 716 tests, 672 pass, **14 fail** (the known families — now explained, see item 2), 30 skipped |
| `node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js` | **30/30 pass** |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | **322 OK** (re-run twice; one earlier run reported 20 errors and was a `/dev/null` flake) |
| `python tests/verify_repo.py` | **all local verification checks passed** |
| `go test ./engine/... ./proxy/... ./shared/...` | **all packages pass** |
| `node scripts/test-windows-compat.mjs` | **windows compatibility gate passed** |
| `packages/cli` runtime suite | 1536 tests, **2 pre-existing `/dev/null` failures** in `tests/wrap.runtime.mjs`, untouched by this branch |
| `native-enable` + `opencode-factory-isolation` | **166 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped** |

Adversarial review of this run's two commits, against each class:

- **Path resolution** — no path, `__dirname` or `../` touched. The change is a flag, a condition and one hook registration inside the generated-plugin template. The generated file keeps its name and location, and the test still runs `node --check` on it as written to disk. N/A.
- **Referenced but not shipped** — no new file. Nothing to add to `installer/install.js` file lists, an `npm` `files` array or the plugin layout. `compile-registries.mjs` ran as part of the build and produced no changes, so no generated file is out of sync with its source.
- **Windows** — no path handling, no `utf8` read/write, no CRLF rewrite, no PowerShell twin (the V2 plugin is JS only), no `$Args`. The added comments use em-dashes, matching the template's pre-existing non-ASCII comments through the same unchanged write path. The handler does one `emit`, the same work the bus branch did, so the hook stays inside its budget.
- **Destructive writes** — none. Nothing writes `settings.json`, `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md` or a user rule file; `enable`/`disable` journaling and owned-path restore are untouched.
- **Silent fail-open** — the handler declines a missing or empty `sessionID` and returns, exactly as the bus branch already did, and no validator returns true on exception. The three bad-input cases are pinned by the test. The guard is not a swallowed error: it declines to report a boundary already reported.
- **Claim drift** — nothing about what ships changed: same files installed, same hosts supported, so no README "What you get" or `INSTALL.md` edit is due. **No benchmark, savings percentage or token-reduction number was added, changed or removed**; no README table touched.

Also re-checked: **`src/hooks/` is untouched**, so `checksums.sha256` needs no regeneration (`verify_repo.py` confirms). **No forbidden path** — nothing under `plugins/caveman/`, `dist/`, `packages/agent/`, `packages/create-caveman-agent/` or `browse/`.

---

## Earlier runs in this PR

Full text of every earlier run is preserved in this description's **edit history**. For orientation:

- **2026-11-19** — @emaxe's #1522 again: `unwrapFileWrapper` was guarded on `main` by `24ed1c1`, but it is the *third* of three unwrappers in `unwrapInput` and the *first*, `unwrapCodexExec`, sliced the same attacker-shaped bytes with the same unchecked arithmetic. A codex exec result cut inside the `"output":"` key — `{"exit_code":0,"output":"}` — panicked `slice bounds out of range [25:24]`. Fixed with 4 cases plus a committed `FuzzUnwrapInput` target over the whole chain (3.37M execs, no panic). @Alexi5000's #1553 found the whitespace-only half independently and is credited.
- **2026-11-18** — @Pduhard's #1543: a pooled upstream connection that died silently was reused forever, because `BoundUpstreamTransport` lacked the HTTP/2 ping health check `cloudlink/warm.go` already had. H2 pings, TCP keep-alive probes in the SSRF dialer, idle-sibling eviction on a network timeout; #1547 adopted. Plus @jerome-benoit's #1484: the generated OpenCode **V1** plugin kept `contexts`, `pending`, `projectDir` and `hostHooks` at module scope, so a second project's factory overwrote the first's — the V1 twin of a fix V2 already had; #1542's fix commit adopted.
- **2026-11-17** — one cluster on both install channels: caveman wrote a path that only exists until the shell exits. @fezarosa-dev's #1541 found it for the CLI's `caveman` script (`durableCavemen()` returned the unresolved fnm per-shell PATH entry); the standalone installer had the same bug for `node` via `absoluteNodePath()`. Plus **#1350**: `caveman-compress` could alter a numeric value and still report "Validation passed".
- **2026-11-16** — the engine's pytest/Jest collector-error reporting (#1538 adopted), and a CLI-reached engine panic reported as an error rather than a trace.
- **2026-11-15 / 2026-11-14** — the Hermes cluster from @jerome-benoit: native status, plugin-membership decoding, MCP-entry disable safety, and the native route writer's indentation.
- **2026-11-13** — the middleware-python Bedrock clone and `google-genai` 3.x transport canary cluster (#1524, #1498 adopted) — the two fixes both failing nightly canaries are still waiting on.

title: fix(compress): default to claude-sonnet-5-5
body:
hey! quick one before sonnet 4.5 goes away.

`claude-sonnet-4-5` resolves to `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, which is deprecated and retires on the Claude API on november 30, 2026 ([model deprecations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations)). caveman-compress uses it as `DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL` on the anthropic SDK path, so anyone compressing without `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_MODEL` or `CAVEMAN_MODEL` set would start getting errors after that date.

what changed:

* `DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL` in `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py` is now `claude-sonnet-5-5`, the replacement the deprecations page recommends. the request sends no temperature, thinking or prefill settings, so nothing else has to change for 5.5, and the SDK path already reads the first text block
* `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` stays at 64000. sonnet 5.5 allows 128K, but keeping 64K means a pinned 64K model (haiku 4.5 for example) still works, so i only reworded the two comments that said the cap "tracks" the default model's max
* `docs/technical/deploy.md` names the new default
* only the source under `skills/` is touched, `sync-skill.yml` mirrors it into the plugin copy after merge like CLAUDE.md describes

what i ran:

* the compress test suites with pytest: 136 passed, same count as on main
* `python tests/verify_repo.py`: all local verification checks passed

commit is signed off for the DCO. thanks for caveman!
