title: fix(ci): use Go 1.26.11 for security and native build checks
body:
The default-branch supply-chain check fails with GO-2026-6859 because `actions/setup-go` selects Go 1.26.10 from `go.mod`. Require Go 1.26.11 so the existing security check, Go CI lanes, and native release build workflow select the patched standard library. Scanner configuration, tests, and assertions stay intact.

Validation on the one-line candidate: the unchanged `govulncheck@v1.8.0 ./...` command reports no vulnerabilities; all 65 module package test commands completed successfully; `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` pass. Package tests ran sequentially to keep temporary files below the review budget. Real Postgres integration, cross-platform release-shape checks, and remote CI remain required; no release or deployment was run.

Scope: the Docker builder independently pins Go 1.27.3, an affected release line requiring a separately verified 1.27.4 digest update. This change does not establish production exploitability or complete remediation of every build path. Existing Google 3.x and Anthropic 2.8 canary failures remain tracked separately; the Bedrock correction already exists in PR #1524.

Evidence: [failing default-branch scan](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/actions/runs/43347363002), [official Go advisory](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-6859.json).

title: fix: run caveman-explore as forked subagent
body:
## Problem

`caveman-explore` reads like a subagent but has no `context:`, so Claude Code runs it inline:

1. `model: haiku` overrides the session model for the turn ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#frontmatter-reference)). The cache is per model, so the whole chat is re-cached on Haiku.
2. `tools:` is a subagent key. Skills ignore it, so nothing enforces read-only.
3. The Grep/Read output lands in the main context, contradicting the description.

## Fix

([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#run-skills-in-a-subagent))

```yaml
context: fork
agent: Explore
background: false
```

`model: haiku` now applies only to the fork. Also in this PR: a test for the keys, the compiled `agent-skills.generated.ts` from `compile-registries.mjs`, and one docs sentence.

## Evidence

I ran `claude -p "/caveman:caveman-explore where is guardExploreAgent defined" --model sonnet` on Claude Code 2.1.323:

- Inline: the session ran on Haiku (0 Sonnet tokens), with 3 Grep/Read calls in the main context.
- Fork: 0 calls in the main context, same answer (`index.ts:1794-1798`).

## Tests

- `skills/caveman-explore/tests`: 5 pass.
- Root `npm test`: 635 pass, 19 fail. The same 19 fail on `main` (agent-registry-scope, bun-runtime).

The commit is DCO signed off.

Updates `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` from 5.11.0 to 5.13.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.13.0 (November 11, 2026)

This release adds automatic client certificate reloading and temporal precision metadata for database/sql. It also fixes a panic on malformed server responses, unsafe retries after connection failures, and range encoding. See Changes for client certificate configuration behavior that may affect existing applications.

Security Fixes

  • Panic in Rows.Values on malformed server responses (GHSA-w9rp-vfrh-q8vv). A server response containing fewer row values than declared fields could cause an index-out-of-range panic in Rows.Values. It now returns an error and closes the rows when the counts differ, including when there are extra values, matching Rows.Scan validation.

Features

  • pgconn: reload client certificates and keys configured through sslcert and sslkey for each TLS certificate request, allowing new connections to pick up rotated credentials without recreating the configuration or restarting the application. Files are still validated during configuration parsing. Relative paths retain their parse-time directory, and reloads follow symlinks (Erin Shepherd)
  • stdlib: expose fractional seconds precision for timestamp, timestamptz, time, timetz, and interval through ColumnTypePrecisionScale and database/sql.ColumnType.DecimalSize. These return precision 0, the fractional seconds precision as scale, and ok=true. The scale defaults to 6 when no fractional seconds precision is declared; precision 0 means numeric precision is not applicable (Danny Xu)

Changes

  • pgconn: file-backed client certificates are no longer stored in the parsed TLSConfig.Certificates slice. Setting TLSConfig.Certificates (including a non-nil empty slice) or TLSConfig.GetClientCertificate overrides automatic reloading. Replacing TLSConfig, including with a direct TLSConfig.Clone, discards the file-backed certificate settings; use pgconn.Config.Copy to preserve them when copying a configuration. Certificate and key files must remain readable for subsequent TLS certificate requests. Encrypted keys reuse the password resolved during configuration parsing; GetSSLPassword is not called again on reload.

Bug Fixes

  • pgconn: do not mark a connection-closed error encountered while receiving a response as safe to retry, since the request may already have reached the server. This prevents database/sql from automatically repeating a statement that may already have executed. The error still supports errors.Is(err, pgconn.ErrConnClosed) (Aayush Shah)
  • pgconn: skip sending a cancel request when a connection fails during startup, avoiding an unnecessary second connection attempt (felipe stival)
  • pgconn: accept unencrypted combined certificate/key PEM files with the certificate before the key, as well as key-first files (Erin Shepherd)
  • pgtype: encode Range[any] values returned by RangeCodec.DecodeValue and Rows.Values in both binary and text formats, allowing decoded ranges and multiranges to be reused as query arguments or in CopyFrom (waw666waw666)
  • stdlib: report ok=false for the precision and scale of unconstrained numeric columns instead of bogus values (Danny Xu)
  • stdlib: report math.MaxInt64 for the lengths of unconstrained varchar, bpchar, and varbit columns instead of negative lengths (PerryLink)

... (truncated)

Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.62.0

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-13 v1.62.1:

    • Connections are now opened with SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX instead of SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX, which takes a mutex lock and unlock off every column read and makes scanning rows noticeably faster. That mutex never kept two goroutines on one connection apart, so nothing else changes for code using the driver's API; code that takes a connection's SQLite handle from unexported fields and calls SQLite with it from another goroutine must now serialize those calls itself. Resolves [GitHub issue #13](modernc-org/sqlite#13), thanks guille-work!

  • 2026-11-07 v1.62.0:

    • Add illumos/amd64, tested on an OmniOS builder. Resolves [GitLab issue #210](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/210), thanks Jasper Siepkes (@​siepkes), who also started the modernc.org/libc port!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.16.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.8.0; SQLite stays 3.54.1 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.80.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in syncing with fdatasync(2), off by default: Fdatasync(true) makes commits sync with fdatasync instead of fsync, process-wide, which skips the timestamp update fsync forces and keeps a commit just as durable. FdatasyncEnabled reports the setting; on macOS and Windows Fdatasync returns ErrFdatasyncUnavailable. Resolves [GitHub issue #10](modernc-org/sqlite#10), thanks aibeshkov!
    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

title: `caveman compress` passes `pytest -v` output through as text (0%), while `caveman shrink` on the same run cuts it 95%
body:
**What happen**

The same `pytest -v` output is compressed by `caveman shrink` but passed through unchanged by `caveman compress` on stdin. `compress` classifies it as `text`, so the terminal compressor that `shrink` uses never runs.

```
# 300 passing parametrized tests + 1 failing test, pytest -v, 25 KB
caveman shrink -- python -m pytest work/pyt -v
  {"content_type":"terminal","tokens_before":6237,"tokens_after":293,"ratio":0.953,"method":"terminal",...}

python -m pytest work/pyt -v > raw.txt
caveman compress < raw.txt
  {"content_type":"text","tokens_before":6236,"tokens_after":6236,"ratio":0,...}
```

The `shrink` result is good: the failure, the assertion and the summary line all survive, and the 300 PASSED lines are elided.

**Expected**

Either `compress` recognises plain test-runner output the way `shrink` does, or the docs say that `compress` only handles the content types it can sniff (JSON, logs, test reports as JSON/JUnit, ...) and that terminal output should go through `shrink`. I could not tell from the README which one is intended.

**Before/after example**
```
Input: pytest -v output of 301 tests, piped into caveman compress
Got:   content_type "text", ratio 0, output identical to input
Want:  the same ~95% reduction that caveman shrink gives for that output
```

<details><summary>Test file used</summary>

```python
import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize("i", range(300))
def test_item(i):
    assert i >= 0

def test_total():
    total = 41
    assert total == 42
```
</details>

Not checked: whether the proxy or SDK path sees tool results the way `compress` does or the way `shrink` does. That is the case that would matter to agents. Logs and repetitive JSON piped into `compress` were detected fine in the same run (`log` and `elision`).

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: CLI only (`caveman compress` / `caveman shrink`), no agent

**Version / install method**
`@caveman-ai/cli` 4.1.0 from npm, `caveman-engine_win32_amd64` from release `bin-v4.1.0` (checksum verified), Windows 11, Node 22.13.1, Python 3.13 / pytest 9.2.0.

title: fix(engine): report Jest suites that fail to run as errors
body:
## Bug

The test-report compressor summarizes a failing Jest run as all-passing when the failure is a **suite that could not run** — a test file whose import fails, or a throwing `beforeAll`/`afterAll`. These are Jest's default behavior (it keeps running the other suites), so this hits ordinary `jest --json` output.

Jest records such a suite only on the suite object: `status: "failed"` plus `message`, and it counts it in `numFailedTestSuites`, **not** in `numFailedTests`. `parseJestJSON` (`engine/compressors/testreport.go`) builds the summary from `numPassedTests`/`numFailedTests` and per-assertion results only, so the failure disappears.

## Repro (real Jest 29.7.0 output, engine built from `main` @ 9b24366, Go 1.26.11)

`src/ok.test.js` has 2 passing tests, `src/user.test.js` does `require('./db')` (missing), `src/hook.test.js` has a passing test and an `afterAll` that throws. `npx jest --json --outputFile=jest.json` gives `success: false, numFailedTestSuites: 2, numPassedTests: 3, numFailedTests: 0`.

```
$ caveman-engine compress < jest.json        # main
TEST SUMMARY: 3 passed
```

```
$ caveman-engine compress < jest.json        # this branch
TEST SUMMARY: 3 passed, 2 errors

ERROR: /…/src/hook.test.js
  afterAll boom: pool not closed
  at Object.<anonymous> (src/hook.test.js:1:24)

ERROR: /…/src/user.test.js
  Cannot find module './db' from 'src/user.test.js'
  at Resolver._throwModNotFoundError (node_modules/jest-resolve/build/resolver.js:427:11)
  at Object.<anonymous> (src/user.test.js:1:27)
```

An agent reading the compressed output on `main` is told a red run is green.

## Fix

Decode the suite's `status` and `message`. A suite marked `failed` with **no failed test of its own** is counted as an error, with the reason taken from the first line after Jest's `● Test suite failed to run` header (ANSI stripped with the existing `ansiRe`, since Jest colors the message under a TTY / `FORCE_COLOR`) and its `at …` frames as the stack. A suite that failed because one of its own tests failed is already reported through that test and is not double-counted.

## Tests

`TestTestReportJestSuiteFailures` uses messages trimmed from the real run above (one captured with `FORCE_COLOR=1`). On `main` it fails for the right reason:

```
--- FAIL: TestTestReportJestSuiteFailures (0.00s)
    testreport_test.go:319: missing "TEST SUMMARY: 3 passed, 2 errors" in:
        TEST SUMMARY: 3 passed
```

and passes with the fix. It also pins that an ordinary assertion failure is not counted twice.

Behavior before/after on real `jest --json` runs (nothing else changes):

| run | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| all passing | `2 passed` | `2 passed` |
| one assertion failure | `1 passed, 1 failed` | `1 passed, 1 failed` |
| skipped test | `1 passed, 1 skipped` | `1 passed, 1 skipped` |
| assertion failure + suite that fails to load | `1 failed` | `1 failed, 1 errors` |
| only a suite that fails to load | passes the raw JSON through (0 tests) | `1 errors` + the reason |
| `testResults: []` | pass-through | pass-through |

Gate (Go 1.26.11, per `go.mod`): `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` — 61 packages ok, identical to `main`.

## Scope

Jest only. pytest has a related gap (a module that fails to import lives only under `collectors[]`), but it only shows up with `--continue-on-collection-errors` — by default pytest aborts with `tests: []` and the compressor already passes that through — so I left it out of this PR.

<sub>Found while auditing the repo for functional bugs; diagnosis and patch drafted with Claude Code, then verified by hand — every output above is from real runs.</sub>

title: fix(cli): resolve fnm multishell dir before wiring caveman hooks
body:
## Problem

With [fnm](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm), `PATH` holds a per-shell link such as `/run/user/1000/fnm_multishells/<id>/bin`. fnm deletes it when the shell exits, and it is gone after a reboot.

`durableCavemen()` only checked the *resolved* path for ephemerality (it resolves into `~/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/...`, which passes) but returned the unresolved multishell path. `caveman enable claude` then wrote hooks like:

```
'/usr/bin/node' '/run/user/1000/fnm_multishells/12345_.../bin/caveman' shrink-hook
```

After a reboot every tool call fails with `Cannot find module`.

`stableNodePath()` already refuses fnm multishell paths for `node`, but the caveman script path was not covered.

## Repro

1. Install node with fnm (`eval "$(fnm env)"`), `npm i -g @caveman-ai/cli`.
2. `caveman enable claude`.
3. Reboot, start Claude Code: every PreToolUse hook errors with `Cannot find module`.

## Fix

In `durableCavemen()`, resolve a `fnm_multishells` PATH dir to the node version dir it links to before looking for `caveman`. Other PATH entries are untouched, so Homebrew keeps its stable `/opt/homebrew/bin` name. The regex is shared with `stableNodePath()`.

## Tests

Extended the existing fnm case in `tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs`: the multishell dir is a symlink to an install dir, and the `shrink-hook` command must name the install dir's `caveman`. It fails before the fix and passes after.

title: fix(opencode): isolate V1 plugin state per factory
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1484.

Keep the generated OpenCode V1 adapter's project directory, hook map, session contexts and pending prompt/tool hints inside each factory invocation. Creating project B or disposing project A no longer changes the other project's callbacks or lifecycle state.

## Root cause

`opencodeNativePluginSourceV1()` emitted module-scoped `projectDir`, `contexts`, `pending` and `hostHooks`. Every factory returned that same hook map, and initializing another factory reassigned the directory read by existing callbacks. Disposal iterated the shared context map and cleared both maps. V2 already owns these values inside `setup()`.

## Before

Baseline: upstream `9b243662ff98d392bc0a95b865a554583d71be75`.

Before editing production source, executed:

```sh
node --test packages/cli/tests/opencode-factory-isolation.runtime.mjs
```

All four initial behavioral tests failed, exit status 1:

- Factory identity: expected separate hook maps; actual maps were strictly equal.
- Initialize A then B: A's `PreToolUse` child cwd was `<temp>/project-B`, expected `<temp>/project-A`.
- Initialize B then A: B's `PreToolUse` child cwd was `<temp>/project-A`, expected `<temp>/project-B`.
- Dispose A: expected SessionEnd `[session-A]`; actual `[session-A, session-B]`.

The same four failures were confirmed again with the final test harness against a saved `git show` copy of that exact upstream source. Each fixture imports one generated module and creates both factories concurrently. It evaluates the actual production generator and replaces only its invocation resolver and generated child-process import with an isolated recorder; it does not copy the adapter implementation.

## After

The factory closes over its own directory, context map, pending-hint map, session helper and hook map. A small instance-bound `emit` passes its directory explicitly to the shared subprocess helper. Invocation constants and pure helpers remain shared, including those needed by the dual V1/V2 entrypoint. The V2 generator is unchanged.

## Regression coverage

14 dependency-free behavioral tests, each documented with the regression it prevents:

- Separate callback/hook identities and cwd/session ownership in both initialization orders.
- Native payload cwd and session IDs, plus shrink-child cwd and command rewriting.
- Cached SessionStart contexts and pending hints survive another factory's disposal; B continues to handle events.
- Disposal ends only owned sessions; repeated disposal adds no duplicate cleanup.
- Reused session IDs remain isolated, including callbacks invoked before awaiting their completion promises.
- Single-factory prompt metadata, tool input/output, compaction, Stop, session deletion and lazy context recreation.
- Missing/empty/invalid directory preserves inherited cwd instead of borrowing another factory's directory.
- Child exceptions and malformed JSON retain existing safe failure behavior.
- Standalone V2 and dual-entrypoint V1/V2 setup, hooks, cwd and independent disposal.

`pending` holds queued context strings, not outstanding asynchronous subprocess jobs; the generated child calls use `execFileSync`. Tests exercise promise completion/disposal ordering without sleeps.

## Verification

Fixed head: `fd60e5987985fa946d1fdef70c925765e0f7a012`.

Hosted verification: https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822 (all jobs passed; tested `cfede71fd39dc0ed57c8540319e722c2540029e1`). Final source/test revision is identical; only the temporary fork verification workflow was removed afterward. The workflow uses Node 22, repository-pinned pnpm 10.14.0, read-only permissions and GitHub-hosted Linux/Windows runners.

Commands actually executed:

```sh
node --test packages/cli/tests/opencode-factory-isolation.runtime.mjs
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter "@caveman-ai/cli..."
pnpm --dir packages/cli lint
pnpm --dir packages/cli build
CAVE_OPENCODE_GENERATOR=../dist/index.js node --test packages/cli/tests/opencode-factory-isolation.runtime.mjs
node --import ./packages/cli/tests/fixtures/sanitize-host-env.mjs --test --test-force-exit packages/cli/tests/native-enable.runtime.mjs
pnpm --dir packages/cli test
npm test
node --test --test-force-exit tests/*.js
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
python tests/verify_repo.py
git diff --exit-code
```

- [Targeted / Ubuntu](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822/job/133950111470): source and compiled generators each **14/14**; existing native integration **139/139**; TypeScript lint, CLI build and generated tracked-file drift check passed.
- [Targeted / Windows](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822/job/133950111473): source and compiled generators each **14/14**; TypeScript lint, CLI build and generated tracked-file drift check passed.
- [Full CLI / Ubuntu](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822/job/133950111046): **1,511 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped** (1,522 total).
- [Root / Ubuntu](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822/job/133950112484): installer/hooks **699 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped**; standalone **30/30**; Python **312 OK**; repository verification passed.
- [Root / Windows](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057380822/job/133950111592): installer/hooks **654 passed, 0 failed, 63 skipped**; standalone **30/30**; Python **312 OK, 7 skipped**; repository verification passed.
- [Untouched upstream comparison](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44057381747): checkout logs confirm `9b243662ff98d392bc0a95b865a554583d71be75`; full CLI **1,497 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped**. Linux/Windows root jobs passed too.

The [first verification run](https://github.com/anirudhqwerty/caveman/actions/runs/44044359239) had two full-CLI failures: `cloud MCP telemetry carries only closed tool outcome fields` and `namespaced telemetry emits resolved command and subcommand`. The temporary workflow's global `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` suppressed the records those tests expect at their local HTTP recorders. The upstream comparison explicitly reproduced exactly those two failures with that environment restored, then verified the full suite without the interfering variable. Telemetry remains disabled by default in the corrected workflow, with the default URL directed to loopback; test opt-ins use local recorders. No product fix or unrelated test edit was made for this verification-environment error. No unexplained baseline failures remain.

## Scope

Only `packages/cli/src/index.ts` and `packages/cli/tests/opencode-factory-isolation.runtime.mjs` remain in the final diff. No dependency, package version, generated distribution, installer configuration, provider routing, telemetry, compression or authentication changes. No permanent workflow changes. All authored commits carry the configured contributor's DCO sign-off.

## Notes

Generated-plugin fixtures and the existing native integration suite were executed; no live OpenCode host/model session was run. The existing POSIX native-enable harness runs on Linux; the new portable generated-plugin regression, compilation and build also run on Windows. This change preserves existing event payloads and subprocess failure handling; it does not add behavior for callbacks invoked after their own factory has been disposed.

title: caveman-proxy hang forever when pooled upstream conn die silently
body:
## What

Network change. Upstream request die with `read: connection timed out`. After that, proxy silent. Every new request hang forever. No error, no log line, no timeout. Only proxy restart fix.

## Env

- caveman-proxy `bin-v4.0.1`, mode `record`, listen `127.0.0.1:8787`
- Claude Code 2.1.326, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/claude`
- Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0, Wi-Fi = phone hotspot (IPv6 prefix change on reconnect)
- `api.anthropic.com` resolve IPv6 first

## Repro (deterministic, no network change needed)

Script below (Linux, `nft` + `sudo`). Start isolated proxy on `:18787`, warm one upstream conn, then silently drop packets of that conn only, like source address gone. New conns stay fine.

Output:

```
1. warm request through proxy: 401 in 1.062595s
2. proxy upstream source ports: 51498, now dropping their packets silently
3. direct curl, fresh connection: 405 in 0.950278s
4. request through proxy (waits up to 120s): no answer after 120s
```

Proxy log during 120 s wait: nothing. No warn, no retry.

Got: request through proxy hang forever. Fresh upstream conn work fine at same moment.

Want: proxy detect dead pooled conn, open fresh one, answer in seconds. Or fail fast with error.

Real-life trigger: phone hotspot reconnect give host new IPv6 prefix. Claude Code then hang (`claude -p "reply ok"` no output after 60 s), until proxy restart.

<details><summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Linux only: needs nft and sudo. Leaves the running caveman-proxy alone.
set -euo pipefail

BIN=${CAVEMAN_PROXY_BIN:-$HOME/.caveman/bin/caveman-proxy}
PORT=${PORT:-18787}
WAIT=${WAIT:-120}
URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/w/claude/v1/messages
TABLE=caveman_repro
DIR=$(mktemp -d)
PID=

cleanup() {
  sudo nft delete table inet "$TABLE" 2>/dev/null || true
  [ -n "$PID" ] && kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$DIR"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

hit() {
  local out
  if out=$(curl -sS -m "$1" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} in %{time_total}s' \
    -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' "$URL" 2>/dev/null); then
    echo "$out"
  else
    echo "no answer after $1s"
  fi
}

sudo -v

CAVEMAN_HOME=$DIR CAVEMAN_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:$PORT CAVEMAN_TELEMETRY=0 "$BIN" >"$DIR/proxy.log" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 50); do ss -ltn | grep -q ":$PORT " && break; sleep 0.2; done
ss -ltn | grep -q ":$PORT " || { echo "proxy did not listen on $PORT"; cat "$DIR/proxy.log"; exit 1; }

echo "1. warm request through proxy: $(hit 15)"

PORTS=$(ss -tnpH state established '( dport = :443 )' | grep "pid=$PID," | awk '{print $3}' | sed 's/.*://' | paste -sd, - || true)
[ -n "$PORTS" ] || { echo "proxy holds no upstream connection, nothing to break"; exit 1; }
echo "2. proxy upstream source ports: $PORTS, now dropping their packets silently"

sudo nft add table inet "$TABLE"
sudo nft "add chain inet $TABLE out { type filter hook output priority 0; }"
sudo nft "add chain inet $TABLE in { type filter hook input priority 0; }"
sudo nft "add rule inet $TABLE out tcp sport { $PORTS } drop"
sudo nft "add rule inet $TABLE in tcp dport { $PORTS } drop"

echo "3. direct curl, fresh connection: $(curl -sS -m 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} in %{time_total}s' https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages || echo failed)"
echo "4. request through proxy (waits up to ${WAIT}s): $(hit "$WAIT")"
echo
echo "healthy proxy: step 4 answers in seconds on a fresh upstream connection"
echo "bug:           step 4 gives no answer while step 3 works"
echo
echo "proxy log tail:"
tail -5 "$DIR/proxy.log"
```

</details>

## Evidence

Last log line before silence (proxy up since 2026-11-14, log stop here, no line after):

```json
{"level":"WARN","msg":"client stream copy failed","error":"read tcp [<old IPv6 prefix>]:58108->[2607:6bc0::10]:443: read: connection timed out"}
```

- Source IPv6 in that line no longer on host. Host now on new prefix.
- Same pattern seen earlier on 2026-11-13 (`read: connection timed out` from previous prefix).
- Direct upstream fine at same time: `curl -4` and `curl -6` to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` answer in < 0.3 s.
- Proxy gone, Claude Code works again at once.

## Cause

Proxy reuse pooled upstream conn after it go dead silently (no RST, no FIN). No health check, no request timeout, so request wait on dead conn forever. Repro above confirm: only pooled conn broken, proxy never try fresh one.

## Fix ideas

- HTTP/2 ping health check on pooled upstream conn (Go: `http2.Transport.ReadIdleTimeout` + `PingTimeout`).
- Per-request header/response timeout.
- Drop pool on `connection timed out`, or on local address change.

title: docs(skills): name UI proof in verify-and-stop
body:
`verify-and-stop` says to translate acceptance conditions into the smallest sufficient proof set, but gives no proof for a UI change. Unit tests and type checks pass while the screen is still wrong.

This adds one bullet in the same terse style:

> UI change: prove in running app. Project has `e2e.config.ts`: `npx e2e run <file>:<line>`, keep screenshot or video as proof.

It applies only when the project already has `e2e.config.ts`, so it adds no new tool or step for anyone else. `<file>:<line>` runs the single test declared on that line, which fits "run focused checks before wider gates".

Generated packs (`skills/generated/*/pack.json`, `proxy/internal/nativepack/native-pack.generated.json`, `packages/cli/src/native-pack.generated.ts`) are regenerated in the same commit with `node packages/cli/scripts/compile-registries.mjs`, per CONTRIBUTING.

Validation:

title: fix(proxy): evict silently dead pooled upstream connections
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1543.

When a pooled upstream connection died silently (no RST/FIN, e.g. after a hotspot reconnect or IPv6 prefix change), `BoundUpstreamTransport` had no HTTP/2 ping health check configured (`Transport.HTTP2 == nil`). Requests riding the dead HTTP/2 connection hung until the 15-minute `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (or client timeout, after which `RST_STREAM` still left the dead connection in the pool), and idle HTTP/1.1 sockets waited ~5 minutes on default TCP keepalive (longer than `IdleConnTimeout`).

### Changes

- **`proxy/internal/gateway/server.go`**: Configure `http.HTTP2Config{SendPingTimeout: 15 * time.Second, PingTimeout: 5 * time.Second}` in `BoundUpstreamTransport` (matching `cloudlink.linkTransport`), preserving any non-zero caller overrides. Healthy slow responses/streams answer PING ACKs and are never cut short; dead connections are closed and evicted within <= 20s.
- **`proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go`**: Evict sibling idle connections (`s.httpClient.CloseIdleConnections()`) when `doUpstream` or `streamResponse` hits an upstream network timeout or lost HTTP/2 connection while the caller context is still active. Preserves the non-replay invariant for ambiguous failures.
- **`shared/platform/ssrf/ssrf.go`**: Configure `net.KeepAliveConfig{Enable: true, Idle: 15 * time.Second, Interval: 5 * time.Second, Count: 3}` (~30s detection for silently dead idle TCP connections, including HTTP/1.1 keep-alives).
- **`proxy/internal/gateway/upstream_bounds_test.go`** & **`proxy/internal/standalone/standalone_test.go`**: Add deterministic blackholed HTTP/2 pooled-connection tests (in-flight fail-fast + recovery, and idle background eviction), idle-pool eviction tests on timeout, and transport config assertions.

### Verification

- Confirmed new tests fail before the fix (reproducing the dead pooled HTTP/2 hang).
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestDeadPooledHTTP2ConnFailsFastAndRecovers|TestUpstreamTimeoutEvictsIdlePool' ./proxy/internal/gateway` — PASS
- `go test -count=1 ./proxy/... ./shared/...` — PASS
- `go vet ./proxy/... ./shared/...` — PASS
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py` — PASS

title: Scope the SubagentStart ruleset by agent type
body:
The SubagentStart hook injects the full caveman ruleset (~4.7 KB) into every subagent, regardless of agent type. On one machine over a 5-day window that was 1,206 subagent spawns, about 5.7 MB of injected text total.

Request: an agent-type allowlist/regex knob for SubagentStart, similar to ponytail's `PONYTAIL_SUBAGENT_MATCHER`, so callers can scope the ruleset to code-writing agent types and skip it for review/research agents.

Separately: does the SessionStart path need the `compact` matcher? Its output appears static (same banner re-sent on every compaction), so dropping `compact` from that matcher may be safe if nothing downstream depends on it changing per-compaction.

title: feat: QuickJS Code-Mode MCP gateway, multi-harness envelopes, and cache-safe proxy optimizations
body:
## Summary

Adds an in-process QuickJS Code-Mode MCP gateway, multi-harness tool-result envelope unwrapping, and cache-safe proxy optimizations across Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, and OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic/Vertex/Azure harnesses.

### 1. Multi-harness envelope unwrapping (`2281bad4`)
- Unwraps and preserves structural envelopes from Claude Code (`<system-reminder>` / `<persisted-output>`), Codex CLI (`Chunk ID` / `Wall time` / `Process exited with code` / `Output:`), OpenCode (`<path>` / `<content>` / `<type>`), and Hermes Agent (`[stderr]` / `[exit_code: ...]` / `<file>` / `[truncated ...]`) in `engine/` so compressors see raw payloads while preserving verbatim boundaries and failing closed toward the original.
- Adds unit and evaluation coverage for all four harness envelope families.

### 2. QuickJS Code-Mode MCP gateway, built-ins & multi-agent overlays (`2637a55d`)
- **`mcp/codemode` & `caveman-mcp tools`**: In-process QuickJS sandbox (`modernc.org/quickjs`, zero-CGO cross-compilable) collapsing arbitrary upstream MCP servers (stdio + Streamable HTTP) into a compact two-tool surface (`search_tools` + `execute_code`) with bounded built-ins (`repo`, `pr`, `browse`), strict memory/CPU/timeout limits, and deterministic recovery handles.
- **`caveman codemode` & `caveman wrap --codemode`**: Ephemeral, non-destructive multi-agent overlays for Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kilo, Gemini, Qwen, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent (with isolated `HERMES_HOME` sync-back), Pi (`packages/pi-extension`), and TypeScript middleware (`@caveman-ai/middleware/codemode`).
- Keeps native Code Mode harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode) un-interfered unless explicitly opted in.

### 3. Cache-safe proxy optimizations & E2E proof (`b5f419d9`)
- **Live-zone duplicate-read collapsing**: Collapses repeated identical tool reads in the uncached live tail with CCR recovery handles while keeping the cached prefix byte-identical.
- **Deterministic canonical `tools[]` sorting**: Stabilizes tool declaration order across turns to prevent spurious prompt-cache busts.
- **Opt-in `defer_loading` + Tool Search**: Supports Anthropic/Vertex and OpenAI/Azure deferred tool loading, plus opt-in `caveman-shrink` on `tools[]`.
- **100% cache-safe stateful per-message `--turn-effort`**:
  - **Anthropic Claude 5+ / Opus 5.5**: Freezes top-level `output_config.effort` to preserve the cached prefix and injects per-message `mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01` marks on mechanical tool turns, restoring full effort on failing/substantive turns.
  - **OpenAI GPT-6**: Freezes top-level reasoning effort and emits `configuration_update` items on mechanical continuations, restoring on substantive prompts.
  - **Legacy/incompatible endpoints**: Leaves top-level effort untouched rather than mutating the cached prefix.

## E2E Benchmark Results (`inferred`)

Measured via `go test -v ./proxy/... -run TestE2ENativeCodemodeHarnessOptimizations` (local simulated cache & pricing accounting — **`inferred`**, **0 Caveman-induced cache busts**):

Updates `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` from 5.11.0 to 5.13.0
Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.13.0 (November 11, 2026)

This release adds automatic client certificate reloading and temporal precision metadata for database/sql. It also fixes a panic on malformed server responses, unsafe retries after connection failures, and range encoding. See Changes for client certificate configuration behavior that may affect existing applications.

Security Fixes

  • Panic in Rows.Values on malformed server responses (GHSA-w9rp-vfrh-q8vv). A server response containing fewer row values than declared fields could cause an index-out-of-range panic in Rows.Values. It now returns an error and closes the rows when the counts differ, including when there are extra values, matching Rows.Scan validation.

Features

  • pgconn: reload client certificates and keys configured through sslcert and sslkey for each TLS certificate request, allowing new connections to pick up rotated credentials without recreating the configuration or restarting the application. Files are still validated during configuration parsing. Relative paths retain their parse-time directory, and reloads follow symlinks (Erin Shepherd)
  • stdlib: expose fractional seconds precision for timestamp, timestamptz, time, timetz, and interval through ColumnTypePrecisionScale and database/sql.ColumnType.DecimalSize. These return precision 0, the fractional seconds precision as scale, and ok=true. The scale defaults to 6 when no fractional seconds precision is declared; precision 0 means numeric precision is not applicable (Danny Xu)

Changes

  • pgconn: file-backed client certificates are no longer stored in the parsed TLSConfig.Certificates slice. Setting TLSConfig.Certificates (including a non-nil empty slice) or TLSConfig.GetClientCertificate overrides automatic reloading. Replacing TLSConfig, including with a direct TLSConfig.Clone, discards the file-backed certificate settings; use pgconn.Config.Copy to preserve them when copying a configuration. Certificate and key files must remain readable for subsequent TLS certificate requests. Encrypted keys reuse the password resolved during configuration parsing; GetSSLPassword is not called again on reload.

Bug Fixes

  • pgconn: do not mark a connection-closed error encountered while receiving a response as safe to retry, since the request may already have reached the server. This prevents database/sql from automatically repeating a statement that may already have executed. The error still supports errors.Is(err, pgconn.ErrConnClosed) (Aayush Shah)
  • pgconn: skip sending a cancel request when a connection fails during startup, avoiding an unnecessary second connection attempt (felipe stival)
  • pgconn: accept unencrypted combined certificate/key PEM files with the certificate before the key, as well as key-first files (Erin Shepherd)
  • pgtype: encode Range[any] values returned by RangeCodec.DecodeValue and Rows.Values in both binary and text formats, allowing decoded ranges and multiranges to be reused as query arguments or in CopyFrom (waw666waw666)
  • stdlib: report ok=false for the precision and scale of unconstrained numeric columns instead of bogus values (Danny Xu)
  • stdlib: report math.MaxInt64 for the lengths of unconstrained varchar, bpchar, and varbit columns instead of negative lengths (PerryLink)

Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.59.0 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.62.0

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-23 v1.64.0:

    • Add vfs.LockOpener and vfs.Locker: a VFS made for vfs.Register can lock its databases against other processes and against other registrations of the same storage. Opt-in: a VFS that does not implement LockOpener works as before, and its databases are still safe inside one registration only. The documentation of Locker says what such a lock must guarantee. See [GitLab merge request #151](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/151), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-11-22 v1.63.0:

    • Connections are now opened with SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX instead of SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX, which takes a mutex lock and unlock off every column read and makes scanning rows noticeably faster. That mutex never kept two goroutines on one connection apart, so nothing else changes for code using the driver's API; code that takes a connection's SQLite handle from unexported fields and calls SQLite with it from another goroutine must now serialize those calls itself. Resolves [GitHub issue #13](modernc-org/sqlite#13), thanks guille-work!
    • A zero-length BLOB now reads as an empty []byte instead of nil, in rows and in the pre-update hook, so it no longer scans like NULL; read and written back, it used to fail a BLOB NOT NULL constraint or turn into NULL. Code that compares a scanned empty BLOB with nil sees the difference, and json.Marshal gives "" for it instead of null; NULL reads as before. Resolves [GitHub issue #14](modernc-org/sqlite#14). See [GitHub pull request #15](modernc-org/sqlite#15), thanks Michael Haddon (@​mhaddon)!
    • Add vfs.Register: a VFS written in Go that a database can be written through, next to the read-only vfs.New. Opt-in: a database goes through such a VFS only when the application registers one and names it in the DSN. The write-ahead log needs locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE for now; the documentation of Register says what the package does for the VFS and what it leaves out. Resolves [GitLab issue #109](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/109). See [GitLab merge request #148](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/148), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix how a VFS of modernc.org/sqlite/vfs copies a database name of 4097 bytes or more: it went into SQLite's path buffer without its terminator, and SQLite then measured it past the bytes written. Opening such a name failed with SQLITE_CANTOPEN and still does; nothing is copied now. See [GitLab merge request #148](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/148), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix 'now' on a connection through a VFS made by vfs.New: its clock moved in steps of one second, so strftime('%f','now') and unixepoch('now','subsec') were the same for a whole second. It has milliseconds now, as on SQLite's own VFS. Found in the review of [GitLab merge request #148](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/148).
    • Fix a crash in the pre-update hook on a row SQLite cannot read. Old and New ignored SQLite's error and used the value anyway, a nil pointer dereference for a row of a damaged database file; they now return SQLite's error. A TEXT value with a NUL now reaches the hook whole. See [GitLab merge request #149](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/149), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A TEXT argument with a NUL now reaches Go functions and virtual tables whole. It used to end at its first NUL unless VolatileArgs was set, so a virtual table that applies a constraint itself could answer with the rows of the shorter value. Code that relied on the cut gets the longer string. See [GitLab merge request #150](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/150), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • vfs.New no longer fails a database with a -journal file next to it as out of memory. It refused to open any journal, so every read failed with SQLITE_NOMEM, even with the journal journal_mode=PERSIST or TRUNCATE leaves behind, which SQLite ignores. Such a database now reads; one with a hot journal, which SQLite would have to roll back first, fails with SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK, as it does opened with mode=ro.

  • 2026-11-07 v1.62.0:

    • Add illumos/amd64, tested on an OmniOS builder. Resolves [GitLab issue #210](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/210), thanks Jasper Siepkes (@​siepkes), who also started the modernc.org/libc port!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.16.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.8.0; SQLite stays 3.54.1 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.80.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add opt-in syncing with fdatasync(2), off by default: Fdatasync(true) makes commits sync with fdatasync instead of fsync, process-wide, which skips the timestamp update fsync forces and keeps a commit just as durable. FdatasyncEnabled reports the setting; on macOS and Windows Fdatasync returns ErrFdatasyncUnavailable. Resolves [GitHub issue #10](modernc-org/sqlite#10), thanks aibeshkov!
    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!

title: Hermes Code Mode loses flow-style MCP servers when syncing config edits
body:
**What happen**

An opt-in `caveman wrap --codemode` Hermes session can remove existing MCP servers from the real `config.yaml` on exit. A valid flow-style `mcp_servers` map is treated as empty when the temporary configuration is written back.

**Expected**

Preserve unmodified MCP definitions in both flow and block style, apply the session edit, and do not persist the temporary `caveman-codemode` entry. If the merge cannot preserve the input, leave the original file untouched and warn.

**Before/after example**

I ran the exported `mergeHermesConfigEdits` with Bun against unmodified Caveman source. The inputs represent the original file and a temporary config with only the model changed:

```ts
import { mergeHermesConfigEdits } from './packages/cli/src/codemode.ts'

const original = 'model: old\nmcp_servers: {existing: {url: https://example.invalid/mcp}}\n'
const edited = 'model: new\nmcp_servers:\n  caveman-codemode:\n    command: caveman-mcp\n'
console.log(JSON.stringify(mergeHermesConfigEdits(edited, original)))
// Observed: "model: new\n" — `existing` is missing.
```

[The extractor](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/70f4f34e834893ea9af9f4fc6022266bd56d18b1/packages/cli/src/codemode.ts#L1205-L1268) reads indented entries, not the value on the `mcp_servers:` line. [Sync-back](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/70f4f34e834893ea9af9f4fc6022266bd56d18b1/packages/cli/src/codemode.ts#L1377-L1401) writes the incomplete merge back to the real file. This is separate from native enable/disable ownership; #1559 introduced the Code Mode path.

**Platform**

Other: Hermes Agent; isolated source probe on Linux x86-64. No live provider session or user config used.

**Version / install method**

Caveman 4.2.0, source `70f4f34` (also `main` when checked), Bun 1.4.4. AI-assisted source review and reproduction.

title: Code Mode does not disable bridged MCP servers on OpenCode V2
body:
**What happen**

Caveman 4.2.0 writes a V1-style `{ enabled: false }` override for every already-bridged OpenCode MCP server. OpenCode V2 drops that override before merging configuration. The bridged original can therefore remain enabled alongside Code Mode. Discovery also reads the flat V1 map rather than V2 `mcp.servers`.

**Expected**

Recognize the host's config format and disable exactly the bridged OpenCode-owned servers in the temporary overlay. Preserve the V1 path and leave on-disk config unchanged. If the V2 mask cannot be applied, report that limitation rather than treating it as active.

**Evidence**

- [Caveman overlay producer](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/70f4f34e834893ea9af9f4fc6022266bd56d18b1/packages/cli/src/codemode.ts#L1035-L1059) writes `mcp.docs = { enabled: false }` when `docs` is supplied as a bridged name.
- [OpenCode V2 at `71cd8c0`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/71cd8c064c8b93c31604c4c4074adb8b45790fc1/packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts#L268-L280) explicitly omits an enabled-only legacy entry. Its native contract uses `mcp.servers.<name>.disabled`. Related OpenCode tracking: anomalyco/opencode#61589 and #61760. This report is for the Caveman overlay and discovery, not a second issue on OpenCode.

**Platform / version**

OpenCode V2 (`71cd8c0`), Caveman 4.2.0 (`70f4f34`). Source trace only; no live MCP server or user config used. AI-assisted review.

title: SessionEnd caveman-stats --record cancelled by 5s timeout on large transcripts
body:
## Bug

The SessionEnd hook `caveman-stats.js --record` is cancelled on long sessions:

```
SessionEnd hook [... node "$HOOK_ROOT/src/hooks/caveman-stats.js" --record] failed: Hook cancelled
```

## Cause

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` sets `"timeout": 5` for this hook. `recordFromHook` calls `parseSession`, which does `fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')`, `raw.split('\n')` and `JSON.parse` per line over the whole transcript. Transcripts of long sessions are 240-400 MB, so the parse cannot finish in 5 s and the hook is cancelled on every session end.

Version: 4.2.0 (also present in 4.1.0 cache). macOS, Node via `command -v node`.

## Workaround

Skip large transcripts in `recordFromHook`, before `parseSession`:

```js
try { if (fs.statSync(sessionFile).size > 50 * 1024 * 1024) return; } catch (e) { return; }
```

With this a 397 MB transcript exits 0 in about 0.07 s. The session is not recorded in `.caveman-history.jsonl`.

## Suggested fix

- Stream the transcript (`readline` over `fs.createReadStream`) instead of reading it whole, or
- read only the tail of the file, or
- skip above a size cap and log the skip, and/or raise the hook timeout.

A whole-file `readFileSync` also hits V8's ~512 MB string limit on very large transcripts.

title: shrink-hook command rewrite fails on Windows for Gemini CLI
body:
**What happen**                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
   <!-- What caveman do wrong -->                                                                                                                                                                                                   
   On Windows, when `shrink-hook` intercepts a `run_shell_command` tool call in Gemini CLI, it rewrites the command as:                                                                                                             
   `'C:/.../caveman.CMD' shrink -- <cmd>` (missing the PowerShell `&` call operator).                                                                                                                                               

   Because Gemini CLI executes shell commands via `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command <command>`, PowerShell treats `'C:/.../caveman.CMD'` as a string literal expression and fails immediately with (in french):                               
```ps
Jeton inattendu « shrink » dans l’expression ou l’instruction.
       + CategoryInfo          : ParserError: (:) [], ParentContainsErrorRecordException
       + FullyQualifiedErrorId : UnexpectedToken
```                                                                                                                                                                               

   In `shrinkHook()`, `cavemanBinForHook(false)` is hardcoded under the assumption that all Windows hosts use Git Bash (Claude Code), but Gemini CLI uses native PowerShell.                                                        

   **Expected**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
   <!-- What caveman should do -->                                                                                                                                                                                                  
   `shrinkHook()` should account for Gemini CLI on Windows by enabling the PowerShell invocation format (`powershell = isGemini && process.platform === "win32"`), producing:                                                       
   `& 'C:/.../caveman.CMD' shrink -- <cmd>`                                                                                                                                                                                         

   **Before/after example**                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  Input: Gemini CLI runs git push origin <branch> with shrink-hook enabled                                                                                                                                                          
  Got:   'C:/.../caveman.CMD' shrink -- git push origin <branch> (PowerShell syntax error: UnexpectedToken 'shrink')                                                                                                                
  Want:  & 'C:/.../caveman.CMD' shrink -- git push origin <branch> (valid PowerShell command execution)                                                                                                                             


   **Platform**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
   - [ ] Claude Code                                                                                                                                                                                                                
   - [ ] Codex                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
   - [x] Other: Gemini CLI 0.70 on Windows (win32)                                                                                                                                                                                       

   **Version / install method**                                                                                                                                                                                                     
   `@caveman-ai/cli` v4.0.1 (installed globally via npm) on Windows, Node v24.22.1                                                                                                                                                  

   **Suggested fix**                                                                                                                                                                                                                
   In `shrinkHook()`:                                                                                                                                                                                                               
  // updatedInput.command executes in host shell (Git Bash on Claude Windows,                                                                                                                                                       
  // but PowerShell on Gemini Windows). Only include & for Gemini PowerShell.                                                                                                                                                       
  const powershell = isGemini ? process.platform === "win32" : false;                                                                                                                                                               
  const rewritten = ${cavemanBinForHook(powershell)} shrink -- ${command.trim()};

title: fix(compress): keep frontmatter that ends at end of file local
body:
## Bug

`FRONTMATTER_REGEX` in `skills/caveman-compress/scripts/compress.py` requires a newline after the closing `---`. A frontmatter-only file saved without a final newline (`---\nname: task\n---`) is not split, so the whole file goes to the provider as body and the reply replaces the frontmatter. The same file with a final newline is correctly refused ("body is empty after frontmatter removal").

Repro (Python 3.13, `call_claude` stubbed to return `"x"`):

```
'---\ntitle: x\n---\n'  -> refused, 0 provider calls
'---\ntitle: x\n---'    -> compressed, 1 provider call, frontmatter sent, file now "x"
'---\r\ntitle: x\r\n---' -> same
```

## Fix

Accept the closing `---` at end of file: `---(?:\r?\n|\Z)`. Edited the source only; `plugins/caveman/` is the CI mirror.

Behavior diff, old vs new regex, over 18 edge cases and the 191 `.md`/`.txt` files in the repo: only the three end-of-file cases change; `----`, `---x`, `--- `, thematic breaks and body blocks are unchanged.

## Tests

- New cases in `tests/test_compress_frontmatter.py`; they fail on main (3 failures) and pass with the fix.
- Python 3.13.14: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` 337 OK (main: 335 OK); `python tests/verify_repo.py` passes.

title: fix(installer): keep hooks and statusline whose path the shell expands
body:
## Bug

The Claude install "self-heal" (`pruneOrphanedManagedHooks`, `installer/lib/settings.js`) deletes a working hand-written statusline or hook whose path uses `$HOME` or `~`. Claude Code runs the command through a shell, which expands those; the prune pass joins the literal token under the config dir, finds nothing, and removes the entry as orphaned. With the plugin already installed, nothing re-wires it, so the statusline is just gone.

Repro (fake `HOME`, stub `claude` reporting the plugin installed, `settings.json` statusLine `bash $HOME/.claude/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh`, script present and exits 0):

```
$ node installer/install.js --only claude --non-interactive
  caveman plugin already installed (use --force to reinstall)
  removed 1 orphaned caveman hook entry from settings.json (target script missing)
settings.json after: { "theme": "dark" }
```

## Fix

Treat a token with `$` or a leading `~` as unknown (not missing), the same rule `statuslineScripts()` in `caveman-activate.js` already uses (#1159). Genuinely missing absolute/relative paths are still pruned.

Behavior diff, main vs patched, `linux` and `win32`: only the `$HOME`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR}` and `~` rows change; missing absolute, relative, `a~b`, quoted-with-spaces, foreign-platform and non-managed rows are unchanged.

## Tests

- Two new cases in `tests/installer/unit.settings.test.mjs`; both fail on main (`1 !== 0`, `2 !== 0`), pass with the fix.
- Node 18.20.8 and 22.12.0 (darwin/arm64): installer + hooks + standalone tests run per file with stdin closed: 77/78 files green on this branch, same as main (unit.settings 44 → 46). `shim-security.test.mjs` hangs identically on main here (its pty helper needs a real tty), so that file is unverified locally.
- Same repro after the fix: no prune message, statusLine kept.
