title: OpenCode V2: Code Mode drops the configured MCP working directory
body:
**What happen**
A local MCP server with a configured `cwd` loses that working directory when Caveman bridges it. A server resolving a relative fixture can then see a different file.

**Expected**
The bridged process should use the same workspace-relative working directory as the native OpenCode process.

**Evidence**
[Caveman maps the local server without `cwd`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/b89752f6bca5a26bfde8b019813554241800ca99/packages/cli/src/codemode.ts#L240-L280); [OpenCode applies it at spawn](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/a3bf3758103ff2d3e5d9d49598ead6f74d16caf1/packages/core/src/mcp/stdio.ts#L38-L44). A regression test can compare the cwd reported by an inert fixture server, without a model call. This is not the native hook cwd in #1443.

**Platform**: OpenCode V2.

**Version / install method**: Caveman source `b89752f6` (includes #1565); OpenCode `a3bf3758`. Identified during a Nix integration audit. Source trace only; no live model session. AI-assisted audit and drafting.

title: OpenCode V2: wrapping `machine` injects unsupported `--standalone`
body:
**What happen**
`caveman wrap opencode machine list` is routed to `opencode --standalone machine list`. OpenCode deliberately rejects machine commands in standalone mode.

**Expected**
Preserve the `machine` arguments and use the normal persistent service. Keep standalone routing for commands that support it.

**Evidence**
[The subcommand exceptions omit `machine`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/b89752f6bca5a26bfde8b019813554241800ca99/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L6767-L6799). [The OpenCode handler rejects standalone mode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/a3bf3758103ff2d3e5d9d49598ead6f74d16caf1/packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/machine/common.ts#L20-L33). A routing test can assert the forwarded argv without connecting to a service.

**Platform**: OpenCode V2.

**Version / install method**: Caveman source `b89752f6` (includes #1565); OpenCode `a3bf3758`. Identified during a Nix integration audit. Source trace only; no live model session. AI-assisted audit and drafting.

title: OpenCode Shrink runs commands outside the served project
body:
**What happen**
When the OpenCode service starts outside a served project, the standalone Shrink adapter launches rewritten commands without that project as their cwd. Relative command paths can resolve against the service directory.

**Expected**
Run the rewritten command in the served project in both OpenCode plugin APIs.

**Evidence**
The generated adapter in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` calls `execFileSync` without `cwd`. [The downstream patch](https://github.com/jerome-benoit/dotfiles/blob/f8a17aaf/patches/caveman-opencode-shrink-workdir.patch) shows the affected call and both adapters. A fixture with distinct files in the host and project directories can distinguish them. #1443 covers native hooks; #1445 covers loading the V2 plugin.

**Platform**: OpenCode V2.

**Version / install method**: Caveman source `b89752f6` (includes #1565); OpenCode `a3bf3758`. Identified during a Nix integration audit. Source trace only; no live model session. AI-assisted audit and drafting.

title: `doctor hermes` reports `installed` when MCP recovery is unavailable
body:
**What happen**
With a healthy ownership journal and launchable binaries, a disabled Hermes MCP entry can leave `components.mcp_recovery=false` while `doctor` reports `installed` and `doctor --fix` reports `not_needed`.

**Expected**
Make the overall status reflect unavailable recovery. Do not reactivate a user-owned disabled MCP entry.

**Evidence**
[The verdict](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/b89752f6bca5a26bfde8b019813554241800ca99/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L12335-L12342) uses launchability; [the component also checks the Hermes route](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/b89752f6bca5a26bfde8b019813554241800ca99/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L12385-L12402). #1490 corrected component presence, not the overall verdict. Check the JSON, exit status and unchanged user config together.

**Platform**: Hermes.

**Version / install method**: Caveman source `b89752f6` (includes #1565). Identified during a Nix integration audit. Source trace only; no live model session. AI-assisted audit and drafting.

title: proxy: /messages route returns 401 when x-api-key and Authorization are both present
body:
## Summary

`caveman-proxy` rejects requests to an Anthropic-style `/messages` route when `x-api-key` and `Authorization: Bearer` are both present, returning `401 authentication_error` for a key the upstream accepts. Any client that routes an Anthropic-format model through an OpenAI-compatible provider hits this, because the two layers add different auth headers.

## Environment

- caveman: `bin-v4.0.1` (modules.lock.json), proxy listening on `127.0.0.1:8787`, `mode=compress`, `basis=inferred`, `inbound_auth=none`
- opencode: v2.4.1, Linux 7.0.0-44-generic, x86_64
- Provider under test: `opencode-go`, `baseURL http://127.0.0.1:8787/w/opencode/compat/opencode-go/v1`
- Upstream behind the proxy: OpenCode Go (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go`)

## Reproduction

1. Start `caveman-proxy` on 127.0.0.1:8787.
2. Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider whose `baseURL` points at the proxy, with a valid provider API key stored.
3. Pick a model whose catalog package is Anthropic-style (`@opencode/ai/providers/anthropic`), for example `opencode-go/qwen3.8-flash`. The client sends `x-api-key` (Anthropic package) and `Authorization: Bearer` (provider auth layer) to `<baseURL>/messages`.
4. Send the same request by hand to compare header variants.

## Expected Behavior

`POST /w/opencode/compat/opencode-go/v1/messages` succeeds whenever the key is valid, regardless of whether the request also carries an `Authorization` header. The upstream accepts both.

## Actual Behavior

Header matrix, same key, same body, against the proxy:

| path | headers | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/messages` | `x-api-key` only | 200 |
| `/v1/messages` | `x-api-key` + `Authorization: Bearer` | **401** `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"OpenCode Go requires an API key"}}` |
| `/v1/messages` | `Authorization: Bearer` only | **401**, same body |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | `Authorization: Bearer` | 200 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | both headers | 200 |

Bypassing the proxy and calling the upstream directly with the same key:

| upstream path | headers | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages` | `x-api-key` only | 200 |
| `inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages` | `x-api-key` + `Bearer` | 200 |
| `inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages` | `Bearer` only | 200 |
| `inference/go/v1/messages` | either | 200 |

So the 401 originates in the proxy, not upstream. Through opencode the failure surfaces as `Error: OpenCode Go requires an API key` and no inference request ever reaches the provider's request log.

## Additional Context

Dropping the proxy from the provider's `baseURL` (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1`) makes the same model respond normally, which is the workaround in use:

```
opencode run -m opencode-go/qwen3.8-flash "reply with: ok"      -> ok
opencode run -m opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash "reply with: ok" -> ok
```

Suggested fix: on `/messages`, forward auth headers untouched instead of treating a present `Authorization` as an auth-mode switch, or strip `Authorization` when a valid `x-api-key` is already present. Either keeps OpenAI-compatible provider routing working for Anthropic-format models.

Reproduced with and without OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` calls in the same session; only the `/messages` route is affected.

Updates `ossf/scorecard-action` from 2.5.0 to 2.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from ossf/scorecard-action's releases.

v2.6.0

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.7.0, built with Go 1.27.4. For changes to checks and results, and the security fixes in this Scorecard release, see the Scorecard v5.7.0 release notes.

Getting started

This is the first release with ready-to-use workflows in this repository. To add Scorecard to a repository, copy one into .github/workflows/scorecard.yml:

  • examples/scorecard.yml for public repositories. It publishes results to the Scorecard API, which enables the badge and the REST API, and fails the step if the API rejects them.
  • examples/scorecard-private.yml for private repositories. It doesn't publish.

Both pin every action to a full commit SHA, set cache-mode: none, and upload results even when an earlier step fails. CI lints them with zizmor, actionlint and yamllint. If your linter reports cache-mode as unknown, see Workflow Linters.

Copy the examples from main, which pins this release. A tagged commit can't pin its own SHA, so the copies at the v2.6.0 tag still name v2.5.0.

To add the workflow to many repositories at once, the installer opens a pull request in each one. See docs/installer.md.

What's Changed

  • New fail_on_publish_error input (default false): when set, the step fails if the Scorecard API rejects the results. Network errors and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx stay warnings. New outputs results_published and publication_status report whether publishing worked, and the job summary says so. A rejected (4xx) publish is now sent once instead of three times, and the publish error and warning show as annotations. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1721
  • Example workflows for public and private repositories in examples/, with every action pinned to a full SHA. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1722
  • The examples set cache-mode: none and upload results even when an earlier step fails. The README's new Workflow Linters section lists which linter versions recognize cache-mode. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1727
  • The installer (cmd/installer) adds the generated example workflow with the repository's default branch, and no longer needs a starter-workflows checkout. Usage is in docs/installer.md. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1728

Other

  • Point getting started at the v2.6.0 example workflows by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1750
  • Lint the example workflows in CI by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1724
  • Move CI to golangci-lint v2 by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1725

title: fix(cli): start the stopped local runtime when setup runs again
body:
After a reboot or `caveman stop`, the local runtime is down but wired agents still point at its address, so every request fails. Running `caveman setup --yes` again printed "This will change nothing" and "Ready" and left the runtime down; only `caveman doctor <agent> --fix` restarted it.

**Cause:** `planModules` only planned "RUN caveman-proxy start local runtime" when wiring a new agent, so an already-wired agent with a dead runtime gave an empty plan, and `applyModules` returned before starting anything.

**Fix:** when an agent that stays wired (not aider) points at a local runtime that is down and allowed to autostart, the plan includes the existing RUN line, and applying it starts the runtime through `ensureLocalProxyForNative`, the same path `enable` and `doctor <agent> --fix` use. Plans scoped to modules that do not wire agents are unchanged.

**Test:** `setup --yes after a reboot starts the runtime the wired agents point at` (`packages/cli/tests/onboard-setup.runtime.mjs`). It fails on main ("change nothing" printed, no proxy spawn) and passes with this change.

**Checked locally:** `pnpm --filter @caveman-ai/cli run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `test:fast` (252 passing), the onboard / native-enable / modules suites (259/259), and `python tests/verify_repo.py`. Not run end to end with the real Go proxy (the start path itself is unchanged and already tested).

title: fix(proxy): map duplicated x-api-key credential to x-api-key on opencode-go /v1/messages
body:
Fixes #1585.

When an Anthropic-style client talking through an OpenAI-compatible provider sends the same key in both `Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key`, `standalone.go` mapped the matched credential to the default `bearer` scheme. On `/compat/opencode-go/v1/messages` (and `wire_dialect: anthropic`), `openaicompat` kept `Authorization: Bearer` instead of forwarding `x-api-key`, causing upstream 401 responses.

Changes:
- Set `credential.Scheme = bearer_and_api_key` in `proxy/internal/standalone/standalone.go` when an inbound bearer token duplicates an already extracted `x-api-key`.
- Limit the `Authorization: Bearer` preservation rule in `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat.go` to generic OpenAI-compatible mounts (`prefix != /compat/opencode-go` and `wireDialect != anthropic` and `key != no-key-required`), so `/v1/messages` translates the duplicated credential to `x-api-key` and strips `authorization`.
- Add regression tests in `proxy/internal/standalone/compat_duplicate_credential_test.go` and `proxy/providers/openaicompat/openaicompat_test.go`.

Tested locally:
- `go test ./proxy/internal/standalone ./proxy/providers/openaicompat` (388 passed across both packages)
- `python tests/verify_repo.py`

title: docs: installation page pins one-liners to v3.2.0 instead of v4.2.0
body:
## What happens

The installation page at https://docs.caveman.so/caveman/installation still pins the one-liners to **v3.2.0**:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v3.2.0/install.ps1 | iex
```

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v3.2.0/install.sh | bash
```

The repository's `INSTALL.md` and the latest release (Caveman 4.2.0, 2026-11-22) use **v4.2.0**. So anyone who follows the docs site installs a release that is two majors old.

## Impact observed

I installed on Windows 11 with the v3.2.0 PowerShell one-liner from the docs page, with Claude Code 2.1.318, Codex and GitHub Copilot present:

- Codex and Copilot got their skills via `npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman --skill * -a <agent> --yes -g`, so the skills went to `~/.agents/skills`.
- Claude Code got only the standalone hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json`. The plugin was never installed (`claude plugin list` shows no plugins), so no caveman skills were available in Claude Code.

I have not checked whether v4.2.0 behaves the same. The first problem is that the docs point to an outdated release.

## Suggestion

- Update the docs page to v4.2.0, or generate it from `INSTALL.md` so the tag can't drift again.
- Possibly also publish a stable alias that always points to the latest release, for example a `latest` installer URL that redirects to the current tag or a release asset under `releases/latest/download/`. The docs could then show it next to the pinned command. I understand pinning is intentional for reproducibility, so the pinned command could stay the recommended one.

title: fix(opencode): run shrink-hook subprocess in served project
body:
Fixes #1578

When the OpenCode service starts outside a served project, the standalone Shrink adapter launched its shrink-hook decision subprocess without that project as cwd. Relative command paths could resolve against the service directory.

This carries the served project into the generated shrink plugin the same way the native plugin already does (see #1443, #92512e1f):
- rewrite(command, cwd) passes cwd to execFileSync
- V1 factory takes ctx and passes ctx.directory
- V2 setup passes ctx.location.directory

Verification:
- python tests/verify_repo.py passes (All local verification checks passed)
- tsc --noEmit passes, windows-platform.runtime.mjs 16/16 pass
- hooks.runtime.mjs opencode tests blocked by Windows symlink EPERM in this env (pre-existing, unrelated to this change); verified generated source contains cwd wiring via direct source check

The rewritten command itself still runs under the host cwd handling; this only scopes the decision subprocess, byte-safe fail-open preserved.

title: perf(tests): parallelize JS/Go test suites and eliminate avoidable waits
body:
## Summary
- **JS / Installer / Hook tests:**
  - Remove `--test-concurrency=2` in `package.json` so `node --test` uses default parallelism across files.
  - Replace per-agent `/bin/sh -c command -v` forks in `installer/install.js` (`hasCmd`) with pure-JS `resolvePosixCommand()` (`statSync` + `X_OK`), speeding up both tests and real POSIX installs.
  - Add optional `CAVEMAN_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` override (defaulting to `10000`, pinned by test assertions) so hang-recovery tests exercise the real timeout kill path in 300ms instead of sleeping 10s each.
  - Convert `spawnSync` helpers in PowerShell/standalone hook tests to bounded async `spawn`, add PowerShell telemetry/update-check opt-out env vars, parallelize `tests/test_hook_stdin_lifecycle.js`, and replace the serial `for` loop in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `node --test tests/test_*.js`.

title: Dependency advisories in locked versions: 56 advisories across 10 packages, all with proven fixes
body:
Hi — I was doing an independent security review of this repo and ran its locked dependencies through OSV.dev. The repo's own code looks clean to me, and this is only about the locked dependency versions. I checked each advisory firsthand, including re-querying OSV at the fixed versions to confirm they come back clean.

## What I found

56 advisories, all with a fixed version that exists and re-queries clean:

| Package (locked) | Advisories | Fixed version (verified exists + re-query clean) |
|---|---|---|
| undici@7.29.0 | 18 | 7.30.1 |
| hono@4.13.1 | 10 | 4.13.16 |
| fast-uri@3.1.5 | 10 | 3.1.9 |
| ip-address@10.4.0 | 5 | 10.7.4 |
| @modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0 | 4 | 2.3.0 |
| @hono/node-server@2.1.0 | 3 | 2.1.6 |
| qs@6.15.3 | 3 | 6.16.1 |
| body-parser@2.3.0 | 1 | 2.4.0 |
| js-yaml@3.15.1 | 1 | 3.15.2 |
| zod@4.4.3 | 1 | 4.6.6 |

The floor (manifest) check found nothing — the 21 direct dependency floors came back with 0 advisories. All 56 come from the lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml, 434 packages queried). I re-queried the same set at the fixed versions and the result came back clean — **0 advisories**.

## Notes, in case they help

- One care point on `@hono/node-server`: 2.1.3 looks like the fix for one of the advisories, but another needs 2.1.6, so 2.1.6 is the version that closes all three at once. I re-queried at 2.1.6 and it came back clean.
- I saw your undici work while checking for duplicates — PR #1500 (override undici to 8.12.4 so the release audit passes). The lock at this pin still has undici@7.29.0 with 18 advisories. If #1500 already covers that path on a newer commit, please just ignore this part — I scanned a pinned commit, not live HEAD.
- The zod one (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) is on the 4.x line, so 4.6.6 is a minor bump, not a major.
- Happy to be wrong on any of this; if a locked version I flagged is already gone on main, no action needed.

Thanks for Caveman — the keychain handling and the careful Gemini trust scoping in the installer are genuinely thoughtful, and I hope this is useful. Sorry if anything here reads as presumptuous; it is only a suggestion.

title: fix(deps): bump gobwas/ws to v1.5.0 for GO-2026-6940
body:
## TL;DR

Bumps `github.com/gobwas/ws` from **v1.4.0** to **v1.5.0** to fix [GO-2026-6940](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6940): v1.4.0 allocates as much memory as a peer's declared frame length asks for, with no upper bound. Lockfile change only, no code touched. Found alongside #1601 / #1602.

## What changes

| Module | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `github.com/gobwas/ws` (indirect) | v1.4.0 | v1.5.0 |
| `github.com/gobwas/pool` (indirect) | v0.2.1 | removed (ws v1.5.0 no longer requires it) |
| `golang.org/x/sys v0.6.0/go.mod` checksum | in go.sum | removed (was only needed by ws v1.4.0; selected x/sys stays v0.49.0) |

No other module version moves. The repo has a single `go.mod` at the root, so nothing else locks gobwas/ws.

**Where it comes from:**

```
$ go mod why -m github.com/gobwas/ws
# github.com/gobwas/ws
github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/browse
github.com/chromedp/chromedp
github.com/gobwas/ws
```

`chromedp/chromedp v0.16.0` (used by `browse/` for its CDP websocket) requires ws v1.4.0. MVS now picks v1.5.0.

## Evidence

Go 1.26.11, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`.

- `go build ./...`: exit 0
- `go test ./...`: exit 0. 62 packages `ok`, 4 with no test files, 0 failures. Includes `browse`, `browse/cmd/caveman-browse`, all of `engine/...`, `proxy/...`, `shared/...`.
- `govulncheck ./...` (v1.10.0, DB updated 2026-11-24):
  ```
  No vulnerabilities found.
  ```
- OSV.dev `querybatch` over every module@version in `go.sum`:
  - before: 3 hits: `gobwas/ws v1.4.0` (GO-2026-6940), `x/sys v0.6.0` (GO-2026-5024, go.mod-only line), `yaml.v3 v3.0.0-20200313…` (GO-2022-0603)
  - after: 1 hit: `yaml.v3 v3.0.0-20200313…`. That one was already there and is a `/go.mod`-only checksum line. The selected version is `gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1`, which is patched, and govulncheck agrees. Left out of scope.
- `python3 tests/verify_repo.py`: `All local verification checks passed`

## Upstream `caveman-browse`

`browse/` is a consumer copy of [`JuliusBrussee/caveman-browse`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman-browse). It has no `go.mod` of its own here, so this PR covers everything built from this repo, and a later sync of the `.go` files will not bring v1.4.0 back. The upstream repo has its own `go.mod` (still `gobwas/ws v1.4.0` via `chromedp v0.15.1`) and publishes its own binaries, so it gets the same fix separately: JuliusBrussee/caveman-browse#7.

title: Unable to reselect caveman-auto in Claude Code after an automatic safeguard model switch

I selected `caveman-auto[1m]` in Claude Code with automatic model switching on safeguard events enabled. I asked Claude Code to check whether a local session hook was firing. During that check, it displayed `Details: [cyber]` and `Switched to Opus 4.8`. I saw the notice twice during the session.

After the switch, I couldn't get back to `caveman-auto` through the model picker in that session. I didn't test whether asking an unrelated question would restore automatic routing.

title: ci: run the slow gates as parallel jobs
body:
Cuts the time from push to a green PR by running the slowest gates as parallel jobs. Coverage stays the same: every step, suite, package and test that ran before still runs.

## Baseline (last 30 completed runs per workflow)

| Workflow | Wall (median, green) | Slowest job (median) |
|---|---|---|
| engine-ci | 19.1 min | windows 17.3 min, middleware-postgres 7.7 min, typescript 4.9 min |
| CI | 4.7 min | macos 3.9 min |
| codeql | 2.3 min | analyze / go 2.1 min |
| middleware-conformance | 1.8 min | e2e 1.8 min |

Reds: supply-chain's govulncheck failed on every run since GO-2026-6940 (gobwas/ws v1.4.0, reachable from browse's chromedp driver and the codemode HTTP upstream). middleware-postgres once hit go test's 10-minute default timeout. The other engine-ci reds were test flakes (Windows `TestPrefixReplacementConcurrentWrites` SQLITE_BUSY, `TestProviderStreamsFlushBeforeCompletion/chatgpt`, a CLI onboarding test). Most "failed" runs in the list are fork PRs waiting for workflow approval (`action_required`), not failures.

## Changes

- **engine-ci / windows**: runs as six parallel jobs instead of one: `go test` sharded two ways (each shard gets one of the two packages that take about 3 min on Windows), the root/Python/extension suites, `npm run test:windows`, the workspace suites, and the pi extension. Each job gets the same toolchain and `pnpm install` as the old job (some Go tests validate against `node_modules`). A `windows` job reports one result: green when every part passed, or when the PR touched nothing Windows can break.
- **engine-ci / windows compat**: `npm run test:windows` spent about 4 min cross-compiling every package into a Go cache under the temp dir that started empty each run. Pull requests now restore the newest saved copy; pushes to main and manual runs save one.
- **engine-ci / changes**: the Windows scope check moves out of root-surfaces into a job that only checks out the repo, so the Windows jobs start right away instead of waiting about 1.7 min for root-surfaces' tests.
- **engine-ci / typescript**: the CLI suite is split by test file across two jobs. Each shard runs the package's own `test` script minus the build it starts with, and fails if that script changes shape. The pi extension gets its own job. The `typescript` job runs the rest.
- **engine-ci / middleware-postgres**: each package's top-level tests come from `go test -list` and are dealt across jobs (store 2, middleware 3). `TestLargeSessionDeletesUnderTheDefaultDeadline/sqlite` (about 4 min alone under `-race`) runs in a job of its own, which fails unless that subtest actually ran; the middleware shards skip only that subtest, so its other backends still run there.
- **`.github/scripts/shard.mjs`**: builds shards from the real `go list ./...`, `go test -list` or file list at run time. It fails unless the shards together are exactly that list: no duplicates, nothing dropped, no empty shard.
- **supply-chain**: gobwas/ws bumped to v1.5.0 (same change as #1603).
- Action pins: setup-go updated to v7.1.0, and the version comments now match the pinned SHAs (the `# v4` / `# v5` comments were wrong: those SHAs are v7.0.1 / v7.0.0). All pinned actions are on their Node 24 majors.
- `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout that never pushes.
- docs-links runs on every PR, because a relative link breaks when the file it points to moves; it takes about 15 s. It also gets a concurrency group.
- Path filters that missed files their jobs read: verify-codex now includes `agents/probe-installed.mjs` and `agents/version.mjs`; middleware-conformance now includes the signing pubkey, `scripts/sign-binary-checksums.mjs` and the pnpm manifests.

No job or test was removed, skipped, or relaxed.

## Measured on this PR

engine-ci wall clock (push to last job done), pull_request runs on this branch:

| Commit | engine-ci wall | Critical path |
|---|---|---|
| fbe65fe8 (first split, cold caches) | 7.9 min | |
| e243b9ab (Postgres sharded by test name) | 7.1 min | |
| 5f65dd19 (solo subtest, warm compat cache) | 7.1 min | |
| a0404854 (head) | 8.2 min | middleware solo 7.5 min; every other job 4.5 min or less |

At head: windows parts 2.5 to 4.5 min, typescript parts 1.4 to 3.4 min, store shards 3.4 / 4.4 min, middleware shards 1.7 to 1.9 min. CI 3.8 min, codeql 2.4 min, middleware-conformance 1.5 min, middleware-python 1.7 min, supply-chain 1.3 min, verify-codex 1.0 min, docs-links 0.2 min. All checks green at head.

The remaining long pole is the single `-race` SQLite subtest above (5.5 to 7.5 min across runs); it can only get shorter by changing the test itself.
